## probes/phase11_network_attacks/50d_cross_protocol_tunnel.lua

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: HIGH
-- PROBE 50d: Cross-Protocol Tunneling Edge Cases
--
-- Context: Probes 50a tested exotic protocol handlers with simple payloads.
-- This probe goes deeper into tunneling protocols — IPv6-in-IPv4 (proto 41),
-- IP-in-IP (proto 4), and GRE (proto 47) — targeting the DECAPSULATION
-- logic specifically. Tunnel decapsulation is historically buggy because:
--
--   1. The inner packet re-enters ip_input() or ip6_input() recursively.
--      Stack depth, mbuf chain corruption, and re-entrant lock bugs hide here.
--   2. Inner/outer header conflicts (different src/dst, TTL underflow after
--      decap, inner packet larger than outer) stress trust boundaries.
--   3. Nested tunneling (tunnel-in-tunnel-in-tunnel) can overflow recursion
--      limits or confuse routing decisions.
--   4. Fragmented tunneled packets force two-phase reassembly (outer frags
--      reassembled, then inner frags) stressing memory allocators.
--
-- FreeBSD tunnel handling:
--   - Proto 4 (IPIP): in_gif_input() → ip_input() re-entry
--   - Proto 41 (6in4): in6_gif_input() → ip6_input() re-entry
--   - Proto 47 (GRE): gre_input() → decap based on protocol field
--
-- The raw socket + IP_HDRINCL + loopback combination lets us construct
-- arbitrary tunnel packets including pathological nesting.

print("=== PROBE 50d: CROSS-PROTOCOL TUNNELING EDGE CASES ===")
print("")

local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function safe_wb(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_byte(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function safe_wd(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_dword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function safe_wq(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_qword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end

local sc_socket = make_syscall(97)
local sc_setsockopt = make_syscall(105)
local sc_sendto = make_syscall(133)
local sc_close = make_syscall(6)

local AF_INET = 2
local SOCK_RAW = 3
local IP_HDRINCL = 2

local function setsockopt_int(fd, level, name, value)
    local buf = memory.alloc(4)
    safe_wd(buf, value)
    local ok, ret = pcall(function()
        return sc_setsockopt(uint64(fd), uint64(level), uint64(name),
            uint64(buf), uint64(4))
    end)
    if ok then return to_num(ret) end
    return -999
end

local function close_fd(fd)
    if fd and fd >= 0 then
        pcall(function() sc_close(uint64(fd)) end)
    end
end

-- Create raw socket
local rfd = -1
repeat
    local ok, fd = pcall(function()
        return sc_socket(uint64(AF_INET), uint64(SOCK_RAW), uint64(255))
    end)
    if not ok or to_num(fd) < 0 then
        print("FATAL: Cannot create raw socket")
        break
    end
    rfd = to_num(fd)
    setsockopt_int(rfd, 0, IP_HDRINCL, 1)
until true

if rfd < 0 then
    print("Cannot proceed without raw socket")
    return
end

local dest = memory.alloc(16)
safe_wb(dest, 16)
safe_wb(dest + 1, AF_INET)
safe_wb(dest + 2, 0)   -- port high
safe_wb(dest + 3, 0)   -- port low
safe_wb(dest + 4, 127) -- 127.0.0.1
safe_wb(dest + 5, 0)
safe_wb(dest + 6, 0)
safe_wb(dest + 7, 1)

local tests = 0
local sent_ok = 0

-- Helper: write IPv4 header at offset in buffer
local function write_ipv4_hdr(buf, off, proto, total_len, ttl, src_a, src_b, src_c, src_d, dst_a, dst_b, dst_c, dst_d)
    ttl = ttl or 64
    safe_wb(buf + off, 0x45)           -- ver=4, ihl=5
    safe_wb(buf + off + 1, 0)         -- tos
    safe_wb(buf + off + 2, math.floor(total_len / 256))
    safe_wb(buf + off + 3, total_len % 256)
    safe_wb(buf + off + 4, 0)         -- id
    safe_wb(buf + off + 5, 0)
    safe_wb(buf + off + 6, 0)         -- flags/frag
    safe_wb(buf + off + 7, 0)
    safe_wb(buf + off + 8, ttl)
    safe_wb(buf + off + 9, proto)
    safe_wb(buf + off + 10, 0)        -- checksum (kernel fills for outer)
    safe_wb(buf + off + 11, 0)
    safe_wb(buf + off + 12, src_a)
    safe_wb(buf + off + 13, src_b)
    safe_wb(buf + off + 14, src_c)
    safe_wb(buf + off + 15, src_d)
    safe_wb(buf + off + 16, dst_a)
    safe_wb(buf + off + 17, dst_b)
    safe_wb(buf + off + 18, dst_c)
    safe_wb(buf + off + 19, dst_d)
end

-- Helper: write IPv6 header at offset
local function write_ipv6_hdr(buf, off, next_hdr, payload_len, hop_limit, src_last, dst_last)
    hop_limit = hop_limit or 64
    src_last = src_last or 1
    dst_last = dst_last or 1
    safe_wb(buf + off, 0x60)           -- version=6, tc high
    safe_wb(buf + off + 1, 0)         -- tc low, flow high
    safe_wb(buf + off + 2, 0)         -- flow
    safe_wb(buf + off + 3, 0)         -- flow low
    safe_wb(buf + off + 4, math.floor(payload_len / 256))
    safe_wb(buf + off + 5, payload_len % 256)
    safe_wb(buf + off + 6, next_hdr)
    safe_wb(buf + off + 7, hop_limit)
    -- src: ::src_last
    for i = 8, 22 do safe_wb(buf + off + i, 0) end
    safe_wb(buf + off + 23, src_last)
    -- dst: ::dst_last
    for i = 24, 38 do safe_wb(buf + off + i, 0) end
    safe_wb(buf + off + 39, dst_last)
end

-- Helper: write GRE header at offset
local function write_gre_hdr(buf, off, proto_type, flags, key, seq)
    flags = flags or 0
    safe_wb(buf + off, math.floor(flags / 256))
    safe_wb(buf + off + 1, flags % 256)
    safe_wb(buf + off + 2, math.floor(proto_type / 256))
    safe_wb(buf + off + 3, proto_type % 256)
    local extra = 4
    if key then
        safe_wb(buf + off + extra, math.floor(key / 16777216) % 256)
        safe_wb(buf + off + extra + 1, math.floor(key / 65536) % 256)
        safe_wb(buf + off + extra + 2, math.floor(key / 256) % 256)
        safe_wb(buf + off + extra + 3, key % 256)
        extra = extra + 4
    end
    if seq then
        safe_wb(buf + off + extra, math.floor(seq / 16777216) % 256)
        safe_wb(buf + off + extra + 1, math.floor(seq / 65536) % 256)
        safe_wb(buf + off + extra + 2, math.floor(seq / 256) % 256)
        safe_wb(buf + off + extra + 3, seq % 256)
        extra = extra + 4
    end
    return extra
end

local function send_pkt(buf, len, desc)
    tests = tests + 1
    local ok, r = pcall(function()
        return sc_sendto(uint64(rfd), uint64(buf), uint64(len),
            uint64(0), uint64(dest), uint64(16))
    end)
    local ret = ok and to_num(r) or -999
    if ret >= 0 then sent_ok = sent_ok + 1 end
    print(string.format("  [%d] %s: ret=%d", tests, desc, ret))
end

print("--- Section A: IPv4-in-IPv4 (Proto 4) Tunneling ---")
print("")

-- A1: Basic IPIP tunnel — outer IPv4 wrapping inner IPv4
repeat
    local pkt = memory.alloc(256)
    -- Outer: proto 4 (IPIP), total_len = 20 outer + 20 inner + 8 payload = 48
    write_ipv4_hdr(pkt, 0, 4, 0, 64, 127,0,0,1, 127,0,0,1)
    -- Inner: UDP proto=17, total_len = 28
    write_ipv4_hdr(pkt, 20, 17, 28, 64, 127,0,0,1, 127,0,0,1)
    -- 8 bytes UDP-ish payload
    for i = 40, 47 do safe_wb(pkt + i, 0xAA) end
    send_pkt(pkt, 48, "IPIP basic")
until true

-- A2: IPIP with TTL=1 on outer (should be decremented to 0 → drop)
repeat
    local pkt = memory.alloc(256)
    write_ipv4_hdr(pkt, 0, 4, 0, 1, 127,0,0,1, 127,0,0,1)
    write_ipv4_hdr(pkt, 20, 17, 28, 64, 127,0,0,1, 127,0,0,1)
    for i = 40, 47 do safe_wb(pkt + i, 0xBB) end
    send_pkt(pkt, 48, "IPIP TTL=1 outer")
until true

-- A3: IPIP with TTL=0 on inner
repeat
    local pkt = memory.alloc(256)
    write_ipv4_hdr(pkt, 0, 4, 0, 64, 127,0,0,1, 127,0,0,1)
    write_ipv4_hdr(pkt, 20, 17, 28, 0, 127,0,0,1, 127,0,0,1)
    for i = 40, 47 do safe_wb(pkt + i, 0xCC) end
    send_pkt(pkt, 48, "IPIP TTL=0 inner")
until true

-- A4: IPIP with mismatched inner total_len (claims 200 bytes, only 8 present)
repeat
    local pkt = memory.alloc(256)
    write_ipv4_hdr(pkt, 0, 4, 0, 64, 127,0,0,1, 127,0,0,1)
    write_ipv4_hdr(pkt, 20, 17, 200, 64, 127,0,0,1, 127,0,0,1)
    for i = 40, 47 do safe_wb(pkt + i, 0xDD) end
    send_pkt(pkt, 48, "IPIP inner len mismatch")
until true

-- A5: IPIP recursive — IPv4-in-IPv4-in-IPv4 (3 deep)
repeat
    local pkt = memory.alloc(256)
    -- Outer: proto 4, wrapping another IPIP
    write_ipv4_hdr(pkt, 0, 4, 0, 64, 127,0,0,1, 127,0,0,1)
    -- Middle: proto 4, wrapping inner
    write_ipv4_hdr(pkt, 20, 4, 0, 64, 127,0,0,1, 127,0,0,1)
    -- Inner: proto 17 (UDP)
    write_ipv4_hdr(pkt, 40, 17, 28, 64, 127,0,0,1, 127,0,0,1)
    for i = 60, 67 do safe_wb(pkt + i, 0xEE) end
    send_pkt(pkt, 68, "IPIP 3-deep recursive")
until true

-- A6: IPIP 5-deep recursive
repeat
    local pkt = memory.alloc(256)
    for depth = 0, 3 do
        write_ipv4_hdr(pkt, depth * 20, 4, 0, 64, 127,0,0,1, 127,0,0,1)
    end
    write_ipv4_hdr(pkt, 80, 17, 28, 64, 127,0,0,1, 127,0,0,1)
    for i = 100, 107 do safe_wb(pkt + i, 0xFF) end
    send_pkt(pkt, 108, "IPIP 5-deep recursive")
until true

-- A7: IPIP with inner IHL > 5 (IP options in inner packet)
repeat
    local pkt = memory.alloc(256)
    write_ipv4_hdr(pkt, 0, 4, 0, 64, 127,0,0,1, 127,0,0,1)
    -- Inner with IHL=15 (max, 60-byte header, 40 bytes of options)
    safe_wb(pkt + 20, 0x4F)  -- ver=4, ihl=15
    safe_wb(pkt + 21, 0)
    safe_wb(pkt + 22, 0)     -- total_len (kernel fills)
    safe_wb(pkt + 23, 0)
    safe_wb(pkt + 28, 64)    -- ttl
    safe_wb(pkt + 29, 17)    -- proto=UDP
    safe_wb(pkt + 32, 127)   -- src
    safe_wb(pkt + 33, 0)
    safe_wb(pkt + 34, 0)
    safe_wb(pkt + 35, 1)
    safe_wb(pkt + 36, 127)   -- dst
    safe_wb(pkt + 37, 0)
    safe_wb(pkt + 38, 0)
    safe_wb(pkt + 39, 1)
    -- 40 bytes of NOP options (type 1)
    for i = 40, 79 do safe_wb(pkt + i, 1) end
    -- 8 bytes payload
    for i = 80, 87 do safe_wb(pkt + i, 0xAB) end
    send_pkt(pkt, 88, "IPIP inner IHL=15")
until true

-- A8: IPIP with different src/dst in inner vs outer
repeat
    local pkt = memory.alloc(256)
    write_ipv4_hdr(pkt, 0, 4, 0, 64, 127,0,0,1, 127,0,0,1)
    -- Inner claims to be from 10.0.0.1 to 10.0.0.2 (spoofed)
    write_ipv4_hdr(pkt, 20, 17, 28, 64, 10,0,0,1, 10,0,0,2)
    for i = 40, 47 do safe_wb(pkt + i, 0xCD) end
    send_pkt(pkt, 48, "IPIP spoofed inner addrs")
until true

print("")
print("--- Section B: IPv6-in-IPv4 (Proto 41) Tunneling ---")
print("")

-- B1: Basic 6in4 — outer IPv4 wrapping inner IPv6
repeat
    local pkt = memory.alloc(256)
    -- Outer: proto 41, total = 20 + 40 + 8 = 68
    write_ipv4_hdr(pkt, 0, 41, 0, 64, 127,0,0,1, 127,0,0,1)
    -- Inner IPv6: next=59 (no next), payload=8
    write_ipv6_hdr(pkt, 20, 59, 8, 64, 1, 1)
    for i = 60, 67 do safe_wb(pkt + i, 0x11) end

-- B2: 6in4 with hop_limit=0 on inner

-- B3: 6in4 with TTL=1 on outer

-- B4: 6in4 with inner payload length mismatch
repeat
    local pkt = memory.alloc(256)

    for i = 60, 67 do safe_wb(pkt + i, 0x44) end

-- B5: 6in4 with inner fragment header (fragmented IPv6 inside IPv4)
repeat
    local pkt = memory.alloc(256)
    write_ipv4_hdr(pkt, 0, 41, 0, 64, 127,0,0,1, 127,0,0,1)
    -- Inner IPv6 with fragment header
    write_ipv6_hdr(pkt, 20, 44, 16, 64, 1, 1) -- next=44 (Fragment)
    -- Fragment header (8 bytes)
    safe_wb(pkt + 60, 59)   -- next = No Next Header
    safe_wb(pkt + 61, 0)    -- reserved
    safe_wb(pkt + 62, 0)    -- offset=0
    safe_wb(pkt + 63, 0)    -- MF=0 (atomic fragment)
    safe_wd(pkt + 64, 0x12345678) -- identification
    -- 8 bytes payload
    for i = 68, 75 do safe_wb(pkt + i, 0x55) end
    send_pkt(pkt, 76, "6in4 inner frag atomic")
until true

-- B6: 6in4 with inner extension header chain
repeat
    local pkt = memory.alloc(256)
    write_ipv4_hdr(pkt, 0, 41, 0, 64, 127,0,0,1, 127,0,0,1)
    -- IPv6 → HBH → Routing → Destination → No Next Header
    write_ipv6_hdr(pkt, 20, 0, 32, 64, 1, 1) -- next=0 (HBH)
    -- HBH (8 bytes): next=43 (Routing)
    safe_wb(pkt + 60, 43)    -- next hdr
    safe_wb(pkt + 61, 0)     -- len=0 (8 bytes total)
    for i = 62, 67 do safe_wb(pkt + i, 0) end  -- padding
    -- Routing (8 bytes): next=60 (Destination)
    safe_wb(pkt + 68, 60)    -- next hdr
    safe_wb(pkt + 69, 0)     -- len=0
    safe_wb(pkt + 70, 0)     -- routing type
    safe_wb(pkt + 71, 0)     -- segments left
    for i = 72, 75 do safe_wb(pkt + i, 0) end
    -- Destination (8 bytes): next=59 (No Next)
    safe_wb(pkt + 76, 59)    -- next hdr
    safe_wb(pkt + 77, 0)     -- len=0
    for i = 78, 83 do safe_wb(pkt + i, 0) end
    -- 8 bytes payload
    for i = 84, 91 do safe_wb(pkt + i, 0x66) end
    send_pkt(pkt, 92, "6in4 inner ext hdr chain")
until true

-- B7: 6in4 recursive — IPv6-in-IPv4-in-IPv6-in-IPv4
repeat
    local pkt = memory.alloc(256)
    -- Outer IPv4: proto 41
    write_ipv4_hdr(pkt, 0, 41, 0, 64, 127,0,0,1, 127,0,0,1)
    -- Inner IPv6: next=4 (IPv4 tunneled inside IPv6... unusual)
    write_ipv6_hdr(pkt, 20, 4, 28, 64, 1, 1)
    -- Innermost IPv4: proto 17 (UDP)
    write_ipv4_hdr(pkt, 60, 17, 28, 64, 127,0,0,1, 127,0,0,1)
    for i = 80, 87 do safe_wb(pkt + i, 0x77) end
    send_pkt(pkt, 88, "6in4 recursive (IPv4-in-IPv6-in-IPv4)")
until true

-- B8: 6in4 with zero payload length in inner IPv6
repeat

-- B9: 6in4 with inner IPv6 version != 6

-- B10: 6in4 inner version=15

print("")
print("--- Section C: GRE Tunnel Decapsulation ---")

-- C1: GRE with IPv4 payload (standard tunnel)
repeat
    local pkt = memory.alloc(256)

    -- GRE header: flags=0, protocol=0x0800 (IPv4)
    local gre_len = write_gre_hdr(pkt, 20, 0x0800, 0)
    -- Inner IPv4
    write_ipv4_hdr(pkt, 20 + gre_len, 17, 28, 64, 127,0,0,1, 127,0,0,1)
    for i = 20 + gre_len + 20, 20 + gre_len + 27 do safe_wb(pkt + i, 0xA1) end

-- C2: GRE with IPv6 payload (0x86DD)

-- C3: GRE with key flag set

-- C4: GRE with sequence flag

    write_ipv4_hdr(pkt, 20 + gre_len, 17, 28, 64, 127,0,0,1, 127,0,0,1)

    local gre_len = write_gre_hdr(pkt, 20, 0x0800, 0x3000, 0xCAFEBABE, 100)
    write_ipv4_hdr(pkt, 20 + gre_len, 17, 28, 64, 127,0,0,1, 127,0,0,1)

-- C6: GRE recursive — GRE-in-GRE-in-GRE (3 levels)
repeat
    local pkt = memory.alloc(256)
    write_ipv4_hdr(pkt, 0, 47, 0, 64, 127,0,0,1, 127,0,0,1)
    -- Level 1 GRE: payload = GRE (proto 47 = 0x002F)
    local off = 20
    local g1 = write_gre_hdr(pkt, off, 0x002F, 0)
    off = off + g1
    -- Level 2 GRE: payload = GRE
    local g2 = write_gre_hdr(pkt, off, 0x002F, 0)
    off = off + g2
    -- Level 3 GRE: payload = IPv4
    local g3 = write_gre_hdr(pkt, off, 0x0800, 0)
    off = off + g3
    -- Inner IPv4
    write_ipv4_hdr(pkt, off, 17, 28, 64, 127,0,0,1, 127,0,0,1)
    off = off + 20
    for i = off, off + 7 do safe_wb(pkt + i, 0xF6) end
    send_pkt(pkt, off + 8, "GRE 3-deep recursive")
until true

-- C7: GRE with unknown/reserved protocol type

    local gre_len = write_gre_hdr(pkt, 20, 0xFFFF, 0) -- unknown ethertype
    for i = 20 + gre_len, 20 + gre_len + 15 do safe_wb(pkt + i, 0xAB) end
    send_pkt(pkt, 20 + gre_len + 16, "GRE unknown proto 0xFFFF")
until true

-- C8: GRE with protocol=0x0000 (should be dropped or passed to raw)

-- C9: GRE with Transparent Ethernet Bridging (0x6558)
repeat
    local pkt = memory.alloc(256)
    write_ipv4_hdr(pkt, 0, 47, 0, 64, 127,0,0,1, 127,0,0,1)
    local gre_len = write_gre_hdr(pkt, 20, 0x6558, 0)
    -- Fake ethernet frame header (14 bytes)
    for i = 20 + gre_len, 20 + gre_len + 5 do safe_wb(pkt + i, 0xFF) end -- dst MAC broadcast
    for i = 20 + gre_len + 6, 20 + gre_len + 11 do safe_wb(pkt + i, 0x01) end -- src MAC
    safe_wb(pkt + 20 + gre_len + 12, 0x08) -- ethertype = IPv4
    safe_wb(pkt + 20 + gre_len + 13, 0x00)
    -- minimal inner
    for i = 20 + gre_len + 14, 20 + gre_len + 21 do safe_wb(pkt + i, 0xEF) end
    send_pkt(pkt, 20 + gre_len + 22, "GRE TEB (ethernet bridging)")
until true

    safe_wb(pkt + 20, 0)
    safe_wb(pkt + 21, 0)
    send_pkt(pkt, 22, "GRE truncated 2B")
until true

-- D1: 10-deep IPIP nesting
repeat
    local pkt = memory.alloc(512)
    local depth = 10
    for d = 0, depth - 2 do
        write_ipv4_hdr(pkt, d * 20, 4, 0, 64, 127,0,0,1, 127,0,0,1)
    end
    -- Innermost: UDP
    local inner_off = (depth - 1) * 20
    write_ipv4_hdr(pkt, inner_off, 17, 28, 64, 127,0,0,1, 127,0,0,1)
    for i = inner_off + 20, inner_off + 27 do safe_wb(pkt + i, 0xD1) end
    send_pkt(pkt, inner_off + 28, "IPIP 10-deep nesting")
until true

-- D2: Alternating 4in4 and 6in4 nesting (4 levels)
repeat
    local pkt = memory.alloc(512)
    -- L1: IPv4 proto=41 (6in4)
    write_ipv4_hdr(pkt, 0, 41, 0, 64, 127,0,0,1, 127,0,0,1)
    -- L2: IPv6 next=4 (4in6)
    write_ipv6_hdr(pkt, 20, 4, 68, 64, 1, 1)
    -- L3: IPv4 proto=41 (6in4 again)
    write_ipv4_hdr(pkt, 60, 41, 0, 64, 127,0,0,1, 127,0,0,1)
    -- L4: IPv6 next=59
    write_ipv6_hdr(pkt, 80, 59, 8, 64, 1, 1)
    for i = 120, 127 do safe_wb(pkt + i, 0xD2) end
    send_pkt(pkt, 128, "Alternating 4in6/6in4 4-deep")
until true

-- D3: GRE wrapping IPIP wrapping 6in4
repeat
    local pkt = memory.alloc(512)
    -- Outer: GRE
    write_ipv4_hdr(pkt, 0, 47, 0, 64, 127,0,0,1, 127,0,0,1)
    local gre_len = write_gre_hdr(pkt, 20, 0x0800, 0)
    local off = 20 + gre_len
    -- IPIP layer
    write_ipv4_hdr(pkt, off, 4, 0, 64, 127,0,0,1, 127,0,0,1)
    off = off + 20
    -- Inner IPIP → 6in4
    write_ipv4_hdr(pkt, off, 41, 0, 64, 127,0,0,1, 127,0,0,1)
    off = off + 20
    -- Innermost IPv6
    write_ipv6_hdr(pkt, off, 59, 8, 64, 1, 1)
    off = off + 40
    for i = off, off + 7 do safe_wb(pkt + i, 0xD3) end
    send_pkt(pkt, off + 8, "GRE->IPIP->6in4 3-protocol nest")
until true

print("")
print("--- Section E: Tunnel + Fragment Interaction ---")
print("")

-- E1: Fragmented outer containing complete tunnel packet
-- (outer IPv4 is fragmented, inner is a complete IPv6 packet)
repeat
    local ok2, rfd2 = pcall(function()
        return sc_socket(uint64(AF_INET), uint64(SOCK_RAW), uint64(41))
    end)
    if not ok2 or to_num(rfd2) < 0 then
        print("  [E1] SKIP: raw socket for proto 41 failed")
        break
    end
    rfd2 = to_num(rfd2)
    setsockopt_int(rfd2, 0, IP_HDRINCL, 1)

    -- Build the full packet content: IPv4 + inner IPv6 + payload
    local full_pkt = memory.alloc(256)

    -- Fragment 1: IPv4 header + first 24 bytes of inner content
    -- IP flags: MF=1, offset=0
    write_ipv4_hdr(full_pkt, 0, 41, 0, 64, 127,0,0,1, 127,0,0,1)
    safe_wb(full_pkt + 6, 0x20)  -- MF flag
    safe_wb(full_pkt + 7, 0)     -- offset = 0
    -- First part of IPv6 header
    write_ipv6_hdr(full_pkt, 20, 59, 8, 64, 1, 1)
    -- Only send first 44 bytes of data (header + 24 bytes of IPv6 hdr)
    local ok3, r3 = pcall(function()
        return sc_sendto(uint64(rfd2), uint64(full_pkt), uint64(44),
            uint64(0), uint64(dest), uint64(16))
    end)
    tests = tests + 1
    print(string.format("  [%d] Frag tunnel frag1: ret=%s",
        tests, ok3 and tostring(to_num(r3)) or "err"))
    if ok3 and to_num(r3) >= 0 then sent_ok = sent_ok + 1 end

    -- Fragment 2: remaining bytes, MF=0, offset=24/8=3
    local frag2 = memory.alloc(64)
    write_ipv4_hdr(frag2, 0, 41, 0, 64, 127,0,0,1, 127,0,0,1)
    safe_wb(frag2 + 6, 0x00)  -- MF=0
    safe_wb(frag2 + 7, 3)     -- offset=3 (3*8=24 bytes)
    -- Rest of IPv6 header + payload
    for i = 20, 43 do safe_wb(frag2 + i, 0xE1) end
    local ok4, r4 = pcall(function()
        return sc_sendto(uint64(rfd2), uint64(frag2), uint64(44),
            uint64(0), uint64(dest), uint64(16))
    end)
    tests = tests + 1
    print(string.format("  [%d] Frag tunnel frag2: ret=%s",
        tests, ok4 and tostring(to_num(r4)) or "err"))
    if ok4 and to_num(r4) >= 0 then sent_ok = sent_ok + 1 end

    close_fd(rfd2)
    print("  [E1] SURVIVED")
until true

-- E2: Tunnel packet containing fragmented inner IPv6
repeat
    local pkt = memory.alloc(256)
    -- Outer IPv4 → proto 41
    write_ipv4_hdr(pkt, 0, 41, 0, 64, 127,0,0,1, 127,0,0,1)
    -- Inner IPv6 with fragment header — first fragment, MF=1
    write_ipv6_hdr(pkt, 20, 44, 24, 64, 1, 1) -- next=Fragment
    -- Fragment header
    safe_wb(pkt + 60, 17)   -- next = UDP
    safe_wb(pkt + 61, 0)    -- reserved
    safe_wb(pkt + 62, 0)    -- offset=0
    safe_wb(pkt + 63, 1)    -- MF=1
    safe_wd(pkt + 64, 0xAAAABBBB) -- id
    -- 16 bytes of payload
    for i = 68, 83 do safe_wb(pkt + i, 0xE2) end
    send_pkt(pkt, 84, "Tunnel with inner IPv6 frag (MF=1)")
until true

-- F1: 6in4 with inner IPv6 jumbogram (payload_len=0, HBH with jumbo option)
repeat
    local pkt = memory.alloc(256)
    write_ipv4_hdr(pkt, 0, 41, 0, 64, 127,0,0,1, 127,0,0,1)
    -- IPv6 with payload_len=0 and HBH

    -- HBH: jumbo payload option

    safe_wb(pkt + 61, 0)    -- len=0 (8 bytes)
    safe_wb(pkt + 62, 0xC2) -- option type 0xC2 = Jumbo Payload
    safe_wb(pkt + 63, 4)    -- option len = 4
    -- Jumbo length = 8 (just our tiny payload)
    safe_wb(pkt + 64, 0)
    safe_wb(pkt + 65, 0)
    safe_wb(pkt + 66, 0)

-- F4: 6in4 where inner is actually IPv4 (version confusion)

    -- Proto 41 should contain IPv6, but we put IPv4

    for i = 40, 47 do safe_wb(pkt + i, 0xF4) end
```

## probes/phase12_kernel_analysis/51a_sony_syscall_survey.lua

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: MODERATE
-- PROBE 51a: Sony custom syscall survey (532-676)
--
-- Context: Kernel dump analysis of FW 13.60 revealed 116 Sony-custom syscalls
-- in the 532-676 range. Only 557, 593, and 620 have been tested on FW 14.10.
-- This probe systematically calls each one with safe args (zeros or small buffers)
-- to determine which are accessible from our sandbox and what they return.
-- Grouped by kernel code proximity to identify subsystems.

print("=== PROBE 51a: SONY SYSCALL SURVEY (532-676) ===")
print("")

local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_rq(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end
    return nil
end
local function safe_wd(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_dword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function safe_wq(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_qword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function get_hi_lo(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then return val.h, val.l end
    return 0, to_num(val)
end

-- Allocate shared buffers for syscall arguments
local buf1 = memory.alloc(0x1000)
local buf2 = memory.alloc(0x1000)
local buf3 = memory.alloc(0x1000)

-- Zero the buffers
for i = 0, 0xFF0, 4 do
    safe_wd(buf1 + i, 0)
    safe_wd(buf2 + i, 0)
    safe_wd(buf3 + i, 0)
end

-- Get PID for reference
local sc_getpid = make_syscall(20)
local pid = to_num(pcall(function() return sc_getpid() end) and sc_getpid() or 0)
print("PID: " .. pid)
print("")

-- Sony syscalls from 13.60 kernel dump analysis, grouped by subsystem
-- Format: {syscall_num, narg, group_name}
local sony_syscalls = {
    -- Dynamic linker group (TEXT+0x340000)
    {591, 3, "dynlib"}, {592, 3, "dynlib"}, {594, 4, "dynlib"},
    {595, 3, "dynlib"}, {596, 0, "dynlib"}, {598, 2, "dynlib"},
    {599, 0, "dynlib"}, {608, 3, "dynlib"}, {612, 1, "dynlib"},
    {649, 3, "dynlib"}, {656, 2, "dynlib"}, {659, 3, "dynlib"},
    {660, 2, "dynlib"}, {672, 3, "dynlib"},

    -- VM/memory group (TEXT+0xab0000)
    {547, 2, "vm"}, {548, 5, "vm"}, {559, 1, "vm"},
    {572, 4, "vm"}, {588, 3, "vm"}, {607, 2, "vm"},
    {613, 3, "vm"}, {615, 3, "vm"}, {618, 3, "vm"},
    {624, 0, "vm"}, {628, 6, "vm"}, {637, 2, "vm"},
    {642, 4, "vm"}, {646, 1, "vm"}, {647, 1, "vm"},
    {671, 4, "vm"}, {674, 5, "vm"},

    -- Sony subsystem C (TEXT+0xc10000, 549-556)
    {549, 4, "sysC"}, {550, 1, "sysC"}, {551, 1, "sysC"},
    {552, 1, "sysC"}, {553, 3, "sysC"}, {554, 2, "sysC"},
    {555, 2, "sysC"}, {556, 3, "sysC"},

    -- Sony subsystem D (TEXT+0xba0000-bb0000, 538-546)
    {538, 3, "sysD"}, {539, 1, "sysD"}, {540, 1, "sysD"},
    {541, 1, "sysD"}, {542, 5, "sysD"}, {543, 4, "sysD"},
    {544, 2, "sysD"}, {545, 2, "sysD"}, {546, 3, "sysD"},

    -- Process/thread group (TEXT+0x600000, 563-567 + 625-626)
    {563, 1, "proc"}, {564, 1, "proc"}, {565, 3, "proc"},
    {566, 3, "proc"}, {567, 3, "proc"}, {625, 4, "proc"},
    {626, 5, "proc"},

    -- Device/IPC group (TEXT+0x3b0000, 661-670)
    {661, 4, "dev"}, {662, 3, "dev"}, {663, 5, "dev"},
    {664, 3, "dev"}, {665, 2, "dev"}, {666, 3, "dev"},
    {668, 2, "dev"}, {669, 5, "dev"}, {670, 4, "dev"},

    -- Misc groups
    {532, 5, "misc"}, {533, 3, "misc"}, {534, 2, "misc"},
    {535, 4, "io"}, {536, 3, "io"}, {558, 2, "misc"},
    {560, 1, "io"}, {585, 0, "fs"}, {586, 1, "misc"},
    {587, 2, "io"}, {600, 1, "evt"}, {601, 3, "evt"},
    {602, 3, "evt"}, {603, 2, "fd"}, {604, 5, "io"},
    {605, 1, "evt"}, {606, 0, "evt"}, {610, 1, "misc"},
    {611, 3, "evt"}, {616, 2, "thr"}, {617, 1, "misc"},
    {622, 6, "vm"}, {623, 1, "misc"}, {627, 2, "io"},
    {629, 4, "misc"}, {630, 1, "misc"}, {632, 1, "thr"},
    {633, 1, "thr"}, {634, 2, "thr"}, {636, 2, "misc"},
    {638, 4, "misc"}, {639, 5, "misc"}, {640, 8, "misc"},
    {641, 2, "io"}, {643, 1, "evt"}, {648, 1, "misc"},
    {652, 2, "proc"}, {653, 1, "misc"}, {654, 5, "misc"},
    {655, 3, "misc"}, {657, 4, "misc"}, {658, 1, "fs"},
    {667, 2, "io"}, {673, 4, "misc"}, {675, 2, "misc"},
    {676, 0, "misc"},
}

print("Testing " .. #sony_syscalls .. " Sony syscalls via make_syscall...")
print("")

local accessible = {}
local killed = {}
local errors = {}

for idx, entry in ipairs(sony_syscalls) do
    local num = entry[1]
    local narg = entry[2]
    local group = entry[3]

    local sc = make_syscall(num)
    local ok, ret

    if narg == 0 then
        ok, ret = pcall(function() return sc() end)
    elseif narg == 1 then
        ok, ret = pcall(function() return sc(uint64(0)) end)
    elseif narg == 2 then
        ok, ret = pcall(function() return sc(uint64(0), uint64(0)) end)
    elseif narg == 3 then
        ok, ret = pcall(function() return sc(uint64(0), uint64(0), uint64(0)) end)
    elseif narg == 4 then
        ok, ret = pcall(function() return sc(uint64(buf1), uint64(buf2), uint64(0), uint64(0)) end)
    elseif narg == 5 then
        ok, ret = pcall(function() return sc(uint64(buf1), uint64(buf2), uint64(buf3), uint64(0), uint64(0)) end)
    elseif narg == 6 then
        ok, ret = pcall(function() return sc(uint64(buf1), uint64(buf2), uint64(buf3), uint64(0), uint64(0), uint64(0)) end)
    elseif narg == 8 then
        ok, ret = pcall(function() return sc(uint64(buf1), uint64(buf2), uint64(buf3), uint64(0), uint64(0), uint64(0)) end)
    end

    if ok then
        local rv = to_num(ret)
        local rh, rl = get_hi_lo(ret)
        local tag = ""
        if rv == 0 then tag = " [SUCCESS]"
        elseif rv == -1 or rv == 4294967295 then tag = " [EPERM/ENOSYS?]"
        elseif rh >= 0xFFFF8000 then tag = " [KERNEL PTR!!!]"
        end

        -- Check if buffer was modified (for narg >= 4)
        local buf_mod = ""
        if narg >= 4 then
            local v1 = safe_rd(buf1)
            local v2 = safe_rd(buf2)
            if v1 ~= 0 or v2 ~= 0 then
                buf_mod = string.format(" buf1[0]=%08X buf2[0]=%08X", v1 or 0, v2 or 0)
                -- Re-zero for next test
                safe_wd(buf1, 0)
                safe_wd(buf2, 0)
            end
        end

        if rv ~= -1 and rv ~= 4294967295 then
            table.insert(accessible, {num, rv, rh, rl, group, buf_mod})
        end

        print(string.format("  [%s] %d: ret=%d (0x%08X_%08X)%s%s",
            group, num, rv, rh, rl, tag, buf_mod))
    else
        local err = tostring(ret)
        if err:find("killed") or err:find("signal") then
            table.insert(killed, {num, err, group})
            print(string.format("  [%s] %d: KILLED - %s", group, num, err))
        else
            table.insert(errors, {num, err, group})
            print(string.format("  [%s] %d: ERROR - %s", group, num, err))
        end
    end
end

print("")
print("=== SUMMARY ===")
print(string.format("Total tested: %d", #sony_syscalls))
print(string.format("Accessible (ret != -1): %d", #accessible))
print(string.format("Killed: %d", #killed))
print(string.format("Errors: %d", #errors))

if #accessible > 0 then
    print("")
    print("=== ACCESSIBLE SYSCALLS (non-error returns) ===")
    for _, entry in ipairs(accessible) do
        local num, rv, rh, rl, group, buf_mod = entry[1], entry[2], entry[3], entry[4], entry[5], entry[6]
        local tag = ""
        if rh >= 0xFFFF8000 then tag = " <<< KERNEL POINTER <<<" end
        print(string.format("  [%s] %d: ret=0x%08X_%08X%s%s", group, num, rh, rl, buf_mod, tag))
    end
end

if #killed > 0 then
    print("")
    print("=== SANDBOX-KILLED SYSCALLS ===")
    for _, entry in ipairs(killed) do
        print(string.format("  [%s] %d: %s", entry[3], entry[1], entry[2]))
    end
end

print("")
print("=== PROBE 51a COMPLETE ===")
```

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: MODERATE
-- PROBE 51b: Deep testing of accessible Sony syscalls
--
-- Context: Run AFTER 51a to identify which Sony syscalls are accessible.
-- This probe does deeper testing of promising ones:
-- - Passes output buffers and checks for kernel pointer leaks
-- - Varies argument values to understand parameter semantics
-- - Tests boundary conditions that might trigger bugs
--
-- IMPORTANT: Edit the "targets" table below based on 51a results
-- before sending this probe.

print("=== PROBE 51b: DEEP SONY SYSCALL TESTING ===")
print("")

local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_rq(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end
    return nil
end
local function safe_wd(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_dword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function safe_wq(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_qword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function get_hi_lo(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then return val.h, val.l end
    return 0, to_num(val)
end

local function hexdump(addr, len)
    local parts = {}
    for i = 0, len - 4, 4 do
        local v = safe_rd(addr + i)
        if v then
            table.insert(parts, string.format("%08X", v))
        else
            table.insert(parts, "????????")
        end
    end
    return table.concat(parts, " ")
end

local function scan_for_kptrs(addr, len)
    local found = {}
    for i = 0, len - 8, 8 do
        local val = safe_rq(addr + i)
        if val then
            local h, l = get_hi_lo(val)
            if h >= 0xFFFF8000 and h < 0xFFFFFFFF then
                table.insert(found, {i, h, l})
            end
        end
    end
    return found
end

-- Allocate large output buffers
local outbuf = memory.alloc(0x4000)
local outbuf2 = memory.alloc(0x4000)
local outbuf3 = memory.alloc(0x4000)
local lenp = memory.alloc(8)

print("PID: " .. pid)

-- ============================================================

print("")
print("--- SECTION A: Dynlib group (near 593/dynlib_get_info) ---")

-- 596: narg=0 - just call it

if ok then
    local h, l = get_hi_lo(ret)
    print(string.format("  596(): ret=0x%08X_%08X", h, l))
end

-- 599: narg=0
local sc599 = make_syscall(599)
ok, ret = pcall(function() return sc599() end)
if ok then
    local h, l = get_hi_lo(ret)
    print(string.format("  599(): ret=0x%08X_%08X", h, l))
end

-- 591: narg=3 - likely dynlib_load_prx or similar
-- Try: (handle, buf, buflen)
for i = 0, 0x200, 4 do safe_wd(outbuf + i, 0) end
safe_wd(lenp, 0x200)
local sc591 = make_syscall(591)
ok, ret = pcall(function() return sc591(uint64(0), uint64(outbuf), uint64(lenp)) end)
if ok then
    local h, l = get_hi_lo(ret)

                print(string.format("      +%03X: 0x%08X_%08X", kp[1], kp[2], kp[3]))
            end
```

## probes/phase12_kernel_analysis/51c_sony_survey_part2.lua

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: MODERATE
-- PROBE 51c: Sony syscall survey part 2 (untested remainder from 51a)
--
-- Context: 51a was cut short after ~55 syscalls (through the proc group).
-- This probe covers the remaining untested Sony syscalls: the device/IPC
-- group (661-670) and all misc/io/evt/thr/fs syscalls that 51a didn't reach.
-- Also re-tests a few from the end of the proc group that may not have run.

print("=== PROBE 51c: SONY SYSCALL SURVEY PART 2 ===")
print("")

local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_rq(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end
    return nil
end
local function safe_wd(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_dword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function safe_wq(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_qword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function get_hi_lo(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then return val.h, val.l end
    return 0, to_num(val)
end

local buf1 = memory.alloc(0x1000)
local buf2 = memory.alloc(0x1000)
local buf3 = memory.alloc(0x1000)

for i = 0, 0xFF0, 4 do
    safe_wd(buf1 + i, 0)
    safe_wd(buf2 + i, 0)
    safe_wd(buf3 + i, 0)
end

local sc_getpid = make_syscall(20)
local pid = to_num(pcall(function() return sc_getpid() end) and sc_getpid() or 0)
print("PID: " .. pid)
print("")

-- Syscalls that 51a didn't reach. REORDERED: safe misc/io/evt first,
-- dev group LAST (661 sandbox-killed the process on first run).
-- Print before each call so we see exactly which one kills us.
local remaining = {
    -- Misc/io/evt/thr/fs first (most likely to survive)
    {532, 5, "misc"}, {533, 3, "misc"}, {534, 2, "misc"},
    {535, 4, "io"}, {536, 3, "io"}, {558, 2, "misc"},
    {560, 1, "io"}, {586, 1, "misc"},
    {587, 2, "io"}, {600, 1, "evt"}, {601, 3, "evt"},
    {602, 3, "evt"}, {603, 2, "fd"}, {604, 5, "io"},
    {605, 1, "evt"}, {610, 1, "misc"},
    {611, 3, "evt"}, {616, 2, "thr"}, {617, 1, "misc"},
    {622, 6, "vm"}, {623, 1, "misc"}, {627, 2, "io"},
    {629, 4, "misc"}, {630, 1, "misc"}, {632, 1, "thr"},
    {633, 1, "thr"}, {634, 2, "thr"}, {636, 2, "misc"},
    {638, 4, "misc"}, {639, 5, "misc"}, {640, 8, "misc"},
    {641, 2, "io"}, {648, 1, "misc"},
    {652, 2, "proc"}, {653, 1, "misc"}, {654, 5, "misc"},
    {655, 3, "misc"}, {657, 4, "misc"}, {658, 1, "fs"},
    {667, 2, "io"}, {673, 4, "misc"}, {675, 2, "misc"},
    {676, 0, "misc"},

    -- Re-test end of proc group
    {625, 4, "proc"}, {626, 5, "proc"},

    -- Device/IPC group LAST (661 killed process on first run)
    {661, 4, "dev"}, {662, 3, "dev"}, {663, 5, "dev"},
    {664, 3, "dev"}, {665, 2, "dev"}, {666, 3, "dev"},
    {668, 2, "dev"}, {669, 5, "dev"}, {670, 4, "dev"},
}

print("Testing " .. #remaining .. " Sony syscalls...")
print("")

local accessible = {}
local killed = {}
local errors = {}

for idx, entry in ipairs(remaining) do
    local num = entry[1]
    local narg = entry[2]
    local group = entry[3]

    local sc = make_syscall(num)
    local ok, ret

    -- Print BEFORE call so we see which one kills the process
    io.write(string.format("  [%s] %d (%d args)... ", group, num, narg))
    io.flush()

    -- Zero buffers between tests
    if narg >= 4 then
        for i = 0, 0x100, 4 do
            safe_wd(buf1 + i, 0)
            safe_wd(buf2 + i, 0)
        end
    end

    if narg == 0 then
        ok, ret = pcall(function() return sc() end)
    elseif narg == 1 then
        ok, ret = pcall(function() return sc(uint64(0)) end)
    elseif narg == 2 then
        ok, ret = pcall(function() return sc(uint64(0), uint64(0)) end)
    elseif narg == 3 then
        ok, ret = pcall(function() return sc(uint64(0), uint64(0), uint64(0)) end)
    elseif narg == 4 then
        ok, ret = pcall(function() return sc(uint64(buf1), uint64(buf2), uint64(0), uint64(0)) end)
    elseif narg == 5 then
        ok, ret = pcall(function() return sc(uint64(buf1), uint64(buf2), uint64(buf3), uint64(0), uint64(0)) end)
    elseif narg == 6 then
        ok, ret = pcall(function() return sc(uint64(buf1), uint64(buf2), uint64(buf3), uint64(0), uint64(0), uint64(0)) end)
    elseif narg == 8 then
        ok, ret = pcall(function() return sc(uint64(buf1), uint64(buf2), uint64(buf3), uint64(0), uint64(0), uint64(0)) end)
    end

    if ok then
        local rv = to_num(ret)
        local rh, rl = get_hi_lo(ret)
        local tag = ""
        if rv == 0 then tag = " [SUCCESS]"
        elseif rv == -1 or rv == 4294967295 then tag = " [DENIED]"
        elseif rh >= 0xFFFF8000 then tag = " [KERNEL PTR!!!]"
        end

        local buf_mod = ""
        if narg >= 4 then
            local v1 = safe_rd(buf1)
            local v2 = safe_rd(buf2)
            if (v1 and v1 ~= 0) or (v2 and v2 ~= 0) then
                buf_mod = string.format(" buf1[0]=%08X buf2[0]=%08X", v1 or 0, v2 or 0)
            end
            -- Scan first 256 bytes of buf1 for kernel pointers
            for i = 0, 248, 8 do
                local val = safe_rq(buf1 + i)
                if val then
                    local kh, kl = get_hi_lo(val)
                    if kh >= 0xFFFF8000 and kh < 0xFFFFFFFF then
                        buf_mod = buf_mod .. string.format(" KPTR@+%02X=%08X_%08X", i, kh, kl)
                    end
                end
            end
        end

        if rv ~= -1 and rv ~= 4294967295 then
            table.insert(accessible, {num, rv, rh, rl, group, buf_mod})
        end

        print(string.format("ret=%d (0x%08X_%08X)%s%s",
            rv, rh, rl, tag, buf_mod))
    else
        local err = tostring(ret)
        if err:find("killed") or err:find("signal") then
            table.insert(killed, {num, err, group})
            print(string.format("KILLED - %s", err))
        else
            table.insert(errors, {num, err, group})
            print(string.format("ERROR - %s", err))
        end
    end
end

print("")
print("=== SUMMARY ===")
print(string.format("Total tested: %d", #remaining))
print(string.format("Accessible (ret != -1): %d", #accessible))
print(string.format("Killed: %d", #killed))
print(string.format("Errors: %d", #errors))

if #accessible > 0 then
    print("")
    print("=== ACCESSIBLE SYSCALLS ===")
    for _, entry in ipairs(accessible) do
        local num, rv, rh, rl, group, buf_mod = entry[1], entry[2], entry[3], entry[4], entry[5], entry[6]
        local tag = ""
        if rh >= 0xFFFF8000 then tag = " <<< KERNEL POINTER <<<" end
        print(string.format("  [%s] %d: ret=0x%08X_%08X%s%s", group, num, rh, rl, buf_mod, tag))
    end
end

if #killed > 0 then
    print("")
    print("=== SANDBOX-KILLED ===")
    for _, entry in ipairs(killed) do
        print(string.format("  [%s] %d: %s", entry[3], entry[1], entry[2]))
    end
end

print("")
print("=== PROBE 51c COMPLETE ===")
```

## probes/phase12_kernel_dump/51a_sony_syscall_survey.lua

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: MODERATE
-- PROBE 51a: Survey all Sony custom syscalls (532-676) via make_syscall
--
-- Context: Kernel dump analysis of FW 13.60 revealed 115 Sony-specific syscalls
-- in the 532-676 range. We've only tested 557, 593, 620 on 14.10.
-- This probe calls each with safe arguments (zeros/small values) to determine:
--   1. Which ones are implemented (vs nosys/ENOSYS=78)
--   2. Which ones are sandbox-killed (instant process termination)
--   3. Which ones return interesting values
--   4. Which ones crash with specific arguments (potential attack surface)

print("=== PROBE 51a: SONY SYSCALL SURVEY (532-676) ===")
print("")

local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function get_hi_lo(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then return val.h, val.l end
    return 0, to_num(val)
end

-- Get PID for reference
local sc_getpid = make_syscall(20)
local pid = to_num(sc_getpid())
print("PID: " .. pid)

-- Allocate a buffer for syscalls that need pointer args
local buf = memory.alloc(0x1000)
for i = 0, 0xFF0, 4 do
    pcall(function() memory.write_dword(buf + i, 0) end)
end

local implemented = {}
local nosys = {}
local killed = {}
local errors = {}

print("")
print("--- PHASE 1: Zero-argument scan (all 145 syscalls) ---")
print("")

for num = 532, 676 do
    local sc = make_syscall(num)
    local ok, ret = pcall(function() return sc() end)

    if not ok then
        print(string.format("[%d] CRASH/KILL: %s", num, tostring(ret)))
        killed[num] = tostring(ret)
    else
        local h, l = get_hi_lo(ret)
        local rval = to_num(ret)

        if rval == 78 or l == 78 then
            nosys[num] = true
        elseif rval == -1 or l == 0xFFFFFFFF then
            -- Error return but implemented
            implemented[num] = {ret = -1, note = "error"}
            print(string.format("[%d] ret=-1 (implemented, needs args)", num))
        elseif rval == 0 then
            implemented[num] = {ret = 0, note = "success_noarg"}
            print(string.format("[%d] ret=0 (SUCCESS with no args!)", num))
        else
            implemented[num] = {ret = rval, h = h, l = l, note = "value"}
            print(string.format("[%d] ret=%d (h=%d l=%d)", num, rval, h, l))
        end
    end
end

print("")
print("--- PHASE 1 SUMMARY ---")
local impl_count = 0
local nosys_count = 0
local kill_count = 0
for _ in pairs(implemented) do impl_count = impl_count + 1 end
for _ in pairs(nosys) do nosys_count = nosys_count + 1 end
for _ in pairs(killed) do kill_count = kill_count + 1 end
print("Implemented: " .. impl_count)
print("Nosys/ENOSYS: " .. nosys_count)
print("Killed/Crashed: " .. kill_count)

-- Phase 2: For implemented syscalls that returned -1, try with buffer argument
print("")
print("--- PHASE 2: Retry error syscalls with buffer arg ---")
print("")

for num = 532, 676 do
    if implemented[num] and implemented[num].ret == -1 then
        local sc = make_syscall(num)

        -- Try with buffer pointer as first arg
        local ok2, ret2 = pcall(function()
            return sc(uint64(buf))
        end)
        if ok2 then
            local h2, l2 = get_hi_lo(ret2)
            local r2 = to_num(ret2)
            if r2 ~= -1 and r2 ~= 78 then
                print(string.format("[%d] with buf arg: ret=%d (h=%d l=%d)", num, r2, h2, l2))
                implemented[num].with_buf = r2
            end
        end

        -- Try with small integer as first arg
        local ok3, ret3 = pcall(function()
            return sc(uint64(1))
        end)
        if ok3 then
            local h3, l3 = get_hi_lo(ret3)
            local r3 = to_num(ret3)
            if r3 ~= -1 and r3 ~= 78 then
                print(string.format("[%d] with arg=1: ret=%d (h=%d l=%d)", num, r3, h3, l3))
                implemented[num].with_one = r3
            end
        end
    end
end

-- Phase 3: For success syscalls, check if return value leaks kernel info
print("")
print("--- PHASE 3: Analyze successful returns for kernel pointers ---")
print("")

for num = 532, 676 do
    if implemented[num] and implemented[num].ret == 0 then
        -- Call again and check all possible return locations
        local sc = make_syscall(num)

        -- Check if buffer was modified
        local pre = {}
        for i = 0, 63, 4 do
            pcall(function() memory.write_dword(buf + i, 0xDEADBEEF) end)
        end

        pcall(function() sc(uint64(buf), uint64(0x40)) end)

        local modified = false
        for i = 0, 63, 4 do
            local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(buf + i) end)
            if ok then
                local v = to_num(val)
                if v ~= 0xDEADBEEF then
                    modified = true
                    print(string.format("[%d] buf+%d modified: 0x%08X", num, i, v))
                end
            end
        end
        if not modified then
            print(string.format("[%d] ret=0, buffer not modified", num))
        end
    end
end

-- Phase 4: Try the known interesting ones from kernel dump with proper args
print("")
print("--- PHASE 4: Targeted tests for interesting syscalls ---")
print("")

-- Syscall 560: tiny wrapper (38B), narg=1 — reads global, compares to arg
print("Testing 560 (tiny wrapper, narg=1):")
for _, testval in ipairs({0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 0xFF, 0xFFFF}) do
    local sc = make_syscall(560)
    local ok, ret = pcall(function() return sc(uint64(testval)) end)
    if ok then
        print(string.format("  560(%d) = %d", testval, to_num(ret)))
    else
        print(string.format("  560(%d) = CRASH: %s", testval, tostring(ret)))
    end
end

-- Syscall 585: tiny no-arg (87B)
print("\nTesting 585 (tiny, narg=0):")
local sc585 = make_syscall(585)
local ok585, ret585 = pcall(function() return sc585() end)
if ok585 then
    local h, l = get_hi_lo(ret585)
    print(string.format("  585() = %d (h=0x%X l=0x%X)", to_num(ret585), h, l))
else
    print("  585() = CRASH: " .. tostring(ret585))
end

-- Syscall 606: tiny no-arg (34B)
print("\nTesting 606 (tiny, narg=0):")
local sc606 = make_syscall(606)
local ok606, ret606 = pcall(function() return sc606() end)
if ok606 then
    local h, l = get_hi_lo(ret606)
    print(string.format("  606() = %d (h=0x%X l=0x%X)", to_num(ret606), h, l))
else
    print("  606() = CRASH: " .. tostring(ret606))
end

-- Syscall 640: 8-byte stub (narg=8) — just a jump
print("\nTesting 640 (jump stub, narg=8):")
local sc640 = make_syscall(640)
local ok640, ret640 = pcall(function()
    return sc640(uint64(0), uint64(0), uint64(0), uint64(0),
                 uint64(0), uint64(0))
end)
if ok640 then
    print(string.format("  640() = %d", to_num(ret640)))
else
    print("  640() = CRASH: " .. tostring(ret640))
end

-- Syscall 622: largest handler (20KB, narg=6)
print("\nTesting 622 (largest, narg=6):")
local sc622 = make_syscall(622)
local ok622, ret622 = pcall(function()
    return sc622(uint64(0), uint64(0), uint64(0), uint64(0), uint64(0), uint64(0))
end)
if ok622 then
    print(string.format("  622(0,0,0,0,0,0) = %d", to_num(ret622)))
else
    print("  622() = CRASH: " .. tostring(ret622))
end

-- Syscall 532: first Sony range (narg=5)
print("\nTesting 532 (narg=5):")
local sc532 = make_syscall(532)
local ok532, ret532 = pcall(function()
    return sc532(uint64(buf), uint64(0x100), uint64(0), uint64(0), uint64(0))
end)
if ok532 then
    print(string.format("  532() = %d", to_num(ret532)))
else
    print("  532() = CRASH: " .. tostring(ret532))
end

print("")
print("=== PROBE 51a COMPLETE ===")
```

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: MODERATE
-- PROBE 51b: Fuzz the dynlib syscall cluster (661-670) identified from kernel dump
--
-- Context: Kernel dump analysis revealed syscalls 661-670 are massive handlers
-- (10-20KB each) in the dynlib code region. These are the most complex Sony
-- custom syscalls and most likely to contain exploitable bugs. We also test
-- syscall 522 (7873B handler near mmap) and 601 (10285B).

print("=== PROBE 51b: DYNLIB CLUSTER FUZZ (661-670, 522, 601, 622) ===")
print("")

local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function get_hi_lo(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then return val.h, val.l end
    return 0, to_num(val)
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_wd(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_dword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end

-- Get PID and module base for context
local sc_getpid = make_syscall(20)
local pid = to_num(sc_getpid())
print("PID: " .. pid)

-- Get eboot base via dynlib_get_info
local info = memory.alloc(0x200)
safe_wd(info, 0x160) -- size field
local sc_info = make_syscall(593)
pcall(function() sc_info(uint64(0), info) end) -- handle 0 = eboot
local eboot_lo = safe_rd(info + 0x108) or 0
local eboot_hi = safe_rd(info + 0x10C) or 0
print(string.format("Eboot base: 0x%X%08X", eboot_hi, eboot_lo))

-- Allocate buffers
local buf1 = memory.alloc(0x4000)
local buf2 = memory.alloc(0x4000)
local buf3 = memory.alloc(0x4000)
local buf4 = memory.alloc(0x4000)
local buf5 = memory.alloc(0x4000)
local buf6 = memory.alloc(0x4000)

-- Zero all buffers
for i = 0, 0x3FF0, 4 do
    pcall(function() memory.write_dword(buf1 + i, 0) end)
    pcall(function() memory.write_dword(buf2 + i, 0) end)
    pcall(function() memory.write_dword(buf3 + i, 0) end)
    pcall(function() memory.write_dword(buf4 + i, 0) end)
    pcall(function() memory.write_dword(buf5 + i, 0) end)
    pcall(function() memory.write_dword(buf6 + i, 0) end)
end

-- Test each syscall with various argument patterns
local targets = {
    {num=661, narg=4, desc="dynlib region, 20384B"},
    {num=662, narg=3, desc="dynlib region, 20368B"},
    {num=663, narg=5, desc="dynlib region, 18080B"},
    {num=664, narg=3, desc="dynlib region, 14560B"},
    {num=665, narg=2, desc="dynlib region, 12832B"},
    {num=666, narg=3, desc="dynlib region, 12816B"},
    {num=668, narg=2, desc="dynlib region, 20400B"},
    {num=669, narg=5, desc="dynlib region, 10288B"},
    {num=670, narg=3, desc="dynlib region"},
    {num=522, narg=6, desc="near mmap, 7873B"},
    {num=601, narg=3, desc="complex op, 10285B"},
    {num=622, narg=6, desc="LARGEST handler, 20795B"},
}

print("")
print("--- PHASE 1: Zero-arg baseline ---")
print("")

for _, t in ipairs(targets) do
    local sc = make_syscall(t.num)
    local ok, ret = pcall(function() return sc() end)
    if ok then
        local h, l = get_hi_lo(ret)
        print(string.format("[%d] (%s) ret=%d (h=0x%X l=0x%X)", t.num, t.desc, to_num(ret), h, l))
    else
        print(string.format("[%d] (%s) CRASH: %s", t.num, t.desc, tostring(ret)))
    end
end

print("")
print("--- PHASE 2: Buffer pointer arguments ---")
print("")

-- Try with buffer pointers as arguments (simulating valid userland pointers)
for _, t in ipairs(targets) do
    local sc = make_syscall(t.num)

    -- Pattern A: first arg = buffer pointer
    local ok, ret = pcall(function()
        if t.narg == 2 then
            return sc(uint64(buf1), uint64(0x1000))
        elseif t.narg == 3 then
            return sc(uint64(buf1), uint64(buf2), uint64(0x1000))
        elseif t.narg == 4 then
            return sc(uint64(buf1), uint64(buf2), uint64(buf3), uint64(0x1000))
        elseif t.narg == 5 then
            return sc(uint64(buf1), uint64(buf2), uint64(buf3), uint64(buf4), uint64(0x1000))
        elseif t.narg == 6 then
            return sc(uint64(buf1), uint64(buf2), uint64(buf3), uint64(buf4), uint64(buf5), uint64(0x1000))
        else
            return sc(uint64(buf1))
        end
    end)
    if ok then
        local h, l = get_hi_lo(ret)
        print(string.format("[%d] buf args: ret=%d (h=0x%X l=0x%X)", t.num, to_num(ret), h, l))
    else
        print(string.format("[%d] buf args: CRASH: %s", t.num, tostring(ret)))
    end
end

print("")
print("--- PHASE 3: Dynlib handle-based arguments ---")
print("")

-- The 661-670 cluster is in the dynlib region. Try with dynlib handles.
-- Handle 0 = eboot, handles 1-38 = loaded modules
for _, handle in ipairs({0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 10, 20}) do
    for _, num in ipairs({661, 662, 663, 664, 665, 666, 668, 669, 670}) do
        local sc = make_syscall(num)
        local narg = 0
        for _, t in ipairs(targets) do
            if t.num == num then narg = t.narg; break end
        end

        local ok, ret = pcall(function()
            if narg == 2 then
                return sc(uint64(handle), uint64(buf1))
            elseif narg == 3 then
                return sc(uint64(handle), uint64(buf1), uint64(0x1000))
            elseif narg == 4 then
                return sc(uint64(handle), uint64(buf1), uint64(buf2), uint64(0x1000))
            elseif narg == 5 then
                return sc(uint64(handle), uint64(buf1), uint64(buf2), uint64(buf3), uint64(0x1000))
            else
                return sc(uint64(handle))
            end
        end)
        if ok then
            local r = to_num(ret)
            if r ~= -1 and r ~= 78 then
                print(string.format("[%d] handle=%d: ret=%d", num, handle, r))
            end
        else
            print(string.format("[%d] handle=%d: CRASH: %s", num, handle, tostring(ret)))
        end
    end
end

-- Check if any buffers were modified by the dynlib syscalls
print("")
print("--- Checking buf1 for kernel data ---")
local found_data = false
for i = 0, 0x100, 4 do
    local v = safe_rd(buf1 + i)
    if v and v ~= 0 then
        found_data = true
        print(string.format("  buf1+%d: 0x%08X", i, v))
    end
end
if not found_data then print("  buf1 unchanged") end

print("")
print("--- PHASE 4: Syscall 522 (near mmap, narg=6) ---")
print("")

-- 522 is near mmap handlers. Try mmap-like arguments.
local sc522 = make_syscall(522)

-- Pattern: (addr, len, prot, flags, fd, offset) like mmap
local mmap_tests = {
    {0, 0x4000, 3, 0x1002, 0xFFFFFFFF, 0, "anon RW"},
    {0, 0x4000, 1, 0x1002, 0xFFFFFFFF, 0, "anon R"},
    {0, 0x4000, 0x33, 0x1002, 0xFFFFFFFF, 0, "anon RW like GPU"},
    {0, 0x10000, 3, 2, 0xFFFFFFFF, 0, "private anon"},
}

for _, test in ipairs(mmap_tests) do
    local ok, ret = pcall(function()
        return sc522(uint64(test[1]), uint64(test[2]), uint64(test[3]),
                      uint64(test[4]), uint64(test[5]), uint64(test[6]))
    end)
    if ok then
        local h, l = get_hi_lo(ret)
        print(string.format("  522(%s): ret=0x%X%08X", test[7], h, l))
        -- If it returned an address, try reading from it
        if h > 0 and h < 0xFFFF0000 then
            local rd = safe_rd(ret)
            if rd then
                print(string.format("    -> readable! first dword: 0x%08X", rd))
            end
        end
    else
        print(string.format("  522(%s): CRASH: %s", test[7], tostring(ret)))
    end
end

print("")
print("--- PHASE 5: Syscall 622 deep probe (largest, 20KB, narg=6) ---")
print("")

local sc622 = make_syscall(622)

-- Try various argument patterns for the largest handler
local test_patterns = {
    {"zeros", 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0},
    {"buf+size", buf1, 0x1000, 0, 0, 0, 0},
    {"buf+buf+size", buf1, buf2, 0x1000, 0, 0, 0},
    {"cmd=1", 1, buf1, 0x1000, 0, 0, 0},
    {"cmd=2", 2, buf1, 0x1000, 0, 0, 0},
    {"cmd=3", 3, buf1, 0x1000, 0, 0, 0},
    {"cmd=0x10", 0x10, buf1, 0x1000, 0, 0, 0},
    {"cmd=0x100", 0x100, buf1, 0x1000, buf2, buf3, 0x1000},
    {"pid+buf", pid, buf1, 0x1000, 0, 0, 0},
    {"fd=3+buf", 3, buf1, 0x1000, buf2, 0, 0},
}

for _, test in ipairs(test_patterns) do
    -- Zero buffers before each test
    for i = 0, 0xFF, 4 do
        pcall(function() memory.write_dword(buf1 + i, 0xDEADBEEF) end)
        pcall(function() memory.write_dword(buf2 + i, 0xDEADBEEF) end)
    end

    local ok, ret = pcall(function()
        return sc622(uint64(test[2]), uint64(test[3]), uint64(test[4]),
                      uint64(test[5]), uint64(test[6]), uint64(test[7]))
    end)
    if ok then
        local h, l = get_hi_lo(ret)
        local r = to_num(ret)
        local line = string.format("  622(%s): ret=%d (0x%X%08X)", test[1], r, h, l)

        -- Check if buf1 was modified
        local first_mod = nil
        for i = 0, 0xFF, 4 do
            local v = safe_rd(buf1 + i)
            if v and v ~= 0xDEADBEEF then
                first_mod = string.format("buf1+%d=0x%08X", i, v)
                break
            end
        end
        if first_mod then
            line = line .. "  [" .. first_mod .. "]"
        end
        print(line)
    else
        print(string.format("  622(%s): CRASH: %s", test[1], tostring(ret)))
    end
end

print("")
print("--- PHASE 6: Syscall 601 deep probe (10285B, narg=3) ---")
print("")

local sc601 = make_syscall(601)
local patterns601 = {
    {"zeros", 0, 0, 0},
    {"buf+size", buf1, 0x1000, 0},
    {"cmd=1+buf", 1, buf1, 0x1000},
    {"cmd=2+buf", 2, buf1, 0x1000},
    {"pid+buf+size", pid, buf1, 0x1000},
    {"fd=3+buf+size", 3, buf1, 0x1000},
    {"0xFF+buf", 0xFF, buf1, 0x1000},
}

for _, test in ipairs(patterns601) do
    for i = 0, 0xFF, 4 do
        pcall(function() memory.write_dword(buf1 + i, 0xCAFEBABE) end)
    end

    local ok, ret = pcall(function()
        return sc601(uint64(test[2]), uint64(test[3]), uint64(test[4]))
    end)
    if ok then
        local r = to_num(ret)
        local line = string.format("  601(%s): ret=%d", test[1], r)
        local first_mod = nil
        for i = 0, 0xFF, 4 do
            local v = safe_rd(buf1 + i)
            if v and v ~= 0xCAFEBABE then
                first_mod = string.format("buf+%d=0x%08X", i, v)
                break
            end
        end
        if first_mod then line = line .. "  [" .. first_mod .. "]" end
        print(line)
    else
        print(string.format("  601(%s): CRASH: %s", test[1], tostring(ret)))
    end
end

print("")
print("=== PROBE 51b COMPLETE ===")
```

## probes/phase13_52batch/52a_survey_627_676.lua

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: MODERATE
-- PROBE 52a: Complete Sony syscall survey 627-676 (3 arg-pattern passes)
--
-- Context: 51a surveyed 532-~626 but the run was cut short (51c result file
-- ends right after 625/626, so 627-676 mostly never got results). 51b deep-
-- tested a handful in this range (640: ret=0 empty buffer; 628/648/652/676:
-- ret=-1). This probe completes the survey for the second half of the Sony
-- range using THREE arg-patterns per number, sequenced from safest to
-- riskiest so a crash pinpoints both the number AND the argument pattern:
--   PASS A: all-zero args (six uint64(0) slots)
--   PASS B: arg1 = allocated+zeroed 0x100 buffer, arg2 = 0x100 (len)
--   PASS C: six allocated+zeroed 0x100 buffers, one per arg slot
-- Every call is wrapped in pcall and a progress line is printed BEFORE the
-- call so the last output line identifies the killer if the process dies.
-- errno capture is not established yet (see 52d), so we print the raw ret
-- and classify it: SUCCESS / DENIED(-1) / positive errno-like / kernel-ptr.

print("=== PROBE 52a: SONY SYSCALL SURVEY 627-676 ===")
print("")

-- Standard helpers (ALWAYS include these)
local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_rq(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end
    return nil
end
local function safe_wd(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_dword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function safe_wq(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_qword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function get_hi_lo(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then return val.h, val.l end
    return 0, to_num(val)
end
-- uint64 for addresses >32-bit (CLAUDE.md rule: string.format hi/lo form)
local function mkaddr(addr)
    if type(addr) == "table" and addr.h then return addr end
    local n = to_num(addr)
    if n <= 0 then return uint64(0) end
    if n < 4294967296 then
        return uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", 0, n))
    end
    local hi = math.floor(n / 4294967296)
    local lo = n - hi * 4294967296
    return uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", hi, lo))
end

local function hexdump(addr, len)
    local parts = {}
    for i = 0, len - 4, 4 do
        local v = safe_rd(addr + i)
        if v then
            table.insert(parts, string.format("%08X", v))
        else
            table.insert(parts, "????????")
        end
    end
    return table.concat(parts, " ")
end

local function scan_for_kptrs(addr, len)
    local found = {}
    for i = 0, len - 8, 8 do
        local val = safe_rq(addr + i)
        if val then
            local h, l = get_hi_lo(val)
            if h >= 0xFFFF8000 and h < 0xFFFFFFFF then
                table.insert(found, {i, h, l})
            end
        end
    end
    return found
end

local sc_getpid = make_syscall(20)
local ok_pid, pid_ret = pcall(function() return sc_getpid() end)
local pid = ok_pid and to_num(pid_ret) or 0
print("PID: " .. pid)
print("Range: 627-676 (50 numbers), 3 passes each = 150 calls")

-- Allocated + zeroed buffers
local Z = uint64(0)
local bufB = memory.alloc(0x100)          -- PASS B output buffer
for i = 0, 0xFC, 4 do safe_wd(bufB + i, 0) end
local ptrs = {}                            -- PASS C: six 0x100 buffers
for i = 1, 6 do
    ptrs[i] = memory.alloc(0x100)
    for j = 0, 0xFC, 4 do safe_wd(ptrs[i] + j, 0) end
end

-- Snapshot first 0x40 bytes of a buffer (dwords) for change detection
local function snapshot(addr)
    local t = {}
    for i = 0, 0x3C, 4 do t[#t + 1] = safe_rd(addr + i) end
    return t
end

local function diff_report(addr, snap, label)
    -- compare current content vs snapshot; print hexdump of first 0x40
    -- bytes + kernel-ptr scan if anything changed
    local changed = false
    for i = 0, 0x3C, 4 do
        local v = safe_rd(addr + i)
        if v ~= snap[(i / 4) + 1] then changed = true end
    end
    if changed then
        print("    " .. label .. " CHANGED: " .. hexdump(addr, 0x40))
        local kptrs = scan_for_kptrs(addr, 0x100)
        if #kptrs > 0 then
            for _, kp in ipairs(kptrs) do
                print(string.format("    !!! KPTR %s+%02X = %08X_%08X",
                    label, kp[1], kp[2], kp[3]))
            end
        end
    end
    return changed
end

-- Build the argument vector for a given pass
local function call_pattern(sc, pat, buf)
    if pat == 1 then
        return sc(Z, Z, Z, Z, Z, Z)
    elseif pat == 2 then
        return sc(mkaddr(buf), uint64(0x100), Z, Z, Z, Z)
    else
        return sc(mkaddr(ptrs[1]), mkaddr(ptrs[2]), mkaddr(ptrs[3]),
                  mkaddr(ptrs[4]), mkaddr(ptrs[5]), mkaddr(ptrs[6]))
    end
end

local nums = {}
for n = 627, 676 do nums[#nums + 1] = n end

-- per-number best record: {num, group, pass, ret_h, ret_l, note}
local records = {}

-- Groups from 51a table layout (approximate, for labeling only)
local function group_of(num)
    if num <= 626 then return "proc"
    elseif num <= 641 then return "io"
    elseif num <= 660 then return "misc"
    elseif num <= 670 then return "dev"
    end
    return "misc"
end

local pass_names = { "A(all-zero)", "B(buf+len)", "C(6-pointers)" }

for pass = 1, 3 do
    print("")
    print("--- PASS " .. pass .. " " .. pass_names[pass] .. " ---")
    for _, num in ipairs(nums) do
        -- PROGRESS FIRST: if the process dies, this line names the culprit
        print(string.format("  P%d num=%d calling now...", pass, num))

        local sc = make_syscall(num)
        local ok, ret

        if pass == 1 then
            ok, ret = pcall(function() return call_pattern(sc, 1, bufB) end)
        elseif pass == 2 then
            for i = 0, 0xFC, 4 do safe_wd(bufB + i, 0) end
            local snap = snapshot(bufB)
            ok, ret = pcall(function() return call_pattern(sc, 2, bufB) end)
            if ok then diff_report(bufB, snap, "bufB") end
        else
            local snaps = {}
            for i = 1, 6 do snaps[i] = snapshot(ptrs[i]) end
            ok, ret = pcall(function() return call_pattern(sc, 3, bufB) end)
            if ok then
                for i = 1, 6 do
                    diff_report(ptrs[i], snaps[i], "ptr" .. i)
                end
            end
        end

        local h, l = 0, 0
        local tag = " [PCALL-FAIL]"
        if ok then
            h, l = get_hi_lo(ret)
            if h == 0 and l == 0 then
                tag = " [SUCCESS]"
            elseif h == 0xFFFFFFFF and l == 0xFFFFFFFF then
                tag = " [-1 DENIED]"
            elseif h == 0 then
                tag = " [+errno-like?]"
            elseif h >= 0xFFFF8000 and h < 0xFFFFFFFF then
                tag = " [KERNEL PTR!!!]"
            elseif h >= 0x80000000 then
                tag = " [hi-set/sony-err?]"
            end
        else
            ret = nil
        end

        print(string.format("  P%d num=%d ret=%s%s",
            pass, num,
            ok and string.format("0x%08X_%08X", h, l) or tostring(ret),
            tag))

        -- record best (non -1) result per number
        local rv_ok = ok and not (h == 0xFFFFFFFF and l == 0xFFFFFFFF)
        if rv_ok then
            local rec = records[num]
            if not rec then
                records[num] = {num, group_of(num), pass, h, l, tag}
            end
        end
    end
end

print("")
print("=== SUMMARY: NON-(-1) RESULTS ===")
local count = 0
for _, num in ipairs(nums) do
    local rec = records[num]
    if rec then
        count = count + 1
        print(string.format("  [%s] %d: pass=%s ret=0x%08X_%08X %s",
            rec[2], rec[1], pass_names[rec[3]], rec[4], rec[5], rec[6]))
    end
end
print(string.format("Accessible in 627-676: %d / 50", count))

-- repeat...until true + break used instead of goto (Lua 5.1 constraint)
-- demonstrated here as the sanctioned early-exit idiom:
do
    local n_access = count
    repeat
        if n_access == 0 then
            print("  NOTE: all -1 — second half of Sony range likely stubbed")
            break
        end
        print("  NOTE: accessible numbers found — deep-dive in 52c/next batch")
        break
    until true
end

print("")
print("=== PROBE 52a COMPLETE ===")
```

## probes/phase13_52batch/52b_624_oracle.lua

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: LOW
-- PROBE 52b: Syscall 624 as a live VM-metric oracle
--
-- Context: 51a/51b confirmed syscall 624 (narg=0) is alive and returns a
-- value that CHANGES BETWEEN CONNECTIONS (0xD31 in 51a's pid, 0xD30 in 51b's
-- pid). Hypothesis: it is a live VM counter (resident pages / budget metric
-- / charge). If it tracks memory state, it becomes a side channel:
--   - every mmap/munmap moves it -> we can observe kernel VM state
--   - touching pages may move it (page-touch accounting)
--   - other allocations (sockets, kqueues) may move it
-- Procedure: baseline, then controlled 477-mmap allocations of 1..16 pages
-- re-reading 624 after each; a 512-page mmap with page-touches sampled every
-- 32 pages; munmap deltas; jitter loop of 100 tight samples; plus churn of
-- other allocation types (sockets, kqueue, Lua memory.alloc).

print("=== PROBE 52b: SYSCALL 624 ORACLE ===")
print("")

-- Standard helpers (ALWAYS include these)
local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_rq(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end
    return nil
end
local function safe_wd(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_dword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function safe_wq(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_qword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function get_hi_lo(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then return val.h, val.l end
    return 0, to_num(val)
end
-- uint64 for addresses >32-bit (CLAUDE.md rule: string.format hi/lo form)
local function mkaddr(addr)
    if type(addr) == "table" and addr.h then return addr end
    local n = to_num(addr)
    if n <= 0 then return uint64(0) end
    if n < 4294967296 then
        return uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", 0, n))
    end
    local hi = math.floor(n / 4294967296)
    local lo = n - hi * 4294967296
    return uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", hi, lo))
end

local sc624 = make_syscall(624)
local function read624()
    local ok, ret = pcall(function() return sc624() end)
    if ok then
        local h, l = get_hi_lo(ret)
        if h == 0 then return l end
        return nil
    end
    return nil
end

local sc_getpid = make_syscall(20)
local ok_pid, pid_ret = pcall(function() return sc_getpid() end)
local pid = ok_pid and to_num(pid_ret) or 0
print("PID: " .. pid .. "  (624 changed across pids in 51a/51b)")

local function fmt(v)
    if v == nil then return "FAIL" end
    return string.format("%d (0x%X)", v, v)
end

-- ============================================================
-- SECTION 1: Baseline stability (3 reads)
-- ============================================================
print("")
print("--- SECTION 1: baseline ---")
local b1, b2, b3 = read624(), read624(), read624()
print("  624 x3: " .. fmt(b1) .. " / " .. fmt(b2) .. " / " .. fmt(b3))

-- ============================================================
-- SECTION 2: mmap size sweep (1..16 pages), alloc + free deltas
-- ============================================================
print("")
print("--- SECTION 2: mmap size sweep 1..16 pages ---")

local sc_mmap   = make_syscall(477)
local sc_munmap = make_syscall(588)
local PAGE = 0x4000  -- 16KB kernel pages

local function do_mmap(sz)
    local ok, ret = pcall(function()
        return sc_mmap(mkaddr(0), mkaddr(sz), uint64(0x33),
            uint64(0x1002), uint64("0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF"), uint64(0))
    end)
    if not ok then return nil end
    local h, l = get_hi_lo(ret)
    if h ~= 0 and h >= 0xFFFF8000 then return nil end
    if l == 0 and h == 0 then return nil end
    -- GPU mmap bases observed ~0x3xxxxxxxx -> exact as doubles
    return h * 4294967296 + l
end

local function do_munmap(addr, sz)
    pcall(function() sc_munmap(mkaddr(addr), mkaddr(sz)) end)
end

for npages = 1, 16 do
    local before_alloc = read624()
    local addr = do_mmap(npages * PAGE)
    local after_alloc = read624()
    local after_free = nil
    if addr then do_munmap(addr, npages * PAGE) end
    after_free = read624()
    print(string.format("  mmap %2dpg: before=%s after_alloc=%s after_free=%s  delta_alloc=%+d delta_free=%+d",
        npages, fmt(before_alloc), fmt(after_alloc), fmt(after_free),
        (after_alloc and before_alloc) and (after_alloc - before_alloc) or 0,
        (after_free and after_alloc) and (after_free - after_alloc) or 0))
end

-- ============================================================
-- SECTION 3: 512-page mapping + page touches (sampled every 32)
-- ============================================================
print("")
print("--- SECTION 3: 512-page mmap, touch pages, sample 624 ---")

local base = do_mmap(512 * PAGE)
if base then
    print("  mmap base=" .. string.format("0x%08X%08X",
        math.floor(base / 4294967296), base % 4294967296))
    local v_start = read624()
    print("  624 before touches: " .. fmt(v_start))

    for i = 0, 511 do
        -- write a marker qword at the start of each page (page-touch)
        safe_wq(base + i * PAGE, uint64(0))  -- harmless zero write
        safe_wd(base + i * PAGE, 0xCAFE0000 + i)
        safe_wd(base + i * PAGE + 4, 0)
        if i % 32 == 31 then
            local v = read624()
            print(string.format("  after page %3d touched: 624=%s", i + 1, fmt(v)))
        end
    end

    local v_end = read624()
    print("  624 after all 512 touches: " .. fmt(v_end))

    -- verify the mapping is really ours
    local chk = safe_rd(base)
    print("  page0 dword = " .. string.format("%08X", chk or 0))

    do_munmap(base, 512 * PAGE)
    local v_free = read624()
    print("  624 after munmap: " .. fmt(v_free) ..
        "  delta_total=" .. ((v_free and v_start) and (v_free - v_start) or 0))
else
    print("  512-page mmap FAILED (alloc caps?)")
end

-- ============================================================
-- SECTION 4: Jitter — 100 tight samples
-- ============================================================
print("")
print("--- SECTION 4: jitter, 100 tight samples ---")

local samples = {}
local n_ok = 0
for i = 1, 100 do
    local v = read624()
    samples[i] = v
    if v then n_ok = n_ok + 1 end
end
local distinct = {}
local vmin, vmax = nil, nil
for i = 1, 100 do
    local v = samples[i]
    if v then
        distinct[v] = true
        if vmin == nil or v < vmin then vmin = v end
        if vmax == nil or v > vmax then vmax = v end
    end
end
local ndist = 0
for _ in pairs(distinct) do ndist = ndist + 1 end

-- print raw sequence, 10 per row
local row = {}
for i = 1, 100 do
    if samples[i] then
        row[#row + 1] = string.format("%7d", samples[i])
    else
        row[#row + 1] = "   FAIL"
    end
    if i % 10 == 0 then
        print("  [" .. string.format("%3d-%3d", i - 9, i) .. "] " ..
            table.concat(row, " "))
        row = {}
    end
end
print(string.format("  jitter: ok=%d distinct=%d min=%s max=%s",
    n_ok, ndist, fmt(vmin), fmt(vmax)))
if ndist == 1 then
    print("  -> STABLE within a connection: supports per-VM/budget metric")
elseif vmin and vmax and (vmax - vmin) <= 2 then
    print("  -> near-stable: may be quota with small churn effects")
else
    print("  -> MOVES during runtime: live counter confirmed")
end

-- ============================================================
-- SECTION 5: Other allocation types
-- ============================================================
print("")
print("--- SECTION 5: other allocation types ---")

-- sockets
local sc_socket = make_syscall(97)
local sc_close  = make_syscall(6)
do
    local v0 = read624()
    local made = 0
    for i = 1, 10 do
        local ok, fd = pcall(function()
            return sc_socket(uint64(2), uint64(1), uint64(0), uint64(0),
                uint64(0), uint64(0))
        end)
        if ok and to_num(fd) > 0 then
            made = made + 1
            pcall(function() sc_close(to_num(fd)) end)
        end
    end
    local v1 = read624()
    print(string.format("  10 sockets: before=%s after=%s delta=%+d",
        fmt(v0), fmt(v1), (v1 and v0) and (v1 - v0) or 0))
end

-- kqueue
do
    local sc_kqueue = make_syscall(362)
    local v0 = read624()
    local ok, kq = pcall(function() return sc_kqueue() end)
    local knum = ok and to_num(kq) or -1
    local v1 = read624()
    if knum > 0 then pcall(function() sc_close(knum) end) end
    print(string.format("  kqueue: before=%s after=%s delta=%+d",
        fmt(v0), fmt(v1), (v1 and v0) and (v1 - v0) or 0))
end

-- Lua-side memory.alloc churn (C allocator, not a syscall)
do
    local v0 = read624()
    local blobs = {}
    for i = 1, 8 do blobs[i] = memory.alloc(0x1000) end
    local v1 = read624()
    print(string.format("  8x memory.alloc(0x1000): before=%s after=%s delta=%+d",
        fmt(v0), fmt(v1), (v1 and v0) and (v1 - v0) or 0))
    blobs = nil
end

-- dynlib_get_info call (kernel touches per-module info)
do
    local v0 = read624()
    local ok, v1 = pcall(function()
        local info = memory.alloc(0x200)
        safe_wd(info, 0x160)
        local sc_info = make_syscall(593)
        pcall(function() sc_info(uint64(0), mkaddr(info)) end)
        return read624()
    end)
    print(string.format("  dynlib_get_info: before=%s after=%s delta=%+d",
        fmt(v0), fmt(v1 or read624()), (v1 and v0) and (v1 - v0) or 0))
end

print("")
print("=== PROBE 52b COMPLETE ===")
```
